*uktaṃ devādhidevena śraddhātavyaṃ dvijātibhiḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

130-131. Or otherwise, by listening to a single episode of this Purana, a person is adored in the Brahmaloka. Lord Visnu who took to the form of Kurma or tortoise and as such this Purana earned the title of Kurma Purana. Because of this, it is also called Kurma Purana as well. It is a matter of faith for the Brahmanas.

## Chapter 2. Description of Varnas and Asramas

## \|\| 1.2.1 \|\|

*śrīkūrma uvāca*  
*śṛṇudhvamṛṣayaḥ sarve yatpṛṣṭo 'haṃ jagaddhitam \|*  
*vakṣyamāṇaṃ mayā sarvamindradyumnāya bhāṣitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Kurma said, “For the benefit of the universe, the question you have from me, all the sages should listen to the reply attentively. I am repeating the entire speech which had been delivered by me to Indradyumna.

## \|\| 1.2.2 \|\|

*bhūtairbhavyairbhaviṣyadbhiścaritairupabṛṃhitam \|*  
*purāṇaṃ puṇyadaṃ nṛṇāṃ mokṣadharmānukīrtanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. This Kurma Purana which comprises of the events relating to the present, past and future, is extremely auspicious for the followers of the path of moksa.

## \|\| 1.2.3 \|\|

*ahaṃ nārāyaṇo devaḥ pūrvamāsaṃ na me param \|*  
*upāsya vipulāṃ nidrāṃ bhogiśayyāṃ samāśritaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I happen to be lord Narayana, there was none before me. 1 had been reclining over the serpent bed in deep sleep.

## \|\| 1.2.4-5 \|\|

*cintayāmi punaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ niśānte pratibudhya tu \|*  
*tato me sahasotpannaḥ prasādo munipuṅgavā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*caturmukhastato jāto brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tadantare 'bhavat krodhaḥ kasmāccit kāraṇāt tadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Then at the end of the night, I woke up and thought about the creation. Then, О sages, I suddenly felt blissful, Then Brahma, the creator of the universe was bom of the same. At that point of time, I some how got enraged.

## \|\| 1.2.6-7 \|\|

*ātmano muniśārdūlāstatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*rudraḥ krodhātmajo jajñe śūlapāṇistrilocanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tejasā sūryasaṃkāśastrailokyaṃ saṃharanniva \|*  
*tataḥ śrīrabhavad devi kamalāyatalocanā \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. О best of the sages, then Mahes'vara, with the terrific form emerged out of me, holding a trident in his hand and having three eyes. He looked as if burning all the three lokas with his flames. Thereafter Lakshmi having the lotus like eyes was bom.

## \|\| 1.2.8-9 \|\|

*surūpā saumyavadanā mohinī sarvadehinām \|*  
*śucismitā suprasannā maṅgalā mahimāspadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*divyakāntisamāyuktā divyamālyopaśobhitā \|*  
*nārāyaṇī mahāmāyā mūlaprakṛtiravyayā \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. She had a beautiful form, the charming face, who could attract all the living beings, wearing the serene smile over the face, was delightful, auspicious as well as the glorious one. She possessed the divine luster, adorned with a divine garland, and was known as NarayanI, Mahamaya (great deluding Potency) and the eternal Mulaprakrti (primordial nature).

## \|\| 1.2.10 \|\|

*svadhāmnā pūrayantīdaṃ matpārśvaṃ samupāviśat \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭavā bhagavān brahmā māmuvāca jagatpatiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. She filled the universe with her lustre, she arrived and seated herself by my side. Looking at her, Brahma addressed me as the lord of the universe.

## \|\| 1.2.11 \|\|

*mohāyāśeṣabhūtānāṃ niyojaya surūpiṇīm \|*  
*yeneyaṃ vipulā sṛṣṭirvardhate mama mādhava \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “O Madhava, you depute this beauty to overpower the living beings of the universe in delusion, which will result in the expansion of my creation.”

## \|\| 1.2.12 \|\|

*tathokto 'haṃ śriyaṃ devīmabruvaṃ prahasanniva \|*  
*devīdamakhilaṃ viśvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At these words of Brahma, I spoke smilingly to the goddess Lakshmi, “O Goddess, after confusing all the gods, demons, and the humans, in the world, at my command, you spread yourself in the entire world.

## \|\| 1.2.13-15 \|\|

*mohayitvā mamādeśāt saṃsāre vinipātaya \|*  
*jñānayogaratān dāntān brahmiṣṭhān brahmavādinaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*akrodhanān satyaparān dūrataḥ parivarjaya \|*  
*dhyāyino nirmamān śāntān dhārmikān vedapāragān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*jāpinastāpasān viprān dūrataḥ parivarjaya \|*  
*vedavedāntavijñānasaṃchinnāśeṣasaṃśayān \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. But leave aside untouched those engaged in path of knowledge, those who possessing self- control, devoted to Brahman, who expound the Vedas. Keep yourself far off those who are devoid of anger besides those who are devoted to tmth. Those who are engaged in meditation, who are spotless, peaceful, religious minded, well-versed in the Vedas, performers of the yajnas, and the Brahmanas besides the ascetics. Those who have been cleared of all the doubts in the Vedas as well as the Vedanta, or the Brahmanas who perform the yajnas regularly, should be left out.

## \|\| 1.2.16-17 \|\|

*mahāyajñaparān viprān dūrataḥ parivarjaya \|*  
*ye yajanti japairhemairdevadevaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

*svādhyāyenejyayā dūrāt tān prayatnena varjaya \|*  
*bhaktiyogasamāyuktānīśvarārpitamānasān \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Such of the people, who perform japa, religious studies, and meditate upon Mahesvara, by performing of the yajnas they should be left out making all the efforts. Those whose minds are engaged in the path of devotion (Bhakti- yoga), and those who are devoted to the lord and having the spotless minds, should be left out from a distance.

## \|\| 1.2.18-20 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmādiṣu ratān dūrāt pariharāmalān \|*  
*praṇavāsaktamanaso rudrajapyaparāyaṇān \|\| 18 \|\|*

*atharvaśiraso 'dhyetṛn dharmajñān parivarjaya \|*  
*bahunātra kimuktena svadharmaparipālakān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*īśvarārādhanaratān manniyogānna mohaya \|*  
*evaṃ mayā mahāmāyā preritā harivallabhā \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Those who are devoted to the Pranava doctrine, engaged in the tapas for Rudra, well- versed in the Atharva siras and other religious minded people should be left out. What more should be spoken in this connection? At my command, do not delude those who follow dharma and those engaged in the adoration of the lord should not be deluded.” In this way, Mahamaya, the spouse of lord Hari, was thus influenced by me.

## \|\| 1.2.21-22 \|\|

*yathādeśaṃ cakārāsau tasmāllakṣmīṃ samarcayet \|*  
*śriyaṃ dadāti vipulāṃ puṣṭiṃ medhāṃ yaśo balam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*arcitā bhagavatpatnī tasmāllakṣmīṃ samarcayet \|*  
*tato 'sṛjat sa bhagavān brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. She acted as per my command and because of this, Lakshmi should be adored. When so adored, the said Lakshmi, bestows enormous riches, progress, wisdom, glory and the prowess. Because of this, Lakshmi, the spouse of Visnu, should be adored. Thereafter Brahma, the grandsire, resorted to the creation of the universe.

## \|\| 1.2.23-26 \|\|

*carācarāṇi bhūtāni yathāpūrvaṃ mamājñayā \|*  
*parīcibhṛgvaṅgirasaḥ pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dakṣamatriṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca so 'sṛjad yogavidyayā \|*  
*navaite brahmaṇaḥ putrā brahmāṇo brāhmaṇottamāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*brahmavādina evaite marīcyādyāstu sādhakāḥ \|*  
*sasarja brāhmaṇān vaktrāt kṣatriyāṃśca bhujād vibhuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vaiśyānūrudvayād devaḥ pādārchūdrān pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*yajñaniṣpattaye brahmā śūdravarjaṃ sasarja ha \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. Then Brahma as per my earlier command, created several types of moveable and immoveable living beings. Thereafter by yogic power he created (nine sons) Marichi, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Daksa, Atri and Vasistha. These nine sons of Brahma are the best among the Brahmanas, who were expounders of the Vedas. Marichi and others were sadhakas. Brahma created Brahmanas, out of his mouth and the Ksatriyas out of the arms. Brahma, the grand sire created the Vaisyas out of both the thighs and the Sudras out of his feet. Thereafter for the performance of the yajhas, the three varnas, except the Sudras were created.

## \|\| 1.2.27-28 \|\|

*guptaye sarvavedānāṃ tebhyo yajño hi nirbabhau \|*  
*ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni tathaivātharvaṇāni ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*brahmaṇaḥ sahajaṃ rūpaṃ nityaiṣā śaktiravyayā \|*  
*anādinidhanā divyā vāgutsṛṣṭā svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. The yajna was created for the protection of the gods. Thereafter the mantras of Rgveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda were created. All of them are the natural forms of Brahma. They represent the eternal and immutable Potency (Shakti). Brahma then created the divine speech (Vak) which was free from the beginning or the end.

## \|\| 1.2.29-32 \|\|

*ādau vedamayī bhūtā yataḥ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ \|*  
*ato 'nyānitu śāstrāṇipṛthivyāṃyānikānicit \|\| 29 \|\|*

*na teṣu ramate dhīraḥ pāṣaṇḍī tena jāyate \|*  
*vedārthavittamaiḥ kāryaṃ yatsmṛtaṃ munibhiḥ purā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sa jñeyaḥ paramo dharmo nānyaśāstreṣu saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*yā vedabāhyāḥ smṛtayo yāśca kāśca kudṛṣṭayaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sarvāstā niṣphalāḥ pretyatamoniṣṭhāhitāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*pūrvakalpe prajā jātāḥ sarvabādāvivarjitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. Initially, it was the speech of the Vedas, which produced the perseverance, the people with wisdom do not indulge in the scriptures other them these in the world. Only the cheats do so. In earlier times, the sages well versed in the interpretation of the Vedas, had remembered for the accomplishment of the task, it should be treated as the supreme dharma and not the one available in the other literature. The Smrtis which are contrary to the Vedas,1 and the evil practices, bestow no good reward after the death, because all of them are shrouded in tamas. At the start of the kalpas the people devoid of all the obstruction were bom.

## \|\| 1.2.33 \|\|

*śuddhāntaḥ karaṇāḥ sarvāḥ svadharmaniratāḥ sadā \|*  
*tataḥ kālavaśāt tāsāṃ rāgadveṣādiko 'bhavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. All of them have spotless minds and devoted to dharma. Then under the influence of the time, the attractions and jealousies were developed in them.

## \|\| 1.2.34 \|\|

*adharmo muniśārdūlāḥ svadharmapratibandhakaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sā sahajā siddhistāsāṃ nātīva jāyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О Best of sages, the adharma (unrighteousness) becomes the obstruction for dharma. Because of this it does not possess the best of the siddhis (yogic power).

## \|\| 1.2.35 \|\|

*rajomātrātmikāstāsāṃ siddhayo 'nyāstadābhavan \|*  
*tāsu kṣīṇāsvaśeṣāsu kālayogena tāḥ punaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then they atained other siddhis of purely rajasic nature. Thereafter because of the kalayoga e.i. in course of time, they faced decline and they again re-emerged.

## \|\| 1.2.36 \|\|

*vārtopāyaṃ punaścakrurhastasiddhiṃ ca karmajām \|*  
*tatastāsāṃ vibhurbrahmā karmājīvamakalpayat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Again in due course of time, the means of livelihood and the handicrafts were created. Thereafter the omniscient Brahma, created the best means of livelihood.

## \|\| 1.2.37-41 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvo manuḥ pūrvaṃ dharmān provāca dharmadṛk \|*  
*sākṣāt prajāpatermūrtirnisṛṣṭā brahmaṇā dvijāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bhṛgvādayastadvadanācchrutvā dharmānathocire \|*  
*yajanaṃ yājanaṃ dānaṃ brāhmaṇasya pratigraham \|\| 38 \|\|*

*adhyāpanaṃ cādhyayanaṃ ṣaṭ karmāṇi dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*dānamadhyayanaṃ yajño dharmaḥ kṣatriyavaiśyayoḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*daṇḍo yuddhaṃ kṣatriyasya kṛṣirvaiśyasya śasyate \|*  
*śuśrūṣaiva dvijātīnāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ dharmasādhanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kārukarma tathājīvaḥ pākayajño 'pi dharmataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sthiteṣu varṇeṣu sthāpayāmāsa cāśramān \|\| 41 \|\|*

37-41. Initially, Manu, the son of self-bom deity, with all pervading vision and the form of the eternal one proclaimed the righteous duties of all persons. О Brahmanas, he was very embodiment of Prajapati created by god Brahma himself. Bhrgu and others Brahmanas beared the Dharma-sastra from his mouth as narreted by him and again they proclaimed them as follows : The performing of the yajna, presiding over other’s sacrifices, the giving of charitable gifts, and the receiving of the charities, study of the Vedas and it’s teaching, are the six duties which were prescribed for the Brahmana. The giving of charities, studies and to function as the performer of the yajnas, are the activities meant for the Ksatriyas and Vaisyas out of them, the waging of the war and the awarding of the punishment, were to be carried out by the Ksatriyas, the Vaisyas were also made responsible for farming. The Sudras were meant for serving the Brahmanas and others. Their Paka-yajHa (whatever they cook) with righteousness and serving as an artisan, was also their livelihood. Thereafter with the establishment of all the four classes (varnas) Brahma also established four As'ramas.

## \|\| 1.2.42-47 \|\|

*gṛhasthaṃ ca vanasthaṃ ca bhikṣukaṃ brahmacāriṇam \|*  
*agnayo 'tithiśuśrūṣā yajño dānaṃ surārcanam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*gṛhasthasya samāsena dharmo 'yaṃ munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*homo mūlaphalāśitvaṃ svādhyāyastapa eva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*saṃvibhāgo yathānyāyaṃ dharmo 'yaṃ vanavāsinām \|*  
*bhaikṣāśanaṃ ca maunitvaṃ tapo dhyānaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*samyagjñānaṃ ca vairāgyaṃ dharmo 'yaṃ bhikṣuke mataḥ \|*  
*bhikṣācaryā ca śuśrūṣā guroḥ svādhyāya eva ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sandhyākarmāgnikāryaṃ ca dharmo 'yaṃ brahmacāriṇām \|*  
*brahmacārivanasthānāṃ bhikṣukāṇāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*sādhāraṇaṃ brahmacaryaṃ provāca kamalodbhavaḥ \|*  
*ṛtukālābhigāmitvaṃ svadāreṣu na cānyataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

42-47. The four as'ramas are those of householders, the forest dweller (Vanaprasthas), the mendicant (Bhiksukas), and Brahmacarin (religious student). О Best of sages, protection of fire, serving the quests, performing of the yajnas, to give away charities, adoration of the gods, are briefly the duties of the householder. Performing of homa, consuming of the fruits and roots, studies, tapas and judicious distribution are the duties of the forest dwellers. To receive the food by begging alms, to keep silence, performing of tapas and meditation, achieving of the realistic knowledge and detachment, are the duties of a Bhiksu or a Sannyasl. Begging of alms, serving the preceptors, studies of the Vedas, performing of Sandhyas, and performing of the oblation in fire are the duties of Brahmacarin. О Best of the Brahmana, to maintain celibacy (brahmacarya), are also essential for the Vanaprastha and a Sannyasl. This has been ordained by Brahma. They should enjoy the company of their spouses during the menstruation only and not other wise.

## \|\| 1.2.48 \|\|

*parvavarjaṃ gṛhasthasya brahmacaryamudāhṛtam \|*  
*āgarbhasaṃbhavādādyāt kāryaṃ tenāpramādataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. A house holder who does not have union with his wife, except on the festive occasions, he is considered to be performing the brahmacarya. Therefore, discarding the arrogance and upto the conception of the wife, this process has been allowed to be preserved.

## \|\| 1.2.49-51 \|\|

*akurvāṇastu viprendrā bhrūṇahā tu prajāyate \|*  
*vedābhyāso 'nvahaṃ śaktyā śrāddhaṃ cātithipūjanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*gṛhasthasya paro dharmo devatābhyarcanaṃ tathā \|*  
*vaivāhmamagnimindhīta sāyaṃ prātaryathāvidhi \|\| 50 \|\|*

*deśāntaragato vātha mṛtapatnīka eva vā \|*  
*trayāṇāmāśramāṇāṃ tu gṛhastho yonirucyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. О Indras among the Brahmanas, in case the process is not followed, one earns the sin of killing of the foetus. It is incumbent on the householder to study Vedas regularly, to perform Srddha as per one’s capacity, to serve the quests, and the adoration of the gods. The marriage fire should be ignited in the morning and the evening, whether he is out of his city or even when his wife is dead. Thus the householder's as'rama is the best of the three asramas.

## \|\| 1.2.52-53 \|\|

*anye tamupajīvanti tasmācchreyān gṛhāśramī \|*  
*aikāśramyaṃ gṛhasthasya trayāṇāṃ śrutidarśanāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tasmād gārhasthyamevaikaṃ vijñeyaṃ dharmasādhanam \|*  
*parityajedarthakāmau yau syātāṃ dharmavarjitau \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Rest of the three asramas are dependent on the Grhasthasrama or the as'rama of the householder. Therefore the householder's as'rama is the best. Therefore the Grhasthasrama should be considered to be the means of dharma. The dharma devoid of artha and kama should be discarded.

## \|\| 1.2.54 \|\|

*sarvalokaviruddhaṃ ca dharmamapyācarenna tu \|*  
*dharmāt saṃjāyate hyartho dharmāt kāmo 'bhijāyate \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. One should not follow the dharma which is against all the people of the world. Artha is earned out of dharma and the kama also gets increased with dharma.

## \|\| 1.2.55 \|\|

*dharma evāpavargāya tasmād dharmaṃ samāśrayet \|*  
*dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca trivargastriguṇo mataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Dharma (righteousness) is the cause of moksa (final emancipation), therefore, one should take refuge in dharma. Dharma, artha and kama comprise of the three gunas.

## \|\| 1.2.56-58 \|\|

*sattvaṃ rajastamaśceti tasmāddharmaṃ samāśrayet \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ \|*  
*yasmin dharmasamāyuktāvarthakāmau vyavasthitau \|\| 57 \|\|*

*iha loke sukhī bhūtvā pretyānantyāya kalpate \|*  
*dharmāt saṃjāyate mokṣo hyarthāt kāmo 'bhijāyate \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. These three gunas are sattva, rajas and tamas) Therefore one should depend upon dharma. Those who take refuge in Sattvaguna, they proceed to the higher regions. Those possessing rajoguna proceed on to the middle region, while embracing tamoguna proceed to the netherworld. A person in whom artha and кйта remain unitedly, he enjoying all the comforts in this loka and enjoys all the pleasures even after death. Moksa is achieved by dharma and kama gets increased by artha.

## \|\| 1.2.59-60 \|\|

*evaṃ sādhanasādhyatvaṃ cāturvidhye pradarśitam \|*  
*ya evaṃ veda dharmārthakāmamokṣasya mānavaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*māhātmyaṃ cānutiṣṭheta sa cānantyāya kalpate \|*  
*tasmādarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca tyaktvā dharmaṃ samāśrayet \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Thus there appears that there is utility and purposefulness in the combination of dharma, artha, kama and moksa. A person who is aware of the glory of dharma, artha, kama and moksa, and makes use of them accordingly, he enjoys the unending pleasure. Therefore discarding artha and kama one should depend on dharma.

## \|\| 1.2.61 \|\|

*dharmāt saṃjāyate sarvamityāhurbrahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*dharmeṇa dhāryate sarvaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The expounders of the Vedas say that Dharma yields everything. The entire moveable and immoveable universe is held by means of dharma.

## \|\| 1.2.62 \|\|

*anādinidhanā śaktiḥ saiṣā brāhmī dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā prāpyate dharmo jñānena ca na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. О Best of the Brahmanas, this is the Brahml- s'akti, which is beyond beginning or the end. One can achieve dharma by means of deeds (karmas) and the knowledge. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.2.63-64 \|\|

*tasmājjñānena sahitaṃ karmayogaṃ samācaret \|*  
*pravṛttaṃ ca nivṛttaṃ ca dvividhaṃ karma vaidikam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*jñānapūrvaṃ nivṛttaṃ syāt pravṛttaṃ yadato 'nyathā \|*  
*nivṛttaṃ sevamānastu yāti tat paramaṃ padam \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Therefore, one should take refuge with activity filled with knowledge. There are two types of Vedic karma according to the methods of nivrtti and pravrtti. The activity which is supported by knowledge, it is based on nivrtti. The activity which is sided by ignorance, it is known as based of pravrtti. The one who performs activity based on nivrtti, he achieves the highest position.

## \|\| 1.2.65-68 \|\|

*tasmānnivṛttaṃ saṃsevyamanyathā saṃsaret punaḥ \|*  
*kṣamā damo dayā dānamalobhastyāga eva ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ārjavaṃ cānasūyā ca tīrthānusaraṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*satyaṃ santoṣa āstikyaṃ śraddhā cendriyanigrahaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*devatābhyarcanaṃ pūjā brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*āhiṃsā priyavāditvamapaiśunyamakalkatā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*sāmāsikamimaṃ dharmaṃ cāturvarṇye 'bravīnmanuḥ \|*  
*prājāpatyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ smṛtaṃ sthānaṃ kriyāvatām \|\| 68 \|\|*

65-68. Therefore, one should resort to nivrtti activity, otherwise one shall have to wander again in world. As ordained by Manu, forgiveness, control of the sense organs, compassion, giving of charities, absence of greed, renunciation, simplicity, free from jealousy, making of pilgrimage, truthfulness, satisfaction, belief in god, devotion, control of sense organs, adoration of gods and the Brahmanas, non-violence, sweet talk, not to indulge in backbiting, sinlessness, are the qualities which should be applicable in all the Varnas, as ordained by Manu. The active Brahmanas have been equated with Brahma-the Prajapati.

## \|\| 1.2.69-71 \|\|

*sthānamaindraṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ saṃgrāmeṣvapalāyinām \|*  
*vaiśyānāṃ mārutaṃ sthānaṃ svadharmamanuvartatām \|\| 69 \|\|*

*gāndharvaṃ śūdrajātīnāṃ paricāreṇa vartatām \|*  
*aṣṭāśītisahastrāṇāmṛṣīṇāmūrdhvaretasām \|\| 70 \|\|*

*smṛtaṃ teṣāṃ tu yatsthānaṃ tadeva guruvāsinām \|*  
*saptarṣoṇāṃ tu yatsthānaṃ smṛtaṃ tad vai vanaukasām \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. The Ksatriyas who do not desert the battle ground, achieve the place of Indra, the Vaisyas who follow their dharma achieve the place of Maruts and the Stidras who serve the Brahmanas achieve the position of Gandharvas. The place which has been earmarked for eighty eight urdhvareta ascetics the same place is eannarked for a student who carries on his studies with the preceptor. The Vanaprasthas achieve the position of SaptaRishis. ятяточ здпр; wrgem

## \|\| 1.2.72-73 \|\|

*prājāpatyaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ sthānamuktaṃ svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*yatīnāṃ yatacittānāṃ nyāsināmūrdhvaretasām \|\| 72 \|\|*

*hairaṇyagarbhaṃ tat sthānaṃ yasmānnāvartate punaḥ \|*  
*yogināmamṛtaṃ sthānaṃ vyomākhyaṃ paramākṣaram \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. Svayambhfi Brahma has prescribed the place of Prajapatyas for the householders. Hiranyagarbha is the abode for the ascetics, those who have restrained their passions and abandoned the world. This is the exactly the place from where, one does not have to return to the earth. For the yogis, the place is blissful abode in the space, which nectar like, blissful, filled with all the riches, which is extreme as well as supreme.

## \|\| 1.2.74 \|\|

*ānandamaiśvaraṃ dhāma sā kāṣṭhā sā parāgatiḥ \|*  
*ṛṣaca ūcuḥ bhagavan devatārighna hiraṇyākṣaniṣūdana \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The Rishis said, "O Lord you are the killer of the enemies, destroyer of Hiranyaksa, you have described the asramas as four, but you have prescribed a single asrama for the yogis.

## \|\| 1.2.75-76 \|\|

*catvāro hyāśramāḥ proktā yogināmeka ucyate \|*  
*śrīkūrma ūvāca sarvakarmāṇi saṃnyasya samādhimacalaṃ śritaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*ya āste niścalo yogī sa saṃnyāsī na pañcamaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmāśramāṇāṃ tu dvaividhyaṃ śrutadarśitam \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. Khrma said- “Whosoever discarding all the activities is always absorbed in meditation, he surely is a yogin, besides being a Pancama Sannyasi. The s'ruti has prescribed all the asramas of two types.

## \|\| 1.2.77 \|\|

*brahmacāryupakurvāṇo naiṣṭhiko brahmatatparaḥ \|*  
*yo 'dhītyavidhivadvedān gṛhasthāśramamāvrajet \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The Brahmacarins are also of two types i.e. Upakurvana and Naistika, who is absorbed in Brahman. The one who enters the household life after studying the Vedas, he is known as upakurvana. The Naisthika Brahmacarin is the person who observes Brahmacarya till death.

## \|\| 1.2.78-83 \|\|

*upakurvāṇako jñeyo naiṣṭhiko maraṇāntikaḥ \|*  
*udāsīnaḥ sādhakaśca gṛhastho dvividho bhavet \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kuṭumbabharaṇe yattaḥ sādhako 'sau gṛhī bhavet \|*  
*ṛṇānitrīṇyapākṛtyatyaktvā bhāryādhanādikam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*ekākī yastu vicaredudāsīnaḥ sa maukṣikaḥ \|*  
*tapastapyati yo 'raṇye yajed devān juhoti ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

*svādhyāye caiva nirato vanasthastāpaso mataḥ \|*  
*tapasā karṣito 'tyarthaṃ yastu dhyānaparo bhavet \|\| 81 \|\|*

*sāṃnyāsikaḥ sa vijñeyo vānaprasthāśrame sthitaḥ \|*  
*yogābhyāsarato nityamārurukṣurjitendriyaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*jñānāya vartate bhikṣuḥ procyate pārameṣṭhikaḥ \|*  
*yastvātmaratireva syānnityatṛpto mahāmuniḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

78-83. Even the householders are of two type known as Udaslna and Sadhaka. A person or a householder who remains engaged in the upkeep of the family he is called the sadhaka and the one who getting relieved of the three types of debts, discarding the wife and the riches, wanders alone, getting desirous of moksa he is called Udaslna or detached. The householder who performs lapas in the forest, adores the gods, performing the yajna, and keeps himself in studies, such a mendicant is called a Vanaprastha. The one who reduces his body, becoming lean and thin, remains engaged in meditation, he should be taken to be a Sannyasl. The one who is always engaged in yogic practices, controlling all the sense organs, becoming a bhiksu, he is called Paramesthika. One who sports with his soul, always remains blissful, becoming studious, and is possessed with Samyag-dars'ana, such a yogin is called the Bhiksu.

## \|\| 1.2.84-87 \|\|

*samyag darśanasaṃpannaḥ sa yogī bhikṣurucyate \|*  
*jñānasaṃnyāsinaḥ kecid vedasaṃnyāsino 'pare \|\| 84 \|\|*

*karmasanyāsinaḥ kecit trividhāḥ parāmeṣṭhikāḥ \|*  
*yogī ca trividho jñeyo bhautikaḥ sāṃkhya eva ca \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tṛtīyotyāśramī proktī yogamuttamamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*prathamā bhāvanā pūrve sāṃkhye tvakṣarabhāvanā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*tṛtīye cāntimā proktā bhāvanā pārameśvarī \|*  
*tasmādetad vijānīdhvamāśramāṇāṃ catuṣṭayam \|\| 87 \|\|*

84-87. Some are known as Jhana-Sannyasins.1 Others are Veda-sannyasins2 and some are karma-sannyasins (renouncers of actions). In this way the Paramesthika are of three type. The Yogins are also of three types viz. Bhautikas (Vaidikas), Samkhyas and third are Asramins, who have resorted to the excellent Yoga. Initially there is the first bhdvana (meditation) of Yoga is said for the first type of Yogins. For the Samkhyas aksara-bhavand3 is said and in the third there is the Paramesvarl-bhdvana or the meditation on Supreme soul. Thus the as'ramas should be known to be of four types.

## \|\| 1.2.88-90 \|\|

*sarveṣu vedaśāstreṣu pañcamo nopapadyate \|*  
*evaṃ varṇāśramān sṛṣṭvā devadevo nirañjanaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*dakṣādīn prāha viśvātmā sṛjadhvaṃ vividhāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇo vacanāt putrā dakṣādyā munisattamāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*asṛjanta prajāḥ sarvā devamānuṣapūrvikāḥ \|*  
*ityeṣa bhagavān brahmā straṣṭvatve sa vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

88-90. There is no mention of the fifth as'rama in any one of the Vedas and the Sastras. In this way the spotless god of gods, the lord who is the soul of the universe, explained the details of the varnas and as'ramas after creating them to the sages like Daksa and others. Then he said, “Now you can create various types of living beings.” Listening to the words of Brahma, his son Daksa and other sages, besides the gods and the humans resorted to the various types of creations.

## \|\| 1.2.91-95 \|\|

*ahaṃ vai pālayāmīdaṃ saṃhariṣyati śūlabhṛt \|*  
*tistrastu mūrtayaḥ proktā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*rajaḥ sattvatamoyogāt parasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*anoyanyamanuraktāste hyanyonyamupajīvinaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*anyonyaṃ praṇatāścaiva līlayā parameśvarāḥ \|*  
*brāhmī māheśvarī caiva tathaivākṣarabhāvanā \|\| 93 \|\|*

*tistrastu bhāvanā rudre vartante satataṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*pravartate mayyajastramādyā cākṣarabhāvanā \|\| 94 \|\|*

*dvitīyā brahmaṇaḥ proktā devasyākṣarabhāvanā \|*  
*ahaṃ caiva mahādevo na bhinnau paramārthataḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

91-95. Thus getting engaged in the task of the creation, Brahma said, “I shall maintain the earth and Lord Shiva shall look after its destruction. With the combination of Sattva, rajas and tamas there are three images of the supremer soul, known as Brahma, Visnu and Mahes'a. They are self supporters and are attached with one and other. They adore one another playfully only. There are three Bhavanas Brahml (concerning lord Brahma), Mahesvari (concerning lord Shiva) and Aksarabhavana (meditation on the Eternal). All are always lodged in Rudra. The first Aksarabhavana, functions perpetually in me. The second Aksara-bhavana is said to belong to Brahma. In fact, myself and Mahadeva have no separate entity.

## \|\| 1.2.96-98 \|\|

*vibhajyasvecchayātmānaṃ so 'nyaryāmīśvaraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*trailokyamakhilaṃ straṣṭuṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 96 \|\|*

*puruṣaḥ parato 'vyaktād brahmatvaṃ samupāgamat \|*  
*tasmād brahmā mahādevo viṣṇurviśveśvaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*ekasyaiva smṛtāstistrastanūḥ kāryavaśāt prabhoḥ \|*  
*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena vandyāḥ pūjyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

96-98. Ishvara-the supreme being, for the creation of the gods, humans and the three worlds, remains there dividing himself. The Supreme person who is unmanifest (Avyakta) achieved the form of Brahman. Therefore, Brahma, Visnu and Shiva- all the three of them were divided into three. Therefore all the three of them are equally respectable besides being adorable.

## \|\| 1.2.99-100 \|\|

*yadīcchedacirāt sthānaṃ yattanmokṣākhyamavyayam \|*  
*varṇāśramaprayuktena dharmeṇa prītisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*pūjayed bhāvayuktena yāvajjīvaṃ pratijñayā \|*  
*caturṇāmāśramāṇāṃ tu prokto 'yaṃ vidhivaddvijāḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. In case one is desirous of achieving eternal state of moksa without delay, then lovingly following the duties of cast and stages of life, should adore the lord as one lives, with utmost devotion. О Brahmanas, thus I have explained the position about all the varmsrama dharma elaborately.

## \|\| 1.2.101-102 \|\|

*āśramo vaiṣṇavo brāhmo harāśrama iti trayaḥ \|*  
*talliṅgadhārī satataṃ tadbhaktajanavatsalaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*dhyāyedathārcayedetān brahmavidyāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva bhaktānāṃ śaṃbhorliṅgamanuttamam \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. There are three types of asramas known as Vaisnava, Brahma and Harasrama (relating to lord Visnu, Brahma and Shiva). One who is devotee of a perticular sect he should wear a perticuar mark. The devotee, engaged in the practice of Brahmavidya, should adore and meditate upon them. The Linga of Shiva is the best for all the devotees.

## \|\| 1.2.103-105 \|\|

*sitena bhasmanā kāryaṃ lalāṭe tu tripuṇḍrakam \|*  
*yastu nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ prapannaḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*dhārayet sarvadā śūlaṃ lalāṭe gandhavāribhiḥ \|*  
*prapannā ye jagadbījaṃ brahmāṇaṃ parameṣṭhinam \|\| 104 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ lalāṭe tilakaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ tu sarvadā \|*  
*yo 'sāvanādirbhūtādiḥ kālātmāsau dhṛto bhavet \|\| 105 \|\|*

103-105. They should plaster their foreheads with white bhasma (sacrificial ashes) with tripundra. Those who have taken refuge with Narayana, should mark a trident with the sandal paste on forehead. Such of the devotees, who have taken refuge with Brahma-the Paramesthin, the seed- creator of the world, he should always apply tilaka (a circular mark) over the forehead. Thereby it is as the devotee wears the form of beginningless and eternal kalatma (presiding god of time).

## \|\| 1.2.106 \|\|

*uparyadho bhāvayogāt tripuṇḍrasya tu dhāraṇāt \|*  
*yattat pradhānaṃ triguṇaṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivātmakam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. With the application of tripundra over the upper and the lower part of body, thereby Pradhana is worn, which is consisting of three qualities in the form of Brahma, Visnu and Shiva. There is no doubt that they are so worn by wearing the trident mark.

## \|\| 1.2.107-108 \|\|

*dhṛtaṃ triśūladharaṇād bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*brahmatejomayaṃ śuklaṃ yadetan maṇḍalaṃ raveḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*bhavatyeva dhṛtaṃ sthānamaiśvaraṃ tilake kṛte \|*  
*tasmāt kāryaṃ triśūlāṅkaṃ tathā ca tilakaṃ śubham \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. With the application of tilaka, a person holds the place of riches in solar region which is white and endowed with the lustre of Brahman. By wearing this tilaka mark he certainly holds the region of Tsvara. Therefore the symbol of a trident and the tilaka are auspicious and bestows welfare.

## \|\| 1.2.109-111 \|\|

*triyāyuṣaṃ ca bhaktānāṃ trayāṇāṃ vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*yajeta juhuyādagnau japed dadyājjitendriyaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*śānto dānto jitakrodho varṇāśramavidhānavit \|*  
*evaṃ paricared devān yāvajjīvaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ saṃsthānamacalaṃ so 'cirādadhigacchati \|\| 111 \|\|*

109-111. By performing this appropriately, there is an increase in the age of all the three types of devotees. The one who has controlled his sense organs, is peaceful and the one who has overpowered the anger, should adore the lord. One should perform homa (oblation) in fire and give away the charities performing the japa. In this way one should adore through out the life and by doing so he shall achieve the infallible place of the gods in no time.

## Chapter 3. Chronology of Asramas

## \|\| 1.3.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*varṇā bhagavatoddiṣṭāścatvāro 'pyāśramāstathā \|*  
*idānīṃ kramamasmākamāśramāṇāṃ vada prabho \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis asked, “O Lord, you have spoken on all the four varnas as well as the four asramas. Now you kindly speak on the asramas in a sequence.

## \|\| 1.3.2 \|\|

*śrīkūrma uvāca*  
*brahmacārī gṛhasthaśca vānaprastho yatistathā \|*  
*krameṇaivāśramāḥ proktāḥ kāraṇādanyathā bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Lord Kurma said, Brahmacarin, Householder, Vanaprastha, and Sannyasins are the four asramas prescribed in a sequence. There could be a difference in sequence due to some reasons.

## \|\| 1.3.3 \|\|

*utpannajñānavijñāno vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*pravrajed brahmacaryāt tu yadicchet paramāṃ gatim \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A person who had gained the divine knowledge, or a detached person with forethought, being desirous is of moksa then he can embrace Sannyasa while in Brahmacarya.

## \|\| 1.3.4-5 \|\|

*dārānāhṛtya vidhivadanyathā vividhairmakhaiḥ \|*  
*yajedutpādayet putrān virakto yadi saṃnyaset \|\| 4 \|\|*

*aniṣṭvā vidhivad yajñairanutpādya tathātmajam \|*  
*nagārhasthyaṃ gṛhītyaktvā saṃnyased buddhimān dvijaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Otherwise a householder should after marriage perform several yajnas with his wife, and produce sons. In case of his feeling detached, he should embrace Sannyasa. But without performing the yajna appropriately and without producing sons, a householder with wisdom, should not accept Sannyasa, renouncing the householder responsibilities.

## \|\| 1.3.6 \|\|

*atha vairāgyavegena sthātuṃ notsahate gṛhe \|*  
*tatraiva saṃnyased vidvānaniṣṭvāpi dvijottamaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In case, however, because of the being of his attaining vairagya, a householder is not inclined to live in the household, then the best of the Brahmana should at once embrace Sannyasa.

## \|\| 1.3.7 \|\|

*anyathā vividhairyajñairiṣṭvā vanamathākṣayet \|*  
*tapastaptvā tapoyogād viraktaḥ saṃnyased yadi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Besides, he, after performing several types of karmas should embrace the Vanaprastha as'rama and after performing tapas in that position, developing the feeling of renunciation, should embrace Sannyasa.

## \|\| 1.3.8 \|\|

*vānaprasthāśramaṃ gatvā na gṛhaṃ praviśet punaḥ \|*  
*na saṃnyāsī vanaṃ cātha brahmācaryaṃ na sādhakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Accepting the Vanaprastha-as'rama, he should never enter his house- thereafter. Similarly the sadhaka as well as the Sannvasl should hot re-enter his house.

## \|\| 1.3.9-10 \|\|

*prājāpatyāṃ nirūpyeṣṭimāgneyīmathavā dvijaḥ \|*  
*pravrajeta gṛhī vidvān vanād vā śruticodanāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*prakartumasamartho 'pi juhotiyajatikriyāḥ \|*  
*andhaḥ paṅgurdaridro vā viraktaḥ saṃnyased dvijaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. An intelligent householder, after performing the Agneyi and Prajapatya sacrifices, should enter Sannyasa from Vanaprastha’s position according to the provision of the scriptures. In case, he is capable to do so, he continues in all the activities, while performing the homa. A blind, lame, and pauper Brahmana should, getting detached accept Sannyasa.

## \|\| 1.3.11 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva vairāgyaṃ saṃnyāsāya vidhīyate \|*  
*patatyevāvirakto yaḥ saṃnyāsaṃ kartumicchati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The renunciation is essential for embracing Sannyasa. In case, an unattached person becomes desirous of embracing Sannyasa, he is sure to fall.

## \|\| 1.3.12 \|\|

*ekasminnathavā samyag vartetāmaraṇaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*śraddhāvanāśrame yuktaḥ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Otherwise, one should continue to perform in one and the same asrama always. In this way, one who performs himself dutifully in one and the same as'rama, he is bound to achieve the place of nectar.

## \|\| 1.3.13 \|\|

*nyāyāgatadhanaḥ śānto brahmavidyāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*svadharmapālako nityaṃ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A person who earns his livelihood judiciously, remains peaceful, devoted to Brahmavidya, and follows his own dharma, he always aspires for Brahman.

## \|\| 1.3.14 \|\|

*brahmaṇyādhāya kramāṇi niḥsaṅgaḥ kāmavarjitaḥ \|*  
*prasannenaiva manasā kurvāṇo yāti tatpadam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The one who absorbing all the karmas in Brahman, and the engages himself in other activities delightfully, he surely achieves the position of Brahman.

## \|\| 1.3.15 \|\|

*brahmaṇā dīyate deyaṃ brahmaṇe saṃpradīyate \|*  
*brahmaiva dīyate ceti brahmārpaṇamidaṃ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Whatever is to be given is given by Brahman, therefore the whole thing is dedicated to Brahman. Since Brahman, is given therefore it is treated as Brahmarpana (highest kind of dedication).

## \|\| 1.3.16 \|\|

*nāhaṃ kartā sarvametad brahmaiva kurute tathā \|*  
*etad brahmārpaṇaṃ proktamṛṣibhiḥ tattvadarśibhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The feeling that everything is Brahman and all the activities are performed by him, is considered to be Brahmdrpana by the Rishis well versed in the tattva)

## \|\| 1.3.17 \|\|

*prīṇātu bhagavānīśaḥ karmaṇānena śāśvataḥ \|*  
*karoti satataṃ buddhyā brahmārpaṇamidaṃ param \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A person with wisdom who tries to please the lord with his performance, for him thus feeling should be treated as Brahmarpana.

## \|\| 1.3.18 \|\|

*yadvā phalānāṃ saṃnyāsaṃ prakuryāt parameśvare \|*  
*karmaṇāmetadapyāhuḥ brahmārpaṇamanuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Otherwise, the one who dedicates the rewards of his karmas to the lord always, intelligently, for him the dedication of the karmas is treated to be Brahmdrpana.

## \|\| 1.3.19 \|\|

*kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṃ saṅgavarjitam \|*  
*kriyate viduṣā karma tadbhavedapi mokṣadam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A man of letters, getting unattached performs the activities as prescribed in the Sastras taking them to be his duty, regularly, such of his activities bestow moksa for him.

## \|\| 1.3.20 \|\|

*anyathā yadi karmāṇi kuryānnityamapi dvijaḥ \|*  
*akṛtvā phalasaṃnyāsaṃ badhyate tatphalena tu \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Otherwise when a Brahmana, without foregoing the reward, performs the activities, he is not bound with reward of those karmas.

## \|\| 1.3.21 \|\|

*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena tyaktvā karmāśritaṃ phalam \|*  
*avidvānapi kurvota karmāpnotyacirāt padam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Due to this, discarding the reward of the karmas by all means, in case one engages himself in activities, he, in due course of time, achieves the desired position.

## \|\| 1.3.22 \|\|

*karmaṇā kṣīyate pāpamaihikaṃ paurvikaṃ tathā \|*  
*manaḥ prasādamanveti brahma vijñāyate tataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. With the performing of the karmans, all the sins of the earlier births are washed out. Then the mind of the said person gets delighted and he is considered to be the one who knows Brahman.

## \|\| 1.3.23 \|\|

*karmaṇā sahitājjñānāt samyag yogo 'bijāyate \|*  
*jñānaṃ ca karmasahitaṃ jāyate doṣavarjitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Jhana in combination with karmas, surely bestows the appropriate yoga. The jhana with karma gives rise to spotlessness.

## \|\| 1.3.24 \|\|

*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena tatra tatrāśrame rataḥ \|*  
*karmāṇīśvaratuṣṭyarthaṃ kuryānnaiṣkarmyamāpnuyāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Because of this, while making all the efforts and living in a ds'rama, for the pleasure of the god, discarding the detachment, one should engage himself in activities and by doing so one develops the feeling of detachment.

## \|\| 1.3.25 \|\|

*saṃprāpya paramaṃ jñānaṃ naiṣkarmyaṃ tatprasādataḥ \|*  
*ekākī nirmamaḥ śānto jīvanneva vimucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Because of the lord's grace, achieving the supreme knowledge, with an unattached view, he being deprived of the confusion, spending the life peacefully, achieves liberation.

## \|\| 1.3.26 \|\|

*vīkṣate paramātmānaṃ paraṃ brahma maheśvaram \|*  
*nityānandaṃ nirābhāsaṃ tasminneva layaṃ vrajet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thereafter, he has an audience with lord Paramesvara, and feeling blissful, is absorbed in Brahman in an invisible manner.

## \|\| 1.3.27 \|\|

*tasmāt seveta satataṃ karmayogaṃ prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*tṛptaye parameśasya tat padaṃ yāti śāśvatam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Therefore a person with a delightful mind, for the continuous pleasure of Paramesvara, should take refuge with karmayoga (the path of action) and by doing so, the achieves the eternal position.

## \|\| 1.3.28 \|\|

*etad vaḥ sathitaṃ sarvaṃ cāturāśramyamuttamam \|*  
*na hyetat samatikramya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In this way, all the four asramas have been explained by me in the best possible way. By transgressing them, a person, can never achieve success.

## Chapter 4. Description of Prakrta-Sarga

## \|\| 1.4.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śrutvā'śramavidhiṃ kṛtsanamṛṣayo hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya hṛṣīkeśaṃ punarvacanamabruvan \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “After listening to the methodology of all the four asramas, the Rishis felt delighted. All of them again, offering their salutation to lord Hrishikesa (Lord Kurma), again spoke.

## \|\| 1.4.2 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*bhāṣitaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ cāturāśramyamuttamam \|*  
*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmo yathā saṃbhavate jagat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Rishis said, “you have well described all the four stages of life {asramas). Now we would like to know about the creation of the universe.

## \|\| 1.4.3 \|\|

*kutaḥ sarvamidaṃ jātaṃ kasmiṃśca layameṣyati \|*  
*niyantā kaśca sarveṣāṃ vadasva puruṣottama \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Lord Purusottama, wherefrom has the universe emerged? Where shall it be absorbed? Who is the controller of the same? You kindly speak it out.

## \|\| 1.4.4 \|\|

*śrutvā nārāyaṇo vākyamṛṣīṇāṃ kūrmarūpadhṛk \|*  
*prāha gambhīrayā vācā bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Lord Narayana, taking to the form of Kurma, the eternal one, creator of bhutas, listening to the words of the ascetics, spoke out in deep voice.

## \|\| 1.4.5 \|\|

*śrīkūrma uvāca*  
*maheśvaraḥ paro 'vyaktaścaturvyūhaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*anantaścāprameyaśca niyantā viśvatomukhaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Kurma said, “Lord Mahesvara, the supreme one, unmanifest, the everlasting one, Caturvyuha (lord of four manifestation i.e. Vasudeva, Sankarsana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha), infinite, beyond measure, boundless, the face of all the living beings, is the controller of all.

## \|\| 1.4.6 \|\|

*avyaktaṃ kāraṇaṃ yattannityaṃ sadasadātmakam \|*  
*pradhānaṃ prakṛtiśceti yadāhustattvacintakāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Those who are well-versed in tattvas, have termed him invisible, cause, eternal, form of truth and falsehood, Pradhana and Prakrti.

## \|\| 1.4.7 \|\|

*gandhavarṇarasairhenaṃ śabdasparśavivarjitam \|*  
*ajaraṃ dhruvamakṣayyaṃ nityaṃ svātmanyavasthitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The same supreme soul is free from smell and colour, free from essence, beyond the sound and touch, beyond old age, Dhruva, indestructible, eternal and the one who is absorbed in his own soul.

## \|\| 1.4.8-9 \|\|

*jagadyonirmahābhūtaṃ paraṃ brahma sanātanam \|*  
*vigrahaḥ sarvabhūtānāmātmanādhiṣṭhitaṃ mahat \|\| 8 \|\|*

*anādyantamajaṃ sūkṣmaṃ triguṇaṃ prabhavāpyayam \|*  
*asāṃpratamavijñeyaṃ brahmāgre samavartata \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. It is the place of origin of the universe, and the Primary element. Parabrahman, infinite, the cosmic body of all creatures, the mahat presided over by the soul. It has neither beginning nor end, unborn, subtle, having three qualities (gunas), origin of all beings, imperishable, and beyond the knowledge. It is only Brahman was in existence in the beginning.

## \|\| 1.4.10 \|\|

*guṇasāmye tadā tasmin puruṣe cātmani sthite \|*  
*prākṛtaḥ pralayo jñeyo yāvad viśvasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When there is the comlete equation of the gunas and the purusa exists in his blissful state, this should be known as Prakrta-pralaya or the dessolution pertaining till the creation of the universe.

## \|\| 1.4.11 \|\|

*brāhmī rātririyaṃ proktā ahaḥ sṛṣṭirudāhṛtā \|*  
*aharna vidyate tasya na rātrirhyupacārataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. This dissolution is considered to be the night of Brahma, while the same is the day for the creation. Practically there is neither a day nor the night for Brahma, it is only figurative application.

## \|\| 1.4.12-13 \|\|

*niśānte pratibuddho 'sau jagadādiranādimān \|*  
*sarvabhūtamayo 'vyakto hyantaryāmīśvaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva praviśyāśu maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*kṣobhayāmāsa yogena pareṇa parameśvaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. At the end of the night by waking up, Mahesvara, who is the being the eternal, representing all the bhutas, invisible, all pervading and the form of the supreme soul, -the same Prakrti and Purusa, entered the space and disturbed it violently.

## \|\| 1.4.14 \|\|

*yathā mado narastrīṇāṃ yathā vā mādhavo 'nilaḥ \|*  
*anupraviṣṭaḥ kṣobhāya tathāsau yogamūrtimān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. - As the wind of the spring season or the god of love, entering the male and a female, disturbs them both, similarly Brahman the form of yoga, disturbed both of them.

## \|\| 1.4.15 \|\|

*sa eva kṣobhako viprāḥ kṣobhyaśca parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*sa saṃkocavikāsābhyāṃ pradhānatve 'pi ca sthitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О Brahmanas, the same Supreme lord is the subject and object of agitation. By means of removel and increase, the same is established as being Pradhana.

## \|\| 1.4.16 \|\|

*pradhānāt kṣobhyamāṇācca tathā puṃsaḥ purātanāt \|*  
*prādurāsīnmahad bījaṃ pradhānapuruṣātmakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Being agitation of Pradhana and ancient Purusa, a great seed called mahat was bom out from them.

## \|\| 1.4.17 \|\|

*mahānātmā matirbrahmā prabuddhiḥ khyātirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*prajñādhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ saṃvidetasmāditi tat smṛtam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This Mahat is Atman, Май, Brahma, Prabuddhi, khyati, Is'vara, Prajnct, Dhrti, Smrti, and Samvit. This has been ordained by the scriptures.

## \|\| 1.4.18 \|\|

*vaikārikastaijasaśca bhūtādiścaiva tāmasaḥ \|*  
*trividho 'yamahaṅkāro mahataḥ saṃbabhūva ha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The ahamkara (Ego) of three types i.e. Vaikdrika (product of sattva-guna), taijas (product of rajas-guna) and bhutadi (all elements), the product of Tamas were bom out of Mahat.

## \|\| 1.4.19 \|\|

*ahaṅkāro 'bimānaśca kartā mantā ca sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ātmā ca pudgalo jīvo yataḥ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Ahamkara is said by name of Abhimana, the the agent and the thinker. The supreme soul and jlva (individual soul) abide in all and from them all actions arise.

## \|\| 1.4.20 \|\|

*pañcabhūtānyahaṅkārāt tanmātrāṇi ca jajñire \|*  
*indriyāṇi tathā devāḥ sarvaṃ tasyātmajaṃ jagat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Out of the same ahamkara, bom five mahabhutas,1 five tanmatras,2 besides the sense organs were formed. Thus entire universe born of it.

## \|\| 1.4.21 \|\|

*manastvavyaktajaṃ proktaṃ vikāraḥ prathamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*yenāsau jāyate kartā bhūtādīṃścānupaśyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The mind is believed to have been created from Avyakta, which is said the first product. Because of this the same happens to be doer, besides being the viewer of other type of bhutadi ahamkdra.

## \|\| 1.4.22-23 \|\|

*vaikārikādahaṅkārāt sargo vaikāriko 'bhavat \|*  
*taijasānīndriyāṇi syurdevā vaikārikā daśa \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ekādaśaṃ manastatra svaguṇenobhayātmakam \|*  
*bhūtatanmātrasargo 'yaṃ bhūtāderabhavan prajāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The vaikarika-aharhkara produced the vaikarika creation.3 The sense organs are taijas or the product of Rajoguna, and the ten devas are Vaikdrika (who preside over sense organs). The eleventh mind is of the nature of both because of its own qualities. О Brahmanas, the creation of Bhdta-tanmatra (gross and subtle elements) was made from Bhutadi or the tamasic ego.

## \|\| 1.4.24 \|\|

*bhūtādistu vikurvāṇaḥ śabdamātraṃ sasarja ha \|*  
*ākāśaṃ śuṣiraṃ tasmādutpannaṃ śabdalakṣaṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When Bhutadi (Tamasa-ahamkara) undergoes modifications, it created the subtle element of sound (sabda-tanmatra). The ether was created out of it and sound happens to be its quality.

## \|\| 1.4.25 \|\|

*ākāśastu vikurvāṇaḥ sparśamātraṃ sasarja ha \|*  
*vāyurutpadyate tasmāt tasya sparśo guṇo mataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. When ether, after mutation of the original form, it creates subtle element of touch (Sparsa- tanmatra). The wind emerged out of it, and the touch is known as its quality.

## \|\| 1.4.26 \|\|

*vāyuścāpi vikurvāṇo rūpamātraṃ sasarja ha \|*  
*jyotirutpadyate vāyostadrūpaguṇamucyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The wind also, after getting modification creates nipa-tanmatra (form or colour subtle element). The fire emerged out of the wind, having the quality of form.

## \|\| 1.4.27 \|\|

*jyotiścāpi vikurvāṇaṃ rasamātraṃ sasarja ha \|*  
*saṃbhavanti tato 'mbhāṃsi rasādhārāṇi tāni tu \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The fire after having changes created subtle element of test {rasa-tanmatra) and the waters emerged out of it which are the sources of rasa.The water also getting modificatons, created subtle element of smell (gandha-tanmatra), as a result of which the mass of earth bom of it. Smell is said the quality for the same.

## \|\| 1.4.28 \|\|

*āpaścāpi vikurvantyo gandhamātraṃ sasarjire \|*  
*saṃghāto jāyate tasmāt tasya gandho guṇo mataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Ether has only Sabda-tanmatra which enveloped the sparsa-tanmatra. Therefore Vayu had the two qualities of sabda and sparsa.

## \|\| 1.4.29 \|\|

*ākāśaṃ śabdamātraṃ yat sparśamātraṃ samāvṛṇot \|*  
*dviguṇastu tato vāyuḥ śabdasparśātmako 'bhavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Both the gunas of sabda and sparsa, entered into гйра, as a result of which Agni had possessed the three gunas i.e. Sabda, Sparsa and Rupa.

## \|\| 1.4.30 \|\|

*rūpaṃ tathaivāviśataḥ śabdasparśau guṇāvubhau \|*  
*triguṇaḥ syāt tato vahniḥ sa śabdasparśarūpavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then sabda, spars'a and гйра entered into rasa-tanmatrd. Therefore waters having Rasa quality, should be known possessing of the four gunas.

## \|\| 1.4.31 \|\|

*śabda sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca rasamātraṃ samāviśan \|*  
*tasmāccaturguṇā āpo vijñeyāstu rasātmikāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The sabda, sparsa, гйра and rasa entered gandha (smell). As a result of this, the earth was possessed of five gurias? It is therefore considered as grossest among the five Mah&bhutas.

## \|\| 1.4.32 \|\|

*śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaṃ samāviśan \|*  
*tasamāt pañcaguṇā bhūmiḥ sthūlā bhūteṣu śabdyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Calmness, terrableness, and dullness have been said the special charateristics of the bhutas. All of them entering among themselves and sustain one another.

## \|\| 1.4.33 \|\|

*śāntā ghorāśca mūḍhāśca viśeṣāstena te smṛtāḥ \|*  
*parasparānupraveśād dhārayanti parasparam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. All the seven of them, having the great soul, depending on one another live on earth. Inspite of that, they cannot engage themselves in creation.

## \|\| 1.4.34 \|\|

*ete sapta mahātmāno hyanyonyasya samāśrayāt \|*  
*nāśaknuvan prajāḥ straṣṭumasamāgamya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Because it is presided over by Purusa2 3 and with the grace of the Avyakta, right from Mahat ending with Vis'esa, all combined create the cosmic egg.

## \|\| 1.4.35 \|\|

*puruṣādhiṣṭhitātvācca avyaktānugraheṇa ca \|*  
*mahādādayo viśeṣāntā hmaṇḍamutpādayanti te \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The egg, emerging at one and the same time, resembled the bubble in water with the cumulative effect of the aforesaid visesas, it grew into a gigantic form, and slept in the water.

## \|\| 1.4.36 \|\|

*ekakālasamutpannaṃ jalabudbudavacca tat \|*  
*viśeṣebhyo 'ṇḍamabhavad bṛhat tadudakeśayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. In the process, Paramesthin, the cause of the task, the egg bom of Prahu started growing therm. The presided soul (ksetrjna) was given the name of Brahma.

## \|\| 1.4.37 \|\|

*tasmin kāryasya karaṇaṃ saṃsiddhiḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*prākṛte 'ṇḍe vivṛttaḥ sa kṣetrajño brahmasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He is the first embodied person, also known as Purusa. He happens to be the first creator of all beings. That Brahma was existed in the beginning of universe.

## \|\| 1.4.38 \|\|

*sa vai śarīrī prathamaḥ sa vai puruṣa ucyate \|*  
*ādikartā sa bhūtānāṃ brahmāgre samavartata \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The one who is considered to be beyond Pradhdna-Prakrti} He is called Наша, Hiranyagarbha, of tawny-colour, the ancient form of the Vedas and Sanatana.

## \|\| 1.4.39 \|\|

*yamāhuḥ puruṣaṃ haṃsaṃ pradhānāt parataḥ sthitam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaṃ kapilaṃ chandomūrti sanātanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The Meru became his placenta and the mountains became the embryo, while the ocean became the foetal fluid of that great soul

## \|\| 1.4.40 \|\|

*merurulbamabhūt tasya jarāyuścāpi parvatāḥ \|*  
*garbhodakaṃ samudrāśca tasyāsan paramātmanaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Within that cosmic Egg evolved the whole world including gods, the asuras, the human beings, the moon, the sun, the constellations, the planets, and wind.

## \|\| 1.4.41 \|\|

*tasminnaṇḍe 'bhavad viśvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*candrādityau sanakṣatrau sagrahau saha vāyunā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The outer part of the egg was covered with the water which was ten times more than the egg. The outer part of the same was covered with ten times more of fire.

## \|\| 1.4.42 \|\|

*adbhirdaśaguṇābhiśca bāhyato 'ṇḍaṃ samāvṛtam \|*  
*āpo daśaguṇenaiva tejasā bāhyato vṛtāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. That tejas (fire) was further covered with the ten times more of Vayu. Similarly Vayu was covered with ether, besides ether was surrounded by BhUtadi.

## \|\| 1.4.44-46 \|\|

*bhūtādirmahatā tadvadavyaktenāvṛto mahān \|*  
*ete lokā mahātmanaḥ sarvatattvābhimāninaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*vasanti tatra puruṣāstadātmāno vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*īśvarā yogadharmāṇo ye cānye tattvacintakāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sarvajñāḥ śāntarajaso nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ \|*  
*etairāvaraṇairaṇḍaṃ saptabhiḥ prākṛtairvṛtam \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. Similarly Bhutadi is covered with Mahat and Mahat was covered with Avyakta. All these lokas combined, besides great-souled persons all skilled in Supreme knowledge, inhabit them. They are influential, and devoted to the Yogas. Some are devoted to the search of the reality. They are omniscient, devoid of rajoguna, and always remained delightful. This cosmic Egg was surrounded with the seven sheaths originating from Prakrti.

## \|\| 1.4.47 \|\|

*etāvacchakyate vaktuṃ māyaiṣā gahanā dvijāḥ \|*  
*etat prādhānikaṃ kāryaṃ yanmayā bījamīritam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. О Brahmanas, it can only be said, that the Maya is quite mysterious. This is the task of Prakrti, which has been termed as the seed by me.

## \|\| 1.4.48-49 \|\|

*prajāpateḥ parā mūrtiritīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇḍametat sakalaṃ saptalokatalānvitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*dvitīyaṃ tasya devasya śarīraṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbho bhagavān brahmā vai kanakāṇḍajaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. This is the highest form of Prajapati, according to the Vedic texts. The Brahmanda is the second body of Paramesthin (Brahma), having the strength of the seven lokas. Brahma having been bom out of the golden egg, is known as Hiranyagarbha.

## \|\| 1.4.50 \|\|

*tṛtīyaṃ bhagavadrūpaṃ prāhurvedārthavedinaḥ \|*  
*rajoguṇamayaṃ cānyad rūpaṃ tasyaiva dhīmataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Those who well-versed in the Vedas describe him to be the third form of the lord Brahma. There is another form of the intelligent one, which is embodied with rajoguna.

## \|\| 1.4.51 \|\|

*caturmukhaḥ sa bhagavān jagatsṛṣṭau pravartate \|*  
*sṛṣṭaṃ ca pāti sakalaṃ viśvātmā viśvatomukhaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The four-faced Brahma engages himself in the task of the creation of the universe. While Visnu, the lord of universe, resorting to Sattva- guna, maintains all this creation. He is the soul of the universe, and having faces all round.

## \|\| 1.4.52-54 \|\|

*sattvaṃ guṇamupāśritya viṣṇurviśveśvaraḥ svayam \|*  
*antakāle svayaṃ devaḥ sarvātmā parameśvaraḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tamoguṇaṃ samāśritya rudraḥ saṃharate jagat \|*  
*eko 'pi sanmahādevastridhāsau samavasthitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sargarakṣālayaguṇairnirguṇo 'pi nirañjanaḥ \|*  
*ekadhā sa dvidhā caiva tridhā ca bahudhā punaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. At the time of dissolution of the world, Paramesvara, the soul of the universe, himself being lord Rudra, under the influence of tamoguna, destroys the universe. Lord Mahadeva, inspite of his being spotless and absolute, is active in creation, maintenance and destruction. He remains present in all the three forms. With the influence of the different gunas of creation, protection and dissolution, he sometimes appears in one form, two forms or divides himself some times in three forms.

## \|\| 1.4.55 \|\|

*yogeśvaraḥ śarīrāṇi karoti vikaroti ca \|*  
*nānākṛtikriyārūpanāmavanti svalīlayā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The lord of Yoga, by his sportive activity, creates and dissolves the several types of bodies of different forms, activity, features and names.

## \|\| 1.4.56 \|\|

*hitāya caiva bhaktānāṃ sa eva grasate punaḥ \|*  
*tridhā vibhajya cātmānaṃ traikālye saṃpravartate \|*  
*sṛjate grasate caiva vīkṣate ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. With the sole desire of the welfare of the devotees, he devours them again. He divides himself in three forms and then changes in the three world.

## \|\| 1.4.57-58 \|\|

*yasmāt sṛṣṭvānugṛhṇāti grasate ca punaḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*guṇātmakatvāt traikālye tasmādekaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

*agre hiraṇyagarbhaḥ sa prādurbhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*āditvādādidevo 'sau ajātatvādajaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. He resorts to the special creation, destroys as well, while protecting the same at the same time. Because of the said quality, he is conceived to be one in all the three times, i.e. past, present and future. The eternal Hiranyagarbha Brahma appeared first of all.

## \|\| 1.4.59 \|\|

*pātiyasmāt prajāḥ sarvāḥ prajāpatiriti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*deveṣu ca mahādevo māhadeva iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Because of his emerging on earth, first of all, he has been known as Adideva. Because of his being unborn, he is also called as Aja. All the people are maintained by him because of which he is also known as Prajapati.

## \|\| 1.4.60 \|\|

*bṛhattvācca smṛto brahmā paratvāt parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*vaśitvādapyavaśyatvādīśvaraḥ paribhāṣitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Since he happens to be the greatest of all the gods, he is also known as Mahadeva. Because of his being of the gigantic form, he is known as Brahma. Since he happens to be above all, he has been known as Paramesvara.

## \|\| 1.4.61 \|\|

*ṛṣiḥ sarvatragatvena hariḥ sarvaharo yataḥ \|*  
*anutpādācca pūrvatvāt svayaṃbhūriti sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Because of his possessing the quality of overpowering others and because he cannot be overpowered by others, he is known as Ishvara. Because of his movement in all the places, he has been known as Rsi. Because he can steel everything, he is known by the name of Hari.

## \|\| 1.4.62 \|\|

*narāṇāmayano yasmāt tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*haraḥ saṃsāraharaṇād vibhutvād viṣṇurucyate \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Since he is beyond birth, besides being the earliest one, he has been known as Svayambhu. Similarly since he is the abode of the Naras, he is known as Narayana.

## \|\| 1.4.63 \|\|

*bhagavān sarvavijñānādavanādomiti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sarvajñaḥ sarvavijñānāt sarvaḥ sarvamayo yataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He is called Нага, because of he removes bondages of the world. Besides being endless, he is called Visnu. Because of his being all knowledgeable, he has been known Bhagavan and because of his protecting the living beings, he has been called as Om.

## \|\| 1.4.64 \|\|

*śivaḥ sa nirmalo yasmād vibhuḥ sarvagato yataḥ \|*  
*tāraṇāt sarvaduḥ khānāṃ tārakaḥ parigīyate \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Because of his possessing all the knowledge, he is known as Sarvajna (omniscient). He is Sarva, because he is identcal with all. He is called as Shiva, because of his being spotlessness and because he is present everywhere, he is called Vibhu.

## \|\| 1.4.65 \|\|

*bahunātra kimuktena sarvaṃ brahmamayaṃ jagat \|*  
*anekabhedabhinnastu krīḍate parameśvaraḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Because of his relieving all the living beings from all the miseries, he is known as Taraka. What is the use of speaking much? Actually, the entire world is like Brahman. This Parames'vara appears in various forms.

## \|\| 1.4.66 \|\|

*ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargaḥ saṃkṣepāt kathito mayā \|*  
*abuddhipūrvako viprā brāhmīṃ sṛṣṭiṃ nibodhata \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. In this way, the creation starting from Prakrti,1 has been described by me in brief. О Sages, now you listen about the creation of Brahma, prior to Mahat (the principle of Cosmic intelligence).

## Chapter 5. Details of numbers of Kalas

## \|\| 1.5.1-4 \|\|

*śrīkūrma uvāca*  
*anutpādācca pūrvasmāt svayaṃbhūriti sa spṛtaḥ \|*  
*narāṇāmayanaṃ yaspāttena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*haraḥ saṃsāraharaṇādvabhutavādiṣṇurucyate \|*  
*bhagavān sarvavijjañānādavanādomiti smṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sarvajñaḥ sarvavijñānātsarvaḥ sarvamayo yataḥ \|*  
*svayaṃbhuvo vivṛttasya kālasaṃkhyā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*na śakyate samākhyātuṃ bahuvarṣairapi svayam \|*  
*kālasaṃkhyā samāsena parārdhadvayakalpitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Lord Kurma said, “Because he is not born from any prior person, he is called Svayambhu and because of the collection of the waters, he is called Narayana. Because of his possessing all the Vibhutis (fortunes), he is called Visnu. Because of his being all knowledgeable, he is called Bhagavan and because of his extending protection to all, he is called Om. Because of his possessing the knowledge of sattva, he is known as omniscient. О Best of the Brahmanas, the life span of lord Brahma cannot be described in a large number of years. In brief, the said period of life has been known to be of two types.

## \|\| 1.5.5 \|\|

*sa eva syāt paraḥ kālaḥ tadante pratisṛjyate \|*  
*nijena tasya mānena āyurvarṣaśataṃ smṛtam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. That is the end of everything, after which the new creation follows. With the own standards of Svayambhu, his age has been prescribed to be of a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.5.6 \|\|

*tat parākhyaṃ tadardhaṃ ca parārdhamabhidīyate \|*  
*kāṣṭhā pañcadaśa khyātā nimeṣā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It is known as padartha or the half of it- the Parardha. О Best of the Brahmanas, fifteen nimesas (winking of the eyes), make a kdstha.

## \|\| 1.5.7 \|\|

*kāṣṭhāstriṃśat kalā triṃśat kalā mauhūrtikī gatiḥ \|*  
*tāvatsaṃkhyairahorātraṃ muhūrtairmānuṣaṃ smṛtam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thirty kasthas make a kcLla, while three kasthas make a Muhurta. The thirty muhurtas make an ahoratra.

## \|\| 1.5.8 \|\|

*ahorātrāṇi tāvanti māsaḥ pakṣadvayātmakaḥ \|*  
*taiḥ ṣaḍbhirayanaṃ varṣaṃ dve 'yane dakṣiṇottare \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Again thirty ahoratras make two fortnights (bright and dark) are equivalent to a month; six months make an ayana. Two ayanas as known as Uttardyana and Daksinayana, which make a year.

## \|\| 1.5.9-10 \|\|

*ayanaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ rātrirdevānāmuttaraṃ dinam \|*  
*divyairvarṣasahastraistu kṛtatretādisaṃjñitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*caturyugaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ tadvibhāgaṃ nibodhata \|*  
*catvāryāhuḥ sahastrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tatkṛtaṃ yugam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Daksinayana is the night for the gods, while uttardyana is the day for them. Twelve thousand divine years make the four yugas known as Satya, Treta, Dvapara and Kaliyuga. You listen to their division. Out of them Krtayuga or Satya comprises of four thousand years.

## \|\| 1.5.11 \|\|

*tasya tāvacchatī sandhyā sandhyāṃśaśca kṛtasya tu \|*  
*triśatī dviśatī sandhyā tathā caikaśatī kramāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Satyayuga has the evening of four hundred years. The part of Sandhyd is of equal duration. This sandhya is respectively for three hundred, two hundred and a hundred years duration.

## \|\| 1.5.12-13 \|\|

*aṃśakaṃ ṣaṭśataṃ tasmāt kṛsandhyāṃśakaṃ vinā \|*  
*tridvyekasāhastramato vinā sandhyāṃśakena tu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tretādvāparatiṣyāṇāṃ kālajñāne prakīrtitam \|*  
*etad dvādaśasāhastraṃ sādhikaṃ parikalpitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Leaving the part of sandhya of Satyayuga out of them, the period of the rest of the sandhyas extends to six hundred years. Without the part of Sandhya, two, and a thousand years for Treta, have been cowered into the time span of Dvapara and Kali.

## \|\| 1.5.14 \|\|

*tadekasaptatiguṇaṃ manorantaramucyate \|*  
*brahmaṇo divase viprā manavaḥ syuścaturdaśa \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Seven times that number (or seventy one divine yogas) make a Manvantara. О Brahmanas, day of Brahma comprises of fourteen Manvantaras.

## \|\| 1.5.15-17 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvādayaḥ sarve tataḥ sāvarṇikādayaḥ \|*  
*tairiyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā saparvatā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pūrṇaṃ yugasahastraṃ vai paripālyā nareśvaraiḥ \|*  
*manvantareṇa caikena sarvāṇyevāntarāṇi vai \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vyākhyātāni na saṃdehaḥ kalpaṃ kalpena caiva hi \|*  
*brāhmamekamahaḥ kalpastāvatī rātririṣyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Svayambhuva and all other Manus, thereafter the kings like Savamika and others rule the earth with seven dvipas, seven mountains, for a thousand yugas. In each Manvantara, the kalpas are described. There is no doubt about it. A single day of Brahma comprises of a kalpa. The night is of the same duration.

## \|\| 1.5.18-19 \|\|

*caturyugasahastraṃ tu kalpamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*trīṇi kalpaśatāni syuḥ tathā ṣaṣṭirdvijottamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*brahmaṇaḥ kathitaṃ varṣaṃ parākhyaṃ tacchataṃ viduḥ \|*  
*tasyānte sarvatattvānāṃ svahetau prakṛtau layaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The learned person, have conceived the duration of the kalpas as equivalent to a thousand Caturyugas. О Brahmanas, in this way, three hundred and sixty kalpas are completed. After this the people well-versed with the calculation of time have considered it to be one year of Brahma. The same span when multiplied by hundred times, is called Parardha.

## \|\| 1.5.20 \|\|

*tasyānte sarvasattvānāṃ sahetau prakṛtau layaḥ \|*  
*tenāyaṃ procyate sadbhiḥ prākṛtaḥ pratisaṃcaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Ultimately the entire universe is absorbed into Prakrti, which is the cause of the creation of all the living beings. Because of this, the noble people, call it as reabsoption into Prakrti (Prakrta-Pratisahcara).

## \|\| 1.5.21 \|\|

*brahmanārāyaṇeśānāṃ trayāṇāṃ prakṛtau layaḥ \|*  
*procyate kālayogena punareva ca saṃbhavaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Brahma, Narayana and Mahesa, all the three combined get absorbed in Prakrti and in due course of time they re-emerge on earth.

## \|\| 1.5.22 \|\|

*evaṃ brahmā ca bhūtāni vāsudevo 'pi śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*kālenaiva tu sṛjyante sa eva grasate punaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In this way, Brahma, all the living beings, Vasudeva besides Sankara, because of the movement of times, meet with their end on earth.

## \|\| 1.5.23 \|\|

*anādireṣa bhagavān kālo 'nanto 'jaro 'maraḥ \|*  
*sarvagatvāt svatantratvāt sarvātmāsau maheśvaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The same lord is called Mahes'vara, because of his having no beginning, form of Kaia, endless and imperishable.

## \|\| 1.5.24 \|\|

*brahmāṇo bahavo rudrā hyanye nārāyaṇādayaḥ \|*  
*eko hi bhagavānīśaḥ kālaḥ kaviriti śruti \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. There are innumerable Brahmas, Rudras, and Narayanas. Only Omniscient form of Kala, and lord Ishvara is one. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.5.25 \|\|

*ekamatra vyatītaṃ tu parārdhaṃ brahmaṇo dvijāḥ \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ vartate tadvat tasya kalpo 'yamaṣṭamaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О Brahmanas, a Parardha of Brahma has already lapsed and the second Parardha is passing presently and happens to be his earlier

## \|\| 1.5.26 \|\|

*yo 'tītaḥ saptamaḥ kalpaḥ pādma ityucyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*vārāho vartate kalpaḥ tasya vakṣyāmi vistaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The fcz/pa which has already lapsed has been known as the Padma-kalpa. Presently Varaha- kalpa is passing and I shall speak about it in detail.

## Chapter 6. Recovery of Earth from Water

## \|\| 1.6.1 \|\|

*śrīkūrma uvāca*  
*āsīdekārṇavaṃ ghoramavibhāgaṃ tamomayam \|*  
*śāntavātādikaṃ sarvaṃ na prajñāyata kiñcana \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Lord Kurma said, “Initially there was a vast sheet of waters, a terrible ocean full of darkness, which was undivided and undisturbed by the wind. Nothing could be visible.

## \|\| 1.6.2 \|\|

*ekārṇave tadā tasmin naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame \|*  
*tadā samabhavad brahmā sahastrākṣaḥ sahastrapāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. With the destruction of all the moveables and immoveables, Brahma emerged with a thousand eyes and a thousand feet.

## \|\| 1.6.3 \|\|

*sahastraśīrṣā puruṣo rukmavarṇastvatīndriyaḥ \|*  
*brahmā nārāyaṇākhyastu suṣvāpa salile tadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The same Purusa-Narayana, who had a thousand heads, having complexion of gold, went to sleep in the ocean.

## \|\| 1.6.4 \|\|

*imaṃ codāharantyatra ślokaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prati \|*  
*brahmasvarūpiṇaṃ devaṃ jagataḥ prabhavāpyayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. This verse speaks about Narayana, who is the form of Brahman, creator of the universe, and indestructible.

## \|\| 1.6.5 \|\|

*āpo nārā iti proktā nāmnā pūrvamiti śrutiḥ \|*  
*ayanaṃ tasya tā yasmāt tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Waters are known by the name oiNard, since the waters are bom of Nara (the cosmic man), and since the waterr constitute his abode, he is known as Narayana.

## \|\| 1.6.6-7 \|\|

*tulyaṃ yugasahastrasya naiśaṃ kālamupāsya saḥ \|*  
*śarvaryante prakurute brahmatvaṃ sargakāraṇāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tatastu salile tasmin vijñāyāntargatāṃ mahīm \|*  
*anumānāt taduddhāraṃ kartukāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. He enjoyed the sleep for a thousand yugas and at the end of the night, He assumed the function of Brahma for the purpose of creation. Thereafter the earth was lodged at the bed of the ocean. Thus anticipating, Prajapati desired to rescue the same.

## \|\| 1.6.8 \|\|

*jalakrīḍāsu ruciraṃ vārāhaṃ rupamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*adhṛṣyaṃ manasāpyanyairvāṅmayaṃ brahmasaṃjñitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then the lord took to the form of a boar which was interested in the water sports, which was undefeated by others. Because of its being the form of speech he was equated with Brahman.

## \|\| 1.6.9 \|\|

*pṛthivyuddharaṇārthāya praviśya ca rasātalam \|*  
*daṃṣṭrayābhyujjahāraināmātmādhāro dharādharaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. For the redemption of the earth, he entered the nether-world. The Atmddhara (selfsupporter) or Dharadhara (carrier of the earth) god Varaha lifted up the earth, with his sharp tusk.

## \|\| 1.6.10 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā daṃṣṭrāgravinyastāṃ pṛthivīṃ prathitapauruṣam \|*  
*astuvañjanalokasthāḥ siddhā brahmarṣayo harim \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Finding the earth lodged over the tip of the tusk of Varaha, all the Siddhas, and BrahmaRishis, stationed in the Janaloka started praising Hari.

## \|\| 1.6.11 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*namaste devadevāya brahmaṇe parameṣṭhine \|*  
*puruṣāya purāṇāya śāśvatāya jayāya ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The sages said, “Salutation to the lord of gods, the form of Brahman, Paramesthin, Purana-purusa, eternal one, and to the form of victory.

## \|\| 1.6.12 \|\|

*namaḥ svayaṃbhuve tubhyaṃ straṣṭre sarvārthavedine \|*  
*namo hiraṇyagarbhāya vedhase paramātmane \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. You are self-bom, creator of the universe, well-versed in all the knowledge, salutation to you, О Hiranyagarbha, О Brahma, Visnu and Shiva, besides being the supreme soul, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.6.13 \|\|

*namaste vāsudevāya viṣṇave viśvayonaye \|*  
*nārāyaṇāya devāya devānāṃ hitakāriṇe \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Obeisance to Lord Vasudeva, to Visnu, to the creator of universe, to the lord Naiayana, bestower of welfare on the gods, form of the gods, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.6.14 \|\|

*namo 'stu te caturvaktre śārṅgacakrāsidhāriṇe \|*  
*sarvabhūtātmabhūtāya kūṭasthāya namo namaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О four-faced one, holder of Sarriga bow, cakra and sword, salutation to you. You are the fonn of soul for all the bhtitas the unchanging, one, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.6.15 \|\|

*namo vedarahasyāya namaste vedayonaye \|*  
*namo buddhāya śuddhāya namaste jñānarūpiṇe \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Salutation to the secret of the Vedas. Salutation to origin of the Vedas, salutation to the one possessing all the wisdom and being the spotless one and the form of knowledge.

## \|\| 1.6.16 \|\|

*namo 'stvānandarūpāya sākṣiṇe jagatāṃ namaḥ \|*  
*anantāyāprameyāya kāryāya karaṇāya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Salutation to the blissful one and the witness of the universe. Salutation to the one, who is beyond measure, the limitless one, and the form of cause and the task.

## \|\| 1.6.17 \|\|

*namaste pañcabūtāya pañcabhūtātmane namaḥ \|*  
*namo mūlaprakṛtaye māyārūpāya te namaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Salutation to the one, having the form of five elements. Salutation to soul of the five elements, and the one, having the form of Mulaprakrti (Primordial nature) and Maya.

## \|\| 1.6.18 \|\|

*namo 'stu te varāhāya namaste matsyarūpiṇe \|*  
*namo yogādhigamyāya namaḥ sakarṣaṇāya te \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Salutation to the one, who has taken to the form of Varaha. Salutation to the one who could be known by the yogic practices, salutation to Samkarsana.

## \|\| 1.6.19 \|\|

*namastrimūrtaye tubhyaṃ tridhāmne divyatejase \|*  
*namaḥ siddhāya pūjyāya guṇatrayavibhāvine \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Salutation to TrimDrti, Salutation to Tridhama (having three abodes), one of divine lustre, the Siddha, adorable one and the one who divides the gunas into three.

## \|\| 1.6.20 \|\|

*tamo 'stvādityavarṇāya namaste padmayonaye \|*  
*namo 'mūrtāya mūrtāya mādhavāya namo namaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Salutation to the form of Aditya. Salutation to the form of lotus-bom one, and the one who is formless, to the embodied one and Madhava (the consort of Lakshmi).

## \|\| 1.6.21 \|\|

*tvayaiva sṛṣṭamakhilaṃ tvayyeva layameṣyati \|*  
*pālayaitajjagat sarvaṃ trātā tvaṃ śaraṇaṃ gati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. It is you who has created the eternal universe. The entire universe is lodged in you. You are the preserver of the universe. You are the protector as well as the refuge of all.

## \|\| 1.6.22 \|\|

*itthaṃ sa bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sanakādyairabhiṣṭutaḥ \|*  
*prasādamakarot teṣāṃ varāhavapurīśvaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When so eulogised by the sages like Sanaka and others, lord Visnu, who had taken to the form of Varaha, was pleased.

## \|\| 1.6.23 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃsthānamānīya pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*mumoca rūpaṃ manasā dhārayitvā prijāpatiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The Varaha- the lord of the earth, established her at the proper place. Thereafter lord Dharadhara (supporter of the earth) discarded the form of boar.

## \|\| 1.6.24 \|\|

*tasyopari jalaughasya mahatī nauriva sthitā \|*  
*vitatatvācca dehasya na mahī yāti saṃplavam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the earth was lodged over the oceanic waters like a boat. Because of the vastness of her body, the earth could not drown in water.

## \|\| 1.6.25 \|\|

*pṛthivīṃ tu samīkṛtya pṛthivyāṃ so 'cinod girīn \|*  
*prāksargadagdhānakhilāṃstataḥ sarge 'dadhanmanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The lord made the earth plain, re-established all the mountains which had been burnt earlier. Thereafter he thought of re-creation.

## Chapter 7. Description of Sarga or Creation

## \|\| 1.7.1 \|\|

*śrīkūrma uvāca*  
*sṛṣṭiṃ cintayatastasya kalpādiṣu yathā purā \|*  
*abuddhipūrvakaḥ sargaḥ prādurbhūtastamomayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Lord Kurma said, “Whom the Prajapati, as before, conceived of starting the creation, then there emerged the dark creation which was devoid of wisdom.

## \|\| 1.7.2 \|\|

*tamo moho mahāmohastāmistraścāndhasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*avidyā pañcaparvaiṣā prādurbhūtā mahātmanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It was covered with five sheaths of Tama (darkness), Moha (delusion), Mahamoha (great delusion), Andhatamisra (blinding darkness) and the fifth one among them was Avidya. All came out of the great-souled Prajapati.

## \|\| 1.7.3 \|\|

*pañcadhāvasthitaḥ sargo dhyāyataḥ so 'bhimāninaḥ \|*  
*saṃvṛtastamasā caiva bījakambhuvanāvṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Thus the sarga remained five-fold, even he was meditating and identified himself with it. It was covered with darkness like the seed in the well.

## \|\| 1.7.4 \|\|

*varhirantaścāprakāśaḥ stabdho niḥ saṃjña eva ca \|*  
*mukyā nagā iti proktā mukhyasargastu sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The said sarga was devoid of light inside and outside, besides being surprised and lonely. Its prominent mountains were treated as the creation.

## \|\| 1.7.5 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvāsādhakaṃ sargamamanyadaparaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*tasyābhidhyāyataḥ sargastiryakstroto 'bhyavartata \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The lord, then thinking such a creation to be incomplete, thought of resorting to some other creation, which influenced the tiryak source.

## \|\| 1.7.6 \|\|

*yasmāt tiryak pravṛttaḥ sa tiryakstrotastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*paśvādayaste vikhyātā utpathagrāhiṇo dvijāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Since it was influenced in a slanting way, therefore, it was known as tiryak-srotas. О Brahmanas, therefore, they come to be known as beasts etc. which followed the unstraight path.

## \|\| 1.7.7 \|\|

*tamapyasādhakaṃ jñātvā sargamanyaṃ sasarja ha \|*  
*ūrdhvastrota iti prokto devasargastu sāttvikaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Finding it also to be of no use, he resorted to another creation, which was the sattvik creation of the gods and was called as Urdhvasrotas.

## \|\| 1.7.8 \|\|

*te sukhapratibahulā bahirantaśca nāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*prakāśā bahirantaśca svabhāvād devasaṃjñitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All of them were more comfortable and loveable. They were uncovered and had the same light inside and outside. They came to be known as Devas.

## \|\| 1.7.9 \|\|

*tato 'bidhāyāyatastasya satyābhidhyāyinastadā \|*  
*prādurāsīt tadāvyaktādarvākstrotastu sādhakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thereafter thinking over the truth, they started meditating at the same time. Then from the unmenifest appeared as Arvak-srotas creation, compitent of performing his purpose.

## \|\| 1.7.10 \|\|

*tatra prakāśabahulāstamodriktā rajodhikāḥ \|*  
*duḥ khotkaṭāḥ sattvayutā manuṣyāḥ parikīrtitā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. They came to be known as the human beings. Those are possessing enough of light of knowledge, having the quality of Sattva, defiled and aflicted with Tamas and dominated with Rajas. t cjgT iarurt

## \|\| 1.7.11-12 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā cāparaṃ sargamamanyad bhagavānajaḥ \|*  
*tasyābhidhyāyataḥ sargaṃ sargo bhūtādiko 'bhavat \|\| 11 \|\|*

*te 'parigrāhiṇaḥ sarve saṃvibhāgaratāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*khādanāścāpyaśīlāśca bhūtādyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Observing that creation, lord Aja (the unborn Brahma), thought of another-creation. While so doing, the creation of the bhutadika was formed. They were filled with detachment, desirous of good as per their own wishes, desirous of eating and were deprived of the qualities of gentleness and other noble qualities.

## \|\| 1.7.13 \|\|

*ityete pañca kathitāḥ sargā vai dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*prathamo mahataḥ sargo vijñeyo brahmaṇastu saḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О Brahmanas, thus five Sargas have been explained here. Out of them, Mahat is to be known the first creation of Brahma.

## \|\| 1.7.14 \|\|

*tanmātrāṇāṃ dvitīyastu bhūtasargo hi sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*vaikārikastṛtīyastu sarga aindriyakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. There is the second creation of the subtle elements, which is called BhUtasarga. The third is the Vaikarika creation known as Aindriyaka (produced from sense organ).

## \|\| 1.7.15 \|\|

*ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargaḥ saṃbhūto 'buddhipūrvakaḥ \|*  
*mukhyasargaścaturthastu mukhyā vai sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

Then he created humans, Kinnaras, Rakshasas, birds, animals, deer and serpents and other eternal and temporary creation, both the moveable or immovable.
