*tatāpa sumahad ghoraṃ taporāśistapaḥ param \|*  
*prapannā viṣṇumavyaktaṃ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ harim \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Indra with all the gods, fought a great battle with him. Indra on the other hand having been defeated at the hands of Bali, took refuge with lord Visnu.

## \|\| 1.17.16 \|\|

*kṛtvā hṛtpadmakiñjalke niṣkalaṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*vāsudevamanādyantamānandaṃ vyoma kevalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the meantime, due to the defeat of Indra, Aditi, ’the mother of gods feeling extremely painful, performed great penance with the desire of getting a son, who could defeat the lord of the Daityas. For this purpose, she took refuge with lord Visnu.

## \|\| 1.17.17 \|\|

*prasanno bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ \|*  
*āvirbabhūva yogātmā devamātuḥ puro hariḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. She witnessed in her lotus like heart, Visnu in his unchangeable form, who was beyond the beginning or end, blissful, resembling the sky and unparalleled one known as Vasudeva.

## \|\| 1.17.18 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ viṣṇumaditirbhaktisaṃyutā \|*  
*mene kṛtārthamātmānaṃ toṣayāmāsa keśavam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Hl Then lord Visnu, the holder of conch, discus and mace, the Yogic soul, appeared before her in a delightful form.

## \|\| 1.17.19 \|\|

*jayāśeṣaduḥ khaughanāśaikaheto*  
*jayānantamāhātmyayogābhiyukta \|*  
*jayānādimadhyāntavijñānamūrte*  
*jayāśeṣakalpāmalānandarūpa \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Finding the arrival of lord Visnu, with her mind filled with devotion, Aditi thought her to be successful. Then she offered prayer to lord Kesava.

## \|\| 1.17.20 \|\|

*namo viṣṇave kālarūpāya tubhyaṃ*  
*namo nārasiṃhāya śeṣāya tubhyam \|*  
*namaḥ kālarudrāya saṃhārakartre*  
*namo vāsudevāya tubhyaṃ namaste \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Aditi said, “О Lord you are the cause of destruction of all miseries, hail to you. You are enormously glorious, lord of the yogic practices, victory to you. You are beyond beginning, middle and the end. О Form of Vijhana, victory to you. О Lord resembling the sky, О Blissful one, victory to you.

## \|\| 1.17.21 \|\|

*namo viśvamāyāvidhānāya tubhyaṃ*  
*namo yogagamyāya satyāya tubhyam \|*  
*namo dharmavijñānaniṣṭhāya tubhyaṃ*  
*namaste varāhāya bhūyo namaste \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О Visnu, О Form of Kala, salutation to you. Salutations to you the Man-lion. Bow to you, to Sesa. Salutations to you being Kalarudra and the destroyer. Salutation to you, О Vasudeva.

## \|\| 1.17.22 \|\|

*namaste sahastrārkacandrābhamūrte*  
*namo vedavijñānadharmābhigamya \|*  
*namo devadevādidevādideva*  
*prabho viśvayone 'tha bhūyo namaste \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О the producer of the Maya of the universe, salutation to you. Salutation to the one who could be achieved by means of Yoga and is the form of truth. Salutation to you having faith in dharma. Salutation to you in the form of Varaha, again and again.

## \|\| 1.17.23 \|\|

*namaḥ śaṃbhave satyaniṣṭhāya tubhyaṃ*  
*namo hetave viśvarūpāya tubhyam \|*  
*namo yogapīṭhāntarasthāya tubhyaṃ*  
*śivāyaikarūpāya bhūyo namaste \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О God, having resplendence comparable to thousands of suns and the moons, salutation to you again and again. You can be known by means of the Vedas, Vijndna and dharma, salutation to you. You are the upholder of the earth and beyond change, salutation to you. You are the source of the origin of the universe, salutation to you again and again.

## \|\| 1.17.24 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bhagavān kṛṣṇo devamātrā jaganmayaḥ \|*

24\. Salutation to truthful Sambhu. You are the cause of the world as well as the form of the universe, salutation to you. You are lodged in the yogapltha (middle of Yogic seat), salutation to you. You have an unique and auspicious form, salutations to you again and again.”

## \|\| 1.17.25 \|\|

*praṇamya śirasā bhūmau sā vabre varamuttamam \|*

25\. When so eulogised by the mother of the gods, Lord Visnu, the form of the universe, smilingly said to her, You ask for a boon.

## \|\| 1.17.26 \|\|

*tathāstvityāha bhagavān prapannajanavatsalaḥ \|*  
*dattvā varānaprameyastatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. At this, the lord who is benevolent on those who take refuge in him, said, “Be it so.” Thus bestowing a boon on her, he disappeared from the scene.

## \|\| 1.17.27 \|\|

*tato bahutithe kāle bhagavantaṃ janārdanam \|*

## \|\| 1.17.28 \|\|

*samāviṣṭe hṛṣīkeśe devamāturathodaram \|*

28\. When lord Hrslkesa entered the womb of the mother of the goddess, great disturbances were created in the city of Bali, the son of Virocana.

## \|\| 1.17.29 \|\|

*nirīkṣya sarvānutpātān daityendro bhayavihvalaḥ \|*

29\. Observing these evil portents, the panicky king of the Daityas spoke to his old grandfather Prahlada.

## \|\| 1.17.30 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*pitāmaha mahāprājña jāyante 'smatpure 'dhunā \|*  
*kimutpātā bhavet kāryamasmākaṃ kiṃnimittakāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Bali said, “O Grand sire, why are these disturbances being created in our city? What should be done by us?”

## \|\| 1.17.31 \|\|

*niśamya tasya vacanaṃ ciraṃ dhyātvā mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya hṛṣīkeśamidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Listening to the words of Bali, Prahlada-the great asura thought for a long time and bowing in reverence to lord Hrslkesa, spoke to Bali.

## \|\| 1.17.32 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca*  
*yo yajñairijyate viṣṇuryasya sarvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*dadhārāsuranāśārthaṃ mātā taṃ tridivaukasām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Prahlada said, “Lord Visnu, who is adored in the world by performing of the yajnas and who controls the entire universe, has entered the womb of the mother of the gods, for the destruction of the Daityas. The one who is separate from all, and from whom all are separated, the same Vasudeva has entered the womb of the mother of the gods.

## \|\| 1.17.33 \|\|

*yasmādabhinnaṃ sakalaṃ bhidyate yo 'khilādapi \|*  
*sa vāsudevo devānāṃ māturdehaṃ samāviśat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The one about whose form even the gods are not aware, the same lord Visnu, of his own accord has entered the womb of the mother of the gods, Aditi.

## \|\| 1.17.34 \|\|

*na yasya devā jānanti svarūpaṃ paramārthataḥ \|*  
*sa viṣṇuraditerdehaṃ svecchayādya samāviśat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The one from whom all the living beings emerge, and also get absorbed, the same MahayogI, Hari, the Parana Purusa has incarnated on earth.

## \|\| 1.17.35 \|\|

*yasmād bhavanti bhūtāni yatra saṃyānti saṃkṣayam \|*  
*so 'vatīrṇo mahāyogī purāṇapuruṣo hariḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The one whose name and caste can not be conceived, and who is of the mere form of existence, is being bom with a portion of himself.

## \|\| 1.17.36 \|\|

*na yatra vidyate nāmajātyādiparikalpanā \|*  
*sattāmātrātmarūpo 'sau viṣṇuraṃśena jāyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The goddess Lakshmi happens to be his Мйуа or his Shakti, the same Janardana has incarnated into the womb of Aditi, the mother of the gods.

## \|\| 1.17.37 \|\|

*yasya sā jagatāṃ mātā śaktistaddharmadhāriṇī \|*  
*māyā bhagavatī lakṣmīḥ so 'vatīrṇo janārdanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The one whose tamasic form is Shiva, and Rajasic form is Brahma, the same Visnu, having the form of Sattvaguna, incarnates in an ams'a.

## \|\| 1.17.38 \|\|

*yasya sā tāmasī mūrtiḥ śaṅkaro rājasī tanuḥ \|*  
*brahmā saṃjāyate viṣṇuraṃśenaikena sattvabhṛt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus thinking, feeling humble with devotion, you go and take refuge with the same Govinda and by so doing you will achieve eternal bliss.

## \|\| 1.17.39 \|\|

*itthaṃ vicintya govindaṃ bhaktinamreṇa cetasā \|*  
*tameva gaccha śaraṇaṃ tato yāsyasi nirvṛtim \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then listening to the words of Prahlada, Bali, the son of Virocana, went and took refuge with Hari. Thereafter, he kept on ruling the country with a righteous mind.

## \|\| 1.17.40 \|\|

*tataḥ prahlādavacanād balirvairocanirharim \|*  
*jagāma śaraṇaṃ viśvaṃ pālayāmāsa dharmataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In due course of time, Aditi the mother of the gods herself produced lord Visnu as son, in union with Kasyapa.

## \|\| 1.17.41 \|\|

*kāle prāpte mahāviṣṇuṃ devānāṃ harṣavardhanam \|*  
*asūta kaśyapāccainaṃ devamātāditiḥ svayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The lord was four armed, with vast eyes, and his chest was studded with Srivatsa mark. He was illumining like the blue clouds. He looked graceful with his own lustre.

## \|\| 1.17.42 \|\|

*caturbhujaṃ viśālākṣaṃ śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam \|*  
*nīlameghapratīkāśaṃ bhrājamānaṃ śriyāvṛtam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He happened to be the younger brother of Visnu, thus realising, all the Gods, Siddhas,

## \|\| 1.17.43 \|\|

*upatasthuḥ surāḥ sarve siddhāḥ sādhyāśca cāraṇāḥ \|*  
*upendramindrapramukhā brahmā carṣigamairvṛtaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Sadhyas and the Ca.ran.as, besides the Its is, started adoring him, with Brahma.

## \|\| 1.17.44 \|\|

*kṛtopanayano vedānadhyaiṣṭa bhagavān hariḥ \|*  
*samācāraṃ bharadvājāt trilokāya pradarśayan \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Lord Hari, whose investiture with the sacred thread was performed, studied the Vedas and the code of good conduct from sage Bharadvaja holding it as a model for the people in the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.17.45 \|\|

*evaṃ hi laukikaṃ mārgaṃ pradarśayati sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*sa yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus the lord displayed the human traditions. Because, whatever is done by an eminent person, his actions are followed by the people as an authority.

## \|\| 1.17.47 \|\|

*brāhmaṇān pūjayāmāsa dattvā bahutaraṃ dhanam \|*  
*brahmarṣayaḥ samājagmuryajñavāṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After sometime, Daitya king Bali,1 the son of Virocana, himself organized yajnas in favour of Visnu, the all-pervading Lord of Yajnas.

## \|\| 1.17.48 \|\|

*vijñāya viṣṇurbhagavān bharadvājapracoditaḥ \|*  
*āsthāya vāmanaṃ rūpaṃ yajñadeśamathāgamat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In these yajnas, he distributed enough of wealth to the Brahmanas, welcoming them. Several of the BrahmaRishis participated in the yajnas.

## \|\| 1.17.49 \|\|

*kṛṣṇājinopavītāṅga āṣāḍhena virājitaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇo jaṭilo vedānudgiran bhasmamaṇḍitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Learning about this and having been inspired by the sage Bharadvaja, lord Visnu taking to the form of a dwarf reached the place of yajna.

## \|\| 1.17.50 \|\|

*saṃprāpyāsurarājasya samīpaṃ bhikṣuko hariḥ \|*  
*svapādairvimitaṃ deśamayācata baliṃ tribhiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He had worn the skin of a black antelope and the sacred thread and hold a staff of the Palas'a wood. He was in the form of a Brahmana with matted locks of hair over the head. He was quite resplendent to look at and was reciting the Vedic hymns.

## \|\| 1.17.51 \|\|

*prakṣālya caraṇau viṣṇorbalirbhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*ācāmayitvā bhṛṅgāramādāya svarṇanirmitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thus lord Hari, in the form of Bhiksu arrived at the place of Bali and begged for space traversed by three steps of his own feet.

## \|\| 1.17.52 \|\|

*dāsye tavedaṃ bhavate padatrayaṃ*  
*prīṇātu devo hariravyayākṛtiḥ \|*  
*vicintya devasya karāgrapallave*  
*nipātayāmāsa jalaṃ suśītalam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The king Bali, getting emotional, carrying a golden vase filled with water, washed the feet of lord Visnu and sipped the water with which the feet of the lord were washed.

## \|\| 1.17.53 \|\|

*vicakrame pṛthivīmeṣa etā-*  
*mathāntarikṣaṃ divamādidevaḥ \|*  
*vyapetarāgaṃ ditijeśvaraṃ taṃ*  
*prakartukāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ prapannam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then Bali said, “I shall give you three feet length of earth. Let lord Hari, the eternal one, be pleased with me.” Thus contemplating, Bali poured the cool water on the sprout-like hands of Lord Hari.

## \|\| 1.17.54 \|\|

*ākramya lokatrayamīśapādaḥ*  
*prājāpatyād brahmalokaṃ jagāma \|*  
*praṇemurādityasahastrakalpaṃ*  
*ye tatra loke nivasanti siddhāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The Lord of Daityas had sought refuge in him. Thereafter desirous of making him free from covetousness and other passions, Vamana the eternal lord, expanded himself to the earth, the sky as well as the space.

## \|\| 1.17.55 \|\|

*athopatasthe bhagavānanādiḥ*  
*pitāmahāstoṣayāmāsa viṣṇum \|*  
*bhittvā tadaṇḍasya kapālamūrdhvaṃ*  
*jagāma divyāvaraṇāni bhūyaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The foot of the lord, covered all the three lokas and crossing through the loka of Prajapati, reached Brahmaloka and he was adored by Adityas, the Siddhas and other gods there.

## \|\| 1.17.56 \|\|

*athāṇḍabhedānnipapāta śītalaṃ*  
*mahājalaṃ tat puṇyakṛdbhiścajuṣṭam \|*  
*pravartate cāpi saridvarā tadā*  
*gaṅgetyuktā brahmaṇā vyomasaṃsthā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The eternal lord, the beginningless grandsire of the world, offered worship to him and propitiated him. Then Visnu, clad in divine garments, breaking through the upper crest of the Cosmic egg, rose to further heights.

## \|\| 1.17.57 \|\|

*gatvā mahāntaṃ prakṛtiṃ pradhānaṃ*  
*brahmāṇamekaṃ puruṣaṃ svabījam \|*  
*atiṣṭhadīśasya padaṃ tadavyayaṃ*  
*dṛṣṭvā devāstatra tatra stuvanti \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. With the piercing through of the globe, a lot of water started falling, which was converted into the form of an excellent river which was tenned by god Brahma as Ganga stationed in the sky way.

## \|\| 1.17.58 \|\|

*ālokya taṃ puruṣaṃ viśvakāyaṃ*  
*mahān balirbhaktiyogena viṣṇum \|*  
*nanāma nārāyaṇamekamavyayaṃ*  
*svacetasā yaṃ praṇamanti devāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After reaching the great Prakrti, Pradhana, the source of Brahman and then the sole Purusa, the origin of the universe, he stabilised his foot at the unchanging region of the Isa. The gods dwelling in these places started praising the imperishable foot of the lord.

## \|\| 1.17.59 \|\|

*tamabravīd bhagavānādikartā*  
*bhūtvā punarvāmano vāsudevaḥ \|*  
*mamaiva daityādhipate 'dhunedaṃ*  
*lokatrayaṃ bhavatā bhāvadattam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Finding the lord with the gigantic body, the great king Bali, having been filled with devotion, bowed in reverence to everlasting Visnu, who is revered even by the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.17.60 \|\|

*praṇamya mūrdhnā punareva daityo*  
*nipātayāmāsa jalaṃ karāgre \|*  
*dāsye tavātmānamanantadhāmne*  
*trivikramāyāmitavikramāya \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then the eternal lord Vasudeva, again took to the form of Vamana and said to Bali, “O Daitya king, you have presented all the three lokas to' me just now.”

## \|\| 1.17.61 \|\|

*pragṛhya sūnorapi saṃpradattaṃ*  
*prahlādasūnoratha śaṅkhapāṇiḥ \|*  
*jagāda daityaṃ jagadantarātmā*  
*pātālamūlaṃ praviśeti bhūyaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then the Daitya king, again bowed in reverence to lord Visnu, poured the water at the tip of the hand of Vamana and said, “O Trivikrama, О Valorous one, Immensely illustrious one, I shall offer myself unto you.

## \|\| 1.17.62 \|\|

*samāsyatāṃ bhavatā tatra nityaṃ*  
*bhuktvā bhogān devatānāmalabhyān \|*  
*dhyāyasva māṃ satataṃ bhaktiyogāt*  
*pravekṣyase kalpadāhe punarmām \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After accepting danci from the son of Prahlada, i.e., Bali, the lord who is the soul of the universe and is holder of the conch in his hand, again spoke to the Daitya, “Now you enter the nether world.”

## \|\| 1.17.63 \|\|

*uktvaivaṃ daityasiṃhaṃ taṃ viṣṇuḥ satyaparākramaḥ \|*  
*purandarāya trailokyaṃ dadau viṣṇururukramaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. You enjoying always the pleasures which are beyond the reach of even the gods, live there, devoting your mind to me. By so doing, you will get absorbed in me at the end of the kalpa.1 The truthful, victorious and immensely valorous Visnu, thus speaking to the lion-like Daitya king, gave the three worlds unto Indra.

## \|\| 1.17.64 \|\|

*saṃstuvanti mahāyogaṃ siddhā devarṣikinnarāḥ \|*  
*brahmā śakro 'tha bhagavān rudrādityamarudgaṇāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. At that point of time, lord Visnu was praised by Siddhas, divine Rishis, Kinnaras, Brahma, lord Indra, Rudra, Aditya and Maruts.

## \|\| 1.17.65-66 \|\|

*kṛtvaitadadbhutaṃ karma viṣṇurvāmanarūpadhṛk \|*  
*paśyatāmeva sarveṣāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 65 \|\|*

*so 'pi daityavaraḥ śrīmān pātālaṃ prāpa coditaḥ \|*  
*prahlādenāsuravarairviṣṇunā viṣṇutatparaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. After performing this unique and astonishing feat, Visnu in the form of Vamana, disappeared in full view of all. The fortunate Daitya also, at the instance of lord Hari and being urged by Prahlada and other Daityas, went to Patala with. Because of his being devoted to Visnu, he was obedient to him.

## \|\| 1.17.67 \|\|

*apṛcchad viṣṇumāhātmayaṃ bhaktiyogamanuttamam \|*  
*pūjāvidhānaṃ prahlādaṃ tadāhāsau cakāra saḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Thereafter, Bali, listened to the glory of lord Visnu from Prahlada, besides the excellent Bhaktiyoga and the method of worship. Then Bali did as per the advice of Prahlada.

## \|\| 1.17.68 \|\|

*atha rathacaraṇāsiśaṅkhapāṇiṃ*  
*sarasijolacanamīśamaprameyam \|*  
*śaraṇamupapayau sa bhāvayogāt*  
*praṇatagatiṃ praṇidhāya karmayogam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Then the king Bali with great emotional attachment, practicing karmayoga through bhavayoga, took refuge in lord Visnu, the holder of conch, having lotus-like eyes and beyond measure.

## \|\| 1.17.69 \|\|

*eṣa vaḥ kathito viprā vāmanasya parākramaḥ \|*  
*sa devakāryāṇi sadā karoti puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. О Brahmanas, I have narrated the entire story of Vamana to you. Lord Purusottama always performs the tasks of the gods.

## Chapter 18. Description of the race of Kasyapa

## \|\| 1.18.1 \|\|

*baleḥ putraśataṃ tvāsīnmahābalaparākramam \|*  
*teṣāṃ pradhāno dyutimān bāṇo nāma mahābalaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “The king Bali had a hundred sons who were immensely valorous. Bana happened to be the bravest and the chief among them.

## \|\| 1.18.2 \|\|

*so 'tīva śaṅkare bhakto rājā rājyamapālayat \|*  
*trailokyaṃ vaśamānīya bādhayāmāsa vāsavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The king Bana had been a great devotee of Shiva. He, conquering the three worlds, ruled the universe. He even troubled Indra.

## \|\| 1.18.3 \|\|

*tataḥ śakrādayo devā gatvocuḥ kṛttivāsasam \|*  
*tvadīyo bādhate hyasmān bāṇo nāma mahāsuraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then Indra and other gods went to Krttivasas (elephant-hide-robed Shiva) and said to him, “Bana, Your devotee is troubling us the most.”

## \|\| 1.18.4 \|\|

*vyāhṛto daivadaiḥ sarvairdevadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dadāha bāṇasya puraṃ śareṇaikena līlayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the prayer of all the gods, lord Mahesvara, shooting a single arrow burnt the city of Bana, quite playfully.

## \|\| 1.18.5-6 \|\|

*dahyamāne pure tasmin bāṇo rudraṃ triśūlinam \|*  
*yayau śaraṇamīśānaṃ gopatiṃ nīlalohitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mūrdhanyādhāya talliṅgaṃ śāṃbhavaṃ bhītavarjitaḥ \|*  
*nirgatya tu purāt tasmāt tuṣṭāva parameśvaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. While the city was burning, Bana took refuge with Shiva, the holder of a trident, lord of the Bull, Is'ana and having blue-red complexion known as Rudra. Placing Shivalinga over his head, becoming unattached, he left the city and started praying lord Shiva.

## \|\| 1.18.7 \|\|

*saṃstuto bhagavānīśaḥ śaṅkaro nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*gāṇapatyena bāṇaṃ taṃ yojayāmāsa bhāvataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Having been thus praised, the brown complexioned lord Shiva established him over the position of Ganapati.

## \|\| 1.18.8 \|\|

*athābhavan danoḥ putrāstārādyā hyatibhīṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*tārastathā śambaraśca kapilaḥ śaṅkarastathā \|*  
*svarbhānurvṛṣaparvā ca prādhānyena prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Danu has sons like Tara and others who were quite strong. They were terrific. Among them Tara, Sambara, Kapila, Sankara, Svarbhanu and Vrsaparva were the foremost.

## \|\| 1.18.9 \|\|

*surasāyāḥ sahastraṃ tu sarpāṇāmabhavad dvijāḥ \|*  
*anekaśirasāṃ tadvat khecarāṇāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О Brahmanas, a thousand serpents were bom of the womb of Surasa as well as thousands of noble-souled, multi-headed and heaven- wanderers.

## \|\| 1.18.10 \|\|

*ariṣṭā janayāmāsa gandharvāṇāṃ sahastrakam \|*  
*anantādyā mahānāgāḥ kādraveyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Arista gave birth to a thousand Gandharvas. Ananta and other great serpents having been bom of Kadrfl came to be known as Kadraveyas.

## \|\| 1.18.11 \|\|

*tāmrā ca janayāmāsa ṣaṭ kanyā dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*śukīṃ śyenīṃ ca bhāsīṃ ca sugrīvāṅgṛdhrikāṃ śucim \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О Best of the Brahmanas, Tamra gave birth to six daughters, namely, SukI, Syeni, BhasI, Sugriva, Granthika and Suci.

## \|\| 1.18.12 \|\|

*gāstathā janayāmāsa surabhirmahiṣīstathā \|*  
*irā vṛkṣalatāvallīstṛṇajātīśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The cows and buffaloes were bom of Surabhi. Ira gave birth to the trees, creepers, vines and all types of grasses.

## \|\| 1.18.13 \|\|

*khasā vai yakṣarakṣāṃsi munirapsarasastathā \|*  
*rakṣogaṇaṃ krodhavaśā janayāmāsa sattamāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О Excellent sages, Muni gave birth to the Yaksas, Raksasas and Apsaras. It was out of anger that she gave birth to the group of Raksasas.

## \|\| 1.18.14 \|\|

*vinatāyāśca putrau dvau prakhyātau garuḍāruṇau \|*  
*tayośca garuḍo dhīmān tapastaptvā suduścaram \|*  
*prasādācchūnilaḥ prāpto vāhanatvaṃ hareḥ svayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Vinata, the daughter of Daksa had his famous sons named Garuda and Aruna. The wise Garuda performed severe tapas and with the grace of Shiva, became the vehicle of lord Yisnu.

## \|\| 1.18.15 \|\|

*ārādhya tapasā rudraṃ mahdevaṃ tathāruṇaḥ \|*  
*sārathye kalpitaḥ pūrvaṃ prītenārkasya śaṃbhunā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Aruna also performed severe tapas for Mahadeva, who was pleased and by his grace, he became the charioteer of Sun-god.

## \|\| 1.18.16 \|\|

*ete kaśyapadāyādāḥ kīrtitāḥ sthāṇujaṅgamāḥ \|*  
*vaivasvate 'nte hyasmiñchṛṇvatāṃ pāpanāśanāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the Vaivasvata Manvantara, these mobile and immobile beings are the descendants of Kasyapa, which have been described to you. They remove the sins of the listeners.

## \|\| 1.18.17 \|\|

*saptaviṃśat sutāḥ proktāḥ somapatnyaśca suvratāḥ \|*  
*ariṣṭanemipatnīnāmapatyānīha ṣoḍaśa \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О man of holy vows, the twenty-seven daughters of Daksa, were married to the moon. The wives of Aristanemi, also gave birth to many sons and daughters.

## \|\| 1.18.18 \|\|

*bahuputrasya viduṣaścatastro vidyutaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*tadvadaṅgirasaḥ putrā ṛṣayo brahmasatkṛtāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The intelligent Bahuputra had four Devaganas known as Vidyuta. The excellent sages Angirasas became adorable due to their piety.

## \|\| 1.18.19 \|\|

*kuśāśvasya tu devarṣerdevapraharaṇāḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*ete yugasahastrānte jāyante punareva hi \|*  
*manvantareṣu niyataṃ tulyaiḥ kāryaiḥ svanāmabhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The sons of Devarsi Krsasva, became the attributes of the gods. All of them at the end of the thousands of yugas in the different Manvantaras, are bom again with similar achievements and with their respective designations.

## Chapter 19. Description of the dynasty of Rishis

## \|\| 1.19.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*etānutpādya putrāṃstu prajāsaṃtānakāraṇāt \|*  
*kaśyapo gotrakāmastu cacāra sumahat tapaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “With the desire of begetting more sons, for the increase in worldly population, Kasyapa performed great tapas for the continuity of progeny.

## \|\| 1.19.2 \|\|

*tasya vai tapato 'tyarthaṃ prādurbhūtau sutāvimau \|*  
*vatsaraścāsitaścaiva tāvubhau brahmavādinau \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. As a result of his performing so severe penances, he produced two sons named Vatsara and Asita. Both of them were well-versed in Brahman.

## \|\| 1.19.3 \|\|

*vatsarānnaidhruvo jajñe raibhyaśca sumahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*raibhyasya jajñire raibhyāḥ putrā dyutimatāṃ varāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Vatsara had a son named Naidhruva and Raibhya who were immensely glorious. Raibhya produced the sons known as Stidras who were the most excellent among the learned ones.

## \|\| 1.19.4 \|\|

*cyavanasya sutā patnī naidhruvasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*sumedhā janayāmāsa putrān vai kuṇḍapāyinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Mahatma Naidhruva’s wife was Sumedha, the daughter of the sage Cyavana, who gave birth to the sons known as Kundapayins.

## \|\| 1.19.5 \|\|

*asitasyaikaparṇāyāṃ brahmiṣṭhaḥ samapadyata \|*  
*nāmnā vai devalaḥ putro yogācāryo mahātapāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Asita produced a son who was well-versed in the Vedas, from his wife Ekaparna. He was know as Devala, who was a great preceptor of Yoga as well as performed great penance.

## \|\| 1.19.6 \|\|

*śāṇḍilyānāṃ paraḥ śrīmān sarvatattvārthavit sudhīḥ \|*  
*prasādāt pārvatīśasya yogamuttamamāptavān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The second son was known as Sandilya, who possessed enormous fortunes and was knower of the true principles. He, by the grace of Parvati, achieved the best of the yogic Siddhis.

## \|\| 1.19.7 \|\|

*śāṇḍilyā naidhru vāraibhyāstrayaḥ pakṣāstu kāśyapāḥ \|*  
*naraprakṛtayo viprāḥ pulastyasya vadāmi vaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Sandilya, Naidhruva and Raibhya, having human temperament, belonged to the race of Kasyapa. О Brahmanas, now I shall speak about the children of Pulastya.

## \|\| 1.19.8 \|\|

*tṛṇabindoḥ sutā viprā nāmnā tvilavilā smṛtā \|*  
*pulastyāya sa rājarṣistāṃ kanyāṃ pratyapādayat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О Brahmanas, Ailavila was the daughter of the sage Tmabindu, who was given over by the royal sage in marriage to the sage Pulastya.

## \|\| 1.19.9-10 \|\|

*ṛṣistvailavilistasyāṃ viśravāḥ samapadyata \|*  
*tasya patnyaścatastrastu paulastyakulavardhikāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*puṣpotkaṭā ca rākā ca kaikasī devavarṇinī \|*  
*rūpalāvaṇyasaṃpannāstāsāṃ vai śṛṇuta prajāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. From Ailavila, the sage known as Visravas was bom. He had four wives, who flourished the race of Pulastya. They were known by the names of Puspotkata, Vaka, KaikasI and Devavaminl, all of them possessed excellent beauty. You listen to their progeny.

## \|\| 1.19.11-13 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ tasya suṣuve devarūpiṇī \|*  
*kaikasī janayat putraṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kumbhakarṇaṃ śūrpaṇakhāṃ tathaiva ca vibhīṣaṇam \|*  
*puṣpotkaṭā vyajanayat putrān viśravasaḥ śubhān \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca mahāpārśvaṃ kharaṃ tathā \|*  
*kumbhīnasīṃ tathā kanyāṃ rākāyāṃ śṛṇuta prajāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Devavaminl gave birth to the eldest of the sons known as Vaisravana. KaikasI gave birth to Ravana, the lord of Raksasas. Thereafter, the son Kumbhakarna, Surpanakha, the daughter and Vibhlsana, another son were bom to her. Puspotkata on the other hand, gave birth to Mahodara, Prahasta, Mahaparsva and Khara, the sons, besides a daughter named Kumbhlnasi. Now you listen about the children of Vaka.

## \|\| 1.19.14 \|\|

*triśirā dūṣaṇaścaiva vidyujjihvo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*ityete krūrakarmāṇaḥ paulastyā rākṣasā daśa \|*  
*sarve tapobalotkṛṣṭā rudrabhaktāḥ subhīṣaṇāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. She gave birth to Trisiras, Dusana and Vidyujjihva of great strength. All of them were performers of the cmel deeds and came to be known as the ten Paulastya demons. All of them were endowed with the power of penance and physical strength. They were quite awful, and were immensely devoted to Rudra.

## \|\| 1.19.15 \|\|

*pulahasya mṛgāḥ putrāḥ sarve vyālāśca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ \|*  
*bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ sarpāśca śūkarā hastinastathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Pulaha’s sons were deer, all kind of serpents, fanged beasts, goblins, Pis'acas, bears, boars and the elephants.

## \|\| 1.19.16 \|\|

*anapatyaḥ kratustasmin smṛto vaivasvate 'ntare \|*  
*marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ putraḥ svayameva prajāpatiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the Vaivasvata Manvantara, Kratu was without progeny. Kasyapa who himself was Prajapati, was the son of Marichi.

## \|\| 1.19.17 \|\|

*bhṛgorapyabhavacchukro daityācāryo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*svādhyāyayoganirato harabhakto mahādyutiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. From Bhrgu, was bom Sukra, who became the preceptor of the demons. He engaged himself always in stutis and the yogic practices. Не was quite illustrious and was devoted to Shiva.

## \|\| 1.19.18 \|\|

*atreḥ patnyo 'bhavan bahvyaḥ sodaryāstāḥ pativratāḥ \|*  
*kṛśāśvasya tu viprendrā ghṛtācyāmiti me śrutam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Vahni was the son of Atri and Naidhruva was his uterine-brother. It is heard that some sons were bom of GhrtacI from the Brahmana sage Krs'asva.

## \|\| 1.19.19 \|\|

*sa tāsu janayāmāsa svastyātreyān mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*vedavedāṅganiratāṃstapasā hatakilbiṣān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The sons known as Svastyatreyas were included in them. All of them were fully devoted to the study of the Vedas and the post Vedic literature and destroyed their sins by performing tapas.

## \|\| 1.19.20 \|\|

*nāradastu vasiṣṭhāya dadau devīmarundhatīm \|*  
*ūrdhvaretāstatra muniḥ śāpād dakṣasya nāradaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Narada had given over Arundhati to Vasistha but at the same time, because of the curse of Daksa, he himself become a Brahmacarl.

## \|\| 1.19.21-22 \|\|

*haryaśveṣu tu naṣṭeṣu māyayā nāradasya tu \|*  
*śaśāpa nāradaṃ dakṣaḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yasmānmama sutāḥ sarve bhavato māyayā dvija \|*  
*kṣayaṃ nītāstvaśeṣeṇa nirapatyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. I This was due to the fact that when Haryasvas (the sons of Daksa) were lost due to the Maya of Narada, Daksa Prajapati, with eyes red shot with anger, pronounced a curse on Narada- “Since you have destroyed all my sons with your illusion, therefore you will never have any sons.”

## \|\| 1.19.23 \|\|

*arundhatyāṃ vasiṣṭhastu śaktimutpādayat sutam \|*  
*śakteḥ parāśaraḥ śrīmān sarvajñastapatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Vasistha on the other hand, produced a son named Shakti, from his wife Arundhati. Parasara, the best of the ascetics, who was omniscient was bom as a son to Shakti.

## \|\| 1.19.24 \|\|

*ārādhya devadeveśamīśānaṃ tripurāntakam \|*  
*lebhe tvapratimaṃ putraṃ kṛṣṇādvaipāyanaṃ prabhum \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Paras'ara, the great sage, adored the slayer of Tripuras, the Lord of the chief of Devas, Shiva and produced a great sage son named Lord Krisnadvaipayana.

## \|\| 1.19.25 \|\|

*dvaipāyanācchrako jajñe bhagavāneva śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*aṃśāṃśenāvatīryorvyāṃ svaṃ prāpa paramaṃ padam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Suka was bom of Dvaipayana, who resembled lord Shiva himself. He was bom out of the arhs'a of lord Shiva and then he attained his own great region.

## \|\| 1.19.26-28 \|\|

*śukasyāpyabhavan putrāḥ pañcātyantatapasvinaḥ \|*  
*bhūriśravāḥ prabhuḥ śaṃbhuḥ kṛṣṇo gauraśca pañcamaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kanyā kīrtimatī caiva yogamātā dhṛtavratā \|*  
*ete 'tra vaṃśyāḥ kathitā brāhmaṇā brahmavādinām \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ata ūrdhvaṃ nibodhadhvaṃ kaśyapādrājasaṃtatim \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Sukadeva, on the other hand, was immensely illustrious and produced five ascetic sons who came to be known by the names of Bhurisravas, Prabhu, Sambhu, Krisna and Gaura, besides three daughters known by the names of Klrtimatl, Yogamata and Dhrtavrata. These persons of the family of Atri, the expounders of Brahman, have been narrated by Brahma. Now you listen about the royal progeny from Kasyapa.

## Chapter 20. Description of Royal Dynasty

## \|\| 1.20.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*aditiḥ suṣuve putramādityaṃ kaśyapāt prabhum \|*  
*tasyādityasya caivasīd bhāryāṇāṃ tu catuṣṭayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*saṃjñā rājñī prabhā chāyā putrāṃstāsāṃ nibodhata \|*  
*saṃjñā tvāṣṭrī ca suṣuve sūryānmanumanuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said, “From Kasyapa, Aditi produced a powerful son named Aditya, who had four wives named Sarhjna, Rajfil, Prabha and Chaya. Listen to the names of their sons, Sarhjna, the daughter of Tvastr, produced from the Sun-god, Yama, Yamuna and Vaivasvata, the best of Manus.

## \|\| 1.20.3-4 \|\|

*yamaṃ ca yamunāṃ caiva rājñī raivatameva ca \|*  
*prabhā prabhātamādityācchāyā sāvarṇamātmajam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śaniṃ ca tapatīṃ caiva viṣṭiṃ caiva yathākramam \|*  
*manostu prathamasyāsan nava putrāstu saṃyamāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. While Prabha gave birth to Prabhata as son from Aditya. Chaya gave birth to sons Savarni, Sani, Tapatl and Viti in the same order. The first Manu had nine sons who were as valorous as their father.

## \|\| 1.20.5-6 \|\|

*ikṣvākurnabhagaścaiva dhṛṣṭaḥ śaryātireva ca \|*  
*nariṣyantaśca nābhāgo hyariṣṭaḥ kāruṣakastathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pṛṣadhraśca mahātejā navaite śakrasannibhāḥ \|*  
*ilā jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhā ca somavaṃśavivṛddhaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Their names were Iksvaku, Nabhaga, Dhrsta, Saryati, Narisyanta, Nabhaga, Arista, Karusa and illustrious Prsadhra. All these nine were glorious like Indra. Ila, the eldest and the most excellent, contributed to the growth of the race of the moon.

## \|\| 1.20.7 \|\|

*budhasya gatvā bhavanaṃ somaputreṇa saṃgatā \|*  
*asūta saumyajaṃ devī purūravasamuttamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Reaching the abode of Buddha, in union with the son of the moon, the goddess Ila, produced a son named Purflravas.

## \|\| 1.20.8-10 \|\|

*pitṝṇāṃ tṛptikartāraṃ budhāditi hi naḥ śrutam \|*  
*saṃprāpya puṃstvamamalaṃ sudyumna iti viśrutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ilā putratrayaṃ lebhe punaḥ strītvamavindata \|*  
*utkalaśca gayaścaiva vinatāśvastathaiva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sarve te 'pratimaprakhyāḥ prapannāḥ kamalodbhavam \|*  
*ikṣvākoścābhavad vīro vikukṣirnāma pārthivaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Pururavas, who had been bom of Budha, was the propitiator of the Pips. This has been heard by us. Ila, after getting spotless son, well-known as Sudyumna, again attained womanhood, and gave birth to three sons named- Utkala, Gaya and Vinata. All these sons were immensely intelligent and were devoted to Brahma. The valorous king Vikuksi was bom of Iksavaku.

## \|\| 1.20.11 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhaḥ putraśatasyāpi daśa pañca ca tatsutāḥ \|*  
*teṣāñjyeṣṭhaḥ kakutstho 'bhūt kākutstho hi suyodhanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He was the eldest son-of Iksavaku, who had fifteen other sons. Kakustha was the eldest of them. Suyodhana was the son of Kakustha.

## \|\| 1.20.12 \|\|

*suyodhanāt pṛthuḥ śrīmān viśvakaśca pṛthoḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*viśvakādārdrako dhīmān yuvanāśvastu tatsutaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The glorious Prthu was bom of Suyodhana. while Visvaka was Prthu’s son. The intelligent Ardraka was born from Visvaka, who had a son named Yuvanas'va.

## \|\| 1.20.13 \|\|

*sa gokarṇamanuprāpya yuvanāśvaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tu gautamaṃ vipraṃ tapantamanalaprabham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Once, the glorious Yuvanasva, desirous of begetting a son, went to Gokama-tlrtha, where he found the sage Gautama resembling the fire, performing the tapas.

## \|\| 1.20.14 \|\|

*praṇamya daṇḍavad bhūmau putrakāmo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*apṛcchat karmaṇā kena dhārmikaṃ prāpnuyāt sutam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. With the desire to have a son, king prostrated before the sage Gautama and then asked him, “By what means can I achieve a righteous- minded son?”

## \|\| 1.20.15 \|\|

*gautama uvāca*  
*ārādhya pūrvapuruṣaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam \|*  
*anādinidhanaṃ devaṃ dhārmikaṃ prāpnuyāt sutam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Gautama said, “By adoring the primordial person, lord Visnu, having no beginning, middle or end, you can achieve the religious-minded son.

## \|\| 1.20.16 \|\|

*yasya putraḥ svayaṃ brahmā pautraḥ syānnīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*tamādikṛṣṇamīśānamārādhyāpnoti satsutam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He is the one having Brahma as his son, while the brown-bodied Shiva is his grandson, by adoring the same Krisna Isana, everyone can achieve the best of son.

## \|\| 1.20.17 \|\|

*na yasya bhagavān brahmā prabhāvaṃ vetti tattvataḥ \|*  
*tamārādhya hṛṣīkeśaṃ prāpnuyāddhārmikaṃ sutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The one whose power and influence is unknown even to Brahma, by adoring the same lord Hrslkes'a, you can achieve the excellent son, with a religious mind.”

## \|\| 1.20.18 \|\|

*sa gautamavacaḥ śrutvā yuvanāśvo mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*ārādhayanmahāyogaṃ vāsudevaṃ sanātanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then king Yuvanas'va, listening to the words of the sage Gautama, started adoring the eternal HrshIkesa.

## \|\| 1.20.19 \|\|

*tasya putro 'bhavad vīraḥ śrāvastiriti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*nirmitā yena śrāvastirgauḍadeśe mahāpurī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In due course of time, he had a valorous son, named Savasti, who established the city of Savasti in the land of Gauda.

## \|\| 1.20.20 \|\|

*tasmācca bṛhadaśvo 'bhūt tasmāt kuvalayāśvakaḥ \|*  
*dhundhumāratvamagamad dhundhuṃ hatvā mahāsuram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Brhadasva was bom of him. Kuvalayasva was born of Brhadasva. He became known as Dhundhumara by killing the great Asura Dhundhu.

## \|\| 1.20.21-23 \|\|

*dhundhumārasya tanayāstrayaḥ proktā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*dṛḍhāśvaścaiva daṇḍāśvaḥ kapilāśvastathaiva ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dṛḍhāśvasya pramodastu haryaśvastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*haryaśvasya nikumbhastu nikumbhāt saṃhatāśvakaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kṛśāśvaśca raṇāśvaśca saṃhatāśvasya vai sutau \|*  
*yuvanāśvo raṇāśvasya śakratulyabalo yudhi \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. After killing the demon Dhundhu,1 he came to be known as Dhundhumara, who had three sons, who were known as the excellent Brahmanas. They were known as Dandasva, Drdhas'va and Kapilasva. Drdhasva had the son named Pramoda, whose son was known as Haryasva. Nikumbha was bom to Haryasva while Saruhatasva was bom to Nikumbha as a son. Saruhatasva had two sons known as Kftasva and Ranasva. Yuvanasva, the son of Ranasva, was as strong as Indra in the battlefield.

## \|\| 1.20.24-26 \|\|

*kṛtvā tu vāruṇīmiṣṭimṛṣīṇāṃ vai prasādataḥ \|*  
*lebhe tvapratimaṃ putraṃ viṣṇubhaktamanuttamam \|*  
*māndhātāraṃ mahāprājñaṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*māndhātuḥ purukutso 'bhūdambarīṣaśca vīryavān \|*  
*mucukundaśca puṇyātmā sarve śakrasamā yudhi \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ambarīṣasya dāyādo yuvanāśvo 'paraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*harito yuvanāśvasya hāritastatsuto 'bhavat \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. By performing the Varuril yajha and by the grace of the sages, Yuvanasva got a son named Mandhata, who was immensely wise, virtuous and was the best of all the carriers of the weapons. Mandhata had three sons known as Purukutsa, valorous Ambarisa and the auspicious Mucukunda. All of them were like Indra on the battle-field. Ambarlsa’s successor was another Yuvanas'va.

## \|\| 1.20.27-28 \|\|

*purukutsasya dāyādastrasadasyurmahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*narmadāyāṃ samutpannaḥ saṃbhūtistatsuto 'bhavat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*viṣṇuvṛddhaḥ sutastasya tvanaraṇyo 'bhavat paraḥ \|*  
*bṛhadaśavo 'naraṇyasya haryaśvastatsuto 'bhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Harita was the son of Yuvanasva, and his son was known as Harita. Pumkutsa’s successor was Trasadasyu of great fame. He had a son named Sambhflti, who was bom of Narmada. Visnuvrddha was the son of Sambhuti, while Anaranya was the son of Visnuvrddha. Brhadasva was the son of Anaranya, who had a son named Haryasva.

## \|\| 1.20.29 \|\|

*so 'tīva dhārmiko rājā kardamasya prajāpateḥ \|*  
*prasādāddhārmikaṃ putraṃ lebhe sūryaparāyaṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He was an extremely righteous king. By the grace of Kardama, the Prajapati, he begot a son who was quite a religious one and was devoted to the sun.

## \|\| 1.20.30 \|\|

*sa tu sūryaṃ samabhyarcya rājā vasumanāḥ śubham \|*  
*lebhe tvapratimaṃ putraṃ tridhanvānamarindamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Vasumanas was his name, who adored the sun, bestowed welfare on all and got a unique son named Tridhanvan who could subjugate his enemies.

## \|\| 1.20.31 \|\|

*ayajaccāśvamedhena śatrūn jitvā dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*svādhyāyavān dānaśīlastitikṣurdharmatatparaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. О Excellent Brahmanas, the king Vasumanas, after conquering the enemies, performed the As'vamedha sacrifice. He was quite studious, charitable, devoted to dharma and was desirous of achieving moksa.

## \|\| 1.20.32 \|\|

*ṛṣayastu samājagmuryajñavāṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhakaśyapamukhā devāścendrapurogamāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In the yajna performed by him, Vasishtha, Kasyapa and other Rishis participated, besides the gods headed by Indra.

## \|\| 1.20.33 \|\|

*tān praṇamya mahārājaḥ papraccha vinayānvitaḥ \|*  
*samāpya vidhivad yajñaṃ vasiṣṭhādīn dvijottamān \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After completing the yajna appropriately and bowing in reverence to Vasistha and other excellent Brahmanas, he asked them.

## \|\| 1.20.34 \|\|

*vasumanā uvāca*  
*kiṃsviccheyaskarataraṃ loke 'smin brāhmaṇarṣabhāḥ \|*  
*yajñastapo vā saṃnyāso brūta me sarvavedinaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Vasumanas said, “O Excellent Brahmanas, which is more conductive to welfare in this world? Is it sacrifice, penance or renunciation? Be pleased to tell me, О knowers of everything.”

## \|\| 1.20.35 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca*  
*adhītya vedān vidhivat putrānutpādya dharmataḥ \|*  
*iṣṭvā yajñeśvaraṃ yajñair gaccheda vanamathātmavān \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Vasistha said, “After appropriate study of the Vedas, after begetting and assiduously bringing them up, one should worship the lord of yajnas by performing sacrifices and realising the Atman should repair to the forest.”

## \|\| 1.20.36 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca*  
*ārādhya tapasā devaṃ yoginaṃ parameṣṭhinam \|*  
*pravrajed vidhivad yajñairiṣṭvā pūrvaṃ surottamān \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Pulastya said, “Initially one should adore the gods, Paramesvara and perform the yajnas, then one should embrace sannyasa (renunciation) appropriately.”

## \|\| 1.20.37 \|\|

*pulaha uvāca*  
*yamāhurekaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*tamārādhya sahastrāṃśuṃ tapasā mokṣamāpnuyāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Puloha said, “By means of penance, one shall propitiate that thousand-rayed deity whom they call the sole ancient Person and the Supreme Lord, and shall obtain liberation.”

## \|\| 1.20.38 \|\|

*jamadagniruvāca*  
*ajasya nābhāvadhyekamīśvareṇa samarpitam \|*  
*bījaṃ bhagavatā yena sa devastapasejyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Jamadagni said, “The one who is the seed of the universe, and is well aware of the inner feelings of all, is eternal, beyond birth, creator of the universe, the same Visnu can be achieved with the performing of tapas.

## \|\| 1.20.39 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca*  
*yo 'gniḥ sarvātmako 'nantaḥ svayaṃbhūrviśvatomukhaḥ \|*  
*sa rudrastapasogreṇa pūjyate netarairmakhaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Visvamitra said, “The one who has the form of fire, is the universal soul, beyond measure, having faces all-round, besides being self-bom, the same Rudra can be achieved by severe tapas and not with the performing of other sacrifices.”

## \|\| 1.20.40 \|\|

*bharadvāja uvāca*  
*yo yajñairijyate devo jātavedāḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*sa sarvadaivatatanuḥ pūjyate tapaseśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Bharadvaja said, “The eternal Vasudeva, who is adored with the performing of the yajnas, and whose form is constituted of all deities, is the Supreme Lord and he should be adored.”

## \|\| 1.20.41 \|\|

*atriruvāca*  
*yataḥ sarvamidaṃ jātaṃ yasyāpatyaṃ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ sumahadāsthāya pūjyate sa maheśvaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Atri said, “The one from whom the entire universe has emerged, and who has the son like Prajapati Brahma, the same Mahesvara should be adored performing the severe tapas."

## \|\| 1.20.42 \|\|

*gautama uvāca*  
*yataḥ pradhānapuruṣau yasya śaktimayaṃ jagat \|*  
*sa devadevastapasā pūjanīyaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Gautama said, “The one from whom Pradhana and Purusa were bom, and the one whose Shakti is represented by the universe, the same eternal god of gods, can be achieved with the performing of tapas."

## \|\| 1.20.43 \|\|

*kaśyapa uvāca*  
*sahastranayano devaḥ sākṣī sa tu prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*prasīdati mahāyogī pūjitastapasā paraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Kasyapa said, “The god who is the witness of all, having a thousand eyes, besides being the excellent yogi and Prajapati, the same Sambhu is pleased with the performing of the tapas.”

## \|\| 1.20.44 \|\|

*kraturuvāca*  
*prāptādhyayanayajñas labdhaputrasya caiva hi \|*  
*nāntareṇa tapaḥ kaściddharmaḥ śāstreṣu dṛśyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Kratu said, “The one who has achieved Vedic studies and performed yajnas, besides the sons, for such a person, there could be no other way, except to perform the penance. Nothing else is adviced in the dharmasastras."

## \|\| 1.20.45 \|\|

*ityākarṇya sa rājarṣistān praṇamyātihṛṣṭadhīḥ \|*  
*visarjayitvā saṃpūjya tridhanvānamathābravīt \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hearing this from the Royal-Rishis, that saintly king, feeling extremely delighted, bowed in reverence before the sages and after adoring them, sent them off. Then he spoke to Tridhanvan.

## \|\| 1.20.46 \|\|

*ārādhayiṣye tapasā devamekākṣarāhvayam \|*  
*prāṇaṃ bṛhantaṃ puruṣamādityāntarasaṃsthitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. “By means of penance I shall now worship the Lord designated with the single syllable Om, the great purusa who is lodged in the middle of the solar disc.

## \|\| 1.20.47 \|\|

*tvaṃ tu dharmarato nityaṃ pālayaitadatandritaḥ \|*  
*cāturvarṇyasamāyuktamaśeṣaṃ kṣitimaṇḍalam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. You getting free from laziness, devoting yourself to dharma, protect the entire earth comprising of the four castes of people.”

## \|\| 1.20.48 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa tadrājyaṃ nidhāyātmabhave nṛpaḥ \|*  
*jagāmāraṇyamanaghastapaścartumanuttamam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thus speaking, the sinless king entrusted the care of his kingdom to his son and retired to the forest for the performing of severe tapas.

## \|\| 1.20.49 \|\|

*himavacchikhare ramye devadāruvane śubhe \|*  
*kandamūlaphalāhāro munyannairayajat surān \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He reached the beautiful peaks of Himalaya, in the forest of Devadaru and started worshipping the gods with bulbous and other roots and fruits grown in the forest and subsisted on them.

## \|\| 1.20.50 \|\|

*saṃvatsaraśataṃ sāgraṃ taponirdhūtakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*jajāpa manasā devīṃ sāvitrariṃ vedamātaram \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He burnt all his sins performing tapas for more than a hundred years and continued reciting the Mantras of goddess Savitrl, the mother of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.20.51 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ japato devaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbho viśvātmā taṃ deśamagamat svayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Finding him so engaged in hard penance, Hiranyagarbha, lord Svayambhuva, the soul of the world, himself reached there.

## \|\| 1.20.52 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā devaṃ samāyāntaṃ brahmāṇaṃ viśvatomukham \|*  
*nanāma śirasā tasya pādayornāma kīrtayan \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Finding the arrival of the Lord Brahma, having faces in all the four directions, the king reciting his name, fell over the feet of 'lord Brahma in reverence.

## \|\| 1.20.53 \|\|

*namo devādhidevāya brahmaṇe paramātmane \|*  
*hirṇyamūrtaye tubhyaṃ sahastrākṣāya vedhase \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He said, “O God of gods, О Brahma, О Supreme soul, the gold-complexioned creator having a thousand eyes, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.20.54 \|\|

*namo dhātre vidhātre ca namo vedātmamūrtaye \|*  
*sāṃkhyayogādhigamyāya namaste jñānamūrtaye \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. You are Dhdta and Vidhata, salutation^ to you. Salutation to the form of the soul of'the gods. You could be achieved through the knowledge and practice of sdmkhya and yoga, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.20.55 \|\|

*namastrimūrtaye tubhyaṃ straṣṭre sarvārthavedine \|*  
*puruṣāya purāṇāya yogināṃ gurave namaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Salutation to you having the form of Trimurti. Salutation to the Purana Purusa and the preceptor of the yogis.”

## \|\| 1.20.56 \|\|

*tataḥ prasanno bhagavān viriñco viśvabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te varado 'smītyabhāṣata \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Then, lord Brahma feeling pleased, said, “Let you meet with welfare. I intend to bestow a boon on you. I am the granter of boons.”

## \|\| 1.20.57 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*japeyaṃ devadeveśa gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram \|*  
*bhūyo varṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ tāvadāyurbhavenmama \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The king said, “O Lord of gods, I should have the longevity for the period of a hundred years and more so that I could continue to recite the mantra of Gayatrl, the mother of the Vedas.”

## \|\| 1.20.58 \|\|

*bāḍhamityāha viśvātmā samālokya narādhipam \|*  
*spṛṣṭvā karābhyāṃ suprītastatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The universal soul-Brahma, said looking at the king, “Very well.” Thereafter, the delightful Brahma touched the king with both his hands and disappeared thereafter.

## \|\| 1.20.59 \|\|

*so 'pi labdhavaraḥ śrīmān jajāpātiprasannadhīḥ \|*  
*śāntastriṣavaṇasnāyī kandamūlaphalāśanaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Soon after the receiving of the boon, the delightful king continued the reciting of the mantra. He took bath thrice a day, feeling calm continued to consume fruits and roots.

## \|\| 1.20.60 \|\|

*tasya pūrṇe varṣaśate bhagavānugradīdhitiḥ \|*  
*prādurāsīnmahāyogī bhānormaṇḍalamadhyataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. After completion of a hundred years, the lord of fierce-rays, the great Yogin, appeared in front of him from the solar disc of the sun.

## \|\| 1.20.61 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā vedaviduṣaṃ maṇḍalasthaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*svayaṃbhuvamanādyantaṃ brahmāṇaṃ vismayaṃ gataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Finding Brahma, having the body of the Vedas, being eternal, lodged in the solar disc, the king felt surprised.

## \|\| 1.20.62 \|\|

*tuṣṭāva vaidikairmantraiḥ sāvitryā ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇādapaśyat puruṣaṃ tameva parameśvaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He started offering prayer to him reciting the Vedic hymns, more particularly the Savitri mantra. After a moment, he found him in the form of Parames'vara.

## \|\| 1.20.63 \|\|

*caturmukhaṃ jaṭāmaulimaṣṭahastaṃ trilocanam \|*  
*candrāvayavalakṣamāṇaṃ naranārītanuṃ haram \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He had four faces, had matted locks of hair over the head, had eight hands and three eyes. He was marked with the moon’s digits; infact he was Ardhanarls'vara (half male and half female body) Shiva.

## \|\| 1.20.64 \|\|

*bhāsayantaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ svaraśmibhiḥ \|*  
*raktāmbaradharaṃ raktaṃ raktamālyānulepanam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The entire universe had been covered with his rays. He had a blue throat, was clad in red garments, garlands and unguents. He himself was red in colour.

## \|\| 1.20.65 \|\|

*tadbhāvabhāvito dṛṣṭvā sadbhāvena pareṇa hi \|*  
*nanāma śirasā rudraṃ sāvitryānena caiva hi \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Having an audience with such a Rudradeva, the king becoming emotional, with an overwhelming mind, reciting the Gayatrl mantra, with devotion, offered his salutation to Rudradeva, lowering his head.

## \|\| 1.20.66 \|\|

*namaste nīlakaṇṭhāya bhāsvate parameṣṭhine \|*  
*trayīmayāya rudrāya kālarūpāya hetave \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Then the king said, “O Nllakantha, О Illustrious ParamesthI, the form of the Vedas, Rudra, Kalaruipa and the cause of all, salutation to you.”

## \|\| 1.20.67 \|\|

*tadā prāha mahādevo rājānaṃ prītamānasaḥ \|*  
*imāni me rahasyāni nāmāni śṛṇu cānagha \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Then Mahadeva, getting pleased spoke to the king, “O sinless king, these are my secret names and you care to listen to them.

## \|\| 1.20.68 \|\|

*sarvavedeṣu gītāni saṃsāraśamanāni tu \|*  
*namaskuruṣva nṛpate ebhirmāṃ satataṃ śuciḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. All of them have been described in the Vedas and are blissful for the world. О King, keeping yourself always pure, you adore me with the reciting of these names.

## \|\| 1.20.69 \|\|

*adhyāyaṃ śatarudrīyaṃ yajuṣāṃ sāramuddhṛtam \|*  
*japasvānanyacetasko mayyāsaktamanā nṛpa \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. О King, completely devoting yourself in me, you study and recite the Satarudriya-adhyaya which is the gist of Yajurveda.

## \|\| 1.20.70 \|\|

*brahmacārī mitāhāro bhasmaniṣṭhaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*japedāmaraṇād rudraṃ sa yāti paramaṃ padam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A person, who, being a celibate, observing fast, applying ashes over the body, with a devoted mind, recites my .Тара of Rudra, till the time of death, he achieves the supreme position.”

## \|\| 1.20.71 \|\|

*ityuktvā bhagavān rudro bhaktānugrahakāmyayā \|*  
*punaḥ saṃvatsaraśataṃ rājñe hyāyurakalpayat \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Thus speaking, lord Rudra, bestowed to him another lease of life of a hundred years. He is always benevolent on his devotees.

## \|\| 1.20.72 \|\|

*dattvāsmai tat paraṃ jñānaṃ vairāgyaṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇādantardadhe rudrastadadbhutamivābhavat \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Paramesvara Rudra, bestowing the supreme knowledge and detachment, disappeared in a moment. In this way, the astonishing event happened.

## \|\| 1.20.73 \|\|

*rājāpi tapasā rudraṃ jajāpānanyamānasaḥ \|*  
*bhasmacchannastriṣavaṇaṃ snātvā śāntaḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The king also, applied ashes over his body, taking bath every day, remaining calm, with a devoted mind, started performing the japam of Satarudriya.

## \|\| 1.20.74-75 \|\|

*japatastasya nṛpateḥ pūrṇe varṣaśate punaḥ \|*  
*yogapravṛttirabhavat kālāt kālātmakaṃ param \|\| 74 \|\|*

*viveśa tad vedasāraṃ sthānaṃ vai parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*bhānoḥ sa maṇḍalaṃ śubhraṃ tato yāto maheśvaram \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. While so performing the japam for a period of full hundred years, the Yogic activity began to function (resulting in deeper mediation). Then after some time, the king entered the place of Brahma, the ParamesthI, who is the gist of the Vedas. Then achieving the solar region, finally achieved the place of Mahesvara, which happened to be the supreme.

## \|\| 1.20.76 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyād vāpi rājñaścaritamuttamam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. A person who reads or even listens to the excellent conduct of the king Vasumanas, he getting relieved of all the sins, is adored in the Brahmaloka.

## Chapter 21. Description of Iksvaku Dynasty (Story of Rama)

## \|\| 1.21.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tridhanvā rājaputrastu dharmeṇāpālayanmahīm \|*  
*tasya putro 'bhavad vidvāṃstrayyāruṇa iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “Thereafter Tridhanvan, the son of the king, started ruling the country with a righteous mind. He got a son who was well-read and was known by the name of Trayaruna.

## \|\| 1.21.2 \|\|

*tasya satyavrato nāma kumāro 'bhūnmahābalaḥ \|*  
*bhāryā satyadhanā nāma hariścandramajījanat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Не had a son named Satyavrata who was extremely strong. Satyadhana was the name of his wife and Haris'candra was bom of her.

## \|\| 1.21.3-7 \|\|

*hariścandrasya putro 'bhūd rohito nāma vīryavān \|*  
*harito rohitasyātha dhundhustasya suto 'bhavat \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vijayaśca sudevaśca dhundhuputrau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*vijayasyābhavat putraḥ kāruko nāma vīryavān \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kārukasya vṛkaḥ putrastasmād bāhurajāyata \|*  
*sagarastasya putrau'bhūd rājā paramadhārmikaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dve bhārye sagarasyāpi prabhā bhānumatī tathā \|*  
*tābhyāmārādhitaḥ prādādaurvāgnirvaramuttamam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ekaṃ bhānumatī putramagṛhṇādasamañjasam \|*  
*prabhā ṣaṣṭisahastraṃ tu putrāṇāṃ jagṛhe śubhā \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. Rohita was the son of Hariscandra who was quite valorous. Vrka was the son of Rohita, from whom was bom Bahu. Harita was Rohita’s son. Harita's son was known as Dhundhu. Sudeva and Vijaya were the two sons of Dhundhu. Karuka, the son of Vijaya was extremely valorous. Sagara, his son, was an extremely virtuous king. Sagara had two wives, known as Prabhavatl and Bhanumatl. Both of them had been bestowed with a boon each by lord Agni. Bhanumatl gave birth to a son named Asamanjasa, while Prabhavatl produced sixty thousand sons. The son of Asamanjasa was known as the king Arhsuman.

## \|\| 1.21.8 \|\|

*asamañsasya tanayo hyaṃśumān nāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro dilīpastu dilīpāt tu bhagīrathaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Dillpa was his son and Bhagiratha was born to Dillpa. Bhagiratha, after performing severe tapas, brought Ganga over the earth. Because of this she came to be known as Bhaglrathl.

## \|\| 1.21.9 \|\|

*yena bhāgīrathī gaṅgā tapaḥ kṛtvāvatāritā \|*  
*prasādād devadevasya mahādevasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The wise Mahadeva, the god of gods, had been merciful on him. With the tapas performed by Bhaglratha, lord Shiva felt delighted.

## \|\| 1.21.10 \|\|

*bhagīrathasya tapasā devaḥ prītamanā haraḥ \|*  
*babhāra śirasā gaṅgāṃ somānte somabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then the moon-bedecked Mahadeva bore Gauga on his head near the moon-crest. Sruta was known as the son of Bhaglratha.

## \|\| 1.21.11 \|\|

*bhagīrathasutaścāpi śruto nāma babhūva ha \|*  
*nābhāgastasya dāyādaḥ sindhudvīpastato 'bhavat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Не had a son named Nabhaga, while Sindhudvipa was the son of Nabhaga. His son came to be known as Ayutayu who had a son named Rtuparna.

## \|\| 1.21.12 \|\|

*ayutāyuḥ sutastasya ṛtuparṇastu tatsutaḥ \|*  
*ṛtuparṇasya putro 'bhūt sudāso nāma dhārmikāḥ \|*  
*saudāsastasya tanayaḥ khyātaḥ kalmāṣapādakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Saudasa was the most religious-minded son of Rtuparna. Saudasa had a son named Kalmasapada.

## \|\| 1.21.13-15 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhastu mahātejāḥ kṣetre kalmāṣapādake \|*  
*aśmakaṃ janayāmasā tamikṣvākukuladhvajam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*aśmakasyotkalāyāṃ tu nakulo nāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*sa hi rāmabhayād rājā vanaṃ prāpa suduḥ khitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vibhrat sa nārīkavacaṃ tasmācchataratho 'bhavat \|*  
*tasmād bilibiliḥ śrīmānvṛddhaśarmācatatsutaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Vasistha of great splendour begot of the wife of Kalmasapada the son named Asmaka, who was established as the flag for the Iksvaku dynasty. From Utkala, the wife of Asmaka, a son named Nakula was bom, who became the king. The said king went on exile getting frightened from Parasurama. Reaching in the forest, he took to the form of a woman. Sataratha was bom of Nakula, while Bilibili was bom as son of Sataratha. Vrddhasarma was bom to him as his son. He had a son named Vis'vasaha, who had a well-known son named Khatvariga. Dlrghabahu was his son. Raghu was bom of Dlrghabahu.

## \|\| 1.21.16-17 \|\|

*tasmād viśvasahastasmāt khaṭvāṅga iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*dīrghabāhuḥ sutastasya raghustasmādajāyata \|\| 16 \|\|*

*raghorajaḥ samutpanno rājā daśarathastataḥ \|*  
*rāmo dāśarathirvoro dharmajño lokaviśrutaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Aja was bom as son to Raghu, while Dasaratha was bom as son to Aja. The valorous and great Rama was bom as a son to Das'aratha. He was immensely strong, religious-minded and glorious. Besides Rama, Dasaratha had three more sons known as Bharata, Laksmana and valorous Satrughna. All of them having possessed the Shakti of Visnu, were comparable to Indra in the battlefield.

## \|\| 1.21.18-19 \|\|

*bharato lakṣmaṇaścaiva śatrughnaśca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sarve śakrasamā yuddhe viṣṇuśaktisamanvitāḥ \|*  
*jajñe rāvaṇanāśārthaṃ viṣṇuraṃśena viśvakṛt \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rāmasya subhagā bhāryā janakasyātmajā śubhā \|*  
*sītā trilokavikhyātā śīlaudāryaguṇānvitā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Lord Visnu, the consumer of the universe, had incarnated on earth from his own arusa for the killing of Ravana. The extremely virtuous wife of Rama was Sita, the daughter of Janaka and was well known in the three worlds. She was quite humble and extremely beautiful. Because the king Janaka had pleased Parvati, the daughter of Himalaya, therefore Parvati gave away Sita to Janaka as his daughter. Sita on the other hand, had the support of Rama who became her husband.

## \|\| 1.21.20-22 \|\|

*tapasā toṣitā devī janakena girīndrajā \|*  
*prāyacchajjānakīṃ sītāṃ rāmamevāśritā patim \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prītaśca bhagavānīśastriśūlī nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*pradadau śatrunāśārthaṃ janakāyādbhutaṃ dhanuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sa rājā janako vidvān dātukāmaḥ sutāmimām \|*  
*aghoṣayadamitraghno loke 'smin dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. The bluish-red complexioned, trident bearer Shiva, feeling extremely delighted, for the destmction of the enemies, handed over an astonishing bow to Janaka. О Best of the Brahmanas, the intelligent king Janaka, the destroyer of his enemies on earth, desirous of the marriage of his daughter, declared that who- so-ever shall lift up the bow would achieve Sita in the marriage.

## \|\| 1.21.23-24 \|\|

*idaṃ dhanuḥ samādātuṃ yaḥ śaknoti jagattraye \|*  
*devo vā dānavo vāpi sa sītāṃ labdhumarhati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vijñāya rāmo balavān janakasya gṛhaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*bhañjayāmāsa cādāya gatvāsau līlayaiva hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Knowing about the vow of Janaka, the valorous lord Rama, reached the abode of Janaka and lifting the bow playfully, broke it. Then Sita was married to Rama, the highly virtuous soul, as Parvati had been wedded t1 Shiva, or Sena was married to six-headed god Karttikeya. Thus Sita was married to Rama.

## \|\| 1.21.25-28 \|\|

*udvavāha ca tāṃ kanyāṃ pārvatīmiva śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*rāmaḥ paramadharmātmā senāmiva ca ṣaṇmukhaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tato bahutithe kāle rājā daśarathaḥ svayam \|*  
*rāmaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ sutaṃ vīraṃ rājānaṃ kartumārabhat \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasyātha patnī subhagā kaikeyī cārubhāṣiṇī \|*  
*nivārayāmāsa patiṃ prāha saṃbhrāntamānasā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*matsutaṃ bharataṃ vīraṃ rājānaṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*pūrvameva varo yasmād datto me bhavatā yataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. Thereafter the lapse of a long period, the king Dasaratha, himself desired to crown his son Rama as the king. Then his wife Kaikeyl who was quite beautiful and fortunate, stopped her husband and said, “My valorous son Bharata is fit enough to be crowned as the king, because earlier you had promised me to give two boons. The king Das'aratha felt dejected in his mind with the listening to her words.

## \|\| 1.21.29 \|\|

*sa tasyā vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā duḥ khitamānasaḥ \|*  
*bāḍhamityabravīd vākyaṃ tathā rāmo 'pi dharmavit \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. But inspite of his mind having been hurt, Dasaratha agreed to her words with a heavy heart, saying, “So be it.” Accordingly the unwavering Rama, the knower of Dharma, who could not transgress the traditions, accompanied by Laksmana, bowing at the feet of Dasaratha, proceeded on to the forest with his wife Sita.

## \|\| 1.21.30-32 \|\|

*praṇamyātha pituḥ pādau lakṣmaṇena sahācyutaḥ \|*  
*yayau vanaṃ sapatnīkaḥ kṛtvā samayamātmavān \|\| 30 \|\|*

*saṃvatsarāṇāṃ catvāri daśa caiva mahābalaḥ \|*  
*uvāsa tatra matimān lakṣmaṇena saha prabhuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kadācid vasato 'raṇye rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ \|*  
*parivrājakaveṣeṇa sītāṃ hṛtvā yayau purīm \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. In this way, the valorous Rama dwelt in the forest for a period of fourteen years along with Laksmana. During his stay in the forest, a Raksasa named Ravana, taking to the form of an ascetic, kidnapped Sita and took her to his place. Both Rama and Laksmana finding Sita absent from Pancavatl, became extremely anguish and sorrow. He was the destroyer of the enemies, but still they were overpowered with grief and pain.

## \|\| 1.21.33-36 \|\|

*adṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇo rāmaḥ sītāmākulitendriyau \|*  
*duḥ khaśokābhisaṃtaptau babhūvaturarindamau \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tataḥ kadācit kapinā sugrīveṇa dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*vānarāṇāmabhūt sakhyaṃ rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sugrīvasyānugo vīro hanumān nma vānaraḥ \|*  
*vāyuputrau mahātejā rāmasyāsīt priyaḥ sadā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sa kṛtvā paramaṃ dhairyaṃ rāmāya kṛtaniścayaḥ \|*  
*ānayiṣyāmi tāṃ sītāmityuktvā vicacāra ha \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. О Best of the sages, then at some time Rama of indefatigable energy, the performer of the great deeds, made friendship with Sugrlva

## \|\| 1.21.37-39 \|\|

*mahīṃ sāgaraparyantāṃ sītādarśanatatparaḥ \|*  
*jagāma rāvaṇapurīṃ laṅkāṃ sāgarasaṃsthitām \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tatrātha nirjane deśe vṛkṣmūle śucismitām \|*  
*apaśyadamalāṃ sītāṃ rākṣasībhiḥ samāvṛtām \|\| 38 \|\|*

*aśrupūrṇekṣaṇāṃ hṛdyāṃ saṃsmarantīmaninditām \|*  
*rāmamindīvaraśyāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ cātmasaṃsthitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. He ultimately reached the city of Lanka- the capital of Ravana, which was lodged in the midocean. There he saw Sita lodged in a lonely forest under the shade of a tree. The spotless and chaste Sita was surrounded by the demonesses. Her eyes were wet with tears, still she appeared quite graceful. She looked innocent while uttering the name of Rama. Her mind was absorbed in the memories of dark blue- complexioned Rama and the self-possessed Laksmana. Hanuman, finding Sita in seclusion, introduced himself to her.

## \|\| 1.21.40-42 \|\|

*nivedayitvā cātmānaṃ sītāyai rahasi svayam \|*  
*asaṃśayāya pradadāvasyai rāmāṅgulīyakam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvāṅgulīyakaṃ sītā patyuḥ paramaśobhanam \|*  
*mene samāgataṃ rāmaṃ prītivisphāritekṣaṇā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*samāśvāsya tadā sītāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmasya cāntikam \|*  
*nayiṣye tvāṃ mahābāhuruktvā rāmaṃ yayau punaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. For the removal of any doubt, Hanuman handed over the finger ring of Rama to Sita. At that point of time finding the beautiful finger ring of her husband, Sita whose eyes blossomed because of the love of her husband, accepted it as if Rama himself had met her. Hanuman on the other hand, reassured Sita variously and said, “I shall myself carry you to the largearmed Rama.” Thus speaking he again returned to Rama. Hanuman who had controlled all his senses, narrated to Rama about his audience with Sita. Thus having been adored by Laksmana, he stood before Rama.

## \|\| 1.21.43-46 \|\|

*nivedayitvā rāmāya sītādarśanamātmavān \|*  
*tasthau rāmeṇa purato lakṣmaṇena ca pūjitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa rāmo balavān sārdhaṃ hanumatā svayam \|*  
*lakṣmaṇena ca yuddhāya buddhiṃ cakre hi rakṣasām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kṛtvātha vānaraśatairlaṅkāmārgaṃ mahodadheḥ \|*  
*setuṃ paramadharmātmā rāvaṇaṃ hatavān prabhuḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sapatnīkaṃ ca sasutaṃ sabhrātṛkamaridamaḥ \|*  
*ānayāmāsa tāṃ sītāṃ vāyuputrasahāyavān \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-46. Thereafter, the valorous Rama, in the company of Laksmana and Hanuman, together with the hundreds of monkeys built a bridge over the ocean and prepared a road for reachin Lanka. Thereafter, the religious Rama, killing Ravana, together with his wife, son and the brothers, with the help of Hanuman, the son of the wind-god, got Sita back from Lanka. He also built a temple in the middle of the bridge, dedicated to lord Krttivasa Shiva, enshrining Shivalinga therein. Thereafter Raghava Rama adored Shiva.

## \|\| 1.21.47-49 \|\|

*setumadhye mahādevamīśānaṃ kṛttivāsasam \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa liṅgasthaṃ pūjayāmāsa rāghavaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasya devo mahādevaḥ pārvatyā saha śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣameva bhagavān dattavān varamuttamam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yat tvayā sthāpitaṃ liṅgaṃ drakṣyantīha dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*mahāpātakasaṃyuktāsteṣāṃ pāpaṃ vinaśyatu \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. Thereafter, lord Shiva appeared before Rama with Parvati. Lord Shiva bestowed an excellent boon on Rama saying, “The linga which has been consecrated by you, shall be visited by all the people. Even the grave sinners who would visit this place shall be relieved of all the sins. Similarly, a person who shall take bath in the ocean, all his sins will be washed out.

## \|\| 1.21.50-51 \|\|

*anyāni caiva pāpāni snātasyātra mahodadhau \|*  
*darśanādeva liṅgasalya nāśaṃ yānti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*yāvat sthāsyanti girayo yāvadeṣā ca medinī \|*  
*yāvat setuśca tāvacca sthāsyāmyatra tirohitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. With the mere look at the Ramesvara linga, all the sins of a person shall be washed out. There is not the slightest doubt about it. Till the mountain are there on earth, and the earth remains, the bridge will continue here. I shall stay here in an invisible form. The bath taken here and the charities performed at this place shall remain undecaying. The Sraddhas performed here shall also be undecaying or everlasting.

## \|\| 1.21.52-53 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ japaḥ śrāddhaṃ bhaviṣyatyakṣyaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*smaraṇādeva liṅgasya dinapāpaṃ praṇaśyati \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ityuktvā bhagavāñchaṃbhuḥ pariṣvajya tu rāghavam \|*  
*sanandī sagaṇo rudrastatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. With the mere recollection of this linga, the sins performed during the day shall be wiped out.” Thus speaking, Lord Shiva embraced Rama. Then lord Shiva together with Nandin and other attendants, disappeared from the scene. Thereafter, the religious-minded Rama ruled the country with due devotion to piety.

## \|\| 1.21.54-57 \|\|

*rāmo 'pi pālayāmāsa rājyaṃ dharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*abhiṣikto mahātejā bharatena mahābalaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*viśeṣāḍh brāhmaṇān sarvān pūjayāmasaceśvaram \|*  
*yajñena yajñahantāramaśvamedhena śaṅkaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

*rāmasya tanayo jajñe kuśa ityabhiviśrutaḥ \|*  
*lavaśca sumahābhāgaḥ sarvatattvārthavit sudhīḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*atithistu kuśājjajñe niṣadhastatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*nalastu niṣadhasyābhūnnabhastamādajāyata \|\| 57 \|\|*

54-57. Bharata on the other hand, crowned Rama as the king. He especially honoured the lord as well as the Brahmanas. Rama pleased lord Shiva, the destroyer of the sacrifice of Daksa, with the performing of Asvamedha sacrifice. Rama had a son named Kusa. He had another son named Lava, who was well-versed in the entire scriptures as well as the principles. A son named Atithi was bom to Kus'a, who had a son named Nisadha. Nala was bom as son to Nisadha. Nabhas was bom of him. Pundarlkaksa was the son of Nabhas, while Ksemadhanvan was his son.

## \|\| 1.21.58 \|\|

*nabhasaḥ puṇḍarīkākhyaḥ kṣemadhanvā ca tatsutaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro 'bhavad vīro devānīkaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. A son named Devanlka was bom to Ksemadhanvan. Ahinagu was his son and had Mahasvan as his son.

## \|\| 1.21.59-61 \|\|

*ahīnagustasya suto sahasvāṃstatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*tasmāccandrāvalokastu tārāpīḍastu tatsutaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tārāpīḍāccandragirirbhānuvittastato 'bhavat \|*  
*śrutāyurabhavat tasmādete ikṣvākuvaṃśajāḥ \|*  
*sarve prādhānyataḥ proktāḥ samāsena dvijottamāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*ya imaṃ śṛṇuyānnityamikṣvākorvaṃśamuttamam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. Candravaloka was born to him. Taradhis'a happened to be his son. Candragiri was bom of Taradhis'a. Bhanuvitta was bom of him. He had a son named Srutayu. All of them were bom in Iksavaku dynasty. О Excellent Brahmanas, I have spelt out the names of prominent kings in brief. A person who listens to the story of the Iksavaku dynasty, he getting relived of all the sins, achieves Devaloka (the heavenly region).

## Chapter 22. Description of Lunar Dynasty

## \|\| 1.22.1 \|\|

*romaharṣaṇa uvāca*  
*ailaḥ purūravāścātha rājā rājyamapālayat \|*  
*tasya putrā babhūvurhi ṣaḍindrasamatejasaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “Thereafter Puraravas, the son of Ila, started ruling the country. He had six sons who were as valorous as Indra.

## \|\| 1.22.2 \|\|

*āyurmāyuramāvāyurviśvāyuścaiva vīryavān \|*  
*śatāyuśca śrutāyuśca divyāścaivorvaśīsutāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The divine sons of UrvasI were- Ayu, Mayu, Amayu, valorous Visvayu, Satayu and Srutayu.

## \|\| 1.22.3 \|\|

*āyuṣastanayā vīrāḥ pañcaivāsan mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*svarbhānutanayāyāṃ vai prabhāyāmiti naḥ śrutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The five valorous sons of Ayu, were bom of Prabha, the daughter of Svarbhanu. This is what has been heard by us.

## \|\| 1.22.4-5 \|\|

*nahuṣaḥ prathamasteṣāṃ dharmajño lokaviśrutaḥ \|*  
*nahuṣasya tu dāyādāḥ ṣaḍindropamatejasaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*utpannāḥ pitṛkanyāyāṃ virajāyāṃ mahābalāḥ \|*  
*yatiryayātiḥ saṃyātirāyātiḥ pañcako 'śvakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Nahusa was the first among them, who had been well-versed in dharma and was quite famous. Nahusa had five illustrious successors, comparable with Indra in splendour. They were born of Viraja, the daughter of Pitrs. They were known by the names of Yati, Yayati, Samyati, Ayati and Asvaka.

## \|\| 1.22.6 \|\|

*teṣāṃ yayātiḥ pañcānāṃ mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*devayānīmukhanasaḥ sutāṃ bhāryāmavāpa saḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Out of these five sons, Yayati possessed enormous prowess and was quite strong. He got Devayani, the daughter of Sukra as his wife.

## \|\| 1.22.7 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhāmāsurīṃ caiva tanayāṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|*  
*yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva devayānī vyajāyata \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Besides, Yayati had Sarmistha, as his wife as well. DevayanT produced Turvasu and Yadu as sons.

## \|\| 1.22.8-9 \|\|

*druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca śarmiṣṭhā cāpyajījanat \|*  
*so 'bhyaṣiñcadatikramya jyeṣṭhaṃ yadumaninditam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*purumeva kanīyāsaṃ piturvacanapālakam \|*  
*diśi dakṣiṇapūrvasyāṃ turvasuṃ putramādiśat \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Sarmistha, on the other hand, produced Druhyu, Anu and Ptiru. Yayati, neglecting his eldest son Yadu, who disobeyed the command of his father, crowned his youngest son Ptiru as the king. The kingdom of the south-east was given over to Turvasu.

## \|\| 1.22.10 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāparayo rājā yaduṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ nyayojayat \|*  
*pratīcyāmuttārāyāṃ ca druhyuṃ cānumakalpayat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The king out of the five sons gave away, south and the west part of the kingdom to his excellent son, Yadu.1 Druhyu and Anu were given the rule of the western and the northern territories respectively.

## \|\| 1.22.11 \|\|

*tairiyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā dharmataḥ paripālitā \|*  
*rājāpi dārasahito navaṃ prāpa mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All the kings started ruling the countries with a religious mind, while the glorious king Yayati, together with his wife left for the forest.

## \|\| 1.22.12 \|\|

*yadorapyabhavan putrāḥ pañca devasutopamāḥ \|*  
*sahastrajit tathājyeṣṭhaḥ kroṣaṭurnālo 'jitoraghuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Yadu also had five sons resembling the gods. Sahasrajit was the best of them all. The remaining four were known by the names of Krostu, NTla, Jina and Raghu.

## \|\| 1.22.13-14 \|\|

*sahastrajitsutastadvacchatajinnāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*sutāḥ śatajito 'pyāsaṃstrayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*haihayaśca hayaścaiva rājā veṇuhayaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*haihayasyābhavat putro dharma ityabhiviśrutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Satajit was the son of Sahasrajit. Satajit had extremely religious three sons known as Haihaya, Haya and Venuhaya. Dharma was well known as the son of Haihaya.

## \|\| 1.22.15 \|\|

*tasya putro 'bhavad viprā dharmanetraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*dharmanetrasya kīrtistu saṃjitastatsuto 'bhavat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О Brahmanas, the glorious Dharmanetra, had been the son of Dharma. Dharmanetra had a son named Kirti who had a son named Sanjita.

## \|\| 1.22.16 \|\|

*mahiṣmān saṃjitasyābhūd bhadraśreṇyastadanvayaḥ \|*  
*bhadraśreṇyasya dāyādo durdamo nāma pārthivaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Mahisma was the son of Sanjita, while Bhadras'renya was the son of the former. The son of Bhadrasrenya was known as Durdama.

## \|\| 1.22.17-18 \|\|

*durdamasya suto dhīmān dhanako nāma vīryavān \|*  
*dhanakasya tu dāyādāścatvāro lokasammatāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kṛtavīryaḥ kṛtāgniśca kṛtavarmā tathaiva ca \|*  
*kṛtaujāśca caturtho 'bhūt kārtavīryor'juno 'bhavat \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Durdama’s son was the intelligent and valiant king Andhaka. Andhaka had four famous sons, known as Krtavlrya, Krtagni, Krtavarma and Krtaujas. Krtavlrya had a son named Arjuna with thousand arms.

## \|\| 1.22.19 \|\|

*sahastrabāhurdyutimān dhanurvedavidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*tasya rāmo 'bhavanmṛtyurjāmadagnyo janārdanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Arjuna had a thousand hands and was the foremost of those well-versed in archery. He met defeat at the hands of Rama, the son of Jamadagni and the incarnation of Janardana (Visnu).

## \|\| 1.22.20-21 \|\|

*tasya putraśatānyāsan pañca tatra mahārathāḥ \|*  
*kṛtāstrā balinaḥ śūrā dharmātmāno namasvinaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śūraśca śūrasenaśca dhṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇastathaiva ca \|*  
*jayadhvajaśca balavān nārāyaṇaparo nṛpaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Arjuna had a hundred sons, five out of whom were quite strong, valorous, powerful, righteous-minded as well as learned. They were known by the names of Sura, Sfirasena, Krisna, Dhrsna and Jayadhvaja. Jayadhvaja was quite strong and was also devoted to Narayana.

## \|\| 1.22.22 \|\|

*śūrasenādayaḥ sarve catvāraḥ prathitaujasaḥ \|*  
*rudrabhaktā mahātmānaḥ pūjayanti sma śaṅkaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The first four sons including Sura and others were quite famous, strong, devoted to Rudra and were the noble souls. They all worshipped lord Shiva.

## \|\| 1.22.23 \|\|

*jayadhvajastu matimān devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim \|*  
*jagāma śaraṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ daivataṃ dharmatatparaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Jayadhvaja was quite intelligent, devoted to religion and took refuge with lord Narayana-Hari, and worshipped him alone.

## \|\| 1.22.24 \|\|

*tamūcuritare putrā nāyaṃ dharmastavānagha \|*  
*īśvarārādhanarataḥ pitāsmākamabhūditi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The other sons spoke to him, “O Sinless one, this is not your faith. Our father worshipped Shiva. This is what has been heard by us.”

## \|\| 1.22.25 \|\|

*tānabravīnmahātejā eṣa dharmaḥ paro mama \|*  
*viṣṇoraṃśena saṃbhūtā rājāno yanmahītale \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The immensely illustrious Jayadhvaja replied, “This is my faith, all the kings of the earth derive their lineage from Visnu and are his arhsa?'

## \|\| 1.22.26 \|\|

*rājyaṃ pālayatāvaśyaṃ bhagavān puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*pūjanīyo yato viṣṇuḥ pālako jagato hariḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Lord Purusottama will surely maintain the kingdom. Hari, the preserver of the universe and invincible Visnu are adorable.

## \|\| 1.22.27 \|\|

*sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ca svayaṃbhuvaḥ \|*  
*tistrastu mūrtayaḥ proktāḥ sṛṣṭisthityantahetavaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There are three forms of the self-born lord, relating to the creation, sustenance and destruction, also known as the Sattva, Rajas and Tamas.

## \|\| 1.22.28 \|\|

*sattvātmā bhagavān viṣṇuḥ saṃsthāpayati sarvadā \|*  
*sṛjed brahmā rajomūrtiḥ saṃharet tāmaso haraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Lord Visnu is the form of Sattva and is always engaged in the sustainment of the universe. Brahma, the form of Rajas is engaged in the creation and Mahesa, representing Tamas is engaged in destruction of the universe.

## \|\| 1.22.29 \|\|

*tasmānmahīpatīnāṃ tu rājyaṃ pālayatāmayam \|*  
*ārādhyo bhagavān viṣṇuḥ keśavaḥ keśimardanaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Therefore, Lord Visnu, Kes'ava the suppressor of Kesin, is the adorable lord being propitiated by the kings who protect their respective kingdoms.

## \|\| 1.22.30 \|\|

*niśamya tasya vacanaṃ bhrātaro 'nye manasvinaḥ \|*  
*procuḥ saṃhārakṛd rudraḥ pūjanīyo mumukṣubhiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Listening to the words of the king, his other steady-minded brothers spoke. “The people desirous of moksa (liberation), should adore Rudra, the destroyer.

## \|\| 1.22.31 \|\|

*ayaṃ hi bhagavān rudraḥ sarvaṃ jagadidaṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*tamoguṇaṃ samāśritya kalpānte saṃharet prabhuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The lord Rudra is verily the Supreme deity. Under the influence of tamoguna, he destroys the whole universe at the end of the kalpa.

## \|\| 1.22.32 \|\|

*yā sā ghoratarā mūrtirasya tejāmayī parā \|*  
*saṃhared vidyayā sarvaṃ saṃsāraṃ śūlabhṛt tayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The trident-bearing lord dissolves the world by means of Vidya at the outset and then with his terrific and illustrious form, he destroys the universe.”

## \|\| 1.22.33 \|\|

*tatastānabravīd rājā vicintyāsau jayadhvajaḥ \|*  
*sattvena mucyate jantuḥ sattvātmā bhagavān hariḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thereafter the king Jayadhvaja, after the deep thinking, spoke to those people, “A living being is redeemed by means of Sattvaguna and lord Hari is the form of Sattva.”

## \|\| 1.22.34 \|\|

*tamūcurbhrātaro rudraḥ sevitaḥ sāttvikairjanaiḥ \|*  
*mocayet sattvasaṃyuktaḥ pūjayeśaṃ tato haram \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. His brothers said, “The Sattvika people too adore Rudra. Lord Shiva also liberates the Sattvika persons. One who is endowed with Sattva Guna shall always worship Shiva.”

## \|\| 1.22.35 \|\|

*athābravīd rājaputraḥ prahasan vai jayadhvajaḥ \|*  
*svadharmo muktaye panthā nānyo munibhiraṣyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At this, the prince Jayadhvaja laughingly said, “For achieving salvation, one's own dharma is always favourable and none else. This is opinion of the sages as well.

## \|\| 1.22.36 \|\|

*tathā ca vaiṣṇavī śaktirnṛpāṇāṃ devatā sadā \|*  
*ārādhanaṃ paro dharmo purāreramitaujasaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Therefore, embracing the Vaisnavl Shakti, the rulers should always adore the resplendent lord Visnu which is the greatest Dharma of kings.”

## \|\| 1.22.37-38 \|\|

*tamabravīd rājaputraḥ kṛṣṇo matimatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*yadarjuno 'smajjanakaḥ svadharmaṃ kṛtavāniti \|\| 37 \|\|*

*evaṃ vivāde vitate śūraseno 'bravīd vacaḥ \|*  
*pramāṇamṛṣayo hyatra brūyuste yat tathaiva tat \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Thereafter the prince Krisna, who was the best among the learned people, said to him, “This had been established by Arjuna, our father. Therefore, his adoration is the dharma for us.” With the escalation of the controversy, Surasena spoke these words, “The sages are the authority in this case. We should therefore do whatever is told by them”

## \|\| 1.22.39 \|\|

*tataste rājaśārdūlāḥ papracchurbrahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*gatvā sarve susaṃrabdhāḥ saptarṣoṇāṃ tadāśramam \|\| 39 \|\|*
