39\. Thereafter, all of them consulted the learned Rishis. Then all of them feeling enthusiastic, reached the hermitage of SaptaRishis or the seven divine sages.

## \|\| 1.22.40 \|\|

*tānabruvaṃste munayo vasiṣṭhādyā yathārthataḥ \|*  
*yā yasyābhimatā puṃsaḥ sā hi tasyaiva devatā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Vasistha and other sages enlightened them about the reality that in whomsoever deity one is inclined, the same becomes adorable for him.

## \|\| 1.22.41 \|\|

*kintu kāryaviśeṣeṇa pūjitāśceṣṭadā nṛṇām \|*  
*viśeṣāt sarvadā nāyaṃ niyamo hyanyathā nṛpāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. But if the gods are adored for a particular purpose, they surely establish the task of their devotees. Therefore, О kings, it is not the rule that after the establishment of the task, all have to adore the same deity.

## \|\| 1.22.42 \|\|

*nṛpāṇāṃ daivataṃ viṣṇustathaiva ca purandaraḥ \|*  
*viprāṇāmagnirādityo brahmā caiva pinākadhṛk \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Visnu, Shiva and Indra, all are the lords of the kings, while Agni, Aditya (sun-god), Brahma and Sankara (Pinaka-wielding deity) are the gods for the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 1.22.43 \|\|

*devānāṃ daivataṃ viṣṇurdānavānāṃ triśūlabhṛt \|*  
*gandharvāṇāṃ tathā somo yakṣāṇāmapi kathyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Visnu is the god of gods, the trident-bearing Shiva is the god for the demons, while the Soma (moon) is the god for the Yaksas and Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.22.44 \|\|

*vidyādharāṇāṃ vāgdevī sādhyānāṃ bhagavānraviḥ \|*  
*rakṣasāṃ śaṅkaro rudraḥ kiṃnarāṇāṃ ca pārvatī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Sarasvatl is the deity for the Vidyadharas, Lord Hari is meant for the siddhas, while Rudra-Shiva is the deity for the Raksasas. Parvati is the deity for the Kinnaras.

## \|\| 1.22.45 \|\|

*ṛṣīṇāṃ daivataṃ brahmā mahādevaśca śūlabhṛt \|*  
*manūnāṃ syādumā devī tathā viṣṇuḥ sabhāskaraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Brahma happens to be the deity for the Rishis, besides the trident-bearing Shiva. Visnu is the deity for the women, besides goddess Uma, Surya and Isa.

## \|\| 1.22.46 \|\|

*gṛhasthānāṃ ca sarve syurbrahmā vai brahmacāriṇām \|*  
*vaikhānasānāmarkaḥ syād yatīnāṃ ca maheśvaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. All these gods can be adored by the householders. Brahma is the god for Brahmacarins, Arka (Surya) for the

## \|\| 1.22.47 \|\|

*bhūtānāṃ bhagavān rudraḥ kūṣmāṇḍānāṃ vināyakaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ bhagavān brahmā devadevaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Vaikhanasas (recluses) while Mahes'vara is for the Sannyasins.

## \|\| 1.22.48 \|\|

*ityevaṃ bhagavān brahmā svayaṃ devo 'bhyabhāṣata \|*  
*tasmājjayadhvajo nūnaṃ viṣṇvārādhanamarhati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Rudra is the god of the goblins, while Vinayaka is the god of Kusrhandas. Prajapati Brahma happens to be the god of all.

## \|\| 1.22.49 \|\|

*kintu rudreṇa tādātmyaṃ budhvā pūjyo harirmaraḥ \|*  
*anyathā tapateḥ śatraṃ na hariḥ saṃharedyataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. This is what has been stated by Brahma himself. Thus, Jayadhvaja is surely entitled to adore lord Visnu.

## \|\| 1.22.50 \|\|

*tān praṇamyātha te jagmuḥ purīṃ paramaśobhanām \|*  
*pālayāñcakrire pṛthvīṃ jitvā sarvaripūn raṇe \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. But taking Rudra to be the same as Visnu, one should adore lord Hari. Otherwise the enemies of the kings cannot be destroyed by lord Visnu.

## \|\| 1.22.51 \|\|

*tataḥ kadācid viprendrā videho nāma dānavaḥ \|*  
*bhīṣaṇaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ purīṃ teṣāṃ samāyayau \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thereafter the kings offering their salutation to the sages, retired to the beautiful city and after conquering the enemies in the battlefield started protecting the earth.

## \|\| 1.22.52-53 \|\|

*daṃṣṭrākarālo dīptātmā yugāntadahanopamaḥ \|*  
*śūlamādāya sūryābhaṃ nādayan vai diśo daśa \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tannādaśravaṇānmartyāstatra ye nivasanti te \|*  
*tatyajurjovitaṃ tvanye dudruvurbhayavihvalāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. О Best of the Brahmanas, thereafter, once, a terrific Danava known by the name of Videha reached the city.

## \|\| 1.22.54 \|\|

*tataḥ sarve susaṃyattāḥ kārtavīryātmajāstadā \|*  
*śarasenādayaḥ pañca rājānastu mahābalāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. He was awful to look at with his fangs; his body was burning like the fire flames and appeared like the fire of the time of dissolution. His trident was dazzling like the sun and was issuing horrible sound which was spread in all the directions. All the people living there started dying listening to his thunder. Some people started fleeing out of terror.

## \|\| 1.22.55-56 \|\|

*yuyudhurdānavaṃ śaktigirikūṭāsimudgaraiḥ \|*  
*tān sarvān dānavo viprāḥ śūlena prahasanniva \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yuddhāya kṛtasaṃrambhā videhaṃ tvabhiuduvuḥ \|*  
*śūro'craṃ prāhiṇodra śūrasenastu vāruṇam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Then, the sons of Karttavlrya, the five powerful kings including Surasena and others got ready for a fight.

## \|\| 1.22.57 \|\|

*prājāpatyaṃ tathā kṛṣṇo vāyavyaṃ dhṛṣṇa eva ca \|*  
*jayadhvajaśca kauberamaindramāgneyameva ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. All of them rushed towards the Danava, carrying mountains, swords, clubs. О Best of Brahmanas, all the five kings, getting determined for a war, attacked the demon. With his trident he single-handedly fought all of them laughingly. Sura shot the the miraculous weapon of Rudra, while the missile of Vanina was shot by Surasena.

## \|\| 1.22.58-59 \|\|

*bhañjayāmāsa śūlena tānyastrāṇi sa dānavaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kṛṣṇo mahāvīryo gadāmādāya bhīṣaṇām \|\| 58 \|\|*

*spṛṣṭvā mantreṇa tarasā cikṣepa na nanāda ca \|*  
*saṃprāpya sā gādāsyoro videhasya śilopamam \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Krisna shot Prajapatya weapon, while the weapon of Vayu was shot by Dhrsna. Jayadhvaja discharged the mighty weapons of Kubera, Indra and Agni.

## \|\| 1.22.60 \|\|

*na dānavaṃ cālayituṃ śaśākāntakasaṃnibham \|*  
*dudruvuste bhayagrastā dṛṣṭvā tasyātipauruṣam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The Danava destroyed all those weapons with his trident. Thereafer, the immensely strong Krisna, picked up his horrible club and threw it against the Danava with full force. As soon as it touched him, he roared loudly. The iron club hit the chest of Videha which was like a rock.

## \|\| 1.22.61-62 \|\|

*jayadhvajastu matimān sasmāra jagataḥ patim \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ grasiṣṇuṃ lokādimaprameyamanāmayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*trātāraṃ puruṣaṃ pūrvaṃ śrīpatiṃ pītavāsasam \|*  
*tataḥ prādurabhūccakraṃ sūryāyutasamaprabham \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. The club could do no harm to the chest of the horrible Danava; witnessing the strength of the Danava, all the kings fled away in terror.

## \|\| 1.22.63 \|\|

*ādeśād vāsudevasya bhaktānugrahakāraṇāt \|*  
*jagrāha jagatāṃ yoniṃ smṛtvā nārāyaṇaṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. At that point of time, the intelligent Jayadhvaja recited the name of Visnu, the lord of the universe, who is beyond change, is protector of all, eternal Purusa, lord of Lakshmi and the one who is clad in Pltambara. Then the Sudarsana-cakra having the lustre of a million suns, appeared on the spot.

## \|\| 1.22.64-65 \|\|

*prāhiṇod vai videhāya dānavebhyo yathā hariḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya tasya ghorasya skandhadeśaṃ sudarśanam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*pṛthivyāṃ pātayāmāsa śiro 'driśikharākṛti \|*  
*tasmin hate devaripau śīrādyā bhrātaro nṛpāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. At the command of lord Vasudeva, the king Jayadhvaja held it in his hand, reciting the name of Narayana, the place of the origin of the universe.

## \|\| 1.22.66 \|\|

*taddhi cakraṃ purā viṣṇustapasārādhya śaṃkaram \|*  
*yasmādavāpa tattasmādasurāṇāṃ vināśakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The king then shot the cakra at Danava Videha, in the same way as lord Visnu, issues the same on his enemies. The cakra crossing through the shoulders of the Danava, cut off his head, which fell down on earth. At the killing of the Daitya, all the kings including the king Sura were delighted.

## \|\| 1.22.67-68 \|\|

*samāyayuḥ purīṃ ramyāṃ bhrātaraṃ cāpyapūjayan \|*  
*śrutvājagāma bhagavān jayadhvajaparākramam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*kārtavīryasutaṃ draṣṭuṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tamāgatamatho dṛṣṭvā rājā saṃbhrāntamānasaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. In earlier times, lord Visnu, performed tapas for Shiva, and received that cakra for the destruction of the Daityas and Raksasas. The cakra had been received by Visnu for the same purpose.

## \|\| 1.22.69-71 \|\|

*samāveśyāsane ramye pūjayāmāsa bhāvataḥ \|*  
*uvāca bhagavān ghoraḥ prasādād bhavato 'suraḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*nipātito mayā saṃkhye videho dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*tvadvākyācchinnasaṃdeho viṣṇuṃ satyaparākramam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*prapannaḥ śaraṇaṃ tena prasādo me kṛtaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*yakṣyāmi parameśānaṃ viṣṇuṃ padmadalekṣaṇam \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. The kings reached in the beautiful city and they adored their brother. Listening to the prowess of Jayadhvaja, lord Vis'vamitra arrived there to meet the son of Karttavlrya. On his arrival, the eyes of the king were confused a little.

## \|\| 1.22.72 \|\|

*kathaṃ kena vidhānena saṃpūjyo harirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*ko 'yaṃ nārāyaṇo devaḥ kiṃprabhāvaśca suvrata \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The king made him sit over a magnificent seat, adored him and said, “0 Lord, by your grace, the terrible demon Videha has been killed by me. My doubt has been cleared at your words. I have taken refuge with the valorous Visnu, who is quite truthful. Because of this, he has shown his grace on me. I shall adore the lotus-eyed lord Visnu.

## \|\| 1.22.73 \|\|

*sarvametanmamācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|*  
*jayadhvajasya vacanaṃ śrutvā śānto munistataḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭā harau parāṃ bhakti viśvāmitra uvāca ha\|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. You tell me, as to how lord Hari should be adored. Who is Narayanadeva and what is his influence?

## \|\| 1.22.74-75 \|\|

*viśvāmitra uvāca*  
*yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yasmin sarvamidaṃ jagat \|\| 74 \|\|*

*sa viṣṇuḥ sarvabhūtātmā tamāśritya vimucyate \|*  
*yamakṣarātparatarātyaraṃ prāhargahāśrayam \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. “You kindly enlighten me on all these points because, I am quite anxious about all of them.” Then listening to the words of Jayadhvaja, and realising about the true devotion of the king towards lord Visnu, sage Visvamitra having a peaceful mind, spoke calmly.

## \|\| 1.22.76-77 \|\|

*ānandaṃ paramaṃ vyoma sa vai nārāyaṇaḥ spṛtaḥ \|*  
*nityodito nirvikalpo nityānando nirañcanaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*catuvyahadharo viṣṇuravyūhaḥ procyate svayam \|*  
*paramātmā paraṃ dhāma paraṃ vyoma paraṃ padam \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. Vis'vamitra said, “The one from whom all the living beings emerge, and in whom all the living beings get absorbed, he is Visnu the supreme soul. One gets redeemed by taking refuge in him. He is called the knower of the tattva, undecaying Brahman, and even beyond that and is the one who resides in the cave like heart of all.

## \|\| 1.22.78 \|\|

*tripādamakṣaraṃ brahma tamāhūrbahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*sa vāsudevo viśvātmā yogātmā puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. He is the highest bliss and the form of the sky. He is also remembered as Narayana. He always appears on earth, without substitute, always blissful, spotless, possessing Caturvyuhas (four manifestations), but he himself is said to be devoid of Vyuha. Visnu is the supreme soul, the supreme abode resembling the supreme sky, and is the final place.

## \|\| 1.22.79-80 \|\|

*yasyāṃśasambhavo brahmā sdro'pi parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*svavarṇāśramadharmeṇa puṃsāṃ yaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*etāvaduktvā bhagavāna viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. The Rishis well-versed in Brahman call him as tripada or the one having three amsas, besides undecaying Brahman. He is soul of the universe, Yogatma, Purusottama and Vasudeva. Paramesvara Rudra and Brahma, were born of his aths'a. Each and every person, following the Varnasrama-dharma (caste and stage of life), shedding away the desires, should adore lord Visnu. Thus speaking the sage Vis'vamitra, getting adored from Sura and other kings left for his place.

## \|\| 1.22.81-82 \|\|

*śūrādyaiḥ pūjito viprā jagāmātha svamālayam \|*  
*atha śūrādayo devamayajanta maheśvaram \|\| 81 \|\|*

*yajñena yajñagamyaṃ taṃ niṣkāmā rudramavyayam \|*  
*tān vasiṣṭhastu bhagavān yājayāmāsa sarvavit \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. Thereafter, Sura and others started adoring Shiva-who is pleased, with the performing of yajnas. They worshipped him with the performing of the sacrifice. The yajna was presided over by lord Vasistha who was well- versed in dharma.

## \|\| 1.22.83-85 \|\|

*gautamo 'triragastyaśca sarve rudraparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitrastu bhagavān jayadhvajamarindamam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*yājayāmāsa bhūtādimādidevaṃ janārdanam \|*  
*tasya yajñe mahāyogī sākṣād devaḥ svayaṃ hariḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*āvirāsīt sa bhagavān tadadbhutamivābhavat \|\| 85 \|\|*

83-85. The performers of the yajna were Gautama, Agastya and Atri. All of them were devoted to Rudra. The yajna of Jayadhvaja was organised by the sage Visvamitra, in which the primordial god Janardana (Visnu), too was adored. In the said yajna, lord Hari himself appeared which was quite astonishing.

## \|\| 1.22.86 \|\|

*jayadhvajo'pi taṃ viṣṇu sdrasya paramāṃ tanum \|*  
*ityevaṃ sarvadā vuddhvā yalenāyajadacyutam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Tayadhvaja after realising Visnu to be the best form of Rudra, adored him making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.22.87 \|\|

*ya imaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ jayadhvajaparākramam \|*  
*sarvapāpavimuktātmā viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. A person who listens to the prowess of Jayadhvaja daily, he getting relived of all the sins, finally achieves Visnuloka.

## Chapter 23. Description of Jayadhvaja Dynasty

## \|\| 1.23.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*jayadhvajasya putro 'bhūt tālājaṅgha iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*śataputrāstu tasyāsan tālajaṅghāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Maharsi Suta said, “The king Jayadhvaja had a son who was known by the name of Talajangha, who had a hundred sons, who were known as Talajanghas.

## \|\| 1.23.2 \|\|

*teṣāṃ jyeṣṭho mahāvīryo vītihotro 'bhavannṛpaḥ \|*  
*vṛṣaprabhṛtayaścānye yādavāḥ puṇyakarmiṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Vltihotra had been the eldest of all his sons, who succeeded him as the king. AH other descendants of Yadu starting from Vrsa, were the perfonners of the noble deeds.

## \|\| 1.23.3 \|\|

*vṛṣo vaṃśakarasteṣāṃ tasya putro 'bhavanmadhuḥ \|*  
*madhoḥ putraśataṃ tvāsīd vṛṣaṇastasya vaṃśabhāk \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Vrsa was the one who expanded the dynasty. His son was known as Madhu, who also had a hundred sons. Vrsana was the one who prolonged their race.

## \|\| 1.23.4 \|\|

*vītihotrasutaścāpi viśruto 'nanta ityuta \|*  
*durjayastasya putro 'būt sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The son of Vltihotra came to be known by the name of Anata. His son Durjaya was well- versed in the scriptures and was invincible.

## \|\| 1.23.5 \|\|

*tasya bhāryā rūpavatī guṇaiḥ sarvairalaṅkṛtā \|*  
*pativratāsīt patinā svadharmaparipālikā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. His wife was extremely beautiful besides being all virtuous. She was quite chaste and devoted to her husband. She performed her dharma remaining devoted to her husband.

## \|\| 1.23.6 \|\|

*sa kadācinmahābhāgaḥ kālindītīrasaṃsthitām \|*  
*apaśyadurvaśīṃ devīṃ gāyantīṃ madhurasvanām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Once the king while seating on the banks of KalindT, spotted the beautiful damsel UrvasT, who was singing sweet songs, in tune with music.

## \|\| 1.23.7 \|\|

*tataḥ kāmāhatamanāstatsamīpamupetya vai \|*  
*provāca suciraṃ kālaṃ devi rantuṃ mayār'hasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the sight of UrvasT, the mind of the king was filled with passions. Moving close to her, the king spoke to her, “O Goddess, you are good enough to enjoy sexual pleasures with me for long.

## \|\| 1.23.8 \|\|

*sā devī nṛpatiṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpalāvaṇyasaṃyutam \|*  
*reme tena ciraṃ kālaṃ kāmadevamivāparam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The goddess UrvasT, too finding the king full of youth and beauty, resembling Kamadeva, enjoyed the sexual pleasures with him for long.

## \|\| 1.23.9 \|\|

*kālāt prabuddho rājā tāmurvaśīṃ prāha śobhanām \|*  
*gamiṣyāmi purīṃ ramyāṃ hasantī sābravīd vacaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Getting enlightened after a long time, the king then spoke to UrvasT, “I shall now move on to my beautiful city.” At this, UrvasT spoke to him smilingly.

## \|\| 1.23.10 \|\|

*na hyanenopabhogena bhavatā rājasundara \|*  
*prītiḥ saṃjāyate mahyaṃ sthātavyaṃ vatsaraṃ punaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. She said, “0 Beautiful king, I do not feel satisfied after having enjoyed the sexual pleasures with you for so long. Therefore you should stay on with me for one more year.

## \|\| 1.23.11 \|\|

*tāmabravīt sa matimān gatvā śīghrataraṃ purīm \|*  
*āgamiṣyāmi bhūyo 'tra tanme 'nujñātumarhasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the intelligent king spoke to her, “Presently I shall go to my city and shall come back again. Therefore you please permit me to go back.”

## \|\| 1.23.12 \|\|

*tamabravīt sā subhagā tathā kuru viśāṃpate \|*  
*nānyayāpsarasā tāvad rantavyaṃ bhavat punaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The excellent bodied damsel then said to the king, “O Lord of the people, you do as you like. But you should in the mean time, do not have sexual relations with any other celestial lady.”

## \|\| 1.23.13 \|\|

*omityuktvā yayau tūrṇaṃ purīṃ paramaśobhanām \|*  
*gatvā pativratāṃ patnīṃ dṛṣṭvā bīto 'bhavannṛpaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The king said, “Very well.” Thereafter he went back to his charming abode, but finding his chaste wife here, the king got extremely frightened.

## \|\| 1.23.14 \|\|

*saṃprekṣya sā guṇavatī bhāryā tasya pativratā \|*  
*bhītaṃ prasannayā prāha vācā pīnapayodharā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Looking at the frightened king, his virtuous and chaste wife having well-developed breasts, said to him with delight.

## \|\| 1.23.15 \|\|

*svāmin kimatra bhavato bhītiradya pravartate \|*  
*tad brūhi me yathā tattvaṃ na rājñāṃ kīrtaye tvidam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “O Master, why are you feeling frightened here today? Such fear is not conducive to the enhancement of your reputation as a king. You better tell me correctly.”

## \|\| 1.23.16 \|\|

*sa tasyā vākyamākarṇya lajjāvanatacetanaḥ \|*  
*novāca kiñcinnṛpatirjñānadṛṣṭyā viveda sā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Listening to the words of his wife, the king was overwhelmed with shame in his mind. He gave no reply. But still the chaste queen, could know the truth by her yogic powers, the factual position.

## \|\| 1.23.17 \|\|

*na bhetavyaṃ tvayā svāmin kāryaṃ pāpaviśodhanam \|*  
*bhīte tvayi mahārāja rāṣṭraṃ te nāśameṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then the wife spoke to her husband, “0 King, you should not be afraid at all. Whatever sin has been committed by you, a repentance should be performed for the same. 0 King by your so remaining frightened, your entire nation shall get destroyed.

## \|\| 1.23.18 \|\|

*tadā sa rājā dyutimān nirgatya tu purāt tataḥ \|*  
*gatvā kaṇvāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra mahāmunim \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thereafter, that brilliant king getting out of his abode, went to the hermitage of the sage Kanva, where he could have an audience with the great sage.

## \|\| 1.23.19 \|\|

*niśamya kaṇvavadanāt prāyaścittavidhiṃ śubham \|*  
*jagāma himavatpṛṣṭhaṃ samuddiśya mahābalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He came to know about the way of repentance from the mouth of the sage Kanva. The valorous king then proceeded on to the ridge of the Himalaya mountain as directed.

## \|\| 1.23.20 \|\|

*so 'paśyat pathi rājendro gandharvavaramuttamam \|*  
*bhrājamānaṃ śriyā vyomni bhūṣitaṃ divyamālayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The best of the kings then came across a Gandharva on the way, who looked quite resplendent, wearing a divine garland around his neck.

## \|\| 1.23.21 \|\|

*vīkṣya mālāmamitraghnaḥ sasmārāpsarasāṃ varām \|*  
*urvaśīṃ tāṃ manaścakre tasyā eveyamarhati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The king who was the destroyer of the enemies, had enjoyed sexual pleasure with the UrvasI, wearing the same garland. The king then thought, “This garland either belongs to her or is suitable for her only.”

## \|\| 1.23.22 \|\|

*so 'tīva kāmuko rājā gandharveṇātha tena hi \|*  
*cakāra sumahad yuddhaṃ mālāmādātumudyataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The king had been quite passionate. Therefore, the king fought with Gandharva, a terrific war and became ready to snatch away the garland from him.

## \|\| 1.23.23 \|\|

*vijitya samare mālāṃ gṛhītvā durjayo dvijāḥ \|*  
*jagāma tāmapsarasaṃ kālindīṃ draṣṭumādarāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The king defeated the Gandharva in the battle ground and the invincible king snatched away the garland. Thereafter he reached the same bank of Kalindl in search of the celestial lady Urvas'I.

## \|\| 1.23.24 \|\|

*adṛṣṭvāpsarasaṃ tatra kāmabāṇābhipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*babhrāma sakalāṃ pṛthvīṃ saptadvīpasamanvitām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He could not find the Apsara there. He became extremely passionate and started roaming about on earth in the seven continents.

## \|\| 1.23.25 \|\|

*ākramya himavatpārśvamurvaśīdarśanotsukaḥ \|*  
*jagāma śailapravaraṃ hemakūṭamiti śrutam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Feeling anxious for finding Urvas'I, he went to the ridges of the Himalayas and scaled Hemakuta. This has been heard.

## \|\| 1.23.26 \|\|

*tatra tatrāpsarovaryā dṛṣṭvā taṃ siṃhavikramam \|*  
*kāmaṃ saṃdadhire ghoraṃ bhūṣitaṃ citramālayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The best of the apsaras dwelling in those places, finding the king having been adorned with the divine garland, took him to be the god of love.

## \|\| 1.23.27 \|\|

*saṃsmarannurvaśīvākyaṃ tasyāṃ saṃsaktamānasaḥ \|*  
*na paśyati smatāḥ sarvāgiriśṛṅgāṇijagmivān \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The king having been reminded of the words of UrvasI, did not care for these apsaras. And he climbed the peaks of the mountain.

## \|\| 1.23.28 \|\|

*tatrāpyapsarasaṃ divyāmadṛṣṭvā kāmapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*devalokaṃ mahāmeruṃ yayau devaparākramaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Being unable to find the celestial damsel there, the passionate king, then reached the great Meru, the region of the Devas.

## \|\| 1.23.29-30 \|\|

*sa tatra mānasaṃ nāma sarastrailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*bheje śṛṅgāṇyatikramya svabāhubalabhāvitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sa tasya tīre subhagāṃ carantīmatilālasām \|*  
*dṛṣṭavānanavadyāṅgīṃ tasyai mālāṃ dadau punaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The king who was respected because of the strength of his arms, reached the lake Manasa, which is famous in the three worlds. There he found Urvas'I the virtuous one, full of passion, and having spotless limbs. The king them handed over the garland to her.

## \|\| 1.23.31 \|\|

*sa mālayā tadā devīṃ bhūṣitāṃ prekṣya mohitaḥ \|*  
*reme kṛtārthamātmānaṃ jānānaḥ suciraṃ tayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. At that point of time, the king finding the apsara UrvasI with the divine garland, was filled with passions and treating himself to be successful, enjoyed sexual pleasures with her for a long time.

## \|\| 1.23.32 \|\|

*athorvaśī rājavaryaṃ ratānte vākyamabravīt \|*  
*kiṃ kṛtaṃ bhavatā pūrvaṃ purīṃ gatvā vṛthā nṛpa \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. At the end of the sexual exercises, Urvas'I, spoke to the excellent king, “What did you do after your return to your city?”

## \|\| 1.23.33-34 \|\|

*sa tasyai sarvamācaṣṭa patnyā yat samudīritam \|*  
*kaṇvasya darśanaṃ caiva mālāpaharaṇaṃ tathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śrutvaitad vyāhṛtaṃ tena gacchetyāha hitaiṣiṇī \|*  
*śāpaṃ dāsyati te kaṇvo mamāpi bhavataḥ priyā \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. At these words of Urvas'I, the king repeated the words spoken to him by his wife. He also narrated to her, about his visit to the sage Kanva and his acquiring the garland from a Gandharva. Listening to the words of the king, then UrvasI, who wished welfare of the king, said to him, “You should go back, because the sage Kanva shall otherwise pronounce a curse on you, and your wife will curse myself.”

## \|\| 1.23.35 \|\|

*tayāsakṛnmahārājaḥ prokto 'pi madamohitaḥ \|*  
*na tatyajātha tatpārśvaṃ tatra saṃnyastamānasaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. When she so repeatedly insisted, the passionate king refused to act according to her words because his mind was completely attached to her.

## \|\| 1.23.36 \|\|

*tatorvaśī kāmarūpā rājñe svaṃ rūpamutkaṭam \|*  
*suromaśaṃ piṅgalākṣaṃ darśayāmāsa sarvadā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then UrvasI, who could take to any form at will, displayed her hideous form to the king, having thick hair over the body, and the tawny coloured eyes.

## \|\| 1.23.37 \|\|

*tasyāṃ viraktacetaskaḥ smṛtvā kaṇvābhibhāṣitam \|*  
*dhiṅmāmiti viniścityatapaḥ kartuṃ samārabhat \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Witnessing such a ugly form, the king felt detached from her, and recalling the words of the sage Kanva, he felt “Disgrace to me.” He then decided and started performing penance.

## \|\| 1.23.38 \|\|

*saṃvatsaradvādaśakaṃ kandamūlaphalāśanaḥ \|*  
*bhūya eva dvādaśakaṃ vāyubhakṣo 'bhavannṛpaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He lived on the forest roots and fruits for twelve years. Thereafter, he lived for a further period of twelve years on the air alone.

## \|\| 1.23.39 \|\|

*gatvā kaṇvāśramaṃ bhītyā tasmai sarvaṃ nyavedayat \|*  
*vāsamapsarasā bhūyastapoyogamanuttamam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Thereafter the king went to the hennitage of the sage Kanva, narrated the entire story of his tapas including his enjoying of the sexual pleasure with the apsara.

## \|\| 1.23.40 \|\|

*vīkṣya taṃ rājaśārdūlaṃ prasanno bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*kartukāmo hi nirbojaṃ tasyāghamidamabravīt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The great sage felt delighted at the sight of the great king, then with the idea of removing all his sins, he spoke to the king.

## \|\| 1.23.41 \|\|

*gaccha vārāṇasīṃ divyāmīśvarādhyuṣitāṃ purīm \|*  
*āste mocayituṃ lokaṃ tatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Kanva said, “O King, you go to Varanasi, which is quite divine and is the living place for Ishvara (Shiva). Lord Mahesvara lives there in order to relieve all the people of their sins.

## \|\| 1.23.42 \|\|

*snātvā saṃtarpya vidhivad gaṅgāyāndevatāḥ pitṝn \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā viśveśvaraṃ liṅgaṅkilbiṣānmokṣyase 'khilāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Taking a bath in the Gariga appropriately, offering oblation to the gods and the Pitrs, and having an audience with the Linga of Visvesvara (lord Shiva) there, you shall be relieved of all the sins in a moment.

## \|\| 1.23.43 \|\|

*praṇamya śirasā kaṇvamanujñāpya ca durjayaḥ \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ haraṃ dṛṣṭvā pāpānmukto 'bhavat tataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then the invincible king, bowing in reverence to the sage Kanva, seeked his permission and proceeded on to Varanasi. By having a sight of lord Нага, there, he was relieved of all his sins.

## \|\| 1.23.44 \|\|

*jagāma svapurīṃ śubhrāṃ pālayāmāsa medinīm \|*  
*yājayāmāsa taṃ kaṇvo yācito ghṛṇayā muniḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thereafter the king returned to his shining city and performed a sacrifice on the earth. On being requested, the sage Kanva, out of compassion, presided over the yajna.

## \|\| 1.23.45-46 \|\|

*tasya putro 'tha matimān supratīka iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*babhūva jātamātraṃ taṃ rājānamupatasthire \|\| 45 \|\|*

*urvaśyāṃ ca mahāvīryāḥ sapta devasutopamāḥ \|*  
*kanyā jagṛhire sarvā jandharvadayitā dvijāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. An intelligent son named Supratlka was born to the king. People acclaimed him as their king since his very birth. UrvasI too gave birth to seven sons who looked quite divine and were extremely valorous. О Brahmanas, all of them were married to the pleasing daughters of the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.23.47 \|\|

*eṣa va kathitaḥ samyak sahastrajita uttamaḥ \|*  
*vaṃśaḥ pāpaharo nṛṇāṃ kroṣṭorapi nibodhata \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus, I have described the race of Sahasrajit which relieves the people of all the sins. Now you listen from me, the details of the race of Krostu.

## Chapter 24. Description of the glory of Yadu Vamsa

## \|\| 1.24.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*kroṣṭoreko 'bhavat putro vṛjinīvāniti śrutiḥ \|*  
*tasya putro mahān svātiruśadgustatsuto 'bhavat \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “Vajravan was a famous son bom to Krostu. He had a son named Santi who had a son named Kus'ika.

## \|\| 1.24.2 \|\|

*uśadgorabhavat putro nāmnā citraratho balī \|*  
*atha caitrarathirloke śaśabinduriti smṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Citraratha was the valorous son of Kus'ika. The son of Citraratha was known as Sasabindu in the world.

## \|\| 1.24.3 \|\|

*tasya putraḥ pṛthuyaśā rājābhūd dharmatatparaḥ \|*  
*pṛthukarmā ca tatputrastasmāt pṛthujayo 'bhavat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Prthuyas'as was his son, who was quite a religious one. The name of his son was Prthukarman, who had a son named Prthujaya.

## \|\| 1.24.4 \|\|

*pṛthukīrtirabhūt tasmāt pṛthudānastato 'bhavat \|*  
*pṛthuśravāstasya putrastasyāsīt pṛthusattamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He had a son named PrthukTrti, who had a son named Prthudana. Prthusravas was the son of Prthudana and Prthusattama was bom as a son to the Prthusravas.

## \|\| 1.24.5 \|\|

*uśanā tasya putro 'būt siteṣustatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*tasyābhūd rukmakavacaḥ parāvṛt tasya sattamāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Prthusattama had a son named Usanas, who had a son named Satesu. Rulunakavaca was born to him as his son. His son was known as Paravrtta.

## \|\| 1.24.6 \|\|

*parāvṛtaḥ suto jajñe jyāmagho lokaviśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasmād vidarbhaḥ saṃjajñe vidarbhāt krathakaiśikau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Paravrtta had a son named Yamagha who was quite popular in the world. A son named Vidarbha was bom to him. Vidarbha had the sons named Kratha and Kausika.

## \|\| 1.24.7 \|\|

*romapādastṛtīyastu babhrustasyātmajo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*dhṛtistasyābhavat putraḥ saṃstastasyāpyabhūt sutaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Lomapada was the name of his third son. His son became the king Babhru. The name of his son was Dhrti, and Dhrti had a son named Sveta.

## \|\| 1.24.8 \|\|

*saṃstasya putro balavān nāmnā viśvasahastu saḥ \|*  
*tasya putro mahāvīryaḥ prajāvān kauśikastataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The valorous Visvasaha was the son of Sveta. His son Kaus'ika of great virility is known for his prowess.

## \|\| 1.24.9 \|\|

*abhūt tasya suto dhīmān sumantustatsuto 'nalaḥ \|*  
*kaiśikasya sutaścediścaidyāstasyābhavan sutāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The intelligent Sumanta was his son and Anala was born to him as his son. Sveni was the son of Anala, who produced many sons.

## \|\| 1.24.10 \|\|

*teṣāṃ pradhāno jyotiṣmān vapuṣmāṃstatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*vapuṣmato bṛhanmedhā śrīdevastatsuto 'bhavat \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Dyutiman was the foremost of them. Vapusman was the son of Dyutiman, while Vapusman had a son named Brhanmedhas. Srldeva happened to be his son.

## \|\| 1.24.11 \|\|

*tasya vītaratho viprā rudrabhakto mahābalaḥ \|*  
*krathasyāpyabhavat kuntī vṛṣṇī tasyābhavat sutaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О Brahmanas, the son of Srldeva was devoted to Shiva and extremely valorous, known by the name of Vltaratha. Kunti was the son of Kratha and Vrsni was born to Kunti.

## \|\| 1.24.12 \|\|

*tasmānnavaratho nāma babhūva sumahābalaḥ \|*  
*kadācinmṛgayāṃ yāto dṛṣā rākṣasamūrjajitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. An extremely valorous son named Navaratha was bom to him. Once he went out for hunting and he had an encounter with a terrific demon.

## \|\| 1.24.13 \|\|

*dudrāva mahatāviṣṭo bhayena munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*anvadhāvata saṃkaruddho rākṣasastaṃ mahābalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О Best of the sages, the king getting terrified tried to flee from the place. But the enraged and powerful demon followed him.

## \|\| 1.24.14-15 \|\|

*duryodhano 'gnisaṃkāśaḥ śūlāsaktamahākaraḥ \|*  
*rājā navaratho bhītyā nātidūrādanuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*apaśyat paramaṃ sthānaṃ sarasvatyā sugopitam \|*  
*sa tadvegena mahatā saṃprāpya matimān nṛpaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The invincible demon known as Duryodhana, looked like the burning flames, issuing lustre and holding a trident in his hand. Looking at him, the king Navaratha spotted a temple of the goddess Sarasvatl, from a distance which happened to be quite a safe place. The intelligent king reached there while running.

## \|\| 1.24.16 \|\|

*vavande śirasā dṛṣṭvā sākṣād devīṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vāgbhiriṣṭābhirbaddhāñjaliramitrajit \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There he had an audience with the goddess Sarasvatl, he bowed in reverence to her. The king, the conqueror of the enemies, offered prayer to the goddess with folded hands.

## \|\| 1.24.17 \|\|

*papāta daṇḍavad bhūmau tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*namasyāmi mahādevīṃ sākṣād devīṃ sarasvatīm \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He prostrated himself on the ground and said, “O Goddess, I take refuge with you. I offer my salutation to the goddess Sarasvatl.

## \|\| 1.24.18 \|\|

*vāgdevatāmanādyantāmīśvarīṃ brahmacāriṇīm \|*  
*namasye jagatāṃ yoniṃ yoginīṃ paramāṃ kalām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. You are the goddess of speech, beyond the beginning or the end, you are Isvau, BrahmacarinI, the place of the origin of the world, Yogini, the supreme form of death, I offer my salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.24.19 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbhamahiṣīṃ trinetrāṃ candraśekharām \|*  
*namasye paramānandāṃ citkalāṃ brahmarūpiṇīm \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. You were bom of Brahma, having three eyes, with the crescent lodged over the head. You are the form of Cit, the very embodiment of the Brahman itself.

## \|\| 1.24.20-21 \|\|

*pāhi māṃ parameśāni bhītaṃ śaraṇamāgatam \|*  
*etasminnantare kruddho rājānaṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*hantuṃ samāgataḥ sthānaṃ yatra devī sarasvatī \|*  
*samudyamya tadā śūlaṃ praveṣṭuṃ baladarpitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. О Parames'vari, you protect me, since, I am frightened and have taken refuge in you.” In the meantime, the enraged Rdksasa also arrived there for the killing of the king, in the holy shrine of Sarasvatl, filled with arrogance and holding a trident in his hand.

## \|\| 1.24.22 \|\|

*trilokamātustatsthānaṃ śaśāṅkādityasaṃnnibham \|*  
*tadantare mahad bhūtaṃ yugāntādityasannibham \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then Sarasvatl, the mother of the universe, had her abode like the sun and the moon. In the meantime, a great spirit resembling the sun at the end of Yugas, pierced the Raksasa.

## \|\| 1.24.23 \|\|

*śūlenorasi nirbhidya pātayāmāsa taṃ bhuvi \|*  
*gacchetyāha mahārāja na sthātavyaṃ tvayā punaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Не attacked at the chest of the Raksasa with his trident, felling him on the ground. Then he spoke to the king. “O King you better leave this place, because you should stay here no more.

## \|\| 1.24.24-25 \|\|

*idānīṃ nirbhayastūrṇaṃ sthāne 'smin rākṣaso hataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ praṇamya hṛṣṭātmā rājā navarathaḥ parām \|\| 24 \|\|*

*purīṃ jagāma viprendrāḥ purandarapuropamām \|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa deveśīṃ tatra bhaktisamanvitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. You should atonce become fearless. The Raksasa has been killed here.” О Best of the Brahmanas, thereafter, the king Navaratha, feeling extremely pleased, offering his salutation to the goddess, retired to his city which resembled Indrapurl. Reaching there, he consecrated the image of goddess Sarasvatl there with utmost devotion.

## \|\| 1.24.26-27 \|\|

*īje ca vividhairyajñairhemairdevīṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*tasya cāsīd daśarathaḥ putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*devyā bhakto mahātejāḥ śakunistasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*tasmāt karambhaḥ saṃbhūto devarāto 'bhavat tataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Не adored the goddess Sarasvatl, performing various yajnas, and the homas. The extremely religious Dasaratha was the son of Navaratha. He was also devoted to the goddess and was quite illustrious. Sakuni was his son, to whom a son named Karambha was bom. Devarata was the son of Karambha.

## \|\| 1.24.28 \|\|

*īje sa cāśvamedhena devakṣatraśca tatsutaḥ \|*  
*madhustasya tu dāyādastasmāt kuruvaśo 'bhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Devarata perfonned the Asvamedha sacrifice. A son named Devaksatra was born to him. Madhu was the son of Devakasatra, while Kuru was bom to Madhu.

## \|\| 1.24.29 \|\|

*putradvayamabhūt tasya sutrāmā cānureva ca \|*  
*anostu purukutso 'bhūdaṃśustasya ca rikthabhāk \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Kuru had two sons, known as Sumatra and Anu. Priyagotra was the son of Anu, and Amsu was born as son to him.

## \|\| 1.24.30 \|\|

*athāṃśoḥ sattvato nāma viṣṇubhaktaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*mahātmā dānanirato dhanurvedavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Andhaka was the glorious son of Ams'u, who was devoted to Visnu. He was a noble soul, engaged in charitable gifts and the best among those having the knowledge of archery.

## \|\| 1.24.31 \|\|

*sa nāradasya vacanād vāsudevārcanānvitam \|*  
*śāstraṃ pravartayāmāsa kuṇḍagolādibhiḥ śrutam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He remained devoted to Vasudeva, at the advice of Narada. He composed sacred scripture listened to by Kunda (son bom of an adulterous woman) and Gola (widow’s son).

## \|\| 1.24.32 \|\|

*tasya nāmnā tu vikhyātaṃ sāttvataṃ nāma śobhanam \|*  
*pravartate mahāśāstraṃ kuṇḍādīnāṃ hitāvaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Sastras well known after his name, auspicious to Satvatas and conducive to the welfare of Kunda and others has been still current.

## \|\| 1.24.33 \|\|

*sāttvatastasya putro 'bhūt sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*puṇyaśloko mahārājastena vai tatpravartitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Satvata was the son of Andhaka, who was well-versed in all the sastras. The king with the meritorious reputation, also founded the sacred lore.

## \|\| 1.24.34-35 \|\|

*sāttvataḥ sattvasaṃpannaḥ kauśalyāṃ suṣuve sutān \|*  
*andhakaṃ vai mahābhojaṃ vṛṣṇiṃ devāvṛdhaṃ nṛpam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhaṃ ca bhajamānākhyaṃ dhanurvedavidāṃ varam \|*  
*teṣāṃ devāvṛdho rājā cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Kausalya his wife, produced powerful sons known as Satvatas, endowed with Sattvaguna, and were known by the names of Andhaka, Mahabhoja, Vrsni and king Devavrdha and Bhajamana. Bhajamana was the eldest of all, who was the best in the art of archery. Out of these brothers, the king Devavrdha, performed severe tapas.

## \|\| 1.24.36 \|\|

*putraḥ sarvaguṇopeto mama bhūyāditi prabhuḥ \|*  
*tasya babhruriti khyātaḥ puṇyaśloko 'bhavannṛpaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He prayed to the lord to have a son possessing all the virtues. His son came to be known as Babhru, who possessed the auspicious glory and was the sovereign ruler over all.

## \|\| 1.24.37 \|\|

*dhārmiko rūpasaṃpannastattvajñānarataḥ sadā \|*  
*bhajamānasya sṛñjayyāṃ bhajamānā vijajñire \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Babhru was quite a religious-minded one, besides being beautiftil, and was always engaged in the knowledge of the Truth. Bhajamana produced the sons who possessed enormous riches and were known as Bhajamanas.

## \|\| 1.24.38 \|\|

*teṣāṃ pradhānau vikhyātau nimiḥ kṛkaṇa eva ca \|*  
*mahābhojakule jātā bhojā vaimārtikāstathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Two of his sons were quite prominent who were known as Nimi and Krkana. In the dynasty of Mahabhoja, Bhojas and Vaimatrkas were bom.

## \|\| 1.24.39 \|\|

*vṛṣṇeḥ sumitro balavānanamitraḥ śinastathā \|*  
*anamitrādabhūnnighno nighnasya dvau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Sumitra, Anamitra and Timi were the sons of Vrsni. Nighna was bom as son to Anamitra. Nighna had two sons.

## \|\| 1.24.40 \|\|

*prasenastu mahābhāgaḥ satrājinnāma cottamaḥ \|*  
*anamitrācchinirjajñe kaniṣṭhād vṛṣṇinandanāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One of them was highly fortunate Prasena, and the other was excellent Satrajit. Sini was the youngest son bom of Anamitra, the son of Vrsni.

## \|\| 1.24.41 \|\|

*satyavān satyasaṃpannaḥ satyakastatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*sātyakiryuyudhānastu tasyāsaṅgo 'bhavat sutaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Satyaka was the name of his son, who because of his tmthful nature was known as Satyasampanna. Yuyudhana was the son of Satyaka, while Asanga was the son of Yuyudhana.

## \|\| 1.24.42 \|\|

*kuṇistasya suto dhīmāṃstasya putro yugandharaḥ \|*  
*mādrayā vṛṣṇeḥ suto jajñe pṛśnirvai yadunandanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The intelligent Kuni was the son of Asanga. While Yugandhara was the son of Kuni. Vrsni II was bom of Madri by Yadu.

## \|\| 1.24.43 \|\|

*jajñāte tanayau pṛśneḥ śvaphalkaścitrakaśca ha \|*  
*śvaphalkaḥ kāśirājasya sutāṃ bhāryāmavindata \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Vrsni had two sons, known as Svaphalka and Citraka. Svaphalka married the daughter of the king of KasI as his wife.

## \|\| 1.24.44 \|\|

*tasyāmajanayat putramakrūraṃ nāma dhārmikam \|*  
*upamaṅgustathā maṅguranye ca bahavaḥ sutāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A religious-minded son named Akrura was bom of her. She had other sons named Upamangu, Mangu and several others.

## \|\| 1.24.45 \|\|

*akrūrasya smṛtaḥ putro devavāniti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*upadevaśca puṇyātmā tayorviśvapramāthinau \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Akrura’a son was well known as Devavan and the divine-souled Upadeva who had sons called Vis'va and Pramathin.

## \|\| 1.24.46 \|\|

*citrakasyābhavat putraḥ pṛthurvipṛthureva ca \|*  
*aśvagrīvaḥ subāhuśca supārśvakagaveṣaṇau \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The sons of Citraka were known as Prthu,Viprthu, Asvagrlva, Subahu, Sudhasvaka and Gaveksaka.

## \|\| 1.24.47 \|\|

*andhakāt kāśyaduhitā lebhe ca caturaḥ sutān \|*  
*kukuraṃ bhajamānaṃ ca śuciṃ kambalabarhiṣam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He begot of the daughter of Andhaka, four sons, viz. Kukura, Bhajamana, Samlka and Balagarvita.

## \|\| 1.24.48 \|\|

*kukurasya suto vṛṣṇirvṛṣṇestu tanayo 'bhavat \|*  
*kapotaromā vipulastasya putro vilomakaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. О Kukura’s son was Vrsni, and Kapotaroman was the son of Vrsni. Vilomaka was his son.

## \|\| 1.24.49 \|\|

*tasyāsīt tumburusakhā vidvān putro nalaḥ kila \|*  
*khyāyate tasya nāmānuranorānakadundubhiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Tama was the intelligent son of Vilomaka, who was the friend of Gandharva Tumburu. Similarly, Anakadundubhi was the son of Tama.

## \|\| 1.24.50-51 \|\|

*sa govardhanamāsādya tatāpa vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ tasmai dadau devo brahmā lokamaheśvaraḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vaṃśasya cākṣayāṃ kīrti gānayogamanuttamam \|*  
*gurorabhyadhikaṃ viprāḥ kāmarūpitvameva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Не performed great penance over the peak of the Govardhana mountain. Lord Brahma, the lord of the universe bestowed a boon on him, for the expansion of his race, glory and the best of jnartayoga. О Brahmanas, he also achieved the boon that he could have power greater than the preceptor Brhaspati, and the changing of his own form at will.

## \|\| 1.24.52-53 \|\|

*sa labdhvā varamavyagro vareṇyaṃ vṛṣavāhanam \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa gānena sthāṇuṃ tridaśapūjitam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tasya gānaratasyātha bhagavānambikāpatiḥ \|*  
*kanyāratnaṃ dadau devo durlabhaṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. After securing boon from that excellent deity, he propitiated with music unagitatedly with a composed, concentrated mind the bull-bannered deity, Lord Shiva, adored by Devas. To him who was engaged in music, Lord Shiva, the consort of Parvati, gave the jewel of a girl inaccessible even to Devas.

## \|\| 1.24.54 \|\|

*tayā sa saṅgato rājā gānayogamanuttamam \|*  
*aśikṣayadamitraghnaḥ priyāṃ tāṃ bhrāntalocanām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The king, killer of the enemies, united with her, trained his beloved wife of tremulous eye, the excellent art of music.

## \|\| 1.24.55 \|\|

*tasyāmutpādayāmāsa subhujaṃ nāma śobhanam \|*  
*rūpalāvaṇyasaṃpannāṃ hrīmatīmapi kanyakām \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In union with his wife, he produced a splendid son named Subhuja and a charming daughter known as Hrlmatl.

## \|\| 1.24.56 \|\|

*tatastaṃ jananī putraṃ bālye vayasi śobhanam \|*  
*śikṣayāmāsa vidhivad gānavidyāṃ ca kanyakām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The mother then trained her son and the daughter, during the childhood itself, the art of music and singing.

## \|\| 1.24.57 \|\|

*kṛtopanayano vedānadhītya vidhivad guroḥ \|*  
*udvavāhātmajāṃ kanyāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ tu mānasīm \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The child Subhuja, after his thread ceremony studied the Vedas appropriately from his preceptor, and married the mind-born daughter ManasI of the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.24.58 \|\|

*tasyāmutpādayāmāsa pañca putrānanuttamān \|*  
*vīṇāvādanatattvajñān gānaśāstraviśāradān \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. She produced five excellent sons from Subhuja. All of them, were well-versed in the playing of Vina, knowing all the related secrets. They were experts in the science of music.

## \|\| 1.24.59 \|\|

*putraiḥ pautraiḥ sapatnīko rājā gānaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa gānena devaṃ tripuranāśanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The king who was well-versed in the art of music, used to adore Shiva-the destroyer of Tripuras, together with his sons, wife and the grandsons.

## \|\| 1.24.60 \|\|

*hrīmatī cāpi yā kanyā śrīrivāyatalocanā \|*  
*subāhurnāma gandharvastāmādāya yayau purīm \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. A Gandharva named Subahu took Hr-Imatl who was beautiful in all limbs, with large eyes like Lakshmi, to his city,

## \|\| 1.24.61 \|\|

*tasyāmapyabhavan putrā gandharvasya sutejasaḥ \|*  
*suṣeṇavīrasugrīvasubhojanaravāhanāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. She also produced the sons of Gandharva who were quite illustrious and were known by the names of Susena, Dhlra, Sugriva, Subhoja and Naravahana.

## \|\| 1.24.62 \|\|

*athāsīdabhijit putro vīrastvānakadundubheḥ \|*  
*punarvasuścābhijitaḥ saṃbabhūvāhukaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Thereafter, Candanodakadundubhi got a son named Abhijit, who had a son named Punarvasu. He had a son named Ahuka.

## \|\| 1.24.63 \|\|

*āhukasyograsenaśca devakaśca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*devakasya sutā vīrā jajñire tridaśopamāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О Best of the Brahmanas, Ahuka had two sons, known as Ugrasena and Devaka. Out of them, Devaka produced many sons resembling the gods and were quite powerful.

## \|\| 1.24.64-67 \|\|

*devavānupadevaśca sudevo devarakṣitaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ svasāraḥ saptāsan vasudevāya tā dadau \|\| 64 \|\|*

*vṛkadevopadevā ca tathānyā devarakṣitā \|*  
*śrīdevā śāntidevā ca sahadevā sahadevā ca suvratā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*devakī cāpi tāsāṃ tu variṣṭhābhūt sumadhyamā \|*  
*agrasenasya putro 'bhūnnyagrodhaḥ kaṃsa eva ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

*subhūmī rāṣṭrapālaśca tuṣṭimāñchaṅkureva ca \|*  
*bhajamānādabūt putraḥ prakhyāto 'sau vidūrathaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

64-67. They were known by the names of Devavan, Upadeva, Sudeva, and Devaraksita. They had seven sisters, known as Dhrtadeva, Upadeva, Devaraksita, Srldeva, Santideva, Sahadeva of holy rites and Devaki. DevakI, of beautiful waist, was the best among them, who had been married to Vasudeva.1 The sons of Ugrasena were known as Nyagrodha, Karnsa, Subhumi, Rastrapala, Tustiman and Sanku. The well- known son Vidtiratha was bom of Bhajamana.

## \|\| 1.24.68 \|\|

*tasya śūraḥ śamistasmāt pratikṣatrastato 'bhavat \|*  
*svayaṃbhojastatastasmād hṛdikaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Viduratha had a son named Surasama, and his son was known as Pratiksatra. Svayambhoja was the son of Pratiksatra and Dhatrlka was his son, who could subjugate his enemies.

## \|\| 1.24.69 \|\|

*kṛtavarmātha tatputro devarastatsutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*vasudevo'tha tatputro nityaṃ dharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Krtavarma was the son of Dhatrika. Krtavarma had a son named Surasena. Vasudeva was the son of Surasena, who was engaged in religious rites.

## \|\| 1.24.70 \|\|

*vasudevāvanmahābāhurvāsudevo jagadguruḥ \|*  
*babhūva devakīputro devairabhyarthito hariḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The powerful-armed Vasudeva, the preceptor of the universe, was bom of Vasudeva. At the prayer of the gods, lord Visnu, became the son of Devaki.

## \|\| 1.24.71 \|\|

*rohiṇī ca mahābhāgā vasudevasya śobhanā \|*  
*asūta patnī saṃkarṣaṃ rāmaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ halāyudham \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The other beautiful wife of Vasudeva, known as the virtuous Rohini, produced Satikarsana, the eldest son known as Rama, the carrier of a plough as his special weapon.

## \|\| 1.24.72 \|\|

*sa eva paramātmāsau vāsudevo jaganmayaḥ \|*  
*halāyudhaḥ svayaṃ sākṣāccheṣaḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The one who has been called as Vasudeva, the son of Vasudeva, had been the lord of the universe, while Balarama, the carrier of the plough, was the incarnation of serpent Sesa.

## \|\| 1.24.73 \|\|

*bhṛguśāpacchalenaiva mānayan mānuṣīṃ tanum \|*  
*babhūta tasyāṃ devakyāṃ rohiṇyāmapi mādhavaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. In fact on the pretext of the curse of Bhrgu, Visnu accepted the human body and incarnated as Krisna from the womb of Devaki and Balarama from the womb of Rohini.

## \|\| 1.24.74 \|\|

*umādehasamudbhūtā yoganidrā ca kauśīkī \|*  
*niyogād vāsudevasya yaśodātanayā hyabhūt \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Similarly at the command of Vasudeva, KausikI, the Yogic-slumber, emerged out of the body of Uma and was bom as the daughter of Yas'oda.

## \|\| 1.24.75 \|\|

*ye cānye vasudevasya vāsudevāgrajāḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*prāgeva kaṃsastān sarvān jaghāna munipuṅgavāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. О Best of the sages, the other sons of Vasudeva and the elder brothers of Krisna, had been killed by Kamsa earlier.

## \|\| 1.24.76 \|\|

*suṣeṇaśca tathodāyī bhadraseno mahābalaḥ \|*  
*ṛjudāso bhadradāsaḥ kīrtimānapi pūrvajaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Vasudeva had also the sons named Susena, Dayin, Bhadrasena, Mahabala, Vajradambha, Bhadrasena, and adorable Klrtiman.

## \|\| 1.24.77 \|\|

*hateṣveteṣu sarveṣu rohiṇī vasudevataḥ \|*  
*asūta rāmaṃ lokeśaṃ balabhadraṃ halāyudham \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. When all of them had been killed, RohinI gave birth to Halayudha Balabhadra, the lord of the worlds.

## \|\| 1.24.78 \|\|

*jāte 'tha rāme devānāmādimātmānamacyutam \|*  
*asūta devakī kṛṣṇaṃ śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. After the birth of Balarama, Krisna, Acyuta, the first among Devas, was bom from the womb of DevakI with a Srivatsa mark over the chest.

## \|\| 1.24.79 \|\|

*revatī nāma rāmasya bhāryāsīt suguṇānvitā \|*  
*tasyāmutpādayāmāsa putrau dvau niśaṭholmukau \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The virtuous Revatl was married to Balarama, who gave birth to two sons named Nis'ita and Ulmuka.

## \|\| 1.24.80 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśastrīsahastrāṇi kṛṣṇasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*babhūvurātmajāstāsu śataśo 'tha sahastraśaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Lord Krisna, the performer of the noble tasks, had sixteen thousand wives, and hundreds and thousands of sons were bom to them.

## \|\| 1.24.81-82 \|\|

*cārudeṣṇaḥ sucāruśca cāruveṣo yaśodharaḥ \|*  
*cāruśravāścāruyaśāḥ pradyumnaḥ śaṅkha eva ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

*rukmiṇya vāsudevasyāṃ mahābalaparākramāḥ \|*  
*viśiṣṭāḥ sarvaputrāṇāṃ saṃbabhūvurim sutāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. The prominent among them were Camdesna, Sucaru, Caruvesa, Yasodhara, Camsravas, Camyasas, Pradyumna and Samba. All of them were bom from RukminI, as sons of Krisna. They were quite strong besides being foremost of all.

## \|\| 1.24.83 \|\|

*tān dṛṣṭvā tanayān vīrān raukmiṇeyāñjanārdanam \|*  
*jāmbavatyabravīt kṛṣṇaṃ bhāryā tasya śucismitā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Observing the valorous sons of Krisna from RukminI, Jambavatl of smiling face, said to Krisna.

## \|\| 1.24.84 \|\|

*mama tvaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa viśiṣṭaṃ guṇavattamam \|*  
*sureśasadṛśaṃ putraṃ dehi dānavasūdana \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. She said, “O Lotus-eyed one, О Killer of demons, you also bestow a son on me who should be excellent and resemble Indra in prowess.”

## \|\| 1.24.85 \|\|

*jātbavatyā vacaḥ śrutvā jagannāthaḥ svayaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*samārebhe tapaḥ kartuṃ taponidhirarindamaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Listening to the words of Jambavatl, Hari, the God, who subjugated his enemies, a storehouse of penance, started performing tapas himself.

## \|\| 1.24.86 \|\|

*tacchṛṇudhvaṃ muniśreṣṭhā yathāsau devakīsutaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā lebhe sutaṃ rudraṃ taptvā tīvraṃ mahat tapaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. О Rishis, then Krisna, the son of DevakI, performed severe austerities, and had an audience with Shiva, and got the son. You listen to the relevant story.

## Chapter 25. Glory of Krisna and Yaduvamsa

## \|\| 1.25.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*atha devo hṛṣīkeśo bhagavān puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*tatāpa ghoraṃ putrārthaṃ nidānaṃ tapasastapaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “Thereafter, Hrslkesa-lord Purusottama, performed a severe penance for begetting a son, though he, himself was the lord of tapas.

## \|\| 1.25.2 \|\|

*svecchayāpyavatīrṇo 'sau kṛtakṛtyo 'pi viśvadhṛk \|*  
*cacāra svātmano mūlaṃ bodhayan bhāvamaiśvaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He is the creator of the entire universe, he had incarnated on earth of his own free-will. Inspite of that, he indicating that Parames'vara was his own root, performed penance for him in the world.

## \|\| 1.25.3 \|\|

*jagāma yogibhirjuṣṭaṃ nānāpakṣisamākulam \|*  
*āśramaṃ tūpamanyorvai munīndrasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He went to the hermitage of the noble-souled sage Upamanyu for the purpose, which had a large number of birds chirping in the same, and was served by a large number of yogis.

## \|\| 1.25.4 \|\|

*tapattrirājamārūḍhaḥ suparṇamatitejasam \|*  
*śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiḥ śrīvatsakṛtalakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At that point of time he was riding over the resplendant bird king Garuda and carried a conch, cakra and iron club in his hands. The Srlvatsa mark was at his chest.

## \|\| 1.25.5 \|\|

*nānādrumalatākīrṇaṃ nānāpuṣpopaśobhitam \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāmāśramairjuṣṭaṃ vedaghoṣanināditam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The hennitage had a large number of trees and the creepers besides a number of varieties of flowers. It had several hermitages of the sages, besides the sound of the reciting of the Vedic hymns, was emerging there.

## \|\| 1.25.6 \|\|

*siṃharkṣaśarabhākīrṇaṃ śārdūlagajasaṃyutam \|*  
*vimalasvādupānīyaiḥ sarobhirupaśobhitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I was infested with bears, Sarabhas (the fabulous animal having eight feet), lions, elephants, which kept on wandering in the hermitage. It also had lakes containing pure and sweet water.

## \|\| 1.25.7-8 \|\|

*ārāmairvividhairjuṣṭaṃ devatāyatanaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*ṛṣikairṛṣiputraiśca mahāmunigaṇaistathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vedādhyayanasaṃpannaiḥ sevitaṃ cāgnihotribhiḥ \|*  
*yogibhirdhyānaniratairnāsāgragatalocanaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. There were several orchards and auspicious temples for deities in the hermitage. There were Rishis, the sons of Rishis, the great ascetics in groups, the performers of Agnihotras (fire- worship) engaged in the study of the Vedas, besides the Yogins engaged in meditation concentrating their gaze on the tips of the noses.

## \|\| 1.25.9 \|\|

*upetaṃ sarvataḥ puṇyaṃ jñānibhistattvadarśibhiḥ \|*  
*nadībhirabhito juṣṭaṃ jāpakairbrahmavādibhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It was auspicious from all the sides, and it was being served well by the wise seers having excellence in tattvas, the rivers, which surrounded it from all the sides as well as the ascetics muttering the mantras.

## \|\| 1.25.10 \|\|

*sevitaṃ tāpasaiḥ puṇyairīśārādhanatatparaiḥ \|*  
*praśāntaiḥ satyasaṃkalpairniḥ śokairnirupadravaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The hermitage was saved by the ascetics, engaged in the auspicious tapas for lord Shiva, who had been quite calm by nature, always had truthful resolve, free from agonies, and undisturbed by troubles.

## \|\| 1.25.11-12 \|\|

*bhasmāvadātasarvāṅgai rudrajāpyaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*muṇḍitairjaṭilaiḥ śuddhaistathānyaiśca śikhājaṭaiḥ \|*  
*sevitaṃ tāpasairnitya jñānibhirbrahmacāribhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tatrāśramavare ramye siddhāśramavibhūṣite \|*  
*gaṅgā bhagavatī nityaṃ vahatyevāghanāśinī \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The inmates of the asrama had applied ashes over the body, reciting the mantra of Rudra. Some of them had their heads clean shaven, while others had the matted locks of hair over the heads. The place was resorted to always by wise ascetics and expounders of the Brahman. The ds'rama was the best and quite charming and appeared more graceful because of the hermitages of the Siddha Yogins.

## \|\| 1.25.13-15 \|\|

*sa tānanviṣya viśvātmā tāpasān vītakalmaṣān \|*  
*praṇāmenātha vacasā pūjayāmāsa mādhavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*te te dṛṣṭvā jagadyoniṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam \|*  
*praṇemurbhaktisaṃyuktā yogināṃ paramaṃ gurum \|\| 14 \|\|*

*stuvanti vaidikairmantraiḥ kṛtvā hṛdi sanātanam \|*  
*procuranyonyamavyaktamādidevaṃ mahāmunim \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. The auspicious Gariga which removed the sins of the people always flowed there. Reaching there, Krisna, the soul of the universe, had an audience with the ascetics, who were devoid of all the sins. Madhava-Krisna honoured them speaking sweet words and also adored them. All the ascetics on their part, having an audience with Krisna, the holder of conch, discus and an iron club, besides being the preceptor of the yogis, offered their salutation to him. Thereafter, they began to eulogise him with the Mantras of Vedic origin, after retaining the eternal deity in the heart.

## \|\| 1.25.16 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa bhagavānekaḥ sākṣānnārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*agacchatyadhunā devaḥ purāṇapuruṣaḥ svayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. At the sight of the invisible Mahamuni Krisna, all of them conversed among themselves, “He is lord Narayana himself who is beyond the supreme being and is the cosmic witness of all.

## \|\| 1.25.17 \|\|

*ayamevāvyayaḥ straṣṭā saṃhartā caiva rakṣakaḥ \|*  
*amūrto mūrtimān bhūtvā munīn draṣṭumihāgataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The lord Krisna, inspite of his being Pradhaha Purusa has himself arrived here. He is beyond decay, the creator, the destroyer as well as the protector of all.

## \|\| 1.25.18 \|\|

*eṣa dhātā vidhātā ca samāgacchati sarvagaḥ \|*  
*anādirakṣayo 'nanto mahābhūto maheśvaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He himself is formless, but has arrived here in human form, to meet the sages. He is the creator and the dispenser of destiny. He is omnipresent and is arriving here.

## \|\| 1.25.19 \|\|

*śrutvā śrutvā haristeṣāṃ vacāṃsi vacanātigaḥ \|*  
*yayau sa tūrṇaṃ govindaḥ sthānaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He is eternal, beyond decay, beyond measure, limitless, MahabhUta (the great spirit) as well as the Mahes'vara.” Hari, Govinda, who is beyond the scope of words, heard and understood their words.

## \|\| 1.25.20 \|\|

*upaspṛśyātha bhāvena tīrthe tīrthe sa yādavaḥ \|*  
*cakāra devakīsūnurdevarṣipitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then, Govinda hurriedly reached the hermitage of Upamanyu. Madhava, belonging to the Yaduvamsa, visiting each and every tlrtha touched the water of that place.

## \|\| 1.25.21-22 \|\|

*nadīnāṃ tīrasaṃsthāni sthāpitāni munīśvaraiḥ \|*  
*liṅgāni pūjayāmāsa śaṃbhoramitatejasaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā samāyāntaṃ yatra yatra janārdanam \|*  
*pūjayāñcakrire puṣpairakṣataistatra vāsinaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Krisna, the son of DevakI, performed the holy rite of tarpana for the Gods, Sages and Pitrs. He also adored the Shivalingas of unmeasured brilliance, consecrated by the sages over the banks of the river.

## \|\| 1.25.23-24 \|\|

*samīkṣya vāsudevaṃ taṃ śārṅgaśaṅkhāsidhāriṇam \|*  
*tasthire niścalāḥ sarve śubhāṅgaṃ tannivāsinaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yāni tatrārurukṣūṇāṃ mānasāni janārdanam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā samīhitānyāsan niṣkrāmanti purāhiram \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Wherever lord Janardana went, the people of those places welcomed the lord offering him the flowers and the unbroken rice-grains. At the very sight of lord Vasudeva, the holder of the Sarnga bow, a conch and a sword, the people stood there motionless. All of them felt totally devoted to lord Krisna, with auspicious limbs.

## \|\| 1.25.25 \|\|

*athāvagāhya gaṅgāyāṃ kṛtvā devāditarpaṇam \|*  
*ādāya puṣpavaryāṇi munīndrasyāviśad gṛham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Such of the sages who were desirous of getting involved in yogic exercises, they at the sight of lord Janardana, were atonce engaged in meditation and they did not move out their limbs. Thereafter, Vasudeva, entered the holy Ganga and taking his bath, he performed oblation for the Gods, Pitrs and the Rishis. Then, carrying the best flowers in his hands, he entered the hermitage of the sage Upamanyu.

## \|\| 1.25.26-27 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā taṃ yogināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhasmoddhūlitavigraham \|*  
*jaṭācīradharaṃ śāntaṃ nanāma śirasā munim \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ālokya kṛṣṇamāyāntaṃ pūjayāmāsa tattvavit \|*  
*āsane cāsayāmāsa yogināṃ prathamātithim \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Reaching there, he had a look at the great sage, the best of the Yogins, having body besmeared with the holy ashes, wearing the matted locks of hair as well as the bark garments, and who looked peaceful. He offered his salutation to the sage lowering his head. The learned sage also finding the arrival of lord Krisna, adored him.

## \|\| 1.25.28-29 \|\|

*uvāca vacasāṃ yoniṃ jānīmaḥ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*viṣṇumavyaktasaṃsthānaṃ śiṣyabhāvena saṃsthitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*svāgataṃ te hṛṣīkeśa saphalāni tapāṃsi naḥ \|*  
*yad sākṣādeva viśvātmā madgehaṃ viṣṇurāgataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. He offered Krisna, the preceptor of the yogis, and the prominent guest, a seat and speaking like a pupil he addressed lord Visnu, saying. “I am quite well aware about you. О Hrslkesa, you are welcome here. Our penance has met with success today.

## \|\| 1.25.30-31 \|\|

*tvāṃ na paśyanti munayo yatanto 'pi hi yoginaḥ \|*  
*tādṛśasyātha bhavataḥ kimāgamanakāraṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śrutvopamanyostad vākyaṃ bhagavān keśimardanaḥ \|*  
*vyājahāra mahāyogī vacanaṃ praṇipatya tam \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Because lord Visnu has himself reached my place and You are the soul of the universe, we are glad. The people fail to have an audience with you making all the efforts. What is the cause of an adorable person to arrive here?” Listening to the words of Upamanvu the great sage, the great yogi and son of DevakI, offered his salutation to the sage and said.

## \|\| 1.25.32-33 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca*  
*bhagavan draṣṭumicchāmi girīśaṃ kṛttivāsasam \|*  
*saṃprāpto bhavataḥ sthānaṃ bhagavaddarśanotsukaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kathaṃ sa bhagavānīśo dṛśyo yogavidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*mayācireṇa kutrāhaṃ drakṣyāmi tamumāpatim \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Krisna said, “O Lord, I would like to have an audience with Krttivasa lord Shiva (wearing elephant-hide). Getting anxious to meet lord Shiva, I have arrived at your hermitage. You tell me, how could I have a meeting with lord Shiva, who is the best among those well-versed in the yogic exercises?

## \|\| 1.25.34-35 \|\|

*ityāha bhagavānukto dṛśyate parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā cogreṇa tapasā tatkuruṣveha yatnataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*iheśvaraṃ devadevaṃ munīndrā brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*dhyāyanto 'trāsate devaṃ jāpinastāpasāśca ye \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. I would like to meet the lord of Uma, without delay.” When so asked by Krisna, lord Upamanyu replied, “One can meet lord Shiva by devotion or by performing severe penance. Concentrating your mind, you perform penance here itself.

## \|\| 1.25.36 \|\|

*iha devaḥ sapatnīko bhagavān vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*krīḍate vividhairbhūtairyogibhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The best of the sages, well-versed in Brahman, meditate for Ishvara, the god of gods, here. The yogis and ascetics also adore him here.

## \|\| 1.25.37-41 \|\|

*ihāśrame purā rudrāt tapastaptvā sudāruṇam \|*  
*lebhe maheśvarād yogaṃ vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ihaiva bhagavān vyasaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā taṃ paramaṃ jñānaṃ labdhavānīśvareśvaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ihāśramavare ramye tapastaptvā kapardinaḥ \|*  
*avindat putrakān rudrāt surabhirbhaktisaṃyutā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*ihaiva devatāḥ pūrvaṃ kālād bhītā maheśvaram \|*  
*dṛṣṭavanto haraṃ śrīmannirbhayā nirvṛtiṃ yayuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ihārādhya mahādevaṃ sāvarṇistapatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*labdhavān paramaṃ yogaṃ granthakāratvamuttamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

37-41. The bull-bannered lord Shiva accompanied with his consort, the goblins and the Yogins enjoy their sports here. This is the place, where the blessed sage Vasistha, performing severe tapas, achieved Rudra and achieved the Yogic power from Mahesvara. Blessed Krisna Dvaipayana as well, had an audience with lord Shiva here and he achieved the divine knowledge. In this charming asrama, adoring lord Shiva, the sages endowed with devotion, performed penance and secured sons from Rudra having matted hair. The gods with their mind filled with devotion offer prayer to the goddess BhavanI, Mahadevi as well as Mahadeva and fearlessly achieve ecstatic pleasure.

## \|\| 1.25.42-43 \|\|

*pravartayāmāsa śubhāṃ kṛtvā vai saṃhitāṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*paurāṇikīṃ supuṇyārthāṃ sacchiṣyeṣu dvijātiṣu \|\| 42 \|\|*

*ihaiva saṃhitāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāpeyaḥ śāṃśapāyanaḥ \|*  
*mahādevaṃ cakāremāṃ paurāṇīṃ tanniyogataḥ \|*  
*dvādaśaiva sahastrāṇi ślokānāṃ puruṣottama \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. It is here, that Savarni, the best of the ascetics, adoring Mahadeva, had achieved the best of yoga, besides the proficiency in the composing of the splendid Saruhita of Puranas for the good people. The same Savarni, again, had modified the Puranic Samhitas for the good and welfare of the people. It was here that Kama saw Mahadeva and composed the Saruhita of Sasipayins based on Puranas at his behest. It contained twelve thousand verses. The Purana named Vayavlyottara, acceptable to the Vedas, a Saruhita containing sixteen thousand verses was enunciated here. This Vayavlyottara Purana is recognised by the Vedas. The best of the Brahmana disciples, mercifully, popularized this Samhita, which was composed by Vaisampayana.

## \|\| 1.25.44 \|\|

*iha pravartitā puṇyā dvyaṣṭasāhastrikottarā \|*  
*vāyavīyottaraṃ nāma purāṇaṃ vedasaṃmitam \|*  
*ihaiva khyāpitaṃ śiṣyaiḥ śāṃśapāyanabhāṣitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. This is the same place where the sage Yajnavalkya perfomring the severe tapas, had an audience with Shiva and by his grace composed the excellent Yogas'astra.

## \|\| 1.25.45 \|\|

*yājñavalkyo mahāyogī dṛṣṭvātra tapasā haram \|*  
*cakāra tanniyogena yogaśāstramanuttamam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In earlier times, the sage Bhrgu, performing hard tapas, had achieved a son named Sukra who was well versed in the Yoga, by the grace of Shiva.

## \|\| 1.25.46 \|\|

*ihaiva bhṛguṇā pūrvaṃ taptvā vai paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*śukro maheśvarāt putro labdho yogavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Therefore, О Lord of gods, you also perform the severe tapas here and should have an audience with lord Shiva, the wearer of the matted locks of hair who is known as the lord of the universe.”

## \|\| 1.25.47-48 \|\|

*tasmādihaiva deveśaṃ tapastaptvā maheśvaram \|*  
*draṣṭumarhasi viśveśamugraṃ bhīmaṃ kapardinam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*evamuktvā dadau jñānamupamanyurmahāmuniḥ \|*  
*vrataṃ pāśupataṃ yogaṃ kṛṣṇāyākliṣṭakarmaṇe \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Thus the sage Upamanyu granted the perfect knowledge, the holy rite pertaining to Pas'upata doctrine and its Yogic practice to Krisna of indefatigable activity.

## \|\| 1.25.48 \|\|

*evamuktvā dadau jñānamupamanyurmahāmuniḥ \|*  
*vrataṃ pāśupataṃ yogaṃ kṛṣṇāyākliṣṭakarmaṇe \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Similarly at the advice of the sage, lord Madhusudana Krisna, started performing tapas for lord Shiva.

## \|\| 1.25.49 \|\|

*sa tena munivaryeṇa vyāhṛto madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*tatraiva tapasā devaṃ rudramārādhayat prabhuḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Vasudeva then applied ashes all over his body, getting his head shaved, clad in the bark garments, devoting his mind in Shiva, continued to perform the Japa of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.25.50 \|\|

*bhasmauddhūlitasarvāṅgo muṇḍo valkalasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*jajāpa rudramaniśaṃ śivaikāhitamānasaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After the lapse of a considerable time, lord Shiva accompanied by Uma, and adorned with the crescent moon, was spotted by Krisna in the sky.

## \|\| 1.25.51 \|\|

*tato bahutithe kāle somaḥ somārdhabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*adṛśyata mahādevo vyomni devyā maheśvaraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He was adorned with the kirlta crown, carrying a club, wearing a wonderful garland of variegated colours and was holding Pinaka bow, as well as the trident. Such a Mahadeva, accompanied with Parvati, the great goddess, was spotted by Krisna. He was clad in the tiger skin.

## \|\| 1.25.52 \|\|

*kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ citramālaṃ*  
*pinākinaṃ śūlinaṃ devadevam \|*  
*śārdūlacarmāmbarasaṃvṛtāṅgaṃ*  
*devyā mahādevamasau dadarśa \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Vasudeva found before him the ancient purusa, the lord of the vital airs, eternal, the great Yogi, Is'vara, smaller than the smallest, and extremely powerful Shiva.

## \|\| 1.25.53 \|\|

*paraśvadhāsaktakaraṃ trinetraṃ*  
*nṛsiṃhacarmāvṛtasarvagātram \|*  
*samudgirantaṃ praṇavaṃ bṛhantaṃ*  
*sahastrasūryapratimaṃ dadarśa \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He held a battle axe in his hand, and had three eyes. His body was plastered with the ashes and he wore the tiger skin. He was uttering Pranava OM from his mouth. He possessed the lustre of a thousand suns. Lord Shiva appeared in this form.

## \|\| 1.25.54 \|\|

*prabhuṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ purastāt*  
*sanātanaṃ yoginamīśitāram \|*  
*aṇoraṇīyāṃsamanantaśaktiṃ*  
*prāṇeśvaraṃ śaṃbhumasau dadarśa \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. His gloiy is beyond the description of the gods, Brahma, Indra, Agni, Varuna and even Mrtyu (the god of Death). Such a type of Rudra was found by Krisna before him.

## \|\| 1.25.55 \|\|

*na yasya devā na pitāmaho 'pi*  
*nendro na cāgnirvaruṇo na mṛtyuḥ \|*  
*prabhāvamadyāpi vadanti rudraṃ*  
*tamādidevaṃ purato dadarśa \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He found on the left of Girisa his self, the unmanifest form of infinite, who was praising the lord variously with various words and who was holding conch, sword and discus in the form of Adi-purusa.

## \|\| 1.25.56 \|\|

*tadānvapaśyad giriśasya vāme*  
*svātmānamavyaktamanantarūpam \|*  
*stuvantamīśaṃ bahubhirvacobhiḥ*  
*śaṅkhāsicakrārpitahastamādyam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. He found lord Brahma, the grandsire of the universe, mounted over the swan, being the preceptor of the world, standing to the right side, who stood in the sky in human form and was adoring Shiva with folded hands.

## \|\| 1.25.57 \|\|

*kṛtāñjaliṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sureśaṃ*  
*haṃsādhirūḍhaṃ puruṣaṃ dadarśa \|*  
*stuvānamīśasya paraṃ prabhāvaṃ*  
*pitāmahaṃ lokaguruṃ divastham \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The immensely glorious Nandlsvara having the lustre of thousands of suns, besides Ganesa, the lord of the three worlds and Kumara, as refulgent as the fire, were also spotted by him.

## \|\| 1.25.58 \|\|

*gaṇeśvarānarkasahastrakalpān*  
*nandīśvarādīnamitaprabhāvān \|*  
*trilokabhartuḥ purato 'nvapaśyat*  
*kumāramagnipatimaṃ saśākham \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The sages like Marichi, Atri, Pulaha, Pulaslya, Pracetas, Daksa, Kanva, Paras'ara, Vasistha and Svayambhuva Manu were also seen by him.

## \|\| 1.25.59 \|\|

*marīcimatriṃ pulahaṃ pulastyaṃ*  
*pracetasaṃ dakṣamathāpi kaṇvam \|*  
*parāśaraṃ tatparato vasiṣṭhaṃ*  
*svāyaṃbhuvaṃ cāpi manuṃ dadarśa \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Then contemplating over the universal Atman within his self, the large-hearted and wise Visnu, offered his salutation to the Goddess and Girisa with folded hands. Thus thinking, he pleased the lord with prayers.

## \|\| 1.25.60 \|\|

*tuṣṭāva mantrairamarapradhānaṃ*  
*baddhāñjalirviṣṇurudārabuddhiḥ \|*  
*praṇamya devyā giriśaṃ sabhaktyā*  
*svātmanyathātmānamasau vicintya \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Krisna said, “О Eternal lord, О Sarvayoga (possessor of all Yogas), salutation to you. Brahma and other Rishis regard you as ‘AIT, i.e., embodiment of everything like sattva, rajas and tamas.

## \|\| 1.25.61 \|\|

*namo 'stu te śāśvata sarvayone*  
*brahmādhipaṃ tvāmṛṣayo vadanti \|*  
*tapaśca sattvaṃ ca rajastamaśca*  
*tvāmeva sarva pravadanti santaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. You yourself are Brahma, Hari, Rudra, Vis'vakarma, and the destroyer. You also dwell in the solar disc. You are Prana (vital breath), Agni and Indra, besides other forms. I take refuge with the same Isa.

## \|\| 1.25.62 \|\|

*tvaṃ brahmā hariratha viśvayoniragniḥ*  
*saṃhartā dinakaramaṇḍalādhivāsaḥ \|*  
*prāṇastvaṃ hutavahavāsavādibheda-*  
*satvāmekaṃ śaraṇamupaimi devamīśam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Those believing in the Sarhkhya philosophy, visualise you as nirguna (devoid of gunas). Those believing in Yoga system, say that you are Ekarupa and always adore you in their hearts. The Vedas also describe you in the form of Rudra, the praiseworthy deity; I offer my salutation to you and take refuge in you.

## \|\| 1.25.63 \|\|

*sāṃkhyāstvāṃ viguṇamathāhurekarūpaṃ*  
*yogāstvāṃ satatamupāsate hṛdistham \|*  
*vedāstvāmabhidadhatīha rudramagniṃ*  
*tvāmekaṃ śaraṇamupaimi devamīśam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. By offering a single flower or tree leaf at your foot, a person is freed from the worldly bondage. By your grace, with the mere remembering of your lotus-like feet served by Siddhas and Yogins, a person is freed from all the sins.

## \|\| 1.25.64-65 \|\|

*tvātpāde kusumamathāpi patramekaṃ*  
*dattvāsau bhavati vimuktaviśvabandhaḥ \|*  
*sarvāghaṃ praṇudati siddhayogijuṣṭaṃ*  
*smṛtvā te padayugalaṃ bhavatprasādāt \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yasyāśeṣavibhāgahīnamamalaṃ hṛdyantarāvasthitaṃ*  
*tattvaṃ jyotiranantamekamacalaṃ satyaṃ paraṃ sarvagam \|*  
*sthānaṃ prāhuranādimadhyanidhanaṃ yasmādidaṃ jāyate*  
*nityaṃ tvāmahamupaimi satyavibhavaṃviśveśvarantaṃśivam \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. Your place is spotless, without any division, is lodged in the heart, the one who is without the beginning, middle or the end. You are treated to be the origin of all. You are endless, immobile, truthful, and omnipresent; the entire world has emerged out of you. I therefore take refuge in lord Shiva who is Visvesvara.

## \|\| 1.25.66 \|\|

*oṃ namo nīlakaṇṭhāya trinetrāya ca raṃhase \|*  
*mahādevāya te nityamīśānāya namo namaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О Nllakantha (blue-throated), О trident bearer, О three-eyed and the form of Ekanta, salutation to you. I bow in reverence to Isana and Mahadeva.

## \|\| 1.25.67 \|\|

*namaḥ pinākine tubhyaṃ namo muṇḍāya daṇḍine \|*  
*namaste vajrahastāya digvastrāya kapardine \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Salutation to the holder of the bow Pinaka. Salutation to the form of munda (staff-bearer of tonsured head) and the carrier of a trident. Salutation to the holder of thunderbolt in his hand, without robes, and having the locks of hair over the head.

## \|\| 1.25.68 \|\|

*namo bhairavanādāya kālarūpāya daṃṣṭriṇe \|*  
*nāgayajñopavītāya namaste vahniretase \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. You are the creator of the Bhairva sound, the form of Kala, wearing the serpent as the sacred thread, and the form of fire, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.25.69 \|\|

*namo 'stu te girīśāya svāhākārāya te namaḥ \|*  
*namo muktāṭṭahāsāya bhīmāya ca namo namaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Salutation to the lord of the mountains. Salutation to you, О Svahakara (the consecrator by the utterance of Svaha), Salutation to you having the gigantic form and the one who indulges in the loud laughter.

## \|\| 1.25.70 \|\|

*namaste kāmanāśāya namaḥ kālapramāthine \|*  
*namo bhairavaveṣāya harāya ca niṣaṅgiṇe \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. You are the destroyer of Kamadeva and the subjugator of Kala, salutation to you. Salutation to Нага of terrible apparel, to Нага, the archer.

## \|\| 1.25.71 \|\|

*namo 'stu te tryambakāya namaste kṛttivāsase \|*  
*namo 'mbikādhipataye paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. You are having three eyes and are clad in tiger skin, salutation to you. You are the lord of the goddess Ambika, as well as the animals. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.25.72 \|\|

*namaste vyomarūpāya vyomādhipataye namaḥ \|*  
*naranārīśarīrāya sāṃkhyayogapravartine \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. You have the form of sky, also the lord of the sky, salutation to you. You have the body of a man and a woman and are the propounder of Sarhkhya and Yoga systems of philosophy. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.25.73 \|\|

*namo daivatanāthāya devānugataliṅgine \|*  
*kumāragurave tubhyaṃ devadevāya te namaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. You are the lord of Bhairavas, whose Linga is adored by the gods. You are the preceptor of Kumara Karttikeya, salutation to you. Salutation to the god of gods.

## \|\| 1.25.74 \|\|

*tamo yajñādhipataye namaste brahmacāriṇe \|*  
*mṛgavyādhāya mahate brahmādhipataye namaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. You are the lord of the yajnas and Brahmacarin, salutation to you. You are great hunter of deer, and lord of Brahma, salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.25.75 \|\|

*namo haṃsāya viśvāya mohanāya namo namaḥ \|*  
*yogine yogagamyāya yogamāyāya te namaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. You are Hamsa (the Swan), to the universe, salutation to you again and again. You are a Yogin who can be known by the yogic practices. You possess Yogamaya and as such salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.25.76 \|\|

*namaste prāṇapālāya ghaṇṭānādapriyāya ca \|*  
*kapāline namastubhyaṃ jyotiṣāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. You are protector of life, you like the sound of the bells, bearer of the skull, besides being the lord of luminaries. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.25.77 \|\|

*namo namo namastubhyaṃ bhūya eva namo namaḥ \|*  
*mahyaṃ sarvātmanā kāmān prayaccha parameśvara \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Salutation to you again and again. Salutation to you again and again. О Parames'vara, You better fulfil my wishes in a universal form.”

## \|\| 1.25.78 \|\|

*evaṃ hi bhaktyā deveśamabhiṣṭūya sa mādhavaḥ \|*  
*papāta pādayorviprā devadevyoḥ sa daṇḍavat \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Suta said, “Lord Madhava, thus offered prayer to the lord with utmost devotion and О Brahmanas, he fell at the feet of the lord and the goddess prostrate like a staff.

## \|\| 1.25.79 \|\|

*utthāpya bhagavān somaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ keśiniṣūdanam \|*  
*babhāṣe madhuraṃ vākyaṃ meghagambhīraniḥ svanaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Then lord Shiva, having the majestic voice like the rumbling sound of clouds, lifted up Krisna, the killer of Kes'in, and spoke sweet words to him.

## \|\| 1.25.80 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa tapastaptaṃ tvayāvyaya \|*  
*tvameva dātā sarveṣāṃ kāmānāṃ kāmināmiha \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Shiva said, “O Lotus-eyed one, what for are you performing the hard tapasl You yourself are the bestower of the reward of all the deeds and holy rites in this world.

## \|\| 1.25.81 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi sā paramā mūrtirmama nārāyaṇāhvayā \|*  
*nānavāptaṃ tvayā tāta vidyate puruṣottama \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. You yourself are my Narayana form. О Purusottama, without you, there could be no existence for the universe.

## \|\| 1.25.82 \|\|

*vettha nārāyaṇānantamātmānaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*mahādevaṃ mahāyogaṃ svena yogena keśava \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. О Narayana, you know the infinite Atman, the Supreme Lord, Mahadeva, the master of great Yoga, by means of your own Yoga, О Kesava.”

## \|\| 1.25.83 \|\|

*śrutvā tadvacanaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ prahasan vai vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*uvāca vīkṣya viśveśaṃ devīṃ ca himaśailajām \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Lord Krisna, listening to the words of lord Mahadeva, smilingly looking at the bull- bannered Shiva as well as Parvati-the great goddess, said to them.

## \|\| 1.25.84 \|\|

*jñātaṃ hi bhavatā sarvaṃ svena yogena śaṅkara \|*  
*icchāmyātmasamaṃ putraṃ tvadbhaktaṃ dehi śaṅkara \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. He said, “O Sankara, you have understood everything by means of your Yoga. I am desirous of a devoted son like myself. You kindly bestow the same to me.”

## \|\| 1.25.85 \|\|

*tathāstvityāha viśvātmā prahṛṣṭamanasā haraḥ \|*  
*devīmālokya girijāṃ keśavaṃ pariṣasvaje \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Thereafter Shiva, the universal soul, with a delightful heart, said, “Be it so.” Then, looking at the goddess Girija, he embraced lord Krisna.

## \|\| 1.25.86 \|\|

*tataḥ sā jagatāṃ mātā śaṅkarārdhaśarīriṇī \|*  
*vyājahāra hṛṣīkeśaṃ devī himagirīndrajā \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Then Girija, the mother of the worlds, the sharer of half the body of Shiva and the daughter of Himagiri, spoke to Krisna.

## \|\| 1.25.87 \|\|

*vatsa jāne tavānantāṃ niścalāṃ sarvadācyuta \|*  
*ananyāmīśvare bhaktimātmanyapi ca keśava \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. She said, “O Limitless one, О Infallible one, I am well aware of your utmost devotion towards Shiva as well as myself.

## \|\| 1.25.88 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi nārāyaṇaḥ sākṣāt sarvātmā puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*prārthito daivataiḥ pūrvaṃ saṃjāto daivakīsutaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. I am also aware of the fact that you are none else then Narayana yourself, besides being the universal soul and Purusottama. You were bom as the son of DevakI, as you had been entreated to do so by gods formerly.

## \|\| 1.25.89 \|\|

*paśya tvamātmanātmānamātmīyamamalaṃ padam \|*  
*nāvayorvidyate bheda evaṃ paśyanti sūrayaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. See Atman through your own Atman now. There is no difference between us. Sages consider both of us as identical.

## \|\| 1.25.90 \|\|

*imānimān varāniṣṭān matto gṛhṇīṣva keśava \|*  
*sarvajñatvaṃ tathaiśvaryaṃ jñānaṃ tat pārameśvaram \|*  
*īśvare niścalāṃ bhaktimātmanyapi paraṃ balam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Still, О Kesava, you should accept my desired boons. You receive from me the universal knowledge, fortunes, knowledge relating to Parames'vara, utmost devotion in Is'vara, and strength in your soul.”

## \|\| 1.25.91-92 \|\|

*evamuktastayā kṛṣṇo mahādevyā janārdanaḥ \|*  
*āśiṣaṃ śirasāhṛṅṇād devo 'pyāha maheśvaraḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*pragṛhya kṛṣṇaṃ bhagavānatheśaḥ*  
*kareṇa devyā saha devadevaḥ \|*
