22\. The city of Varanasi is my sacred and most secret place which makes all the living beings on earth to cross the ocean of the worldy existence.

## \|\| 1.31.23 \|\|

*tatra bhaktā mahādevi madīyaṃ vratamāsthitāḥ \|*  
*nivasanti mahātmānaḥ paraṃ niyamamāsthitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The great-souled devotees of mine who have taken to the observance of my vows and who adhere to those great observances, stay at that place.

## \|\| 1.31.24 \|\|

*uttamaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ sthānānāmuttamaṃ ca tat \|*  
*jñānānāmuttamaṃ jñānamavimuktaṃ paraṃ mama \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Varanasi happens to be my Avimukta-ksetra, is the best of all the places and the places of pilgrimage. It also possesses the best of all the knowledge.

## \|\| 1.31.25 \|\|

*sthānāntaraṃ pavitrāṇi tīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*śmaśānasaṃsthitānyeva divyabhūmigatāni ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. All the auspicious places of pilgrimage in the heaven and the earth, besides the temples in other places, are all lodged in the cremation ground here.

## \|\| 1.31.26 \|\|

*bhūrloke naiva saṃlagnamantarikṣe mamālayam \|*  
*ayuktāstanna paśyanti yuktāḥ paśyanti cetasā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I instead of having my abode in the earth, it is lodged in the space. The people who are not liberated do not perceive it. But it could be visualised by meditation.

## \|\| 1.31.27 \|\|

*śmasānametad vikhyātamavimuktamiti śrutam \|*  
*kālo bhūtvā jagadidaṃ saṃharāmyatra sundari \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О Beautiful one, this region of the cremation ground is known as Avimukta-region (not deserted by me). I, in the form of Kala, destroy the universe here.

## \|\| 1.31.28 \|\|

*devīdaṃ sarvaguhyānāṃ sthānaṃ priyatamaṃ mama \|*  
*madbhaktāstatra gacchanti māmeva praviśanti te \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О Goddess, this place is particularly dear to me of all the places. My devotees, who live here, get absorbed in me ultimately.

## \|\| 1.31.29 \|\|

*dattaṃ japtaṃ hutaṃ ceṣṭaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat \|*  
*dhyānamadhyayanaṃ jñānaṃ sarvaṃ tatrākṣayaṃ bhavet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The charities, japam, homa, yajna, tapas and the meditation performed here, besides the studies, and the knowledge gained here, becomes everlasting.

## \|\| 1.31.30 \|\|

*janmāntarasahastreṣu yatpāpaṃ pūrvasaṃcitam \|*  
*avimuktaṃ praviṣṭasya tatsarvaṃ vrajati kṣayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The sins performed in the thousands of earlier births, are washed out with the mere entry in the Avimukta region.

## \|\| 1.31.31-33 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā ye varṇasaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*striyo mlecchāśca ye cānye saṃkīrṇāḥ pāpayonayaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*koṭāḥ pipīlikāścaiva ye cānye mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*kālena nidhanaṃ prāptā avimukte varānane \|\| 32 \|\|*

*candrārdhamaulayastryakṣā mahāvṛṣabhavāhanāḥ \|*  
*śive mama pure devi jāyante tatra mānavāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. О Beautiful one, irrespective of one being a Brahmana, Ksatriya, Vaisya, Sudra, or a person of mixed breed, women, Mlecchas, and persons of degraded castes, insects, flies, animals, birds, whosoever meets his death in this region, О Goddess, О Shiva, all of them get absorbed in lord Shiva, having a crescent moon over his head, having three eyes, with the great Nandi-bull as his vehicle. They are then reborn as human beings in my loka.

## \|\| 1.31.34 \|\|

*nāvimukte mṛtaḥ kaścinnarakaṃ yāti kilbiṣī \|*  
*īśvarānugṛhītā hi sarve yānti parāṃ gatim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Even a great sinner, meeting with his death in the Avimukta ksetra, never falls in the hell. All of them getting indebted to Is'vara, achieve the best of positions.

## \|\| 1.31.35 \|\|

*mokṣaṃ sudurlabhaṃ matvā saṃsāraṃ cātibhīṣaṇam \|*  
*aśmanā caraṇau hatvā vārāṇasyāṃ vasennaraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Realising that salvation to be extremely difficult to achieve, and treating the world to be extremely terrific, one should strike his feet with stone and stay on in Kas'I.

## \|\| 1.31.36 \|\|

*durlabhā tapasā cāpi pūtasya parameśvari \|*  
*yatra tatra vipannasya gatiḥ saṃsāramokṣaṇī \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. О Paramesvarl, it is difficult for a person to perform the penance here, but whenever one dies in Kas'I, he achieves salvation.

## \|\| 1.31.37 \|\|

*prasādājjāyate hyetanmama śailendranandini \|*  
*aprabuddhā na paśyanti mama māyāvimohitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. О Daughter of the mountain, the person who dies in Varanasi, all his sins are burnt out due to my grace. The ignorant people getting deluded with my illusion, are unable to see this place.

## \|\| 1.31.38 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ na sevanti mūḍhā ye tamasāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*viṇmūtraretasāṃ madhye te vasanti punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. An ignorant person, overpowered with the darkness do not perceive Avimukta. He enters in the midst of faeces, urine and semen again and again.

## \|\| 1.31.39-40 \|\|

*hanyamāno 'pi yo vidvān vased vighnaśatairapi \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati \|\| 39 \|\|*

*janmamṛtyujarāmuktaṃ paraṃ yāti śivālayam \|*  
*apunarmaraṇānāṃ hi sā gatirmokṣakāṅkṣiṇām \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. O Goddess, when a person badly suffering from various obstructions, reaches KasI, he achieves the supreme position, and reaching that place, he is relieved of all the gloom. He is freed from birth, old age, death and achieves the best place of Shiva. The people desirous of moksa and are not interested in re-birth, they achieve the supreme position.s

## \|\| 1.31.41-43 \|\|

*yāṃ prāpya kṛtakṛtyaḥ syāditi manyanti paṇḍatāḥ \|*  
*na dānairna tapobhiśca na yajñairnāpi vidyayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*prāpyate gatirutkṛṣṭā yāvimukte tu labhyate \|*  
*nānāvarṇā vivarṇāśca caṇḍālādyā jugupsitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kilbiṣaiḥ pūrṇadehā ye viśiṣṭaiḥ pātakaistathā \|*  
*bheṣajaṃ paramaṃ teṣāmavimuktaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. A person by achieving Kas'I, feels successful, this is what the learned people believes. Such a best position cannot be achieved by performing charities, tapas, yajnas or even by means of knowledge, as compared to the one achieved by the death in the Avimukta region. The Avimukta region serves as the divine penacea for the people of different castes, the hated ones, the Candalas and others, those who are full of serious and intense sins. This is what the learned people speak.

## \|\| 1.31.44-45 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ paraṃ jñānamavimuktaṃ paraṃ padam \|*  
*avimuktaṃ paraṃ tattvamavimuktaṃ paraṃ śivam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kṛtvā vai naiṣṭhikīṃ dīkṣāmavimukte vasanti ye \|*  
*teṣāṃ tatparamaṃ jñānaṃ dadāmyante paraṃ padam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. The Avimukta-ksetra is the region of supreme knowledge, the greatest principle, the greatest region, and the form of supreme bliss. The people, who receiving dlkm, live in KasI, with utmost devotion, they ultimately achieve the supreme knowledge, and the supreme position.

## \|\| 1.31.46-50 \|\|

*prāyāgaṃ naimiṣaṃ puṇyaṃ śrīśailo 'tha mahālayaḥ \|*  
*kedāraṃ bhadrakarṇaṃ ca gayā puṣkarameva ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śāligrāmaṃ ca kubjāmraṃ kokāmukhamanuttamam \|*  
*prabhāsaṃ vijayeśānaṃ gokarṇaṃ bhadrakarṇakam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*prabhāsaṃ vijayeśānaṃ gokarṇaṃ bhadrakarṇakam \|*  
*etāni puṇyasthānāni trailokye viśrutāni ha \|\| 48 \|\|*

*na yāsyanti paraṃ mokṣaṃ vārāṇasyāṃ yathā mṛtāḥ \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ viśeṣeṇa gaṅgā tripathagāminī \|\| 49 \|\|*

*praviṣṭā nāśayet pāpaṃ janmāntaraśataiḥ kṛtam \|*  
*anyatra sulabhā gaṅgā śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ tapo japaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

46-50. The auspicious places of pilgrimage known as Prayaga,1 the sacred Naimisaranya, Srls'aila, Himalaya, Kedara, Bhadrakarna, Gaya, Puskara, Kuruksetra, Rudrakoti, Narmada, Hatakesvara, Saligrama, Puspagra, Varhsa, Kokamukha, Prabhasa, Vijayes'ana, Gokarna, and Sahkukarna, are well known in the three worlds. But the way, one achieves salvation after his death in Varanasi, is not found elsewhere. The three way moving Ganga, while entering KasI, destroys the sins of a person, committed during the past hundred years or so.

## \|\| 1.31.51-52 \|\|

*vratāni sarvamevaitad vārāṇasyāṃ sudurlabham \|*  
*yajeta juhuyānnityaṃ dadātyarcayate 'marān \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vāyubhakṣaśca satataṃ vārāṇasyāṃ stito naraḥ \|*  
*yadi pāpo yadi śaṭho yadi vādhārmiko naraḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. The bath in the Ganga, performing of Sraddha, charities, Japam and other religious rites can be had elsewhere as weli, but the results of performing of these activities in Varanasi are difficult to be achieved elsewhere. One should always perform Yajna and Нота in Varanasi everyday, offer charitable gifts, besides adoring the other gods. A person who lives in Varanasi inhailing air alone, even if he is a degraded one, sinful, wicked and irreligious, still, he reaching Varanasi, purifies his three generations.

## \|\| 1.31.53 \|\|

*vārāṇasīṃ samāsādya punāti sakalaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevaṃ yer'cayanti stuvanti vai \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The people who adore and praise Mahadeva in Varanasi, they getting relieved of all the sins, become Ganesvaras of Shiva. It should be known accordingly.

## \|\| 1.31.54-56 \|\|

*sarvapāpavinirmuktāste vijñeyā gaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*anyatra yogajñānābhyāṃ saṃnyāsādathavānyataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*prāpyate tat paraṃ sthānaṃ sahastreṇaiva janmanā \|*  
*ye bhaktā devadeveśe vārāṇasyāṃ vasanti vai \|\| 55 \|\|*

*te vindanti paraṃ mokṣamekenaiva tu janmanā \|*  
*yatra yogastathā jñānaṃ muktirekena janmanā \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. At other holy centres, the greatest abode (Moksa) could be achieved through Yoga or knowledge or renunciation in a thousand births, but by adoring Vis'ves'vara Shiva with devotion at Varanasi, by the devotees there, they achieve the same in a single birth alone. One need not go to any other penance grove after reaching Avimukta where Yoga, perfect knowledge and salvation, are acquired in a single birth.

## \|\| 1.31.57-58 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ samāsādya nānyad gacchet tapovanam \|*  
*yato mayā na muktaṃ tadavimuktaṃ tataḥ smṛtam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tadeva guhyaṃ guhyānāmetad vijñāya mucyate \|*  
*jñānājñānābhiniṣṭhānāṃ paramānandamicchatām \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. This region is secret of all the secrets, and realising this, a person achieves moksa. О lady of fine eyebrows, the blissful position which is achieved by the people engaged in prana- dhyana, the same position is achieved by a person, who dies in Avimukta-ksetra.

## \|\| 1.31.59-63 \|\|

*yā gatirvihitā subhru sāvimukte mṛtasya tu \|*  
*yāni caivāvimuktasya dehe tūktāni kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*purī vārāṇasī tebhyaḥ sthānebhyo hyadhikāśubhā \|*  
*yatra sākṣānmahādevo dehānte svayamīśvaraḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*vyācaṣṭe tārakaṃ brahma tatraiva hyavimuktakam \|*  
*yat tat parataraṃ tattvamavimuktamiti śrutam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*ekena janmanā devi vārāṇasyāṃ tadāpnuyāt \|*  
*bhrūmadhye nābhimadhye ca hṛdaye caiva mūrdhani \|\| 62 \|\|*

*yathāvimuktāditye vārāṇasyāṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*varaṇāyāstathā cāsyā madhye vārāṇasī purī \|\| 63 \|\|*

59-63. The Avimukta regions which have been spelt out by the gods, Varanasi happens to be the best and more rewarding as compared to all of them besides being auspicious. Lord Ishvara, himself, explains the Tamkabrahman (i.e. Brahman that enables one to cross the ocean of worldy existence). О Goddess, that great principle which is greater than the greatest, is obtained in a single birth at Varanasi. The Avimukta lodged in Aditya lokas between the two eyebrows, inside the navel, in the heart, over the forehead, similarly, the same is lodged in Varanasi as well. This city is lodged between the rivers Varana and Asi, earning the name of Varanasi.

## \|\| 1.31.64-65 \|\|

*tatraiva saṃsthitaṃ tattvaṃ nityamevāvimuktakam \|*  
*vārāṇasyāḥ paraṃ sthānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yatra nārāyaṇo devo mahādevo diveśvaraḥ \|*  
*tatra devāḥ sagandharvāḥ sayakṣoragarākṣasāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. The supreme tattva of Avimukta is pennanently located in Varanasi. Therefore, there had been no other place better on earth, as compared to Varanasi in the past, nor shall it be there in future. Like Narayana, Mahadeva and Sun-god abide there, so do other gods along with Gandharvas, Yaksas, serpents and Raksasas. God Brahma, the grand-sire of the world and the god of gods always propitiates me there.

## \|\| 1.31.66-67 \|\|

*upāsate māṃ satataṃ devadevaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*mahāpātakino ye ca ye tebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*vārāṇasīṃ samāsādya te yānti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*tasmānmumukṣurniyato vased vai maraṇāntikam \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. The people who commit sins much more than the great sinners, they get redeemed by reaching Varanasi. Therefore, he who seeks liberation should invariably reside in Varanasi till death, О Mahadevl.

## \|\| 1.31.68 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ mahādevājjñānaṃ labdhvā vimucyate \|*  
*kintu vighnā bhaviṣyanti pāpopahatacetasaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. О Great Goddess achieving perfect knowledge at Varanasi, one gets liberated. But those whose minds are overpowered with sins, they will have to face difficulties.

## \|\| 1.31.69 \|\|

*tato naiva caret pāpaṃ kāyena manasā girā \|*  
*etad rahasyaṃ vedānāṃ purāṇānāṃ ca suvratāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. O Excellent Brahmanas, one should not indulge in sins at KasI, by action, thought, or behaviour. This is the gist of the Vedas and Puranas.

## \|\| 1.31.70-71 \|\|

*avimuktāśrayaṃ jñānaṃ na kaścid vetti tattvataḥ \|*  
*devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca śṛṇvatāṃ parameṣṭhinām \|\| 70 \|\|*

*devyai devena kathitaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*yathā nārāyaṇaḥ śreṣṭho devānāṃ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. The knowledge which is attained by staying in the Avimukta-ksetra, there is nothing better known, than this. This is what lord Shiva had told Parvati, in the presence of the great sages, Devas and Paramesthin, about the city of Varanasi, which removes all the sins.

## \|\| 1.31.72-73 \|\|

*yatheśvarāṇāṃ giriśaḥ sthānānāṃ caitaduttamam \|*  
*yaiḥ samārādhito rudraḥ pūrvasminneva janmani \|\| 72 \|\|*

*te vindanti paraṃ kṣetramavimuktaṃ śivālayam \|*  
*kalikalmaṣasaṃbhūtā yeṣāmupahatā matiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. As Narayana is the best among the gods, as Mahadeva is the best among Ishvaras, similarly, Varanasi is the best among all the sacred places. Those who have adored Rudra in the earlier birth, they achieve the best of Avimukta-ksetra, the place of Shiva. Those who have lost the wisdom because of the sins of Kaliyuga, they are unable to visit the auspicious place of Paramesthin.

## \|\| 1.31.74 \|\|

*na teṣāṃ vedituṃ śakyaṃ sthānaṃ tat parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*ye smaranti sadā kālaṃ vindanti ca purīmimām \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Those who always remember Kala (lord Shiva) and live in the city of Varanasi, they are freed from the sins of this as well the future worlds.

## \|\| 1.31.75 \|\|

*teṣāṃ vinaśyati kṣipramihāmutra ca pātakam \|*  
*yāni ceha prakurvanti pātakāni kṛtālayāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. In case, some people living in the abode of Shiva, commit sins, they are destroyed by lord Shiva, having the form of Kala.

## \|\| 1.31.76-79 \|\|

*nāśayet tāni sarvāṇi devaḥ kālatanuḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*āgacchatāmidaṃ sthānaṃ sevituṃ mokṣakāṅkṣiṇām \|\| 76 \|\|*

*mṛtānāṃ ca punarjanam na bhūyo bhavasāgare \|*  
*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena vārāṇasyāṃ vasennaraḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*yogī vāpyathavāyogī pāpī vā puṇyakṛttamaḥ \|*  
*na vedavacanāt pitrorna caiva guruvādataḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*matirutkramaṇīyā syādavimuktagatiṃ prati \|\| 79 \|\|*

76-79. The persons who arriving here for seeking moksa, but meet with their end here, then they are never reborn on earth. Therefore, making all the efforts, a person should live in KasT, irrespective of his being a Yogin or otherwise, a sinner or an auspicious soul, one should not become averse to avoiding of the benefit of living in the Avimukta-ksetra, even at the advice of the people, his parents or even the elderly persons.”

## \|\| 1.31.80 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ityevamuktvā bhagavān vyāso vedavidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*sahaiva śiṣyapravarairvārāṇasyāṃ cacāra ha \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Suta said, “After thus speaking lord Vyasa, the best among those well-versed in the Vedas, went to Varanasi along with his disciples.

## Chapter 32. The Glory of Vranasi

## \|\| 1.32.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*sa śiṣyaiḥ saṃvṛto dhīmān gururdvaipāyano muniḥ \|*  
*jagāma vipulaṃ liṅgamoṅkāraṃ muktidāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “Then Krisna Dvaipayana Vyasa, accompanied with his pupils, went to the great Omkaresvara Linga, which is the bestower of salvation.

## \|\| 1.32.2 \|\|

*tatrābhyarcya mahādevaṃ śiṣyaiḥ saha mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*provāca tasya māhātmyaṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The sage adored Mahadeva there with his disciples and then explained to them about the glory of the said Linga.

## \|\| 1.32.3 \|\|

*idaṃ tad vimalaṃ liṅgamoṅkāraṃ nāma śobhanam \|*  
*asya smaraṇamātreṇa mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He said, “This is known as Omkares'vara Linga which is spotless besides being beautiful. With the sheer memory of it, all the sins of a person are washed out.

## \|\| 1.32.4 \|\|

*etat parataraṃ jñānaṃ pañcayatanamuttamam \|*  
*sevitaṃ sūribhirnityaṃ vārāṇasyāṃ vimokṣadam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It is here that the excellent supreme knowledge of five Ayatanas (five-faced Shiva?), capable of granting absolute emancipation from world, has been always worshipped by the sages.

## \|\| 1.32.5 \|\|

*atra sākṣānmahādevaḥ pañcāyatanavigrahaḥ \|*  
*ramate bhagavān rudro jantūnāmapavargadaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It is here that lord Rudra, taking to the form of five deities (Pancayatana), bestow moksa to the people.

## \|\| 1.32.6 \|\|

*yat tat pāśupataṃ jñānaṃ pañcārthamiti śabdyate \|*  
*tadetad vimalaṃ liṅgamoṅkāre samavasthitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The knowledge pertaining to Pasupati, which has five topics or imports, the same is enshrined in the Omkaresvara linga.

## \|\| 1.32.7 \|\|

*śāntyatītā tathā śāntirvidyā caiva parā kalā \|*  
*pratiṣṭhā ca nivṛttiśca pañcārthaṃ liṅgamaiśvaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The five topics are super-quiescence, supreme peace, knowledge, stability and cessation. All these aspects are enshrined in this Linga.

## \|\| 1.32.8 \|\|

*pañcānāmapi devānāṃ brahmādīnāṃ sadāśrayam \|*  
*oṅkārabodhakaṃ liṅgaṃ pañcāyatanamucyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This Linga is the place of abode of five deities viz. Brahma and other deities (stated above), earning it the name of Pancayatana.

## \|\| 1.32.9 \|\|

*saṃsmaredaiśvaraṃ liṅgaṃ pañcāyatanamavyayam \|*  
*dehānte tatparaṃ jyotirānandaṃ viśate budhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A person who at the time of death, remembers, the Pancayatana Shivalinga, he enters into the supreme flame of bliss.

## \|\| 1.32.10 \|\|

*atra devarṣayaḥ pūrvaṃ siddhā brahmarṣayastathā \|*  
*upāsya devamīśānaṃ prāptavantaḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The divine sages, Siddhas and BrahmaRishis, by adoring the Lord Isana here had attained liberation.

## \|\| 1.32.11 \|\|

*matsyodaryāstaṭe puṇyaṃ sthānaṃ guhyatamaṃ śubham \|*  
*gocarmamātraṃ viprendrā oṅkāreśvaramuttamam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О Best of the Brahmanas, there is an extremely auspicious place, which is quite secret, at the bank of the river Matsyodarl. The best of the Omkares'vara linga of the size of the cow’s hide is installed there.

## \|\| 1.32.12-13 \|\|

*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ liṅgaḥ madhyameśvaramuttamam \|*  
*viśveśvaraṃ tathoṅkāraṃ kapardeśvarameva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*etāni guhyaliṅgāni vārāṇasyāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*na kaścidiha jānāti vinā śaṃbhoranugrahāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. О Excellent Brahmanas, the Krttivasesvaralinga, Madhyamesvara-linga, Visvesvaralinga, Omkaralinga and the excellent Kapardlsvaralinga are the Litigas which have been consecrated at the secret spots in Varanasi. No one on earth can know about them without the grace of lord Shiva, in this world.

## \|\| 1.32.14 \|\|

*evamuktvā yayau kṛṣṇaḥ pārāśaryo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ liṅgaṃ draṣṭuṃ devasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the great sage, Krisnadvaipayana, the son of Paras'ara, went to see the Krttivcisesvara Linga of the trident-bearer Mahadeva.

## \|\| 1.32.15 \|\|

*samabhyarcya tathā śiṣyairmāhātmyaṃ kṛttivāsasaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmāsa śiṣyebhyo bhagavān brahmavittamaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then the sage, adoring the Linga with his disciples, highlighted about the glory to the Brahmanas, of the Krttivasesvaralinga.

## \|\| 1.32.16 \|\|

*asmin sthāne purā daityo hastī bhūtvā bhavāntikam \|*  
*brāhmaṇān hantumāyāto ye 'tra nityamupāsate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He said, “In earlier times, a demon had arrived in the form of a wild elephant for the killing of the Brahmanas, who had been adoring Bhava (Shiva) always.

## \|\| 1.32.17 \|\|

*teṣāṃ liṅgānmahādevaḥ prādurāsīt trilocanaḥ \|*  
*rakṣaṇārthaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhā bhaktānāṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О Best of the Brahmanas, then for the protection of his devotees, the three-eyed lord Shiva emerged out of that Linga.

## \|\| 1.32.18 \|\|

*hatvā gajākṛtiṃ daityaṃ śūlenāvajñayā haraḥ \|*  
*vasastasyākarot kṛttiṃ kṛttivāseśvarastataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Lord Shiva, striking with his trident, killed the demon in an elephant form, and used the elephant hide as his garment. Since that day he came to be known as Krttivases'vara.

## \|\| 1.32.19 \|\|

*atra siddhiṃ parāṃ prāptā munayo munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*tenaiva ca śarīreṇa prāptāstat paramaṃ padam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О Excellent Sages, the ascetics had achieved the excellent Siddhis here and also achieved the liberation with the same body.

## \|\| 1.32.20 \|\|

*vidyā vidyeśvarā rudrāḥ śivāye ca prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*kṛttivāseśvaraṃ liṅgaṃ nityamāvṛtya saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Those who are glorified as Vidya, Vidyesvaras, Rudras and Shivas surround the Krttivasesvaralinga forever, and are established here.

## \|\| 1.32.21 \|\|

*jñātvā kaliyugaṃ ghoramadharmabahulaṃ janāḥ \|*  
*kṛttivāsaṃ na muñcanti kṛtārthāste na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A person who considering the Kaliyuga as full of Adharma, do not discard the Krttivasa- linga, they are successful in their lives. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.32.22 \|\|

*janmāntarasahastreṇa mokṣo 'nyatrāpyate na vā \|*  
*ekena janmanā mokṣaḥ kṛttivāse tu labhyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Elsewhere, whether a person might not achieve liberation by having births for thousands of times, but during a single birth with the devotion of Krttivasa, one achieves liberation.

## \|\| 1.32.23 \|\|

*ālayaḥ sarvasiddhānāmetat sthānaṃ vadanti hi \|*  
*gopitaṃ devadevena mahādevena śaṃbhunā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. This place has been described to be the abode of all the Siddhas, which is protected by lord Sambhu.

## \|\| 1.32.24-25 \|\|

*yuge yuge hyatra dāntā brāhmaṇā vedapārāgāḥ \|*  
*upāsate mahādevaṃ japanti śatarudriyam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*stuvanti satataṃ devaṃ tryambakaṃ kṛttivāsasam \|*  
*dhyāyanti hṛdaye devaṃ sthāṇuṃ sarvāntaraṃ śivam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. In each and every Yuga, the Brahmanas controlling their senses, well-versed in the Vedas, recite the Satarudrlya. They always eulogize the three-eyed lord Shiva with a devoted heart on Sthanu, who is present within everyone.

## \|\| 1.32.26 \|\|

*gāyanti siddhāḥ kila gītakāni*  
*ye vārāṇasyāṃ nivasanti viprāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmathaikena bhavena muktir*  
*ye kṛttivāsaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapannāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Surely the songs are sung by the Siddhas for the Brahmanas, who live in Varanasi and those who take refuge with the Krttivasalinga. They achieve liberation in this birth itself.

## \|\| 1.32.27 \|\|

*saṃprāpya loke jagatāmabhīṣṭaṃ*  
*sudurlabhaṃ viprakuleṣu janma \|*  
*dhyāne samādhāya japanti rudraṃ*  
*dhyāyanti citte yatayo maheśam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After securing the birth in the families of the Brahmanas very rare in the world and liked by all the worlds, the ascetics have recourse to meditation, perform the Japa of Rudra and meditate on Mahes'a in their minds.

## \|\| 1.32.28 \|\|

*ārādhayanti prabhumīśitāraṃ*  
*vārāṇasīmadhyagatā munindrāḥ \|*  
*yajanti yajñairabhisaṃdhihīnāḥ*  
*stuvanti rudraṃ praṇamanti śaṃbhum \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Similarly the great Rishis who live in Varanasi adoring lord Shiva, and freeing themselves from all the attachments, perform the yajnas for Mahadeva in a selfless manner, praising Rudra, and offering salutation to Shiva.

## \|\| 1.32.29 \|\|

*namo bhavāyāmalayogadhāmne*  
*sthāṇuṃ prapadye giriśaṃ purāṇam \|*  
*smarāmi rudraṃ hṛdaye niviṣṭaṃ*  
*jāne mahādevamanekarūpam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Salutation to lord Bhava, having pure emotions and splendour. I take refuge with the lord of Mountains, who also is Purana Purusa. I remember Rudra, who is lodged in my heart. I am well aware of lord Shiva having many forms.

## Chapter 33. The Glory of Varanasi

## \|\| 1.33.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*samābhāṣya munīn dhīmān devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*jagāma liṅgaṃ tad draṣṭuṃ kapardeśvaramavyayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “The intelligent Vyasa, after delivering the lecture, want to see the indestructible Kapardlsvaralinga, that unchanging Linga of the trident-bearing lord.

## \|\| 1.33.2 \|\|

*snātvā tatra vidhānena tarpayitvā pitṝn dvijāḥ \|*  
*piśācamocane tīrthe pūjayāmāsa śūlinam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Brahmanas, then he took his bath appropriately at the holy Pisacamocana-tlrthu and offering oblations to the Pitrs, adored Shiva, the trident-bearing deity.

## \|\| 1.33.3 \|\|

*tatrāścaryamapaśyaṃste munayo guruṇā saha \|*  
*menire kṣetramāhātmyaṃ praṇemurgiriśaṃ haram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The sages had a chance of visualising the astonishing tlrtha with their preceptor. They well understood the glory of the place and offered their salutation to GirIshvara.

## \|\| 1.33.4 \|\|

*kaścidabhyājagāmedaṃ śārdūlo ghorarūpadhṛk \|*  
*mṛgīmekāṃ bhakṣayituṃ kapardeśvaramuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Suddenly, they found that a terrific tiger arrived near the Kapardlsvaralinga in order to devour a hind.

## \|\| 1.33.5 \|\|

*tatra sā bhītahṛdayā kṛtvā kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*dhāvamānā susaṃbhrāntā vyāghrasya vaśamāgatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The terrified hind, ran round and round the Shivalinga in agitation, and ultimately submitted to the tiger.

## \|\| 1.33.6 \|\|

*tāṃ vidārya nakhaistīkṣṇaiḥ śārdūlaḥ sumahābalaḥ \|*  
*jagāma cānyaṃ vijanaṃ deśaṃ dṛṣṭvā munīśvarān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The immensely strenghtful tiger, tore out the hind with its sharp nails and at the sight of the sages moved to some other secluded place.

## \|\| 1.33.7 \|\|

*mṛtamātrā ca sā bālā kapardeśāgrato mṛgī \|*  
*adṛśyata mahājvālā vyomni sūryasamaprabhā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When the hind met with death in front of the KapardI Shivalinga, a huge fire flame appeared in the sky, like the sun rays.

## \|\| 1.33.8-9 \|\|

*trinetrā nīlakaṇṭhā ca śaśāṅkāṅkitamūrdhajā \|*  
*vṛṣādhirūḍhā puruṣaistādṛśaireva saṃvṛtā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ vimuñcinti khecarāstasya mūrdhani \|*  
*gaṇeśvaraḥ svayaṃ bhūtvā na dṛṣṭastatkṣaṇāt tataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The flame of fire had three eyes, blue throated, with the head adorned with the crescent mark, mounted over a bull, and was surrounded by the men. The inmates of the space started showering flowers on his head. He, then suddenly was turned into a Ganes'vara and disappeared from that place.

## \|\| 1.33.10 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvaitadāścaryavaraṃ jaiminipramukhā dvijāḥ \|*  
*kapardeśvaramāhātmyaṃ papracchurgurumacyutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At that point of time, Jaimini and other disciples witnessing a great event, enquired of their preceptor, the glory about Kapardlsvara.

## \|\| 1.33.11 \|\|

*teṣāṃ provāca bhagavān devāgre copaviśya saḥ \|*  
*kapardeśasya māhātmyaṃ praṇamya vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After bowing down to the bull-bannered deity, all of them took their seats before Vyasa, who started narrating the glory of Kapardlsvara to his disciples.

## \|\| 1.33.12 \|\|

*idaṃ devasya talliṅgaṃ kapardośvaramuttamam \|*  
*smṛtvaivāśeṣapāpaughaṃ kṣipramasya vimuñcati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. (With the recalling of the name of Kapardlsa, all the sins are washed out.) With the adoration of Kapardlsvara, and by living in Varanasi, all the blemishes like desire, anger etc., are washed out. Because of this, one shpuld always visit Kapardlsvaralinga periodically). Therefore, one should adore Kapardlsvaralinga appropriately, offering prayer to it with the vedic stotras.

## \|\| 1.33.13 \|\|

*kāmakrodhādayo doṣā vārāṇasīnivāsinām \|*  
*vighnāḥ sarve vinaśyanti kapardeśvarapūjanāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Yogins with peaceful minds, who appropriately meditate upon Shiva there, meet with success in Yogic Siddhi in six months. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.33.14 \|\|

*tasmāt sadaiva draṣṭavyaṃ kapardeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*pūjitavyaṃ prayatnena stotavyaṃ vaidikaiḥ stavaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. By so adoring the linga and by taking a bath in the Pisacamocana-tlrtha, the terrific sins like the killing of a Brahmana and other similar sins are removed.

## \|\| 1.33.15 \|\|

*dhyāyatāmatra niyataṃ yogināṃ śāntacetasām \|*  
*jāyate yogasaṃsiddhiḥ sā ṣaṇmāse na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О Brahmanas, an excellent ascetic Sankukama, of praiseworthy holy rites, had in earlier times worshipped the trident-bearing lord.

## \|\| 1.33.16 \|\|

*brahmahatyādayaḥ pāpā vinaśyantyasya pūjanāt \|*  
*piśācamocane kuṇḍe snātasyātra samīpataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Не adored Shiva throughout the day and night, offering his salutation as well as the flowers, incense etc. He also muttered the Rudra- Pranava mantra, circumambulating the linga.

## \|\| 1.33.17-19 \|\|

*asmin kṣetre purā viprāstapasvī śaṃsitavrataḥ \|*  
*śaṅkukarṇa iti khyātaḥ pūjayāmāsa śaṅkaram \|*  
*jajāpa rudramaniśaṃ praṇavaṃ brahmarūpiṇam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*puṣpadhūpādibhiḥ stotrairnamaskāraiḥ pradakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*uvāsa tatra yogātmā kṛtvā dīkṣāṃ tu naiṣṭhikīma \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kadācidāgataṃ pretaṃ paśyati sma kṣudhānvitam \|*  
*asthicarmapinaddhāṅgaṃ niḥ śvasantaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. The said Yogdtma, after receiving the religious initiation, lived there. Once he spotted a preta (ghost), who had arrived there, and was suffering from hunger, having been reduced to skeleton. He was breathing heavily. Looking at him, the heart of the sage was filled with compassion, and he asked him, “who are you? Where from have you come?” Then the pis'aca who had been suffering from hunger, spoke to the sage.

## \|\| 1.33.20 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa muniśreṣṭhaḥ kṛpayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*provāca ko bhavān kasmād deśād deśamimaṃśritaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Не said, “I had been a Brahmana in my earlier birth having enough of cereals and riches, I had sons and grandsons, and I always remained busy in looking after them.

## \|\| 1.33.21 \|\|

*tasmai piśācaḥ kṣudhayā pīḍyamāno 'bravīd vacaḥ \|*  
*pūrvajanmanyahaṃ vipro dhanadhānyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*putrapautrādibhiryuktaḥ kuṭumbabharaṇotsukaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Besides that, I had never taken care of the gods, cows and the guests. I performed no merits even of the smallest quantity.

## \|\| 1.33.22 \|\|

*na pūjitā mayā devā gāvo 'pyatithayastathā \|*  
*na kadācit kṛtaṃ puṇyamalpaṃ vā svalpameva vā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Once I had a look at lord Rudra, with the lordly bull as his vehicle, at Varanasi. I touched him offering my salutation to him.

## \|\| 1.33.23 \|\|

*ekadā bhagavān devo govṛṣeśvaravāhanaḥ \|*  
*viśveśvaro vārāṇasyāṃ dṛṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭe namaskṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Soon thereafter, I met with my end. О Sage, I have not witnessed the horrible face of Yama.

## \|\| 1.33.24 \|\|

*tadācireṇa kālena pañcatvamahamāgataḥ \|*  
*na dṛṣṭaṃ nanmayā ghoraṃ yamasya vadanaṃ mune \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Presently, achieving the position of a pisaca, am suffering from hunger and thirst, unable to think about my good or bad.

## \|\| 1.33.25 \|\|

*īdṛśīṃ yonimāpannaḥ paiśācīṃ kṣudhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*pipāsayādhunākrānto na jānāmi hitāhitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О Lord, in case you have in view any means for my liberation then you speak out the same to me. I take refuge with you.”

## \|\| 1.33.26-27 \|\|

*yadi kañcit samuddhartumupāyaṃ paśyasi prabho \|*  
*kuruṣva taṃ namastubhyaṃ tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ityuktaḥ śaṅkukarṇo 'tha piśācamidamabravīt \|*  
*tvādṛśo na hi loke 'smin vidyate puṇyakṛttamaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. After saying this, Sankukarna said to the ghost, “There is no other person as meritorious as you are, in this world because you had an audience with the lord and also touched him, offering your salutation at the same time. Who could then be there comparable with you.

## \|\| 1.33.28-29 \|\|

*yat tvayā bhagavān pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭo viśveśvaraḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*saṃspṛṣṭo vandito bhūyaḥ ko 'nyastvatsadṛśo bhuvi \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tena karmavipākena deśametaṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*snānaṃ kuruṣva śīghraṃ tvamasmin kuṇḍe samāhitaḥ \|*  
*yenemāṃ kutsitāṃ yoniṃ kṣiprameva prahāsyasi \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. As a reward of the same deed, you have reached this place. With a devoted mind, you enter this kunda (holy pond) and have a bath. By doing so you will be liberated from this horrible form.”

## \|\| 1.33.30 \|\|

*sa evamukto muninā piśāco*  
*dayālunā devavaraṃ trinetram \|*  
*smṛtvā kapardeśvaramīśitāraṃ*  
*cakre samādhāya mano 'vagāham \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At these words of the compassionate sage, the pisaca, with his devoted mind, remembering lord Shiva, with matted locks of hair, having three eyes, took his bath into the holy pond.

## \|\| 1.33.31 \|\|

*tadāvagāḍho munisaṃnidhāne*  
*mamāra divyābharaṇopapannaḥ \|*  
*adṛśyatārkapratime vimāne*  
*śaśāṅkacihnāṅkitacārumauliḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After taking his bath, he met with his end near the sage. Then getting adorned with the divine ornaments, he was seen over an aerial chariot that resembled the sun itself, and appeared there with his crest marked by the moon.

## \|\| 1.33.32 \|\|

*vibhāti rudrairabhito divasthaiḥ*  
*samāvṛto yogibhairaprameyaiḥ \|*  
*sabālakhilyādibhireṣa devo*  
*yathodaye bhānuraśeṣadevaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The pis'dca then appeared having been surrounded with Rudras, the great Yogins, like the rising sun, the lord of all, surrounded by Valakhilya sages and others at the time of dawn.

## \|\| 1.33.33 \|\|

*stuvanti siddhā divi devasaṅghā*  
*nṛtyanti divyāpsaraso 'bhirāmāḥ \|*  
*muñcanti vṛṣṭiṃ kusumāmbumiśrāṃ*  
*gandharvavidyādharakiṃnarādyāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The gods and the Siddhas started praising him in the sky. The divine and beautiful Apsaras, started dancing. The Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, Kinnaras, and others, started raining flowers over him.

## \|\| 1.33.34 \|\|

*saṃstūyamāno 'tha munīndrasaṅghai-*  
*ravāpya bodhaṃ bhagavātprasādāt \|*  
*samāviśanmaṇḍalametadagryaṃ*  
*trayīmayaṃ yatra vibhāti rudraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Groups of the sages were praising him, and by the grace of lord Shiva, he achieved the divine knowledge as well. Then he entered the solar disc consisting of three Vedas, where Rudra resides always.

## \|\| 1.33.35 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā vimuktaṃ sa piśācabhūtaṃ*  
*muniḥ prahṛṣṭo manasā maheśam \|*  
*vicintya rudraṃ kavimekamagniṃ*  
*praṇamya tuṣṭāva kapardinaṃ tam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Having been relieved of the position of a pisaca, the sage was immensely delighted, and devoting his mind to lord Rudra-Mahesa, offering his salutation to him, he engaged himself in pleasing the lord with matted locks of hair.

## \|\| 1.33.36 \|\|

*kapardinaṃ tvāṃ parataḥ parastād*  
*goptāramekaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam \|*  
*vrajāmi yogeśvaramīśitāra-*  
*mādityamagniṃ kapilādhirūḍham \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Sankukama said, “I offer my salutation to the eternal lord, who is better than the best, secretive, and the ancient Purusa. I take refuge with Yogesvara, Ts'vara, Aditya, fonn of fire, and the one who is lodged in the hearts of all.

## \|\| 1.33.37 \|\|

*tvāṃ brahmapāraṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭaṃ*  
*hiraṇmayaṃ yoginamādimantam \|*  
*vrajāmi rudraṃ śaraṇaṃ divasthaṃ*  
*mahāmuniṃ brahmamayaṃ pavitram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. О Lord, You are beyond Brahma, are lodged in the hearts of all, the form of gold, a Yogin, beyond birth, the protector, living in the sky and the great sage resembling Brahman and are auspicious. I take refuge with you.

## \|\| 1.33.38 \|\|

*sahastrapādākṣiśiro 'bhiyuktaṃ*  
*sahastrabāhuṃ namasaḥ parastāt \|*  
*tvāṃ brahāmapāraṃ praṇamāmi śaṃbhuṃ*  
*hiraṇyagarbhādhipatiṃ trinetram \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O Lord, You are having a thousand feet, a thousand eyes, a thousand heads, a thousand arms, beyond darkness, beyond Brahman, the lord of Hiranyagarba, having three eyes, besides being lord Sambhu. I offer my salutation to you.

## \|\| 1.33.39 \|\|

*yataḥ prasūtirjagato vināśo*  
*yenāvṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ śivena \|*  
*taṃ brahmapāraṃ bhagavantamīśaṃ*  
*praṇamya nityaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. You are the creator and the destroyer of the universe, you are Shiva, Lord Isa, the other shore of Brahman, I take refuge with the same Shiva, offering my salutation to you forever.

## \|\| 1.33.40 \|\|

*aliṅgamālokavihīnarūpaṃ*  
*svayaṃprabhaṃ citpatimekarudram \|*  
*taṃ brahmapāraṃ parameśvaraṃ tvāṃ*  
*namaskariṣye na yato 'nyadasti \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. You are beyond all symbols, having the invisible form, self-luminous, the Lord of consciousness, exclusive Rudra, salutation to you. I offer my salutation to the lord who is beyond Brahman, and beyond whom nothing exists.

## \|\| 1.33.41 \|\|

*yaṃ yoginastyaktasabījayogā*  
*labdhvā samādhiṃ paramārthabhūtāḥ \|*  
*paśyanti devaṃ praṇato 'smi nityaṃ*  
*taṃ brahmapāraṃ bhavataḥ svarūpam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The god, who is visualised by Yogins by yogic practices and meditations, wherein the Sabija fonn is eschewed, I always offer my salutation to your same form which is beyond Brahman.

## \|\| 1.33.42 \|\|

*na yatra nāmādiviśeṣakḷpti-*  
*r na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati yatsvarūpam \|*  
*taṃ brahmapāraṃ praṇato 'smi nityaṃ*  
*svayaṃbhuvaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О Lord, where there is no name, where there is no special pleasure and its satisfaction, the one who is invisible having no fonn, I bow in reverence to Shiva who is beyond Brahman. I take refuge in you, the self-bom god.

## \|\| 1.33.43 \|\|

*yad vedavādābhiratā videhaṃ*  
*sabrahmavijñānamabhedamekam \|*  
*paśyantyanekaṃ bhavataḥ svarūpaṃ*  
*sabrahmapāraṃ praṇato 'smi nityam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The learned people well-versed in the Vedas, describe him bodyless, indivisible, having non-duality, having the form resembling Brahmavijnana, one without a second yet perceived in many forms. I, therefore, bow in reverence to the one who is beyond Brahman.

## \|\| 1.33.44 \|\|

*yataḥ pradhānaṃ puruṣaḥ purāṇo*  
*vivartate yaṃ praṇamanti devāḥ \|*  
*namāmi taṃ jyotiṣi saṃniviṣṭaṃ*  
*kālaṃ bṛhantaṃ bhavataḥ svarūpam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. You are the one by whose grace Pradhana and Ancient Purusa exist, I bow in reverence to the form of Kala, who is respected by the Devas and which is enveloped in brilliance.

## \|\| 1.33.45 \|\|

*vrajāmi nityaṃ śaraṇaṃ guheśaṃ*  
*sthāṇuṃ prapadye giriśaṃ purārim \|*  
*śivaṃ prapadye haramindumauliṃ*  
*pinākinaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. I always take refuge with Mahesa. I resort to Sthanu, Girfsa, the Purana-Purusa, besides being moon-crested, Нага and take refuge with the holder of the Pinaka-bow.”

## \|\| 1.33.46 \|\|

*stutvaivaṃ śaṅkukarṇo 'sau bhagavantaṃ kapardinam \|*  
*papāta daṇḍavad bhūmau proccaran praṇavaṃ param \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In this way the sage Sankukama, kept on offering prayer to Shiva having locks of hair over the head. Then repeating the auspicious Pranava Mantra (От), he prostrated on earth like a staff.

## \|\| 1.33.47 \|\|

*tatkṣaṇāt paramaṃ liṅgaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ śivātmakam \|*  
*jñānamānandamadvaitaṃ koṭikālāgnisannibham \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. At the same time, the greatest Linga of the nature of Shiva appeared which was the form of knowledge, blissful, form of non-duality, resembling a crore of fires annihilating the universe.

## \|\| 1.33.48 \|\|

*śaṅkukarṇo 'tha muktātmā tadātmā sarvago 'malaḥ \|*  
*nililye vimale liṅge tadbhutamivābhavat \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then the spotless sage Sankukama, of the nature of the soul of all, was absorbed in the spotless linga. This was an astonishing event.

## \|\| 1.33.49 \|\|

*etad rahasyamākhyātaṃ māhātmyaṃ vaḥ kapardinaḥ \|*  
*na kaścid vetti tamasā vidvānapyatra muhyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. I have thus revealed the secret as well as the glory of the Kapardilinga. Because of tamoguna, no one understands it. Even the learned people get confused about it.

## \|\| 1.33.50 \|\|

*ya imāṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*bhaktaḥ pāpaviśuddhātmā rudrasāmīpyamāpnuyāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The devotees who listen daily to this auspicious story, all their sins are removed, and they achieve the vicinity of Rudra.

## \|\| 1.33.51 \|\|

*paṭhecca satataṃ śuddho brahmapāraṃ mahāstavam \|*  
*prātarmadhyāhnasamaye sa yogaṃ prāpnuyāt param \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A person who getting purified shall recite this Brahmapara stotra daily in the morning as well as in the noon, he will surely achieve Yoga.

## \|\| 1.33.52-53 \|\|

*ihaiva nityaṃ vatsyāmo devadevaṃ kapardinam \|*  
*drakṣyāmaḥ satataṃ devaṃ pūjayāmo 'tha śūlinam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ityuktvā bhagavān vyāsaḥ śiṣyaiḥ saha mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*uvāsa tatra yuktātmā pūjayan vai kapardinam \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Then the sages said- “All of us shall stay here and see Kapardin, the lord of the Devas forever. We shall constantly worship the three-eyed deity.” Thus speaking, the illustrious holy sage Vyasadeva, lived there along with his disciples, adoring lord Kapardl there with concentrated mind.

## Chapter 34. The Glory of Varanasi

## \|\| 1.34.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*uṣitvā tatra bhagavān kapardeśāntike punaḥ \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ yayau madhyameśaṃ bahuvarṣagaṇān prabhuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “They lived for many years near KapardIshvara Shiva, then the sage Vedavyasa, moved on to have a look at the Madhyamesvara-linga.

## \|\| 1.34.2 \|\|

*tatra mandākinīṃ puṇyāmṛṣisaṅganiṣevitām \|*  
*nadīṃ vimalapānīyāṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭo 'bhavanmuniḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Surrounded by the groups of Rishis, at the bank of the auspicious and pure MandakinI river, with the spotless water flowing in it, the sage Vyasa was immensely pleased.

## \|\| 1.34.3 \|\|

*sa tāmanvīkṣya munibhiḥ saha dvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*cakāra bhāvapūtātmā snānaṃ snānavidhānavit \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Looking at the auspicious river, the sage Vyasa with auspicious soul, well-versed in the rites of ablution, took his bath in the sacred river with other sages.

## \|\| 1.34.4 \|\|

*saṃtarpya vidhivad devānṛṣīn pitṛgaṇāṃstathā \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa lokādiṃ puṣpairnānāvidhairbhavam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. (Entering with his disciples in the auspicious river water, Vyasa-the son of Satyavati, adored lord Shiva, the eternal one with many flowers.) He offered oblation, appropriately to the gods, Rishis and Pitrs and then adored the Madhyamesvara-linga of trident-bearing lord Shiva.

## \|\| 1.34.5-7 \|\|

*praviśya śiṣyapravaraiḥ sārdhaṃ satyavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*madhyameśvaramīśānamarcayāmāsa śūlinam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tataḥ pāśupatāḥ śāntā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahāḥ \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ samāgatā rudraṃ madhyameśvaramīśvaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

*oṅkārāsaktamanaso vedādhyayanatatparāḥ \|*  
*jaṭilā muṇḍitāścāpi śuklayajñopavītinaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Then the devotees of Madhyamesvara Shiva, with ashes applied over their bodies, with a peaceful mind, arrived there to have a look at Madhyames'vara-Shiva. All of them were devoted to Orhkara and were engaged in the Vedic studies. They had matted locks of hair over the heads, some of them were with shaven heads, wearing the auspicious yajnopavltas. Some of them wore kauplna (had only the loin cloth), while others were without robes. All of them practiced celibacy and were peaceful by nature, possessing divine knowledge, having controlled their sense organs.

## \|\| 1.34.8-9 \|\|

*kaupīnavasanāḥ kecidapare cāpyavāsasaḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryaratāḥ śāntā vedāntajñānatatparāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā dvaipāyanaṃ viprāḥ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtaṃ munim \|*  
*pūjayitvā yathānyāyamidaṃ vacanamabruvan \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. O Brahmanas, “The sage Vyasa, surrounded by his disciples, was adored by the sages who put him a question, “O Great sage, who are you? Where from have you arrived with your disciples?” Then Paila and other disciples, overwhelmed by the religious feelings, spoke to the Rishis.

## \|\| 1.34.10 \|\|

*ko bhavān kuta āyātaḥ saha śiṣyairmahāmune \|*  
*procuḥ pailādayaḥ śiṣyāstānṛṣīn brahmabhāvitān \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “He himself is Hrsikesa, son of Satyavati, lord Krisnadvaipayana Vyasa, who himself had classified the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.34.11-13 \|\|

*ayaṃ satyavatīsūnuḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ \|*  
*vyāsaḥ svayaṃ hṛṣīkeśo yena vedāḥ pṛthak kṛtāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yasya devo mahādevaḥ sākṣādeva pinākadhṛk \|*  
*aṃśāṃśenābhavat putro nāmnā śuka iti prabhuḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yaḥ sa sākṣānmahādevaṃ sarvabhāvena śaṅkaram \|*  
*prapannaḥ parayā bhaktyā yasya tajjñānamaiśvaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Suka is the name of his son. He is the one who was bom of the ams'a of Shiva-the holder of the Pinaka bow, who has taken refuge with lord Mahadeva with utmost devotion. He is the one who has attained the full knowledge about Ishvara. Thereafter all the devotees of Shiva, thrilled with delight, spoke to Vyasa-the son of Satyavati with a quiescent mind.

## \|\| 1.34.14 \|\|

*tataḥ pāśupatāḥ sarve hṛṣṭasarvatanūruhāḥ \|*  
*nemuravyagramanasaḥ procuḥ satyavatīsutam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “You know well about Paramcsthin-Shiva, who is the god of gods. You have also achieved the complete knowledge about Mahesvara.

## \|\| 1.34.15 \|\|

*bhagavan bhavatā jñātaṃ vijñānaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*prisādād devadevasya yat tanmāheśvaraṃ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You kindly enlighten us on this excellent, unrevealed secret about Shiva without any agitation. By so listening from you the glory of Shiva, may we see the lord quickly.

## \|\| 1.34.16 \|\|

*tadvadāsmākamavyaktaṃ rahasyaṃ guhyamuttamam \|*  
*kṣipraṃ paśyema taṃ devaṃ śrutvā bhagavato mukhāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then sending off disciples whose chief was sage Sumantu, from that place, the best among the knowers of Yogic practices, narrated to the great Yogins, about the best of the knowledge.

## \|\| 1.34.17 \|\|

*visarjayitvā tāñchiṣyān sumantupramukhāṃstataḥ \|*  
*provāca tatparaṃ jñānaṃ yogibhyo yogavittamaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At the same time, the excellent flame, divine in nature, appeared there. All the Brahmanas were absorbed in the same and then disappeared.

## \|\| 1.34.18 \|\|

*tatkṣaṇādeva vimalaṃ saṃbhūtaṃ jyotiruttamam \|*  
*līnāstatraiva te viprāḥ kṣaṇādantaradhīyata \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then calling Paila and other disciples before him, Vyasa, who was best among those who were the speakers on Brahman, explained to them the glory of the Madhyamesvara linga.

## \|\| 1.34.19-20 \|\|

*tataḥ śiṣyān samāhūya bhagavān brahmavittamaḥ \|*  
*provāca madhyameśasya māhātmyaṃ pailapūrvakān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*asmin sthāne svayaṃ devo devyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*ramate bhagavān nityaṃ rudraiśca parivāritaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. He said, “This is the place, where lord Shiva, in company of Parvati and ganas, keeps on sporting always. In earlier times Krisna, the universal soul, son of DevakI, had lived here for a year with the Pas'upatas.

## \|\| 1.34.21-22 \|\|

*atra pūrvaṃ hṛṣīkeśo viśvātmā devakīsutaḥ \|*  
*uvāsa vatsaraṃ kṛṣṇaḥ sadā pāśupatairvṛtaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*bhasmoddhūlitasarvāṅgo rudrādhyayanatatparaḥ \|*  
*ārādhayan hariḥ śaṃbhuṃ kṛtvā pāśupataṃ vratam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Applying ashes over his body, and devoting himself to the propitiation of Rudra, Hari was engaged in the meditation of Shiva, embracing Pasupata vows. Many of his disciples who were observing Brahmacarya, having been enlightened by his words, had an audience with Mahesvara.

## \|\| 1.34.23 \|\|

*tasya te bahavaḥ śiṣyā brahmacaryaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*labdhvā tadvacanājjñānaṃ dṛṣṭavanto maheśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Lord Mahadeva, the blue-red complexioned God appeared directly before Krisna. The besotwer of boons that he is, the lord conferred upon him excellent boons.

## \|\| 1.34.24 \|\|

*tasya devo mahādevaḥ pratyakṣaṃ nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*dadau kṛṣṇāsya bhagavāna varado varamuttamam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Shiva said, “O Universal form, such of my devotees who adore Govinda appropriately, shall achieve the divine knowledge pertaining to Is'vara.

## \|\| 1.34.25 \|\|

*yer'cayiṣyanti govindaṃ madbhaktā vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*teṣāṃ tadaiśvaraṃ jñānamutpatsyati jaganmaya \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. By my grace, О Lord, You shall be adored by my devotees as well as the Brahmanas. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.34.26 \|\|

*namasyor'cayitavyaśca dhyātavyo matparairjanaiḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyasi na saṃdeho matprasādād dvijātibhiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Such of the people who meditating on Shiva, the holder of the Pinaka bow, shall have an audience with you, all their sins like Brahmahatya and others shall disappear.

## \|\| 1.34.27 \|\|

*ye 'tra drakṣyanti deveśaṃ snātvā rudraṃ pinākinam \|*  
*brahmahatyādikaṃ pāpaṃ teṣāmāśu vinaśyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Such of the Brahmanas who inspite of their being sinful, give up their life here, they shall achieve liberation, there is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 1.34.28 \|\|

*prāṇāṃstyajanti ye martyāḥ pāpakarmaratā api \|*  
*te yānti tat paraṃ sthānaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Graceful are the Brahmanas who taking bath in the river Mandakini, adore the excellent Madhyamesvara-linga.

## \|\| 1.34.29 \|\|

*dhanyāstu khalu te viprā mandākinyāṃ kṛtodakāḥ \|*  
*arcayanti mahādevaṃ madhyameśvaramīśvaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Whosoever takes bath and perfonns charities, tapas, sraddha and pindadana (offering of the balls of rice as pmda) duly at this place, he sanctifies his seven generations.

## \|\| 1.34.30 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ tapaḥ śrāddhaṃ piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ tviha \|*  
*ekaikaśaḥ kṛtaṃ viprāḥ punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The merit one gets by taking a bath at Kuruksetra, during the solar eclipse, one achieves ten times more the merit by taking a bath here.”

## \|\| 1.34.31 \|\|

*saṃnihatyāmupaspṛśya rāhugraste divākare \|*  
*yat phalaṃ labhate martyastasmād daśaguṇaṃ tviha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thus speaking Vyasa- the great Yogin, adoring lord Mahes'vara stayed at the place of Madhyames'vara for a long time.

## Chapter 35. The Glory of Varnasi

## \|\| 1.35.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tataḥ sarvāṇi guhyāni tīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*jagāma bhagavān vyāso jaiminipramukhairvṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “Thereafter, accompanied with the disciples like JaiminI and others, visited all the sacred places as well as the temples mentioned below.

## \|\| 1.35.2-3 \|\|

*prayāgaṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ prayāgādadhikaṃ śubham \|*  
*viśvarūpaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ tālatīrthamanuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ākāśākhyaṃ mahātīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ caivārṣabhaṃ param \|*  
*svarnolaṃ ca mahātīrthaṃ gaurītīrthamanuttamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. He visited the excellent Prayaga-tlrtha, Visvarupa-tlrtha, which is greater in sanctity than the Prayaga-tlrtha. He went to the unsurpassable pond kalatlrtha, Akasa- mahatfrtha, the excellent Anusa-tlrtha, Mahatlrtha named Svaralina, besides the GaurJtirtha that surpasses all.

## \|\| 1.35.4-9 \|\|

*prājāpatyaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ svargadvāraṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*jambukeśvaramityuktaṃ dharmākhyaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*gayātīrthaṃ mahātīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ caiva mahānadī \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ vāyutīrthamanuttamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*jñānatīrthaṃ paraṃ guhyaṃ vārāhaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*yamatīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ tīrthaṃ saṃvartakaṃ śubham \|\| 6 \|\|*

*agnitīrthaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ kalaśeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*nāgatīrthaṃ somatīrthaṃ sūryatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*parvatākhyaṃ mahāguhyaṃ maṇikarṇamanuttamam \|*  
*ghaṭotkacaṃ tīrthavaraṃ śrītīrthaṃ ca pitāmaham \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gaṅgātīrthaṃ tu deveśaṃ yayātestīrthamuttamam \|*  
*kāpilaṃ caiva someśaṃ brahmatīrthamanuttamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

4-9. “О Best of the Brahmanas, he visited the holy places like Prajapatya, Svargadvara, Jambukesvara and the excellent tlrtha known as the Carma, then Gaya, MahanadT-Irtha, the highly sacred Narayana-tlrtha, the best Vayu- tlrtha, the extremely auspicious Juana-tlrtha, the excellent Varaha-tlrtha, the extremely meritorious Yama-tirtha, the excellent Samvartaka-tlrtha, Agni-tlrtha, Kalakesvara- tlrtha, Nagatlrtha, Somatlrtha, Suryatirtha, Parvata-tirtha, Manikarna-tlrtha, Gatotkaca- tlrtha, Srl-tlrtha and Pitamaha-tirtha, Ganga- tlrtha, the excellent Devesa-tlrtha, Kapila-tlrtha, Somesa-tlrtha and excellent Brahma-tlrtha were visited by them.

## \|\| 1.35.10-12 \|\|

*atra liṅgaṃ purānīya brahmā snātuṃ yadā gataḥ \|*  
*tadānīṃ sthāpayāmāsa viṣṇustalliṅgamaiśvaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tataḥ snātvā samāgatya brahmā provāca taṃ harim \|*  
*mayānītamidaṃ liṅgaṃ kasmāt sthāpitavānasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tamāha viṣṇustvatto 'pi rudre bhaktirdṛḍhā mama \|*  
*tasmāt pratiṣṭhitaṃ liṅgaṃnāmnā tava bhaviṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. The place where the adorable Shivalinga is consecrated, Brahma arrived there for taking bath. At the same time Visnu, consecrated the divine Shivalinga there. Then when Brahma arrived thereafter taking his bath, he said to Visnu, “I have brought this lirigci here, wherefore did you consecrate it?” Then Visnu said to him, “I am fully devoted to Rudra, therefore, I consecrated the Shivalinga.” But this Shivalinga will be known by your name.) О best of the Brahmanas, then he went to Bhutesvara- tlrtha, Dharmasamudbhava-tlrtha, extremely auspicious Gandharva-tlrtha, the excellent Vahneya-tlrtha, Daurvasika-tirtha, Homa-tlrtha, Candra-tlrtha, auspicious Citrangadesvara-tirtha, auspicious Vidyadhares'vara-tTrtha, Kedara- tirtha, Mukhya-tlrtha, Kalanjara- tlrtha, Sarasvata-Irtha, Prabhasa-tlrtha, Khetakarna and Harallrtha were the spots visited by them.

## \|\| 1.35.13-15 \|\|

*bhūteśvaraṃ tathā tīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ dharmasamudbhavam \|*  
*gandharvatīrthaṃ paramaṃ vāhneyaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*daurvāsikaṃ vyomatīrthaṃ candratīrthaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*citrāṅgadeśvaraṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyaṃ vidyādhareśvaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kedāratīrthamugrākhyaṃ kālañjaramanuttamam \|*  
*sārasvataṃ prabhāsaṃ ca bhadrakarṇaṃ hradaṃ śubham \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Thereafter he visited the Laukika-mahatlrtha, Himalaya-tlrtha, Hiranyagarbha- tlrtha, Gopreksya-tlrtha, Vrsadhvaja-tlrtha, Upasanta, Shiva, very excellent Vyaghres'vara-tlrtha, the great Trilocana-tlrtha, Lolarka and Uttara-tlrtha, Kapalamocana-tirtha which is remover of sins created by Brahmahatya (slaughter of the Brahmanas), extremely auspicious Sukresvara- tlrtha and the Anandapura-tlrtha.

## \|\| 1.35.16 \|\|

*laukikākhyaṃ mahātīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ caiva vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaṃ goprekṣyaṃ tīrthaṃ caiva vṛṣadhvajam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Best of the Brahmanas, thus I have narrated to you the prominent holy places. Practically it is impossible to describe the names of the holy places in detail.

## \|\| 1.35.17-18 \|\|

*upaśāntaṃ śivaṃ caiva vyāghreśvaramanuttamam \|*  
*trilocanaṃ mahātīrthaṃ lolārkaṃ cottarāhvayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kapālamocanaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmahatyāvināśanam \|*  
*śukreśvaraṃ mahāpuṇyamānandapuramuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Then the great sage Vyasa, the son of Parasara, took bath in all the holy places, adored the eternal lord, and observed fast there. Then he offered oblation to the gods and the manes performing the Pindadana at the same time. Then he returned the place of Shiva, the lord of universe.

## \|\| 1.35.19 \|\|

*evamādīni tīrthāni prādhānyāt kathitāni tu \|*  
*na śakyaṃ vistarād vaktuṃ tīrthasaṃkhyā dvijāttamāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The religious minded, the great sage Vyasa, taking bath with his disciples addressed to them, “Now you are free to go to your respective places.”

## \|\| 1.35.20 \|\|

*teṣu sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snātvābhyarcya pinākinam \|*  
*upoṣya tatra tatrāsau pārāśaryo mahāmuniḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О Brahmanas, then Paila and other disciples, bowing in reverence to the great souled Vyasa, retired to their respective places while Vyasa himself continued to stay in Varanasi.

## \|\| 1.35.21 \|\|

*tarpayitvā pitṝn devān kṛtvā piṇḍapridānakam \|*  
*jagāma punarevāpi yatra viśveśvaraḥ śivaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Remaining calm, controlling his sense organs, taking bath thrice a day, with a purified soul, he lived by getting food by begging and adoring Shiva at the same time.

## \|\| 1.35.22 \|\|

*snātvābhyarcya paraṃ liṅgaṃ śiṣyaiḥ saha mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*uvāca śiṣyān dharmātmā svān deśān gantumarhathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О Excellent Brahmanas, once, when he was so living at KasT, the immensely illustrious Vyasa, while wandering for begging food, could not get the alms.

## \|\| 1.35.23 \|\|

*te praṇamya mahātmānaṃ jagmuḥ pailādayo dvijāḥ \|*  
*vāsaṃ ca tatra niyato vārāṇasyāṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then the sage, having been filled with anger said, “I shall resort to creation which could cause obstructions for the people living here, as a result of which the Siddhis possessed by all of them would decline.”

## \|\| 1.35.24-25 \|\|

*śānto dāntastriṣavaṇaṃsnātvābhyarcya pinākinam \|*  
*bhaikṣāhāro viśuddhātmā brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kadācid vasatā tatra vyāsenāmitatejasā \|*  
*bhramamāṇena bhikṣā tu naiva labdhā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Then suddenly the goddess Parvati- the spouse of Shiva, appeared there livingly herself and spoke to Vyasa, “O Learned one, don't pronounce a curse on the city of Varanasi. You better receive the alms from me.” Thus speaking Shiva gave alms to the sage Vyasa.

## \|\| 1.35.26 \|\|

*tataḥ krodhāvṛtatanurnarāṇāmiha vāsinām \|*  
*vighnaṃ sṛjāmi sarveṣāṃ yena siddhirvihīyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. MahadevI said, “O Sage, the cause for which you have been angered, therefore you should not stay in this region, because you are ungrateful.”

## \|\| 1.35.27 \|\|

*tatkṣaṇe sā mahādevī śaṅkarārdhaśarīriṇī \|*  
*prādurāsīt svayaṃ prītyā veṣaṃ kṛtvā tu mānuṣam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. At these words of Parvati, lord Vyasa, looked attentively at the supreme power and bowed in reverence to her praising her with several excellent hymns.

## \|\| 1.35.28 \|\|

*bho bho vyāsa mahābuddhe śaptavyā bhavatā na hi \|*  
*gṛhāṇa bhikṣāṃ mattastvamuktvaivaṃ pradadau śivā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He said, “O Spouse of Sarhkara, you allow me to enter in Varanasi on the eighth and the fourteenth day of the moon.” She replied, “Be it so,” and then disappeared.

## \|\| 1.35.29 \|\|

*uvāca ca mahādevī krodhanastvaṃ bhavān yataḥ \|*  
*iha kṣetre na vastavyaṃ kṛtaghno 'si tvayā sadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thus the illustrious one, the great Yogin, the ancient sage Vyasa being aware of all the merits of KasI, started living close to the same.

## \|\| 1.35.30 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ sa bhagavān dhyānājjñātvā parāṃ śivām \|*  
*uvāca praṇato bhūtvā stutvā ca pravaraiḥ stavaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The learned people therefore, because of the association of Vyasa with KasI serve this region. Therefore a man should try to stay at KasT, making all the efforts.

## \|\| 1.35.31 \|\|

*caturdaśyāmathāṣṭamyāṃ praveśaṃ dehi śāṅkari \|*  
*evamastvityanujñāya devī cāntaradhīyata \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Suta said, “A person who reads about the glory of the Avimukta-ksetra, listens to it or recites the same to the peaceful Brahmanas, he achieves the final emancipation.

## \|\| 1.35.32-33 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bhagavān vyāso mahāyogī purātanaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā kṣetraguṇān sarvān sthitastasyātha pārśvataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*evaṃ vyāsaṃ sthitaṃ jñātvā kṣetraṃ sevanti paṇḍitāḥ \|*  
*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena vārāṇasyāṃ vasennaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. О Brahmanas, the one, who while performing the Sraddhas, or the auspicious rites for the gods, during the day or the night, discarding the lust and anger, with a concentrated mind, well realising about the glory of KasI, shall offer his salutation to the Lord of universe, he would surely achieve final and the greatest goal.

## Chapter 36. The Glory of Prayaga

## \|\| 1.36.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*māhātmyamavimuktasya yathāvat tadudīritam \|*  
*idānīṃ tu prayāgasya māhātmyaṃ brūhi suvrata \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The sages said, “O Suvrata, you have narrated the glory of Avimukta-ksetra appropriately. Now you kindly speak out the glory of Prayaga.

## \|\| 1.36.2 \|\|

*yāni tīrthāni tatraiva viśrutāni mahānti vai \|*  
*idānīṃ kathayāsmākaṃ sūta sarvārthavid bhavān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. You also enlighten us over the important holy and sacred places there, О Suta, you are well aware of all such topics.

## \|\| 1.36.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śṛṇudhvamṛṣayaḥ sarve vistareṇa bravīmi vaḥ \|*  
*prayāgasya ca māhātmyaṃ yatra devaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Suta said, “Listen О Rishis, I am going to speak out the glory of Prayaga in details. This is the place where Brahma is lodged.

## \|\| 1.36.4 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeyena kathitaṃ kaunteyāya mahātmane \|*  
*yathā yudhiṣṭhirāyaitat tadvakṣye bhavatāmaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The details about the region which were revealed by the sage Markandeya to the great- souled Yudhistira, the son of KuntI, are being revealed by me to you.

## \|\| 1.36.5-6 \|\|

*nihatya kauravāna sarvān bhrātṛbhiḥ saha pārthivaḥ \|*  
*śokena mahātāviṣṭā mumoha sa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*acireṇātha kālena mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpto hāstinapuraṃ rājadvāre sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. After killing all the Kauravas, the king Yudhisthira together with his brothers, became deluded and was filled with gloom. After some time, Markandeya, the great sage, reached Hastinapura and stood at the royal gate of the palace.

## \|\| 1.36.7 \|\|

*dvārapālo 'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā rājñaḥ kathitavān drutam \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyo draṣṭumicchaṃstvāmāste dvāryasau muniḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Finding him there, the door-keeper atonce rushed to the king and said, “The sage Markandeya wants to meet you. He is waiting at

## \|\| 1.36.8-9 \|\|

*tvarito dharmaputrastu dvārametyāha tatparam \|*  
*svāgataṃ te mahāprājña svāgataṃ te mahāmune \|\| 8 \|\|*

*adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me tāritaṃ kulam \|*  
*adya me pitarastuṣṭāstvayi tuṣṭe mahāmune \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Then the king Yudhithira, the son of Dharma, reached at the gate with speed, and said to the sage, “O Great sage, you are welcome, My birth has been successful. You have redeemed my race today. With your satisfaction today, my ancestors will ever feel contented.”

## \|\| 1.36.10-11 \|\|

*siṃhāsanamupasthāpya pādaśaucārcanādibhiḥ \|*  
*yudhiṣṭhiro mahātmeti pūjayāmāsa taṃ munim \|\| 10 \|\|*

*mārkaṇḍeyastatastuṣṭaḥ provāca sa yudhiṣṭhiram \|*  
*kimarthaṃ muhyase vidvan sarvaṃ jñātvāhamāgataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Then the sage was seated over the lion- throne. Yudhisthira washed his feet adoring him at the same time. Then adoring the sage, he asked about his welfare. Then the sage Markandeya said to Yudhisthira, “O Intelligent one, why do you get bewildered? I have arrived here, getting well aware of the situation.”

## \|\| 1.36.12 \|\|

*tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā praṇamyāha mahāmunim \|*  
*kathaya tvaṃ samāsena yena mucyeta kilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then the king Yudhisthira, bowing his head, offered his salutation to the sage and said, “You kindly tell me in brief the means to rid myself of the sin?

## \|\| 1.36.13-14 \|\|

*nihatā vahavo yuddhe puṃso niraparādhinaḥ \|*  
*asmābhiḥ kauravaiḥ sārdhaṃ prasaṅgānmunipuṅgava \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yena hiṃsāsamudbhūtājjanmāntarakṛtādapi \|*  
*mucyate pātakādasmāt tad bhavān vaktumarhati \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. О Best of the sages, while fighting with the Kauravas, I have surely killed many innocent people. You tell me the way out to get myself relieved of the sins committed by me in this birth as well as in several previous births. You are competent enough to speak out the related means for the purpose.”

## \|\| 1.36.15-16 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājan mahābhāga yanmāṃ pṛcchasi bhārat \|*  
*prayāgagamanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ narāṇāṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatra devo mahādevo rudro viśvāmareśvaraḥ \|*  
*samāste bhagavān brahmā svayaṃbhūrapi daivadaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Markandeya said, “O King, О Fortunate one, О Scion of the family of Bharata, you listen to the reply to the question you have asked me. It would be better for you to visit Prayaga on pilgrimage, which removes the sins of the people. О Lord of kings, Mahadeva Rudra, dwells there. Lord Brahma too lives there with other gods.

## \|\| 1.36.17-18 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*bhagavañcchrotumicchāmi prayāgagamane phalam \|*  
*mṛtānāṃ kā gatistatra snātānāmapi kiṃ phalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ye vasanti prayāge tu brūhi teṣāṃ tu kiṃ phalam \|*  
*bhavatā viditaṃ hyetat tanme brūhi namo 'stu te \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Yudhisthira said, “О holy Lord, I would like to listen to the glory of going on pilgrimage to Prayaga. What is the goal attained by those who meet with their end there? What merit accrues to a person who takes his bath there, what is the reward achieved by the people, who lives in Prayaga? You kindly tell me. You are well aware of everything. Salutation to you.”

## \|\| 1.36.19 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*kathayiṣyāmi te vatsa yā ceṣṭā yacca tatphalam \|*  
*purā maharṣibhiḥ samyak kathyamānaṃ mayā śrutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Markandeya said, “О Son, I shall speak out the reward achieved by a person who takes his bath at Prayaga. Whatever had been heard by me from the mouth of the great sages earlier, the same is going to be repeated by me.

## \|\| 1.36.20 \|\|

*etat prajāpatikṣetraṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*atra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. This is the region of Prajapati and is well known in the three world. A bath here, earns for a person a place in the heaven and those who meet with their death here, are never reborn.

## \|\| 1.36.21 \|\|

*tatra brahmādayo devā rakṣāṃ kurvanti saṃgatāḥ \|*  
*bahūnyanyāni tīrthāni sarvapāpāpahāni tu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. All the gods including Brahma collectively protect the place. There are several other places there which removes all the sins.

## \|\| 1.36.22 \|\|

*kathituṃ neha śaknomi bahuvarṣaśatairapi \|*  
*saṃkṣepeṇa pravakṣyāmi prayāgasyeha kīrtanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Its glory cannot be explained in hundreds of years. Therefore I shall narrate the glory of Prayaga, in brief.

## \|\| 1.36.23-24 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭirdhanuḥ sahastrāṇi yāni rakṣanti jāhnavīm \|*  
*yamunāṃ rakṣati sadā savitā saptavāhanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*prayāge tu viśeṣeṇa svayaṃ vasati vāsavaḥ \|*  
*maṇḍalaṃ rakṣati hariḥ sarvadevaiśca sammitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The region of Prayaga is spread in an area of sixty thousand Dahnus, that includes Ganga. The sun-god mounted over the chariot of seven horses, protects the river Yamuna. Indra particularly dwells in Prayaga. Lord Visnu, together with all the gods, protects the entire area of Prayaga.

## \|\| 1.36.25 \|\|

*nyagrodhaṃ rakṣate nityaṃ śūlapāṇirmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sthānaṃ rakṣanti vai devāḥ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Mahes'vara-the holder of the trident, protects the Nvagrodha (holy fig-tree) for ever, then all the gods protect this place which is the remover of all the sins.

## \|\| 1.36.26 \|\|

*svakarmaṇāvṛto loko naiva gacchati tatpadam \|*  
*svalpaṃ svalpataraṃ pāpaṃ yadā tasya narādhipa \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О King, the people having been surrounded by the sins and those whose slightest sins are left with them, are unable to visit that place.

## \|\| 1.36.27-28 \|\|

*prayāgaṃ smaramāṇasya sarvamāyāti saṃkṣayam \|\| 27\|\|*

*muttikālambhanād vāpi naraḥ pāpāt pramucyate \|*  
*pañca kuṇḍāni rājendra yeṣāṃ madhye tu jāhnavī \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. With the mere remembering of the name of Prayaga, or the sight of the place or wdth the reciting of its name, all the sins of a person are washed out. О Son, the touch of the dust of that place removes all the sins. There are five kundas there, through which flows the holy Ganga.

## \|\| 1.36.29-30 \|\|

*prayāgaṃ viśataḥ puṃsaḥ pāpaṃ naśyati tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahastreṣu gaṅgāṃ yaḥ smarate naraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*api duṣkṛtakarmāsau labhate paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*kīrtanānmucyate pāpād dṛṣṭvā bhadrāṇi paśyati \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The moment a person enters the city of Prayaga, all his sins are removed. A person who remembers the Ganga thousands of yojanas away, he, inspite of his being a grave sinner, achieves liberation. With reciting of its name, a person is freed from his sins and at the sight of the same, one achieves welfare.

## \|\| 1.36.31 \|\|

*tathopaspṛśya rājendra svargaloke mahīyate \|*  
*vyādhito yadi vā dīnaḥ krūddho vāpi bhavennaraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In case an ailing person, miserable or an angered person, sips the water of the Ganga, he achieves great glory in the heaven.

## \|\| 1.36.32-33 \|\|

*pitṛṇāṃ tārakañcaiva sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*yaiḥ prayāge kṛto vāsa uttīrṇo bhavasāgaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*gaṅgāyamunamāsādya tyajet prāṇān prayatnataḥ \|*  
*dīptakāñcanavarṇābhairvimānairbhānuvarṇibhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The holy place of Prayaga, destroys all the sins, redeems the manes, therefore, those who live in Prayaga, they should be taken as having been redeemed from the ocean of the universe. The excellent sages say that a person who making all the efforts goes to the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna and ends his life there, he achieves the desired fruits.

## \|\| 1.36.34-35 \|\|

*īpsitāṃllabhate kāmān vadanti munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*sarvaratnamayairdivyairnānādhvajasamākulaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*varāṅganāsamākīrṇairmodate śubhalakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*gītavāditranirghoṣaiḥ prasuptaḥ pratibudhyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Such a person enjoys his stay in the divine plane, having the shade of the molten gold, stationed on the sphere of the sun, studded with the divine gems all over, with various banners fluttering, and crowded with damsels. After his sleep, he is woken up with several songs and playing on musical instruments.

## \|\| 1.36.36 \|\|

*yāvanna smarate janma tāpat svarge mahīyate \|*  
*tasmāt svargāt paribhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇakarmā narottama \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Even before he remembers his birth, he is honoured in heaven. Therefore, О Best of the people, with the decline of the merits, he falls from the heaven.

## \|\| 1.36.37 \|\|

*hiraṇyaratnasaṃpūrṇe samṛddhe jāyate kule \|*  
*tadeva smarate tīrthaṃ smaraṇāt tatra gacchati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then he is reborn in a prosperous family possessing gems studded in gold and other precious stones. Then he remembers the same holy place of Prayaga and by so doing, he reaches there.

## \|\| 1.36.38-39 \|\|

*deśastho yadi vāraṇye videśe yadi vā gṛhe \|*  
*prayāgaṃ smaramāṇastu yastu prāṇān parityajet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*brahmalokamavāpnoti vadanti munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmaphalā vṛkṣā mahī yatra hiraṇmayī \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. A person who with his mind devoted in Prayaga, meets with his end in a city, forest, or a foreign country, he achieves Brahmaloka. This is what has been ordained by the best of sages. The land of Brahmaloka is where the earth is golden and contains trees yielding all desires.

## \|\| 1.36.40-41 \|\|

*ṛṣayo munayaḥ siddhāstatra loke sa gacchati \|*  
*strīsahastrākule ramye mandākinyāstaṭe śubhe \|\| 40 \|\|*

*modate munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ svakṛteneha karmaṇā \|*  
*siddhacāraṇagandharvaiḥ pūjyate divi daivataiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. He achieves the loka, which is the dwelling place of the Rishis, sages and the siddhas. The said person enjoys all the pleasures earned by his merits over the charming banks of the river MandakinI and is adored by the Siddhas, Caranas, Gandharvas, the Gods and the Danavas.

## \|\| 1.36.42-43 \|\|

*tataḥ svargāt paribhraṣṭo jambudvīpapatirbhavet \|*  
*tataḥ śubhāni karmāṇi cintayānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*guṇavān vittasaṃpanno bhavatīha na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā satyadharmapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. After falling from the heaven, he becomes the lord of Jambudvipa. Then thinking about the noble deeds, he turns virtuous as well as possesses high character. He is then established in dharma (truth and piety) by his action, thought and behaviour.

## \|\| 1.36.44-45 \|\|

*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye yastu grāmaṃ pratīcchati \|*  
*suvarṇamatha muktāṃ vā tathaivānyān pratigrahān \|\| 44 \|\|*

*svakārye pitṛkārye vā devatābhyarcane 'pi vā \|*  
*niṣphalaṃ tasya tat tīrthaṃ yāvat tatphalamaśnute \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. A person, who at the time of the adoration of the gods, performing the rites for manes, at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, and receives charity, food, gold, jewels, or any other thing, he then enjoys the reward of the same. Thereafter his stay at the holy place becomes infnictuous.

## \|\| 1.36.46 \|\|

*atastīrthe na gṛhṇīyāt puṇyeṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*nimitteṣu ca sarveṣu apramatto dvijo bhavet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Therefore, one should not receive charities in the holy places as well as the temples. The Brahman as, should remain alert in all the situations.

## \|\| 1.36.47-48 \|\|

*kapilāṃ pāṭalāvarṇāṃ yastu dhenuṃ prayacchati \|*  
*svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ cailakaṇṭhāṃ payasvinīm \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasya yāvanti lomāni santi gatreṣu sattama \|*  
*tāvad varṣasahastrāṇi rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. О Best of the persons, a person who gives away in charity at Prayaga, a white, red or black milking cow, with horns and hoofs covered with gold and gems, covering its body with garments from back to the ears, he gets established in the Rudraloka, for the number of years, equivalent to the number hair on the cow's body.

## Chapter 37. The Glory of Prayaga

## \|\| 1.37.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*kathayiṣyāmi te vatsa tīrthayātrāvidhikramam \|*  
*ārṣeṇa tu vidhānena yathā dṛṣṭaṃ yathā śrutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The sage Markandeya said, ‘‘I shall explain the sequence and procedure of the pilgrimage to the holy centres. This is the procedure, which has been witnessed or heard on the basis of the ancient tradition. I am going to repeat the same to you.

## \|\| 1.37.2 \|\|

*prayāgatīrthayātrārtho yaḥ prayāti naraḥ kvacit \|*  
*balīvardaṃ samārūḍhaḥ śṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When a person desirous of going on pilgrimage to Prayaga, mounted over a bull, you listen to the related reward.

## \|\| 1.37.3-4 \|\|

*tato nivartate ghoro gavāṃ krodho hi dāruṇaḥ \|*  
*salilaṃ ca na gṛhṇanti pitarastasya dehinaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*salilaṃ ca na gṛhṇanti pitarastasya dehinaḥ \|*  
*yastu putrāṃstathā bālān snāpayet pāyayet tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. A person who travels for pilgrimage mounted over the bull, falls in the hell for thousands of kalpas. On his return home, the rage of all the cows and bulls falls on him. If a man leaves off his sons in their childhood without food to eat, the Pitrs do not accept the water libations offered by him.

## \|\| 1.37.5-7 \|\|

*yathātmanā tathā sarvān dānaṃ vipreṣu dāpayet \|*  
*aiśvaryāllobhamohād vā gacched yānena yo naraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*niṣphalaṃ tasya tat tīrthaṃ tasamādyānaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye yastu kanyāṃ prayacchati \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ārṣeṇa tu vivāhena yathā vibhavavistaram \|*  
*na sa paśyati taṃ ghoraṃ narakaṃ tena karmaṇā \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Thereafter, he should give away all his belongings in charity to the Brahmanas. A person who because of his possessing fortunes, greed or confusion, undertakes the pilgrimage travelling in a vehicle, his pilgrimage becomes infructuous. Therefore, no vehicle should be used. A person who at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna performs kanyadana according to the Arsa procedure (i.e., pertaining to sages), he because of the merit of the same, never has to face the hell.

## \|\| 1.37.8-11 \|\|

*uttarān sa kurūn gatvā modate kālamakṣayam \|*  
*vaṭamūlaṃ samāśritya yastu prāṇān parityajet \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sarvalokānatikramya rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*tatra brahmādayo devā diśaśca sadigīśvarāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*lokapālāśca siddhāśca pitaro lokasaṃmatāḥ \|*  
*sanatkumārapramukhāstathā brahmarṣayo 'pare \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nāgāḥ supārṇāḥ siddhāśca tathā nityaṃ samāsate \|*  
*hariśca bhagavānāste prajāpatipuraskṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. Then he, reaching Kuruksetra in the north, enjoys pleasures for a long time. A Brahmana, who taking refuge of the banyan tree, meets with the end of his life, he transgressing the heaven reaches Rudraloka, which is the dwelling place of Brahma and the gods, all the directions with their lord, all the Lokapalas, the manes who are the dwellers of Pitrloka, Sanatkumara and other Rishis, besides BrahmaRishis, Nagas, Supramas, and Siddhas. Lord Visnu honoured by Prajapati also lives there.

## \|\| 1.37.12 \|\|

*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye pṛthivyā jaghanaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*prayāgaṃ rājaśārdūla triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О Excellent king, “The holy place of Prayaga, which is the place of the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, is the hip or the centre of the earth. Because of this it is well known, the world over.

## \|\| 1.37.13 \|\|

*tatrābhiṣekaṃ yaḥ kuryāt saṃgame saṃśitavrataḥ \|*  
*tulyaṃ phalavāpnoti rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A person performing the praiseworthy religious vows, taking bath in the confluence appropriately, he earns the merit equivalent to the Rajasuya1 and the horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.37.14-15 \|\|

*na mātṛvacanāt tāta na lokavacanādapi \|*  
*matirutkramaṇīyā te prayāgagāmanaṃ prati \|\| 14 \|\|*

*daśa tīrtha sahastrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathāpare \|*  
*teṣāṃ sānnidhyamatraiva tīrthānāṃ kurunandana \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Therefore, О Dear one, one should not change the decision for visiting Prayaga, even at the instance of one's own mother or anyone else. О Son of Kum, one gets the association of sixty thousand tlrthas and other sixty crores of sacred places here.

## \|\| 1.37.16 \|\|

*yā gatiryogayuktasya sattvasthasya manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*sā gatistyajataḥ prāṇān gaṅgāyamunasaṃgame \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The merits which are earned by the Yogins, Sannyasins, or the learned persons, the same merits are achieved by a person who gives up his life at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna.

## \|\| 1.37.17 \|\|

*na te jīvanti loke 'smin yatra tatra yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*ye prayāgaṃ na saṃprāptāstriṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О Yudhisthira, the people who live here and there on earth, do not live a real life in this world, unless they visit Prayaga. Those who have not reached Prayaga, they are the most deceived ones in the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.37.18 \|\|

*evaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tat tīrthaṃ prayāgaṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ śaśāṅka iva rāhuṇā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus by seeing the holy place of Prayaga, the greatest region, a person is freed of all the sins like the moon from the clutches of Rahu.

## \|\| 1.37.19 \|\|

*kambalāśvatarau nāgau yamunādakṣiṇe taṭe \|*  
*tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On the southern bank of the river Yamuna, there live two Nagas known by the names of Kambala and Asvatara. By taking a bath there and sipping its water, a person is relived of all his sins.

## \|\| 1.37.20 \|\|

*tatra gatvā naraḥ sthānaṃ mahādevasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṃ tārayet pūrvaṃ daśātītān daśāparān \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. An intelligent person, by taking a bath there, redeems ten past and ten future generations by the grace of Shiva.

## \|\| 1.37.21 \|\|

*kṛtvābhiṣekaṃ tu naraḥ so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*svargalokamavāpnoti yāvadāhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By taking a bath there, a person earns the merit of Asvamedha sacrifice and live in the heaven till the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 1.37.22 \|\|

*pūrvapārśve tu gaṅgāyāstrailokyakhyātimān nṛpa \|*  
*avacaḥ sarvasāmudraḥ pratiṣṭhānaṃ ca viśrutam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Towards the eastern region of the Ganga, there is a cavity which is known to have the water of all the oceans, known by the name of Avatakupa. The sacred place of Pratisthana is also established there.

## \|\| 1.37.23 \|\|

*brahmacārī jitakrodhastrirātraṃ yadi tiṣṭhati \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 23 \|\|*
