3-4. Sanatkumara, the great lord always adores lord Brahma, the chief of the Devas, the soul of the universe, there. With his soul absorbed in Yoga, he drinks the excellent nectar. He stays there while being worshipped by the Siddhas, Rishis, Gandharvas, besides the gods.

## \|\| 1.46.5 \|\|

*tatra devādidevasya śaṃbhoramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*dīptamāyatanaṃ śubhraṃ purastād brahmaṇaḥ sthitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is a splendid and brilliant abode of lord Shiva, of immeasurable splendour, the overload of Devas, in front of the abode of god Brahma.

## \|\| 1.46.6 \|\|

*divyakāntisamāyuktaṃ caturdhāraṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*maharṣigaṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ brahmavidbhirniṣevitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It possesses the divine lustre, having four gates. It is extremely beautiful. It is surrounded by the great Rishis and is served by the ascetics well-versed in Brahman.

## \|\| 1.46.7 \|\|

*devyā saha mahādevaḥ śaśāṅkārkāgnilocanaḥ \|*  
*ramate tatra viśveśaḥ pramathaiḥ pramatheśvaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Lord Shiva, the ruler of the universe, having the moon, sun and fire as his eyes, enjoy sports there with the goddess Parvati accompanied by the Pramathas (goblins, ghosts and other attendants of Shiva).

## \|\| 1.46.8 \|\|

*tatra vedavidaḥ śāntā munayo brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*pūjayanti mahādevaṃ tāpasāḥ satyavādinaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Rishis with peaceful mind, well-versed in the Vedas, Brahmacarls and the truthful sages adore lord Mahadeva there by means of their penance.

## \|\| 1.46.9 \|\|

*teṣāṃ sākṣānmahādevo munīnāṃ brahmavādinām \|*  
*gṛhṇāti pūjāṃ śirasā pārvatyā parameśvaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The worship performed by those sages of lord Mahadeva and Parvati, is accepted by the divine couple gracefully.

## \|\| 1.46.10 \|\|

*tatraiva parvatavare śakrasya paramā purī \|*  
*nāmnāmarāvatī pūrve sarvaśobhāsamanvitā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The excellent city of AmravatT, belonging to Indra, is located to the east of the excellent Meru mountain, which is endowed with all splendour and beauty.

## \|\| 1.46.11 \|\|

*tamindramapsaraḥ saṅghā gandharvā gītatatparāḥ \|*  
*upāsate sahastrākṣaṃ devāstatra sahastraśaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The groups of Apsaras, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Caranas and the gods in thousands, adore Indra having a thousand eyes.

## \|\| 1.46.12 \|\|

*ye dhārmikā vedavido yāgahomaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tat paramaṃ sthānaṃ devānāmapi durlabham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Those who are quite religious-minded and well-versed in the Vedas, besides being devoted to the performing of homas, the place is best suited for them; which is beyond the reach of the gods.

## \|\| 1.46.13 \|\|

*tasya dakṣiṇadigbhāge vahneramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*tejovatī nāma purī divyāścaryasamanvitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. To the south of the Meru mountain, there is the city of Agni, known by the name of Tejovatl, which is full of surprises.

## \|\| 1.46.14 \|\|

*tatrāste bhagavān vahnirbhrājamānaḥ svatejasā \|*  
*japināṃ homināṃ sthānaṃ dānavānāṃ durāsadam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Lord Agni, who illumines with his own lustre, lives there. This place is the abode of the people performing the japas and homas, and is beyond the reach of the Danavas.

## \|\| 1.46.15 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe parvatavare yamasyāpi mahāpurī \|*  
*nāmnā saṃyamanī divyā siddhagandharvasevitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. To the south of the excellent mountain, there is a great city of Yamraja, the god of death, known as SamyamanI, and which is divine and endowed with all types of splendour.

## \|\| 1.46.16 \|\|

*tatra vaivasvataṃ devaṃ devādyāḥ paryupāsate \|*  
*sthānaṃ tat satyasaṃdhānāṃ loke puṇyakṛtāṃ nṛṇām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The gods and others adore lord Vaivasvata (i.e. Yama) there. The place is meant for the auspicious and truthful souls.

## \|\| 1.46.17 \|\|

*tasyāstu paścime bhāge nirṛtestu mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*rakṣovatī nāma purī rākṣasaiḥ sarvato vṛtā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. To the west of the said mountain, there is the city named Raksovatl, which belongs to the lord Nirrti and is surrounded by the Raksasas from all the sides.

## \|\| 1.46.18 \|\|

*tatra taṃ nirṛtiṃ devaṃ rākṣasāḥ paryupāsate \|*  
*gacchanti tāṃ dharmaratā ye vai tāmasavṛttayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The demons adore the lord Nairrta there. Those who are devoted to piety but whose deeds are urged by Tamas, go to that place.

## \|\| 1.46.19 \|\|

*paścime parvatavare varuṇasya mahāpurī \|*  
*nāmnā suddhavatī puṇyā sarvakāmardhisaṃyutā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. T0 the west of the mountain, there is the city of Varuna, known as Suddhavatl. It is quite auspicious, which fulfills all the desires and bestows welfare.

## \|\| 1.46.20 \|\|

*tatrāpsarogaṇaiḥ siddhaiḥ sevyamāno 'marādhipaḥ \|*  
*āste sa varuṇo rājā tatra gacchanti ye 'mbudāḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātrāparī nityaṃ ye ca loke 'dhamarṣiṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. King Varuna is being adored there by celestial damsels, Siddhas and the lord of immortal beings. Only such of the people who donate water, reach that place.

## \|\| 1.46.21 \|\|

*tasyā uttaradigbhāge vāyorapi mahāpurī \|*  
*nāmnā gandhavatī puṇyā tatrāste 'sau prabhañjanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. То the north of Varunapurl, there is an auspicious place of the wind-god, known as Gandhavatl. The wind-god lives there.

## \|\| 1.46.22 \|\|

*apsarogaṇagandharvaiḥ sevyamāno 'maraprabhuḥ \|*  
*prāṇāyāmaparāmartyāsthānantadyānti śāśvatam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The great wind-god is served by the apsaras and the Gandharvas. Only such of the Brahmanas who are devoted to Pranayamas1 can live there.

## \|\| 1.46.23 \|\|

*tasyāḥ pūrveṇa digbhāge somasya paramā purī \|*  
*nāmnā kāntimatī śubhrā tatra somo virājate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. То the east of that city, there is a city named Kantimati which belongs to the moon-god. The moon-god lives there.

## \|\| 1.46.24 \|\|

*tatra ye bhoganiratā svadharmaṃ puryapāsate \|*  
*teṣāṃ tad racitaṃ sthānaṃ nānābhogasamanvitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Such of the people who follow dharma, the place is meant for such people, who can enjoy all the pleasures there.

## \|\| 1.46.25 \|\|

*tasyāśca pūrvadigbhāge śaṅkarasya mahāpurī \|*  
*nāmnā yaśovatī puṇyā sarveṣāṃ sudurāsadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. To the east of the moon's city, there is the city of Shiva, known by the name of Yasovatl, which is beyond the reach of all.

## \|\| 1.46.26 \|\|

*tatreśānasya bhavanaṃ rudraviṣṇutanoḥ śubham \|*  
*ghameśvarasya vipulaṃ tatrāste sa gaṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The palace of Is'ana, Shiva, the lord of Ganas, is located there. Rudra lives there. The vast palace of Ganesvara is also located there where he lives surrounded by the Lord of Ganas.

## \|\| 1.46.27 \|\|

*tatra bhogābhilipsūnāṃ bhaktānāṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*nivāsaḥ kalpitaḥ pūrvaṃ devadevena śūlinā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In earlier times, Paramesthin Shiva, the holder of trident, had conceived that place as the dwelling complex for his devotees.

## \|\| 1.46.28 \|\|

*viṣṇupādād viniṣkrāntā plāvayitvendumaṇḍalam \|*  
*samantād brahmaṇaḥ puryāṃ gaṅgā patati vai divaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The Ganga which emerged from the feet of lord Visnu, flowing through the lunar region, falls round the city of god Brahma.

## \|\| 1.46.29 \|\|

*sā tatra patitā dikṣu caturdhā hyabhavad dvijāḥ \|*  
*sītā cālakanandā ca sucakṣurbhadranāmikā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О Brahmanas, falling there, she became divided into four branches in accordance with the four quarters, known as Slta, Alakananda, Sucaksu and Bhadra.

## \|\| 1.46.30 \|\|

*pūrveṇa sītā śailāt tu śailaṃ yātyantarikṣataḥ \|*  
*tataśca pūrvavarṣeṇa bhadrāśvenaiti cārṇavam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Slta (Ganga) flowing from one mountain to the other, flows to the east of Meru through the sub-continent across Bhadrasva, and then joins the ocean.

## \|\| 1.46.31 \|\|

*tathaivālakanandā ca dakṣiṇādetya bhāratam \|*  
*prayāti sāgaraṃ bhittvā saptabhedā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. О Best of the sages, similarly Alakananda, entering Bharata-varsa from the south of the Meru, is divided into the seven parts, and it flows towards the ocean.

## \|\| 1.46.32 \|\|

*sucakṣuḥ paścimagirīnatītya sakalāṃstathā \|*  
*paścimaṃ ketumālākhyaṃ varṣaṃ gatvaiti cārṇavam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Similarly, the river Sucaksu, crossing all the mountains from the western region, enters Ketumala-varsa and then joins the ocean.

## \|\| 1.46.33 \|\|

*bhadrā tathottaragirīnuttarāṃśca tathā kurūn \|*  
*atītya cottarāmbhodhiṃ samabhyeti maharṣayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О Great Rishis, Bhadra on the other hand, passing through northern mountain ranges, flows through the region of northern Kurus, joins the northern ocean.

## \|\| 1.46.34 \|\|

*ānīlaniṣadhāyāmau mālyavān gandhamādanaḥ \|*  
*tayormadhyagato meruḥ karṇikākārasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The vast Malyavan and Gandhamadana mountains are spreading upto Nila and Nisadha mountain. Meru is lodged in the centre of both of them as the pericarp of a lotus.

## \|\| 1.46.35 \|\|

*bhāratāḥ ketumālāśca bhadrāśvāḥ kuravastathā \|*  
*patrāṇi lokapadmasya maryādāśailabāhyataḥ \|\| 1.46.35 \|\|*

35\. The sub-continents like, Bharata, Ketumala, Bhadrasva and Kurus are the petals of the lotus of the universe outside the Border-mountains.

## \|\| 1.46.36 \|\|

*jaṭharo devakūṭaśca maryādāparvatāvubhau \|*  
*dakṣiṇottaramāyāmāvānīlaniṣadhāyatau \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Towards the" south to the north, the boundary mountains of Jathara and Devakuta are spreading upto the Nila and Nisadha mountains.

## \|\| 1.46.37 \|\|

*gandhamādanakailāsau pūrvapaścāyatāvubhau \|*  
*aśītiyojanāyāmāvarṇavāntarvyavasthitau \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Gandhamadana and Kailasa, are lodged to the east and west respectively. Both of them go deep within the ocean extending upto eighty Yojanas.

## \|\| 1.46.38 \|\|

*niṣadhaḥ pāriyātraśca maryādāparvatāvimau \|*  
*meroḥ paścimadigbhāge yathāpūrvau tathā sthitau \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The mountains known by the name of Nisadha and Pariyatra are located with their limits touching to the west of the Meru.

## \|\| 1.46.39 \|\|

*triśṛṅgo jārudhaistadvaduttare varṣaparvatau \|*  
*pūrvapaścāyatāvetau arṇavāntarvyavasthitau \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Similarly, two mountains known by the name of Trias'niga and Jarudhi, are located in the north. Both of them run east and west, reaching the oceans ultimately.

## \|\| 1.46.40 \|\|

*maryādāparvatāḥ proktā aṣṭāviha mayā dvijāḥ \|*  
*jaṭharādyāḥ sthitā meroścaturdikṣu maharṣayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О Brahmanas, thus, I have described the eight border-mountains. These mountains like Jathara and others are located around the Meru mountain.

## Chapter 47. Division of the Earth

## \|\| 1.47.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ketumāle narāḥ kālāḥ sarve panasabhojanāḥ \|*  
*striyaścotpalapatrābhā jīvanti ca varṣāyutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, Ketumala's people are of black colour like the crows, and they consume the jack fruit. The women of the land are extremely beautiful having the complexion of the lotus leaves. All of them live upto the age of ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.47.2 \|\|

*bhadrāśve puruṣāḥ śuklāḥ striyaścandrāṃśusannibhāḥ \|*  
*daśa varṣasahastrāṇi jīvante āmrabhojanāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The people of the Bhadras'va region, are of fair complexion and the women have the white complexion resembling the moon rays. All of them consume the cereals and live to the age of ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.47.3 \|\|

*ramyake puruṣā nāryo ramante rajataprabhāḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣasahastrāṇi śatāni daśa pañca ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The men and women of the Ramyaka-varsa have the complexion of silver and they sport for eleven thousand five hundred years. Getting established in their own temperament, they consume the Nyagrodha fruits as their food and adhere to Sattvaguna.

## \|\| 1.47.4-5 \|\|

*hiraṇmaye hiraṇyābhāḥ sarve ca lakucāśanāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ekādaśasahastrāṇi śatāni daśa pañca ca \|*  
*jīvanti puruṣā nāryo devalokasthitā iva \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. In the Hiranmaya-varsa, the people have the complexion of gold who consume the fruit of coconut trees. All the men and women have the life of twelve thousand and five hundred years each. They live the divine life.

## \|\| 1.47.6 \|\|

*trayodaśasahastrāṇi śatāni daśa pañca ca \|*  
*jīvanti kuruvarṣe tu śyāmāṅgāḥ kṣīrabhojanāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The people of Kuruvarsa, live on milk alone. They have dark-complexion, and the longevity of their life is fourteen thousand and five hundred years, each.

## \|\| 1.47.7 \|\|

*sarve mithunajātāśca nityaṃ sukhaniṣevinaḥ \|*  
*candradvīpe mahādevaṃ yajanti satataṃ śivam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In Candradvipa, the people are bom by sexual intercourse, enjoy all the pleasures. They daily adore lord Shiva, the great lord.

## \|\| 1.47.8 \|\|

*tathā kiṃpuruṣe viprā mānavā hemasannibhāḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣahastrāṇi jīvanti plakṣabhojanāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then the Kimpurusa-varsa is inhabited by the people of the Brahmana race, having the reflection of gold. They live on the fruits of the holy fig tree and enjoy the age of ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.47.9 \|\|

*yajanti satataṃ devaṃ caturmūrti caturmukham \|*  
*dhyāne manaḥ samādhāya sādaraṃ bhaktisaṃyutāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They having been filled with devotion, concentrating their minds, always adore the four-armed and four-faced lord Brahma.

## \|\| 1.47.10 \|\|

*tathā ca harivarṣe tu mahārajatasannibhāḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣasahastrāṇi jīvantīkṣurasāśinaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Similarly, the people living in the Harivarsha, have the complexion of gold, they consume the sugarcane juice, and live upto the age of ten thousand years.

## \|\| 1.47.11 \|\|

*tatra nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ viśvayoniṃ sanātanam \|*  
*upāsate sadā viṣṇuṃ mānavā viṣṇubhāvitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The people of this place, devoting themselves to lord Visnu, always adore lord Narayana, the eternal source of the origin of the universe.

## \|\| 1.47.12 \|\|

*tatra candraprabhaṃ śubhraṃ śuddhasphaṭikanirmitam \|*  
*vimānaṃ vāsudevasya pārijātavanāśritam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There is a palace of Vasudeva, in the grove of Parijata tree, which is white in colour resembling the illustrious moon or like the crystal gem.

## \|\| 1.47.13 \|\|

*caturdhāramanopamyaṃ catustoraṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*prākārairdaśabhiryuktaṃ durādharṣaṃ sudurgamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It has four gates, an equal number of toranas (arched door-ways), and ten boundary walls. It is unique, inaccessible and invincible.

## \|\| 1.47.14 \|\|

*sphāṭikairmaṇḍapairyuktaṃ devarājagṛhopamam \|*  
*svarṇastambhasahastraiśca sarvataḥ samalaṅkṛtam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It has the mandapas (halls) of crystal stones, resembling the palace of Indra. It is decorated with thousand pillars of gold which are well decorated.

## \|\| 1.47.15 \|\|

*hemasopānasaṃyuktaṃ nānāratnopaśobhitam \|*  
*divyasiṃhāsanopetaṃ sarvaśobhāsamanvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It has the stepes of gold, studded with various types of gems. It has divine lion thrones, and has several types of decorations.

## \|\| 1.47.16-17 \|\|

*sarobhiḥ svādupānīyairnadībhiścopaśobhitam \|*  
*nārāyaṇaparaiḥ śuddhairvedādhyayanatatparaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yogibhiśca samākīrṇaṃ dhyāyadbhiḥ puruṣaṃ harim \|*  
*stuvadbhiḥ satataṃ mantrairnamasyadbhiśca mādhavam \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. It has a number of lakes and rivers with sweet water. This place abounds in Yogins devoted to Narayana, and is quite auspicious. The people of this place are engaged in the study of the Vedas. The Yogins here are devoted to Hari. They always recite the mantras in praise of Madhava.

## \|\| 1.47.18-19 \|\|

*tatra devādidevasya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*rājānaḥ sarvakālaṃ tu mahimānaṃ prakurvate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*gāyanti caiva nṛtyanti vilāsinyo manoramāḥ \|*  
*striyo yauvanaśālinyaḥ sadā maṇḍanatatparāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The kings of that place alwhys . recite the glory of lord Visnu of unmeasured splendour, the overlord of Devas. The passionate young women there, decorating themselves variously, keep on singing and dancing.

## \|\| 1.47.20 \|\|

*ilāvṛte padmavarṇā jambūphalarasāśinaḥ \|*  
*trayodaśa sahastrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ vai sthirāyuṣaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The people of the Ilavrta-varsa, have the complexion of lotus flowers, consume the juice of Jambu fruits, and live upto the age of thirteen thousand years.

## \|\| 1.47.21 \|\|

*bhārate tu striyaḥ puṃso nānāvarṇāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*nānādevārcane yuktā nānākarmāṇi kurvate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The men and the women of Bharata-varsa, are of various complexions. They adore different types of gods, and are engaged in various types of holy rites and professions.

## \|\| 1.47.22 \|\|

*paramāyuḥ smṛtaṃ teṣāṃ śataṃ varṣāṇi suvratāḥ \|*  
*nānāhārāśca jīvanti puṇyapāpanimittataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О Sages of holy vows, their age is said to be of a hundred years. The Bharata-varsa is spread in an area of nine thousand Yojanas.

## \|\| 1.47.23-25 \|\|

*navayojanasāhastraṃ varṣametat prakīrtitam \|*  
*karmabhūmiriyaṃ viprā narāṇāmadhikāriṇām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimānṛkṣaparvataḥ \|*  
*vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca saptātra kulaparvatāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*indradyumnaḥ kaśerumāṃstāmravarṇo gabhastimān \|*  
*nāgadvīpastathā saumyo gandharvastvatha vāruṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. О Brahmanas, this is the land of holy rites of those people who are eligible. There are seven important mountains known by the names of Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Shaktiman, Rksaparvata, Vindhya, and Pariyatra. Bharatavarsa is lodged at the seashore comprising of the eight other dvipas viz., Indradvipa, Kaserukman, Tamrapama, Gabhastiman, Nagadvipa, Saumya, Gandharva and Vanina.

## \|\| 1.47.26-27 \|\|

*ayaṃ tu navamasteṣāṃ dvīpaḥ sāgarasaṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahastraṃ tu dvīpo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇottaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pūrve kirātāstasyānte paśicame yavanāstathā \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśya madhye śūdrāstathaiva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The dvipa is spread in an area of a thousand Yojanas from south to the north. Kirat is lodged to its east, Yavana in the west, and the people who live herein are the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vais'yas and Sudras. Ksatriyas and Vaisyas earn their livelihood, by performing Yajnas, waging wars and dealing in trade. The Stidras stay amongst them serving them.

## \|\| 1.47.28-29 \|\|

*ijyāyuddhavaṇijyābhirvartayantyatra mānavāḥ \|*  
*stravante pāvanā nadyaḥ parvatebhyo viniḥ sṛtāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śatadruścandrabhāgā ca sarayūryamunā tathā \|*  
*irāvatī vitastā ca vipāśā devikā kuhūḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. On this part of the earth, there flow many holy rivers, starting from the mountains. Satadra, Chandrabhaga, Sarayu, Yamuna, Iravatl, Vitasta (Jehlam), Vipas'a, Devika (Dek), Kuhfl, Gomatl. Dhutapapa, Bahuda, Drsadvatl, Kaus'iki, and Lohini, are the rivers which start from Himalaya.

## \|\| 1.47.30-31 \|\|

*gomatī dhūtapāpā ca bāhudā ca dṛṣadvatī \|*  
*kauśikī lohitā caiva himavatpādaniḥ sṛtāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*vedasmṛtirvedavatī vrataghnī tridivā tathā \|*  
*parṇāśā vandanā caiva sadānīrā manoramā \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The rivers like Vedasmrti, Vedavatl, VrataghnI, Tridiva, Varnas'a, Candana, Carmanvatl, Sura, Vidisa and Vetravatl originate from the Pariyatra mountain.

## \|\| 1.47.32-33 \|\|

*carmaṇvatī tathā dūryā vidiśā vetravatyapi \|*  
*śigruḥ svaśilpāpi tathā pāriyātrāśrayāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*narmadā surasā śoṇa daśārṇā ca mahānadī \|*  
*mandākinī citrakūṭā tāmasī ca piśācikā \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The sacred rivers like Narmada, Surasa, Sona, Das'arna, MahanadI, MandakinI, Citrakuta, Tamasi, Pisacika, Citrotpala, Visala, Manjula, and ValuvahinI, issue from the middle of the Rksavan mountain and remove all the sins of the people.

## \|\| 1.47.34-35 \|\|

*citrotpalā vipāśā ca mañjulā vāluvāhinī \|*  
*ṛkṣavatpādajā nadyaḥ sarvapāpaharā nṛṇām \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tāpī payoṣṇī nirvindhyā śīghrodā ca mahānadī \|*  
*veṇyā vaitaraṇī caiva balākā ca kumudvatī \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. The rivers like Tapi, Payosnl, Nirvindhya, Slghroda, MahanadI, Vinna, VaitaranI, Balaka, Kumudvatl, Mahagaurl, Durga and Antahs'ila, start from the Vindhyacala mountain, which remove all the sins of the people in an instant.

## \|\| 1.47.36 \|\|

*toyā caiva mahāgairī durgā cāntaḥ śilā tathā \|*  
*vindhyapādaprasūtāstā nadyaḥ puṇyajalāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Best of the Brahmanas, Godavari, Bhlmarathl, Krisna, Vena, Vas'yata, Tungabhadra, Suprayoga and Kaverl, are the rivers of the southern region (Deccan), which issue from the Sahya mountain.

## \|\| 1.47.37-38 \|\|

*sodāvarī bhīmarathī kṛṣṇā varṇā ca matsarī \|*  
*tuṅgabhdrā suprayogā kāverī ca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇāpathagā nadyaḥ sahyapādaviniḥ sṛtāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ṛtumālā tāmraparṇo puṣpavatyutpalāvatī \|*  
*malayānniḥ sṛtā nadyaḥ sarvāḥ śītajalāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. The rivers like Rtumala, Tamrapami, Punyavatl and Utpalavatl are the rivers originating from the Malaya mountain. All these rivers flow with cool water. The rivers like Rsikulya and Trisama, pass through the Gandhamadana mountain.

## \|\| 1.47.39 \|\|

*ṛṣikulyā trisāmā ca mandagā mandagāminī \|*  
*rūpā pālāsinī caiva ṛṣikā vaṃśakāriṇī \|*  
*śuktimatpādasaṃjātāḥ sarvapāpaharā nṛṇām \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Ksipra, Palas'inI, Rslka, and Vams'adharinI, are the rivers which start from the base of the Shaktiman mountain and remove all the sins of the people.

## \|\| 1.47.40 \|\|

*āsāṃ nadyupanadyaśca śataśo dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpaharāḥ puṇyāḥ snānadānādikarmasu \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О Excellent Brahmanas, there are hundreds of tributaries to these rivers, which also remove all the sins and are good enough for taking bath and the performing of the charities over their banks, which are quite auspicious.

## \|\| 1.47.41-44 \|\|

*tāsvime kurupāñcālā madhyadeśādayo janāḥ \|*  
*pūrvadeśādikāścaiva kāmarūpanivāsinaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*puṇḍrāḥ kaliṅgāmagadhā dākṣiṇātyāścakṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*tathāparāntāḥ saurāṣṭrāḥ śūdrābhīrāstathār'budāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*mālakā mālavāścaiva pāriyātranivāsinaḥ \|*  
*sauvīrāḥ saindhavā hūṇā śālvāḥ kalpanivāsinaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*madrā rāmāstathāmbaṣṭhāḥ pārasīkāstathaiva ca \|*  
*āsāṃ pibanti salilaṃ vasanti saritāṃ sadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

41-44. The people of the middle countries are Kurus and Pailcalas. The people living in eastern region are residents of Kamanipa. The people of Pundra, Kalihga, Magadha, the entire southern region, the people of Saurastra, Sudras, Hinas (indigent ones), Arbuda, Malaka, Malapa, and those people living in the Pariyatra mountain, besides the people Sauvlra, Saindhava, Huna, Malya, dwellers of Balya country, people of Madra country, Ramas, the Andhras, and the Paraslkas live over the banks of these rivers and drink their waters.

## \|\| 1.47.45 \|\|

*catvāri bhārate varṣe yugāni kavayo 'bruvan \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliścānyatra na kvacit \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The people of learnings have spelt out that there are the four Yugas in the Bharata subcontinent, viz., Krta, Tret a, Dvapara and Kaliyuga. These Yugas are found no where else.

## \|\| 1.47.46 \|\|

*yāni kiṃpuruṣādyāni varṣāṇyaṣṭau maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*na teṣu śoko nāyāso nodvegaḥ kṣudbhayaṃ na ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. О Great sages, in the eight Varsas such as the Kimpurusa-varsa, there are no griefs nor the labour, anxieties or the hunger.

## \|\| 1.47.47 \|\|

*svasthāḥ prajā nirātaṅkāḥ sarvaduḥ khavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*ramanti vividhairbhāvaiḥ sarvāśca sthirayauvanāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. All the people there are healthy, free from terror, totally free from sufferings, having everlasting youthfulness, and enjoy all types of pleasures.

## Chapter 48. Description of Jambudvipa

## \|\| 1.48.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*hemakūṭagireḥ śṛṅge mahākūṭaiḥ suśobhanam \|*  
*sphāṭikaṃ devadevasya vimānaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “At the top of the Hemakuta mountain, there is the dwelling place of Shiva, Parmeshthin and the god of gods, which is made of crystal rock and is quite beautiful.

## \|\| 1.48.2-3 \|\|

*atha devādidevasya bhūteśasya triśūlinaḥ \|*  
*devāḥ siddhagaṇā yakṣāḥ pūjāṃ nityaṃ prakurvate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sa devo giriśaḥ sārdhaṃ mahādevyā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhūtaiḥ parivṛto nityaṃ bhāti tatra pinākadhṛk \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. He (Shiva) is adored there daily by the sages, Siddhas, as well as the gods. He is ruler of all living beings and holder of Pinaka bow as well as the trident. Lord Shiva together with his consort Parvati and his goblins always looks graceful there.

## \|\| 1.48.4 \|\|

*vibhaktacāruśikharaḥ kailāso yatra parvataḥ \|*  
*nivāsaḥ koṭiyakṣāṇāṃ kuberasya ca dhīmataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There is the Kailasa mountain with beautiful peaks, where the intelligent Kubera, together with innumerable Yaksas live.

## \|\| 1.48.5 \|\|

*tatrāpi devadevasya bhavasyāyatanaṃ mahat \|*  
*mandākinī tatra divyā ramyā suvimalodakā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is also a great abode of lord Shiva, the god of gods. There is the auspicious river Mandakini, which flows there, with its auspicious water filled with lotus flowers.

## \|\| 1.48.6-7 \|\|

*nadī nānāvidhaiḥ padmairanekaiḥ samalaṅkṛtā \|*  
*devadānavagandharvayakṣarākṣasakiṃnaraiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*upaspṛṣṭajalā nityaṃ supuṇyā sumanoramā \|*  
*anyāśca nadyaḥ śataśaḥ svarṇapadmairalaṅkṛtāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The Devas, Danavas, Gandharyas, Yaksas, Raksasas and Kinnaras, drink and take bath in the auspicious water of the river Mandakini. There are hundreds of other rivers with golden lotus flowers blossoming in them. They are holy and very beautiful.

## \|\| 1.48.8 \|\|

*tāsāṃ kūleṣu devasya sthānāni parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*devarṣigaṇajuṣṭāni tathā nārāyaṇasya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On the banks of those rivers, there is the abode of Paramesthin Shiva as well as of Narayana, who are daily served there by the gods and the Rishis.

## \|\| 1.48.9-11 \|\|

*tasyāpi śikhare śubhraṃ pārijātavanaṃ śubham \|*  
*tatra śakrasya vipulaṃ bhavanaṃ ratnamaṇḍitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sphāṭikastambhasaṃyuktaṃ hemagopurasaṃyutam \|*  
*tatrātha devadevasya viṣṇorviśvāmareśituḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*supuṇyaṃ bhavanaṃ ramyaṃ sarvaratnopaśobhitam \|*  
*tatra nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān lakṣmyā saha jagatpatiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. At the peak of Hemakuta mountain, there is the forest of the Parijata trees. There is also a gem-studded gigantic palace of Indra there, which is built in crystal stones. It has several pillars, and the domes of gold. There is also a beautiful palace made of gems for the living of Visnu, the soul of the universe, the god of gods. This is quite charming and auspicious; Visnu, the lord of the universe the excellent one, adorable one, and the eternal lord, lives there with Lakshmi.

## \|\| 1.48.12-14 \|\|

*āste sarvāmaraśreṣṭhaḥ pūjyamānaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*tathā ca vasudhāre tu vasūnāṃ ratnamaṇḍitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sthānānāmaṣṭakaṃ puṇyaṃ durādharṣaṃ suradviṣām \|*  
*ratnadhāre girivare saptarṣoṇāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*saptāśramāṇi puṇyāni siddhāvāsayutāni tu \|*  
*tatra haimaṃ caturdvāraṃ vajranīlādimaṇḍitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Similarly at the Vasudhara mountain, there is an auspicious abode of the Vasus, which is most excellent and beyond the reach of the demons. Over the auspicious mountain known as Ratnadhara, there are the dwelling places of the noble-souled seven sages. The Siddhas also live there. There is an auspicious place of Brahma which is built in gold having four entrance gates studded with diamonds, sapphire and other precious gems.

## \|\| 1.48.15-16 \|\|

*supuṇyaṃ sumahat sthānaṃ brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*tatra devarṣayo viprāḥ siddhā brahmarṣayo 'pare \|\| 15 \|\|*

*upāsate sadā devaṃ pitāmahamajaṃ param \|*  
*sa taiḥ saṃpūjito nityaṃ devyā saha caturmukhaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. О Brahmanas, the excellent god of gods, Brahma, the grandsire, is being daily adored there by DevaRishis, BrahmaRishis, Siddhas, and other people. Having been adored by all the people, Brahma, with a peaceful mind, lives there with the goddess Savitrl for the welfare of the people.

## \|\| 1.48.17-19 \|\|

*āste hitāya lokānāṃ śāntānāṃ paramā gatiḥ \|*  
*athaikaśṛṅgaśikhare mahāpadmairalaṅkṛtam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*svacchāmṛtajalaṃ puṇyaṃ sugandhaṃ sumahat saraḥ \|*  
*jaigīṣavyāśramaṃ tatra yogīndrairupaśobhitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tatrāsau bhagavān nityamāste śiṣyaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*praśāntadoṣairakṣudrairbrahmavidbhirmahātmabhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Over one of the high peaks of HemakQta, there is a great lake of nectar-like water which is quite auspicious and very fragrant. An auspicious hermit of Maharsi Jaiglsavya is located there. The sage who is spotless, with peaceful mind, well-versed in Brahman, surrounded by his disciples lives there always.

## \|\| 1.48.20-22 \|\|

*śaṅkho manoharaścaiva kauśikaḥ kṛṣṇa eva ca \|*  
*sumanā vedanādaśca śiṣyāstasya pradhānataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sarve yogaratāḥ śāntā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahāḥ \|*  
*upāsate mahāvīryā brahmavidyāparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*teṣāmanugrihārthāya yatīnāṃ śāntacetasām \|*  
*sānnidhyaṃ kurute bhūyo devyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. His prominent disciples are Sankha, Manohara, Kausika, Krshna, Sumanas, and Vedavada. All of them are devoted to Yogic activities, are peaceful, and smear their bodies with ashes, besides the great Acaryas and those devoted to the Brahman, always adore the Maharsi Jaiglsavya. In order to shower his grace over the Yogins with peaceful minds, lord Shiva, with the goddess Parvati, also lives there.

## \|\| 1.48.23-24 \|\|

*anyānicāśramāṇi syustasmin girivarottame \|*  
*munīnāṃ yuktamanasāṃ sarāṃsi saritastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*teṣu yogaratā viprā jāpakāḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇyāsaktamanaso ramante jñānatatparāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Over the peak of the excellent mountain, there are several other hermitages of the sages. There are several other lakes and the rivers there, which serve as dwelling places for the Yogins engaged in Yogic practices. The blissful Brahmanas, devoted to Brahman, the performers of Japa, of fully controlled sense-organs, and devoted to spiritual learnings, live there.

## \|\| 1.48.25 \|\|

*ātmanyātmānamādhāya śikhāntāntaramāsthitam \|*  
*dhāyāyanti devamīśānaṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. They, while establishing their soul on the supreme (cosmic) souf, meditate on the lord Isana, who stationed on the peak of the mountain, still pervades in the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.48.26 \|\|

*sumeghe vāsavasthānaṃ sahastrādityasaṃnibham \|*  
*tatrāste bhagavānindraḥ śacyā saha sureśvaraḥ \|\| 1.48.26 \|\|*

26\. The mountain Sumegha which issues lustre like thousands of Adityas, is the dwelling place for Indra. Indra, the lord of the gods, lives there with Sacl.

## \|\| 1.48.27 \|\|

*gajaśaile tu durgāyā bhavanaṃ maṇitāraṇam \|*  
*āste bhagavatī durgā tatra sākṣānmaheśvarī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The abode of Durga is lodged over Gajasaila. It has the tornas of gems. The goddess Bhagavatl lives there, who is also known as Durga and Bhavanl.

## \|\| 1.48.28 \|\|

*upāsyamānā vividhaiḥ śaktibhedairitastataḥ \|*  
*pītvā yogāmṛtaṃ labdhvā sākṣādānandamaiśvaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Consuming the Yogic nectar pertaining to lord Shiva, receiving the divine nectar directly from him, she is adored by various types of Shaktis (divine powers).

## \|\| 1.48.29-30 \|\|

*sunīlasya gireḥ śṛṅge nānādhātusamujjvale \|*  
*rākṣasānāṃ purāṇi syuḥ sarāṃsi śataśo dvijāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tathā puraśataṃ viprāḥ śataśṛṅge mahācale \|*  
*sphāṭikastambhasaṃyuktaṃ yakṣāṇāmamitaujasām \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. О Brahmanas, the peak of Sunlla mountain, is resplendent with different types of metals. There are several dwelling places of the Rakshasas there. О Brahmanas, similarly over the peak of Mahacala, there are a hundred towns of Yaksas of boundless prowess which are built in crystal pillars.

## \|\| 1.48.31-32 \|\|

*śvetodaragireḥ śṛṅge suparṇasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*prākāragopuropetaṃ maṇitoraṇamaṇḍitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sa tatra garuḍaḥ śrīmān sākṣād viṣṇurivāparaḥ \|*  
*dhyātvāste tat paraṃ jyotirātmānaṃ viṣṇumavyayam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Over the top of the Svetodara mountain, there is the abode of noble-souled Garuda, with the portals studded with the precious gems and has ramparts and arched gateways. The graceful Garuda resembling Visnu lives there, engaged in the meditation upon the Supreme, immutable refulgence, within his own Atman.

## \|\| 1.48.33 \|\|

*anyacca bhavanaṃ puṇyaṃ śrīśṛṅge munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*śrīdevyāḥ sarvaratnāḍhyaṃ haimaṃ sumaṇitoraṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O Best of Brahmanas, there is an auspicious abode of goddess Sri, at Srlsniga mountain, which is made in gold, studded with gems. It has beautiful toranas studded with gems.

## \|\| 1.48.34 \|\|

*tatra sā paramā śaktirviṣṇoratimanoramā \|*  
*anantavibhavā lakṣmīrjagatsaṃmohanotsukā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Lakshmi, the supreme Shakti of Visnu, with the enormous and endless fortunes lives them, anxious to fascinate the whole world.

## \|\| 1.48.35-36 \|\|

*adhyāste devagandharvasiddhacāraṇavanditā \|*  
*vicintya jagatoyoniṃ svaśaktikiraṇojjvalā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tatraiva devadevasya viṣṇorāyatanaṃ mahat \|*  
*sarāṃsi tatra catvāri vicitrakamalāśrayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Lakshmi, who is adored by the gods, Ganaharvas, Siddhas and Caranas, being self resplendent, devoting her mind towards lord Visnu, the cause of the universe, particularly resides there. There is the great abode of Visnu there, surrounded by four auspicious lakes, with astonishing types of lotuses blossoming there.

## \|\| 1.48.37-38 \|\|

*tathā sahastraśikhare vidyādharapurāṣṭakam \|*  
*ratnasopānasaṃyuktaṃ sarobhiścopaśobhitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nadyo vimalapānīyāścitranīlotpalākarāḥ \|*  
*karṇikāravanaṃ dvivyaṃ tatrāste śaṅkaromayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Similarly over the mountain Sahasras'ikhara (having a thousand peaks), there are eight towns of the Vidyadharas, which are studded with jewelled staircases and are embellished with lakes. The rivers with clean water flow there having several types of blue lotus flowers. There is also a divine forest of Karnikara flowers where Lord Shiva himself remains present.

## \|\| 1.48.39-40 \|\|

*pāriyātre mahāśaile mahālakṣmyāḥ puraṃ śubham \|*  
*ramyaprāsādasaṃyuktaṃ ghaṇṭācāmarabhūṣitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*nṛtyadbhirapsaraḥ saṅghairitaścetaśca śobhitam \|*  
*mṛdaṅgamurajodghuṣṭaṃ vīṇāveṇunināditam \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. There is a beautiful abode of Mahalakshmi, on the Parijata mountain, having charming palaces, decorated with the bells and flywhisks, where the apsaras dance to the tune of the musical instruments like flute, lute, tabors and Panavas, and others the sound of which echoes in the sky.

## \|\| 1.48.41-43 \|\|

*gandharvakiṃnarākīrṇaṃ saṃvṛtaṃ siddhapuṅgavaiḥ \|*  
*bhāsvadbhittisamākīrṇaṃ mahāprāsādasaṃkulam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gaṇeśvarāṅganājuṣṭaṃ dhārmikāṇāṃ sudarśanam \|*  
*tatra sā vasate devī nityaṃ yogaparāyaṇā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*mahālakṣmīrmahādevī triśūlavaradhāriṇī \|*  
*trinetrā sarvaśasaktībhiḥ saṃvṛtā sadasanmayā \|*  
*paśyanti tatra munayaḥ siddhā ye brahmavādinaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. The place is inhabited by Gandharvas and Kinnaras, besides Siddhas, and is filled with shining palatial buildings. It is served by the great Ganes'varas, and is quite an attractive place for the virtuous people. The goddess Mahalakshmi, lives there engaged in Yogic practices. The great Goddess holds a trident, has three eyes, is the combination of all the Shaktis. The sages who speak on Brahman and have accomplished various Siddhis, can only have an audience with her there.

## \|\| 1.48.44-46 \|\|

*supārśvasyottare bhāge sarasvatyāḥ purottamam \|*  
*sarāṃsi siddhajuṣṭāni devabhogyāni sattamāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*pāṇḍurasya gireḥ śṛṅge vicitradrumasaṃkule \|*  
*sandharvāṇāṃ puraśataṃ divyastrībhiḥ samāvṛtam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*teṣu nityaṃ madotsiktā varanāryastathaiva ca \|*  
*krīḍanti muditā nityaṃ vilāsairbhogatatparāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. To the north of the Suparsva mountain, there is the excellent city of Sarasvatl. О Excellent ascetics, there are several lakes there which are used by the Siddhas and being enjoyed by the gods. Over the peak of the mountain Pandura, there are a hundred cities of the Gandharvas, which are surrounded by the trees and the divine damsels The intoxicated men and women enjoy there the worldly pleasures and delightfully engage themselves in love sports forever.

## \|\| 1.48.47-48 \|\|

*añjanasya gireḥ śṛṅge nārīṇāṃ puramuttamam \|*  
*vasanti tatrāpsaraso rambhādyā ratilālasāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*citrasenādayo yatra samāyāntyarthinaḥ sadā \|*  
*sā purī sarvaratnāḍhyā naikaprastravaṇairyutā \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Over the peak of the Anjanagiri, there is the dwelling place for the apsuras. Rambha and other damsels stay there eager for their sexual exercises. Citrasena and other suppliants arrive there as beggars. The city has enough of gems and water springs.

## \|\| 1.48.49-50 \|\|

*anekāni purāṇi syuḥ kaumude cāpi suvratāḥ \|*  
*rudrāṇāṃ śāntarajasāmīśvarārpitacetasām \|\| 49 \|\|*

*teṣu rudrā mahāyogā maheśāntaracāriṇaḥ \|*  
*samāsate paraṃ jyotirārūḍhāḥ sthānamuttamam \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. О Excellent sages, over the Kaumuda mountain, there are the peaceful cities of Rudras, whose Rajoguna (or passion) is subsided. The Rudras are devoted to Is'vara. The great Rudras of Yogic power, moving in the inner circle of Is'vara, the illustrious one, live there.

## \|\| 1.48.51-53 \|\|

*piñjarasya gireḥ śṛṅge gaṇeśānāṃ puratrayam \|*  
*nandīśvarasya kapile tatrāste suyaśā yatiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tathā ca jārudhaiḥ śṛṅge devadevasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*dīptamāyatanaṃ puṇyaṃ bhāskarasyāmitaujasaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tasyaivottaradigbhāge candrasthānamanuttamam \|*  
*ramate tatra ramyo 'sau bhagavān śītadīdhitiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. Over the peak of the mountain Pinjara, there are three cities of Ganas (Shiva’s attendants). The city of Kapila, belonging to Nandlsvara, the chief of ganas, is located there, in which the wise ones are lodged. Similarly over the Jarudhi mountain, there is the auspicious abode of Bhaskara (sun-god), the god of gods who is the illustrious one. Above that place is the excellent abode of the moon-god which is located to the north. The moon-god with excellent rays and beautiful soul lives there.

## \|\| 1.48.54-56 \|\|

*anyacca bhavanaṃ divyaṃ haṃsaśaile maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*sahastrayojanāyāmaṃ suvarṇamaṇitoraṇam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tatrāste bhagavān brahmā siddhasaṅghairabhiṣṭutaḥ \|*  
*sāvitryā saha viśvātmā vāsudevādibhiryutaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tasya dakṣiṇadigbhāge siddhānāṃ puramuttamam \|*  
*sanandanādayo yatra vasanti munipuṅgavāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. О Great sages, over the Hamsa hill, there is another divine palace, which covers the area of a thousand Yojanas. It has portals which are built in gold and gems. Lord Brahma, the universal soul, with his consort Savitri, lives there and is being served by the groups of Siddhas in the company of Vasudeva. To the south of that place, there is an excellent city of the Siddhas, which is also the dwelling place of leading sages headed by Sanandana.

## \|\| 1.48.57-58 \|\|

*pañcaśailasya śikhare dānavānāṃ puratrayam \|*  
*nātidūreṇa tasyātha daityacāryasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*sugandhaśailaśikhare saridbhirupaśobhitam \|*  
*kardamasyāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ tatrāste bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. Over the peak of the Pancas'aila mountain, there are three cities of the Danavas. Close to it, there is the beautiful hermitage of the preceptor of Daityas. The holy hermitage of sage Kardama, the intelligent one, is over the peak of the Sugandha mountain, the beauty of which is heightened by rivers. The great Rishis lives there.

## \|\| 1.48.59-62 \|\|

*tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge kiñcid vai dakṣiṇāśrite \|*  
*sanatkumāro bhagavāṃstatrāste brahmavittamaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sarveṣveteṣu śaileṣu tatānyeṣu munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*sarāṃsi vimalā nadyo devānāmālayāni ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

*siddhaliṅgāni puṇyāni munibhiḥ sthāpitāni tu \|*  
*vanyānyāśramavaryāṇi saṃkhyātuṃ naiva śaknuyām \|\| 61 \|\|*

*eṣa saṃkṣepataḥ prokto jambūdvīpasya vistaraḥ \|*  
*na śakyaṃ vistarād vaktuṃ mayā varṣaśatairapi \|\| 62 \|\|*

59-62. To the east of that place somewhat towards the south, there lives the sage Sanatkumara, the best among those well-versed in Brahman. О MunIshvaras, in all these places as well as the other mountains, several lakes and reservoirs besides the rivers with cool and clean water are there, where the sages have established the auspicious Siddhalingas. These places are beyond counting by me. I have thus spoken about the expansion of Jambudvipa in brief. But full description of the same cannot be made by me even in hundreds of years.

## Chapter 49. Description of Plakshadvipa

## \|\| 1.49.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*jambūdvīpasya vistārād dviguṇena samantataḥ \|*  
*saṃveṣṭayitvā kṣārodaṃ plakṣadvīpo vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Surrounded by the ocean of milk on all the sides, the Plakshadvipa is spread in double the area as compared to Jambudvipa.

## \|\| 1.49.2 \|\|

*plakṣadvīpe ca viprendrāḥ saptāsan kulaparvatāḥ \|*  
*ṛjvāyatāḥ suparvāṇaḥ siddhasaṅghaniṣevitāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Best among the Brahmanas, there are seven prominent mountains in the Plakshadvipa. They have thousands of the Siddhas inhabiting them and are well-divided.

## \|\| 1.49.3 \|\|

*gomedaḥ prathamasteṣāṃ dvitīyaścandra ucyate \|*  
*nārādo dundubhiścaiva somaśca ṛṣabhastathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the Plakshadvipa, first is the Gomeda mountain, the second one is known as Candra, third is Narada, while Dundubhi is the fourth one; then Maniman is the fifth, Meghanisvana is the sixth, Vaibhr&ja is the seventh mountain, which is the favourite place of Brahma.

## \|\| 1.49.4-5 \|\|

*vaibhrājaḥ saptamaḥ prokto brahmaṇo 'tyantavallabhaḥ \|*  
*tatra devarṣigandharvaiḥ siddhaiśca bhagavānajaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*upāsyate sa viśvātmā sākṣī sarvasya viśvasṛk \|*  
*teṣu puṇyā janapadā nādhayo vyādhayo na ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The Gods, Rishis, Gandharvas, and Siddhas worship the unborn god Brahma, the universal soul and the cosmic witness of all. There are the auspicious Janapadas over these mountains. There are no disturbances or the sufferings over that place.

## \|\| 1.49.6-8 \|\|

*na tatra pāpakartāraḥ puruṣā vā kathañcana \|*  
*teṣāṃ nadyaśca saptaiva varṣāṇāṃ tu samudragāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tāsu brahmarṣayo nityaṃ pitāmahapupāsate \|*  
*anutaptā śikhī caiva vipāpā tridivā kṛtā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*amṛtā sukṛtā caiva nāmataḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*kṣudranadyastvasaṃkhyātāḥ sarāṃsi subahūnyapi \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. No sinners are found there. There are seven rivers which issue from those mountains. The BrahmaRishis always adore Brahma, the grandsire, there. The rivers are known by the names of Anutapta, Sikha, Vipapa, Tridiva, Krta, Amrta and Sukrta. Besides these, there are several small rivers as well as the lakes there, which are well known.

## \|\| 1.49.9-10 \|\|

*na caiteṣu yugāvasthā puruṣā vai cirāyuṣaḥ \|*  
*āryakāḥ kuravāścaiva vidaśā bhāvinastathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*brahmakṣatriyaviṭśūdrāstasmin dvīpe prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ijyate bhagavān somo varṇaistatra nivāsibhiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. There is no cycle of Yugas like Satya, Treta, Dvapara and Kaliyuga found there. All the men have long life. The people there are known as Aryakas, Kururas, Videhas and BhSvins, and are said to be of four castes viz. Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vais'yas and Sudras. The people of the place are devoted to lord Isa, who is worshipped by all of them.

## \|\| 1.49.11 \|\|

*teṣāṃ ca somasāyujyaṃ sārūpyaṃ munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*sarve dharmaparā nityaṃ nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О Excellent sages, they achieve the Empire of Soma and similarity of form of Soma. All the people are devoted to dharma having a delightful mind, free from ailments, and live for five thousand years.

## \|\| 1.49.12-13 \|\|

*pañcavarṣasahastrāṇi jīvanti ca nirāmayāḥ \|*  
*plakṣadvīpapramāṇaṃ tu dviguṇena samantataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saṃveṣṭyekṣurasāmbhodhiṃ śālmaliḥ saṃvyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*sapta varṣāṇi tatrāpi saptaiva kulaparvatāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Salmalidvipa has four times the area as compared to Plakshadvipa. It is surrounded by the ocean of sugarcane juice on all the sides. There are seven varsas (sub-continents) and seven dividing ranges of mountains there.

## \|\| 1.49.14-16 \|\|

*ṛjvāyatāḥ suparvāṇaḥ sapta nadyaśca suvratāḥ \|*  
*kumudaśconnataścaiva tṛtīyaśca balāhakaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*droṇaḥ kaṅkastu mahiṣaḥ kakudvān sapta parvatāḥ \|*  
*yonī toyā vitṛṣṇā ca candrā śuklā vimocanī \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nivṛttiścaiti tā nadyaḥ smṛtā pāpaharā nṛṇām \|*  
*na teṣu vidyate lobhaḥ krodho vā dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. О Suvratas (observers of good vows), these mountains are spreading straight, have beautiful knots, and have seven rivers flowing over the land. The names of the seven mountains are Kumuda, Annada, Balahaka, Drona, Karusa, Mahisa and Kukudman. The names of the rivers are YonI, Toya, Vitrsna, Candra, Sukla, VimocanI and Nivrtti. With the mere recalling of the names of these rivers, all the sins are washed out. О Best of the Brahmanas, the people of these countries are free from anger.

## \|\| 1.49.17 \|\|

*na caivāsti yugāvasthā janā jīvantyanāmayāḥ \|*  
*yajanti satataṃ tatra varṇā vāyuṃ sanātanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There is no arrangement for the four Yugas. The people live there without any ailments. The people of all the castes, there always adore the eternal wind-god.

## \|\| 1.49.18 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tasyātha sāyujyaṃ sārūpyaṃ ca salokatā \|*  
*kapilā brāhmaṇāḥ proktā rājānaścāruṇāstathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Because of that they achieve the Sayujya, Sarupya, and Salokata deliverance of the wind- god. The Brahmanas there are of fair complexion and the Ksatriyas are of pink complexion. The Vaisyas are of yellow complexion, while Sudras are of black or darkcomplexion.

## \|\| 1.49.19-20 \|\|

*pītā vaiśyāḥ smṛtāḥ kṛṣṇā dvīpe 'smin vṛṣalā dvijāḥ \|*  
*śālmalasya tu vistārād dviguṇena samantataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*saṃveṣṭya tu surodābdhiṃ kuśadvīpo vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*vidrumaścaiva hemaśca dyutimān puṣpavāṃstathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Kus'advipa is of double the size of Salamalidvipa which is surrounded on all the sides with the ocean of wine. There are seven Kulaparvatas, known by the names of Vidruma, Нота, Dyutiman, Puspavan, Kusesaya, Hari and Mandara.

## \|\| 1.49.21-22 \|\|

*kuśeśayo hariścātha mandaraḥ sapta parvatāḥ \|*  
*dhutapāpā śivā caiva pavitrā saṃmatā tathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vidyudambhā mahī ceti nadyastatra jalāvahāḥ \|*  
*anyāśca śataśoviprā nadyo maṇijalāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. There are seven rivers known by the names of Dhutapapa, Shiva, Pavitra, Sammita, Vidyut, Prabha, and Rama. О Brahmanas, besides the. above, there are hundreds of other rivers having water which is spotless clean like the gems.

## \|\| 1.49.23 \|\|

*tāsu brahmāṇamīśānaṃ devādyāḥ paryupāsate \|*  
*brāhmaṇā draviṇo viprāḥ kṣatriyāḥ śuṣmiṇastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О Brahmanas, the gods living there adore Brahma as their lord. In the said dvipa, the Brahmanas are known as Dravinas, Ksatriyas as Susmins, Vaisyas as Stobhas, and the Sudras as Mandehas.

## \|\| 1.49.24-25 \|\|

*vaiśyāḥ snehāstu mandehāḥ śūdrāstatra prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*sarve vijñānasaṃpannā maitrādiguṇasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yathoktakāriṇaḥ sarve sarve bhūtahite ratāḥ \|*  
*yajanti vividhairyajñairbrahmāṇaṃ parameṣṭhinam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. All the people of that place possess all the knowledge and have the qualities of friendship etc. All of them perform the activities prescribed in the Sastras. They remain engaged for the welfare of the other people. They please Parmesthin Brahma, with the performing of the yajnas.

## \|\| 1.49.26 \|\|

*teṣāṃ ca brahmasāyujyaṃ sārūpyaṃ ca salokatā \|*  
*kuśadvīpasya vistārād dviguṇena samantataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. They achieve the Sayujya (absorption in the deity), Sarupya (similarity with the form of deity) and the Salokya (residence in the region of the deity) types of Muktis with god Brahma. The Kraunca-dvipa is of double the size of Kus'a-dvipa and is surrounded by the ocean of clarified butter.

## \|\| 1.49.27-29 \|\|

*krauñcadvīpastato viprā veṣṭayitvā ghṛtodadhim \|*  
*krauñco vāmanakaścaiva tṛtīyaścāndhakārakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*devāvṛcca vivindaśca puṇḍarīkastathaiva ca \|*  
*nāmnā ca saptamaḥ proktaḥ parvato dundubhisvanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*gaurī kumudvitī caiva saṃdhyā rātrirmanojavā \|*  
*khyātiśca puṇḍarīkāca nadyaḥ prādhānyataḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. There are also seven main mountains known by the names of Kraunca, Vamanaka, Adhikarika, Devabda, Viveda, Pundarika, and Dundubhisvana. The seven rivers of the country are known by the names of Gauri, Kumudvatl, Sandhya, Ratri, Manojava, Kobhi, and Pundarikaksa.

## \|\| 1.49.30 \|\|

*puṣkarāḥ puṣkalā dhanyāstiṣyāstasya krameṇa vai \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścaiva dvijottamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О Excellent Brahmanas, the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras are known there as Puskala, Puskara, Dhanya and Tisya respectively.

## \|\| 1.49.31-32 \|\|

*arcayanti mahādevaṃ yajñadānasamādhibhiḥ \|*  
*vratopavāsairvividhairhemaiḥ svādhyāyatarpaṇaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ vai rudrasāyujyaṃ sārūpyaṃ cātidurlabham \|*  
*salokatā ca sāmīpyaṃ jāyate tatprasādataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. All of them adore lord Mahadeva, giving away charities, sacrifices, remaining peaceful and performing vows, fasting, homas of various types. By the grace of lord Mahadeva, they achieve the Rudra-Sdyujya, Santypa, Salokatd and Samlpya.

## \|\| 1.49.33 \|\|

*krauñcadvīpasya vistārād dviguṇena samantataḥ \|*  
*śākadvīpaḥ sthito viprā āveṣṭya dadhisāgaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. О Brahmanas, Saka-dvipa has double the area as compared to Kraunca-dvipa, and is surrounded by the ocean of curds from all the sides.

## \|\| 1.49.34-35 \|\|

*udayo raivataścaiva śyāmāko 'stagiristathā \|*  
*āmbikeyastathā ramyaḥ keśarī ceti parvatāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sukumārī kumārī ca nalinī reṇukā tathā \|*  
*ikṣukā dhenukā caiva gabhastiśceti nimnagāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. The names of its prominent mountains are Udaya, Raivata, Syama, Kasthagiri, Ambikeya, Ramya, and Kesarin. The names of the seven rivers are Sukumari, Kumari, NalinI, Venuka, Iksuka, Dhenuka, and Gabhasti.

## \|\| 1.49.36-37 \|\|

*āsāṃ pibantaḥ salilaṃ jīvante tatra mānavāḥ \|*  
*anāmayā hyaśokāśca rāgadveṣavivarjitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*magāśca magadhāścaiva mānavā mandagāstathā \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścātra krameṇa tu \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. The people of that country live while consuming the river waters. Those people are healthy, free of sorrows, and the attachments or malice or hatred. The Brahmana, Ksatriyas, Vais'yas and the Sudras, there are known as Mrga, Magadha, Manasa and Mandagas respectively.

## \|\| 1.49.38-39 \|\|

*yajanti satataṃ devaṃ sarvalokaikasākṣiṇam \|*  
*vratopavāsairvividhairdevadevaṃ divākaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ sūryeṇa sāyujyaṃ sāmīpyaṃ ca sarūpatā \|*  
*salokatā ca viprendrā jāyate tatprasādataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. All of them adore the sun-god, the witness of all, performing several of vratas, fasting and other kinds of worship. О Best of the Brahmanas, by the grace of the sun, they achieve the Sayujya (identity) with the sun, Samlpya (nearness) and Sdrupatd (similarity in appearance) and Sdlokata (residence in the solar region).

## \|\| 1.49.40-41 \|\|

*śākadvīpaṃ samāvṛtya kṣīrodaḥ sāgaraḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*śvetadvīpaśca tanmadhye nārāyaṇaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tatra puṇyā janapadā nānāścaryasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*śvetāstatra narā nityaṃ jāyante viṣṇutatparāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. The ocean of milk surrounds the Saka-dvipa. Svetadvipa is lodged in the centre of it. The people there are devoted to Narayana. There are several Janapadas (territories) full of many surprises. The people of the place are of white complexion and are devoted to lord Narayana.

## \|\| 1.49.42 \|\|

*nādhayo vyādhayastatra jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ na ca \|*  
*krodhalobhavinirmuktā māyāmātsaryavarjitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. There are no obstructions or sufferings nor are there any mental or physical ailments. There is no danger of the old age or death. The people of that place are free from greed and anger, illusion or hatred.

## \|\| 1.49.43-44 \|\|

*nityapuṣṭā nirātaṅkā nityānandāśca bhoginaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇaparāḥ sarve nārāyaṇaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*kecid dhyānaparā nityaṃ yoginaḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ \|*  
*kecijjapanti tapyanti kecid vijñānino 'pare \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. They always remain healthy, ever blissful, and enjoy the worldly pleasures. Some of them are engaged in meditation, some in the yogic practices, controlling their sense organs. Some of them are engaged in lapas, others in the performing of the Japas. Some of them are enlightened with perfect spiritual knowledge.

## \|\| 1.49.45 \|\|

*anye nirbojayogena brahmabhāvena bhāvitāḥ \|*  
*dhyāyanti tat paraṃ vyoma vāsudevaṃ paraṃ padam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Some of them with the application of Nirblja- yoga (seedless Yoga) and purified by meditating upon Brahman, meditate on eternal Vasudeva, the supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 1.49.46 \|\|

*ekāntino nirālambā mahābhāgavatāḥ pare \|*  
*paśyanti paramaṃ brahma viṣṇavākhyaṃ tamasaḥ paraṃ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Someone who likes loveliness, discarding all support, devote themselves to the lord. They are beyond Tamoguna and visualise, Visnu as the Supreme Brahman alone.

## \|\| 1.49.47 \|\|

*sarve caturbhujākārāḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharāḥ \|*  
*supītavāsasaḥ sarve śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. All of them have their chests marked with the sign of golden hair called Srlvatsa, and have four arms holding Sankha, Cakra and Gada, clad in yellow lower garment.

## \|\| 1.49.48-49 \|\|

*anye maheśvaraparāstripuṇḍrāṅkitamastakāḥ \|*  
*svayogodbhūtakiraṇā mahāgaruḍavāhanāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sarvaśaktisamāyuktā nityānandāśca nirmalāḥ \|*  
*vasanti tatra puruṣā viṣṇorantaracāriṇaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Some others who are devoted to Shiva, paste their foreheads with tripundra (three lines of ashes on the forehead), possessing all the fortunes through practice of excellent Yoga, healthy bodies, and are like the lord using Garuda as the vehicle. All of them have enormous prowess, always blissful, spotless, dwelling in the heart of lord Visnu roam about there.

## \|\| 1.49.50 \|\|

*tatra nārāyaṇasyānyad durgamaṃ duratikramam \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ nāma puraṃ vyāsādyairupaśobhitam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. There is the city of Visnu, known as Narayanapura, which is beyond encroachment or assailed by anyone, and has enough of beautiful palaces.

## \|\| 1.49.51 \|\|

*hemaprākārasaṃsuktaṃ sphāṭikairmaṇḍapairyutam \|*  
*prabhāsahastrakalilaṃ durādharṣaṃ suśobhanam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The boundary wall of the same is made of gold while the mandapas are of the crystal stone. Its lustre is diffused in a thousand ways and is quite attractive and beautiful.

## \|\| 1.49.52-54 \|\|

*harmyaprākārasaṃyuktamaṭṭālakasamākulam \|*  
*hemagopurasāhastrairnānāratnopaśobhitaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*śubhrāstaraṇasaṃyuktaṃ vicitraiḥ samalaṅkṛtam \|*  
*nandanairvividhākāraiḥ stravantībhīśca śobhitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sarobhiḥ sarvato yuktaṃ vīṇāveṇunināditam \|*  
*patākābhirvicitrābhiranekābhiśca śobhitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. It has high palaces, vast canopies, studded with various types of gems, beautiful floor decorations and hundreds of blissful toranas of different designs, besides the gopuras. Its beauty is enhanced by delightful parks of various shapes and flowing rivers, besides lakes all round. Many banners of variegated colours beautify it. The sound of the playing on vlna and flute spreads everywhere.

## \|\| 1.49.55 \|\|

*vīthībhiḥ sarvato yuktaṃ sopānai ratnabhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*nārīśatasahastrāḍhyaṃ divyagoyasamanvitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The streets and the steps of gems could be seen everywhere. It had hundreds and thousands of rivers. The divine songs and music were heard everywhere.

## \|\| 1.49.56 \|\|

*haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇaṃ cakravākopaśobhitam \|*  
*caturdvāramanaupamyamagamyaṃ devavidviṣām \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The city had enough of swans, ducks, besides the ruddy geese. All the four gates of the city were unique and were beyond the reach of the enemies.

## \|\| 1.49.57-59 \|\|

*tatra tatrāpsaraḥ saṅdhairnṛtyadbhirupaśobhitam \|*  
*nānāgītavidhānajñairdevānāmapi durlabhaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*nānāvilāsasaṃpannaiḥ kāmukairatikomalaiḥ \|*  
*prabhūtacandravadanairnūpurārāvasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*īṣatsmitaiḥ subimboṣṭhairbālamugdhamṛgekṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*aśeṣavibhavopetairbhūṣitaistanumadhyamaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. The Apsaras danced here and there in the city. They were well-versed in several types of singing tunes, which were unknown even to the gods. They were well aware of several sports, passionate, having extremely tender bodies, with faces resembling the moon. They created tinkling sound with their anklets. They wore the serene smile over their faces, had well built and beautiful lips like Bimba (red cherry) fruits. They had the eyes like the fawns. They possessed all the fortunes and had a thin waist.

## \|\| 1.49.60-61 \|\|

*surājahaṃsacalanaiḥ suveṣairmadhurasvanaiḥ \|*  
*saṃlāpālāpakuśalairdivyābharaṇabhūṣaitaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*stanabhāravinamraiśca madaghūrṇitalocanaiḥ \|*  
*nānāvarṇavicitrāṅgairnānābhogaratipriyaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. The said Apsaras walked gracefully like the royal swans, were clad in beautiful garments and had sweet temperament. They were well- versed in speech and were adorned wkh beautiful ornaments. They were bent with the weight of their breasts, had various types of limbs and were good in making love sports.

## \|\| 1.49.62 \|\|

*praphullakusumodyānairitaścetaśca śobhitam \|*  
*asaṃkhyeyaguṇaṃ śuddhamāgamyaṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The city had several orchards with the blossoming flowers, hundreds of living beings, and possessed many excellent qualities. It was also beautified by several gods having numerous attributes.

## \|\| 1.49.63-65 \|\|

*śrīmatpavitraṃ devasya śrīpateramitaujasaḥ \|*  
*tasya madhye 'titejaskamuccaprākāratoraṇam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*sthānaṃ pad vaiṣṇavaṃ divyaṃ yogināmapi durlabham \|*  
*tanmadhye bhagavānekaḥ puṇḍarīkadaladyutiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*śete 'śeṣajagatsūtiḥ śeṣāhiśayane hariḥ \|*  
*vicintyamāno yogīndraiḥ sanandanapurogamaiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-65. The city of illustrious Visnu, is quite auspicious and graceful. In the middle of it, is a highly-splendid spot of lofty ramparts and arched ornamental gateways. This is the place of Visnu which bestows success to the Yogins. In the centre of the same, lord Visnu, having the lustre of lotus petals, lies down over the bed of the serpent Sesa. He is adored by Sanandana and other Yogins.

## \|\| 1.49.66-67 \|\|

*svātmānandāmṛtaṃ pītvā paraṃ tat tamasaḥ param \|*  
*supītavasano 'nanto mahāmāyo mahābhujaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*kṣīrodakanyayā nityaṃ gṛhītacaraṇadvayaḥ \|*  
*sā ca devī jagadvandyā pādamūle haripriyā \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. He wore pitambara, has broad eyes, possesses Mahamaya, large arms, and consumes in the nectar of the bliss of his own Atman. He is the deity beyond darkness. Lakshmi, the daughter of the ocean of milk, always serves at his feet. The goddess who is adored by the universe, is lodged at the feet of the lord being beloved of lord Visnu.

## \|\| 1.49.68-69 \|\|

*samāste tanmanā nityaṃ pītvā nārāyaṇāmṛtam \|*  
*na tatrādhārmikā yānti na ca devāntarāśrayāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*vaikuṇṭhaṃ nāma tat sthānaṃ tridaśairapi vanditam \|*  
*na me 'tra bhavati prajñā kṛtsnaśastannirūpaṇe \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. The goddess consuming the nectar of the lord Narayana, stays there, getting devoted to him with her mind. The evil people of impious activities do not go there; nor those who dwell in the abodes of other Devas. It is the abode named Vaikuntha and is adored even by the gods. It is beyond my wisdom to describe the entire region.

## \|\| 1.49.70-71 \|\|

*etāvacchakyate vaktuṃ nārāyaṇapuraṃ hi tat \|*  
*sa eva paramaṃ brahma vāsudevaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*śete nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān māyayā mohayañjagat \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. This much could only be spoken, that this is the place of Narayana, who is the supreme Brahman, eternal and Vasudeva. Lord Narayana, deluding the universe with his Maya, is sleeping there.

## \|\| 1.49.72 \|\|

*nārāyaṇādidaṃ jātaṃ tasminneva vyavasthitam \|*  
*tamevābhyeti kalpānte sa eva paramā gatiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The entire universe emerges from Narayana, and is also established in him. At the end of the Kalpa period, the world is absorbed in him. He is the ultimate goal.

## Chapter 50. Description of Puskaradvipa

## \|\| 1.50.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śākadvīpasya vistārād dviguṇena vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*kṣīrārṇavaṃ samāśritya dvīpaḥ puṣkarasaṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, PuskaradvTpa is of double the size of the Sakadvipa which is surrounded by the ocean of milk.

## \|\| 1.50.2-3 \|\|

*eka evātra viprendrāḥ parvato mānasottaraḥ \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahastrāṇi sārdhaṃ pañcāśaducchritaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tāvadeva ca vistīrṇaḥ sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalaḥ \|*  
*sa eva dvīpaḥ paścārdhe mānasottarasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. О Best of Brahmanas, “There is a huge mountain known by the name of Manasottara. It has the height of fifty thousand Yojanas. Its expansion on all sides is the same. It is globular all round. The mountain Manasottara is stationed exactly in the middle of the continent.

## \|\| 1.50.4 \|\|

*eka eva mahāsānuḥ saṃniveśād dvidhā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmin dvīpe smṛtau dvau tu puṇyau janapadau śubhau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О Great sage, one and the same establishment has been divided into two parts. It is said that there are two auspicious and purified Janapadas in that island.

## \|\| 1.50.5-6 \|\|

*aparau mānasasyātha parvatasyānumaṇḍalau \|*  
*mahāvītaṃ smṛtaṃ varṣaṃ dhātakīkhaṇḍameva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*svādūdakenodadhinā puṣkaraḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*tasmin dvīpe mahāvṛkṣo nyagrodho 'marapūjitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Both of them are in the semicircle of the Manasa mountain. There are two varsas there known as Mahavita and DhatakI khanda. This dvipa Puskara is surrounded by an ocean of sweet water. There is a huge banyan tree, which is adored even by the immortal.

## \|\| 1.50.7 \|\|

*tasmin nivasati brahmā viśvātmā viśvabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*tatraiva muniśārdūlāḥ śivanārāyaṇālayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There Brahma, the universal soul, resides. О Excellent sage, the abode of Shiva and Narayana is also located there.

## \|\| 1.50.8 \|\|

*vasatyatra mahādevo haror'ddhahariravyayaḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjyamāno brahmādyaiḥ kumārādyaiśca yogibhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Both lord Shiva and Vishnu are lodged in one half of this continent. In one half Нага resides and in the other half Hari resides. Brahma and other gods, besides Sanatkumara, adore them.

## \|\| 1.50.9 \|\|

*gandharvaiḥ kinnarairyakṣairīśvaraḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalaḥ \|*  
*svasthāstatra prajāḥ sarvā brahmaṇā sadṛśatviṣaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Ishvara who is Krisna (black) and Pingala (brown) is adored by Gandharvas, Kinnaras, and Yaksas. The people of that place are quite healthy and normal. The Brahmanas, there, possess hundred times more lustre.

## \|\| 1.50.10 \|\|

*nirāmayā viśokāśca rāgadveṣavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*satyānṛte na tatrāstāṃ nottamādhamamadhyamāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. They are free from ailments, grief, attraction or malice. There is no difference between truth and falsehood, high or low, or the middle ones.

## \|\| 1.50.11-12 \|\|

*na varṇāśramadharmāśca na nadyo na ca parvatāḥ \|*  
*pareṇa puṣkarasyātha sthito mahān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*svādūdakasamudrastu samantād dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*pareṇa tasya mahatī dṛśyate lokasaṃsthitiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. There is no Varnasrama-dharma (rules and rites of the different castes and stages of life), nor the rivers or the mountains. О Best of the Brahmanas, Puskaradvipa is surrounded by the vast ocean of the sweet water from all the sides. Its situation in the world is beyond everything and every world.

## \|\| 1.50.13 \|\|

*kāñcanī dviguṇā bhūmiḥ sarvā caiva śilopamā \|*  
*tasyāḥ pareṇa śailastu maryādātmātmamaṇḍalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The earth, comparable to a single golden rock, is of double in size which is spread in all the sides. Beyond that is the boundary mountain known as Bhanumandala.

## \|\| 1.50.14 \|\|

*prakāśaścāprakāśaśca lokālokaḥ sa ucyate \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahastrāṇi daśa tasyocchrayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The region is known as Lokaloka,1 because a part of it has light and the other part of the same is covered with darkness. Its height is ten thousand Yojanas.

## \|\| 1.50.15-16 \|\|

*tāvāneva ca vistāro lokāloko mahāgiriḥ \|*  
*samāvṛtya tu taṃ śailaṃ sarvato vai tamaḥ sthitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tamaścāṇḍakaṭāhena samantāt pariveṣṭitam \|*  
*etai sapta mahālokāḥ pātālāḥ saptakīrtitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The area of the Lokaloka moimtain is the same. The darkness is surrounding it on all the sides in an oval shape. In this way the seven lokas as well as the seven Patalas (nether worlds) have been described.

## \|\| 1.50.17-18 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍasyaiṣa vistāraḥ saṃkṣepeṇa mayoditaḥ \|*  
*aṇḍānāmīdṛśānāṃ tu koṭyo jñeyāḥ sahastraśaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sarvagatvāt pradhānasya kāraṇasyāvyayātmanaḥ \|*  
*aṇḍeṣveteṣu sarveṣu bhuvanāni caturdaśa \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Thus, the entire cosmic egg has been described by me in brief. Because of the supreme lord being all pervading, these globes are imagined to be crores in number. This should be known. Fourteen worlds are enshrined in all these cosmic eggs.

## \|\| 1.50.19 \|\|

*tatra tatra caturvaktrā rudrā nārāyaṇādayaḥ \|*  
*daśottaramathaikaikamaṇḍāvaraṇasaptakam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The four-faced Brahma, Rudra, Narayana and others live in their respective places. There are several sheaths, which have covered each cosmic egg from all the sides. In these sheaths, one is ten times bigger than the other. О Brahmanas, the learned people visit these places.

## \|\| 1.50.20-21 \|\|

*samantāt saṃsthitaṃ viprā yatra yānti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*anantamekamavyaktanādinidhanaṃ mahat \|\| 20 \|\|*

*atītya vartate sarvaṃ jagat prakṛtirakṣaram \|*  
*anantatvamanantasya yataḥ saṃkhyā na vidyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. The one who is beyond measure, invisible, eternal, beyond birth and death, Mahat, is undecaying, form of Prakrti, dwells there crossing all the barriers. Because of his being Ananta, he is beyond measure.

## \|\| 1.50.22 \|\|

*tadavyaktamiti jñeyaṃ tad brahma paramaṃ padam \|*  
*ananta eṣa sarvatra sarvasthāneṣu paṭhyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The stable, supreme Brahman, should be treated as invisible. It is infinite and endless as it is beyond calculation.

## \|\| 1.50.23-24 \|\|

*tasya pūrvaṃ mayāpyuktaṃ yattanmāhātmyamavyayam \|*  
*gataḥ sa eṣa sarvatra sarvasthāneṣu vartate \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bhūmau rasātale caiva ākāśe pavane 'nale \|*  
*arṇaveṣu ca sarveṣu divi caiva na saśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. I have already explained the best of his glory. He is all pervading, adored by all. He indeed is present on earth, in nether worlds sky, in wind, fire, heaven and the oceans. There is no doubt about the same.

## \|\| 1.50.25 \|\|

*tathā tamasi sattve ca eṣa eva mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*anekadhā vibhaktāṅgaḥ krīḍate puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Similarly, the resplendent supreme Brahman, is present in the light as well as the darkness. The same Purusottama, sports in many ways, dividing himself in many forms.

## \|\| 1.50.26 \|\|

*maheśvaraḥ paro 'vyaktādaṇḍamavyaktasaṃbhavam \|*  
*aṇḍād brahmā samutpannastena sṛṣṭamidaṃ jagat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Lord Mahesvara is beyond that unmanifest from which this cosmic egg has been produced. Infact, lord Brahma has been bom out of the golden egg. The universe was created through him.

## Chapter 51. Glory of Visnu in the Manvantaras

## \|\| 1.51.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*atītānāgatānīha yāni manvantarāṇi tu \|*  
*tāni tvaṃ kathayāsmākaṃ vyāsāṃśca dvāpare yuge \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said, “The Manvantaras which have already passed, and those which are yet to come, about Vyasa (the arranger of the Vedas) in the Dvapara yuga, you enlighten us about all of them.

## \|\| 1.51.2-3 \|\|

*vedaśākhāpraṇayanaṃ devadevasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*tathāvatārān dharmārthamīśānasya kalau yuge \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kiyanto devadevasya śiṣyāḥ kaliyugeṣu vai \|*  
*etat sarvaṃ samāsena sūta vaktumihārhasi \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. О Sirta, Vyasa is the creator of the branches of the Vedas. For how many times has the lord of the gods (i.e. Vyasa) incarnated on earth for the establishment of Dharma, in the Kaliyuga, and the number of his disciples may kindly be spelt in brief?”

## \|\| 1.51.4-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvaḥ pūrvaṃ tataḥ svārociṣo manuḥ \|*  
*uttamastāmasaścaiva raivataścākṣuṣastathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ṣaḍete manavo 'tītāḥ sāṃprataṃ tu raveḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*vaivasvato 'yaṃ yasyaitat saptamaṃ vartate 'ntaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Suta said, “Svayambhuva Manu appeared initially, followed by Svarocisa, Uttama, Tamasa, Raivata and Caksusa. These six Manus have already gone by. Presently, Vaivasvata Manu, the son of the sun-god, the seventh Manvantara is passing.1 ww sh grfsjw чл-чщсмi wi m iwwtgsw trt: witiftiret shn 5 и At the start of the Kalpa, there had been Svayambhuva Manvantara, which has already been described by me. This has been followed by Svarocisa Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.51.6 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvaṃ tu kathitaṃ kalpādāvantaraṃ mayā \|*  
*ata ūrdhvaṃ nibodhadhvaṃ manoḥ svārociṣasya tu \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. During Svarocisa Manvantara, there were the gods called Paravatas and Tirsitas. There also happened to be a Indra known as Vipascit, who was the destroyer the asuras.

## \|\| 1.51.7 \|\|

*pārāvatāśca tuṣitā devāḥ svārociṣe 'ntare \|*  
*vipaścinnāma devendro babhūvāsurasūdanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The names of the contemporary SaptaRishis had been Urja, Stambha, Prana, Danta, Rsabha, Timira, and Arvarlvan.

## \|\| 1.51.8 \|\|

*ūrjastambhastathā prāṇo dānto 'tha vṛṣabhastathā \|*  
*timiraścārvarīvāṃśca sapta saptarṣayo 'bhavan \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Svarocisa had two sons called Caitra and Kimpurusa. This is known as the second Manvantara. Now you listen about the Manu named Uttama.

## \|\| 1.51.9 \|\|

*caitrakiṃpuruṣādyāśca sutāḥ svārociṣasya tu \|*  
*dvitīyamatadākhyātamantaraṃ śṛṇu cottaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Svarocisa, Auttami, Tamasa, Raibhala, Caksusa. The seventh Manu, called Vaivasvata, is the present Manu.

## \|\| 1.51.10-11 \|\|

*tṛtīye 'pyantare viprā uttamo nāma vai manuḥ \|*  
*suśāntistatra devendro babhūvāmitrakarṣaṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sudhāmānastathā satyāḥ śivāścātha pratardanāḥ \|*  
*vaśavartinaśca pañcaite gaṇā dvādaśakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. During the third Manvantara, there had been a Manu named Uttama. Susanti, the suppressor of enemies, was the ruler of gods. The names of the contemporary gods were Sudhamans, Satya, Shiva, Pratardana, and Vasavartins. It is said that these five ganas, came to be known as Pancadvadasakas.

## \|\| 1.51.12 \|\|

*rajordhvaścordhvabāhuśca sabalaścānayastathā \|*  
*sutapāḥ śukra ityete sapta saptarṣayo 'bhavan \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The seven Rishis of the contemporary period had been Rajas, Gatra, Urdhvabahu, Savana, Anagha, Sutupa and Sakra.

## \|\| 1.51.13 \|\|

*tāmasasyāntare devāḥ surā vāharayastathā \|*  
*satyāśca sudhiyaścaiva saptaviṃśatikā gaṇāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. During the Tamasa Manvantara, there had been twenty seven Ganadevatcis and the classes of gods include Surayasahara, Satya, and Sudhls.

## \|\| 1.51.14 \|\|

*śibirindrastathaivāsīcchatayajñopalakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*babhūva śaṅkare bhakto mahādevārcane rataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The name of Indra who performed a hundred yajnas, was Sibi. He was a devotee of Shiva and always remained devoted to his worship.

## \|\| 1.51.15 \|\|

*jyotirdharmā pṛthuḥ kāvyaścaitrognirvanakastathā \|*  
*pīvarastvṛṣayo hyete sapta tatrāpi cāntare \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The SaptaRishis of that Manvantara had been, Jyotis, Dhaman, Prthak, Kalpa, Caitra, Agnivasana, and Plvara.

## \|\| 1.51.16 \|\|

*pañcame cāpi viprendrā raivato nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*manurvasuśca tatrendro babhūvāsuramardanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Best of the Brahmanas, during the fifth Manvantara, name of the Manu was Raivata and name of Indra was Vibhu, who destroyed the asuras.

## \|\| 1.51.17 \|\|

*amitābhā bhūtarayā vaikuṇṭhāḥ svacchamedhasaḥ \|*  
*ete devagaṇāstatra caturdaśa caturdaśa \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There had been fourteen Ganadevatas including Amitas, Bhutis and Vaikunthas, who were the best of all.

## \|\| 1.51.18 \|\|

*hiraṇyaromā vedaśrīrūrdhvabāhustathaiva ca \|*  
*vedabāhuḥ sudhāmā ca parjanyaśca mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*ete saptarṣayo viprāstatrāsan raivate 'ntare \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The names of the SaptaRishis during the Raivata Manvantara were Hiranyaroman, Vedasri, Urdhvabahu, Vedabahu, Subahu, Sapaijanya, and Mahamuni.

## \|\| 1.51.19-20 \|\|

*svārociṣaścottamaśca tāmaso raivatastathā \|*  
*priyavratānvayā hyete catvāro manavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭhe manvantare cāsīccākṣuṣastu manurdvijāḥ \|*  
*manojavastathaivendro devānapi nibodhataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Thus the Manus known by the names of Svarocis, Uttama, Tamasa, and Raivata belonged to the Priyavrata race. О Brahmanas, Cakshusha Manu appeared in the sixth Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.51.21-23 \|\|

*ādyāḥ prasūtā bhāvyāśca pṛthugāśca divaukasaḥ \|*  
*mahānubhāvā lekhyāśca pañcaite hyaṣṭakā gaṇāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sumedhā virajāścaiva haviṣmānuttamo madhuḥ \|*  
*atināmā sahiṣṇuśca saptāsannṛṣayaḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vivasvataḥ suto viprāḥ śrāddhadevo mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*manuḥ sa vartate dhīmān sāṃprataṃ saptame 'ntare \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Similarly Indra named Manojava existed then. You also know about the Devaganas, who were known as Adyas, Prabhutas, Prathanas, Mahanubhavas, and Lekhyas. These were the five groups of Devas. The names of the seven auspicious Rishis had been Virajas, Havisman, Soma, Manu, Sama, Avinaman and Savisnu. Sraddhadeva had been the illustrious son of Vivasvan.

## \|\| 1.51.24 \|\|

*ādityā vasavo rudrā devāstatra marudgaṇāḥ \|*  
*purandarastathaivendro babhūva paravīrahā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О Brahmanas, the present Manu in the seventh Manvantara is Samvartana. The gods were known as Adifyas, Vasus, Rudras and Maruts.

## \|\| 1.51.25 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapaścātrirjamadagniśca gautamaḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitro bharadvājaḥ sapta saptarṣayo 'bhavan \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Purandara was the name of Indra during that period, who could destroy the valorous warriors. The names of the contemporary Rishis were, Vasistha, Kas'yapa, Atri, Jamadagni, Gautama, Visvamitra and Bharadvaja.

## \|\| 1.51.26-28 \|\|

*viṣṇuśaktiranaupamyā sattvodriktā sthitā sthitau \|*  
*tadaṃśabhūtā rājānaḥ sarve ca tridivaukasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare pūrvamākūtyāṃ mānasaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*ruceḥ prajāpateryajñastadaṃśenābhavad dvijāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tataḥ punarasau devaḥ prāpte svārociṣe 'ntare \|*  
*tuṣitāyāṃ samutpannastuṣitaiḥ saha daivataiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. The incomparable Shakti of Visnu, wherein Sattva is predominant, is stationed for the protection of the world. All the gods and the kings were bom of that arhs'a. О Brahmanas, during the Svayambhuva Manvantara, in the early period, he was bom of Prakrti. Akuti and Ruci, the Prajapati, were their mind-bom son. In due course of time, the same gods appeared in Svarocisa Manvantara as Tusita along with the deities Tusitas.

## \|\| 1.51.29-30 \|\|

*auttame 'pyantare viṣṇuḥ satyaiḥ saha surottamaiḥ \|*  
*satyāyāmabhavat satyaḥ satyarūpo janārdanaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tāmasasyāntare caiva saṃprāpte punareva hi \|*  
*haryāyāṃ haribhirdevairharirevābhavaddhariḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Drying the Uttama Manvantara, Vishnu, Jan^rdana, the excellent among Devas was bom from the womb of Satya along with Satyas. He was also called Satya. On the arrival of the Tamasa Manvantara, again lord Hari was produced from Harya, alongwith Devas called Haris.

## \|\| 1.51.31 \|\|

*raivate 'pyantare caiva saṃbhūtyāṃ mānaso 'bhavat \|*  
*saṃbhūto mānasaiḥ sārdhaṃ devaiḥ saha mahādyutiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. During the time of Raivata, Hari was bom as the highly splendoured mental son of Samkalpa alongwith Devas called Manasas.

## \|\| 1.51.32-33 \|\|

*cākṣuṣe 'pyantare caiva vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*vikuṇṭhāyāmasau jajñe vaikuṇṭhairdaivataiḥ saha \|\| 32 \|\|*

*manvantare 'tra saṃprāpte tathā vaivasvate 'ntare \|*  
*vāmanaḥ kaśyapād viṣṇuradityāṃ saṃbabhūva ha \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Thereafter, during the Caksusa Manvantara as well, Visnu, lord Purusottama, was bom of Vaikuntha as Vaikuntha, alongwith Devas known as Vaikunthas. Similarly on the arrival of the Vaivasvata Manvantara, Kasyapa produced from Aditi Visnu in the form of Vamana (Dwarf).

## \|\| 1.51.34-35 \|\|

*tribhiḥ kramairimāṃllokāñjitvā yena mahātmanā \|*  
*purandarāya trailokyaṃ dattaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ityetāstanavastasya sapta manvantareṣu vai \|*  
*sapta caivābhavan viprā yābhiḥ saṃrakṣitāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Then Mahatma, subjugating the earth with three feet, bestowed on Indra, the thornless kingdom of the three worlds. Thus, during all the seven Manvantaras, it was Visnu alone which appeared in the seven forms.

## \|\| 1.51.36-37 \|\|

*yasmād viṣṭamidaṃ kṛtsnaṃ vāmanena mahātmanā \|*  
*tasmāt sa vai smṛto viṣṇurviśerdhātoḥ praveśanāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

*eṣa sarvaṃ sṛjatyādau pāti hanti ca keśavaḥ \|*  
*bhūtāntarātmā bhagavān nārāyaṇa iti śrutiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. О Brahmanas, the people were protected by them, Mahatma Vamana had measured the entire globe with his three steps. Therefore, all the gods remember Vamana, who is the destroyer of the Daityas. Kesava alone creates, the universe initially, then he protects it and ultimately destroys the same.

## \|\| 1.51.38 \|\|

*ekāṃśena jagat sarvaṃ vyāpya nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*caturdhā saṃsthito vyāpī saguṇo nirguṇo 'pi ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Sruti says that Lord Narayana resides in the souls of all. The same Narayana, pervades the universe with his ams'a. He pervades the earth in his four forms, both endowed with and without attributes.1

## \|\| 1.51.39-41 \|\|

*ekā bhagavato mūrtirjñānarūpā śivāmalā \|*  
*vāsudevābhidhānā sā guṇātītā suniṣkalā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*dvitīyā kālasaṃjñānyā tāmasī śeṣasaṃjñitā \|*  
*nihanti sakalaṃ cānte vaiṣṇavī paramā tanuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sattvodriktā tathaivānyā pradyumneti ca saṃjñitā \|*  
*jagat sthāpayate sarvaṃ sa viṣṇuḥ prakṛtirdhruvā \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. The first form of the lord, is spotless, full of all the knowledge, as well as is the bestower of welfare. The form known as Vasudeva, is extremely virtuous, auspicious, pure and beyond all Gunas. His second form is known as the Kala, which is characterised by tamas and is designated as Shiva. It is the highest form of Visnu, the destroyer of everything in the end. The third image is a Sattvika one and is termed Pradyumna.

## \|\| 1.51.42 \|\|

*caturtho vāsudevasya mūrtirbrāhmīti saṃjñitā \|*  
*rājasī cāniruddhākhyā pradyumnaḥ sṛṣṭikārikā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It sustains the entire universe. It is the stable nature of Visnu. The fourth form of Vasudeva is known as Brahma. It is the Rajasa form termed as Aniruddha and is the cause of the universe.

## \|\| 1.51.43-45 \|\|

*yaḥ svapityakhilaṃ bhūtvā pradyumnena saha prabhuḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇākhyo brahmāsau prijāsargaṃ karoti saḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*yā sā nārāyaṇatanuḥ pradyumnākhyā munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*tayā saṃmohayed viśvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*saiva sarvajagatsūtiḥ prakṛtiḥ parikīrtitā \|*  
*vāsudevo hyanantātmā kevalo nirguṇo hariḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. It is the Lord who having annihilated everything sleeps alongwith his manifestation called Pradyumna. Narayana in the form of Brahma, creates the universe. The image of Narayana which is well-known as Pradyumna, fascinates and deludes the world including the gods, Danavas, Humans and the entire world. Because of this, it is called Prakrti, the embodiment of the universe.

## \|\| 1.51.46 \|\|

*pradhānaṃ puruṣaḥ kālastattvatrayamanuttamam \|*  
*vāsudevātmakaṃ nityametad vijñāya mucyate \|\| 46 \|\|*
