*sākṣād devo mahādevastajjñānamiti kīrtitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The knowledge by which, one can have face to face with lord Mahadeva, the same is known as jhana or knowledge,

## \|\| 2.15.37 \|\|

*tanniṣṭhastatparo vidvānnityamakrodhanaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*mahāyajñaparo vipro labhate tadanuttamam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The one who always has faith in him, the truthful one, the learned person who does not resort to anger, auspicious, and the performer of the great yajnas, can only achieve the said knowledge.

## \|\| 2.15.38 \|\|

*dharmasyāyatanaṃ yatnāccharīraṃ paripālayet \|*  
*na hi dehaṃ vinā rudraḥ puruṣairvidyate paraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The body is the abode of dharma and therefore, should be well maintained making all the efforts. A person without a body cannot achieve lord Rudra.

## \|\| 2.15.39 \|\|

*nityadharmārthakāmeṣu yujyeta niyato dvijaḥ \|*  
*na dharmavarjitaṃ kāmamarthaṃ vā manasā smaret \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Controlling one’s own mind, a Brahmana, should devote himself to dharma, artha and kama. But kama and artha devoid of dharma should never be conceived.

## \|\| 2.15.40 \|\|

*sīdannapi hi dharmeṇa na tvadharmaṃ samācaret \|*  
*dharmo hi bhagavān devo gatiḥ sarveṣu jantuṣu \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Following the dharma, when one has to face the pain, even then one should not resort to evil ways. It is dharma alone, which leads one to the lord and is the goal of all creatures.

## \|\| 2.15.41 \|\|

*bhūtānāṃ priyakārī syāt na paradrohakarmadhīḥ \|*  
*na vedadevatānindāṃ kuryāt taiśca na saṃvaset \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All the living beings should also be good to others and should not be jealous of others. One should not denounce the Vedas and the gods and one should not talk to such people who indulge in the same.

## \|\| 2.15.42 \|\|

*yastvimaṃ niyataṃ vipro dharmādhyāyaṃ paṭhecchuciḥ \|*  
*adhyāpayet śrāvayed vā brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A Brahmana, who purifying himself, goes through this chapter on dharma, or recites it, he gets adored in the Brahmaloka.

## Chapter 16. Duties of a householder

## \|\| 2.16.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*na hiṃsyāt sarvabhūtāninānṛtaṃ vāvadet kvacit \|*  
*nāhitaṃ nāpriyaṃ vākyaṃ na stenaḥ syād kadācana \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “No living being should be killed and one should never speak untruth. One should not speak damaging words and the words which offend others. One should not steal things of others.

## \|\| 2.16.2 \|\|

*tṛṇaṃ vā yadi vā śākaṃ mṛdaṃ vā jalameva vā \|*  
*parasyāpaharañjanturnarakaṃ pratipadyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A person who steals even the grass, vegetables, lump of clay, a plant or water, he surely falls in the hell.

## \|\| 2.16.3 \|\|

*na rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna śūdrapatitādapi \|*  
*na cānyasmādaśaktaśca ninditān varjayed budhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. No Brahmana should accept charities from a fallen king, a Sudra or any other fallen person. A person with wisdom should avoid being a suppliant in front of a blameworthy person.

## \|\| 2.16.4 \|\|

*nityaṃ yācanako na syāt punastaṃ naiva yācayet \|*  
*prāṇānapaharatyevaṃ yācakastasya durmatiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One should not beg charities daily nor should one beg from one and the same person again and again. The evil-minded beggar will deprive him of his life there-by.

## \|\| 2.16.5-6 \|\|

*na devadravyahārī syād viśeṣeṇa dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*brahmasvaṃ vā nāpaharedāpadyapi kadācana \|\| 5 \|\|*

*na viṣaṃ viṣamityāhurbrahmasvaṃ viṣamucyate \|*  
*devasvaṃ cāpi yatnena sadā pariharet tataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. An excellent Brahmana, should not steal the property of the deity. A Brahmana should, not steal reaches even in emergency because a poison in all the situations is called a poison only. Therefore, the wealth of a Brahmana is considered to be the poison. Similarly the riches of the gods should also be discarded making all the efforts.

## \|\| 2.16.7 \|\|

*puṣpe śākrodake kāṣṭhe tathā mūle phale tṛṇe \|*  
*adattādānamasteyaṃ manuḥ prāha prajāpatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A person who receives the flower, vegetables, water and firewood, besides fruit and roots without being specifically given, it amounts to theft. This has been ordained by Manu.

## \|\| 2.16.8 \|\|

*grahītavyāni puṣpāṇi devārcanavidhau dvijāḥ \|*  
*naikasmādeva niyatamananujñāya kevalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Brahmanas can take the flowers for the adoration of the gods, but even the flowers should not be collected without the permission of the owner.

## \|\| 2.16.9 \|\|

*tṛṇaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ prakāśaṃ vai hared budhaḥ \|*  
*dharmārthaṃ kevalaṃ viprā hyanyathā patito bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Similarly, the intelligent person, should accept the hay, firewood, fruit and the flowers, openly in the presence of others, for the purpose of religious rite only, failing which he falls in the hell.

## \|\| 2.16.10 \|\|

*tilamudgayavādīnāṃ muṣṭirgrāhyā pathi sthitaiḥ \|*  
*kṣudhārtairnānyathā viprā dharmavidbhiriti sthitiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Still, О Brahmanas, those well-versed in the dharma have prescribed this procedure, that while walking on the road, when feeling hungry, a fist full of sesamum seeds, green gram, and barley can be received without the permission of the owner, otherwise not.

## \|\| 2.16.11-12 \|\|

*na dharmasyāpadeśena pāpaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ caret \|*  
*vratena pāpaṃ pracchādya kurvan strīśūdradambhanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pretyeha cedṛśo vipro garhyate brahmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*chadmanācaritaṃ yacca vrataṃ rakṣāṃsi gacchati \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Even otherwise, on the pretext of dharma committing a crime is a sin, and one should resort to repentance exercise. A Brahmana who conceals his sins by means of holy rites and depends on womenfolk and Sudras, is despised here and hereafter by the expounders of the Brahman. The Vrata which is performed by him deceitfully, the reward of the same goes to the Raksasas, who enjoy the same.

## \|\| 2.16.13 \|\|

*aliṅgī liṅgiveṣeṇa yo vṛttimupajīvati \|*  
*sa liṅgināṃ haredenastiryagyonau ca jāyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The one who actually is not an ascetic, but earns his living pretending to be an ascetic, he shall incur the sins of the ascetics and is reborn as a lower animal.

## \|\| 2.16.14 \|\|

*baiḍālavratinaḥ pāpā loke dharmavināśakāḥ \|*  
*sadyaḥ patanti pāpeṣu karmaṇastasya tat phalam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The religious hypocrites and impostors who perform the deceitful vratas like a cat, they indeed are sinful, become the destroyer of the dharma and they fall in the hell because of their sins.

## \|\| 2.16.15 \|\|

*pāṣaṇḍino vikarmasthān vāmācārāṃstathaiva ca \|*  
*pañcarātrān pāśupatān vāṅmātreṇāpi nārcayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The deceitful people, those who work against the scriptures, those who indulge in wrong actions, followers of Pancaratra doctrine and Pasupata doctrine, should not be extended respect even verbally.

## \|\| 2.16.16 \|\|

*vedanindāratān martyān devanindāratāṃstathā \|*  
*dvijanindāratāṃścaiva manasāpi na cintayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Those who are engaged in the denouncing of the Vedas, or deriving pleasure in the denouncing of the gods and the Brahmanas, should not be kept in mind.

## \|\| 2.16.17 \|\|

*yājanaṃ yonisaṃbandhaṃ sahavāsaṃ ca bhāṣaṇam \|*  
*kurvāṇaḥ patate jantustasmād yatnena varjayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By perfonning their yajhas, or having matrimonial relations with them, or to live with them, or to converse with them, results into the fall of a person. Therefore, one should cut off all the relations with them.

## \|\| 2.16.18 \|\|

*devadrohād gurudrohaḥ koṭikoṭiguṇādhikaḥ \|*  
*jñānāpavādo nāstikyaṃ tasmāt koṭiguṇādhikam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By being treacherous to the preceptor, it would be crores of times more sinful then being treacherous to the gods. The denouncing of the jnana (knowledge or a knowledgeable person) and becoming an athiest or a non believer is crores of times more sinful than that.

## \|\| 2.16.19 \|\|

*gobhiśca daivatairvipraiḥ kṛṣyā rājopasevayā \|*  
*kulānyakulatāṃ yānti yāni hīnāni dharmataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The sale-purchase of the cows or the bulls, paid service of deities, and to serve the king for earning livelihood, make the people to fall from their grace, besides the loss of dharma.

## \|\| 2.16.20 \|\|

*kuvivāhaiḥ kriyālopairvedānadhyayanena ca \|*  
*kulānyakulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. By marrying a denounced spouse, with the disappearing of the religious activities, nonstudy of the Vedas, insulting the Brahmanas, the people in the race have to face their fall.

## \|\| 2.16.21 \|\|

*anṛtāt pāradāryācca tathābhakṣyasya bhakṣaṇāt \|*  
*aśrautadharmācaraṇāt kṣipraṃ naśyati vai kulam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By speaking falsehood, committing adultery, by consuming the forbidden food, and by the following of the non-vedic religious practices, the family perishes in no time.

## \|\| 2.16.22 \|\|

*aśrotriyeṣu vai dānād vṛṣaleṣu tathaiva ca \|*  
*vihitācārahīneṣu kṣipraṃ naśyati vai kulam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Similarly the race and the caste get lost by the giving away of the charities to Asrotriyas (not well-read in the Vedas), Siidras, or the people who conduct themselves, against the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.16.23 \|\|

*nādhārmikairvṛte grāme na vyādhibahule bhṛśam \|*  
*na śūdrarājye nivasenna pāṣaṇḍajanairvṛte \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. One should not live in the place infested with irreligious people or in the village infested with various types of epidemics or in the kingdom of a Sudra king or in a place inhabited by heretics.

## \|\| 2.16.24-25 \|\|

*himavadvindhyayormadhye pūrvapaścimayoḥ śubham \|*  
*muktvā samudrayordeśaṃ nānyatra nivased dvijaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇo vā yatra carati mṛgo nityaṃ svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*puṇyāśca viśrutā nadyastatra vā nivased dvijaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The pleasant region falling between the Himavan and the Vindhya region, and the region between the eastern and the western oceans are the places where a Brahmana should reside. He should not live in any other regions.

## \|\| 2.16.26 \|\|

*ardhakrośānnadīkūlaṃ varjayitvā dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*nānyatra nivaset puṇyaṃ nāntyajagrāmasannidhau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Or otherwise the excellent Brahmana, can live within half a krosa (1 krosa = 3 km.) of the holy river. He should not live anywhere else. He should not live in the village of the low caste people.

## \|\| 2.16.27 \|\|

*na saṃvasecca patitairna caṇḍālairna pukkasaiḥ \|*  
*na mūrkhairnāvaliptaiśca nāntyairnāntyāvasāyibhiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Similarly, with the people who have fallen from dharma, or the Candalas, people of the Pukkasas caste, the foolish people, or those who are proud, people of the degraded castes, or their neighbours; the Brahmanas should never live there.

## \|\| 2.16.28-29 \|\|

*ekaśayyāsanaṃ paṅktirbhāṇḍapakvānnamiśraṇam \|*  
*yājanādhyāpane yonistathaiva sahabhojanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sahādhyāyastu daśamaḥ sahayājanameva ca \|*  
*ekādaśa samuddiṣṭā doṣāḥ sāṅkaryasaṃjñitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Tо sleep with such people over the same bed, or to sit with them, to take food with them, sitting in the same line, to eat in their utencils or to mix the cooked food in them, to perform their yajnas, to teach them, or to have matrimonial relations with them, taking of food together, studying together, are the eleven blemishes, which are caused by the mingling of the castes, known as Sdrhkarya Dosas.

## \|\| 2.16.30 \|\|

*samīpe vā vyavasthānāt pāpaṃ saṃkramate nṛṇām \|*  
*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena sāṅkaryaṃ parivarjayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Not only this, by having close contacts with these people, their sins are infested, therefore the wise people, making all the efforts, should disown the people of the mixed breed.

## \|\| 2.16.31 \|\|

*ekapaṅktyupaviṣṭā ye na spṛśanti parasparam \|*  
*bhasmanā kṛtamaryādā na teṣāṃ saṃkaro bhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. But if some people are seated with them in the same row, and do not touch one another or the limits are drawn by means of ashes, then one does not attract any demerit.

## \|\| 2.16.32 \|\|

*agninā bhasmanā caiva salilenāvasekataḥ \|*  
*dvāreṇa stambhamārgeṇa ṣaḍbhiḥ paṅktirvibhidyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thus with the fire, ashes, particularly with the water, making one stand at the gate, raising a pillar, or by creating an obstruction, the row can be separated.

## \|\| 2.16.33 \|\|

*na kuryācchuṣkavairāṇi vivādaṃ ca na paiśunam \|*  
*parakṣetre gāṃ dhayantīṃ na cācakṣīta kasyacit \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The enmity with anyone should not be developed without any reason, nor should one quarrel without any cause or resort to backbiting others. In case, a cow is grazing in some one’s field, the fact should not be told to anyone.

## \|\| 2.16.34-35 \|\|

*na saṃvadet sūtake ca na kañcinmarmaṇi spṛśet \|*  
*na sūryapariveṣaṃ vā nendracāpaṃ śavāgnikam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*parasmai kathayed vidvān śaśinaṃ vā kadācana \|*  
*na kuryād bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ virodhaṃ bandhubhistathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. One should not sleep with anyone with the impurity of birth. One should not touch the sensitive spot of anyone else. The disc around the sun, the rainbow, the burning fire of the funeral pyre, and the solar disc should not be discussed with anyone. A learned man shall never indicate and mention the moon. One should not pick up controversies with the relations or others.

## \|\| 2.16.36 \|\|

*ātmanaḥ pratikūlāni pareṣāṃ na samācaret \|*  
*tithiṃ pakṣasya na brūyāt na nakṣatrāṇi nirdiśet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A thing which is contrary to one’s liking or is not liked by some one, the same thing should not be extended to others. None should speak about the Tithi of the fortnight, or the constellations.

## \|\| 2.16.37 \|\|

*nodakyāmabhibhāṣeta nāśuciṃ vā dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*na devaguruviprāṇāṃ dīyamānaṃ tu vārayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The best of the Brahmana should not talk to a woman in period and also should not talk to the unclean person. No one should prevent anything from being given to Devas, preceptors or Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.16.38 \|\|

*na cātmānaṃ praśaṃsed vā paranindāṃ ca varjayet \|*  
*vedanindāṃ devanindāṃ prayatnena vivarjayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. One should not indulge in self praise, nor should one denounce others. Making all the efforts, one should avoid blemishing Devas and the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.16.39 \|\|

*yastu devānṛṣīn viprānvedān vā nindati dvijaḥ \|*  
*na tasya niṣkṛtirdṛṣṭā śāstreṣviha munīśvarāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Because, О best of the sages, a Brahmana, who denounces other Brahmanas, the gods, Rishis, and the Vedas, no repentence has been prescribed in the scriptures for such a person in this world.

## \|\| 2.16.40 \|\|

*nindayed vai guruṃ devaṃ vedaṃ vā sopabṛṃhaṇam \|*  
*kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ raurave pacyate naraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. A person who denounces the preceptors, the gods and the Vedas with their branches, he has to fall in the terrific hell for a crore of kalpas.

## \|\| 2.16.41 \|\|

*tūṣṇīmāsīta nindāyāṃ na brūyāt kiñciduttaram \|*  
*karṇau pidhāya gantavyaṃ na caitānavalokayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Similarly when they are denounced, the listener should keep quiet, giving no reply and covering both the ears with his hands, he should leave that place. One should not look at the one who denounces.

## \|\| 2.16.42 \|\|

*varjayed vai rahasyāni pareṣāṃ gūhayed budhaḥ \|*  
*vivādaṃ svajanaiḥ sārdhaṃ na kuryād vai kadācana \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A person with wisdom, should not open one’s secrets before others and should not enter into argument with his own relatives.

## \|\| 2.16.43 \|\|

*na pāpaṃ pāpināṃ brūyādapāpaṃ vā dvijāttamāḥ \|*  
*satenatulyadoṣaḥ syānmithyā dvirdeṣavān bhavet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О Best of the Brahmanas, one should not point out the sinner as a sinner or a sinless person. In either case he will be equally guilty of sins such as that of uttering falsehood.

## \|\| 2.16.44 \|\|

*yāni mithyābhiśastānāṃ patantyaśrūṇi rodanāt \|*  
*tāniputrān paśūnghninti teṣāṃ mithyābhiśaṃsinām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. When a person weeps after the levelling of the false allegations on him, and the tears which fall with his weeping, destroy the sons and animals of those false accusers.

## \|\| 2.16.45 \|\|

*brihmahatyāsurāpāne steyagurvaṅganāgame \|*  
*dṛṣṭaṃ viśodhanaṃ vṛddhairnāsti mithyābhiśaṃsane \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The one who indulges in the killing of a Brahmana, drinking of wine, or develops illicit relation with the wife of the preceptor, the repentence for the same can be there, but a person who levels the false allegation, no atonement has been prescribed for him.

## \|\| 2.16.46 \|\|

*nekṣetodyantamādityaṃ śaśinaṃ cānimittataḥ \|*  
*nāstaṃ yāntaṃ na vāristhaṃ nopasṛṣṭaṃ na maghyagam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The rising sun or the rising moon should not be witnessed by anyone without any reason. The sun and the moon should not be looked at, while setting, their reflection in the water, or their having been freed from the eclipse or in the centre of the sky.

## \|\| 2.16.47 \|\|

*tirohitaṃ vāsasā vā nādarśāntaragāminam \|*  
*na nagnāṃ striyamīkṣeta puruṣaṃ vā kadācana \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Similarly, one should never look at the sun or the moon with the covering of the cloth or their reflections in the mirror. One should never look at the nude man or a woman.

## \|\| 2.16.48 \|\|

*na ca mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā na ca saṃspṛṣṭamaithunam \|*  
*nāśuciḥ sūryasomādīn grahānālokayed budhaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Similarly, one should not see anyone passing urine or discharging faeces. One should also not look at the couples engaged in sexual exercise. Accordingly, the learned persons should not look at the sun and the moon, or a planet, when he is unclean.

## \|\| 2.16.49 \|\|

*patitavyaṅgacaṇḍālānucchiṣṭān nāvalokayet \|*  
*nābhibhāṣeta ca paramucchiṣṭo vāvaguṇṭhitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Similarly, one should not look at the fallen, handicapped, Candala, and the people defiled by Ucchista. When one is himself defiled by Ucchista, then he should not glance at others arrogantly.

## \|\| 2.16.50 \|\|

*spṛśetaretasaṃsaparśaṃ na kraddhasya guropukham \|*  
*na tailodakayośchāyāṃ na patnīṃ bhojane sati \|*  
*nāmuktabandhanāṅgāṃ vā nonmattaṃ mattameva vā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. A person should not be touched who has touched the dead body or should not look at the angry face of the preceptor, one’s own reflection in the water or the oil, one should not touch one’s wife during dinner or while her limbs are exposed due to untying of knot, besides the mad and elated person.

## \|\| 2.16.51 \|\|

*nāśnīyāt bhāryayā sārdhaṃnaināmīkṣeta cāśnatīm \|*  
*kṣuvantīṃ jṛmbhamāṇāṃ vā nāsanasthāṃ yathāsukham \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. One should never take food with one’s own wife. When she is urinating, snnezing, yawning, seated comfortably over a seat, she should not be looked at.

## \|\| 2.16.52 \|\|

*nodake cātmano rūpaṃ na kūlaṃ śvabhrameva vā \|*  
*na laṅghayecca mūtraṃ vā nādhitiṣṭhet kadācana \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Irrespective of one’s face being auspicious or inauspicious, its reflection should not be seen in the water. The urine of any one should never be crossed, nor should one stand over the same.

## \|\| 2.16.53 \|\|

*na śūdrāya matiṃ dadyāt kṛśaraṃ pāyasaṃ dadhi \|*  
*nocchiṣṭaṃ vā madhu ghṛtaṃ na ca kṛṣṇājinaṃ haviḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. No Brahmana should give advice to a Siidra, because he would not be fit for the same. He should not be given Krs'ara (rice cooked with gingelly seeds), the milk-pudding, curds, leavings, ghee or the honey. Similarly, he should not be given the skin of the black buck or the Havis.

## \|\| 2.16.54-55 \|\|

*na caivāsmai vrataṃ dadyānna ca dharmaṃ vaded budhaḥ \|*  
*na ca krodhavaśaṃ gacched dveṣaṃ rāgaṃ ca varjayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

*lobhaṃ dambhaṃ tathā yatnādasūyāṃ jñānakutsanam \|*  
*īrṣyāṃ madaṃ tathā śokaṃ mohaṃ ca parivarjayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. No person of learning, should make the Stidra to perform the vrata or should advise him on dharma. He should not be angry with him and should discard the jealousy or attachment. The greed, arrogance, fault-finding with others, denouncing of the learned people, pride, confusion, fury and the jealousy should be discarded.

## \|\| 2.16.56 \|\|

*na kuryāt kasyacit pīḍāṃ sutaṃ śiṣyaṃ ca tāḍayet \|*  
*na hīnānupaseveta na ca tīkṣṇamatīn kvacit \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. One should not cause pain to anyone, but for the sake of good, the son or the disciple can be scolded. One should never take refuge with a degraded person, nor should he do so with the extremely clever person.

## \|\| 2.16.57 \|\|

*nātmānaṃ cāvamanyeta dainyaṃ yatnena varjayet \|*  
*na viśiṣṭānasatkuryāt nātmānaṃ vā śaped budhaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A wise person should not denounce himself nor should he develop the inferiority complex in himself, making all the efforts. The persons superior to oneself should not be humiliated nor should one develop doubts in himself.

## \|\| 2.16.58 \|\|

*na nakhairvilikhed bhūmiṃ gāṃ ca saṃveśayenna hi \|*  
*na nadīṣu nadīṃ brūyāt parvateṣu ca parvatān \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The nails should not be rubbed on the ground. One should not cohabit with a cow. One should not talk about the other rivers while bathing in one and while wandering over a mountain, he should not talk about the other mountains.

## \|\| 2.16.59 \|\|

*āvāse bhojane vāpi na tyajet hasayāyinam \|*  
*nāvagāhedapo nagno vahniṃ nātivrajet padā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. At the time of going to bed or at the time of taking the food, one’s companion should never be left out. One should not take bath naked in the water and one should not walk over the fire.

## \|\| 2.16.60 \|\|

*śiro 'bhyaṅgāvaśiṣṭena tailenāṅgaṃ na lepayet \|*  
*na sarpaśastraiḥ krīḍeta svāni khāni na saṃspṛśet \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. After rubbing oil on the head, the same should not be applied over the other limbs. One should not play with the serpent or a weapon, nor should the sense organs be touched with them.

## \|\| 2.16.61 \|\|

*romāṇi ca rahasyāni nāśiṣṭena saha vrajet \|*  
*na pāṇipādavāṅnetracāpalyaṃ samupāśrayet \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The hair on the secret parts should not be touched and one should not keep company of an unclutured fellow. One should not place the hands or the feet in the fire.

## \|\| 2.16.62 \|\|

*na śiśnodaracāpalyaṃ na ca śravaṇayoḥ kvacit \|*  
*na cāṅganakhavādaṃ vai kuryānnāñjalinā pibet \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Similarly one should not play with penis, belly and the ears in any way, nor should one create sound from the nails or any other limb of the body. One should not drink water with folded hands.

## \|\| 2.16.63 \|\|

*nābhihanyājjalaṃ padbhyāṃ pāṇinā vā kadācana \|*  
*na śātayediṣṭakābhiḥ phalāni na phalena ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. One should not strike the water with the hands and the feet. One should not pluck the fruit with the striking of the stones or the fruits themselves.

## \|\| 2.16.64-65 \|\|

*na mlecchabhāṣāṃ śikṣeta nākarṣecca padāsanam \|*  
*na bhedanamavasphoṭaṃ chedanaṃ vā vilekhanam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kuryād vimardanaṃ dhīmān nākasmādeva niṣphalam \|*  
*notsaṅgebhakṣayed bhakṣyaṃ vṛthā ceṣṭāṃ ca nācaret \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. One should not learn the language of the Mlecchas (alien tribe), and the seat should not be dragged with the legs. One should not create dissension among friends. A wise person, should not crack the finger joints or snap the fingers. One should not cut or scrape unnecessarily. The sensible man should not thrash aimlessly. The eatables should not be consumed keeping them over the lap. One should not make useless movements of the limbs.

## \|\| 2.16.66 \|\|

*na nṛtyedathavā gāyenna vāditrāṇi vādayet \|*  
*na saṃhatābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ kaṇḍūyedātmanaḥ śiraḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. l.One should neither dance nor sing unecessarily, nor should he unnecessarily play on the musical instruments. One should not rub the other’s head with fingers of both the hands.

## \|\| 2.16.67 \|\|

*na laukikaiḥ stavairdevāṃstoṣayed bāhyajairapi \|*  
*nākṣaiḥ krīḍenna dhāveta nāpsu viṇmūtramācaret \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The gods should not be adored with the worldly hymns, nor should an attempt be made to please them with medicines. One should not play with the dice. One should not ease or drop faeces into the river water.

## \|\| 2.16.68 \|\|

*nocchiṣṭaḥ saṃviśennityaṃ na nagnaḥ snānamācaret \|*  
*na gacchenna paṭhed vāpi na caiva svaśiraḥ spṛśet \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. One should not go to sleep in unclean condition, and should not take a bath without robes. One should not walk, reading and touching his head.

## \|\| 2.16.69 \|\|

*na dantairnakharomāṇi chindyāt suptaṃ na bodhayet \|*  
*na bālātapamāsevet pretadhūmaṃ vivarjayet \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The nails and hair should not be cut with the teeth. The sleeping person should not be woken up. One should not sit in the morning sun shine. One should avoid the smoke of the burning dead body.

## \|\| 2.16.70 \|\|

*naikaḥ supyācchūnyagṛhe svayaṃ nopānahau haret \|*  
*nākāraṇād vā niṣṭhīvenna bāhubhyāṃ nadīṃ taret \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. One should not sleep alone in a lonely house, and should not carry his shoes himself, one should not spit uselessly and one should not cross the river on the strength of his arms.

## \|\| 2.16.71 \|\|

*na pādakṣālanaṃ kuryāt pādenaiva kadācana \|*  
*nāgnau pratāpayet pādau na kāṃsye dhāvayed budhaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. One should never wash his feet with his own feet. A learned person should not warm up his feet in fire. The legs should not be washed in a bronze vessel.

## \|\| 2.16.72 \|\|

*nābhiprāsarayed devaṃ brāhmaṇān gāmathāpi vā \|*  
*vāyvagniguruviprān vā sūryaṃ vā śaśinaṃ prati \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. One should not disregard the gods, Brahmanas, cows, the wind, the fire, the preceptor, besides the sun and the moon.

## \|\| 2.16.73 \|\|

*aśuddhaḥ śayanaṃ yānaṃ svādhyāyaṃ snānavāhanam \|*  
*bahirniṣkramaṇaṃ caiva na kurvota kathañcana \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. To sleep, to travel, to study the Vedas, to take food without bathing and to set out from the house in an unclean state, is prohibited.

## \|\| 2.16.74 \|\|

*svapnamadhyayanaṃ snānamudvartaṃ bhojanaṃ gatim \|*  
*ubhayoḥ saṃdhyayornityaṃ madhyāhne caiva varjayet \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. To sleep, to study the Vedas, to travel, taking of food, walking and excrement, should not be performed at both times of Sandhya as well as at miday.

## \|\| 2.16.75 \|\|

*na spṛśet pāṇinocchiṣṭo viprogobrāhmaṇānalān \|*  
*na cāsanaṃ padā vāpi na devapratimāṃ spṛśet \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A Brahmana defiled by Ucchista should not touch with his hands the cows, Brahmanas, and the fire. No one should touch the cooked rice and the idols of the gods with his feet.

## \|\| 2.16.76 \|\|

*nāśuddho 'gniṃ paricarenna devān kīrtayedṛṣīn \|*  
*nāvagāhedagādhāmbu dhārayennānimittataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. One should not serve the fire or the Gods or the Rishis when he is in an unclean condition. One should not enter the deep water for bathing and should not touch any one of his limbs with fire.

## \|\| 2.16.77 \|\|

*na vāmahastenoddhatya pibed vaktreṇa vā jalam \|*  
*nottaredanupaspṛśya nāpsu retaḥ samutsṛjet \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. One should not drink water raising his left hand, nor should he drink with the mouth directly. One should not reply without the performing of Acamana rite. The semen should not be dropped into the water.

## \|\| 2.16.78 \|\|

*amedhyaliptamanyad vā lohitaṃ vā viṣāṇi vā \|*  
*vyatikramenna stravantīṃ nāpsu maithunamācaret \|*  
*caityaṃ vṛkṣaṃ na vai chindyānnāpsu ṣṭhīvanamācaret \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. One should not cast into water an unclean thing, the blood, the poison, etc. One should not cross a river and should not have sexual intercourse in water.

## \|\| 2.16.79 \|\|

*nāsthibhasmakapālāni na keśānna ca kaṇṭakān \|*  
*tuṣāṅgārakarīṣaṃ vā nādhitiṣṭhet kadācana \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. One should not cut a tree in a monastery, one should not spit in water. One should not consign the ashes, relics, skull, the hair, thorns, paddy husk, fire coal, and the dry balls of cowdung.

## \|\| 2.16.80 \|\|

*na cāgniṃ laṅghayed dhīmān nopadadhyādadhaḥ kvacit \|*  
*na cainaṃ pādataḥ kuryānmukhena na dhamed budhaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. A wise person should never cross the burning fire, nor should he keep it anywhere beneath. No sensible man should kick it with the leg now blow it with the mouth.

## \|\| 2.16.81 \|\|

*na kūpamavaroheta nāvekṣetāśuciḥ kvacit \|*  
*agnau na ca kṣipedagniṃ nādbhiḥ praśamayet tathā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The unclean person should not climb over the well nor should be peep into it lowering the head. The fire should not be dropped into the fire and should not be extinguished by water.

## \|\| 2.16.82 \|\|

*suhṛnmaraṇamārtiṃ vā na svayaṃ śrāvayet parān \|*  
*apaṇyaṃ kūṭapaṇyaṃ vā vikraye na prayojayet \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. No one should convey the news of the death of one’s friend to others. The articles which are unfit for sale due to its quality should not be utilised for merchandise.

## \|\| 2.16.83 \|\|

*na vahniṃ mukhaniśvāsair jvālayennāśucirbudhaḥ \|*  
*puṇyasthānodakasthāne sīmāntaṃ vā kṛṣenna tu \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. The intelligent person, should not ignite the fire with the puffing of the air from his mouth, when he is unclean. He should plough a land in a holy centre, near water or on the border of a -village.

## \|\| 2.16.84 \|\|

*na bhindyāt pūrvasamayamabhyupetaṃ kadācana \|*  
*parasparaṃ paśūn vyālān pakṣiṇo nāvabodhayet \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. One should not break an earlier agreement accompanied by a promise. One should not invite the animals, serpents, birds, etc. to fight among themselves.

## \|\| 2.16.85 \|\|

*parabādhaṃ na kurvota jalavātātapādibhiḥ \|*  
*kārayitvā svakarmāṇi kārūn paścānna vañcayet \|*  
*sāyaṃprātar gṛhadvārān bhikṣārthaṃ nāvaghaṭṭayet \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. One should not create obstructions for others, by means of water, air, and sunshine. An artisan who having performed good work, should not be dispensed without making adequate payment of the wages to him. Similarly those who arrive for begging alms in the morning or at the evening times should not be denied the alms.

## \|\| 2.16.86 \|\|

*bahirmālyaṃ bahirgandhaṃ bhāryayā saha bhojanam \|*  
*vigṛhya vādaṃ kudvārapraveśaṃ ca vivarjayet \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. One should not wear a garland outside. The use of the fragrant material got from outside, taking food with the wife, voilent controversy, or entry from a horrible gate should be avoided.

## \|\| 2.16.87 \|\|

*na khādanbrāhmaṇastiṣṭhenna jalped vā hasan budhaḥ \|*  
*svamagniṃ naiva hastena spṛśennāpsu ciraṃ vaset \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. A learned Brahmana, should not eat food while standing and one should not spend time in excessive talking and laughing. One should not touch the fire with one’s own hand and one should not remain in the water for a long time.

## \|\| 2.16.88 \|\|

*na pakṣakeṇopadhamenna śūrpeṇa na pāṇinā \|*  
*mukhe naiva dhamedagniṃ mukhādagnirajāyata \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The fire should not be ignited by generating the wind with a wing, hand or a winnowing basket. The fire should be ignited with the puffing of the air with the mouth.

## \|\| 2.16.89 \|\|

*parastriyaṃ na bhāṣeta nāyājyaṃ yājayed dvijaḥ \|*  
*naikaścaret sabhāṃ vipraḥ samavāyaṃ ca varjayet \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. A Brahmana should not talk to other’s wife and the one who is not competent to perform the yajna, he should not be made to do so. A Brahmana should not go alone to an assembly, and should do so with one or two people and not with a crowd. One should never enter a shrine of a deity in anti-clockwise direction.

## \|\| 2.16.90 \|\|

*na devāyatanaṃ gacchet kadācid vāpradakṣiṇam \|*  
*na vījayed vā vastreṇa na devāyatane svapet \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. One should not fan with a cloth. A person should not sleep in the temple of a god. One should not undertake a journey alone; now should he travel with unrighteous people.

## \|\| 2.16.91 \|\|

*naiko 'dhvānaṃ prapadyeta nādhārmikajanaiḥ saha \|*  
*na vyādhidūṣitairvāpi na śūdraiḥ patitena vā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. One should not travel in the company of an ailing person, the Sudras or the fallen people. One should never travel without wearing the shoes or without taking the water and other requisites.

## \|\| 2.16.92 \|\|

*nopānadvarjito vātha jalādirahitastathā \|*  
*na rātrau nāriṇā sārdhaṃ na vinā ca kamaṇḍalum \|*  
*nāgnigobrāhmaṇādīnāmantareṇa vrajet kvacit \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. One should not travel with an enemy during the night, or without carrying a kamandalu. One should also not go between fires, cows or Brahmanas etc.

## \|\| 2.16.93 \|\|

*na vatsatantrīṃ vitatāmatikrāmet kvacid dvijaḥ \|*  
*na ninded yoginaḥ siddhān vratino vāyatīṃstathā \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. О Best of Brahmanas, one should never transgress a woman longing for sexual intercourse. The Yogins, the virtuous ascetics and Siddhas should never be denounced.

## \|\| 2.16.94 \|\|

*devatāyatanaṃ prājño devānāṃ caiva satriṇām \|*  
*nākrāmet kāmataśchāyāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca gorapi \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. A wise person, should not cross the shadow of the images of the gods, the Brahmanas or the cows, intentionally.

## \|\| 2.16.95 \|\|

*svāṃ tu nākramayecchāyāṃ patitādyairna rogibhiḥ \|*  
*nāṅgārabhasmakeśādiṣvadhitiṣṭhet kadācana \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Similarly one should not allow his own shadow to be crossed by the degraded people or the ailing persons. One should not stand over the burning fire, ashes or the hair or other similar things.

## \|\| 2.16.96 \|\|

*varjayenmārjanīreṇuṃ snānavastraghacodakam \|*  
*na bhakṣayedabhakṣyāṇi nāpeyaṃ ca pibed dvijaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. О Brahmanas, the dust of the broom, the water that remains in a vase after washing clothes or taking bath, should not be used. Similarly, the prohibited stuffs should not be consumed and the beverages which are unfit for drinking should not be used.

## Chapter 17. The articles fit for consumption or otherwise

## \|\| 2.17.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*nādyācchūdrasya vipro 'nnaṃ mohād vā yadi vānyataḥ \|*  
*sa śūdrayoniṃ vrajati yastu bhuṅkte hyanāpadi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. A Brahmana, should not consume the food offered by a Stidra, leaving aside the case of emergency. One accepts the food from a Stidra, he is born as a Stidra.

## \|\| 2.17.2 \|\|

*ṣaṇmāsān yo dvijo bhuṅkte śūdrasyānnaṃ vigarhitam \|*  
*jīvanneva bhavecchūdro mṛtaḥ śvā cābhijāyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A Brahmana, who consumes the degraded food of a Sudra for six months, he becomes a living Sudra and becomes dog after his death.

## \|\| 2.17.3 \|\|

*brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrasya ca munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*yasyānnenodarasthena mṛtastadyonimāpnuyāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О Best of the sages, when the food of a Brahmana, Ksatriya, Vais у a or Sudra, remains in the belly when he dies, the concerned person achieves the same yoni even after his death.

## \|\| 2.17.4 \|\|

*rājānnaṃ nartakānnaṃ ca takṣṇo 'nnaṃ carmakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca ṣaṇḍhānnaṃ caiva varjayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The cooked food of six people, viz., the actor, the carpenter, the dancer, the smith, a gang of rogues, and the food of a prostitute, should be discarded.

## \|\| 2.17.5 \|\|

*cakropajīvirajakataskaradhvajināṃ tathā \|*  
*gāndharvalohakārānnaṃ sūtakānnaṃ ca varjayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Similarly, the food of an oil-mill owner, the one who is a dyer of clothes, the washer man, thief, seller of wine, singer, black-smith, and of tire house with the impurity of the recent child birth, should be discarded.

## \|\| 2.17.6-7 \|\|

*kulālacitrakarmānnaṃ vārdhuṣeḥ patitasya ca \|*  
*paunarbhavacchatrikayorabhiśastasya caiva hi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*suvarṇakāraśailūṣavyādhabaddhāturasya ca \|*  
*cikitsakasya caivānnaṃ puṃścalyā daṇḍikasya ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Similarly the food of a potter, a painter, a fallen man, a goldsmith, a dancer, a hunter, an imprisoned fellow, an ailing person, a physician, the fallen woman, deceitful person, a thief, nonbeliever, denouncer of the gods, should be discarded.

## \|\| 2.17.8 \|\|

*stenanāstikayorannaṃ devatānindakasya ca \|*  
*somavikrayiṇaścānnaṃ śvapākasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The food offered by the seller of the wine, and of a Candala, should be discarded. The food of a person who is hen-pecked or one who allows the paramour of his wife to remain in his house, the one who is defiled by Ucchista, a miserly person and the one who always eats the left over of the food of others, should not be taken.

## \|\| 2.17.9-10 \|\|

*bhāryājitasya caivānnaṃ yasya copapatirgṛhe \|*  
*utsṛṣṭasya kadaryasya tathaivocchiṣṭabhojinaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*apāṅktyānnaṃ ca saṅghānnaṃ śastrājīvasya caiva hi \|*  
*klībasaṃnyāsinoścānnaṃ mattonmattasya caiva hi \|*  
*bhītasya ruditasyānnamavakruṣṭaṃ parikṣutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The food of an outcaste person, the cooked food meant for a multitude, the one who lives on the weapons, the eunuch, an ascetic, a drunkard, an arrogant one, a fearful person, who always keep on weeping, the one who has been humiliated and an outcaste, should not be taken.

## \|\| 2.17.11 \|\|

*brahmadviṣaḥ pāparuceḥ śrāddhānnaṃ sūtakasya ca \|*  
*vṛthāpākasya caivānnaṃ śāvānnaṃ śvaśurasya ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The food of a person, who is envious of the Brahmanas, the sinful person, that of Sraddha or of an impure house because of new birth, should not be taken. The food that has been cooked for self, disregarding the gods, besides the food of the cunning and an extremely clever person should not be taken.

## \|\| 2.17.12 \|\|

*aprajānāṃ tu nārīṇāṃ bhṛtakasya tathaiva ca \|*  
*kārukānnaṃ viśeṣeṇa śastravikrayiṇastathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The food of a woman without a child, a servant, an artisan and seller of the arms, should not be taken.

## \|\| 2.17.13-15 \|\|

*śauṇḍānnaṃ ghāṭikānnaṃ ca bhiṣajāmannameva ca \|*  
*viddhaprajananasyānnaṃ parivittyannameva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*punarbhuvo viśeṣeṇa tathaiva didhiṣūpateḥ \|*  
*avajñātaṃ cāvadhūtaṃ saroṣaṃ vismayānvitam \|*  
*gurorapi na bhoktavyamannaṃ saṃskāravarjitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*duṣkṛtaṃ hi manuṣyasya sarvamanne vyavasthitam \|*  
*yo yasyānnaṃ samaśnāti sa tasyāśnāni kilbiṣam \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. The food of the addictor of wine, a murderer, the physician, one whose organ of generation is mutilated or the food of a person who marries, when his elder brother is still a bachelor, or a woman who is married twice, should also not be taken. The food served by one who carnally enjoys the wife of his dead brother, the food which is given in anger, the food which is given with a message, or the food devoid of saihskaras should not be taken. Even the cooked food served by the preceptor should not be eaten if it is devoid of due consecration. All the sins of a person are enshrined in the food.

## \|\| 2.17.16-17 \|\|

*ārdhikaḥ kulamitraśca svagopālaśca nāpitaḥ \|*  
*ete śūdreṣu bhojyānnā yaścātmānaṃ nivedayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kuśīlavaḥ kumbhakāraḥ kṣetrakarmaka eva ca \|*  
*ete śūdreṣu bhojyānnā dattvā svalpaṃ paṇaṃ budhaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Therefore, a person who takes the food of which ever person, he actually consumes his sins too. The following persons viz.: a farm- labourer, a friend of the family, cowherd, barber, musician, potter, ploughman of the fields, after eating food among these Sudras, some money is given to them by the wise. The articles made of milk, or those fried in ghee, the milk, the parched grain, the stuff made in oil, can also be accepted from a Sudra.

## \|\| 2.17.18-19 \|\|

*pāyasaṃ snehapakvaṃ yad gorasaṃ caiva saktavaḥ \|*  
*piṇyākaṃ caiva tailaṃ ca śūdrād grāhyaṃ dvijātibhiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vṛntākaṃ nālikāśākaṃ kusumbhāśmantakaṃ tathā \|*  
*palāṇḍuṃ laśunaṃ śuktaṃ niryāsaṃ caiva varjayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The brinjals, the vegetables, safflower, asmantaka (a kind of plant), onion, garlic, sour articles, the gum of the trees, should not be accepted. Similarly, the mushrooms, the wild boar, Slesmantaka fruit, beestings, or the milk of a cow during the first seven days of calving, the eatables named Simukha, and the mushroom, should be discarded.

## \|\| 2.17.20-22 \|\|

*chatrākaṃ viḍvarāhaṃ ca śelaṃ peyūṣameva ca \|*  
*vilayaṃ sumukhaṃ caiva kavakāni ca varjayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*gṛñjanaṃ kiṃśukaṃ caiva kakubhāṇḍaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*udumbaramalābuṃ ca jagdhvā patati vai dvijaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vṛthā kṛśarasaṃyāvaṃ pāyasāpūpameva ca \|*  
*anupākṛtamāṃsaṃ ca devānnāni havīṃṣi ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. The carrot, Palas'a (Butea Frondosa), the meat of animal killed by a poisoned arrow, the wild fig tree, Kimsuka, Udumbara, and the gourd when consumed by a Brahmana, he is fallen. The Krsara (rice mixed with gingelly seeds), the wheatcake, milk pudding, pie, the unconsecrated meat, the food offered to the gods, rice gruel, the citrons, non-consecrated fish, besides the fruits of Kadamba tree, wood- apple and Indian fig-tree, should be discarded.

## \|\| 2.17.23-25 \|\|

*yavāgūṃ mātuliṅgaṃ ca matsyānapyanupākṛtān \|*  
*nīpaṃ kapitthaṃ plakṣaṃ ca prayatnena vivarjayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*piṇyākaṃ coddhṛtasnehaṃ devadhānya tathaiva ca \|*  
*rātrau ca tilasaṃbaddhaṃ prayatnena dadhi tyajet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nāśnīyāt payasā takraṃ na bījānyupajīvayet \|*  
*kriyāduṣṭaṃ bhāvaduṣṭamasatsaṃsargi varjayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. During the day time, the oilcake from which oil has been extracted as well as fried barley, and during the night the curd mixed with sesamum should be carefully avoided. One should not take in milk and butter milk together. A person should discard the stuff which is polluted by the action, served indifferently and polluted by evil conduct, and by falling therein of hair, insects and disrespectfully given.

## \|\| 2.17.26-27 \|\|

*keśakīṭāvapannaṃ ca sahṛllekhaṃ ca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*śvāghrātaṃ ca punaḥ siddhaṃ caṇḍālāvekṣitaṃ tathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*udakyayā ca patitairgavā cāghrātameva ca \|*  
*anarcitaṃ puryuṃ ṣitaṃ paryāyānnaṃ ca nityaśaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. In case the food is smelt by a dog, or is recooked, or over which a Candala has cast his glance, the same should also be abondoned. In case the food is looked by a woman in her menses, or is smelt by a cow, or is seen by fallen man, or the one who is unrespected or the food which has become stale, or the food which has been touched by a crow or a cock, or which is infested with insects, or the food which is smelt by humans or has been touched by a leper, suffering from leprosy, the same should be surely abondoned.

## \|\| 2.17.28-29 \|\|

*kākakukkuṭasaṃspṛṣṭaṃ kṛmibhiścaiva saṃyutam \|*  
*manuṣyairapyavaghrātaṃ kuṣṭhinā spṛṣṭameva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*na rajasvalayā dattaṃ na puṃścālyā saroṣayā \|*  
*malabadvāsasā vāpi paravāso 'tha varjayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The thing which is offered by a woman in period, or by an evil woman, the same should never be used. The thing which is given by an other woman clad in dirty garments, the same should also not be used. This has been ordained by lord Manu, that the milk of the cow, without a calf should not be used. Similarly the milk of a camel, within ten days of her calving, should also not be consumed.

## \|\| 2.17.30-32 \|\|

*vivatsāyāśca goḥ kṣīramauṣṭraṃ vānirdaśaṃ tathā \|*  
*āvikaṃ sandhinīkṣīramapeyaṃ manurabravīt \|\| 30 \|\|*

*balākaṃ haṃsadātyūhaṃ kalaviṅkaṃ śukaṃ tathā \|*  
*kuraraṃ ca cakoraṃ ca jālapādaṃ ca kokilam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vāyasaṃ khañjarīṭaṃ ca śyenaṃ gṛdhraṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ulūkaṃ cakravākaṃ ca bhāsaṃ pārāvatānapi \|*  
*kapotaṃ ṭiṭṭibhaṃ caiva grāmakukkuṭameva ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. In case one is non-vegetarian, even then he should not eat the flesh of a crane, swan, water- crow, sparrow, parrot, osprey, the tusk of hog, the webfooted birds, the cuckoo, blue jay, the wag-tail, falcon, vulture, owl, ruddy goose, the cock, pigeon, lapwing, the village fowl, lion, tiger, cat, dog, the hound, jackal, monkey and of the donkey.

## \|\| 2.17.33-35 \|\|

*siṃhavyāghraṃ ca mārjāraṃ śvānaṃ śūkarameva ca \|*  
*śṛgālaṃ markaṭaṃ caiva gardabhaṃ ca na bhakṣayet \|\| 33 \|\|*

*na bhakṣayet sarvamṛgān pakṣiṇo 'nyān vanecarān \|*  
*jalecarān sthalacarān prāṇinaśceti dhāraṇā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*godhā kūrmaḥ śaśaḥ śvāvicchalyakaśceti sattamāḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyāḥ pañcanakhā nityaṃ manurāha prijāpatiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Similarly the meat of all the species of deer, the flesh of the wild birds, of the aquatic or land should not be consumed. This has been ordained by the scriptures. Manu further says that the meat of a godha (alligator), tortoise, hare, porcupine, or the creatures with five nails, can be eaten. And the fish with thorny scales, the meat of the Ruru-dear, can be consumed by first offering it to the Brahmanas as well as the gods. But no other type of meat should be consumed.

## \|\| 2.17.36 \|\|

*matsyān saśalkān bhuñjīyān māṃsaṃ rauravamevaca \|*  
*nivedya devatābhyastu brāhmaṇebhyastu nānyathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The Prajapati has allowed the consuming of the meat of a peacock, patridge, Kapinjala, rhenoceros, and the panther, as eatables.

## \|\| 2.17.37-40 \|\|

*mayūraṃ tittiraṃ caiva kapotaṃ ca kapiñjalam \|*  
*vādhrīṇasaṃ bakaṃ bhakṣyaṃ mīnahaṃsaparājitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*śapharaṃ siṃhatuṇḍaṃ ca tathā pāṭhīnarohitau \|*  
*matsyāścaite samuddiṣṭā bhakṣaṇāya dvijottamāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*prokṣitaṃ bhakṣayedeṣāṃ māṃsaṃ ca dvijakāmyayā \|*  
*yathāvidhi niyuktaṃ ca prāṇānāmapi cātyaye \|\| 39 \|\|*

*bhakṣayennaiva māṃsāni śeṣabhojī na lipyate \|*  
*auṣadhārthamaśaktau vā niyogād yajñakāraṇāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-40. Similarly, О Sages, the fish Rajlvas with lotus-like face, Sirhhatundas (lion-snouted), the fish called Pathinas, the Rohit-i'ish, have been allowed to be consumed. But the meat of the aforesaid creatures sanctifying it with the sprinkling of the water should be offered to the Brahmanas, when so desired by them specifically or where ones life is in danger, only then it should be taken. In fact, no meat is fit for consumption, still a person, who offering it first to the gods and then takes it as a prasada, he does not earn any sin, or otherwise in case a person, who consumes it as a medicine, or having lost strength, or at the inspiration of others, or as left-over of the yajna, he does not earn the sin. The one who is invited in the performance of sraddha or has been invited for the sake of a god, then in case a person refuses to consume the meat as a prasada then he falls into the hell for the same number of years as the animals has hair on the body and whose meat has been served to the guests.

## \|\| 2.17.41 \|\|

*āmantritastu yaḥ śrāddhe daive vā māṃsamutsṛjet \|*  
*yāvanti paśuromāṇi tāvato narakān vrajet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The established rule is that, wine should not be drunk, should not be touched and should never be thought of by the twice-bom.

## \|\| 2.17.42 \|\|

*adeyaṃ cāpyapeyaṃ ca tathaivāspṛśyameva ca \|*  
*dvijātīnāmanālokyaṃ nityaṃ madyamiti sthitiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Because of this, one should disown wine making all the efforts. A Brahmana, who consumes these forbidden things, he loses all his merits and incurs downfall.

## \|\| 2.17.43 \|\|

*tasmāt sarvaprakāreṇa madyaṃ nityaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*pītvā patati karmabhyastvasaṃbhāṣyo bhaved dvijaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Having become defective by eating prohibited food-stuff and drinking that should not be drunk, a Brahmana loses his rights and faces downfall.

## \|\| 2.17.44 \|\|

*bhakṣayitvā hyabhakṣyāṇi pītvāpeyānyapi dvijaḥ \|*  
*nādhikārī bhavet tāvad yāvad tanna jahātyadhaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Therefore, one should avoid forbidden food with all his efforts. He goes alone after elevation and after death goes to the Raurava hell.

## Chapter 18. Daily performance of the Brahmanas

## \|\| 2.18.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*ahanyahani kartavyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ mahāmune \|*  
*tadācakṣvākhilaṃ karma yena mucyeta bandhanāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rishis said, “O Great sage, you kindly enlighten us on the daily performance of the Brahmanas and their related deeds, with the following of which, he is relieved of all the worldly bondages.”

## \|\| 2.18.2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*vakṣye samāhitā yūyaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama \|*  
*ahanyahani kartavyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ kramād vidhim \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Vyasa said, the deeds to be performed by the Brahmanas daily are being related by me in a sequence. All of you should listen to me with a concentrated mind.

## \|\| 2.18.3 \|\|

*brāhme muhūrte tūtthāya dharmamarthaṃ ca cintayet \|*  
*kāyakleśaṃ tadudbhūtaṃ dhyāyīta manaseśvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Every Brahmanas should get up in the early morning before the sun rise and should think upon his own duties and monetary affairs wherefore he has to exert his body. Then, he should meditate devoting his mind towards Ishvara.

## \|\| 2.18.4-5 \|\|

*uṣaḥ kāle 'tha saṃprāpte kṛtvā cāvaśyakaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*snāyānnadīṣu suddhāsu śaucaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prātaḥ snānena pūyante ye 'pi pāpakṛto janāḥ \|*  
*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena prātaḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. After the sun rise, a learned person should free himself from the daily routine and then take a bath in the auspicious river nearby. By so taking bath in the early morning even the sinful person is relieved of all the sins. Therefore making all the efforts, one should take his bath in the early morning.

## \|\| 2.18.6 \|\|

*prātaḥ snānaṃ praśaṃsanti dṛṣṭādṛṣṭakaraṃ śubham \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāmṛṣitā nityaṃ prātaḥ snānānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Taking of bath in the early morning is praised by the men of learnings because by so doing one gets the visible as well as the invisible merits. The ascetichood of the sages becomes permanent by taking bath in the early morning.

## \|\| 2.18.7 \|\|

*mukhe suptasya satataṃ lālā yāḥ saṃstravanti hi \|*  
*tato naivācaret karma akṛtvā snānamāditaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The saliva constantly flows from the mouth of the sleeping person, therefore without taking morning bath, one should not engage himself in any other activity.

## \|\| 2.18.8 \|\|

*alakṣmīḥ kālakarṇo ca duḥ svapnaṃ durvicintitam \|*  
*prātaḥ snānena pāpāni pūyante nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. By taking bath in the early morning, the poverty, blemish of the water, the effect of a bad dream, and evil thinking is removed. Besides all the sins too are washed out. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.18.9 \|\|

*na ca snānaṃ vinā puṃsāṃ pāvanaṃ karma susmṛtam \|*  
*home japye viśeṣeṇa tasmāt snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Therefore a person should do no work without taking bath. Bath is particularly necessary before the performing of the Japa as well as the Нота. Therefore, one should take a bath in the early morning.

## \|\| 2.18.10 \|\|

*aśaktāvaśiraskaṃ vā snānamasya vidhīyate \|*  
*ārdreṇa vāsasā vātha mārjanaṃ kāpilaṃ smṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. For an ailing person, when he is unable to take his bath, one can take bath without pouring water over the head, otherwise, one could sponge the body with the wet cloth, to purify the body. This is called Kapila bath.

## \|\| 2.18.11 \|\|

*asāmarthye samutpanne snānamevaṃ samācaret \|*  
*brāhmādīni yathāśaktau snānānyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One should take a bath, some how even when he is dependent. The learned people have prescribed the method of purifying the body when he is physically unfit to do so.

## \|\| 2.18.12 \|\|

*brāhmamāgneyamuddiṣṭaṃ vāyavyaṃ divyameva ca \|*  
*vāruṇaṃ yaugikaṃ tadvat ṣoḍhā snānaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There are six types of baths to be taken in brief which include Brahma, Agneya (fire), Vayavya (wind), Divya, Varuna (with water) and Yaugika.

## \|\| 2.18.13 \|\|

*brāhmaṃ tu mārjanaṃ mantraiḥ kuśaiḥ sodakabindubhiḥ \|*  
*āgneyaṃ bhasmanā pādamastakāddehadhūlanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Brahma bath is performed by sprinkling of the water drops with the ten-grass and repeating the mantras. The Agneya bath is performed with the application of the ashes over the body from foot to head.

## \|\| 2.18.14 \|\|

*gavāṃ hi rajasā proktaṃ vāyavyaṃ snānamuttamam \|*  
*yattu sātapavarṣeṇa snānaṃ tad divyamucyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The excellent bath by means of the dust particles raised by the kine is called the Vayavya ablution. The bath which is performed in the sunshine with the rain water, is called the Divya bath.

## \|\| 2.18.15-16 \|\|

*vāruṇaṃ cāvagāhastu mānasaṃ tvātmavedanam \|*  
*yaugikaṃ snānamākhyātaṃ yogo viṣṇuvicintanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ātmatīrthamiti khyātaṃ sevitaṃ brahmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*manaḥ śucikaraṃ puṃsāṃ nityaṃ tat snānamācaret \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The bath taken in a pond, river or reservoir is called the Varuna bath. Similarly, to establish one’s mind in his soul by the Yogins is called the Yaugika bath. In the Yoga, the self thinking of the universe is done. This is also known as the Atma-tirtha, which is adopted by the spoke- persons on Brahman. This bath purifies the minds of the people daily. Therefore it should be performed regularly.

## \|\| 2.18.17-18 \|\|

*śaktaśced vāruṇaṃ vidvān prājāpatyaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*prakṣālya dantakāṣṭhaṃ vai bhakṣayitvā vidhānataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ācamya prayato nityaṃ snānaṃ prātaḥ samācaret \|*  
*madhyāṅgulisamasthaulyaṃ dvādaśāṅgulasaṃmitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. But when a learned man is competent enough, he should perform the Varuna bath. Carefully washing the stick-brush, it should be chewed carefully. Thereafter he should perform the Acamana rite and should take his bath in the early morning. The toothbrush twig should be as thick as the middle finger and should be twelve fingers in length; covered with the skin of the tree. The teeth should be cleaned with its tip.

## \|\| 2.18.19 \|\|

*satvacaṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ syāt tadagreṇa tu dhāvayet \|*  
*kṣīravṛkṣasamudbhūtaṃ mālatīsaṃbhavaṃ śubham \|*  
*apāmārgaṃ ca bilvaṃ ca karavīraṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The tooth stick should be from a tree of milky exudation. The twigs of the Malati tree are auspicious. Apamarga, Bilva and Karavlra are particularly good.

## \|\| 2.18.20 \|\|

*varjayitvā ninditāni gṛhītvaikaṃ yathoditam \|*  
*parihṛtya dinaṃ pāpaṃ bhakṣayed vai vidhānavit \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Leaving aside all other condemned trees the teeth should be washed with a tooth stick daily in the morning. A person who brushes his teeth after the end of the day, he actually attracts sins. This has been ordained by the learned people.

## \|\| 2.18.21 \|\|

*notpāṭayeddantakāṣṭaṃnāṅgulyā dhāvayet kvacit \|*  
*prakṣālya bhaṅktvā tajjahyācchucaudeśe samāhitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The tooth stick should not be plucked from somewhere and should not be held with the fore parts of the fingers. After its use, it should be washed, broken and then thrown at a clean place.

## \|\| 2.18.22 \|\|

*snātvā saṃtarpayed devānṛṣīn pitṛgaṇāṃstathā \|*  
*ācamya mantravannityaṃ punarācamya vāgyataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereafter taking a bath, performing the acamana, a person well-versed in the mantras should perform oblation in favour of the gods and the pitrs. Thereafter, performing acamana again, he should keep quiet.

## \|\| 2.18.23-24 \|\|

*saṃmārjya mantrairātmānaṃ kuśaiḥ sodakabindubhiḥ \|*  
*āpo hiṣṭhā vyāhṛtibhiḥ sāvitryā vāruṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*oṅkāravyāhṛtiyutāṃ gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram \|*  
*japtvā jalāñjaliṃ dadyād bhāskaraṃ prati tanmanāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Then he, sprinkling water over his head with the tea-grass, should recite the auspicious mantras of Lord Vanma beginning with apo hi stha and the Gayatrl-mantra prefixed with Ornkara and Vyahrtis. With the mind fixed on the sun he should offer a handful of water to the sun.

## \|\| 2.18.25 \|\|

*prākkūleṣu samāsīno darbheṣu susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*prāṇāyāmatrayaṃ kṛtvā dhyāyet saṃdhyāmiti śrutiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. One should then be seated over the kusa- asana already spread on ground with a concentrated mind and then perform three Pranayamas and meditate on the Sandhya. This has been ordained by the Smrtis.

## \|\| 2.18.26 \|\|

*yā saṃdhyā sā jagatsūtirmāyātītā hi niṣkalā \|*  
*aiśvarī tu parāśaktistattvatrayasamudbhavā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Since Sandhya is the creator of the universe, therefore, she is free from Maya and is beyond time. She is the complete Isvarl Shakti, who emerged out of the three tattvas viz. Brahma, Visnu and Mahes'a.

## \|\| 2.18.27 \|\|

*dhyātvār'kamaṇḍalagatāṃ sāvitrīṃ vai japan budhaḥ \|*  
*prāṅmukhaḥ satataṃ vipraḥ saṃdhyopāsanamācaret \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A learned Brahmana should recite the mantra of Savitri who is lodged in the solar orbit. He should always perform the worship of Sandhya, facing the east.

## \|\| 2.18.28 \|\|

*saṃdhyāhīno 'śucirnityamanarhaḥ sarvakarmasu \|*  
*yadanyat kurute kiñcinna tasya phalamāpnuyāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A person who does not perform Sandhya, he remains impure and all his activities are of no consequence. Whatever deeds besides Sandhya are performed by him, he receives no reward for them.

## \|\| 2.18.29 \|\|

*ananyacetasaḥ śāntā brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*upāsya vidhivat saṃdhyāṃ prāptāḥ pūrvaṃ parāṃ gatim \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thus realising, instead of devoting one’s mind elsewhere, a Brahmana well-versed in the Vedas, peacefully performing Sandhya achieves the supreme position.

## \|\| 2.18.30 \|\|

*yo 'nyatra kurute yatnaṃ dharmakārye dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*vihāya saṃdhyāpraṇatiṃ sa yāti narakāyutam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The best of a Brahmana, who ignoring Sandhya, engages himself in some other religious activities, he has to face hell and remains there for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 2.18.31 \|\|

*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena saṃdhyopāsanamācaret \|*  
*upāsito bhavet tena devo yogatanuḥ paraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Therefore, all should perform Sandhya, making all the efforts. By so doing lord Shiva, the great Yogesvara also gets adored.

## \|\| 2.18.32 \|\|

*sahasraparamāṃ nityaṃ śatamadhyāṃ daśāvarām \|*  
*sāvitrariṃ vai japed vidvān prāṅmukhaḥ prayataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A learned person, facing east should firstly recite the Savitri-mantra, a thousand times (considered the maximum and best), or a hundred times (considered average), or ten times (considered as the minimum).

## \|\| 2.18.33 \|\|

*athopatiṣṭhedādityamudayantaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*mantraistu vividhaiḥ saurerṛgyajuḥ sāmasaṃbhavaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thereafter, becoming concentrated, the rising sun should be adored with the reciting of the hymns from the Rgveda, Yajurveda and Samaveda, appropriately.

## \|\| 2.18.34 \|\|

*upasthāya mahāyogaṃ devadevaṃ divākaram \|*  
*kurvota praṇatiṃ bhūmau mūrdhnā tenaiva mantrataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus adoring lord Sun-the god of gods, who is the great Yogin, placing the head over the ground, a person should pray to him reciting the mantras.

## \|\| 2.18.35 \|\|

*oṃ khakholkāya śāntāya kāraṇatrayahetave \|*  
*nivedayāmi cātmānaṃ namaste jñānarūpiṇe \|*  
*namaste ghṛṇine tubhyaṃ sūryāya brahmarūpiṇe \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “O Lord Sun, you are the form of sky-meteor, peaceful, the source of the three causes, I submit before you. You are the form of universe, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.18.36 \|\|

*tvameva brahma paramamāpo jyotī raso 'mṛtam \|*  
*bhūrbhuvaḥ svastvamoṅkāraḥ sarve rudrāḥ sanātanāḥ \|*  
*puruṣaḥ sanmaho 'tastvāṃ praṇamāmi kapardinam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. You are the form of light, the form of Brahman, salutation to you. You are the supreme Brahman, the water, the fire flame, the essence, and the nectar like. You are Bhiih, Bhavah, Svah, the Vyahrtis, Omkara, Sarva and the eternal Rudra.

## \|\| 2.18.37 \|\|

*tvameva viśvaṃ bahudhā sadasat sūyate ca yat \|*  
*namo rudrāya sūryāya tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. You are the Parama-Purusa, dwelling in the body of the living beings. You are the form of Shiva having the matted locks of hair over the head, salutation to you. You have the universal form, that had originated in many ways. I bow in reverence to Siirya, the form of Rudra. I take refuge in you.

## \|\| 2.18.38 \|\|

*pracetase namastubhyaṃ namo mīḍhuṣṭamāya te \|*  
*namo namaste rudrāya tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. You are Pracetas, the form of Varuna, saluation to you. You are bountiful, salutation to you. I take refuge with you. You are Hiranyabahu (of golden arms) and Hiranyapati (the lord of god), salutations to you again and again.

## \|\| 2.18.39 \|\|

*hiraṇyabāhave tubhyaṃ hiraṇyapataye namaḥ \|*  
*ambikāpataye tubhyamumāyāḥ pataye namaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. You are the consort of Uma, lord of Ambika, blue-throated one, holder of the Pinaka bow, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.18.40 \|\|

*namo 'stu nīlagrīvāya namastubhyaṃ pinākine \|*  
*vilohitāya bhargāya sahasrākṣāya te namaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. You are Vilohita (very ruddy), Bharga (brilliant), and have a thousand eyes, salutation to you. You remove the darkness always, and are the form of Aditya. Salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.18.41 \|\|

*namo haṃsāya te nityamādityāya namo 'stu te \|*  
*namaste vajrahastāya tryambakāya namo 'stu te \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. You carry a vajra (thunderbolt) in your hand. Salutation to you. You are VirOpaksa, Paramesvara, the great, I take refuge in you.

## \|\| 2.18.42 \|\|

*prapadye tvāṃ virūpākṣaṃ mahāntaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*hiraṇmayaṃ gṛhe guptamātmānaṃ sarvadehinām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You are secretly lodged in the hearts of all the living beings, you are resplendent, form of Brahman, you are the form of nectar, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.18.43 \|\|

*namasyāmi paraṃ jyotirbrahmāṇaṃ tvāṃ parāṃ gatim \|*  
*viśvaṃ paśupatiṃ bhīmaṃ naranārīśarīriṇam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. You have the universal form, you are the lord of animals, and the form of Ardhanarlsvara (half male and half female). You are the form of Rudra, Paramesthin, illustrious, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.18.44 \|\|

*namaḥ sūryāya rudrāya bhāsvate parameṣṭhine \|*  
*ugrāya sarvabhaktāya tvāṃ prapadye sadaiva hi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Being terrific, you are the destroyer of all. I take refuge in you for ever. One should perform the .Тара of this excellent Snrya-Hrdaya hymn.

## \|\| 2.18.45 \|\|

*etad vai sūryahṛdayaṃ japtvā stavamanuttamam \|*  
*prātaḥ kāle 'tha madhyāhne namaskuryād divākaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Mentally reciting the Swya-Hrdaya-stotra, one should offer his salutation to the sun-god in the morning as well as at the noon. The Siirva- Hrdaya-stotra had been revealed by Brahma and it should be surely passed on to the sons, disciples, and to a virtuous twice-born.

## \|\| 2.18.46 \|\|

*idaṃ putrāya śiṣyāya dhārmikāya dvijātaye \|*  
*pradeyaṃ sūryahṛdayaṃ brahmaṇā tu pradarśitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. This stotra removes all the sins, is essence of all the Vedas, beneficial for the best of the Brahmanas, and is resorted to by lhe auspicious Rishis.

## \|\| 2.18.47 \|\|

*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ vedasārasamudbhavam \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ hitaṃ puṇyamṛṣisaṅghairniṣevitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thereafter, a Brahmana after reluming to his abode, performing the Acamana appropriately, kindle the fire duly and then perform the Нота in the fire.

## \|\| 2.18.48 \|\|

*athāgamya gṛhaṃ vipraḥ samācamya yathāvidhi \|*  
*prajvālya vihniṃ vidhivajjuhuyājjātavedasam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The Rtvik’s son, the wife, disciple, or brother can perfonn the Нота rite after receiving special permissions. It can particularly be performed by the Adhvaryu in accordance with the injunction.

## \|\| 2.18.49 \|\|

*ṛtvikputro 'tha patnī vā śiṣyo vāpi sahodaraḥ \|*  
*prāpyānujñāṃ viśeṣeṇa juhuyurvā yatāvidhi \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Wearing Pavitrl (ring of /rush-grass) in hand, becoming neat and clean, clad in white garments, controlling the sense organs, one can perform the Нота with a devoted mind.

## \|\| 2.18.50 \|\|

*pavitrapāṇiḥ pūtātmā śuklāmbaradharottaraḥ \|*  
*ananyamānaso vahniṃ juhuyāt saṃyatendriyaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The deed which is performed without a yajnopavi'(a or the Ansa-grass, the reward of the same goes to the demons and the performer does not get the reward for it either in this world or the next one.

## \|\| 2.18.51 \|\|

*vinā darbheṇa yatkarma vinā sūtreṇa vā punaḥ \|*  
*rākṣasaṃ tadbhavet sarvaṃ nāmutreha phalapradam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Every Brahmana should offer his salutation to the gods, offering eatables to them, besides the flowers. He should welcome the people senior to him in age.

## \|\| 2.18.52 \|\|

*daivatāni namaskuryād deyasārānnivedayet \|*  
*dadyāt puṣpādikaṃ teṣāṃ vṛddhāṃścaivābhivādayet \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Similarly, the preceptor should also be well saved and should engage himself for his welfare. О Brahmanas, he should then practice the Vedas as per his capacity.

## \|\| 2.18.53 \|\|

*guruṃ caivāpyupāsīta hitaṃ cāsya samācaret \|*  
*vedābhyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryāt prayatnācchaktito dvijaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The best of the Brahmanas should perform the .Тара looking at the concerned book. He should make the disciples to study them as well. He should make the disciples to remember them by heart besides discussing them in detail.

## \|\| 2.18.54 \|\|

*japedadhyāpayecchiṣyān dhārayecca vicārayet \|*  
*avekṣeta ca śāstrāṇi dharmādīni dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*vaidikāṃścaiva nigamān vedāṅgāni veśiṣataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Besides these, he should also study the Vedic Nigamas, the Vedangas (post-vedic literature), and for the achievement of Yogaksema (attaining what has not been attained), take refuge in Is'vara.

## \|\| 2.18.55 \|\|

*upeyādīśvaraṃ cātha yogakṣemaprasiddhaye \|*  
*sādhayed vividhānarthān kuṭumbārthe tato dvijaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. A Brahmana should collect various materials for the welfare of his family. Then at noon, he should collect clay for the purpose of a bath.

## \|\| 2.18.56 \|\|

*tato madhyāhnasamaye snānārthaṃ mṛdamāharet \|*  
*puṣpākṣatān kuśatilān gomayaṃ śuddhameva ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. One should collect the flowers, unbroken rice, kus'a grass, sesamum, and the auspicious cowdung. One should always take his bath, in the rivers, reservoirs, tanks, lakes, and natural pits or the flowing springs.

## \|\| 2.18.57 \|\|

*nadīṣu devakhāteṣu taḍāgeṣu saraḥsu ca \|*  
*snānaṃ samācarennityaṃ gartaprastravaṇeṣu ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. One should never take bath in the water reservoirs of others. In case the common reservoirs are not available, then taking out five lumps of mud from the others reservoir, only then the bath should be taken.

## \|\| 2.18.58 \|\|

*parakīyanipāneṣu na snāyād vai kadācana \|*  
*pañcapiṇḍān samuddhṛtya snāyād vāsaṃbhave punaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. First of all, one lump of clay should be applied over the head, then at the portion above the umbilical region, two such lumps should be applied. Similarly, the portion below the navel should be cleaned with three lumps of clay, while the feet should be washed with six lumps of clay.

## \|\| 2.18.59 \|\|

*mṛdaikayā śiraḥ kṣālyaṃ dvābhyāṃ nābhestathopari \|*  
*adhaśca tisṛbhiḥ kāyaṃ pādau ṣaḍbhistathaiva ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. It should be the wet clay and its quantity should be that of the size of a myrobolan. .Then the cowdung of the same quantity should also be applied over the body.

## \|\| 2.18.60 \|\|

*mṛttikā ca samuddiṣṭā tvārdrāmalakamātrikā \|*  
*gomayasya pramāṇaṃ tat tenāṅgaṃ lepayet tataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The cowdung placed over the bank of the reservoir should be applied over the body reciting the relevant mantras. Thereafter, washing the hands, one should sip the water and with the concentration of mind one should take complete bath.

## \|\| 2.18.61 \|\|

*lepayitvā tu tīrasthastalliṅgaireva mantrataḥ \|*  
*prakṣālyācamya vidhivat tataḥ snāyāt samāhitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then the concerned god Varuna should be invoked, sanctifying the water with the reciting of the mantras, purifying the mind one should adore the invisible and indestructible lord Visnu.

## \|\| 2.18.62 \|\|

*abhimantrya jalaṃ mantraistalliṅgairvāruṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*bhāvapūtastadavyaktaṃ dhyāyan vai viṣṇumavyayam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The waters have emerged from Narayana and is the abode of the lord. Therefore, at the time of bath, a learned person should always recite the name of Narayana.

## \|\| 2.18.63-64 \|\|

*āpo nārāyaṇodbhūtāstā evāsyāyanaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tasmānnārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ snānakāle smared budhaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*procya soṃkāramādityaṃ trirnimajjejjalāśaye \|*  
*ācāntaḥ punarācāmenmantreṇānena mantravit \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Uttering the word Om, looking at the sun, one should dip himself in the river water thrice. Thereafter one who is conversent in mantras, should recite the following mantra and should perform the Acamana and then repeat the same.

## \|\| 2.18.65 \|\|

*antaścarasi bhūteṣu guhāyāṃ viśvato mukhaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkāra āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. О Lord having the universe as your face, you live in the cave like heart of all the living beings. You are the Yajna, Vasatkara, waters, brilliance, essence and the nectarine-juice.

## \|\| 2.18.66 \|\|

*drupadāṃ vā trirabhyasyed vyāhṛtipraṇavānvitām \|*  
*sāvitrīṃ vā japed vidvān tathā caivāghamarṣaṇam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Then reciting thrice the drupada-mantra, he should recite Omkara along with Vyahrtis, or alternatively one should recite Gayatri-mantra with Pranava. Besides these, a wise person should also recite the Aghamarsana-mantra.

## \|\| 2.18.67 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃmārjanaṃ kuryādāpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ \|*  
*idamāpaḥ pravahata vyāhṛtibhistathaiva ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Thereafter, reciting the mantra Apo hi stha. mayo bhuvah, and Idam apah pravahato, with Vyahrtis, one should perform the act of sprinkling.

## \|\| 2.18.68 \|\|

*tato 'bhimantrya tat tīrthamāpo hiṣṭhādimantrakaiḥ \|*  
*antarjalagato magno japet triraghamarṣaṇam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. In this way reciting the mantras beginning with "Apo hi stha’ and others, sanctifying the water, dipping himself in the water, the Aghamarsana-mantra should be uttered thrice.

## \|\| 2.18.69 \|\|

*tripadāṃ vātha sāvitrīṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*āvartayed vā praṇavaṃ devaṃ vā saṃsmareddharim \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Similarly, the recitation of Drupada and Savitrl should also be made. Otherwise Omkara should be recited repeatedly or alternatively, one should always recite the name of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.18.70 \|\|

*drupadādiva yo mantro yajurvede pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*antarjale trirāvartya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Remaining in the water, the one who recites the Yajurvedic hymn, mantra of Drupada etc., he is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.18.71 \|\|

*apaḥ pāṇau samādāya japtvā vai mārjane kṛte \|*  
*vinyasya mūrdhni tat toyaṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. For the purification of the body, filling water in the palm, a mantra should be recited and the water should be sprinkle over the head. This action relieves one of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.18.72 \|\|

*yathāśvamedhaḥ kraturāṭ sarvapāpāpanodanaḥ \|*  
*tathāghamarṣaṇaṃ sūktaṃ sarvapāpāpanodanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. As the As'vamedha-yajna is the best of all the yajnas, and removes all the sins, similarly, the Aghamarsana siikta removes all the sins.

## \|\| 2.18.73 \|\|

*athopatiṣṭhedādityaṃ mūrdhni puṣpānvitāñjalim \|*  
*prakṣipyālokayed devamudvayaṃ tamasaspari \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then the water mixed with flowers and the unbroken rice should be sprinkled above towards the sun, who is beyond darkness, facing it.

## \|\| 2.18.74-75 \|\|

*udutyaṃ citramityete taccakṣuriti mantrataḥ \|*  
*haṃsaḥ śuciṣadetena sāvitryā ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*anyaiśca vaidikairmantraiḥ sauraiḥ pāpapraṇāśanaiḥ \|*  
*sāvitrīṃ vai japet paścājjapayajñaḥ sa vai smṛtaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. With the Vedic Mantras beginning with Udu tyam, Citram, Taccaksuh, and ending with Haritsah Sucisat, the sun-god should be adored. Thereafter, Savitri-mantra should be recited. In fact, the recitation of Savitrl mantra is called Japa-yajha.

## \|\| 2.18.76 \|\|

*vividhāni pavitrāṇi guhyavidyāstathaiva ca \|*  
*śatarudrīyamatharvaśiraḥ saurāṃśca śaktitaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Besides this, other Mantras of Sfirya or the related stotras such as Vidyas, Satarudrlya, Atharvasiras can also be recited according to the liking of the devotee and according to his means.

## \|\| 2.18.77 \|\|

*prākkūleṣu samāsīnaḥ kuśeṣu prāṅmukhaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃścedīkṣamāṇor'kaṃ japyaṃ kuryāt samāhitaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Getting seated on the Darbha grass with their tips towards the eastern direction, facing himself east, purifying the mouth, looking at the sun with the concentrated mind, one should keep repeat the Japya.

## \|\| 2.18.78 \|\|

*sphāṭikendrākṣarudrākṣaiḥ putrajīvasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*kartavyā tvakṣamālā syāduttarāduttamā smṛtā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. While performing the Japam, the rosary of crystal beads, of Indraksa, Rudraksa or the seeds of Putrajlva (Rox burghii), should be used. Of course, the later ones are better than the earlier ones.

## \|\| 2.18.79 \|\|

*japakāle na bhāṣeta nānyāni prekṣayed budhaḥ \|*  
*na kampayecchirogrīvāṃ dantānnaiva prakāśayet \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. During the performing of the Japam, an intelligent person should not speak out anything. One should not look at the external things. One should not shake the head or the neck. One should not show even the teeth.

## \|\| 2.18.80 \|\|

*guhyakā rākṣasā siddhā haranti prasabhaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*ekānte suśubhe deśe tasmājjapyaṃ samācaret \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The Japam should be performed at a secluded and an auspicious place, otherwise the Guhyakas, the demons and the Siddhas forcibly usurp the reward of the same.

## \|\| 2.18.81 \|\|

*caṇḍālāśaucapatitān dṛṣṭvācamya punarjapet \|*  
*taireva bhāṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā snātvā caiva japet punaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. In case, the performer of the Japam casts a glance over a Candala, an unclean person, or a fallen person, he should at once perform Acamana and restart .Jара a fresh. In case a performer is forced to talk to such person, he should take a bath again and then start the .Jара a fresh.

## \|\| 2.18.82 \|\|

*ācamya prayato nityaṃ japedaśucidarśane \|*  
*saurān mantrān śaktito vai pāvamānīstu kāmataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. One should carryout his .Jара daily according to his means, performing the acamana and by looking at an unclean person, he should recite the Siirya-mantra or Pavamanl mantra.

## \|\| 2.18.83 \|\|

*yadi syāt klinnavāsā vai vārimadhyagato japet \|*  
*anyathā tu śucau bhūmyāṃ darbheṣu susamāhitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. In case one has to perform the japam clad in wet clothes, then he should do so remaining in water. Otherwise, he should do so, clad in dry costumes seated over an auspicious place on kusasana, with the concentration of his mind.

## \|\| 2.18.84 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ samāvṛtya namaskṛtvā tataḥ kṣitau \|*  
*ācamya ca yathāśāstraṃ śaktyā svādhyāyamācaret \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Thereafter circumambulating the sun, offering his salutaion to the earth, sipping the water, he should carryout his self-study of Vedas with devotion as per the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.18.85 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃtarpayed devānṛṣīn pitṛgaṇāṃstathā \|*  
*adāvoṅkāramuccārya namo 'nte tarpayāmi vaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Thereafter, one should offer oblation to the Devas, Rishis and Pitrs, uttering “tarayam vah” starting with Omkara.

## \|\| 2.18.86 \|\|

*devān brahmaḥṛṣīṃścaiva tarpayedakṣatodakaiḥ \|*  
*tilodakaiḥ pitṝn bhaktyā svasūtroktavidhānataḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. The Tarpana rite for Devas and the Brahminical sages should be performed with water and raw rice grains, while for the Pitrs should be performed with gingelly seeds and water, in accordance with the Grhyasutra.

## \|\| 2.18.87-88 \|\|

*anvārabdhena savyena pāṇinā dakṣiṇena tu \|*  
*devarṣostarpayed dhīmānudakāñjalibhiḥ pitan \|\| 87 \|\|*

*yajñopavītī devānāṃ nivītī ṛṣītarpaṇe \|*  
*prācīnāvītī pitrye tu svena tīrthena bhāvataḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. The wise person should perform oblation to the Gods and the Rishis with his right hand supported by the left hand below, while of the Pitrs, with handfuls of water; Similarly, while offering oblations to the gods, a person should do so properly wearing the yajnopavlta. While performing oblation for the Rishis, the yajnopavlta should be worn like a garland around the neck, and in the oblation of the Pitrs, it should be placed over the right shoulder and under the left arm. After squeezing out the water from the cloth with which he takes bath, he should perform Acamana. He should adore gods with their Mantras by means of flowers, leaves and water.

## \|\| 2.18.89 \|\|

*niṣpīḍya snānavastraṃ tu samācamya ca vāgyataḥ \|*  
*svairmantrairarcayed devān puṣpaiḥ patrairathāmbubhiḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. О Best of the humans, one should adore with devotion all the gods like Brahma, Shiva, Surya, Visnu-the killer of demon Madhu and others according to his desire.

## \|\| 2.18.90 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ śaṅkaraṃ sūryaṃ tathaiva madhusūdanam \|*  
*anyāṃścābhimatān devān bhaktyā cākrodhano 'tvaraḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Or otherwise one should offer prayer with the hymns of Purusa sukta, offering water and flowers. By so doing all the gods get worshipped appropriately.

## \|\| 2.18.91 \|\|

*pradadyād vātha puṣpāṇi sūktena pauruṣeṇa tu \|*  
*āpo vā devatāḥ sarvāstena samyak samarcitāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Then concentrating one’s mind, one should utter Omkara. Then devoting his mind towards all the gods, one should offer salutation to each one of them separately.

## \|\| 2.18.92 \|\|

*dhyātvā praṇavapūrvaṃ vai daivatāni samāhitaḥ \|*  
*namaskāreṇa puṣpāṇi vinyased vai pṛthak pṛthak \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. There is no Vedic rite more meritorious than the worship of lord Visnu. Therefore one should adore Visnu, who is beyond beginning, middle or the end.

## \|\| 2.18.93-94 \|\|

*na viṣṇvārādhanāt puṇyaṃ vidyate karma vaidikam \|*  
*tasmādanādimadhyāntaṃ nityamārādhayeddharim \|\| 93 \|\|*

*tadviṣṇoriti mantreṇa sūktena puruṣeṇa tu \|*  
*naitābhyāṃ sadṛśo mantro sūktena puruṣeṇa tu \|*  
*naitābhyāṃ sadṛśo mantro vedeṣūktaścaturṣvapi \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94. At that point of time, reciting Tad Visnoh mantra or with Pnrusa-sukta, one should propitiate Hari, because there is no hymn better than these two in all the four Vedas. Therefore, with utmost devotion one should devote his mind in Visnu and should peacefully recite the Tad Visnoh mantra, or otherwise one should adore lord Shiva, who is eternal, Mahadeva, Is'anadeva, and Sankara, sanctified by means of good feelings and thoughts.

## \|\| 2.18.95 \|\|

*nivedayeta svātmānaṃ viṣṇāvamalatejasi \|*  
*tadātmā tanmanāḥ śāntastadviṣṇoriti mantrataḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Lord Shiva should be adored with a concentrated mind by means of reciting Rudra- Gayatrl, Pranava, Satarudriya, Is'ana and the Trayambaka or Rudra mantras.

## \|\| 2.18.96 \|\|

*athavā devamīśānaṃ bhagavantaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*ārādhayenmahādevaṃ bhāvapūto maheśvaram \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The flowers, leaves of wood apple tree, or the water mixed with sandal paste, should be offered to lord Mahadeva, reciting the Mantra Om Namah Shivaya.

## \|\| 2.18.97 \|\|

*mantreṇa rudrāgāyatryā praṇavenātha vā punaḥ \|*  
*īśānenātha vā rudraistryambakena samāhitaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Thereafter, salutation should be offered to lord Shiva also known as Mrtyunjaya Mahadeva, reciting the mantra Yo Brahmanam, one should dedicate himself to the lord.

## \|\| 2.18.98 \|\|

*puṣpaiḥ patrairathādbhirvā candanādyairmaheśvaram \|*  
*uktvā namaḥ śivāyeti mantreṇānena yojayet \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. A wise Brahmana should perform circumambulation for five years, and should concentrate his mind over lord Is'ans lodged in the sky.

## \|\| 2.18.99 \|\|

*namaskuryānmahādevaṃ ṛtaṃ satyamitiśvaram \|*  
*nivedayīta svātmānaṃ yo brahmāṇamitīśvaram \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. With the stud from the Rgveda known as Hamsah sucisat, one should look at the sun. Then reaching home, he should perform the five great Yajnas with a devoted mind.

## \|\| 2.18.100 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ dvijaḥ kuryāt pañca brahmāṇi vai japan \|*  
*dhyāyīta devamīśānaṃ vyomamadhyagataṃ śivam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The five mahciyajnas include, Deva-yajna, Pitr-yajna, Bhiita-yajna, Мйпщуа-yajna and Brahma-yajna.

## \|\| 2.18.101 \|\|

*athāvalokayedarkaṃ haṃsaḥ suciṣadityṛcā \|*  
*kuryāt pañca mahāyajñān gṛhaṃ gatvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*
