94\. Even a poor Brahmana should perform the sraddha with a concentrated mind, taking his bath and offering water with sesamum seeds as oblation, fruits and roots.

## \|\| 2.22.95 \|\|

*pitā pitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*yo yasya mriyate tasmai deyaṃ nānyasya tena tu \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. One should not perform pindadana or sraddha when his father is alive. Of course, he can perform the homa. According to another opinion, a son can perform the s'rdddha to those pitrs, to whom his father offers sraddha.

## \|\| 2.22.96 \|\|

*bhojayed vāpi jīvantaṃ yathākāmaṃ tu bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*na jīvantamatikramya dadāti śrūyate śrutiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. At the death of the father, grandfather, the great grandfather, or the beloved one, the sraddha could be performed for the one who is dead and not for any other person.

## \|\| 2.22.97 \|\|

*dvyāmuṣyāyaṇiko dadyād bījikṣetrikayoḥ samam \|*  
*ṛkyādardhaṃ samādadyānniyogotpādito yadi \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. In case the father or others are alive, then they should be served with food with due devotion. One who is pure and self-controlled does not give unto the dead by transgressing the living one.

## \|\| 2.22.98 \|\|

*aniyuktaḥ suto yaśca śulkato jāyate tviha \|*  
*pradadyād bījine piṇḍaṃ kṣetriṇe tu tato 'nyathā \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Dvyamusyayanika son of two fathers (i.e. natural as well as father by adoption) can also perform smddha for both, or a son bom to a widow by the practice of Niyoga rite can also do so. Then he shall be the true heir.

## \|\| 2.22.99 \|\|

*dvau piṇḍau nirvapet tābhyāṃ kṣetriṇe bījine tathā \|*  
*kīrtayedatha caikasmin bījinaṃ kṣetriṇaṃ tataḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. But a son who has been born to a person during his life time due to some illicit relation (without the sanction of Niyoga), he can perform pindadana for the progenitor alone. However, he may perform sraddha to the mother’s husband.

## \|\| 2.22.100 \|\|

*mṛtāhani tu kartavyamekodiṣṭaṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*aśauce sve parikṣīṇe kāmyaṃ vai kāmataḥ punaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. But in case a son is bom by means of Niyoga, he can perform pindadana for Ksetrin (mother’s husband) and Bijin (progenitor) as well. He shall initially utter the name of Ksetrin, offering two pindas for each one of them. On the day of death, the Ekoddista-sraddha has to be performed appropriately.

## \|\| 2.22.101 \|\|

*pūrvāhne caiva kartavyaṃ śrāddhamabhyudayārthinā \|*  
*devavatsarvameva syād yavaiḥ kāryā tilakriyā \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. After the completion of the death impurity, the Kamya-sraddha should be performed as per one’s own liking. A person desirous of his prosperity should perform the Abhyudayika- sraddha in the forenoon alone.

## \|\| 2.22.102 \|\|

*darbhāśca ṛjavaḥ kāryā yugmān vai bhojayed dvijān \|*  
*nāndīmukhāstu pitaraḥ prīyantāmiti vācayet \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. All the performance in this type of s'raddha, resemble the one in the Deva-sraddha. The sesamum should not be used in this sraddha and the Darbha grass should also be placed straight. Besides, food should be offered to even number of Brahmanas at a time.

## \|\| 2.22.103 \|\|

*mātṛśrāddhaṃ tu pūrvaṃ syāt pitṝṇāṃ syādanantaram \|*  
*tato mātāmahānāṃ tu vṛddhau śrāddhatrayaṃ smṛtam \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. As an auspicious beginning, he should recite, “May the Pitrs be pleased.” The sraddha to the mothers should be performed at the outset. Thereafter the sraddha of the pitrs is to be performed.

## \|\| 2.22.104 \|\|

*davapūrvaṃ pradadyād vai na kuryādapradakṣiṇam \|*  
*prāṅmukho nirvapet piṇḍānupavītī samāhitaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Then the sraddha to the maternal grandfather should be performed. Thus, these three sraddhas should be performed when there is a prosperous occasion in the family. This should be performed along with Vaisvadeva rites. The anti-clockwise circumambulation is not performed.

## \|\| 2.22.105 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ tu mātaraḥ pūjyā bhaktyā vai sagaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*sthaṇḍileṣu vicitreṣu pratimāsu dvijātiṣu \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. A learned person, concentrating his mind, wearing the yajhopavlta, facing the east should perform the sraddha. Initially the mothers alongwith the Ganesvaras should be worshipped with devotion.

## \|\| 2.22.106 \|\|

*puṣperdhūpaiśca naivedyairgandhādyairbhūṣaṇairapi \|*  
*pūjayitvā mātṛgaṇaṃ kūryācchrāddhatrayaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. This worship should be performed in the open ground, in images, or in Brahmanas, offering the flowers, the incense, eatables, and the ornaments.

## \|\| 2.22.107 \|\|

*akṛtvā mātṛyāgaṃ tu yaḥ śrāddhaṃ pariveṣayet \|*  
*tasya krodhasamāviṣṭā hiṃsāmicchanti mātaraḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Thus adoring the Matrkas, the Brahmana should perform the three sraddhas. A Brahmana, who performs sraddha, without adoring the sixteen Matrkas, they become infuriated and cause injuries.

## Chapter 23. Views on Impurity

## \|\| 2.23.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*daśāhaṃ prāhurāśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vipaścitaḥ \|*  
*mṛteṣu vātha jāteṣu brāhmaṇānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “O Best of Brahmanas, the sages say, that in case of the birth or death of the Sapindas (to whom pindas are to be offered for six generations), the Brahmanas have to observe impurity for ten days.

## \|\| 2.23.2 \|\|

*nityāni caiva karmāṇi kāmyāni ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*nakuryād vihitaṃ kiñcit svādhyāyaṃ manasāpica \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. During this period of impurity, neither the Nitya (daily) rites, nor the Kamya (for attaining desired ends) rites, nor should any other prescribed rites be performed. The self-studies should not be attempted even mentally.

## \|\| 2.23.3 \|\|

*śucīnakrodhanān bhūmyān śālāgnau bhāvayed dvijān \|*  
*śuṣkānnena phalairvāpi vaitānaṃ juhuyāt tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The performance of homa etc. should be entmsted to the auspicious Brahmana, devoid of anger, having peaceful nature. The Brahmanas should perform homa with dry cereals and fruit etc. in the sacrificial fire.

## \|\| 2.23.4 \|\|

*na spṛśeyurimānanye na ca tebhyaḥ samāharet \|*  
*caturthe pañcame vāhni saṃsparśaḥ kathito budhaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Other people, should neither touch the Sutaki (impure) Brahmana, nor should he be asked to bring anything. The learned people are of the opinion that such Brahmanas can be touched on the fourth or the fifth day.

## \|\| 2.23.5 \|\|

*sūtake tu sapiṇḍānāṃ saṃsparśo na praduṣyati \|*  
*sūtakaṃ sūtikāṃ caiva varjayitvā nṛṇāṃ punaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. During the time of impurity, in case the people of the same row touch each other, then no blemish is involved. Only such of the people attracting the impurity of sutaka, (i.e. the mother giving birth to the new child) should not be touched.

## \|\| 2.23.6 \|\|

*adhīyānastathā yajvā vedavicca pitā bhavet \|*  
*saṃspṛśyāḥ sarva evaite snānānmātā daśāhataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The father who is well versed in the Vedas, or those who study the Vedas, are eligible for touching after taking of a bath. But with the passing of the tenth day, even the mother (who has given birth to the child) is purified after a bath and can be touched, aw ylfbm?

## \|\| 2.23.7 \|\|

*daśāhaṃ nirguṇe proktamaśaucaṃ cātinirguṇe \|*  
*ekadvitriguṇairyuktaṃ catustryekadinaiḥ śuciḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The impurity is said to be for ten days in the case of a Nirguna (devoid of qualities) and Atinirguna (extremely devoid of qualities). One who possesses a single guna, two gunas or three gunas, then he gains purity after four, two and one day respectively.

## \|\| 2.23.8 \|\|

*daśāhāt tu paraṃ samyagadhīyīta juhoti ca \|*  
*caturthe tasya saṃsparśaṃ manurāha prajāpatiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Manu, the Prajapati has said, that after the tenth day, a person can resort to the reciting of the Veda, and can perform homa as well. Under these conditions he can be touched on the fourth day itself.

## \|\| 2.23.9 \|\|

*kriyāhīnasya mūrkhasya mahārogiṇa eva ca \|*  
*yatheṣṭācaraṇasyāhurmaraṇāntamaśauvakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. But a person, who is devoid of the performance as per the Sastras, or is a fool, an ailing person, and the one who acts as per his own wishes, attracts impurity for the whole life till death.

## \|\| 2.23.10 \|\|

*trirātraṃ daśarātraṃ vā brāhmaṇānāmaśaucakam \|*  
*prāksaṃskārāt trirātraṃ syāt tasmādūrdhvaṃ daśāhakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The impurity of the Brahmanas continues for three days or ten nights. If the dead one is less than a year in age, the impurity is for three days, and if the age is beyond one year, the impurity is for ten days.

## \|\| 2.23.11 \|\|

*ūnadvivārṣike prete mātāpitrostadiṣyate \|*  
*trirātreṇa śucistvanyo yadi hyatyantanirguṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In case a dead child is less than two years of age, his parents attracts the similar type of impurity for ten days. Besides them, the others also attract impurity for three nights after which they get purified. In case the child has died before cutting the teeth, or if the dead one is extremely devoid of qualities, then the parents of the child attract impurity for a day. In case a child dies after the growing of his teeth, the parents attract impurity for three nights.

## \|\| 2.23.12 \|\|

*adantajātamaraṇe pitrorekāhamiṣyate \|*  
*jātadante trirātraṃ syād yadi syātāṃ tu nirguṇau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When the child dies at the time of the growing of the teeth, then the people of the same lineage get purified after taking bath. Before the performing of the tonsure ceremony, in case the child dies, the parents attract impurity for a night. In case the death of the child occurs before the performing of the thread ceremony, the people of the same line, attract impurity for three nights.

## \|\| 2.23.13-14 \|\|

*ādantajananāt sadya ācaulādekarātrakam \|*  
*trirātramaupanayanāt sapiṇḍānāmudāhṛtam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*jātamātrasya bālasya yadi syānmaraṇaṃ pituḥ \|*  
*mātuśca sūtakaṃ tat syāt pitā syāt spṛśya eva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. When a child dies soon after his birth, then the parents alone attract the impurity. After the bath, the father can be touched. In the case of a brother, the Sapindas (near kinsmen) should always observe As'auca for the prescribed period. If the brother is not qualified, the impurity is for one more day after ten days.

## \|\| 2.23.15 \|\|

*sadyaḥ śaucaṃ sapiṇḍānāṃ kartavyaṃ sodarasya ca \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ daśāhādekāhaṃ sodaro yadi nirguṇaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When a child dies after the growing of the teeth, then impurity of the kinsmen is attracted for a day, and when he dies after the tonsure ceremony, the impurity is for three nights, for the nirguna people of the same line.

## \|\| 2.23.16 \|\|

*athordhvaṃ dantajananāt sapiṇḍānāmaśaucakam \|*  
*ekarātraṃ nirguṇānāṃ cailādūrdhvaṃ trirātrakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Best of Brahmanas, in case an infant dies before the cutting of the teeth, the extremely nirguna Sapindas have impurity for one day.

## \|\| 2.23.17 \|\|

*(vratādeśāt sapiṇḍānāmarvāk snānaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva guṇināmūrdhvaṃ tu viṣamaṃ punaḥ)*  
*arvāk ṣaṇmāsataḥ strīṇāṃ yadi syād garbhasaṃstravaḥ \|*  
*tadā māsasamaistāsāmaśaucaṃ divasaiḥ smṛtam)*  
*tata ūrdhvaṃ tu patane strīṇāṃ dvādaśarātrikam \|*  
*sadyaḥ śaucaṃ sapiṇḍānāṃ garbhastrāvācca vā tataḥ)*  
*garbhacyutāvahorātraṃ sapiṇḍe 'tyantanirguṇe \|*  
*yatheṣṭācaraṇe jñātau trirātramiti niścayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. (In case of the abortion in the first four months or miscarriage in the 5th or 6lh month, all the Sapindas (kinsmen) are purified with the performing of a vrata. In the case of all Gunins, the contrariness is beyond that. In case the women faces abortion before six months, then the impurity attracted is for the number of days equivalent to the period of the pregnency, carried by a woman. In case the abortion takes place after the six months frequency, then the ladies attract impurity for twelve nights. In the case of abortion upto the fourth month, the Sapindas are instantaneously purified.) After the abortion, all the collateral people are purified in a day and a night. But a person who conducts himself against the family tradition, attracts impurity for three nights. This is the conclusion.

## \|\| 2.23.18 \|\|

*yadi syāt sūtake sūtirmaraṇe vā mṛtirbhavet \|*  
*śeṣeṇaiva bhavecchuddhirahaḥ śeṣe trirātrakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In case an impurity (of birth or death) is followed by another impurity, then the purity is after the remaining impurity is over. If the remainder is only a day, the impurity continues for three days.

## \|\| 2.23.19 \|\|

*maraṇotpattiyoge tu maraṇācchuddhiriṣyate \|*  
*aghavṛddhimadāśaucamūrghvaṃ cet tena śudhyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In case the impurity of death is followed by the impurity of birth or vice versa, then with the relieving from the death impurity, both the impurities come to an end. In case the first impurity is greater, even then its purity is ceased with the earlier one.

## \|\| 2.23.20 \|\|

*atha cet pañcamīrātrimatītya parato bhavet \|*  
*aghavṛddhimadāśaucaṃ tadā pūrveṇa śudhyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then after the lapse of the five nights the impurity shall begin. In case one receives the information about the birth and death at some other place or a land, then the impurity shall continue as long as the remainder of that period is to be concluded.

## \|\| 2.23.21 \|\|

*deśāntaragataṃ śrutvā sūtakaṃ śāvameva tu \|*  
*tāvadaprayato martyo yāvaccheṣaḥ samāpyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When a person comes to know of the impurity after the death, then the people of the same family attract impurity for three nights alone. In case the information for death is received after a year, then the purity is regained after the taking of the bath. But when a person is well-versed in the Vedas, is quite studious, performer of the yajna, and earns living by small means, he gets purified in all the situations simply with the taking of a bath. If the daughter’s are not married, the Asauca for the Sapindakas is for three days; if they are married, the impurity is for the husband alone. A girl who has not yet been married, and when she dies, the relatives attract impurity for a day alone. When a girl who is of less than two year’s of age, the purity is gained soon. Upto the cutting of teeth, no impurity even to the brother, upto the tonsure ceremony the impurity is for a day. Upto the marriage, the impurity is for three days and beyond that it is for ten days.

## \|\| 2.23.22 \|\|

*atīte sūtake proktaṃ sapiṇḍānāṃ trirātrakam \|*  
*tathaiva maraṇe snānamūrdhvaṃ saṃvatsarād yadi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On the death of maternal grandfather, the impurity is for three days. In the case of Siitaka (birth) impurity to the same is the case.

## \|\| 2.23.23 \|\|

*vedāntaviccādhīyāno yo 'gnimān vṛttikarṣitaḥ \|*  
*sadyaḥ śaucaṃ bhavet tasya sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the case of relatives through marriage, the related persons attract impurity for two days with a night between or vice versa. On the death of a Brahmacarin or the preceptor, the case is same.

## \|\| 2.23.24 \|\|

*strīṇāmasaṃskṛtānāṃ tu pradānāt pūrvataḥ sadā \|*  
*sapiṇḍānāṃ trirātraṃ syāt saṃskāre bhartureva hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. At the death of a king, the people living in his domain, attract the impurity upto the rising of the sun. In case the daughter dies in the house of her parents, the father attracts impurity for three nights.

## \|\| 2.23.25-26 \|\|

*ahastvadattakanyānāmaśaucaṃ maraṇe smṛtam \|*  
*ūnadvivarṣānmaraṇe sadyaḥ śaucamudāhṛtam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ādantāt sodare sadya ācaulādekarātrakam \|*  
*āpradānāt trirātraṃ syād daśarātramataḥ param \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. In case a woman, disowning her earlier legally wed husband and lives with some other person, when she dies or her step son dies, besides at the death of the wife of preceptor, whether of the same caste or of another caste, the impurity is for a day and a night. If a priest, or a learned Pandita dies in one’s own village, the impurity is for one day.

## \|\| 2.23.27 \|\|

*mātāmahānāṃ maraṇe trirātraṃ syādaśaucakam \|*  
*ekodakānāṃ maraṇe sūtake caitadeva hi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When a stranger dies while living in a house, it attracts impurity for three nights and at the death of the wife’s brother, the impurity lasts for a day or a night, fort

## \|\| 2.23.28 \|\|

*pakṣiṇī yonisambandhe bāndhaveṣu tathaiva ca \|*  
*ekarātraṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ gurau sabrahmacāriṇi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. At the death of the father-in-law or the mother-in-law, the impurity lasts for three nights and at the death of a person belonging to the same gotra, the purity is gained at once after bath.

## \|\| 2.23.29 \|\|

*prete rājani sajyotiryasya syād viṣaye sthitiḥ \|*  
*gṛhe mṛtāsu dattāsu kanyakāsu tryahaṃ pituḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. During the impurity of the birth and death, a Brahmana is purified after ten days, a Ksatriya in twelve days, a Vaisya in fifteen days and a Shudra in a month.

## \|\| 2.23.30 \|\|

*parapūrvāsu bhāryāsu putreṣu kṛtakeṣu ca \|*  
*trirātraṃ syāt tathācārye svabhāryāsvanyagāsu ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When a Brahmana were to have a Ksatriya. a Vais'ya, or a Sfldra as his kinsman and if he were to die, then the Brahmana is purified in ten days.

## \|\| 2.23.31 \|\|

*ācāryaputre patnyāṃ ca ahorātramudāhṛtam \|*  
*ekāhaṃ syādupādhyāye svagrāme śrotriye 'pi ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In case a Ksatriya is related in a lower caste or is related to a Vaisya, and a death occurs, then the purity shall be gained by him as per his varna.

## \|\| 2.23.32 \|\|

*trirātramasapiṇḍeṣu svagṛhe saṃsthiteṣu ca \|*  
*ekāhaṃ cāsvavarye syādekarātraṃ tadiṣyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. All people should observe impurity for the death of a higher caste man with respect, in accordance with the rules governing that caste. In regard to people of his own caste, he should observe his own purity according to rules of their caste.

## \|\| 2.23.33 \|\|

*trirātraṃ śvaśrūmaraṇe śvaśure vai tadeva hi \|*  
*sadyaḥ śaucaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ sagotre saṃsthite sati \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. With the developing of an impurity with a Sfldra kinsman, the Vaisya gets purified in six days, the Ksatriyas in three nights and a Brahmana in a single night respectively.

## \|\| 2.23.34 \|\|

*śuddhyed vipro daśāhena dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ \|*  
*vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhena śūdro māsena śudyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. О Best of the Brahmanas, when an impurity is attracted by a Vaisya kinsman, Sfldra gets purified in a fortnight, a Ksatriya in six nights and a Erahmana in three nights respectively.

## \|\| 2.23.35 \|\|

*kṣatraviṭśūdradāyādā ye syurviprasya bāndhavāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmaśauce viprasya daśāhācchuddhiriṣyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The impurity to be observed in the case of (birth or death of) Brahmana kinsman by Ksattriya and Vaisya is six nights and ten days respectively.

## \|\| 2.23.36 \|\|

*rājanyavaiśyāvapyevaṃ hīnavarṇāsu yoniṣu \|*  
*svameva śaucaṃ kuryātāṃ viśuddhyarthamasaṃśayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Even otherwise, when a Brahmana attracts impurity through the Sradras, Vaisyas or Ksatriya, then he gets purified in ten nights. This has been ordained by lord Visnu.

## \|\| 2.23.37 \|\|

*sarve tūttaravarṇānāmaśaucaṃ kuryurādṛtāḥ \|*  
*tadvarṇavidhidṛṣṭena svaṃ tu śaucaṃ svayoniṣu \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In case a Brahmana dies, and a Brahmana, unrelated to him performs his funeral rites out of friendship, and taking food with the relatives, lives in his house, then the said Brahmana achieves purity in ten nights.

## \|\| 2.23.38 \|\|

*ṣaḍrātraṃ vā trirātraṃ syādekarātraṃ krameṇa hi \|*  
*vaiśyakṣatriyaviprāṇāṃ śūdreṣvāśaucameva tu \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In case, the said Brahmana consumes the food only in the house of the dead Brahmana, then he achieves purity in three nights. In case he stays there without taking food, he achieves purity on the same day.

## \|\| 2.23.39 \|\|

*ardhamāso 'tha ṣaḍrātraṃ trirātraṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*śūdrakṣatriyaviprāṇāṃ vaiśyeṣvāśaucamiṣyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A person who performs the last rites of the close relatives, after their death, he gets purified in three nights. Those of the relatives who touch the dead body are freed from impurity in ten days.

## \|\| 2.23.40-41 \|\|

*ṣaḍrātraṃ vai daśāhaṃ ca viprāṇāṃ vaiśyaśūdrayoḥ \|*  
*aśaucaṃ kṣatriye proktaṃ krameṇa dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śūdraviṭkṣatriyāṇāṃ tu brāhmaṇe saṃsthite sati \|*  
*daśarātreṇa śuddhiḥ syādityāha kamalodbhavaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. In case a Brahmana, out of covetousness, performs the last rites of some one, then such a Brahmana, gets purified in ten days, a Ksatriya gets purified in twelve days, a Vaisya in fifteen days and a Sudra in a month. Or alternatively all of them get purified in six days, or three nights.

## \|\| 2.23.42 \|\|

*asapiṇḍaṃ dvijaṃ pretaṃ vipro nirhṛtya bandhuvat \|*  
*aśitvā ca sahoṣitvā daśarātreṇa śudhyati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In case some one performs the funeral rites of the poor Brahmana, or an orphan, then he gets purified after taking a bath and consuming the ghee.

## \|\| 2.23.43 \|\|

*yadyannamatti teṣāṃ tu trirātreṇa tataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*anadannannamahnaiva na ca tasmin gṛhe vaset \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. When a person of a lower castes performs the last rites of the person of the higher caste or vice-versa, or touches the dead body during impurity, then he gets purified after his bath.

## \|\| 2.23.44 \|\|

*sodakeṣvetadeva syānmāturāpteṣu bandhuṣu \|*  
*daśāhena śavasparśe sapiṇḍaścaiva śudhyati \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After the death of a Brahmana, when a person walks with the funeral procession for his cremation, he gets purified, after taking the bath with clothes, touching the fire and taking in ghee.

## \|\| 2.23.45 \|\|

*yadi nirharati pretaṃ prolabhākrāntamānasaḥ \|*  
*daśāhena dvijaḥ śudhyed dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In following the dead body, a Ksatriya is purified in a day, a Vaisya in two days, and a Sudra in three days. It is also prescribed that they should perform pranayamas, a hundred times in addition to all these cases.

## \|\| 2.23.46 \|\|

*ardhamāsena vaiśyastu śūdro māsena śudhyati \|*  
*ṣaḍrātreṇāthavā sarve trirātreṇāthavā punaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In case a Brahmana laments in the house of a Sudra, before the collection of the bones of the uead body, he attracts impurity for three nights or otherwise, he attracts the impurity for a day after the collection of the bones.

## \|\| 2.23.47 \|\|

*anāthaṃ caiva nirhṛtya brāhmaṇaṃ dhanavarjitam \|*  
*snātvā saṃprāśya tu ghṛtaṃ śudhyanti brāhmaṇādayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Before the collection of the bones, when a Brahmana laments at the house of a Ksatriya or Vaisya, then he attracts impurity for a day before the collection of the bones; otherwise it is till the rise of the sun or of stars. In case of the death of a Brahmana, the impurity lasts till the performance of bath.

## \|\| 2.23.48 \|\|

*avaraśced varaṃ varṇamavaraṃ vā varo yadi \|*  
*aśauce saṃspṛśet snehāt tadāśaucena śudhyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In case a Brahmana goes to the house of a dead Brahmana and laments there before his bones are collected, then he gets purified by taking a bath with his clothes on. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.23.49 \|\|

*pretībhūtaṃ dvijaṃ vipro yo 'nugacchata kāmataḥ \|*  
*snātvā sacailaṃ spṛṣṭvāgniṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A person who sleeps or takes food with the impure people, irrespective of his being a relative or otherwise, he gets purified after ten days.

## \|\| 2.23.50 \|\|

*ekāhāt kṣatriye śuddhirvaiśye syācca dvyahena tu \|*  
*śūdre dinatrayaṃ proktaṃ prāṇāyāmaśataṃ punaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. A person who at his own will, takes food with the relatives of the deceased person, he gets purified after taking the bath when the period of impurity ceases.

## \|\| 2.23.51 \|\|

*anasthisaṃcite śūdre rauti ced brāhmaṇaḥ svakaiḥ \|*  
*trirātraṃ syāt tathāśaucamekāhaṃ tvanyathā smṛtam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When a person suffering from famine, takes food with the impure person, then he shall remain impure for the equivalent number of days. Then he shall have to perform repentence.

## \|\| 2.23.52 \|\|

*asthisaṃcayanādarvāgekāhaṃ kṣatravaiśyayoḥ \|*  
*anyathā caiva sajyotirbrāhmaṇe snānameva tu \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. At the death of an Agnihotra Brahmana, the impurity continues upto the period of his funeral. The impurity of the birth and the death has to be performed with the people of the same gotra and others.

## \|\| 2.23.53 \|\|

*anasthisaṃcit vipre brāhmaṇo rauti cet tadā \|*  
*snānenaiva bhavecchuddhiḥ sacailena na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Sapinda relationship ceases from the seventh generation. The Samanodakabhava (state of offering water oblation) ceases if the birth and the names are not known

## \|\| 2.23.54 \|\|

*yastaiḥ sahāśanaṃ kuryācchayanādīni caiva hi \|*  
*bāndhavo vāparo vāpi sa daśāhena śudhyati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The father, the grandfather and the great grandfather are those who enjoy the portion of the pindas and their Sapinda relationship continues upto seven generations.

## \|\| 2.23.55 \|\|

*yasteṣāmannamaśnāti sakṛdevāpi kāmataḥ \|*  
*tadāśauce nivṛtte 'sau snānaṃ kṛtvā viśudhyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The women who are not married, their Sapinda relationship continues upto seven generations of the family of their births, while that of a married woman, the Sapinda relationship is the same as of her husband. This has been ordained by the Brahma.

## \|\| 2.23.56 \|\|

*yāvattadannamaśnāti durbhikṣopahato naraḥ \|*  
*tāvantyahānyaśaucaṃ syāt prāyaścittaṃ tataścaret \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Such of the persons who were bom from one and the same father but different mothers, the Sapinda relationship of such sons continues only upto three generations.

## \|\| 2.23.57 \|\|

*dāhādyaśaucaṃ kartavyaṃ dvijānāmagnihotriṇām \|*  
*sapiṇḍānāṃ tu maraṇe maraṇāditareṣu ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The artisans, the skilled workers, the physicians, the slave girls, the slaves, those who perform charities appropriately, knowers of Brahman, Brahmacarins, the performers of the yajnas, besides the performers of the vratas or the king who has been crowned properly and the distributors of food, get purified instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.23.58 \|\|

*sapiṇḍatā ca puruṣe saptame vinivartate \|*  
*samānodakabhāvastu janmanāmnoravedane \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Or otherwise, the purification is achieved atonce, while performing the yajna, during the performing of the marriage, worship of the gods, during the famine, or at the time of some calamity.

## \|\| 2.23.59-60 \|\|

*pitā pitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*lepabhājastrayaścātmā sāpiṇḍyaṃ sāptapauruṣaṇ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*aprattānāṃ tathā strīṇāṃ sāpiṇḍyaṃ sāptapauruṣam \|*  
*ūḍhānāṃ bhartusāpiṇḍyaṃ prāha devaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. At the time of death during the warfare, in the case of the death of near cousins due to snake bite, or when a person dies in the fire, in an imperishable heroic path, for the sake of a Brahmana or cows, or if a person dies after renunciation, one get instant purity.

## \|\| 2.23.61 \|\|

*ye caikajātā bahavo bhinnayonaya eva ca \|*  
*bhinnavarṇāstu sāpiṇḍyaṃ bhavet teṣāṃ tripūruṣam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. A person who embraces Brahmacarya for life long, or becomes a forest dweller, or an ascetic, or a religious student, no impurity is enjoined by such a person. When a fallen man dies, there is no impurity.

## \|\| 2.23.62 \|\|

*kāravaḥ śilpino vaidyā dāsīdāsāstathaiva ca \|*  
*dātāro niyamī caiva brahmavidbrahmacāriṇau \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. At the death of a fallen man, the funeral rites, obsequies, and the collection of the bones are not performed. Besides these, the crying at their death, performing of pindadana and sraddha or similar rite also should not be performed.

## \|\| 2.23.63 \|\|

*satriṇo vratinastāvat sadyaḥ śaucā udāhṛtāḥ \|*  
*rājā caivābhiṣiktaśca prāṇasatriṇa eva ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. A person who kills himself by burning his own body or kills himself with the consumption of poison, no impurity, cremation rites or the oblation of water has been prescribed for them.

## \|\| 2.23.64 \|\|

*yajñe vivāhakāle ca devayāge tathaiva ca \|*  
*sadyaḥ śaucaṃ samākhyātaṃ durbhikṣe cāpyupadrave \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. In case some one dies by through fire, poison etc. due to oversight, then impurity should be observed and water libation should be offered to him.

## \|\| 2.23.65-66 \|\|

*ḍimbāhavahatānāṃ ca vidyutā pārthivairdvijaiḥ \|*  
*sadyaḥ śaucaṃ samākhyātaṃ sarpādimaraṇe tathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*agnau maruprapatane vīrādhvanyapyanāśake \|*  
*brāhmaṇārthe ca saṃnyaste sadyaḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. At the time of the son-birth, during the time of impurity, one can receive following gifts viz. gold, costumes, cow, paddy, sesamum, cereals, jaggery and ghee in charity as per his own liking. Similarly, one can receive the fruits, flowers, vegetables, salt, firewood, buttermilk, curd, ghee, oil, medicines, milk and raw food items.

## \|\| 2.23.67 \|\|

*naiṣṭhikānāṃ vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ brahmacāriṇām \|*  
*nāśaucaṃ kīrtyate sadbhiḥ patite ca tathā mṛte \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The cremation of the Brahmana priest should be performed with three types of fire, and for others the cremation rites should be perfonned by means of the secualr fire as per the provision of the Grhyasiltras.

## \|\| 2.23.68 \|\|

*patitānāṃ na dāhaḥ syānnāntyeṣṭirnāsthisaṃcayaḥ \|*  
*na cāśrupātapiṇḍau vā kāryaṃ śrāddhādi kaṅkvacit \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. In case, one is unable to trace the dead body of a dead person, then his image should be made in Palasa leaves and twigs, the cremation should be performed with devotion by Sapinda relations.

## \|\| 2.23.69 \|\|

*vyāpādayet tathātmānaṃ svayaṃ yo 'gniviṣādibhiḥ \|*  
*vihitaṃ tasya nāśaucaṃ nāgnirnāpyudakādikam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. All the close relatives of such a person should recite his name and gotra, should exercise self- control and perform sraddha for ten days.

## \|\| 2.23.70 \|\|

*atha kaścit pramādena mriyate 'gniviṣādibhiḥ \|*  
*tasyāśaucaṃ vidhātavyaṃ kāryaṃ caivodakādikam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. They should daily perform the pindaddna to the dead man at the entrance to the house during the morning as well as in the evening. On the fourth day, the Brahmana should be served with the food.

## \|\| 2.23.71 \|\|

*jāte kumāre tadahaḥ kāmaṃ kuryāt pratigraham \|*  
*hiraṇyadhānyagovāsastilānnaguḍasarpiṣām \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. On the second day, the heads should be shaven by all the relatives and the bones should be collected on the fourth day. An even number of auspicious Brahmanas should be made to sit facing the east, and should be served food with devotion.

## \|\| 2.23.72 \|\|

*phalāni puṣpaṃ śākaṃ ca lavaṇaṃ kāṣṭhameva ca \|*  
*toyaṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ tailamauṣadhaṃ kṣīrameva ca \|*  
*āśaucināṃ gṛhād grāhyaṃ śuṣkānnaṃ caiva nityaśaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. An even number of Brahmanas should be fed on the fifth, ninth and the eleventh days after the death of a person. This is called the Nava- sraddha by the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.23.73 \|\|

*āhitāgniryathānyāyaṃ dagdhavyastribhiragnibhiḥ \|*  
*anāhitāgnirgṛhyeṇa laukikenetaro janaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The sraddha for the sake of departed soul should be performed on the ninth, eleventh, and twelfth days with great faith. During each one of the srdddha there should be one pavitra (ring of kus'a-grass), one arghya and one vessel for the pindas should be used.

## \|\| 2.23.74 \|\|

*dehābhāvāt palāśaistu kṛtvā pratikṛtiṃ punaḥ \|*  
*dāhaḥ kāryo yathānyāyaṃ sapiṇḍaiḥ śraddhayānvitaiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. In this way, in every month for a year, this srdddha should be performed on the day of the death. At the completion of a year after the death of a person, Sapindlkarana rite is performed.

## \|\| 2.23.75 \|\|

*sakṛtprasiñcantyudakaṃ nāmagotreṇa vāgyatāḥ \|*  
*daśāhaṃ bāndhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ sarve caivārdravāsasaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The Brahmanas should prepare four vases for the dead person, grandfather, great grandfather and the great-great grandfather. Thereafter, the water should be poured in the vessels of the Pitrs.

## \|\| 2.23.76 \|\|

*piṇḍaṃ pratidinaṃ dadyuḥ sāyaṃ prātaryathāvidhi \|*  
*pretāya ca gṛhadvāri caturthe bhojayed dvijān \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Reciting the mantras “Ye samana”, the pindas should be placed in the vases. The Deva- sraddha should be performed before the Sapindlkarana-sraddha.

## \|\| 2.23.77 \|\|

*dvitīye 'hani kartavyaṃ kṣurakarma sabāndhavaiḥ \|*  
*caturthe bāndhavaiḥ sarvairasthanāṃ saṃcayanaṃ bhavet \|*  
*pūrvaṃ tu bhojayed viprānayugmān śraddhayā śucīn \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Thereafter, the Pitrs shoud be invoked. Then he should point out the dead man. But the pretas for whom the Sapindlkarana had already been done, no other activity is required to be performed for them. In case anyone offers pindaddna to them separately, it amounts to the killing of his own Pitrs.

## \|\| 2.23.78 \|\|

*pañcame navame caiva tathaivaikādaśe 'hani \|*  
*ayugmān bhojayed viprān navaśrāddhaṃ tu tadviduḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. After the death of the father, the son should perform pindaddna for a year. The food should be offered with a pot filled with water everyday, with the rites of the dead.

## \|\| 2.23.79 \|\|

*ekādaśe 'hni kurvota pretamuddiśya bhāvataḥ \|*  
*dvādaśe vātha kartavyamanindye tvathavāhani \|*  
*ekaṃ pavitramekor'ghaḥ piṇḍapātraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The yearly srdddha is also performed like the Parvana-sraddha. This is ancient procedure.

## \|\| 2.23.80 \|\|

*evaṃ mṛtāhni kartavyaṃ pratimāsaṃ tu vatsaram \|*  
*sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ proktaṃ pūrṇe saṃvatsare punaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The son alone should perform all the sraddhas and pindaddna for the dead parents. In case there be no son, only then the wife herself should perform the sraddha. In the absence of the wife, the со-uterine brother can perform the smddha.

## \|\| 2.23.81 \|\|

*kuryāccatvāri pātrāṇi pretādīnāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*pretārthaṃ pitṛpātreṣu pātramāsecayet tataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. According to the aforesaid method, a living person, with the concentration of mind, should perform the sraddha with devotion and also give away other charities.

## \|\| 2.23.82 \|\|

*ye samānā iti dvābhyāṃ piṇḍānapyevameva hi \|*  
*sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ śrāddhaṃ devapūrvaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Thus, I have narrated the method of performing of the sraddha by a householder, in a proper manner. But for the women, no other dharma has been prescribed except to serve the husband.

## \|\| 2.23.83 \|\|

*pitṝnāvāhayet tatra punaḥ pretaṃ ca nirdiśet \|*  
*ye sapiṇḍīkṛtāḥ pretāna teṣāṃ syāt pṛthakkriyāḥ \|*  
*yastu kuryāt pṛthak piṇḍaṃ pitṛhā so 'bhijāyate \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Thus the one, who getting devoted to his dharma and also dedicates all the activities to Ishvara, he achieves the best of the place as is spelt out by the people of learnings.

## Chapter 24. Performance of homa by Dvijas

## \|\| 2.24.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*agnihotraṃ tu juhuyādādyante 'harniśoḥ sadā \|*  
*darśena caiva pakṣānte paurṇamāsena caiva hi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “Every Brahmana should perform Agnihotra rite (homa) daily in the morning as well as in the evening. At the end of the dark fortnight (the new moon day), this rite has to be performed days after the conclusion of a beneficial rite and on reaping the harvest afresh.

## \|\| 2.24.2 \|\|

*śasyānte navaśasyeṣṭyā tathartvante dvijo 'dhvaraiḥ \|*  
*paśunā tvayanasyānte samānte saumikairmakhaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A Brahmana should perform a homa (sacrifices) at the end of every season. At the end of a Ay ana, he should perform an animal sacrifice. At the end of the year, the soma- yajhas should be performed by the performer of the homa.

## \|\| 2.24.3 \|\|

*nāniṣṭvā navaśasyeṣṭyā paśunā vāgnimān dvijaḥ \|*  
*navānnamadyānmāṃsaṃ vā dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Agnihotrin Brahmana, desirous of long life, should not take cooked food or meat, without performing the yajna of fresh harvest and the animal sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.24.4 \|\|

*navenānnena cāniṣṭvā paśuhavyena cāganyaḥ \|*  
*prāṇānevāttumicchanti navānnāmiṣagṛddhinaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. An Agnihotrin Brahmana, who without performing the sacrifice with fresh grains or with animals as havyas (oblations), consumes the food or the meat, then the fires of yajna of the same Agnihotrin becomes desirous of taking out his life.

## \|\| 2.24.5 \|\|

*sāvitrān śāntihomāṃśca kuryāt parvasu nityaśaḥ \|*  
*pitṝṃścaivāṣṭakāsvarcan nityamanvaṣṭakāsu ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Agnihotrin should on each and every festive occasion, for the sake of the sun-god, perform homas and in the Astaka and Anvastaka days, he should worship the Pitrs.

## \|\| 2.24.6 \|\|

*eṣa dharmaḥ paro nityamapadharmo 'nya ucyate \|*  
*trayāṇāmiha varṇānāṃ gṛhasthāśramavāsinām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The aforesaid dharma is indeed the best and the rest is called apaddharma (unrighteous). This is the procedure meant for the three varnas including Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.24.7 \|\|

*nāstikyādathavālasyād yo 'gnīn nādhātumicchati \|*  
*yajeta vā na yajñena sa yāti narakān bahūn \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A person who due to his laziness or otherwise does not intend to perform homa or does not adore the gods by means of the yajhas, he has to fall in several hells.

## \|\| 2.24.8 \|\|

*(tāmistramandhatāmistraṃ mahārauravarauravau \|*  
*kumbhīpākaṃ vaitaraṇīmasipatravanaṃ tathā \|*  
*anyāṃśca narakān ghorān saṃprāpyānte sudurmatiḥ \|*  
*antyajānāṃ kule viprāḥ śūdrayonau ca jāyate )*  
*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena brāhmaṇo hi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ādhāyāgniṃ viśuddhātmā yajeta parameśvaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. (О Brahmanas, the evil minded person, falls in the terrific hells including Tamisra,Andhatamisra, Maharaurava, Kumbhlpaka,VaitaranI, Asipatravana, and other terrific hells and thereafter he is bom in the race of the Candalas or Sudras.) Therefore, a Brahmana, getting purified completely, should adore Paramesvara, invoking the fire.

## \|\| 2.24.9 \|\|

*agnihotrāt paro dharmo dvijānāṃ neha vidyate \|*  
*tasmādārādhayennityamagnihotreṇa śāśvatam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is no better dharma for the Brahmanas in this world than the Agnihotra, therefore, he should adore Ishvara always, performing the Agnihotra.

## \|\| 2.24.10 \|\|

*yaścādhāyāgnimālasyānna yaṣṭuṃ devamicchati \|*  
*so 'sau mūḍho na saṃbhāṣyaḥ kiṃ punarnāstiko janaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A person who himself being Agnihotrin, does not perform yajha out of lethargy, such an immensely foolish person is not fit to be conversed with, then what to speak about the atheist?

## \|\| 2.24.11 \|\|

*yasya traivārṣikaṃ bhaktaṃ paryāptaṃ bhṛtyavṛttaye \|*  
*adhikaṃ cāpi vidyeta sa somaṃ pātumarhati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A person who possesses the food for three years to feed his dependants, or more than that, only he is entitled to drink the Soma juice.

## \|\| 2.24.12 \|\|

*eṣa vai sarvayajñānāṃ somaḥ prathama iṣyate \|*  
*somenārādhayed devaṃ somalokamaheśvaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Soma sacrifice is considered to be the best of all the yajnas. With the performing of the yajha in Somaloka, one should propitiate lord Mahesvara of the Region of Soma.

## \|\| 2.24.13 \|\|

*na somayāgādadhiko maheśārādhane kratuḥ \|*  
*samo vā vidyate tasmāt somenābhyarcayet param \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For the worship of Mahesvara Shiva, there is no other yajna better than the Soma-yajna. Therefore, Parames'vara should be propitiatd by means of Soma sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.24.14 \|\|

*pitāmahena viprāṇāmādāvabhihitaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*dharmo vimuktaye sākṣācchrautaḥ smārto dvidhā punaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Lord Brahma, the Grand-sire, in earlier times, for the redemption of the Brahmanas, had specified the sacrificial animal and the dharma, conducive to salvation viz.: Srauta and Smarta.

## \|\| 2.24.15 \|\|

*śrautastretāgnisaṃbandhāt smārtaḥ pūrvaṃ mayoditaḥ \|*  
*śreyaskaratamaḥ śrautastasmācchrautaṃ samācaret \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Out of these two, the srauta-dharma has been related to three types of fires (viz.:- Daksindgni, Garhapatya and Ahavaniya), while the Smarta- dharma has already been described by me. Out of these two, the Srauta-dharma is more beneficial, which should be followed by all.

## \|\| 2.24.16 \|\|

*ubhāvabhihitau dharmau vedādeva viniḥ sṛtau \|*  
*śiṣṭācārastṛtīyaḥ syācchratismṛtyoralābhataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Both these dharmas emerge from the Vedas and are therefore quite beneficial. In the absence of srutis and smrtis, the Sistacara (conduct of the noble people) will be the third source of religion.

## \|\| 2.24.17 \|\|

*dharmeṇābhigato yaistu vedaḥ saparibṛṃhaṇaḥ \|*  
*te śiṣṭā brāhmaṇāḥ proktā nityamātmaguṇānvitāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Those having studied the Vedas and their supplementary works quite extensively, such Brahmanas possessing all the virtues endowed with the qualities of the Atman, are called Sistas (noble).

## \|\| 2.24.18 \|\|

*teṣāmabhimato yaḥ syāccetasā nityameva hi \|*  
*sa dharmaḥ kathitaḥ sadbhirnānyeṣāmiti dhāraṇā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The conduct of such people has also been termed as dharma, by the excellent people. The conduct of the other people (who are ungraceful) cannot be taken to be dharma. This is opinion of the scriptures.

## \|\| 2.24.19 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ dharmaśāstraṃ ca vedānāmupabṛṃhaṇam \|*  
*ekasmād brahmavijñānaṃ dharmajñānaṃ tathaikataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Puranas and the religious treatises represent the expansion of the Vedas. From one, the Brahman is realised, and from the other, dharma (rituals of religion) is realised.

## \|\| 2.24.20 \|\|

*dharmaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ tatpramāṇataraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇaṃ tad brahmajñāne parā pramā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Therefore, those, who are in search for dharma and those in search of Brahman, for them Puranas and Dharmasastras are indeed the best.

## \|\| 2.24.21 \|\|

*nānyato jāyate dharmo brahmavidyā ca vaidikī \|*  
*tasmād dharmaṃ purāṇaṃ ca śraddhātavyaṃ dvijātibhiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Apart from these two, there is no other way by which a person could achieve knowledge about dharma or the Vedic Brahmavidya. Therefore, the learned people should be devoted to Puranas and the Dharmas'astras.

## Chapter 25. Means of livelihood of a Brahmana

## \|\| 2.25.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*eṣa vo 'bhihitaḥ kṛtsno gṛhasthāśramavāsinaḥ \|*  
*dvijāteḥ paramo dharmo vartanāni nibodhata \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “Thus I have explained in details the Dharma of a Brahmana householder. Now all of you should listen to me about their means of livelihood, quite attentively.

## \|\| 2.25.2 \|\|

*dvividhastu gṛhī jñeyaḥ sādhakaścāpyasādhakaḥ \|*  
*adhyāpanaṃ yājanaṃ ca pūrvasyāhuḥ pratigraham \|*  
*kusīdakṛṣivāṇijyaṃ prakurvotāsvayaṅkṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The householders are of two types viz.: Sadhaka and Asadhaka. The means of the livelihood of first type of the householders include teaching, performing of the yajnas, and accepting charities. They can also engage themselves in earning of interest, farming, trading activities himself or through agents.

## \|\| 2.25.3 \|\|

*kṛṣerabhāvād vāṇijyaṃ tadabhāvāt kusīdakam \|*  
*āpatkalpo hyaṃ jñeyaḥ pūrvokto mukhya iṣyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the absence of cultivation, they can engage themselves into trade and in the absence of the same, they can take to earning of interest, which is permissible only during the time of calamity. The teaching, performing of yajnas and charities, indeed should be the main sources of livelihood.

## \|\| 2.25.4 \|\|

*svayaṃ vā karṣaṇaṃ kuryād vāṇijyaṃ vā kusīdakam \|*  
*kaṣṭā pāpīyasī vṛttiḥ kusīdaṃ tad vivarjayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The cultivation, trade or the earning of interest should be performed by a householder himself. Usury is quite sinful involving pain and strain, therefore one should avoid the same.

## \|\| 2.25.5 \|\|

*kṣātravṛttiṃ parāṃ prahurna svayaṃ karṣaṇaṃ dvijaiḥ \|*  
*tasmāt kṣātreṇa varteta vartanenāpadi dvijaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It would be better for the Brahmanas and the learned people to take to pursue the martial activity instead of resorting to the cultivation. A Brahmana can resort to the martial activity even when there is no emergency.

## \|\| 2.25.6 \|\|

*tena cāvāpyajīvaṃstu vaiśyavṛttiṃ kṛṣiṃ vrajet \|*  
*na kathañcana kurvota brāhmaṇaḥ karma karṣaṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In case a Brahmana is unable to take up the activities of a Ksatriya, then he can engage himself in the trading activities of the Vaisyas. But he should not resort to cultivation himself.

## \|\| 2.25.7 \|\|

*labdhalābhaḥ pitṝn devān brāhmaṇāṃścāpi pūjayet \|*  
*te tṛptāstasya taṃ doṣaṃ śamayanti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On gaining profit, one should adore the Pitrs, the gods, and the Brahmanas. There is no doubt that when pleased, all of them remove all the blemishes.

## \|\| 2.25.8 \|\|

*devebhyaśca pitṛbhyaśca dadyād bhāgaṃ tu viṃśakam \|*  
*triṃśadbhāgaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ kṛṣiṃ kurvan na duṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In case a twentieth of the produce is offered to the gods as well as the Pitrs, and by giving a one thirtieth of the same to the Brahmanas, no blemish is earned in cultivation.

## \|\| 2.25.9 \|\|

*vaṇik pradadyād dviguṇaṃ kusīdī triguṇaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣīvalo na doṣeṇa yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In comparison to the cultivation, the contribution in trade should be doubled, and in case of the earning of interest, it should be three times and by so doing one does not earn any blemish in the deal. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 2.25.10 \|\|

*śiloñchaṃ vāpyādadīta gṛhasthaḥ sādhakaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*vidyāśilpādayastvanye bahavo vṛttihetavaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A Sddhaka householder may also live on gleanings of corns or can also take up an irregular occupation, and for that purpose, there are many means of livelihood like, education, craftsmanship, etc.

## \|\| 2.25.11 \|\|

*asādhakastu yaḥ prokto gṛhasthāśramasaṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*śiloñche tasya kathite dve vṛttī paramarṣibhiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. For the Asddhaka householder, the Rishis have prescribed two means of livelihood, viz., the gleaning of corns and irregular occupations.

## \|\| 2.25.12 \|\|

*amṛtenāthavā jīvenmṛtenāpyathavā yadi \|*  
*ayācitaṃ syādamṛtaṃ mṛtaṃ bhekṣaṃ tu yācitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Or otherwise, the livelihood could be earned by means of Amrta or Mrta. In case one gets without begging, it is called Amrta and one that is received by begging is called Mrta (like dead).

## \|\| 2.25.13-14 \|\|

*kuśūladhānyako vā syāt kumbhīdhānyaka eva vā \|*  
*tryahaihiko vāpi bhavedaśvastanika eva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*caturṇāmapi caiteṣāṃ dvijānāṃ gṛhamedhinām \|*  
*śreyān paraḥ paro jñeyo dharmato lokajittamaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. There are four types of Asddhaka Brahmanas, viz., a person who carries on his livelihood with the collection of the cereals for three years, or the one who carries on his livelihood with the cereals collected by him for six days upto one year, or a person who can live for the three days with the food collected by him, and lastly the one who has the grain sufficient for the day but not for the morrow. Out of these, the later ones are better than the earlier ones among these Brahmana householders. By means of piety he conquers the worlds.

## \|\| 2.25.15 \|\|

*ṣaṭkarmaiko bhavatyeṣāṃ tribhiranyaḥ pravartate \|*  
*dvābhyāmekaścaturthastu brahmasatreṇa jīvati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The first type of Brahmana householders shall be Satkarman1. The second one shall perform three of them, the third, two of them and the fourth, one. He should maintain himself by study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.25.16 \|\|

*vartayaṃstu śiloñchābhyāmagnihotraparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*iṣṭīḥ pārvāyaṇāntīyāḥ kevalā nirvapet sadā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Those who earn their living by gleaning com and other such irregular professions, and are devoted to Agnihotra, then they can perform the ordinary sacrifices ending with these on the new moon and lull moon day.

## \|\| 2.25.17 \|\|

*na lokavṛtiṃ varteta vṛttihetoḥ kathañcana \|*  
*ajihmāmaśaṭhāṃ śuddhāṃ jīved brāhmaṇajīvikām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. One should not follow the local practices in earning livelihood. He should not pursue agriculture for livelihood. The means of livelihood which is free from cheating, the arrogance and wickedness, and is extremely auspicious, the same should be adopted by a householder Brahmana.

## \|\| 2.25.18 \|\|

*yācitvā vāpi sadbhyo 'nnaṃ pitṝndevāṃstu toṣayet \|*  
*yācayed vā śuciṃ dāntaṃ na tṛpyeta svayaṃ tataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. One should please the Pitrs by begging alms from a wealthy person, or he should beg of pure person with self-control. He should be himself satisfied thereby.

## \|\| 2.25.19 \|\|

*yastu dravyārjanaṃ kṛtvā gṛhasthastoṣayenna tu \|*  
*devān pitṛṃśca vidhinā śunāṃ yoniṃ vrajatyasau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A person who earning his livelihood does not please his own family members and the gods besides the Pitrs, he is reborn as a dog.

## \|\| 2.25.20 \|\|

*dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca śreyo mokṣaścatuṣṭayam \|*  
*dharmāviruddhaḥ kāmaḥ syād brāhmaṇānāṃ tu netaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. All the four, viz.: dharma, artha, kama and moksa are beneficial. One can create obstructions in dharma, but one should not act against dharma in any way.

## \|\| 2.25.21 \|\|

*yor'tho dharmāya nātmārthaḥ sor'tho 'narthastathetaraḥ \|*  
*tasmādarthaṃ samāsādya dadyād vai juhuyād yajet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The riches which are earned for the sake of dharma are the true riches. But the riches which are earned for the selfish purpose, they are of no use. Therefore, a Brahmana, should donate the same to a well eligible person and should perform the yajna.

## Chapter 26. Giving away of charities

## \|\| 2.26.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi dānadharmamanuttamam \|*  
*brahmaṇābhihitaṃ pūrvamṛṣīṇāṃ brahmavādinām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “Now I shall speak about the excellent dharma of the charities as had been extolled by Brahma to the sages, well-versed in Brahman.

## \|\| 2.26.2 \|\|

*arthānāmudite pātre śraddhayā pratipādanam \|*  
*dānamityabhinirdiṣṭaṃ bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When the riches are given to an appropriate person with faith, only then they are treated as Dana (charitable gift). These charities yields pleasures as well the moksa.

## \|\| 2.26.3 \|\|

*yad dadāti viśiṣṭebhyaḥ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ \|*  
*tad vai vittamahaṃ manye śeṣaṃ kasyāpi rakṣati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A person who gives away his riches in charities to a distinguished person with devotion, it is considered to be the true wealth. The rest of the riches are guarded by a person for the sake of others.

## \|\| 2.26.4 \|\|

*nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ trividhaṃ dānamucyate \|*  
*caturthaṃ vimalaṃ proktaṃ sarvadānottamottamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The charities are of three types, those which are given always, casual and those given with a definite aim. The fourth type of charities are considered to be the spotless one, which indeed is the best in comparison to all other charities.

## \|\| 2.26.5 \|\|

*ahanyahani yat kiñcid dīyate 'nupakāriṇe \|*  
*anuddiśya phalaṃ tasmād brāhmaṇāya tu nityakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When a donor, without the desire for a reward in return gives away charities to a Brahmana, who is unable to repay the kindness, it is called the nitya charity.

## \|\| 2.26.6 \|\|

*yat tu pāpopaśāntyarthaṃ dīyate viduṣāṃ kare \|*  
*naimittikaṃ taduddiṣṭaṃ dānaṃ sadbhiranuṣṭhitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The charities which are given in the hands of the learned persons, for the sake of self-control, it is called the naimittika charity, and it is practiced by the noble people.

## \|\| 2.26.7 \|\|

*apatyavijayaiśvaryasvargārthaṃ yat pradīyate \|*  
*dānaṃ tat kāmyamākhyātamṛṣibhirdharmacintakaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The charity which is performed for getting progeny, victory, fortunes, or the heaven, has been termed as kamyadana by the Rishis who have pondered over topics of piety.

## \|\| 2.26.8 \|\|

*yadīśvaraprīṇanārthaṃ brahmavitsu pradīyate \|*  
*cetasā dharmayuktena dānaṃ tad vimalaṃ śivam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The charity which is given to the Brahmanas, well-versed in the Brahman, for the propitiation of Is'vara, with a righteous mind, such a type of charity is known by the name of vimala or spotless one.

## \|\| 2.26.9 \|\|

*dānadharmaṃ niṣeveta pātramāsādya śaktitaḥ \|*  
*utpatsyate hi tatpātraṃ yat tārayati sarvataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The charities should be given according to one’s own means, on finding an appropriate person, because such an appropriate person can be found with difficulty, who could enable the donor to cross the entire ocean of worldly existence.

## \|\| 2.26.10 \|\|

*kuṭumbabhaktavasanād deyaṃ yadatiricyate \|*  
*anyathā dīyate yaddhi na tad dānaṃ phalapradam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. What remains after providing food, clothing etc. to the family should be given as charitable gift; because the charities given otherwise are of no consequence.

## \|\| 2.26.11 \|\|

*śrotriyāya kulīnāya vinītāya tapasvine \|*  
*vṛttasthāya daridrāya pradeyaṃ bhaktipūrvakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A person with due devotion should give away in charity riches to the Brahmanas, well-versed in the Vedas, who are of spotless race, humble, performers of tapas, Brahmacarins, and who maintains holy rites.

## \|\| 2.26.12 \|\|

*yastu dadyānmahīṃ bhaktyā brāhmaṇāyāhitāgnaye \|*  
*sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A person, who donates land to a Brahmana-the performer of homa, he reaches the supreme place, where one does not have to face any type of sufferings.

## \|\| 2.26.13 \|\|

*ikṣubhiḥ saṃtatāṃ bhumiṃ yavagodhūmaśalinīm \|*  
*dadāti vedaviduṣe yaḥ sa bhūyo na jāyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A person, who, donates the land with the crop of sugarcane, barley, or wheat, to a Brahmana, well-versed in the Vedas, he is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.26.14-15 \|\|

*gocarmamātrāmapi vā yo bhūmiṃ saṃprayacchati \|*  
*brāhmaṇāya daridrāya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhūmidānāt paraṃ dānaṃ vidyate neha kiñcana \|*  
*annadānaṃ tena tulyaṃ vidyādānaṃ tato 'dhikam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. A person who gives away land of the size of a cow hide, to a poor Brahmana, he is relieved of all the sins, because there is no charity better than the donation of the land. But donation of cooked food is also equivalent to the donation of land. And the gift of learning is most excellent.

## \|\| 2.26.16 \|\|

*yo brāhmaṇāya śāntāya śucaye dharmaśāline \|*  
*dadāti vidyāṃ vidhinā brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A person, who appropriately donates Vidya or learning to a religious-minded Brahmana of excellent character, he is adored in Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.26.17 \|\|

*dadyādaharahastvannaṃ śraddhayā brahmacāriṇe \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmaṇaḥ sthānamāpnuyāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A person who gives away in charity with devotion, the food to a Brahmacarin Brahmana, he, getting relieved of all the sins, proceeds on to Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.26.18 \|\|

*gṛhasthāyānnadānena phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*āmamevāsya dātavyaṃ dattvāpnoti parāṃ gatim \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A man obtains great benefit by giving cooked food to a Brahmana. It must be given to him immediately on his arrival. Thus, one obtains the greatest goal.

## \|\| 2.26.19-21 \|\|

*vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu brāhmaṇān sapta pañca vā \|*  
*upoṣya vidhinā śāntaḥ śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā tilaiḥ kṛṣṇairmadhunā na viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*gandhādibhiḥ samabhyarcya vācayed vā svyaṃ vadet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prīyatāṃ dharmarājeti yad vā manasi vartate \|*  
*yāvajjīvakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. On the full moon day of the month of Vaisakha, observing the fast, with a peaceful mind, performing purity, concentrating his mind, a person should adore five or seven Brahmanas offering honey and black sesamum. Then, he should perform their aratl offering fragrant material to them and should say, “You be pleased, О Dharmaraja”. After speaking these words, he should also speak out his desire to them or he can request the Brahmanas to speak it out. By so doing all the sins during the entire life are washed out.

## \|\| 2.26.22 \|\|

*kṛṣṇājine tilān kṛttvā hiraṇyaṃ madhusarpiṣī \|*  
*dadāti yastu viprāya sarvaṃ tarati duṣkṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A person, who placing the gold, honey, ghee, gingelly seeds, on the black antelope skin, and gives them in charity to a Brahmana, he is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.26.23 \|\|

*kṛtānnamudakumbhaṃ ca vaiśākhyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*nirdiśya dharmarājāya viprebhyo mucyate bhayāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. During the month of Vaisakha, in case the cooked food and a vase filled with water is given to a Brahmana, for the sake of Dharmaraja, a person is freed from fear.

## \|\| 2.26.24 \|\|

*suvarṇatilayuktaistu brāhmaṇān sapta pañca vā \|*  
*tarpayedudapātraistu brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A person is relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya. by giving away in charity gold, sesamum, and a vase filled with water, and propitiating five or seven Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.26.25 \|\|

*māghamāse tu viprastu dvādaśyāṃ samupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*śuklāmvaradharaḥ kṛṣṇaistilairhutvā hutāśanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. One should perform fast on twelfth dark day of the month of Magha, wearing the white clothes and should perform homa in fire with sesamum seeds. With great concentration, he should offer gifts to the Brahmanas, well-versed in the Vedas, and by so doing one is relieved of all the sins performed during the life.

## \|\| 2.26.26-27 \|\|

*pradadyād brāhmaṇebhyastu tilāneva samāhitaḥ \|*  
*janmaprabhṛti yatpāpaṃ sarvaṃ tarati vai dvijaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*amāvasyāmanuprāpya brāhmaṇāya tapasvine \|*  
*yatkicid devadeveśaṃ dadyāccoddiśya śaṅkaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. On the new moon day, whatever charities are given to a Brahmana, for the sake of lord Shiva saying, “Let lord Shiva with Uma, be pleased”, the sins committed by a person in the seven births are washed out, in a moment.

## \|\| 2.26.28 \|\|

*prīyatāmīśvaraḥ somo mahādevaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When a person on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, taking his bath, adores the Pinaka-bearing lord Shiva, and serves food to a Brahmana, he is freed from the cycle of rebirth.

## \|\| 2.26.29-30 \|\|

*yastu kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ snātvā devaṃ pinākinam \|*  
*ārādhayed dvijamukhe na tasyāsti punarbhavaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣeṇa dhārmikāya dvijātaye \|*  
*snātvābhyarcya yathānyāyaṃ pādaprakṣālanādibhiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. When a person, taking bath on the eighth day in the dark half of the month, washing the feet of the Brahmanas, adores them appropriately and says, “Let lord Shiva be pleased with me”, and then offers his own wealth in donation, he, getting relieved of all the sins, achieves the highest position.

## \|\| 2.26.31 \|\|

*prīyatāṃ me mahādevo dadyād dravyaṃ svakīyakam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. On the eighth and fourteenth days of the dark fortnight besides on the new moon day, the devoted Brahmanas should specially adore lord Shiva.

## \|\| 2.26.32 \|\|

*dvijaiḥ kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*amāvāsyāyāṃ bhaktaistu pūjanīyastrilocanaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Similarly, observing fast on the eleventh day, lord Visnu -the Purusottama should be adored through a Brahmana on the twelfth day. By so doing, one achieves the best position.

## \|\| 2.26.33 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāro dvādaśyāṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*arcayed bāhmaṇamukhe sa gacchet paramaṃ padam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The twelfth day of the bright fortnight happens to be the day belonging to Visnu. Therefore, on this particular day, lord Visnu should be adored making all the efforts.

## \|\| 2.26.34 \|\|

*eṣā tithirvaiṣṇavīṃ syād dvādaśī śuklapakṣake \|*  
*tasyāmārādhayed devaṃ prayatnena janārdanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus, by inviting lord Is'ana in any form and when a Brahmana is given charities in the name of lord Visnu, it becomes exceedingly

## \|\| 2.26.35 \|\|

*yatkiñcid devamīśānamuddiśya brāhmaṇe śucau \|*  
*dīyate viṣṇave vāpi tadanantaphalapradam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A person who intends to serve his own deity, such an intelligent person should adore the Brahmanas for the pleasure of that deity.

## \|\| 2.26.36 \|\|

*yo hi yāṃ devatāmicchet samārādhayituṃ naraḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇān pūjayed yatnāt satasyāṃ toṣayet tataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All the gods live in the bodies of the Brahmanas always. At times when the Brahmanas are not available then the images of the gods are worshipped.

## \|\| 2.26.37 \|\|

*dvijānāṃ vapurāsthāya nityaṃ tiṣṭhanti devatāḥ \|*  
*pūjyante brāhmaṇālābhe pratimādiṣvapi kvacit \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Therefore, the people desirous of quick reward, should adore the deities in Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.26.38 \|\|

*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena tat tat phalamabhīpsatā \|*  
*dvijeṣu devatā nityaṃ pūjanīyā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A person desirous of fortunes should always adore Indra, and the person desirous of Brahman, or the knowledge of the Vedas should adore Brahma.

## \|\| 2.26.39 \|\|

*vibhūtikāmaḥ satataṃ pūjayed vai purandaram \|*  
*brahmavarcasakāmastu brahmāṇaṃ brahmakāmukaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Similarly, the one who is desirous of good health, should adore Surya, one who is desirous of the cows, should adore Agni, and for the achieving of success in all the matters, one should adore Vinayaka.

## \|\| 2.26.40 \|\|

*ārogyakāmo 'tha raviṃ dhanakāmo hutāśanam \|*  
*karmaṇāṃ siddhikāmastu pūjayed vai vināyakam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One who is desirous of worldly pleasures, should adore the moon, one desirous of strength, should adore the wind-god and the one who is desirous of his salvation from the world, should adore lord Visnu, making all the efforts.

## \|\| 2.26.41 \|\|

*bhogakāmastu śaśinaṃ balakāmaḥ samīraṇam \|*  
*mumukṣuḥ sarvasaṃsārāt prayatnenārcayeddharim \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. But those who are desirous of Yoga, liberation, the divine knowledge ofls'vara, they should worship Vimpaksha-Mahesvara, making all the efforts.

## \|\| 2.26.42 \|\|

*yastu yogaṃ tathā mokṣamanvicchejjñānamaiśvaram \|*  
*sor'cayed vai virūpākṣaṃ prayatneneśvareśvaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Such of the people, who are interested in great Yoga and perfect knowledge, should adore lord Mahadeva. They shall become enjoyers of pleasures, they who worship Bhutesa and Kesava.

## \|\| 2.26.43 \|\|

*ye vāñchanti mahāyogān jñānāni ca maheśvaram \|*  
*te pūjayanti bhūteśaṃ keśavaṃ cāpi bhoginaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. By donating water freely, one achieves satisfaction; with the donation of cooked food, one gets everlasting happiness; by donation of sesamum, one gets desired progeny; and by donating lamp, one gets the best of eyesight.

## \|\| 2.26.44 \|\|

*vāridastṛptimāpnoti sukhamakṣayyamannadaḥ \|*  
*tilapradaḥ prajāmiṣṭāṃ dīpadaścakṣuruttamam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. A person who donates land, he gets everything; one gets long life by donating gold; by donating a house, one gets the best of abodes; and by donating silver, one achieves the excellent beauty.

## \|\| 2.26.45 \|\|

*bhūmidaḥ sarvamāpnoti dīrghamāyurhiraṇyadaḥ \|*  
*gṛhado 'gryāṇi veśmāni rūpyado rūpamuttamam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. By donating the costumes, one lives in the place of moon; by donating the horse, one attains the same world as that of the Asvins; by donating a bull one gets enonnous glory and riches, and by donating a cow, one achieves Bradhna (the world of sun).

## \|\| 2.26.46 \|\|

*vāsodaścandrasālokyamaśvisālokyamaśvadaḥ \|*  
*anaḍudaḥ śriyaṃ puṣṭāṃ godo vradhnasya viṣṭapam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. By donating a vehicle or a bed, one gets a beautiful wife. When a person offers relief from fear, he achievs enormous fortunes. By donating food grains, one achieves the everlasting comforts, and with the donation of the Vedas, one achieves union with Brahman.

## \|\| 2.26.47 \|\|

*yānaśayyāprado bhāryāmaiśvaryamabhayapradaḥ \|*  
*dhānyadaḥ śāśvataṃ saukhyaṃ brahmado brahmasātmyatām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. When a person, as per his own means donates food-grains to the Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas, he enjoys all the comforts in the heaven after his death.

## \|\| 2.26.48 \|\|

*dhānyānyapi yathāśakti vipreṣu pratipādayet \|*  
*vedavitsu viśiṣṭeṣu pretya svargaṃ samaśnute \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. With the donation of the cows, a person is relieved of all the sins. With the donation of fuel, a man becomes like a blazing fire.

## \|\| 2.26.49 \|\|

*gavāṃ ghāsapradānena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*indhanānāṃ pradānena dīptāgnirjāyate naraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A person who donates the fruits, roots, vegetables and several types of eatables to the Brahmanas, he achieves everlasting happiness.

## \|\| 2.26.50 \|\|

*phalamūlāni śākāni bhojyāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*pradadyād brāhmaṇebhyastu mudā yuktaḥ sadā bhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. A person, who gives away to the ailing person, the medicines, oil, and the food mixed with ghee, he becomes healthy, happy and enjoys long life.

## \|\| 2.26.51 \|\|

*auṣadhaṃ snehamāhāraṃ rogiṇe rogaśāntaye \|*  
*dadāno rogarahitaḥ sukhī dīrghāyureva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A person who donates an umbrella and the shoes, he easily crosses the Asipatravana hell full of sharp edges like a shawing blade, and surmounts severe scorching pain.

## \|\| 2.26.52 \|\|

*asipatravanaṃ mārgaṃ kṣuradhārāsamanvitam \|*  
*tīvritāpaṃ ca tarati chatropānatprado naraḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Whatever is dear in this world, or whatever is excessively cherished by one in the house, should be given to a Brahmana, by one who desires the same for himself to be inexhaustible,

## \|\| 2.26.53 \|\|

*yad yadiṣṭatamaṃ loke yaccāpi dayitaṃ gṛhe \|*  
*tattad guṇavate deyaṃ tadevākṣyamicchatā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The articles donated during the time of ayana, or when the day and night are equal, at the time of solar or lunar eclipse, or on the first day of the month, bestow everlasting reward.

## \|\| 2.26.54 \|\|

*apane viṣuve caiva grahaṇe candrasūryayoḥ \|*  
*saṃkrāntyādiṣu kāleṣu dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The charities given to a suitable person at Prayaga or other holy places, auspicious temple, over the bank of a river or a tank, bestow the everlasting reward.

## \|\| 2.26.55 \|\|

*prayāgādiṣu tīrtheṣu puṇyeṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*dattvā cākṣayamāpnoti nadīṣu ca vaneṣu ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. There is no other dharma in the world better than the giving of the charities. Therefore, the twice-boms should donate to the Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.26.56 \|\|

*dānadharmāt paro dharmo bhūtānāṃ neha vidyate \|*  
*tasmād viprāya dātavyaṃ śrotriyāya dvijātibhiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A person desirous of the heaven, long life, the destruction of the sins, fortunes and the one engaged in search of salvation, should perform charities for the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.26.57 \|\|

*svagāyurbhūtikāmena tathā pāpopaśāntaye \|*  
*mumukṣuṇā ca dātavyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyastathānvaham \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The one who prevents others from giving charities, to Brahmanas, the fire and the gods, out of delusion, such a sinful fellow, after his death is bom as an animal.

## \|\| 2.26.58 \|\|

*dīyamānaṃ tu yo mohād goviprāgnisureṣu ca \|*  
*nivārayati pāpātmā tiryagyoniṃ vrajet tu saḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. A person, who, after earning enough of riches, does not adore the gods or the Brahmanas, then the king should exile him, snatching away all his riches.

## \|\| 2.26.59 \|\|

*yastu dravyārjanaṃ kṛtvā nārcayed brāhmaṇān surān \|*  
*sarvasvamapahṛtyainaṃ rājā rāṣṭrāt pravāsayet \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A person who does not distribute the food etc. to the people starving due to the famine, such a Brahmana always earns denouncement.

## \|\| 2.26.60 \|\|

*yastu durbhikṣavelāyāmannādyaṃ na prayacchati \|*  
*mriyamāṇeṣu vipreṣu brāhmaṇaḥ sa tu garhitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The giving and taking of donations to such a person is prohibited. Such people should be driven out from the kingdom, after suitably stamping him.

## \|\| 2.26.61 \|\|

*na tasmāt pratigṛhṇīyurna viśeyuśca tena hi \|*  
*aṅkayitvā svakād rāṣṭrāt taṃ rājā vipravāsayet \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. A person who does not give charities to the noble persons, for the following of the dharma, he sl\\all be considered to be a great sinner and shall be cooked in the hell.

## \|\| 2.26.62-63 \|\|

*yastvasadbhyo dadātīha svadravyaṃ dharmasādhanam \|*  
*sa pūrvābhyadhikaḥ pāpī narake pacyate naraḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*svādhyāyavanto ye viprā vidyāvanto jitendriyāḥ \|*  
*satyasaṃyamasaṃyuktāstebhyo dadyād dvijottamāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. О Best of the Brahmanas, such of the Brahmanas who are engaged in the study of the Vedas, are learned ones, having controlled their senses, are truthful, righteous, and disciplined, the donations should be given to them alone. One should not feed a fool who has no good conduct even if he is starving for ten days.

## \|\| 2.26.64 \|\|

*subhuktamapi vidvāṃsaṃ dhārmikaṃ bhojayed dvijam \|*  
*na tu mūrkhamavṛttasthaṃ daśarātramupoṣitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. A person who leaving aside a Brahmana, well-versed in the Vedas, living closeby, gives charities to some one else, such a sinful fellow, by his misdeeds, reduces to ashes his seven generations.

## \|\| 2.26.65 \|\|

*sannikṛṣṭamatikramya śrotriyaṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*sa tena karmaṇā pāpī dahatyāsaptamaṃ kulam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. In case a Brahmana living at a distance excells in learning and virtues, then the charities can be given to the Brahmana living at a distance, in preference to the one living in the vicinity.

## \|\| 2.26.66 \|\|

*yadisyādadhiko vipraḥ śīlavidyādibhiḥ svayam \|*  
*tasmai yatnena dātavyaṃ atikramyāpi sannidhim \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Therefore one who receives the charities and one who gives the charities with due respect, both of them go to the heaven and in case things are otherwise, both of them achieve the hell.

## \|\| 2.26.67 \|\|

*yo 'rcitaṃ pratigṛhṇīyād dadyādarcitameva ca \|*  
*tāvubhau gacchataḥ svargaṃ narakaṃ tu viparyaye \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Therefore, for the person well-versed in the dharma, he should not extend the charities to an atheist, one who practices falsehood, one who indulges in arguments, wicked and one who is devoid of the knowledge of the Vedas. Even the water should not be given to such a person.

## \|\| 2.26.68 \|\|

*na vāryapi prayaccheta nāstike haituke 'pi ca \|*  
*pāṣaṇḍeṣu ca sarveṣu nāvedavidi dharmavit \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. In case an ignorant person, accepts the gifts of pies, gold, cow, horse, land, sesamum, then he is reduced to ashes like the log of wood.

## \|\| 2.26.69 \|\|

*apūpaṃ ca hiraṇyaṃ ca gāmaśvaṃ pṛthivīṃ tilān \|*  
*avidvān pratigṛhṇāno bhasmī bhavati kāṣṭhavat \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. An excellent Brahmana should expect charities only from high class praise-worthy Brahmanas or from all twice bom people, but charities should not be accepted from a Sudra.

## \|\| 2.26.70 \|\|

*dvijātibhyo dhanaṃ lipset praśastebhyo dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*api vā jātimātrebhyo na tu śūdrāt kathañcana \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Every Brahmana should try for dimunition of his expenditure for livelihood. He should never desire for the expansion of riches, because in greed for riches, he falls off from Brahmanahood.

## \|\| 2.26.71 \|\|

*vṛttisaṅkocamanvicchenneheta dhanavistaram \|*  
*dhanalobhe prasaktastu brāhmaṇyādeva hīyate \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. After studying all the Vedas, and after performing all the 11 yajhas, a person cannot attain that goal, which one attains by means of diminution.

## \|\| 2.26.72 \|\|

*vedānadhītya sakalān yajñāṃścāvāpya sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*na tāṃ gatimavāpnoti saṅkocād yāmavāpnuyāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. One should not be eager to receive donation. One should earn riches for carrying on his livelihood. A Brahmana, who amasses the wealth much more than his actual need, has to face his ultimate downfall.

## \|\| 2.26.73 \|\|

*pratigraharucirna syāt yātrārthaṃ tu samāharet \|*  
*sthityarthādadhikaṃ gṛhṇan brāhmaṇo yātyadhogatim \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. A person who perpetually begs, can never achieve the heaven. He actually annoys all other people like a thief.

## \|\| 2.26.74 \|\|

*yastu yācanako nityaṃ na sa svargasya bhājanam \|*  
*udvejayati bhūtāni yathā caurastathaiva saḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The charities are collected from the people of all the varnas for the uplifting of the preceptors, elders, servants, besides for worshipping deities and the guests. But one should not make use of the same for his selfish purpose.

## \|\| 2.26.75 \|\|

*gurūn bhṛtyāṃścojjihīrṣurarciṣyan devatātithīn \|*  
*sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna tu tṛpyet svayaṃ tataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Thus a householder, who adores the guests as well as the gods and leads his life absorbed in meditation, he achieves the highest position.

## \|\| 2.26.76 \|\|

*evaṃ gṛhastho yuktātmā devatātithipūjakaḥ \|*  
*vartamānaḥ saṃyātātmā yāti tat paramaṃ padam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Or otherwise leaving everything on the son, a person well-versed in the tattvas, retiring himself in the forest, becoming unattached, and concentrating his mind in spiritual activities, should wander alone.

## \|\| 2.26.77 \|\|

*putre nidhāya vā sarvaṃ gatvāraṇyaṃ tu tattvavit \|*  
*ekākī vicarennityamudāsīnaḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. О Best of the Dvijas, I have explained to you all about the duties of a householder. Understanding them well, you should strictly follow them and discourse to the other Brahmanas to follow the same,

## \|\| 2.26.78 \|\|

*eṣa vaḥ kathito dharmo gṛhasthānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*jñātvānutiṣṭhenniyataṃ tathānuṣṭhāpayed dvijān \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thus according to the duties of a householder, the one who adores the primordial lord Tsana, he overcoming the supreme Prakrti, the source of origin of all living beings, does not take another birth.

## Chapter 27. Duties of a Vanaprastha (or the third stage of the life)

## \|\| 2.27.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*evaṃ gṛhāśrame sthitvā dvitīyaṃ bhāgamāyuṣaḥ \|*  
*vānaprasthāśramaṃ gacchet sadāraḥ sāgnireva ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “Thus spending life as a householder in the second part of life, one should retire as Vanaprasthin, accompanied with his wife or alone but maintaining the sacrificial fires.

## \|\| 2.27.2 \|\|

*nikṣipya bhāryāṃ putreṣu gacched vanamathāpi vā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāpatyasya cāpatyaṃ jarjarīkṛtavigrahaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When the body becomes frail with old age, one should go to the forest after entrusting his wife to the care of the sons. After watching his progeny like the sons and grandsons, the old man should proceed to the forest.

## \|\| 2.27.3 \|\|

*śuklapakṣasya pūrvāhne praśaste cottarāyaṇe \|*  
*gatvāraṇyaṃ niyamavāṃstapaḥ kuryāt samāhitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the bright fortnight of Uttarayana (northern transit of the sun), on an auspicious morning, one should proceed to the forest, and with a disciplined mind perform the penances.

## \|\| 2.27.4 \|\|

*phalamūlāni pūtāni nityamāhāramāharet \|*  
*yatāhāro bhavet tena pūjayet pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He should collect the auspicious roots and fruits, for his consumption. In the first instance, the gods and the Pitrs should be adored with the fruits and roots.

## \|\| 2.27.5 \|\|

*pūjayitvātithiṃ nityaṃ snātvā cābhyarcayet surān \|*  
*gṛhādāhṛtya cāśnīyādaṣṭau grāsān samāhitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Taking his bath daily, one should serve the guests and the gods. Thereafter, getting food from the house, he should eat only eight morsels.

## \|\| 2.27.6 \|\|

*jaṭāśca bibhṛyānnityaṃ nakharomāṇi notsṛjet \|*  
*svādhyāyaṃ sarvadā kuryānniyacched vācamanyataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In the life as Vanaprasthin, one should wear the matterd hair over the head. He should not trim off the beard or the nails. He should study the Vedas and should remain silent on other occasions.

## \|\| 2.27.7 \|\|

*agnihotraṃ ca juhuyāt pañcayajñān samācaret \|*  
*munyannaiṃrvividhairmedhyaiḥ śākamūlaphalena vā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Не should perform the five great sacrifices and fire-worship in the morning as well as in the evening. The yajnas should be completed by him with the food received by him from the sages, and other fruits and roots collected from the forest.

## \|\| 2.27.8 \|\|

*cīravāsā bhavennityaṃ snāyāt triṣavaṇaṃ śuciḥ \|*  
*sarvabhūtānukampī syāt pratigrahavivarjitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He should always be clad in the bark garments and should remain clean, taking bath thrice a day. He should not accept monetary charities, and should be compassionate on all the living beings.

## \|\| 2.27.9 \|\|

*darśena paurṇamāsena yajet niyataṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*ṛkṣeṣvāgrayaṇe caiva cāturmāsyāni cāharet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Brahmana should regularly perform Darsaydga and the Paurnamasa-yaga (new moon and full moon days respectively) on the proper Naksatra, besides the yajha for new paddy and the Caturmasya-yajna.

## \|\| 2.27.10 \|\|

*uttarāyaṇaṃ ca kramaśo dakṣasyāyanameva ca \|*  
*vāsantaiḥ śāradairmedhyairmunyannaiḥ svayamāhṛtaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He should himself collect the cereals which are grown in the spring and winter seasons, and should appropriately perform the yajnas in Uttar ay ana and Daksinayana.

## \|\| 2.27.11 \|\|

*puroḍāśāṃścarūṃścaiva vidhivannirvapet pṛthak \|*  
*devatābhyaśca tad hutvā vanyaṃ medhyataraṃ haviḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Cooking both purodasa (sacrificial offerings of ground rice offered in earthen dishes) and caru (oblation of boiled rice and barley) with pure wild grains, he should offered the same to the gods, then he should consume them. In the food, he should use the salt prepared by himself.

## \|\| 2.27.12-13 \|\|

*śeṣaṃ samupabhuñjīta lavaṇaṃ ca svayaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*varjayenmadhumāṃsāni bhaumāni kavakāni ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhūstṛṇaṃ śigrukaṃ caiva śleṣmātakaphalāni ca \|*  
*na phālakṛṣṭamaśnīyādutsṛṣṭamapi kenacit \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. A Vanaprasthin should not consume honey, meat, mushrooms, grass emerging from the gound, and the citron should not be consumed. He should neither consume the cereals grown on earth after ploughing nor the left over of others.

## \|\| 2.27.14 \|\|

*na grāmajātānyārto 'pi puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca \|*  
*śrāvaṇenaiva vidhinā vahniṃ paricaret sadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Even when distressed, he should not consume the fruits or flowers grown in a village. He should maintain and venerate the holy fire as per injunctions in the Vaikhanasa Sutra.

## \|\| 2.27.15 \|\|

*na druhyet sarvabhūtāni nirdvandvo nirbhayo bhavet \|*  
*na naktaṃ kiñcidaśnīyād rātrau dhyānaparo bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He should never betray anyone. He should always remain free from attachment or jealousy and the fear as well. He should not eat during the night and should always engage himself in meditation.

## \|\| 2.27.16 \|\|

*jitendriyo jitakrodhastattvajñānavicintakaḥ \|*  
*brahmacārī bhavennityaṃ na patnīmapi saṃśrayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He should control his sense organs, as well as the anger, and should devote himself over tattva-jnana (perfect knowledge of Reality) and "perform the celibate vows and should not approach carnally even his wife.

## \|\| 2.27.17 \|\|

*yastu patnyā vanaṃ gatvā maithunaṃ kāmataścaret \|*  
*tad vrataṃ tasya lupyeta prāyaścittīyate dvijaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A person, who after retiring in the forest, has sex with his wife becoming passionate, his holy vow is shattered. Such a Brahmana should resort to repentence.

## \|\| 2.27.18 \|\|

*tatra yo jāyate garbho na saṃspṛśyo dvijātibhiḥ \|*  
*na hi vede 'dhikāro 'sya tadvaṃśepyevameva hi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When a child is bom during the observing of the Vanaprastha asrama, then the Brahmana should not touch the child. Such a child as well as the people of his family shall not be entitled to the study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.27.19 \|\|

*adhaḥ śayīta satataṃ sāvitrījāpyatatparaḥ \|*  
*śaraṇyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃvibhāgaparaḥ sadā \|\| 19 \|\|*
