19\. He should always sleep on the ground and should always recite the Gayatrl-mantra. He should always try to provide refuge to all the living beings. The guests should always be given their share of food.

## \|\| 2.27.20 \|\|

*parivādaṃ mṛṣāvādaṃ nidrālasyaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*ekāgniraniketaḥ syāt prokṣitāṃ bhūmimāśrayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He should not pick controversy with anyone, nor should he denounce others. He should not speak falsehood and should also discard sleep and lethargy. He should maintain one single fire, should have no fixed abode, and should resort to a ground purified by sprinkling water.

## \|\| 2.27.21 \|\|

*mṛgaiḥ saha cared vāsaṃ taiḥ sahaiva ca saṃvaset \|*  
*śilāyāṃ śarkarāyāṃ vā śayīta susamāhitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He should roam about in the forest freely alongwith the deer and should sleep with great concentration on a slab of stone or on the gravels.

## \|\| 2.27.22 \|\|

*sadyaḥ prakṣālako vā syānmāsasaṃcayiko 'pi vā \|*  
*ṣaṇmāsanicayo vā syāt samānicaya eva vā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The costumes should be worn washing at once. One should collect fruit etc. which could last with him for a month or otherwise the food grains of wild rice could be stored for six months or a year.

## \|\| 2.27.23 \|\|

*tyajedāśvayuje māsi saṃpannaṃ pūrvasaṃcitam \|*  
*jīrṇāni caiva vāsāṃsi śākamūlaphalāni ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In the month of Asvayuja (september- october), the left overs of the earlier stock of food, the old worn clothes, besides the vegetables, roots etc. should be discarded.

## \|\| 2.27.24 \|\|

*dantolūkhaliko vāsyāt kāpotīṃ vṛttimāśrayet \|*  
*aśmakuṭṭo bhaved vāpi kālapakvabhugeva vā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The food grains should be taken by chewing them with the teeth. One should not eat the grains picking up like a pigeon, or otherwise food should be taken by powdering it with stones. The ripe or cooked food should be taken timely.

## \|\| 2.27.25 \|\|

*naktaṃ cānna samaśnīyād divā cāhṛtya śaktitaḥ \|*  
*caturthakāliko vā syāt syādvāpyaṣṭamakālikaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Collecting the cereals etc. during the day, one should take food in the night, according to one’s own capacity. Or otherwise fasting for a day, the food should be taken at night of the next day, or after fasting for three days, one should take food on the night of the fourth day.

## \|\| 2.27.26 \|\|

*cāndrāyaṇavidhānairvā śukle kṛṣṇe ca vartayet \|*  
*pakṣe pakṣe samaśnīyād yavāgūṃ kvathitāṃ sakṛt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. According to the practice followed for the performing of the Candrayana vrata in the dark as well as in the bright fortnight, one should perform the expiatory rites accordingly, or he should take once in a fortnight boiled rice or barley gruel.

## \|\| 2.27.27 \|\|

*puṣpamūlaphalairvāpi kevalairvartayet sadā \|*  
*svābhāvikaiḥ svayaṃ śīrṇairvaikhānasamate sthitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Or following the doctrine of Vaikhanasas, merely flowers, roots or fruits which has naturally fallen and withered, should be consumed.

## \|\| 2.27.28 \|\|

*bhūmau vā parivarteta tiṣṭhed vā prapadairdinam \|*  
*sthānāsanābhyāṃ viharenna kvacid dhairyamutsṛjet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One should spend the day rolling on the ground or standing on toes on the ground. He should continuously stand for a while and then sit down for a while. He should not lose patience at any time.

## \|\| 2.27.29 \|\|

*grīṣme pañcatapāśca syād varṣāsvabhrāvakāśakaḥ \|*  
*ārdravāsāstu hemante kramaśo vardhayaṃstapaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Gradually increasing his intensity in austere penance, he should face the five types of fire, and during the rainy season, he should stand in the open sky, and in the winter season, should put on wet clothes.

## \|\| 2.27.30 \|\|

*upaspṛśya triṣavaṇaṃ pitṛdevāṃśca tarpayet \|*  
*ekapādena tiṣṭheta marīcīn vā pibet tadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He should take bath thrice a day, oblation should be offered to the manes as well as the gods. He should stand on one foot facing the sun rays.

## \|\| 2.27.31 \|\|

*pañcāgnirdhūmapo vā syāduṣmapaḥ somapo 'pi vā \|*  
*payaḥ pibecchuklapakṣe kṛṣṇāpakṣe tu gomayam \|*  
*śīrṇaparṇāśano vā syāt kṛcchrair vā vartayet sadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. While facing the five types of fires, the hot smoke should be inhaled. One should be an imbiber of heat or Soma juice. One should consume milk in the bright fortnight and the Pancagavya (cowdung, urine etc.) in the dark half of the month.

## \|\| 2.27.32 \|\|

*yogābhyāsarataśca syād rudrādhyāyī bhavet sadā \|*  
*atharvaśiraso 'dhyetā vedāntābhyāsatatparaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Consuming the dry leaves which are fallen from the trees, one should perform the Krcchra penance, resort to yogic practices, and recite the Rudra-sUkta.

## \|\| 2.27.33 \|\|

*yamān seveta satataṃ niyamāṃścāpyatandritaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇājinī sottarīyaḥ śuklayajñopavītavān \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He should study Atharvasiras, practicing the principles of Vedanta at the same time. Resorting to Yamas (restraints) continuously, one should follow all Niyamas (observances and rites).

## \|\| 2.27.34-35 \|\|

*atha cāgnīn samāropya svātmani dhyānatatparaḥ \|*  
*anagniraniketaḥ syānmunirmokṣaparo bhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tāpaseṣveva vipreṣu yātrikaṃ bhaikṣamāharet \|*  
*gṛhamedhiṣu cānyeṣu dvijeṣu vanavāsiṣu \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. One should wear an upper garment of black deer skin, and a yajnopavlta. At the end, establishing the fire in the soul one should be engaged in meditation. Thus, he should be devoid of fire (i.e. give up fire-worship etc.) and a fixed abode; he should be a silent sage engaged in endeavour for salvation. He should take alms necessary.for his journey from saintly Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.27.36 \|\|

*grāmādāhṛtya vāśnīyādaṣṭau grāsān vane vasan \|*  
*pratigṛhya puṭenaiva pāṇinā śakalena vā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. For the livelihood, one should seek alms from the other Brahmana houselholders residing in the forest. Himself residing in the forest, he should eat eight mouthfuls of what he brings from the village.

## \|\| 2.27.37 \|\|

*vividhāścopaniṣada ātmasaṃsiddhaye japet \|*  
*vidyāviśeṣān sāvitrīṃ rudrādhyāyaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In a vase of leaves or holding the palms like a cup or on a potsherd, he should receive bhiksa. For the realisation of Atman, he should perform Japa of different Upanisads, different Mantras, Gayatrl-mantra or Rudradhyaya.

## \|\| 2.27.38 \|\|

*mahāprāsthānikaṃ cāsau kuryādanaśanaṃ tu vā \|*  
*agnipraveśamanyad vā brarhmārpaṇavidhau sthitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. At the end, the body should be placed in dedication to the lord, one should resort to fasting unto death or abide by the procedure of dedication unto the Brahman, and may enter fire.

## \|\| 2.27.39 \|\|

*yastu samyagimamāśramaṃ śivaṃ*  
*saṃśrayedaśivapuñjanāśanam \|*  
*tāpasaḥ sa paramaiśvaraṃ padaṃ*  
*yāti yatra jagato 'sya saṃsthitiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Such of the people, when living in the Vdnaprastha cisrama that destroys unholy things, take refuge with lord, they are lodged in the heaven enjoying the place of Is'vara-Shiva.

## Chapter 28. Duties of Recluse

## \|\| 2.28.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*evaṃ vanāśrame sthitvā tṛtīyaṃ bhāgamāyuṣaḥ \|*  
*caturthamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ saṃnyāsena nayet kramāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “By staying in the stage of life as the forest-hermit during the third period of his life, thus, he should spend the fourth period of his life as Sannydsi (by renunciation).

## \|\| 2.28.2 \|\|

*agnīnātmanī saṃsthāpya dvijaḥ pravrajito bhavet \|*  
*yogābhyāsarataḥ śānto brahmavidyāparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A Brahmana, well-versed in the Brahmavidya, engaged in the practice of yogic exercises, with a peaceflil mind should establish his soul in the fire and then embrace the renunciation.

## \|\| 2.28.3 \|\|

*yadā manasi saṃjātaṃ vaitṛṣṇyaṃ sarvavastuṣu \|*  
*tadā saṃnyāsamicchecca patitaḥ syād viparyaye \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When the mind is no more attracted towards the worldly affairs, only then sannydsa should be embraced. In case it be otherwise, one has to fall from the same.

## \|\| 2.28.4 \|\|

*prājāpatyāṃ nirūpyeṣṭimāgneyīmathavā punaḥ \|*  
*dāntaḥ pakvakaṣāyo 'sau brahmāśramamupāśrayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. First of all, the control should be exercised on the sense organs, the Prajapatya or the Agneya yajna should be performed. Then getting free from attraction, jealousy and blemishes, one should enter the Sannyasa-dsrama.

## \|\| 2.28.5 \|\|

*jñānasaṃnyāsinaḥ kecid vedasaṃnyāsinaḥ pare \|*  
*karmasaṃnyāsinastvanye trividhāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Sannyasins are said to be of three types, viz.: Jnana-Sannyasins, Karma-Sannyasins, and Veda-Sannyasins.

## \|\| 2.28.6 \|\|

*yaḥ sarvasaṅganirmukto nirdvandvaścaiva nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*procyate jñānasaṃnyāsī svātmanyeva vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The one who is not interested in anyone of the worldly affairs, is free from all the controversies, free of fear, and is devoted to the search of the soul, he is said to be a Jnana- Sannyasin.

## \|\| 2.28.7 \|\|

*vedamevābhyasennityaṃ nirāśī niṣparigrahaḥ \|*  
*procyate vedasaṃnyāsī mumukṣurvijitendriyaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The one who is free from the controversies or the receiving of the charities, is engaged in the study of the Vedas, is desirous of liberation, and has exercised control over the sense organs, he is called a Veda-Sannyasin.

## \|\| 2.28.8 \|\|

*yastvagnīnātmasātkṛtvā brahmārpaṇaparo dvijaḥ \|*  
*jñeyaḥ sa karmasaṃnyāsī mahāyajñaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A Brahmana, who facing all the types of fires, dedicate everything to Brahman, such a person who is well versed in the Mahd-yajnas, is known as Karma-Sannyasin.

## \|\| 2.28.9 \|\|

*trayāṇāmapi caiteṣāṃ jñānī tvabhyadhiko mataḥ \|*  
*na tasya vidyate kāryaṃ na liṅgaṃ vā vipaścitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Jnana-Sannyasin out of the aforesaid three catagories of the Sannydsin are considered to be the best. He is a scholar who has no function to be performed nor has he any symbol.

## \|\| 2.28.10 \|\|

*nirmamo nirbhayaḥ śānto nirdvandvaḥ parṇabhojanaḥ \|*  
*jīrṇakaupīnavāsāḥ syānnagno vā dhyānatatparaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Such Sannyasins are free from attachment, fearless, peaceful, free from controversies or charities, wear the kaupin (ragged loin cloth), or even remain without robes, and are engaged in meditation.

## \|\| 2.28.11 \|\|

*brahmacārī mitāhāro grāmādannaṃ samāharet \|*  
*adhyātmamatirāsīta nirapekṣo nirāmiṣaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He should be a Brahmacarin, should take limited food, and should collect cereals from the village. He should be devoted to Brahman, unattached, and should not allow any desire to develop in his mind. Nor does he take meat.

## \|\| 2.28.12 \|\|

*ātmanaiva sahāyena sukhārthaṃ vicarediha \|*  
*nābhinandeta maraṇaṃ nābhinandeta jīvitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. With the help of one’s own soul in this world, remaining desirous of moksa, a Sannydsin should wander here and there. He should neither be happy with the birth, nor with the death.

## \|\| 2.28.13 \|\|

*kālameva pratīkṣeta nideśaṃ bhṛtako yathā \|*  
*nādhyetavyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ śrotavyaṃ na kadācana \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. As a servant waits for the command of his master, similarly he should wait for the kala or the death. He has never anything worth studying or learning. He thus qualifies himself to be identical with Brahman.

## \|\| 2.28.14-15 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā paro yogī brahmabhūyāya kalpate \|*  
*ekavāsāthavā vidvān kaupīnācchādanastathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*muṇḍī śikhī vātha bhavet tridaṇḍī niṣparigrahaḥ \|*  
*kāṣāyavāsāḥ satataṃ dhyānayogaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. A learned Sannyasin, should remain alone, wearing one cloth or a kaupln. He should have either his head shaved or a tuft of hair on the head. Disowning the house, he should hold three staffs. He should be free from acceptance of gifts.

## \|\| 2.28.16 \|\|

*grāmānte vṛkṣamūle vā vased devālaye 'pi vā \|*  
*samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He should wear the ochre-robes, should spend time seated under a tree outside the village, and should engage himself in meditation, or be engaged in yogic practices. He should treat the enemy as the friend and the grace or disgrace, equally.

## \|\| 2.28.17 \|\|

*bhaikṣyeṇa vartayennityaṃ naikānnādī bhavet kvacit \|*  
*yastu mohena vālasyādekānnādī bhaved yatiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He should maintain himself on alms. A Sannyasin, who out of attachment or otherwise consumes food, daily by receiving it from one person alone, then the sin attracted by him (cannot be removed) and no repentence is prescribed for the same in the Dharmasastras.

## \|\| 2.28.18-19 \|\|

*na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ kācid dharmaśāstreṣu kathyate \|*  
*rāgadveṣavimuktātmā samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*prāṇihaṃsānivṛttaśca maunī syāt sarvanispṛhaḥ \|*  
*haṣipūṃ nyasetpādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pivet \|*  
*satyapūtāṃ vaded vāṇīṃ manaḥ pūtaṃ samācaret \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. A Sannyasin should remain unconcerned with attachment or envy. He should treat a piece of gold, a lump of clay, or a piece of stone alike. He should detract himself from the killing of animals and from passions, and he should keep silence. He should place his foot on the road, observing it carefully. The water should be drunk after filtering it by a cloth. He should speak the words purified with the use of the scriptures. He should indulge in the activities which purify the mind.

## \|\| 2.28.20 \|\|

*naikatra nivased deśe varṣābhyo 'nyatra bhikṣukaḥ \|*  
*snānaśaucarato nityaṃ kamaṇḍalukaraḥ śuciḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Except for the rainy season, a Bhiksu should not stay for long at one place. He should carry a kamandalu (waterpot) alone, and should observe purity, taking bath.

## \|\| 2.28.21-22 \|\|

*brahmacaryarato nityaṃ vanavāsarato bhavet \|*  
*mokṣaśāstreṣu nirato brahmasūtrī jitendriyaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dambhāhaṅkāranirmukto nindāpaiśunyavarjitaḥ \|*  
*ātmajñānaguṇopeto yatirmokṣamavāpnuyāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. He should always remain a Brahmacarin, dwelling in the forest. He should be engaged in the study of the literature for liberation, control his sense organs, free from deceitfulness, arrogance, denounce-ment of others and wickedness. He should possess the virtues of self-consciousness. Such a Sannyasin surely achieves moksa.

## \|\| 2.28.23 \|\|

*abhyaset satataṃ vedaṃ praṇavākhyaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*snātvācamya vidhānena śucirdevālayādiṣu \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Performing the bath and acamana appropriately, purifying himself, he should always recite the Pranava mantra (Om) in a temple or any other auspicious place.

## \|\| 2.28.24-25 \|\|

*yajñopavītī śāntātmā kuśapāṇiḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*dhautakāṣāyavasano bhasmacchannatanūrahaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*adhiyajñaṃ brahma japedādhidaivikameva ca \|*  
*ādhyātmikaṃ ca satataṃ vedāntābhihitaṃ ca yat \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Wearing the sacred thread, holding kusa grass in hand, keeping the soul peaceful, wearing the washed ochre-coloured garment, and covering all the hair on the body with the ashes, concentrating his mind, he should recite the Japa of Brahman (Veda) pertaining to Yajna, or connected with the gods and related to the Vedanta.

## \|\| 2.28.26 \|\|

*putreṣu vātha nivasan brahmacārī yatirmuniḥ \|*  
*vedamevābhyasennityaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A Sannyasin who has taken the vow of silence and celibacy may stay with his sons also; when recites the Vedic hymns living in a leaf- hut, he achieves the best position.

## \|\| 2.28.27 \|\|

*ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ tapaḥ param \|*  
*kṣamā dayā ca satoṣo vratānyasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It is the duty of a Sannyasin to follows the vows of ahimsa (non-voilence) truthfulness, not to steal, celibacy, greatest penance, forgiveness, mercifulness, and satisfaction.

## \|\| 2.28.28 \|\|

*vedāntajñānaniṣṭho vā pañca yajñān samāhitaḥ \|*  
*kuryādaharahaḥ snātvā bhikṣānnenaiva tena hi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A Sannyasin should be well-versed in Vedanta, and he should daily perform the Panca-mahayajnas with concentrated mind after receiving food by begging and equipped with knowledge and meditation.

## \|\| 2.28.29 \|\|

*homamantrāñjapennityaṃ kāle kāle samāhitaḥ \|*  
*svādhyāyaṃ cānvahaṃ kuryāt sāvitrīṃ saṃdhyayorjapet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. With a concentrated mind, he should perform the japa of Нота thrice in a day. All the Vedas should be studied daily and the Gayatrl-mantra should be recited in the morning as well as in the evening.

## \|\| 2.28.30 \|\|

*dhyāyīta satataṃ devamekānte parameśvaram \|*  
*ekānnaṃ varjayennityaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then, he should meditate upon the Lord Parames'vara in a secluded place. The desire, anger and gifts should be discarded by him completely.

## \|\| 2.28.31 \|\|

*ekavāsā dvivāsā vā śikhī yajñopavītavān \|*  
*kamaṇḍalukaro vidvān tridaṇḍī yāti tatparam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He should be clad in one or two costumes, wear the sacred thread and hold kamandalu as well as tridanda (three staffs). Such a Sannyasin attains the greatest Being.

## Chapter 29. Duties of an ascetic

## \|\| 2.29.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*evaṃ svāśramaniṣṭhānāṃ yatīnāṃ niyatātmanām \|*  
*bhaikṣeṇa vartanaṃ proktaṃ phalamūlairathāpi vā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “In this way the ascetics are said to spend their life by remaining truthful to their asrama, concentrating their mind, depending on the food received by them by begging or the forest fruits and roots.

## \|\| 2.29.2 \|\|

*ekakālaṃ cared bhaikṣaṃ na prasajyeta vistare \|*  
*bhaikṣe prasakto hi yatirviṣayeṣvapi sajjati \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Even for bhiksa, a Sannyasin should visit a householder once only. He should not go to many people for begging of alms, because when one gets more attracted towards a person, he develops more desires for worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 2.29.3-4 \|\|

*saptāgāraṃ cared bhaikṣamalābhāt tu punaścaret \|*  
*prakṣālya pātre bhuñjīyādadbhiḥ prakṣālayet tu tat \|\| 3 \|\|*

*athavānyadupādāya pātre bhuñjīta nityaśaḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā tat saṃtyajet pātraṃ yātrāmātramalolupaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. One should beg alms from seven houses only and while so doing if one is unable to receive the alms, then once again the bhiksa, can be begged. Washing the vase, one should take food in it, and after finishing food, it should again be washed out or food should be taken in a new vase. But in case one has to manage by washing the vase there, the food should be taken without greed.

## \|\| 2.29.5 \|\|

*vidhūme sannamusale vyaṅgāre bhuktavajjane \|*  
*vṛtte śarāvasaṃpāte bhikṣāṃ nityaṃ yatiścaret \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The ascetic should go to collect alms when there is no smoke or burning coal, at a house where all the people have taken food and where the threshing rod is kept resting and the potsherds are disposed off.

## \|\| 2.29.6 \|\|

*godohamātraṃ tiṣṭheta kālaṃ bhikṣuradhomukhaḥ \|*  
*bhikṣetyuktvā sakṛt tūṣṇīmaśnīyād vāgyataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Sannyasin should utter the words “Bhiksa” and then he should wait upto the time of milking of a cow, lowering his head, keeping silent. Then he should feel satisfied by taking the food once only.

## \|\| 2.29.7 \|\|

*prakṣālya pāṇipādau ca samācamya yathāvidhi \|*  
*āditye darśayitvānnaṃ bhuñjīta prāṅmukhottaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Washing both his hands and feet, performing sipping appropriately, displaying the food to the sun-god, purifying himself facing east, one should take his food.

## \|\| 2.29.8 \|\|

*hutvā prāṇāhutīḥ pañca grāsānaṣṭau samāhitaḥ \|*  
*ācamya devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ dhyāyīta parameśvaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He should utter the Mantra initially, “Pranaya svahd", the five offerings should then be made with a concentrated mind. Then he should eat eight mouthfuls of food and thereafter perform the sipping. The omniscient Parames'vara should be adored then.

## \|\| 2.29.9 \|\|

*alābuṃ dārupātraṃ ca mṛṇmayaṃ vaiṇavaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*catvāri yatipātrāṇi manurāha prajāpatiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The use of four types of vases made of gourd, wood, earthern and the bamboo, have been prescribed by the Prajapati-Manu.

## \|\| 2.29.10 \|\|

*prāgrātre pararātre ca madhyarātre tathaiva ca \|*  
*saṃdhyāsvahni viśeṣeṇa cintayennityamīśvaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. During the starting, middle and the concluding period of the night and at the time of sandhya, one should get devoted to Is'vara. During sandhya, he should particularly make use of sacrificial fires.

## \|\| 2.29.11-12 \|\|

*kṛtvā hṛtpadmanilaye viśvākhyaṃ viśvasaṃbhavam \|*  
*ātmānaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ parastāt tamasaḥ sthitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sarvasyādhārabhūtānāmānandaṃ jyotiravyayam \|*  
*pradhānapuruṣātītamākāśaṃ dahanaṃ śivam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. One should meditate upon the lotus-like lord in his heart, who is the form of universe, but still the cause of the world, the one who is the soul of all, is beyond darkness, who is the support of all the living beings, invisible, blissful, indestructible, beyond Pradhana and Purusa, Shiva stationed in the cavity of the sky, and the flame of welfare.

## \|\| 2.29.13-14 \|\|

*tadantaḥ sarvabhāvānāmīśvaraṃ brahmarūpiṇam \|*  
*dhyāyedanādimadvaitamānandādiguṇālayam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mahāntaṃ paramaṃ brahma puruṣaṃ satyamavyayam \|*  
*sitetarāruṇākāraṃ maheśaṃ viśvarūpiṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Then one should meditate upon lord Mahes'a, the form of the universe, who is lokesvara and seed of the flame, form of Brahman, beyond the beginning, middle or the end, the abode of bliss, the excellent Purusa, the indestructible one, the form of truth, omniscient, the supreme Brahman and resembling the mid-day sun.

## \|\| 2.29.15 \|\|

*oṅkārānte 'tha cātmānaṃ saṃsthāpya paramātmani \|*  
*ākāśe devamīśānaṃ dhyāyītākāśamadhyagam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Lord Isana or Shiva, should be meditated upon, by establishing the soul in Paramatma, present in the middle of the sky, through Omkara.

## \|\| 2.29.16 \|\|

*kāraṇaṃ sarvabhāvānāmānandaikasamāśrayam \|*  
*purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ śaṃbhuṃ dhyāyan mucyeta bandhanāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By meditating upon the ancient pure Purusa, who is the cause of all the beings, and is all blissful, one gets relieved of all the bondages.

## \|\| 2.29.17-19 \|\|

*yadvā guhāyāṃ prakṛtau jagatsaṃmohanālaye \|*  
*vicintya paramaṃ vyoma sarvabhūtaikakāraṇam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jīvanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ yatra lokaḥ pralīyate \|*  
*ānandaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sūkṣmaṃ yat paśyanti mumukṣavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tanmadhye nihitaṃ brahma kevalaṃ jñānalakṣaṇam \|*  
*anantaṃ satyamīśānaṃ vicintyāsīta saṃyataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Or otherwise, one should ponder over the great firmament, the delusion in the world, the form of Mula-prakrti, the sole cause of all the living beings, their life and movement, the form of blissful Brahman, where the world gets dissolved, and to whom those desirous of moksa visualise in him the sutble form of Brahman, such a lord should be meditated upon as the form of perfect knowledge, endless, real, truthful, lord of all, and the supreme Brahman, with a devoted mind.

## \|\| 2.29.20 \|\|

*guhyād guhyatamaṃ jñānaṃ yatīnāmetadīritam \|*  
*yo 'nutiṣṭhenmaheśena so 'śnute yogamaiśvaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I have revealed the secrets of the Sannyasin imparted to ascetics by lord Mahesa. The one who will follow the same, he will achieve the fortunes and Yoga pertaining to Ishvara.

## \|\| 2.29.21 \|\|

*tasmād dhyānarato nityamātmavidyāparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ samabhyased brāhmaṃ yena mucyeta bandhanāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Therefore concentrating one’s mind, getting devoted to self knowledge, one should take refuge in Brahmajhana and by so doing a person is freed from all the bondages.

## \|\| 2.29.22 \|\|

*matvā pṛthak svamātmānaṃ sarvasmādeva kevalam \|*  
*ānandamajaraṃ jñānaṃ dhyāyīta ca punaḥ param \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Treating the soul of the self to be separate from other things, besides being unique, blissful, and without old age, meditate again on that Supreme knowledge.

## \|\| 2.29.23 \|\|

*yasmāt bhavanti bhūtāni yad gatvā neha jāyate \|*  
*sa tasmādīśvaro devaḥ parasmād yo 'dhitiṣṭhati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Is'vara, the god of gods, who is the source of creation of all the bhiitas, and by achieving which, the people do not attain rebirth and who remains present beyond all of them.

## \|\| 2.29.24 \|\|

*yadantare tad gaganaṃ śāśvataṃ śivamavyayam \|*  
*yadaṃśastatparo yastu sa devaḥ syānmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In whose heart the sky is lodged, the same everlasting Shiva, has been described as the bestower of welfare, auspicious, and the greatest.

## \|\| 2.29.25 \|\|

*vratāni yāni bhikṣūṇāṃ tathaivopavratāni ca \|*  
*ekaikātikrame teṣāṃ prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The vratas and upavratas which are to be followed by the Bhiksus, and in case they are not followed, then the repentence for each one of such lapses is being described.

## \|\| 2.29.26-27 \|\|

*upetya ca striyaṃ kāmāt prāyaścittaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*prāṇāyāmasamāyuktaṃ kuryāt sāṃtapanaṃ śuciḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tataścareta niyamāt kṛcchraṃ saṃyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*punarāśramamāgamya cared bhiśruratandritaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The one who even after being a Sannydsin, enjoys sex with a woman, getting infested with passion, then he with concentration, should perform repentence observing the vrata known as Santapana. Thereafter, controlling his mind, the Krcchra vrata should be performed appropriately. Thereafter he should remain with perfect mental control and regularly perform the Krcchra rite. Then entering the hermitage again, he should conduct himself carefully as a Bhiksu.

## \|\| 2.29.28 \|\|

*na dharmayuktamanṛtaṃ hinastīti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi ca na kartavyaṃ prasaṅgo hyeṣa dāruṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. It In case one speaks falsehood in a joke, it does not deprive a person of his merits. This has been ordained by the sages. But such a type of falsehood is prohibited for a Sannyasin, as this is a serious incident.

## \|\| 2.29.29 \|\|

*ekarātropavāsaśca prāṇāyāmaśataṃ tathā \|*  
*uktvānṛtaṃ prakartavyaṃ yatinā dharmalipsunā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The Sannyasin, well-versed in dharma, when speaks falsehood, he should perform repentance by fasting for a night and performing pramyama a hundred times.

## \|\| 2.29.30 \|\|

*paramāpadgatenāpi na kāryaṃ steyamanyataḥ \|*  
*steyādabhyadhikaḥ kaścinnāstyadharma iti smṛtiḥ \|*  
*hiṃsā caiṣāparā diṣṭā yā cātmajñānanāśikā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Even in extreme emergent conditions, a Sannyasin, should not steal the belongings of others. According to the scriptures, there is no other sin worse than stealing .

## \|\| 2.29.31 \|\|

*yadetad draviṇaṃ nāma prāṇa hyete bahiśvarāḥ \|*  
*sa tasya harati prāṇān yo yasya harate dhanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Theft is a terrific voilence which is the destroyer of the self knowledge. The thing which is known as the wealth, happens to be the external life of the person.

## \|\| 2.29.32-33 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā sa duṣṭātmā bhinnavṛtto vratāccyutaḥ \|*  
*bhūyo nirvedamāpannaścareccāndrāyaṇavratam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vidhinā śāstradṛṣṭena saṃvatsaramiti śrutiḥ \|*  
*bhūyo nirvedamāpannaścared bhikṣuratandritaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. A person who steals others wealth, it amounts to extracting the life of that person. By so doing the wicked soul falls from the noble conduct. By indulging in such activities, he should appropriately perform the Candrdyana-vrata according to the injunctions in the scriptures. After repentance, the Bhiksu should conduct himself quite carefully .

## \|\| 2.29.34 \|\|

*akasmādeva hiṃsāṃ tu yadi bhikṣuḥ samācaret \|*  
*kuryātkṛchrātikṛcchraṃ tu cāndrāyaṇamathāpi vā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In case a Sannyasin, out of ignorance resorts to voilence suddenly, then he should perform Krcchratikrcchra or Ccindrayana rite.

## \|\| 2.29.35 \|\|

*skandedindriyadaurbalyāt striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā yatiryadi \|*  
*tena dhārayitavyā vai prāṇāyāmāstu ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*divāskande trirātraṃ syāt prāṇāyāmaśataṃ tathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. In case a Sannyasin, because of his internal weakness, discharges his semen, at the sight of a woman, then he should perform pranayama sixteen times.

## \|\| 2.29.36 \|\|

*ekānne madhumāṃse ca navaśrāddhe tathaiva ca \|*  
*pratyakṣalavaṇe coktaṃ prājāpatyaṃ viśodhanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. If the involuntary emission of the semen takes place during the day time, he should perform hunderd pranayamas every day for three days. By consuming the wine and meat secretly, or openly consuming the salt during the Nava- sraddha (first s'mddha after the person’s death), one should perform Prajapatya vrata for his purification.

## \|\| 2.29.37 \|\|

*dhyānaniṣṭhasya satataṃ naśyate sarvapātakam \|*  
*tasmānmaheśvaraṃ jñātvā tasya dhyānaparo bhavet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. With the continuous meditation of a Sannyasin, all his sins are washed out. Therefore, he should always remain engaged in meditation of lord Mahesvara.

## \|\| 2.29.38 \|\|

*yad brahma paramaṃ jyotiḥ pratiṣṭhākṣaramadvayam \|*  
*yo 'ntarātra paraṃ brahma sa vijñeyo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The Brahman, who is lodged in the supreme flame, is indestructible and undecaying, the one who is lodged in the centre of Brahman, he is known as Mahes'vara.

## \|\| 2.29.39 \|\|

*eṣa devo mahādevaḥ kevalaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*tadevākṣaramadvaitaṃ tadādityāntaraṃ param \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He is the unique god known as Mahadeva, and bestows welfare on all. He is resplendent, the supreme Brahman, undecaying, and the excellent one. He alone is the non-dualistic imperishable deity within the orb of the sun.

## \|\| 2.29.40 \|\|

*yasmānmahīyate devaḥ svadhāmni jñānasaṃjñite \|*  
*ātmayogāhvaye tattve mahādevastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Because of his possessing the divine knowledge, and the one who is adored in his abode by the Atmayoga tattva, and termed as Agni and Jfiana, he is called as lord Mahadeva.

## \|\| 2.29.41 \|\|

*nānyad devānmahādevād vyatiriktaṃ prapaśyati \|*  
*tamevātmānamanveti yaḥ sa yāti paraṃ padam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The one for whom, no other god, except lord Mahadeva, matters, he is self-conscious and as such he achieves

## \|\| 2.29.42 \|\|

*manyate ye svamātmānaṃ vibhinnaṃ parameśvarāt \|*  
*na te paśyanti taṃ devaṃ vṛthā teṣāṃ pariśramaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. A person who considers his own soul separate from Paramesvara, he is unable to achieve the supreme god. The efforts of such people are of no use.

## \|\| 2.29.43 \|\|

*ekameva paraṃ brahma vijñeyaṃ tattvamavyayam \|*  
*sa devastu mahādevo naitad vijñāya badhyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The everlasting form of tattva, the supreme Brahman, is worth knowing and he happens to be Mahadeva. The one who well realises this, he never gets entangled in the worldly bondages.

## \|\| 2.29.44 \|\|

*tasmād yateta niyataṃ yatiḥ saṃyatamānasaḥ \|*  
*jñānayogarataḥ śānto mahādevaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Therefore, a Sannyasin, concentrating his mind, practicing the jnanayoga (path of knowledge), should worship getting devoted to lord Mahadeva.

## \|\| 2.29.45 \|\|

*eṣa vaḥ kathito vipro yatīnāmāśramaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*pitāmahena vibhunā munīnāṃ pūrvamīritam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О Brahmanas, I have narrated the auspicious duties of an ascetic to you, which were spoken in earlier times by lord Brahma to the sages.

## \|\| 2.29.46 \|\|

*nāputraśiṣyayogibhyo dadyādidamanuttamam \|*  
*jñānaṃ svayaṃbhuvā proktaṃ yatidharmāśrayaṃ śivam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The knowledge of the auspicious as'rama- dharma is a sort of welfare knowledge, which should be passed on to the son, a disciple, and the Yogins and none else.

## \|\| 2.29.47 \|\|

*iti yatiniyamānāmetaduktaṃ vidhānaṃ*  
*paśupatiparitoṣe yad bhavedekahetuḥ \|*  
*na bhavati punareṣāmudbhavo vā vināśaḥ*  
*praṇihitamanaso ye nityamevācaranti \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus the rules for the Sannyasins are well described. The one who follows these rules, lord Pasupati, gets pleased with him immensely. The people, who with a devoted mind follow these rules faithfully, they neither have to face destruction nor are they reborn.

## Chapter 30. Method of expiation

## \|\| 2.30.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravalakṣyāmi prāyaścittavidhiṃ śubham \|*  
*hitāya sarvaviprāṇāṃ doṣāṇāmapanuttaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “I shall now speak out the auspicious way of expiation, which is beneficial for the welfare of the Brahmanas that removes all the sins.

## \|\| 2.30.2 \|\|

*akṛtvā vihitaṃ karma kṛtvā ninditameva ca \|*  
*doṣamāpnoti puruṣaḥ prāyaścittaṃ viśodhanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The people attract the sins by not following the auspicious path, prescribed in the scriptures, and with the expiatory rite, a person is purified.

## \|\| 2.30.3 \|\|

*prāyaścittamakṛtvā tu na tiṣṭhed brāhmaṇaḥ kvacit \|*  
*yad brūyurbrāhmaṇāḥ śāntā vidvāṃsastatsamācaret \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A Brahmana, who needs repentance should not sit without it even for a moment. He should follow the words of peaceful and learned Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.30.4 \|\|

*vedārthavittamaḥ śānto dharmakāmo 'gnimān dvijaḥ \|*  
*sa eva syāt paro dharmo yameko 'pi vyavasyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A Brahmana, who is excellently well versed in the Vedas besides being calm, follower of dharma, maintaining sacrificial fires, shall be the greatest virtue even if it be that he alone performs it.

## \|\| 2.30.5 \|\|

*anāhitāgnayo viprāstrayo vedārthapāragāḥ \|*  
*yad brūyurdharmakāmāste tajjñeyaṃ dharmasādhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When three Brahmanas well versed in the Vedas, but not maintaining sacrificial fires, then whatever is spoken by them, becoming Dharmarthins, the same should be treated as the source of dharma.

## \|\| 2.30.6 \|\|

*anekadharmaśāstrajñā ūhāpohaviśāradāḥ \|*  
*vedādhyayanasaṃpannāḥ saptaite parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Seven Brahmanas who are well versed in the several of the Dharmasastras, and are proficient in logical reasoning, as well as the Vedas, their words are considered to be authentic in the religious matters.

## \|\| 2.30.7 \|\|

*mīmāṃsājñānatattvajñā vedāntakuśalā dvijāḥ \|*  
*ekaviṃśatisaṃkhyātāḥ prayāścittaṃ vadanti vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then twenty-one Brahmanas who are well versed in the six systems of philosophy, including mlmamsa and darsana, as well as Vedanta, are considered to be the authority on expiatory rites.

## \|\| 2.30.8 \|\|

*brahmahā madyapaḥ steno gurutalpaga eva ca \|*  
*mahāpātakinastvete yaścaitaiḥ saha saṃvaset \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. One who commits brahmahatya, drinks wine, steals the gold of a Brahmana, and has sex with the wife of the preceptor, are treated to be awful sinners. Those who keep relations with such people are also considered to be sinners.

## \|\| 2.30.9 \|\|

*saṃvatsaraṃ tu patitaiḥ saṃsargaṃ kurute tu yaḥ \|*  
*yānaśayyāsanairnityaṃ jānan vai patito bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The people who live with such people for a year, they also turn as grave sinners. The people, who deliberately travel in the same vehicle with such fallen persons, or sleep with them on one bed, or sit over the same seat, they are also fallen.

## \|\| 2.30.10 \|\|

*yājanaṃ yonisaṃbandhaṃ tathaivādhyāpanaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā sadyaḥ patejjñānāt saha bhojanameva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. To deliberately marry a fallen girl, or serve as a priest for a fallen person, to teach a fallen person or to eat with him in one and the same vase, a Brahmana gets fallen at once.

## \|\| 2.30.11 \|\|

*avijñāyātha yo mohāt kuryādadhyāpanaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*saṃvatsareṇa patati sahādhyayanameva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A person who teaches a fallen person unknowingly or out of delusion, or studies with him, he gets fallen in a year.

## \|\| 2.30.12 \|\|

*brahmāhā dvādaśābdāni kuṭiṃ kṛtvā vane vaset \|*  
*bhaikṣamātmaviśuddhyarthaṃ kṛtvā śavaśirodhvajam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A person who commits brahmahatya should live in a forest for twelve years in a hut, and at the same time he should beg alms with the skull of the dead as a symbol on the flag.

## \|\| 2.30.13 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāvasathān sarvān devāgārāṇi varjayet \|*  
*vinindan svayamātmānaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ ca saṃsmaran \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Discarding the house of Brahmanas or a temple, keeping the dead Brahmana in mind, and in disgust, he should censure himself constantly.

## \|\| 2.30.14-15 \|\|

*asaṃkalpitayogyāni saptāgārāṇi saṃviśet \|*  
*vidhūme śanakairnityaṃ vyaṅgāre bhuktavajjane \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ekakālaṃ cared bhaikṣaṃ doṣaṃ vikhyāpayan nṛṇām \|*  
*vanyamūlaphalairvāpi vartayed dhairyamākṣitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. When the smoke no more rises from the kitchen of a householder, the fire of the kitchen is extinguished, and the immates whereof have taken their meals, then he should quitely and slowly enter seven houses for begging. He should reveal his sin to the people and then beg alms only once or otherwise, keeping patience, he should consume the wild fruits and roots, for his livelihood.

## \|\| 2.30.16 \|\|

*kapālapāṇiḥ khaṭvāṅgī brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*pūrṇe tu dvādaśe varṣe brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Such a grave sinner, at the time of seeking alms, should hold a skull in the form of a begging bowl, Khatvanga and should observe celibacy. After the completion of twelve years, he is relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya.

## \|\| 2.30.17 \|\|

*akāmataḥ kṛte pāpe prāyaścittamidaṃ śubham \|*  
*kāmato maraṇācchuddhirjñeyā nānyena kenacit \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When a brahmahatya is committed unintentionally, this type of repentance is quite auspicious. But when the same is committed deliberately, there is no other way except to put an end to one’s life.

## \|\| 2.30.18 \|\|

*kuryādanaśanaṃ vātha bhṛgoḥ patanameva vā \|*  
*jvalantaṃ vā viśedagniṃ jalaṃ vā praviśet svayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A person who commits brahmahatya knowingly should observe fast imto death, or should end his life by entering into the burning fire or water.

## \|\| 2.30.19 \|\|

*brāhmaṇārthe gavārthe vā samyak prāṇān parityajet \|*  
*brahmahatyāpanodārthamantarā vā mṛtasya tu \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In order to wipe off the sin of Brahmana- slaughter, he should discard his life for the sake of a Brahmana or a cow or for the sake of the dead.

## \|\| 2.30.20 \|\|

*dīrghāmayānvitaṃ vipraṃ kṛtvānāmayameva tu \|*  
*dattvā cānnaṃ sa durbhikṣe brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In case, he makes a Brahmana to be free from a prolonged ailment, or donates cereals to a learned Brahmana, then he gets freed from the sin of brahmahatya.

## \|\| 2.30.21 \|\|

*aśvamedhāvabhṛthake snātvā vā śudhyate dvijaḥ \|*  
*sarvasvaṃ vā vedavide brāhmaṇāya pradāya tu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. At the concluding bath to the Asvamedha sacrifice when the performer gives away everything to the priest who is a master of Vedas, then all his sins are washed out.

## \|\| 2.30.22 \|\|

*sarasvatyāstvaruṇayā saṃgame lokaviśrute \|*  
*śudhyet triṣavaṇasnānāt trirātropoṣito dvijaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Every sinner should perform fast for three nights and should take three baths at the confluence of the rivers, Aruna and Sarasvatl, which relieves him of the sin of brahmahatya.

## \|\| 2.30.23 \|\|

*gatvā rāmeśvaraṃ puṇyaṃ snātvā caiva mahodadhau \|*  
*brahmacaryādibhiryukto dṛṣṭvā rudraṃ vimucyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By going to the holy place Rames'vara, and by taking bath in the great ocean or by concentrating on Rudra, the person who commits brahmahatya, is relieved of the related sin.

## \|\| 2.30.24 \|\|

*kapālamocanaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ devasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*snātvābhyarcya pitṝn bhaktyā brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Going to the Kapala-mocana tirtha (at Varanasi) of lord Shiva, taking a bath there, when a person adores the manes as well as the gods, he is relieved of the sin of brahmahatya.

## \|\| 2.30.25-26 \|\|

*yatra devādidevena bharaveṇāmitaujasā \|*  
*kapālaṃ sthāpitaṃ pūrvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*samabhyarcya mahādevaṃ tatra bhairavarūpiṇam \|*  
*tarpapitvā pitṝn snātvā mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. In ancient times, the illustrious lord Bhairava, had severed the skull of lord Brahma, which was dropped there. One should therefore, take bath there, and adore Mahadeva in the form of Bhairava, offering oblation to the manes, by which one is relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya.

## Chapter 31. Glory of Kapalamocana tirtha

## \|\| 2.31.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ devena rudreṇa śaṅkareṇāmitaujasā \|*  
*kapālaṃ brahmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ sthāpitaṃ dehajaṃ bhuvi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said, “O Lord, how was the skull severed from the body of Brahma, was placed on the earth by the extremely illustrious lord Rudra-Shiva?

## \|\| 2.31.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śṛṇudhvamṛṣayaḥ puṇyāṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśanīm \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ devadevasya mahādevasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suta said, “O Rishis, you please listen to this auspicious story which relieves one of all the sins. In this story, the glory of Shiva, the god of gods is narrated.

## \|\| 2.31.3 \|\|

*purā pitāmahaṃ devaṃ meruśṛṅge maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*procuḥ praṇamya lokādiṃ kimekaṃ tattvamavyayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In ancient times, the great sages, adored the Grandsire, lord Brahma over the peak of the Mem mountain, offering their salutation to him, and asked him about the everlasting Principle.

## \|\| 2.31.4-5 \|\|

*sa māyayā maheśasya mohito lokasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*avijñāya paraṃ bhāvaṃ svātmānaṃ prāha dharṣiṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ahaṃ dhātā jagadyoniḥ svayaṃbhūreka īśvaraḥ \|*  
*anādimatparaṃ brahma māmabhyarcya vimucyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Brahma, the creator of the lokas, getting influenced with the Maya of Shiva, unaware of the supreme ideology, expressed to the Rishis about himself as the undecaying principle, and claimed, “I am Vidhata, source of the origin of the universe, besides being self-bom Ishvara. I am eternal, Aditya, and the supreme Brahman. One is liberated by adoring me.

## \|\| 2.31.6 \|\|

*ahaṃ hi sarvadevānāṃ pravartakanivartakaḥ \|*  
*na vidyate cābhyadhiko matto lokeṣu kaścana \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I am the founder of all the gods, makes all Devas function as well as desist them, and there is no other god on earth superior to me.”

## \|\| 2.31.7-8 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ manyamānasya jajñe nārāyaṇāṃśajaḥ \|*  
*provāca prahasan vākyaṃ roṣatāmravilocanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kiṃ kāraṇamidaṃ brahman vartate tava sāṃpratam \|*  
*ajñānayogayuktasya na tvetaducitaṃ tava \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. At these words of Brahma, the three-eyed Shiva, who was bom from the ams'a of Narayana, spoke smilingly, “what is the reason for your haying developed such an ideology in you. Possibly you have been overpowered with ignorance. Your this claim is not correct.

## \|\| 2.31.9 \|\|

*ahaṃ dhātā hi lokānāṃ yajño nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*na māmṛte 'sya jagato jīvanaṃ sarvadā kvacit \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. I am the creator of these lokas, and have been bom of Narayana. There is no life on earth except myself.

## \|\| 2.31.10 \|\|

*ahameva paraṃ jyotirahameva parā gatiḥ \|*  
*matpreritena bhavatā sṛṣṭaṃ bhuvanamaṇḍalam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I happen to be the supreme brilliance, I am the greatest goal. In case you have created the earth, it is all due to the inspiration from me.”

## \|\| 2.31.11 \|\|

*evaṃ vivadatormohāt parasparajayaiṣiṇoḥ \|*  
*ājagmuryatra tau devau vedāścatvāra eva hi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the same time (while these two deities were arguing), the four Vedas came to the place where these two deities were present.

## \|\| 2.31.12 \|\|

*anvīkṣya devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ yajñātmānaṃ ca saṃsthitam \|*  
*procuḥ saṃvignahṛdayā yāthātmyaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. At that point of time, finding Brahma, and the lord Narayana identical with Yajna, all the four Vedas became auxious and spoke to Parames'vara, about the reality.

## \|\| 2.31.13 \|\|

*ṛgveda uvāca*  
*yasyāntaḥ sthāni bhūtāni yasmātsarvaṃ pravartate \|*  
*yadāhustatparaṃ tattvaṃ sa devaḥ syānmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Rgveda said, “The one in whom all the living beings are lodged, and from whom the universe has been bom, and the one who is considered to be the supreme principle by the sages, he happens to be lord Mahesvara.”

## \|\| 2.31.14 \|\|

*yajurveda uvāca*  
*yo yajñairakhilairīśo yogena ca samarcyate \|*  
*yamāhurīśvaraṃ devaṃ sa devaḥ syāt pinākadhṛk \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Yajurveda said, “The one who is adored be means of Yajnas and the Yoga, and the one who is eulogised as Is'vara by the sages, he happens to be the Pinaka-bearing deity.”

## \|\| 2.31.15 \|\|

*sāmaveda uvāca*  
*yenedaṃ bhrāmyate cakraṃ yadākāśāntaraṃ śivam \|*  
*yogibhirvidyate tattvaṃ mahādevaḥ sa śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Samaveda said, “the one by whom the whole world revolves, who is within the sky, and who is known by the Yogins as the principle Reality, he happens to be lord Sankara.

## \|\| 2.31.16 \|\|

*atharvaveda uvāca*  
*yaṃ prapaśyanti yogeśaṃ yatanto yatayaḥ param \|*  
*maheśaṃ puruṣaṃ rudraṃ sa devo bhagavān bhavaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Atharvaveda said, “Lord Mahesa-the Purana-Purusa, whom the great Yogins visualize and worship, making all the efforts, he happens to be lord Bhava alone.”

## \|\| 2.31.17 \|\|

*evaṃ sa bhagavān brahmā vedānāmīritaṃ śubham \|*  
*śrutvāha prahasan vākyaṃ viśvātmāpi vimohitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thus, listening to the auspicious words of the Vedas, lord Brahma laughed utterly deluded, and the lord of Atman of the universe then spoke.

## \|\| 2.31.18 \|\|

*kathaṃ tatparamaṃ brahma sarvasaṅgavivarjitam \|*  
*ramate bhāryayā sārdhaṃ pramathaiścātigarvitaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. “How could he be the supreme Brahman, who has been devoid of all attachments, and who wanders with his wife, having the company of Pramathas (attendants)?”

## \|\| 2.31.19 \|\|

*itirite 'tha bhagavān praṇavātmā sanātanaḥ \|*  
*amūrto mūrtimān bhūtvā vacaḥ prāha pitāmaham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. At these words of Brahma, the eternal lord, the form of Pranava, the formless one, became embodied and spoke these words to Brahma.

## \|\| 2.31.20-21 \|\|

*praṇava uvāca*  
*na hyeṣa bhagavān patnyā svātmano vyatiriktayā \|*  
*kadācid ramate rudrastādṛśo hi maheśvaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ayaṃ sa bhagavānīśaḥ svayañjyotiḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*svānandabhūtā kathitā devī nāgantukā śivā \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Pranava said, “Lord Isa, at no time, wanders with any one at any time, except with his own soul. The same lord Mahesvara, is Isa, resplendent, and ever lasting. The goddess Shiva is said to be his own blissful form and not extraneous.”

## \|\| 2.31.22 \|\|

*ityevamukte 'pi tadā yajñamūrterajasya ca \|*  
*nājñānamagamannāśamīśvarasyaiva māyayā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even at these words, because of the Maya of Ishvara, the ignorance of Aja (Brahma), whose body is Yajiia, was not removed.

## \|\| 2.31.23 \|\|

*tadantare mahājyotirviriñco viśvabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*prāpaśyadadbhutaṃ divyaṃ pūrayan gaganāntaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. At the same time, Brahma, the creator of the universe, witnessed a divine and great brilliance, filling up the space of the sky.

## \|\| 2.31.24 \|\|

*tanmadhyasaṃsthaṃ vimalaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tejasojjvalam \|*  
*vyomamadhyagataṃ divyaṃ prādurāsīd dvijottamāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. О Best of the Brahmanas, in the middle of it, was stationed a sphere of brilliance shining with splendour. Such as divine splendour appeared in front of him.

## \|\| 2.31.25 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā vadanaṃ divyaṃ mūrdhni lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tena tanmaṇjalaṃ ghoramālokayadaninditam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Brahma, the grandsire, lifting his head looked at the lustre, which was blissful inspite of its being so vast.

## \|\| 2.31.26-27 \|\|

*prajajvālātikopena brahmaṇaḥ pañcamaṃ śiraḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇādadṛśyata mahān puruṣo nīlalohitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*triśūlapiṅgalo devo nāgayajñopavītavān \|*  
*taṃ prāha bhagavān brahmā śaṅkaraṃ nīlalohitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Then the fifth head of Brahma, started illumining with anger, which was noticed by lord'Nilalohita-Shiva, the tawny-coloured tridentbearing lord, having the serpents for his sacred thread, in a moment. Then, lord Brahma said to Nilalohita-Shiva.

## \|\| 2.31.28 \|\|

*jānāmi bhavataḥ pūrvaṃ lalāṭādeva śaṅkara \|*  
*prādurbhāvaṃ maheśān māmeva śaraṇaṃ vraja \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О Sankara, You have been initially bom out of my forehead for the sake of knowledge. You, Mahes'ana, should therefore take refuge in me.

## \|\| 2.31.29-31 \|\|

*śrutvā sagarvavacanaṃ padmayoneratheśvaraḥ \|*  
*prāhiṇot puruṣaṃ kālaṃ bhairavaṃ lokadāhakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sa kṛtvā sumahad yuddhaṃ brahmaṇā kālabhairavaḥ \|*  
*cakarta tasya vadanaṃ viriñcasyātha pañcamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nikṛttavadano devo brahmā devena śaṃbhunā \|*  
*mamāra ceśayogena jīvitaṃ prāpa viśvasṛk \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Then, listening to the arrogant words of Brahma, Shiva deputed Kalabhairava, who waged a terrific war with Brahma, in which the fifth head of Virinca (Brahma) was cut off. Brahma, whose face was cut by lord Sambhu, died; but by means of the Yogic power of Isa, the holder of the universe (Brahma) regained his life.

## \|\| 2.31.32 \|\|

*athānupaśyad giriśaṃ maṇḍalāntarasaṃsthitam \|*  
*samāsīnaṃ mahādevyā mahādevaṃ sanātanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thereafter, Brahma found Tsana, the eternal Mahadeva and the great goddess lodged in an outer sphere of light.

## \|\| 2.31.33 \|\|

*bhujaṅgarājavalayaṃ candrāvayavabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*koṭisūryapratīkāśaṃ jaṭājūṭavirājitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The Lord was adorned with the bracelet of the royal serpents. He had the crescent-moon as an ornament. He had the lustre of crores of suns. He had beautiful matted locks of hair.

## \|\| 2.31.34 \|\|

*śārdūlacarmavasanaṃ divyamālāsamanvitam \|*  
*triśūlapāṇiṃ duṣprekṣyaṃ yoginaṃ bhūtibhūṣaṇam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Mahadeva was clad in the tiger-skin and had a beautiful appearance. He was wearing the beautiful divine garlands. He appeared as a great Yogin who could not be looked at due to his brilliance, and held a trident in his hand.

## \|\| 2.31.35 \|\|

*yamantarā yoganiṣṭhāḥ prapaśyanti hṛdīśvaram \|*  
*tamādidevaṃ brahmāṇaṃ mahādevaṃ dadarśa ha \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At that time, lord Brahma saw the primordial deity, the first deity, great lord whom those who are stabilised in Yoga see within their hearts as Ishvara or Brahman.

## \|\| 2.31.36 \|\|

*yasya sā paramā devī śaktirākāśasaṃsthitā \|*  
*so 'nantaiśvaryayogātmā maheśo dṛśyate kila \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The Supreme goddess, designated as the sky, with infinite divine potencies like omniscience, omnipresence etc., was also present there.

## \|\| 2.31.37 \|\|

*yasyāśeṣajagad bījaṃ vilayaṃ yāti mohanam \|*  
*sakṛtpraṇāmamātreṇa sa rudraḥ khalu dṛśyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The same Rudra, by offering salutation to whom once, the deluding seed of the whole earth gets dissolved, was seen there.

## \|\| 2.31.38 \|\|

*yo 'tha nācāraniratān svabhaktāneva kevalam \|*  
*vimocayati lokānāṃ nāyako dṛśyate kila \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The people who are well disciplined and devoted to the lord, can have an audience with him. The same soul of the universe, leader of the universe, Mahadeva was seen by Brahma.

## \|\| 2.31.39 \|\|

*yasya vedavidaḥ śāntā nirdvandvā brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*vidanti vimalaṃ rūpaṃ sa śaṃbhurdṛśyate kila \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The one whose Linga is adored by Brahma and other gods, and the sages-the expounders of Brahman always, the same Shiva was visible in the circular lustre.

## \|\| 2.31.40 \|\|

*yasya brahmādayo devā ṛṣayo brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*arcayanti sadā liṅgaṃ viśveśaḥ khalu dṛśyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. That Sankara was seen whose proximity is never left off by Is'vara, the form of Vijrnna, appeared before Brahma.

## \|\| 2.31.41 \|\|

*yasyāśeṣajagad bījaṃ vilayaṃ yāti mohanam \|*  
*sakṛtpraṇāmamātreṇa sa rudraḥ khalu dṛśyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. That Isvara was indeed seen, the son of Hiranyagarbha, in whose circular halo of light was seen the Paramesvara accompanied by knowledge.

## \|\| 2.31.42 \|\|

*vidyāsahāyo bhagavān yasyāsau maṇḍalāntaram \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaputro 'sāvīśvaro dṛśyate kila \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. By offering the water, flowers, or leaves, at whose feet, a person is redeemed of the universe, the same Rudra, appeared before Brahma.

## \|\| 2.31.43 \|\|

*yasyāśeṣajagatsūtirvijñānatanurīśvarī \|*  
*na muñcati sadā pārśvaṃ śaṅkaro 'sāvadṛśyata \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. By achieving whose vicinity, the eternal Kala (Time) controls the entire universe. The god whose soul is Yoga and who is the governor of Kala was seen.

## \|\| 2.31.44 \|\|

*puṣpaṃ vā yadi vā patraṃ yatpādayugale jalam \|*  
*dattvā tarati saṃsāraṃ rudro 'sau dṛśyate kila \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The one who represents the life of all, besides being the ornament of the three worlds, whose ornament is the Soma (moon), he appeared as a Somadeva.

## \|\| 2.31.45 \|\|

*tatsannidhāne sakalaṃ niyacchati sanātanaḥ \|*  
*kālaḥ kila sa yogātmā kālakālo hi dṛśyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The great God whose natural eternal union with goddess Uma is ever seen and the great liberation on seeing him is extolled was now seen.

## \|\| 2.31.46 \|\|

*jīvanaṃ sarvalokānāṃ trilokasyaiva bhūṣaṇam \|*  
*somaḥ sa dṛśyate devaḥ somo yasya vibhūṣaṇam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Those who are well-versed in the principle of Yoga, and who are engaged in yogic practices, they meditate upon his union with the goddess. That great Yogin was indeed seen.

## \|\| 2.31.47-48 \|\|

*devyā saha sadā sākṣād yasya yogaḥ svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*gīyate paramā muktiḥ sa yogī dṛśyate kila \|\| 47 \|\|*

*yogino yogatattvajñā viyogābhimukhāniśam \|*  
*yogaṃ dhyāyanti devyāsau sa yogī dṛśyate kila \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Finding Mahadeva, in the company of goddess, seated over the best of the seat, lord Aja, regained the divine memory and pleased lord Shiva, having the crescent as an ornament.

## \|\| 2.31.49 \|\|

*so 'nuvīkṣya mahādevaṃ mahādevyā sanātanam \|*  
*varāsane samāsīnamavāpa paramāṃ smṛtim \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Brahma said, “Salutation to the great lord. Salutation again and again to Mahadevl.

## \|\| 2.31.50 \|\|

*labdhvā māheśvarīṃ divyāṃ saṃsmṛtiṃ bhagavānajaḥ \|*  
*toṣayāmāsa varadaṃ somaṃ somavibhūṣaṇam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Salutation to the extremely peaceful lord Shiva, Salutation to goddess Shiva as well. Salutation to the lord, who is the form of Brahman. Salutation to you who are the vidya. Salutation to the great Isa, as well as the Primordial Prakrti, the root cause of the universe.

## \|\| 2.31.51 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*namo devāya mahate mahādevyai namo namaḥ \|*  
*namaḥ śivāya śāntāya śivāyai śāntaye namaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Salutation to Shiva in the form of vijnana. Salutation to the goddess again and again, who is said to be the form of auxities. Salutation to the lord who is destroyer of Kala. Salutation also to the goddess Is'vara.

## \|\| 2.31.52 \|\|

*oṃ namo brahmaṇe tubhyaṃ vidyāyai te namo namaḥ \|*  
*namo mūlaprakṛtaye maheśāya namo namaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Salutation again and again to the goddess Rudrani and the lord Rudra. Salutation to the form of Kala, and salutation to the goddess having the form of Maya.

## \|\| 2.31.53 \|\|

*namo vijñānadehāya cintāyai te namo namaḥ \|*  
*namaste kālakālāya īśvarāyai namo namaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The one who controls all the activities, the lord, besides the goddess who agitates everyone, salutation to both of You, salutation to the form of Prakrti as well as to lord Narayana.

## \|\| 2.31.54 \|\|

*namo namo 'stu rudrāya rudrāṇyai te namo namaḥ \|*  
*namo namaste kāmāya māyāyai ca namo namaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Salutation to the bestower of Yoga as well as to the preceptor of the Yogins. Salutation to the one who creates the world as well the one who lives in the universe.

## \|\| 2.31.55 \|\|

*niyantre sarvakāryāṇāṃ kṣobhikāyai namo namaḥ \|*  
*namo 'stu te prakṛtaye namo nārāyaṇāya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Salutation to the blissful one, the all pervading one, the form of bliss and the material cause of the universe.

## \|\| 2.31.56 \|\|

*yogādāyai namastubhyaṃ yogināṃ gurave namaḥ \|*  
*namaḥ saṃsāranāśāya saṃsārotpattaye namaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Salutation again and again to the fonn of Omkara, and the one who is lodged in the firmament and to the Shakti (potency) of the firmament.

## \|\| 2.31.57 \|\|

*nityānandāya vibhave namo 'stvānandamūrtaye \|*  
*namaḥ kāryavihīnāya viśvaprakṛtaye namaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thus lord Brahma, offered his salutation to lord Shiva, by means of Somastaka, prostrating on earth and repeating the mantras of Satarudrlya.

## \|\| 2.31.58 \|\|

*oṅkāramūrtaye tubhyaṃ tadantaḥ saṃsthitāya ca \|*  
*namaste vyomasaṃsthāya vyomaśaktyai namo namaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then the lord Shiva, who removes the sufferings of those who offer their salutation to him, lifted up Brahma with both his hands and said to him, “Now I am pleased with you.”

## \|\| 2.31.59 \|\|

*iti somāṣṭakeneśaṃ praṇanāma pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*papāta daṇḍavad bhūmau gṛṇan vai śatarudriyam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Then lord Mahadeva bestowed on Brahma the supreme Yoga and unparallel fortunes and then spoke to lord Nllalohita who was standing in front of him.

## \|\| 2.31.60 \|\|

*atha devo mahādevaḥ praṇatārtiharo haraḥ \|*  
*provācotthāpya hastābhyāṃ prato 'smi tava sāṃpratam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. “You should protect loM Brahma, who is the foremost in this world. He is the first one to stay in this universe. He possesses the best of the virtues, besides being your father.

## \|\| 2.31.61 \|\|

*dattvāsau paramaṃ yogamaiśvaryamatulaṃ mahat \|*  
*provācāgre sthitaṃ devaṃ nīlalohitamīśvaram \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He is the ancient Purusa. О sinless one, he should not be killed by you. He has taken refuge with me, in the context of the glory of Yoga and his fortunes.

## \|\| 2.31.62 \|\|

*eṣa brahmāsya jagataḥ saṃpūjyaḥ prathamaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*ātmano rakṣaṇīyaste gururjyeṣṭhaḥ pitā tava \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He is sacrifice and that is his pride. His pride is to be chastened by you. You have to carry with you Brahma’s head.

## \|\| 2.31.63 \|\|

*ayaṃ purāṇapuruṣo na hantavyastvayānagha \|*  
*svayogaiśvaryamāhātmyānmāmeva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. You, in order to get rid of the sin of brahmahatyd, should wander on earth and whatever riches are received in bhiksa should be given by you to the gods and the Brahmanas.”

## \|\| 2.31.64 \|\|

*ayaṃ ca yajño bhagavān sagarvo bhavatānagha \|*  
*śāsitavyo viriñcasya dhāraṇīyaṃ śirastvayā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thus speaking these words to Paramesvara (Rudra), the supreme lord retired to his divine natural abode, the greatest region.

## \|\| 2.31.65-66 \|\|

*brahmahatyāpanodārthaṃ vrataṃ lokāya darśayan \|*  
*carasva satataṃ bhikṣāṃ saṃsthāpaya suradvijān \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ityetaduktvā vacanaṃ bhagavān parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*sthānaṃ svābhāvikaṃ divyaṃ yayau tatparamaṃ padam \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Thereafter, lord Isa, Nilalohita of matted hair made Kalabhairava hold god Brahma’s head. And in order to get himself free from the sin of Brahmahatya, you perform the beneficial holy rite in the world. With the skull in the hand, you beg for alms all round.”

## \|\| 2.31.67 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bhagavānīśaḥ kaparde nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*grāhayāmāsa vadanaṃ brahmaṇaḥ kālabhairavam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Thus, he sent his daughter named Brahmahatya with terrific face and awful fanges, who had clusters of flames for ornaments to follow him.

## \|\| 2.31.68 \|\|

*cara tvaṃ pāpanāśārthaṃ vrataṃ lokahitāvaham \|*  
*kapālahasto bhagavān bhikṣāṃ gṛhṇātu sarvataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Then he commanded, “Till the arrival of the trident-bearing deity in the divine city of Varanasi, you should follow him.”

## \|\| 2.31.69 \|\|

*uktvaivaṃ prāhiṇot kanyāṃ brahmahatyāmiti śrutām \|*  
*daṃṣṭrākarālavadanāṃ jvālāmālāvibhūṣaṇām \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Thus commanding Kalagni Rudra (Kalabhairava), Mahes'vara said, “At my behest, keep on moving as a begger in all the worlds seeking alms.

## \|\| 2.31.70 \|\|

*yāvad vārāṇasīṃ divyāṃ purīmeṣa gamiṣyati \|*  
*tāvat tvaṃ bhīṣaṇe kālamanugaccha trilocanam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. On your meeting the eternal Narayana, only then you will be relieved of your sin, by means of the method spelt out by him.”

## \|\| 2.31.71-72 \|\|

*evamābhāṣya kālāgniṃ prāha devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*aṭasva nikhilaṃ lokaṃ bhikṣārtho manniyogataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*yadā drakṣyasi deveśaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam \|*  
*tadāsau vakṣyati spaṣṭamupāyaṃ pāpaśodhanam \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. Listening to the word of lord Shiva, the lord of the gods, Kalabhairava, holding the skull in his hand, started wandering in all the three lokas. He assumed a hideous form, and illumined with his own lustre. He form was holy, comely and endowed with glory. He had three eyes.

## \|\| 2.31.73-74 \|\|

*sa devadevatāvākyamākarṇya bhagavān haraḥ \|*  
*kapālapāṇirviśvātmā cacāra bhuvanatrayam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*āsthāya vikṛtaṃ veṣaṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā \|*  
*śrīmat pavitramatulaṃ jaṭājūṭavirājitam \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. That great Lord having the eyes resembling Kalagni (fire of universal destruction), was surrounded by the goblins, Siddhas and Pramathas, was shining like thousands of the suns. Enjoying the divine bliss of Paramesthin, the lord full of divine sports and pastimes, appeared before the world.

## \|\| 2.31.75 \|\|

*koṭisūryapratīkāśaiḥ pramathaiścātigarvitaiḥ \|*  
*bhāti kālāgninayano mahādevaḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. With Kalabhairava or Kalamukha-Shiva who was possessing such a great beauty, the groups of ladies started following him.

## \|\| 2.31.76 \|\|

*pītvā kadamṛtaṃ divyamānandaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*līlāvilāsūbahulo lokānāgacchatīśvaraḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. All of them reached before the lord, started dancing and singing and finding the serene smile over the face of the lord, they knitted their eyebrows.

## \|\| 2.31.77 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā kālavadanaṃ śaṅkaraṃ kālabhairavam \|*  
*rūpalāvaṇyasaṃpannaṃ nārīkulamagādanu \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The trident-bearing lord, while roaming about in the countries of the gods and the demons, ultimately reached the place of Visnu, where lord Purusottama was present.

## \|\| 2.31.78 \|\|

*gāyanti vividhaṃ gītaṃ nṛtyanti purataḥ prabhoḥ \|*  
*sasmitaṃ prekṣya vadanaṃ cakrurbhrūbhaṅgameva ca \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Reaching the divine abode, lord Shiva who is engaged in the welfare of the people, entered the place of lord Visnu along with the goblins.

## \|\| 2.31.79 \|\|

*sa devadānavādīnāṃ deśānabhyetya śūladhṛk \|*  
*jagāma viṣṇorbhavanaṃ yatrāste madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Without knowing the divine and the great being of Parames'vara, the powerful gatekeeper prevented the trident-bearing lord.

## \|\| 2.31.80 \|\|

*nirīkṣya divyabhavanaṃ śaṅkaro lokaśaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*sahaiva bhūtapravaraiḥ praveṣṭumupacakrame \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. He was holding the conch, discus, and the mace in his hands and was clad in the yellow lower garments. He had large arms. He was born of the amsa of Visnu and was known by the name Visvaksena.

## \|\| 2.31.81 \|\|

*avijñāya paraṃ bhāvaṃ divyaṃ tatpārameśvaram \|*  
*nyavārayat triśūlāṅkaṃ dvārapālo mahābalaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Then Visvaksena, born of Visnu, fought a terrific battle with Kalavega, the gana of Shiva who attacked him by the order of Bhairava. The gatekeeper with absolutely red eyes, overpowered Kalavega. Then, he rushed before Kalabhairava-the form of Rudra, and struck him with the Sudars'ana-cakra.

## \|\| 2.31.82 \|\|

*śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiḥ pītavāsā mahābhujaḥ \|*  
*viṣvaksena iti khyāto viṣṇoraṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Then Mahadeva, the conqueror of foes, the trident-bearing god, the destroyer of Tripuras, looked contempously the approaching gatekeeper.

## \|\| 2.31.83 \|\|

*athainaṃ śaṅkaragaṇo yuyudhe viṣṇusaṃbhavam \|*  
*bhīṣaṇo bhairavādeśāt kālavega iti śrutaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. In the meantime, a great goblin comparable to the fire at the end of the Yogas, attacked with a trident over his chest, as a result of which he fell down on earth.

## \|\| 2.31.84 \|\|

*vijitya taṃ kālavegaṃ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|*  
*rudrāyābhimukhaṃ raudraṃ cikṣepa ca sudarśanam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Having been struck with a trident, he lost all his great strength and fell down on the ground like persons afflicted by sickness on seeing death.

## \|\| 2.31.85 \|\|

*atha devo mahādevastripurāristriśūlabhṛt \|*  
*tamāpatantaṃ sāvajñamālokayadamitrajit \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Thus, killing the gatekeeper of Visnu, Mahadeva lifted up his body and entered the place of Visnu with his Pramathas.

## \|\| 2.31.86 \|\|

*tadantare mahadbhūtaṃ yugāntadahanopamam \|*  
*śūlenorasi nirbhidya pātayāmāsa taṃ bhuvi \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Lord Visnu, finding the arrival of Shiva, the cause of the universe, made the stream of blood to flow from his forehead.

## \|\| 2.31.87 \|\|

*sa śūlābhihato 'tyarthaṃ tyaktvā svaṃ paramaṃ balam \|*  
*tatyāja jīvitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mṛtyuṃ vyādhihatā iva \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Visnu said, “O extremely illustrious lord, you kindly accept the alms given by me (in the form of blood). О Destroyer of Tripuras, except this, no other bhiksa would be appropriate for you.

## \|\| 2.31.88 \|\|

*nihatya viṣṇupuruṣaṃ sārdhaṃ pramathapuṅgavaiḥ \|*  
*viveśa cāntaragṛhaṃ samādāya kalevaram \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Thereafter, even in the thousands of divine years, the skull of Brahma could not be filled up, though the blood from the forehead of Visnu continued to flow for a thousand divine years.

## \|\| 2.31.89-90 \|\|

*nirīkṣya jagato hetumīśvaraṃ bhagavān hariḥ \|*  
*śiro lalāṭāt saṃbhidya raktadhārāmapātayat \|\| 89 \|\|*

*gṛhāṇa bhagavan bhikṣāṃ madīyāmamitadyute \|*  
*na vidyate 'nābhyuditā tava tripuramardana \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. Thereafter, lord Narayana, Visnu, offered various prayers to lord Shiva gracefully and said, “Why are you carrying the skull of Brahma?” On hearing this, Mahesvara, the lord of Devas, narrated all the events.

## \|\| 2.31.91 \|\|

*na saṃpūrṇaṃ kapālaṃ tad brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu sā ca dhārā pravāhitā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The Acyuta, Hrsikesa, lord Visnu, called Brahmahatya before him and prayed her to leave lord Shiva.

## \|\| 2.31.92 \|\|

*athābravīt kālarudraṃ harirnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*saṃstūya vaidikairmantrairbahumānapuraḥ saram \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. When lord Visnu, so prayed to Brahmahatya, she still did not leave lord Shiva. Then after meditating on the source of origin of the universe, lord Visnu said to Sankara,

## \|\| 2.31.93 \|\|

*kimarthametad vadanaṃ brahmaṇo bhavatā dhṛtam \|*  
*provāca vṛttamakhilaṃ bhagavān parameśvaraḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. “O Lord, you go to the auspicious city of Varanasi, where Ishvara (lord Shiva) relieves the people of all their sins.

## \|\| 2.31.94 \|\|

*samāhūya hṛṣīkeśo brahmahatyāmathācyutaḥ \|*  
*prārthayāmāsa deveśo vimuñceti triśūlinam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Then for the sake of the welfare of all the people, he proceeded on for sporting in all the holy places.

## \|\| 2.31.95 \|\|

*na tatyājātha sā pārśvaṃ vyāhṛtāpi murāriṇā \|*  
*ciraṃ dhyātvā jagadyoniḥ śaṅkaraṃ prāha sarvavit \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Here and there, he was eulogised by the Pramathas. At that point of time, Kalabhairava carrying the dead body of the gatekeeper on his hands started dancing.

## \|\| 2.31.96 \|\|

*vrajasva bhagavan divyāṃ purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ śubhām \|*  
*yatrākhilajagaddoṣaṃ kṣipraṃ nāśayatāśvaraḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. At that point of time, lord Narayana, assuming another form, too rushed following him in order to witness his dance.

## \|\| 2.31.97 \|\|

*tataḥ śarvāṇi guhyāni tīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*jagāma līlayā devo lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The lord Shiva, the bull-bannered lord, finding lord Govinda present there, kept on dancing there smilingly.

## \|\| 2.31.98 \|\|

*saṃstūyamānaḥ pramathairmahāyogairitastataḥ \|*  
*nṛtyamāno mahāyogī hastanyastakalevaraḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Following Rudra, Hari with the Dharma as his carrier, entered the city of Varanasi belonging to lord Shiva.

## \|\| 2.31.99 \|\|

*tamabhyadhāvad bhagavān harirnārāyaṇaḥ svayam \|*  
*athāsthāyāparaṃ rūpaṃ nṛtyadarśanalālasaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. With the mere entry of Shiva, the lord of the universe with matter hair, in Varanasi, the brahmahatya left Shiva, while crying “Alas, Alas!” and disappeared from that place entering nether-worlds in disgust.

## \|\| 2.31.100 \|\|

*nirīkṣamāṇo novindaṃ vṛṣendrāṅkitaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*sasmito 'nantayogātmā nṛtyati sma punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Mahes'vara, entered his supreme abode, and placed the skull of Brahma before his attendants.

## \|\| 2.31.101 \|\|

*atha sānucaro rudraḥ saharirdharmavāhanaḥ \|*  
*bheje mahādevapurīṃ vārāṇasīmiti śrutām \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Then lord Mahadeva, the ocean of mercy, established the dead body of the gatekeeper in front of the attendants and commanded it to regain his life. Then the body of Visvaksena was given over to Visnu.

## \|\| 2.31.102 \|\|

*praviṣṭamātre deveśe brahmahatyā kapardini \|*  
*hā hetyuktvā sanādaṃ sā pātālaṃ prāpa duḥ khitā \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Then Shiva said, “Those who always adore my Kapalika form carefully, their sins of the present and future life are washed out.

## \|\| 2.31.103 \|\|

*praviśya paramaṃ sthānaṃ kapālaṃ brahmaṇo haraḥ \|*  
*gaṇānāmagrato devaḥ sthāpayāmāsa śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Anyone, who reaching in this excellent holy place, take his bath appropriately, and shall offer oblations to the gods and manes, he will get relieved of the sins of brahmahatya.

## \|\| 2.31.104 \|\|

*sthāpayitvā mahādevo dadau tacca kalevaram \|*  
*uktvā sajīvamastvīśo viṣṇave sa ghṛṇānidhiḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. A person, who taking this world be perishable, lives in the best city of Varanasi, he achieves the heaven and deliverance after death.”

## \|\| 2.31.105-106 \|\|

*ye smaranti mamājastraṃ kāpālaṃ veṣamuttamam \|*  
*teṣāṃ vinaśyati kṣipramihāmutra ca pātakam \|\| 105 \|\|*

*āgamya tīrthapravare snānaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*tarpayitvā pitṝn devān mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 106 \|\|*

105-106. Thus speaking, Mahadeva, embraced Janardana, and soon disappeared with the pramathas. The immensely intelligent lord Visnu, receiving his servant Visvaksena, from the trident-bearing lord Shiva, left for his place.

## \|\| 2.31.107-108 \|\|

*aśāśvataṃ jagajjñātvā ye 'smin sthāne vasanti vai \|*  
*dehānte tat paraṃ jñānaṃ dadāmi paramaṃ padam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*itīdamuktvā bhagavān samāliṅgya janārdanam \|*  
*sahaiva pramatheśānaiḥ kṣaṇādantaradhīyata \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. Thus, I have narrated the meritorious story that quells great sins and the glory of Kapdlamocana-tirtha, which is quite dear to lord Shiva. A person who recites this chapter in the presence of Brahmanas, he is freed from the sins of his action, thought and behaviour,

## Chapter 32. Rules for repentance

## \|\| 2.32.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*surāpastu surāṃ taptāmagnivarṇāṃ svayaṃ pibet \|*  
*tayā sa kāye nirdagdhe mucyate tu dvijottamaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vyasa said, “The Brahmana in the habit of drinking should consume the wine of the red colour like the fire flame. His body being scorched with the same, he shall be relieved of the related sin.

## \|\| 2.32.2 \|\|

*gomūtramagnivarṇaṃ vā gośakṛdrasameva vā \|*  
*payo ghṛtaṃ jalaṃ vātha mucyate pātakāt tataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He should drink cow’s urine of red colour like fire, or the diluted cow’s dung or milk, water or ghee. Then, he shall be liberated from the sin.

## \|\| 2.32.3 \|\|

*jalārdravāsāḥ prayato dhyātvā nārāyaṇaṃ harim \|*  
*brahmahatyāvrataṃ cātha caret tatpāpaśāntaye \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. For the removal of the sin, one should wear the clothes wet with water, and then reciting the name of Narayana, with great purity, should observe the holy rite in expiation for the sin of brahmahatya.

## \|\| 2.32.4 \|\|

*suvarṇasteyakṛd vipro rājānamabhigamya tu \|*  
*svakarma khyāpayan brūyānmāṃ bhavānanuśāstviti \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A Brahmana who steals the gold, should go to the king and admit his guilt and beg for a punishment.

## \|\| 2.32.5 \|\|

*gṛhītvā musalaṃ rājā sakṛd hanyāt tataḥ svayam \|*  
*vadhe tu śuddhyate steno brāhmaṇastapasaiva vā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The king in that case shall strike such a Brahmana with a threshing rod and at his death or by the means of his tapas the Brahmana can be freed from the sin.

## \|\| 2.32.6-7 \|\|

*skandhenādāya musalaṃ lakuṭaṃ vāpi khādiram \|*  
*śaktiṃ cobhayatastīkṣṇāmāyasaṃ daṇḍameva vā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*rājā tena ca gantavyo muktakeśena dhāvatā \|*  
*ācakṣāṇena tatpāpamevaṅkarmāsmi śādhi mām \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Or otherwise, he should himself carry a threshing rod or a wooden staff of Khadira over his shoulder, or an iron club with a pointed blade, loosening his hair, should go to the king rapidly and should reveal his sin before the king, saying “Chastise me.”

## \|\| 2.32.8 \|\|

*śāsanād vā vimokṣād vā stenaḥ steyād vimucyate \|*  
*aśāsitvā tu taṃ rājāstenasyāpnoti kilbiṣam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After the awarding of the punishment by the king, or by chastisement, he is freed from the sin. But in case, the king does not award punishment to him, then he himself attracts the sin of the thief.

## \|\| 2.32.9 \|\|

*tapasāpanunutsustu suvarṇasteyajaṃ malam \|*  
*cīravāsā dvijo 'raṇye cared brahmahaṇo vratam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A Brahmana, who steals the gold, in order to be free from the related sin, should wear bark- garments, and should remain in the forest and perform the expiatory rite of a slayer of a Brahmana there.

## \|\| 2.32.10 \|\|

*snātvāśvamedhāvabhṛthe pūtaḥ syādathavā dvijaḥ \|*  
*pradadyād vātha viprebhyaḥ svātmatulyaṃ hiraṇyakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A Brahmana should purity himself after performing the concluding bath of the Asvamedha sacrifice or alternatively he should give away in charities gold equivalent to his own weight to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.32.11 \|\|

*cared vā vatsaraṃ kṛcchraṃ brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇaḥ svarṇahārī tu tatpāpasyāpanuttaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A Brahmana, in order to free himself of the sin of the gold theft, should perform hard the Krcchra rite for a year observing celibacy.

## \|\| 2.32.12 \|\|

*gurorbhāryāṃ samāruhya brāhmaṇaḥ kāmamohitaḥ \|*  
*avagūhet striyaṃ taptāṃ dīptāṃ kārṣṇāyasīṃ kṛtām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In case a Brahmana, getting passionate, enjoys sex with the wife of his preceptor, then he should be made to embrace the burning image of a woman made of black iron.

## \|\| 2.32.13 \|\|

*svayaṃ vā śiśnavṛṣaṇāvutkṛtyādhāya cāñcalau \|*  
*ātiṣṭhed dakṣiṇāmāśāmānipātādajihmagaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Otherwise, as a repentance, he should himself remove his penis and scrotum, hold them in his palms, and should move to the southern direction, till they fall on the ground.

## \|\| 2.32.14-15 \|\|

*gurvarthaṃ vā hataḥ śuddhyeccared vā brahmahā vratam \|*  
*śākhāṃ vā kaṇṭakopetāṃ pariṣvajyātha vatsaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

*adhaḥ śayīta niyato mucyate gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*kṛcchraṃ vābdaṃ cared vipraścīravāsāḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. For purification of the sin for committing sex with the wife of the preceptor, the sinner should perform the expiatory rite of a slayer of a Brahmana, or should embrace the thorny branch of a tree and should sleep on the bare ground without spreading any cloth etc. By so doing the sinful person is relieved of his sin. Or, otherwise the Brahmana, clad in rags, with a concentrated mind, should perfom the Krchhra rite for a year.

## \|\| 2.32.16-17 \|\|

*aśvamedhāvabhṛthake snātvā vā śuddhyate naraḥ \|*  
*kāle 'ṣṭame vā bhuñjāno brahmacārī sadāvratī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sthānāsanābhyāṃ viharaṃstrirahno 'bhyupayannapaḥ \|*  
*adhaḥ śāyī tribhirvarṣaistad vyapohati pātakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Or otherwise, the Brahmana, performing the concluding bath of the Asvamedha sacrifice can get himself purified. He should take his meal on the eighth occasion after missing seven meals. He should observe celibacy and perform Sadavrata (perpetual rite). He should pass three days by standing and sitting strenuously. He should lie down in the bare ground. This would enable him to free himself from the sin within three years.

## \|\| 2.32.18 \|\|

*cāndrāyaṇāni vā kuryāt pañca catvāri vā punaḥ \|*  
*patitaiḥ saṃprayuktānāmatha vakṣyāmi niṣkṛtim \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Or, the sinful person should perform four or five Candrayana vratas. A person who is closely associated with the fallen or degraded people, I shall speak out for their deliverance.

## \|\| 2.32.19 \|\|

*patitena tu saṃsargaṃ yo yena kurute dvijaḥ \|*  
*sa tatpāpāpanodārthaṃ tasyaiva vratamācaret \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A Brahmana, who maintains relations with a degraded person, he for the removal of the related sin, should perform the same rite.

## \|\| 2.32.20 \|\|

*taptakṛcchraṃ cared vātha saṃvatsaramatandritaḥ \|*  
*ṣāṇmāsike tu saṃsarge prāyaścittārdhamarhati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If the close intimacy is of six months duration, such a Brahmana should perform the Taptakrcchra-vrata quite attentively, for full one year.

## \|\| 2.32.21 \|\|

*ebhirvratairapohanti mahāpātakino malam \|*  
*puṇyatīrthābhigamanāt pṛthivyāṃ vātha niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By performing these vratas even the grave sinner is removed of the sins. Or alternatively one should visit the holy places on earth, by which the sins are removed.

## \|\| 2.32.22-24 \|\|

*brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṅganāgamaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā taiścāpi saṃsargaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ kāmakārataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kuryādanaśanaṃ vipraḥ puṇyatīrthe samāhitaḥ \|*  
*jvalantaṃ vā viśedagniṃ dhyātvā devaṃ kapardinam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*na hyanyā niṣkṛtirdṛṣṭā munibhirdharmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*tasmāt puṇyeṣu tīrtheṣu dahed vāpi svadehakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. The committor of heinous sins like brahmahatya, drinking of wine, stealing gold, or enjoying sex with the preceptor’s wife, or contact with the sinners of these crimes, should observe fasts. In case he is a Brahmana, then he should perform repentance of his own will. In case he commits a grave sin, then a Brahmana should go to a holy place and perform fasting with a pure mind. Otherwise, he should adore lord Shiva with the matted locks of hair, and enter into the burning fire. The religious-minded sages have prescribed no other remedy except one stated above, for getting him purified of such a sin. Therefore, by burning their bodies in the auspicious fires, the purification must be obtained.

## Chapter 33. Rules for repentance

## \|\| 2.33.1 \|\|

*gatvā duhitaraṃ vipraḥ svasāraṃ vā snuṣāmapi \|*  
*praviśejjvalanaṃ dīptaṃ matipūrvamiti sthitiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. When a Brahmana indulges in sexual intercourse with his own daughter, sister or daughter-in-law, then he should enter the burning flames.

## \|\| 2.33.2 \|\|

*mātṛṣvasāṃ mātulānīṃ tathaiva ca pitṛṣvasām \|*  
*bhāgineyīṃ samāruhya kuryāt kṛcchrātikṛcchrakau \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Similarly, when he commits the same sin with his own mother’s sister, wife of the maternal uncle, father’s sister, or the sister’s daughter, then he should perform the Krchha and Atikrchha-vrata.

## \|\| 2.33.3 \|\|

*cāndrāyaṇaṃ ca kurvota tasya pāpasya śāntaye \|*  
*dhyāyan devaṃ jagadyonimanādinidhanaṃ param \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Or otherwise, for the removal of the related sin, he should observe the Candrayana vow meditating on lord Visnu, who happens to be origin of the universe, and is beyond the beginning or the end.

## \|\| 2.33.4 \|\|

*bhrātṛbhāryāṃ samāruhya kuryāt tatpāpaśāntaye \|*  
*cāndrāyaṇāni catvāri pañca vā susamāhitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In case one has intercourse with the brother’s wife, he should with great concentration perfonn four or five Candrayana vratas.

## \|\| 2.33.5 \|\|

*paitṛṣvastreyīṃ gatvā tu svastreyāṃ mātureva ca \|*  
*mātulasya sutāṃ vāpi gatvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Similarly, after having sex with the daughter of the father’s sister, sister’s daughter, the daughter of the mother’s sister, or the daughter of the maternal uncle, then he should as a repentance perform Candrayana vrata.

## \|\| 2.33.6 \|\|

*sakhibhāryāṃ samāruhya gatvā śyālīṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ahorātroṣito bhūtvā taptakṛcchraṃ samācaret \|\| 6 \|\|*
