67-68. I Unite with Prakrti, the twentyfifth Principle known as Purusa. That pure, omnipresent, immovable, unborn god in union with her Prakrti creates this whole universe from Prakrti which is his own form. He is the illustrious god Brahma, of the form of the Universe, the grandsire of the world.

## \|\| 2.35.69 \|\|

*eko 'haṃ bhagavān kalo hyanādiścāntakṛd vibhuḥ \|*  
*samāsthāya paraṃ bhāvaṃ prokto rudro manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. I have narrated to you the method of the creation by the supreme soul. Only, I am the sole lord in the form of Kala, who being eternal, brings to an end of all the living beings.

## \|\| 2.35.70 \|\|

*mama vai sāparā śaktirdevī vidyeti viśrutā \|*  
*dṛṣṭā hi bhavatā nūnaṃ vidyādehastvahaṃ tataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. While creating and destroying, I assume the greatest fonn, which has been called as Rudra by the sages. This goddess is known as Vidya and happens to be my own Para-Shakti (Potency).

## \|\| 2.35.71 \|\|

*evametāni tattvāni pradhānapuruṣeśvarāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇurbrahmā ca bhagavān rudraḥ kāla iti śrutiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. You have yourself witnessed her body having the form of Vidya. So also these principles the Pradhana, the Purusa, and the Is'vara.

## \|\| 2.35.72 \|\|

*trayametadanādyantaṃ brahmaṇyeva vyavasthitam \|*  
*tadātmakaṃ tadavyaktaṃ tadakṣaramiti śrutiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Visnu, Brahma, and Rudra are Kala. These are the words of Sruti. All the three of them are without beginning or end, besides being the form of Brahman.

## \|\| 2.35.73-74 \|\|

*ātmānandaparaṃ tattvaṃ cinmātraṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*ākāśaṃ niṣkalaṃ brahma tasmādanyanna vidyate \|\| 73 \|\|*

*evaṃ vijñāya bhavatā bhaktiyogāśrayeṇa tu \|*  
*saṃpūjyo vandanīyo 'haṃ tatastaṃ paśya śāśvatam \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. Sruti says, “He is unmanifest, imperishable and undecaying. He is blissful, the supreme principle, the knowledge, and consciousness, besides being the greatest region. He is also Brahma, the form of sky. There is nothing beyond him. He should be known by all the means making special efforts taking refuge with hhakti-yoga. I am adorable for you. By this way, you will be able to have an audience with Is'vara.”

## \|\| 2.35.75-76 \|\|

*etāvaduktvā bhagavāñjagāmādarśanaṃ haraḥ \|*  
*tatraiva bhaktiyogena rudrāmārādhayanmuniḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*etat pavitramatulaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmarṣisevitam \|*  
*saṃsevya brāhmaṇo vidvān mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. Thus speaking, lord Shiva disappeared from the scene. The great sages continue to adore lord Shiva with devotion at that very same place. This is the unique and sacred tirtha which is served by the ascetics. By serving this place, the learned Brahmanas are freed from all the sins,

## Chapter 36. Description of holy places

## \|\| 2.36.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*anyat pavitraṃ vipulaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*rudrakoṭiriti khyātaṃ rudrasya parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “There is another large and highly sacred tirtha, which is well known in the three worlds. It is known as Rudrakoti, since the same is dedicated to Shiva.

## \|\| 2.36.2 \|\|

*purā puṇyatame kāle devadarśanatatparāḥ \|*  
*koṭibrahmarṣayo dāntāstaṃ deśamagaman param \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. During some auspicious ancient time, crores of great Rishis, reached there to have an audience with lord Rudra.

## \|\| 2.36.3 \|\|

*ahaṃ drakṣyāmi giriśaṃ pūrvameva pinākinam \|*  
*anyo 'nyaṃ bhaktiyuktānāṃ vyāghāto jāyate kila \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Reaching there, a controversy developed among them for having first the audience with Lord Girisa.

## \|\| 2.36.4 \|\|

*teṣāṃ bhaktiṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā giriśo yogināṃ guruḥ \|*  
*koṭirūpo 'bhavad rudro rudrakoṭistataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Observing their devotion, the Lord of mountains, the preceptor of the Yogins, took to crores of fonns (and had an audience with all of them individually) as a result of which the place came to be known as Rudrakoti tirtha.

## \|\| 2.36.5 \|\|

*te sma sarve mahādevaṃ haraṃ giriguhāśayam \|*  
*paśyantaḥ pārvatīnāthaṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭadhiyo 'bhavan \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. All of them had a look at lord Shiva, living in a mountain, the consort of Parvati, at one and the same time, as a result of which all those Brahmanas developed the auspicious wisdom.

## \|\| 2.36.6 \|\|

*anādyantaṃ mahādevaṃ pūrvamevāhamīśvaram \|*  
*dṛṣṭavāniti bhaktyā te rudranyastadhiyo 'bhavan \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Lord Mahadeva is without beginning or end. Each one of them thought that Shiva “who is beyond the beginning or end” was seen by him first. As a result of this, all of them dedicated their minds unto Rudra.

## \|\| 2.36.7 \|\|

*athāntarikṣe vimalaṃ paśyanti sma mahattaram \|*  
*jyotistatraiva te sarve 'bhilaṣantaḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereafter, they spotted a spotless flame in the sky. Merging in the same flame, they achieved the heaven.

## \|\| 2.36.8 \|\|

*etat sadeśādhyuṣitaṃ tīrthaṃ puṇyatamaṃ śubham \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rudraṃ samabhyarcya rudrasāmīpyamāpnuyāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This is the reason that lord Rudra stayed there. Because of this, the said tirtha is quite auspicious and meritorious. By visiting this place and adoring him there, a devotee achieves the vicinity of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.36.9 \|\|

*anyacca tīrthapravaraṃ nāmnā madhuvanaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*tatra gatvā niyamavānindrasyārdhāsanaṃ labhet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is another auspicious tirtha, known by the name of Madhuvana. A person who reaching there leads a disciplined life, achieves half the throne of Indra.

## \|\| 2.36.10 \|\|

*athānyatpuṣpanagarī deśaḥ puṇyatamaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*tatra gatvā pitṝn pūjya kulānāṃ tārayecchatam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Besides this, there is another auspicious tirtha known by the name of PadmanagrI. One who reaching there adores the manes, he redeems a hundred members of his race.

## \|\| 2.36.11 \|\|

*kālañjaraṃ mahātīrthaṃ loke rudro maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*kālaṃ jaritavān devo yatra bhaktipriyo haraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There is a great tirtha in Rudraloka known by the name of Kalanjara. Нага is fond of the devotees who worship lod Kalanjara.

## \|\| 2.36.12 \|\|

*śveto nāma śive bhakto rājarṣipravaraḥ purā \|*  
*tadāśīstannamaskāraḥ pūjayāmāsa śūlinam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In ancient times, a saintly king, a devotee of Shiva named Sveta, who with the blessings of Shiva, used to adore lord Shiva, the bearer of the trident.

## \|\| 2.36.13 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya vidhinā liṅgaṃ bhaktiyogapuraḥ saraḥ \|*  
*jajāpa rudramaniśaṃ tatra saṃnyastamānasaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He, with all the devotion, consecrated the Shivalinga there. Thereafter, he devoting his mind to Shiva, recited the Rudramantra.

## \|\| 2.36.14 \|\|

*sa taṃ kālo 'tha dīptātmā śūlamādāya bhīṣaṇam \|*  
*netumabhyāgato deśaṃ sa rājā yatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereafter, the time of death of the king arrived. In order to lead the king to Yamaloka, the god of death, Kala, arrived, holding a trident in his hand.

## \|\| 2.36.15 \|\|

*vīkṣya rājā bhayāviṣṭaḥ śūlahastaṃ samāgatam \|*  
*kālaṃ kālakaraṃ ghoraṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ caṇḍadīdhitim \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then the king Sveta, finding the god of death in the terrific form, holding a trident in his hand, was terrified.

## \|\| 2.36.16 \|\|

*ubābhyāmatha hastābhyāṃ spṛṭvāsau liṅgamaiśvaram \|*  
*nanāma śirasā rudraṃ jajāpa śatarudriyam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the king touched Shivalinga with both the hands, bowed in reverence before lord Rudra, reciting the Satarudrlya stotra at the same time.

## \|\| 2.36.17 \|\|

*japantamāha rājānaṃ namantamasakṛd bhavam \|*  
*ehyehīti puraḥ sthitvā kṛtāntaḥ prahasanniva \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Standing in front of the king, Krtanta (God of Death), laughingly said to the king, who' was performing the Japa of Bhava, “You come away, you come away.”

## \|\| 2.36.18 \|\|

*tamuvāca bhayāviṣṭo rājā rudraparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*ekamīśārcanarataṃ vihāyānyaṃ niṣūdaya \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The king who was devoted to Rudra, getting terrified, said to Yama, “You leave me since, I am engaged in the worshipping of Shiva, and carry the other people with you and destroy them.

## \|\| 2.36.19 \|\|

*ityuktavantaṃ bhagavānabravīd bhītamānasam \|*  
*rudrārcanarato vānyo madvaśe ko na tiṣṭhati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then, lord Kala, spoke to the terrified king. Whether he is engaged in the devotion of Rudra or anyone else, who is not overpowered by me?”

## \|\| 2.36.20 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa rājānaṃ kālo lokaprakālanaḥ \|*  
*babandha pāśai rājāpi jajāpa śatarudriyam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thus speaking, Yama bound the king with his noose, but the king continued to recite the Satarudrlya stotra.

## \|\| 2.36.21 \|\|

*athāntarikṣe vimalaṃ dīpyamānaṃ*  
*tejorāśiṃ bhūtabhartuḥ purāṇam \|*  
*jvālāmālāsaṃvṛtaṃ vyāpya viśvaṃ*  
*prādurbhūtaṃ saṃsthitaṃ saṃdadarśa \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then the king Sveta, witnessed the great lustre of lord Shiva, lord of the goblins, adorned with the garlands of flames, which pervaded the entire universe.

## \|\| 2.36.22 \|\|

*tanmadhye 'sau puruṣaṃ rukmavarṇaṃ*  
*devyā devaṃ candralekhojjvalāṅgam \|*  
*tejorūpaṃ paśyati smātihṛṣṭo*  
*mene cāsmannātha āgacchatīti \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He witnessed lord Mahadeva, in the lustre adorned with the digit of the moon over the head, illumining at the same time and accompanied by the goddess. The king was immensely pleased by looking at him and realised the arrival of the lord.

## \|\| 2.36.23 \|\|

*āgacchantaṃ nātidūre 'tha dṛṣṭvā*  
*kālo rudraṃ devadevyā maheśam \|*  
*vyapetabhīrakhileśaikanāthaṃ*  
*rājarṣistaṃ netumabhyājagāma \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Finding Rudra, the lord of everything, walking with goddess, at a distance near to him, the god of death remained unmoved and tried to carry the great king with him in the presence of lord Shiva. The royal sage became free from fear.

## \|\| 2.36.24 \|\|

*ālokyāsau bhagavānugrakarmā*  
*devo rudro bhūtabhartā purāṇaḥ \|*  
*ekaṃ bhaktaṃ matparaṃ māṃ smarantaṃ*  
*dehītīmaṃ kālamūce mameti \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Observing this, Shiva, the lord of the living beings, spoke to the god of death, “You give away my devotee, who is reciting my name.” The devotee who remembers me, О Kala, he remembers my form.

## \|\| 2.36.25 \|\|

*śrutvā vākhyaṃ gopaterugrabhāvaḥ*  
*kālātmāsau manyamānaḥ svabhāvam \|*  
*baddhvā bhaktaṃ punarevātha pāśaiḥ*  
*kruddho rudramabhidudrāva vegāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Listening to the words of lord Shiva, the god of death, because of his nature being horrible, bound the devotee of Shiva in the noose again and in anger he rushed towards lord Shiva.

## \|\| 2.36.26 \|\|

*prekṣyāyāntaṃ śailaputrīmatheśaḥ*  
*so 'nvīkṣyānte viśvamāyāvidhijñaḥ \|*  
*sāvajñaṃ vai vāmapādena mṛtyuṃ*  
*śvetasyainaṃ paśyato vyājaghāna \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Finding the advance of the god of death, lord Shiva, looked at Parvati, the daughter of the mountain, and kicked him with his left foot, while king Sveta was looking on.

## \|\| 2.36.27 \|\|

*mamāra so 'tibhīṣaṇo maheśapādaghātitaḥ \|*  
*rarāja devatāpatiḥ sahomayā pinākadhṛk \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. With the kicking by lord Shiva, the awful Kaladeva, was killed and the pinaka-bearing lord Shiva looked graecful with the goddess Uma.

## \|\| 2.36.28 \|\|

*nirīkṣya devamīśvaraṃ prahṛṣṭamānaso haram \|*  
*nanāma sāmbamavyayaṃ sa rājapuṅgavastadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The king Sveta felt delighted at the sight of lord Shiva. Offering his salutation to Shiva, he started eulogising him.

## \|\| 2.36.29 \|\|

*namo bhavāya hetave harāya viśvasaṃbhave \|*  
*namaḥ śivāya dhīmate namo 'pavargadāyine \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He said, “Salutation to Bhava, the cause of the world. Salutation to Нага and the form of welfare for the world. Salutation to the learned Shiva, Salutation to the bestower of salvation.

## \|\| 2.36.30 \|\|

*namo namo namo 'stu te mahāvibhūtaye namaḥ \|*  
*vibhāgahīnarūpiṇe namo narādhipāya te \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Salutation to the one whose body is besmeared with ashes and the possessor of all the fortunes. You have the undivided form, You are lord of the humans, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.36.31 \|\|

*namo 'stu te gaṇeśvara prapannaduḥ khanāśana \|*  
*anādinityabhūtaye varāhaśṛṅgadhāriṇe \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. You are the lord of all the Ganas, remover of the pain of those who take refuge in you. Saluation to you. You are without beginning, everlasting, possessor of all the fortunes, and carry the hom of a boar, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.36.32 \|\|

*namo vṛṣadhvajāya te kapālamāline namaḥ \|*  
*namo mahānaṭāya te namo vṛṣadhvajāya te \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Salutation to the bull-bannered Lord. О wearing the garlands of skulls, salutation to you. О Great lord of mountain, salutation to you. Salutation to lord Shiva, the bestower of welfare.”

## \|\| 2.36.33 \|\|

*athānugṛhya śaṅkaraḥ praṇāmatatparaṃ nṛpam \|*  
*svagāṇapatyamavyayaṃ sarūpatāmatho dadau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then lord Sankara, showered his grace on him and bestowed on him the position of Ganapati (chief of his ganas) and the indestructible form of his own.

## \|\| 2.36.34 \|\|

*sahomayā sapārṣadaḥ sarājapuṅgavo haraḥ \|*  
*munīśasiddhavanditaḥ kṣaṇādadṛśyatāmagāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then lord Shiva with Parvati, accompanied with the king Sveta, having been adored by the Rishis and the Siddhas, disappeared in a moment.

## \|\| 2.36.35 \|\|

*kāle maheśābhihate lokanāthaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*ayācata varaṃ rudraṃ sajīvo 'yaṃ bhavatviti \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At the destruction of the god of death by Shiva, Brahma, the lord of the lokas, then asked for a boon from Shiva, “The god of death, Kala, should be brought back to life.”

## \|\| 2.36.36 \|\|

*nāsti kaścidapīśāna doṣaleśo vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*kṛtāntasyaiva bhavatā tatkārye viniyojitaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Brahma said, “O Isana, Bull-bannered God, Krtanta, the god of death, is not at all at any fault, because he has been entrusted with this duty of taking away the life of beings by you yourself.”

## \|\| 2.36.37 \|\|

*sa devadevavacanād devadeveśvaro haraḥ \|*  
*tathāstvityāha viśvātmā so 'pi tādṛgvidho 'bhavat \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Listening to the words of Brahma, lord Shiva, the lord of the chief of Devas, said, “Be it so.” The god of death then got back his life.

## \|\| 2.36.38 \|\|

*ityetat paramaṃ tīrthaṃ kālañjaramiti śrutam \|*  
*gatvābhyarcya mahādevaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ sa vindati \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Therefore this tirtha has been given the name of Kalanjara. A person who adores lord Shiva there, he achieves the position of a Shivagana.

## Chapter 37. Description of holy places

## \|\| 2.37.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*idanamanyate paraṃ sthānaṃ guhyād guhyatamaṃ mahat \|*  
*mahādevasya devasya mahālayamiti śrutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “This is the secret most of all the secret places besides being the excellent one. This is the great place of lord Shiva. This has been known as Mahalaya. err wrr 1эттт(тсщ\|

## \|\| 2.37.2 \|\|

*tatra devādidevena rudreṇa tripurāriṇā \|*  
*śilātale padaṃ nyastaṃ nāstikānāṃ nidarśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. At that place, lord Rudra, the enemy of Tripuras, had implanted his foot prints, which remains invisible for the non-believers.

## \|\| 2.37.3 \|\|

*tatra puśupatāḥ śāntā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahāḥ \|*  
*upāsate mahādevaṃ vedādhyayanatatparāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Pasupata people with peaceful minds, applying ashes over their bodies are engaged in the study of the Vedas, adoring lord Shiva at the same time.

## \|\| 2.37.4 \|\|

*snātvā tatra padaṃ śārvaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktipuraḥ saram \|*  
*namaskṛtvātha śirasā rudrasāmīpyamāpnuyāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One who after taking his bath, and reaches this place of lord Sarva, and then offer his salutation in the foot-print of the lord, he achieves the closeness of lord Rudra.

## \|\| 2.37.5 \|\|

*anyacca devadevasya sthānaṃ śaṃbhormahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kedāramiti vikhyātaṃ siddhānāmālayaṃ śubham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is another place of lord Sambhu, the lord of the gods, which is known by the name of Kedara and is the auspicious refuge of the Siddhas.

## \|\| 2.37.6 \|\|

*tatra snātvā mahādevamabhyarcya vṛṣaketanam \|*  
*pītvā caivodakaṃ śuddhaṃ gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By adoring lord Shiva, after taking a bath there and by consuming the spotless water there, one achieve the position of Ganapati.

## \|\| 2.37.7 \|\|

*śrāddhadānādikaṃ kṛtvā hyakṣyaṃ labhate phalam \|*  
*dvijātipravarairjuṣṭaṃ yogibhiryatamānasaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. By perfonning sraddha and charities, one achieves the undecaying reward. This place is served by the people of the three varnas besides the Yogins who have controlled their sense organs.

## \|\| 2.37.8 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ plakṣāvataraṇaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*tatrābhyarcya śrīnivāsaṃ viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There is a tirtha known as Plaksavatarana, which removes all types of sins. By worshipping lord Srinivasa (Visnu) there, a person achieves Visnuloka, where he is adored.

## \|\| 2.37.9 \|\|

*anyaṃ magadharājasya tīrthaṃ svargagatipradam \|*  
*akṣayaṃ vindati svargaṃ tatra gatvā dvijottamaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is another tirtha known by the name of Magadharanya which provides access in all the lokas. By reaching there, a Brahmana achieves the everlasting heaven.

## \|\| 2.37.10 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ kanakhalaṃ puṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*yatra devena rudreṇa yajño dakṣasya nāśitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The tirtha known as Kanakhala is quite auspicious and removes the grave impurities. This is the place, where lord Rudradeva had destroyed the yajna of Daksa prajapati.

## \|\| 2.37.11 \|\|

*tatra gaṅgāmupaspṛśya śucirbhāvasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpaistu brahmalokaṃ labhenmṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By taking a bath there in the holy Ganga, getting purified, filled with devotion, he is relieved of all the sins and then he resides in the Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.37.12 \|\|

*mahātīrthamiti khyātaṃ puṇyaṃ nārāyaṇapriyam \|*  
*tatrābhyarcya hṛṣīkeśaṃ śvetadvīpaṃ nigacchati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There is another tirtha known as Mahatirtha, which is extremely auspicious and is very much liked by lord Narayana. By adoring lord Hrslkes'a there, a person moves on to Svetadvipa.

## \|\| 2.37.13 \|\|

*anyacca tīrthapravaraṃ nāmnā śrīparvataṃ śubham \|*  
*tatra prāṇān parityajya rudrasya dayito bhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There is another place which is considered to be the best of all the tirthas and is known as Srlparvata. In case a person meets with his end here, he becomes quite dear to lord Rudra.

## \|\| 2.37.14 \|\|

*tatra sannihito rudro devyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*snānapiṇḍādikaṃ tatra kṛtamakṣayyamuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Lord Rudra lives there with the goddess Parvati. By taking a bath at this place and performing the pindadana there, (it becomes immensely meritorious) and the money given in charities there multiplies immensely.

## \|\| 2.37.15 \|\|

*godāvarī nadī puṇyā sarvapāpavināśanī \|*  
*tatra snātvā pitṝn devāṃstarpayitvā yathāvidhi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. There is an auspicious river known as Godavari, which removes all the sins. By having a bath in this river, one should offer pindas to the gods as well as the manes in an appropriate manner. By doing so, a person, getting his soul purified, earns the merit of donating a thousand cows.

## \|\| 2.37.16-17 \|\|

*sarvapāpavisuddhātmā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*pavitrasalilā puṇyā kāverī vipulā nadī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ snātvodakaṃ kṛtvā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*trirātropoṣitenātha ekarātroṣitena vā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The river Kaverl, having the auspicious water is quite meritorious. By taking a bath in it and offering the oblation of water to the manes, when a person fasts for three nights or atleast one night, he is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.37.18 \|\|

*dvijātīnāṃ tu kathitaṃ tīrthānāmiha sevanam \|*  
*yasya vāṅmanaso śuddhe hastapādau ca saṃsthitau \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. These are the words spoken by the people of the three varnas. Those having the spotless mind and speech, with healthy hands and feet, should visit this place. A person who is not greedy, is a celibate, only he can have the best reward for visiting the holy places.

## \|\| 2.37.19-20 \|\|

*alolupo brahmacāro tīrthānāṃ phalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*svāmitīrthaṃ mahātīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tatra sannihito nityaṃ skando 'maranamaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*snātvā kumāradhārāyāṃ kṛtvā devāditarpaṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Svamitirtha is also a great tirtha. It is well known in the three worlds. Lord Skanda, being adored by all the immortal beings, always resides there. By taking a bath in the Kumaradhara river there, one should offer oblation to the gods and the manes. The one who adores the god with six heads, Sanmukha, he enjoys all the pleasures with lord Skanda.

## \|\| 2.37.21-22 \|\|

*ārādhya ṣaṇmukhaṃ devaṃ skandena saha modate \|*  
*nadī trailokyavikhyātā tāmraparṇoti nāmataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā pitṝn bhaktyā tarpayitvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*pāpakartṝnapi pitṝstārayennātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The river of Tamraparn! is well known in the three worlds. By taking a bath there, and performing oblation to the Pitrs with devotion (one achieves great merit). Even the sinful Pitrs are redeemed. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.37.23 \|\|

*candratīrthamiti khyātaṃ kāveryāḥ prabhave 'kṣayam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ tatra bhaved vastuṃ mṛtānāṃ svargatirdhruvā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. At the place of origin of the river Kaveri, there is a tirtha named Candratirtha, which is also known as the Aksayatirtha. The donations given at that place, provides everlsating benefits and yields good goal.

## \|\| 2.37.24 \|\|

*vindhyapāde prapaśyanti devadevaṃ sadāśivam \|*  
*bhaktyā ye te na paśyanti yamasya sadanaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Those who have an audience with Sadas'iva at the Vindhyapada mountain, and those who are devoted to Shiva, such Brahmanas never have to face the Yama’s face and they achieve the place of Shiva after their death.

## \|\| 2.37.25 \|\|

*devikāyāṃ vṛṣo nāma tīrthaṃ siddhaniṣevitam \|*  
*tatra snātvodakaṃ datvā yogasiddhiṃ ca vindati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There is a Vrsa-tirtha in the Devika region, which is served by the Siddhas. By taking a bath at that place, performing the oblation for the gods and the manes, a person achieves success in Yoga.

## \|\| 2.37.26 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhikaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ tatrāpnoti phalaṃ naraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The tirtha named Dasasvamedhika is the destroyer of all the sins. By taking a bath at that place, a person achieves merits for performing ten Asvamedha sacrifices.

## \|\| 2.37.27 \|\|

*puṇḍarīkaṃ mahātīrthaṃ brāhmaṇairupasevitam \|*  
*tatrābhigamya yuktātmā pauṇḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There is a tirtha known as Pundarlka which is graced by the Brahmanas visiting that place, a person of self-control approaching it, achieves the merit of Pundarika-yajna.

## \|\| 2.37.28 \|\|

*tīrthebhyaḥ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmatīrthamiti śrutam \|*  
*brahmāṇamarcayitvā tu brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Brahmatirtha is considered to be the best of all the tirthas. A person who adores lord Brahma there, he after his death, reaches the place of Brahma and is well established there.

## \|\| 2.37.29-30 \|\|

*sarasvatyā vinaśanaṃ plakṣaprastravaṇaṃ śubham \|*  
*vyāsatīrthaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ mainākaṃ ca nagottamam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yamunāprabhavaṃ caiva sarvapāpaviśodhanam \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ duhitā devī gandhakālīti viśrutā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Similarly on the banks of the river Sarasvati, the tirthas known as Vinasana, Plaksa- prasravana, and Vyasatirtha are quite well known. There is also a mountain known by the name of Mainaka.

## \|\| 2.37.31 \|\|

*tasyāṃ snātvā divaṃ yāti mṛto jātismaro bhavet \|*  
*kuberatuṅgaṃ pāpaghnaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The place of the origin of the Yamuna too removes all the sins. The river, the goddess Gandhakall, the daughter of the gods, is quite well known there. By having a bath in it, one surely achieves the heaven and after his death. He is reborn with his earlier birth memories.

The tirtha \[ПW5\] known as Kuberaturiga, removes all the sins, and is served by the Siddhas and the Camnas. By meeting with his end there, a person becomes entitled to serving Kubera as his attendant.

## \|\| 2.37.32-33 \|\|

*prāṇāṃstatra parityajya kuberānucaro bhavet \|*  
*umātuṅgamiti khyātaṃ yatra sā rudravallabhā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tatrābhyarcya mahādevīṃ kosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*bhṛgutuṅge tapastaptaṃ śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ tathā kṛtam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. There is a famous tirtha known as Umatunga, where the spouse of Rudradeva resides. By taking a bath there, a person achieves the merit of donating a thousand cows. The tapas performed in the Bhrgutunga tirtha, removes all the sins. The sraddhas and charities performed there or the performing of the other noble deeds, redeems, seven maternal and paternal generations. This is my opinion.

## \|\| 2.37.34 \|\|

*kulānyubhayataḥ sapta punātīti śrutirmama \|*  
*kāśyapasya mahātīrthaṃ kālasarpiriti śrutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There is a great tirtha dedicated to Kasyapa-the great sage and is known by the name of Kalasarpis-as has been heard. One should perform sraddha, the oblations and charities there for the removal of the sins.

## \|\| 2.37.35 \|\|

*tatra śrāddhāni deyāni nityaṃ pāpakṣayecchayā \|*  
*daśārṇāyāṃ tathā dānaṃ śrāddhaṃ homastathā japaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The sraddha, dana, homa and japam performed at the Das'arna -tirtha, are of everlasting and inexhaustible benefits.

## \|\| 2.37.36 \|\|

*akṣayaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva kṛtaṃ bhavati sarvadā \|*  
*tīrthaṃ dvijātibhirjuṣṭaṃ nāmnā vai kurujāṅgalam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The tirtha known as Kumjangala, is served by the people of the three varnas. A person who performs the charities there appropriately, he ultimately reaches Brahmaloka, where he is immensely respected.

## \|\| 2.37.37-38 \|\|

*dattvā tu dānaṃ vidhivad brahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*vaitaraṇyāṃ mahātīrthe svarṇavedyāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dharmapṛṣṭhe ca sarasi brahmaṇaḥ parame śubhe \|*  
*bharatasyāśrame puṇye puṇye śrāddhavaṭe śubhe \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. There are tirthas named VaitaranI, besides Svaranavedi, Dharmaprstha, Brahmatirtha, the auspicious hermitage of Bharata, the auspicious Grdhravana, Mahahrada, which are located over the KausikI river, and the charities performed at these places are everlasting.

## \|\| 2.37.39-40 \|\|

*mahāhrade ca kauśikyāṃ dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|*  
*muñjapṛṣṭhe padaṃ nyastaṃ mahādevena dhīmatā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*hitāya sarvabhūtānāṃ nāstikānāṃ nidarśanam \|*  
*alpenāpi tu kālena naro dharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Lord Mahadeva had established his foot at a tirtha named Mundaprstha. It is for the welfare of all and a proof for the non-believers. A person becomes well-versed in dharma here in a short time. As a serpent removes its skin, similarly all the sins of a person are removed there.

## \|\| 2.37.41-42 \|\|

*pāpmānamutsṛjatyāśu jīrṇāṃ tvacamivoragaḥ \|*  
*nāmnā kanakanandeti tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*udīcyāṃ muñjapṛṣṭhasya brahmarṣigaṇasevitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti saśarīrā dvijātayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. There is a great tirtha named Kanakananda which is well known in the three worlds. The tirtha named Brahmaprstha in the north is served by the BrahmaRishis. In case the people of the three varnas take bath here, they achieve the heaven with their physical bodies.

## \|\| 2.37.43 \|\|

*dattaṃ cāpi sadā śrāddhamakṣayaṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*ṛṇaistribhirnaraḥ snātvā mucyate kṣīṇakalmaṣaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The charities and sraddha performed in this tirtha are always undecaying. A person by taking a bath in this tirtha becomes free from the debts of the gods, Pitrs and the Rishis. Besides he is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.37.44 \|\|

*mānase sarasi snātvā śakrasyārdhāsanaṃ labhet \|*  
*uttaraṃ mānasaṃ gatvā siddhiṃ prāpnotyanuttamām \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Similarly by having a bath in the Manasarovara, one achieves half the throne of Indradeva. By reaching Uttara-manasa, a person achieves the best of Siddhis.

## \|\| 2.37.45 \|\|

*tasmānnirvartayecchrāddhaṃ yathāśakti yathābalam \|*  
*kāmān salabhate divyān mokṣopāyaṃ ca vindati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Therefore, one should perform there the sraddha as per his means. The performer of such a sraddha has his divine desires fulfilled, besides becoming aware of the means for achieving liberation.

## \|\| 2.37.46 \|\|

*parvato himavānnāma nānādhātuvibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi so 'śītistvāyato giriḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. There is a huge mountain known by the name of Himavan in which are enshrined several types of metals. This mountain is spread in an area of eighty thousand yojanas.

## \|\| 2.37.47 \|\|

*siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇo devarṣigaṇasevitaḥ \|*  
*tatra puṣkariṇī ramyā suṣumnā nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. This mountain is the abode of the Siddhas and Caranas. It is also being served by the sages. There is an extremely charming river known by the name of PuskamI, also known as Susumna.

## \|\| 2.37.48 \|\|

*tatra gatvā dvijo vidvān brahmahatyāṃ vimuñcati \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ bhavati cākṣayyaṃ tatra dattaṃ mahodayam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The learned Brahmanas reaching there are relieved of the sin of brahmahatya even. The sraddha performed there is all time rewarding and highly flourishing.

## \|\| 2.37.49 \|\|

*tārayecca pitṝn samyag daśa pūrvān daśāparān \|*  
*sarvatra himavān puṇyo gaṅgā puṇyā samantataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A person by performing the sraddha here, redeems his past as well the coming ten generations. As the Himavan mountain is always auspicious, similarly the holy Ganga is quite auspicious everywhere.

## \|\| 2.37.50 \|\|

*nadyaḥ samudragāḥ puṇyāḥ samudraśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*badaryāśramamāsādya mucyate kalikalmaṣāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. All the rivers flowing towards the ocean are auspicious, while the ocean is particularly meritorious. By reaching Badaryasrama, a person is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.37.51 \|\|

*tatra nārāyaṇo devo nareṇāste sanātanaḥ \|*  
*akṣayaṃ tatra dānaṃ syāt japyaṃ vāpi tathāvidham \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The eternal gods Nara and Narayana are lodged there. Whosoever, performs chartities in Badrinatha Dhama, or the sraddha performed by the people, become immensely rewarding.

## \|\| 2.37.52 \|\|

*mahādevapriyaṃ tīrthaṃ pāvanaṃ tad viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tārayecca pitṝn sarvān dattvā śrāddhaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. This tirtha is particularly like by Mahadeva. It is very auspicious. In case some one performs sraddha there with a devoted mind, he redeems all his pitrs.

## \|\| 2.37.53 \|\|

*devadāruvanaṃ puṇyaṃ siddhagandharvasevitam \|*  
*mahādevena devena tatra dattaṃ mahad varaṃ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. There is a holy centre Devadaruvana in which the Siddhas and Gandharvas are living. Lord Mahesvara, the god of gods is also found there. Whatever is offered there is highly rewarding.

## \|\| 2.37.54-55 \|\|

*mohayitvā munīn sarvān punastaiḥ saṃprapūjitaḥ \|*  
*prasanno bhagavānīśo munīndrān prāha bhāvitān \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ihāśramavare ramye nivasiṣyatha sarvadā \|*  
*madbhāvanāsamāyuktāstataḥ siddhimavāpsyatha \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Lord Shiva was appropriately adored by the sages there, because of which, He felt extremely happy. Then Ishvara said to the sages who have been sanctified, “All of you shall live in this beautiful asrama. By my grace, all of you shall achieve Siddhi.

## \|\| 2.37.56 \|\|

*ye 'tra māmarcayantīha loke dharmaparā janāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ dadāmi paramaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ hi śāśvatam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Becoming religious-minded here, whoever shall adore me, I shall always bestow to him, the everlasting position of Ganapati.

## \|\| 2.37.57 \|\|

*atra nityaṃ vasiṣyāmi saha nārāyaṇena ca \|*  
*prāṇāniha narastyaktvā na bhūyo janma vindati \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. I shall live here with lord Narayana always. The people who meet with their death here, are never reborn on earth.

## \|\| 2.37.58 \|\|

*saṃsmaranti ca ye tīrthaṃ deśāntaragatā janāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ ca sarvapāpāni nāśayāmi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Such of the people, in other countries, who keep on recalling this place, О Best of Brahmanas, I shall also destroy all their sins.

## \|\| 2.37.59 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ tapo homaḥ piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*dhyānaṃ japaśca niyamaḥ sarvamatrākṣayaṃ kṛtam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The sraddha, dana (charities), tapas, homa and pindadana performed here, become everlasting.

## \|\| 2.37.60 \|\|

*tasmāt sarvaprayatnena draṣṭavyaṃ hi dvijātibhiḥ \|*  
*devadāruvanaṃ puṇyaṃ mahādevaniṣevitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Therefore, the people of the three varnas making all the efforts, should surely visit this holy place of Devadaruvana. This forest of the pine trees is inhabited by lord Mahesa.

## \|\| 2.37.61 \|\|

*yatresvaro mahādevo viṣṇurvā puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*tatra sannihitā gaṅgātīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Wherever Lord Mahadeva, and lord (Purusottama-Visnu) remains, the rivers like Ganga, the holy centres and the shrines are also present there.

## Chapter 38. Entry in the Daruvana

## \|\| 2.38.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ dāruvanaṃ prāpto bhagavān govṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*mohayāmāsa viprendrān sūta vaktumihārhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said, “О Suta, How did lord Shiva, the bull-bannered one, fascinated the leading Brahmanas, while entering into the Daruvana (pinewood)?” You speak out the same.

## \|\| 2.38.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*purā dāruvan ramye devasiddhaniṣevite \|*  
*saputradārā munayastapaśceruḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suta said- Earlier, in the beautiful Daruvana resorted to be Devas and Siddhas, thousands of sages performed penance and lived along with their wives, sons, and other kinsmen.

## \|\| 2.38.3 \|\|

*pravṛttaṃ vividhaṃ karma prakurvāṇā yathāvidhi \|*  
*yajanti vividhairyajñaistapanti ca maharṣayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. They were engaged in doing various religious rites in accordance with the scriptural injunctions. The great sages performed various sacrifices and penances there.

## \|\| 2.38.4 \|\|

*teṣāṃ pravṛttivinyastacetasāmatha śūladhṛk \|*  
*khyāpayan sa mahādoṣaṃ yayau dāruvanaṃ haraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thus their minds were devoted to the pointing out of their defects as they were attracted to the path of action. Therefore, the trident-bearing Нага went to Daruvana.

## \|\| 2.38.5 \|\|

*kṛtvā viśvaguruṃ viṣṇuṃ pārśve devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*yayau nivṛttavijñānasthāpanārthaṃ ca śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Accompanied with lord Visnu, the preceptor of the universe, went to that place to enlighten the sages about the NivrttivijMna (the perfect knowledge of renunciation).

## \|\| 2.38.6-8 \|\|

*āsthāya vipulaṃ veśamūnaviṃśativatsaraḥ \|*  
*līlālaso mahābāhuḥ pīnāṅgaścārulocanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*cāmīkaravapuḥ śrīmān pūrṇacandranibhānanaḥ \|*  
*mattamātaṅgagāmano digvāsā jagadīśvaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kuśeśayamayīṃ mālaṃ sarvaratnairalaṅkṛtām \|*  
*dadhāno bhagavānīśaḥ samāgacchati sasmitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Then he took to the form of a twenty years old person. He playfully took to the form of a well built person having long arms, beautiful eyes, gold complexion, the face having the lustre of the moon, who could walk gracefully like an elephant, and was without clothes. He was wearing a garland of gold studded with gems and a serene smile was present on his face.

## \|\| 2.38.9 \|\|

*yo 'nantaḥ puruṣo yonirlokānāmavyayo hariḥ \|*  
*strīveṣaṃ viṣṇurāsthāya so 'nugacchati śūlinam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Besides lord Visnu, the creator of the universe, the infinite Purusa, followed lord Shiva, in the form of a woman.

## \|\| 2.38.10-12 \|\|

*sampūrṇacandravadanaṃ pīnonnatapayodharam \|*  
*śucismitaṃ suprasannaṃ raṇannupurakadvayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*supītavasanaṃ divyaṃ śyāmalaṃ cārulocanam \|*  
*udārahaṃsacalanaṃ vilāsi sumanoharam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*evaṃ sa bhagavānīśo devadāruvane haraḥ \|*  
*cacāra hariṇā bhikṣāṃ māyayā mohayan jagat \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. The face of lord Visnu in the form of a woman was delightful, resembling the full moon, the breasts plump and elevated, face lit up with bright smiles, and the anklets wore in the ankles were issuing gingling sound. She was clad in divine yellow garments, having beautiful eyes, and moves like the swan. She looked quite beautiful. Thus lord Shiva confused the entire world with his Maya accompanied with Visnu in the form of a woman and entered in the Daruvana.

## \|\| 2.38.13 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā carantaṃ viśveśaṃ tatra tatra pinākinam \|*  
*māyayā mohitā nāryo devadevaṃ samanvayuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Finding the wandering of Pinaka-bearing lord of the universe, the damsels of the forest were overpowered with the Maya of Shiva, who also started following the lord.

## \|\| 2.38.14 \|\|

*vistrastavastrābharaṇāstyaktvā lajjāṃ pativratāḥ \|*  
*sahaiva tena kāmārtā vilāsinyaścarantihi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The chaste woman of them shedding av/ay the shyness, were filled with passion and their costumes got disarranged. They also started wandering with Shiva getting passionate.

## \|\| 2.38.15 \|\|

*ṛṣīṇāṃ putrakā ye syuryuvāno jitamānasāḥ \|*  
*anvagacchan hṛṣīkeśaṃ sarve kāmaprapīḍitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The sons of the Rishis who had not yet controlled their sense organs, also became passionate and started wandering, following lord Hrsikesa in the form of a woman.

## \|\| 2.38.16 \|\|

*gāyanti nṛtyanti vilāsabāhyā*  
*nārīgaṇā māyinamekamīśam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sapatnīkamatīvakānta-*  
*micchantyathāliṅganamācaranti \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus, the ladies becoming passionate started singing the glory of lord Shiva-the unique actor, and dancing at the same time in their sportive dalliance. They being desirous of the husband, sometimes even embraced lord Shiva.

## \|\| 2.38.17 \|\|

*pade nipetuḥ smitamācaranti*  
*gāyanti gītāni munīśaputrāḥ \|*  
*ālokya padmāpatimādidevaṃ*  
*bhrūbhaṅgamanye vicaranti tena \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The sons of the sages as well, observing Visnu, the consort of Padma, of auspicious limbs, in the form of a woman, started singing with smiles on their faces. Some other sons of the sages started walking around with him.

## \|\| 2.38.18 \|\|

*āsāmathaiṣāmapi vāsudevo*  
*māyī murārirmanasi praviṣṭaḥ \|*  
*karoti bhogān manasi pravṛttiṃ*  
*māyānubhūyanta itiva samyak \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The illusory lord Narayana, the slayer of Mura, the son of Vasudeva, entering the minds of those men, started attracting them towards the pleasures, as if the pleasures had been well attracted by Maya.

## \|\| 2.38.19 \|\|

*vibhāti viśvāmarabhūtabhartā*  
*sa mādhavaḥ strīgaṇamadhyaviṣṭaḥ \|*  
*aśeṣaśaktyāsanasaṃniviṣṭo*  
*yathaikaśaktyā saha devadevaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In this way the women of the world collected around Shiva and lord Visnu. It appeared as if lord Shiva, the lord of the universe and all immortal beings, had appeared there with Parvati (Madhava).

## \|\| 2.38.20 \|\|

*karoti nṛtyaṃ paramaprabhāvaṃ*  
*tadā virūḍhaḥ punareva bhūyaḥ \|*  
*yayau samāruhya hariḥ svabhāvaṃ*  
*tadīśavṛttāmṛtamādidevaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. At that point of time, again mounting back, he created the permanent great principle Pradhana. Lord Visnu also re-assumed his original nature (form).

## \|\| 2.38.21 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā nārīkulaṃ rudraṃ putrāṇāmapi keśavam \|*  
*mohayantaṃ muniśreṣṭhāḥ kopaṃ saṃdadhire bhṛśam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then the best of the sages were immensely enraged, on seeing the groups of women, Rudra, their sons and Kesava who fascinated them.

## \|\| 2.38.22 \|\|

*atīva paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ procurdevaṃ kapardinam \|*  
*śeṣuśca śāpairvividhairmāyayā tasya mohitāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then the sages spoke extremely harsh words to Shiva, having the matted locks of hair over the head and under the influence of Maya, they started pronouncing curses on Shiva.

## \|\| 2.38.23 \|\|

*tapāṃsi teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pratyāhanyanta śaṅkare \|*  
*yathādityaprakāśena tārakā nabhasi sthitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. But all the word spoken by the sages as well as the curses, became infructuous before lord Shiva, in the same as the stars disappear on the rising of the sun.

## \|\| 2.38.24 \|\|

*te bhagnatapaso viprāḥ sametya vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*ko bhavāniti deveśaṃ pṛcchanti sma vimohitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus finding their tapas being of no consequence, the confused sages, went close to the bull-bannered Shiva and asked him, “Who are you, Sir?”

## \|\| 2.38.25 \|\|

*so 'bravīd bhagavānīśastapaścartumihāgataḥ \|*  
*idānīṃ bhāryayā deśe bhavadbhiriha suvratāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. To this, lord Shiva replied, “O Sages of holy rites, presently, I have arrived here with my wife for the performing of tapas in the forest.”

## \|\| 2.38.26 \|\|

*tasya te vākyamākarṇya bhṛgvādyā munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*ūcurgṛhītvā vasanaṃ tyaktvā bhāryāṃ tapaścara \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Listening to their words, Bhrgu and the other best of sages, said to him, “In case you intend to perform penance here, then put on your clothes and discard your wife.”

## \|\| 2.38.27-28 \|\|

*athovāca vihasyeśaḥ pinākī nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*saṃprekṣya jagato yoniṃ pārśvasthaṃ ca janārdanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kathaṃ bhavadbhiruditaṃ svabhāryāpoṣaṇotsukaiḥ \|*  
*tyaktavyā mama bhāryeti dharmajñaiḥ śāntamānasaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Then Shiva, the Pinaka-bearer, having the reddish-blue complexion, smiled and looking at Janardana, the source of the origin of the worlds, said, “Being well aware of your dharma, having the peaceful mind, being engaged in the upkeep of your wives, why have you asked me to disown my wife.”

## \|\| 2.38.29 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*vyabhicāraratā nāryaḥ saṃtyājyāḥ patineritāḥ \|*  
*asmābhireṣā subhagā tādṛśī tyāgamarhati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The Rishis said, “The woman who follow the evil path, and are influenced by others, should be disowned by the husbands. This woman is not of a noble character. Therefore you will have to get rid of this woman.”

## \|\| 2.38.30 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca*  
*na kadācidiyaṃ viprā manasāpyanyamicchati \|*  
*nāhamenāmapi tathā vimuñcāmi kadācana \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Mahadeva said, “O Brahmanas, this woman is never desirous mentally of anyone else. Nor do I leave her off at any time.”

## \|\| 2.38.31 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*dṛṣṭvā vyabhicarantīha hyasmābhiḥ puruṣādhama \|*  
*uktaṃ hyasatyaṃ bhavatā gamyatāṃ kṣiprameva hi \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Rishis said, “0 degraded person, we have witnessed this woman indulging in evil ways in the forest. You have spoken falsehood. Therefore you leave the place at once.”

## \|\| 2.38.32 \|\|

*evamukte mahādevaḥ satyameva mayeritam \|*  
*bhavatāṃ pratibhātyeṣetyuktvāsau vicacāra ha \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. At these words of the sages, then lord Shiva said, “I have spoken the truth, but you have taken it to be falsehood.” Thus speaking lord Shiva kept on wandering the forest.

## \|\| 2.38.33 \|\|

*so 'gacchaddhariṇā sārdhaṃ munindrasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhasyāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ bhikṣārtho parameśvaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then lord Shiva, accompanied with lord Hari, went to the holy hermitage of the great-souled Vasistha, for begging alms.

## \|\| 2.38.34 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ devaṃ bhikṣamāṇamarundhatī \|*  
*vasiṣṭhasya priyā bhāryā pratyudgamya nanāma nam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Finding the arrival of Shiva, for begging alms, Arundhatl, the beloved wife of Vasistha, came forward and offered her salutation to him.

## \|\| 2.38.35 \|\|

*prakṣālya pādau vimalaṃ dattvā cāsanamuttamam \|*  
*saṃprekṣya śithilaṃ gātramabhighātahataṃ dvijaiḥ \|*  
*saṃdhayāmāsa bhaiṣajyairviṣṇā vadanā satī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then Arundhati- the chaste wife of the sage Vasistha, washed the feet of lord Shiva, and then offered him the auspicious seat for sitting. She found him feeling fatigued because of the attack of the Brahmanas. The chaste Arundhatl, with countenance cast down (due to dejection), then applied medicines over the wounds of lord Shiva.

## \|\| 2.38.36-37 \|\|

*cakāra mahatīṃ pūjāṃ prārthayāmāsa bhāryayā \|*  
*ko bhavān kuta āyātaḥ kimācāro bhavāniti \|*  
*uvāca tāṃ mahādevaḥ siddhānāṃ pravaro 'smyaham \|\| 36 \|\|*

*yadetanmaṇḍalaṃ śuddhaṃ bhāti brahmamayaṃ sadā \|*  
*eṣaiva devatā mahyaṃ dhārayāmi sadaiva tat \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. And she adored him immensely with his wife. She asked him- “Who are you, Sir? Where from have you arrived here with your wife? What are your customs and manners? You tell me.” Then lord Mahadeva replied, “I happen to be the best of the Siddhas and the woman who is spotlessly shining with me is like a god for me. Therefore, I always accompany her.”

## \|\| 2.38.38 \|\|

*hatyuktvā prayayau śrīmānanugṛhya pativratām \|*  
*tāḍayāñcakrire daṇḍairloṣṭibhirmuṣṭibhidvijāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus speaking, lord Shiva, to whom the Brahmanas beat with sticks, stones and lumps of clay, blessed the chaste wonvn Arundhatl, and left the place.

## \|\| 2.38.39 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā carantaṃ giriśaṃ nagnaṃ vikṛtalakṣaṇam \|*  
*procuretad bhavāṃlliṅgamutpāṭayatu durmate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Lord Mahadeva was nude and was in dishevelled condition. Finding him so wandering, the sages said, “O evil-minded one, you uproot your penis and throw it away.”

## \|\| 2.38.40 \|\|

*tānabravīnmahāyogī kariṣyāmīti śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*yuṣmākaṃ māmake liṅge yadi dveṣo 'bhijāyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then lord Sankara, the great Yogin said to them, “In case you are so envious about my phallus, then I shall do as desired by you.”

## \|\| 2.38.41 \|\|

*ityuktvotpāṭayāmāsa bhagavān bhaganetrahā \|*  
*nāpaśyaṃstatkṣaṇeneśaṃ keśavaṃ liṅgameva ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus speaking, lord Shiva, who had removed the eyes of Bhaga, uprooted his linga. But the Brahmanas, at that point of time, could no more find Ishvara, Kesava or the linga as they disappeared instantaneously.

## \|\| 2.38.42 \|\|

*tadotpātā babhūvurhi lokānāṃ bhayaśaṃsinaḥ \|*  
*na rājate sahasrāṃśuścacāla pṛthivī punaḥ \|*  
*niṣprabhāśca grahāḥ sarve cukṣubhe ca mahodadhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. At the same time, evil omens indicating fear and danger started appearing on earth. The lustre of the sun having the thousand rays, disappeared. The earth started shaking. The planets also lost their lustre and the disturbance was created in the ocean.

## \|\| 2.38.43 \|\|

*apaśyaccānusūyātreḥ svapnaṃ bhāryā pativratā \|*  
*kathayāmāsa viprāṇāṃ bhayādākulitekṣaṇā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. At the same time, Anasuya, the chaste wife of the sage Atri, witnessed a dream. Getting frightened, she said to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.38.44 \|\|

*tejasā bhāsayan kṛtsnaṃ nārāyaṇasahāyavān \|*  
*bhikṣamāṇaḥ śivo nūnaṃ dṛṣṭo 'smākaṃ gṛheṣviti \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “Surely, lord Shiva illuminating everything with his lustre, with Narayana had arrived in our abodes for begging alms.”

## \|\| 2.38.45 \|\|

*tasyā vacanamākarṇya śaṅkamānā maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*sarve jagmurmahāyogaṃ brahmāṇaṃ viśvasaṃbhavam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Listening to her words, all the terrified sages went to Brahma of great Yogic power, and the creator of the universe.

## \|\| 2.38.46 \|\|

*upāsyamānamamalairyogibhirbrahmavittamaiḥ \|*  
*caturvedairmūrtimadbhiḥ sāvitryā sahitaṃ prabhum \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. They found Brahma, being adored by the Rishis, well-versed in Brahman, together with Savitrl, the embodied form of four Vedas.

## \|\| 2.38.47 \|\|

*āsīnamāsane ramye nānāścaryasamanvite \|*  
*prabhāsahasrakalile jñānaiśvaryādisaṃyute \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He was seated on a beautiful seat full of surprises, having the lustre of thousands of rays, associated with jnana (perfect knowledge), and the fortunes, besides the others.

## \|\| 2.38.48-49 \|\|

*vibhrājamānaṃ vapuṣā sastitaṃ śubhralocanam \|*  
*caturmukhaṃ mahābāhuṃ chandomayamajaṃ param \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vilokya vedapuruṣaṃ prasannavadanaṃ śubham \|*  
*śirobhirdharaṇīṃ gatvā toṣayāmāsurīśvaram \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. He was having the excellent divine body, looking graceful, wearing the serene smile over the face, having illustrious eyes, long arms, resembling the Vedic metres, unborn, having delightful four-faces. Finding him so seated, all the sages offered their salutation to Brahma, lowering their heads over the ground.

## \|\| 2.38.50 \|\|

*tān prasannamanā devaścaturmūrtiścaturmukhaḥ \|*  
*vyājahāra muniśreṣṭhāḥ kimāgamanakāraṇam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Getting pleased, the four-faced Brahma said, “0 Best of sages, what is the reason of your arrival here?”

## \|\| 2.38.51 \|\|

*tasya te vṛttamakhilaṃ brahmaṇaḥ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*jñāpayāñcakrire sarve kṛtvā śirasi cāñjalim \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then all the sages, joining both the palms in reverence above their heads, narrated the entire factual position to Supreme-souled Brahma.

## \|\| 2.38.52 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kaścid dāruvanaṃ puṇyaṃ puruṣo 'tīvaśobhanaḥ \|*  
*bhāryayā cārusarvāṅgyā praviṣṭo nagna eva hi \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The sages said- “A beautiful, but naked person has entered the Daruvana with a beautiful-limbed wife.

## \|\| 2.38.53 \|\|

*mohayāmāsa vapuṣā nārīṇāṃ kulamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*kanyakānāṃ priyā cāsya dūṣayāmāsa putrakān \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The Lordly person, attracted our wives and the daughters, while his beloved attracted our sons and polluted their minds.

## \|\| 2.38.54 \|\|

*asmābhirvividhāḥ śāpāḥ pradattāśca parāhatāḥ \|*  
*tāḍito 'smābhiratyarthaṃ liṅgantu vinipātitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. We pronounced all types of curses on that person, which proved futile. Then we beat that person severely and made his lingo, to fall down.

## \|\| 2.38.55 \|\|

*antarhitaśca bhagavān sabhāryo liṅgameva ca \|*  
*utpātāścābhavan ghorāḥ sarvabhūtabhayaṅkarāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. But the lord then disappeared with his wife. Since then, frightening disturbances are appearing on the earth.

## \|\| 2.38.56 \|\|

*ka eṣa puruṣo deva bhītāḥ sma puruṣottama \|*  
*bhavantameva śaraṇaṃ prapannā vayamacyuta \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. О Lord, you tell us, as to who that person had been? We all are frightened. О Unerring being, all of us have arrived to take refuge with you.

## \|\| 2.38.57 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi vetsi jagatyasmin yatkiñcidapi ceṣṭitam \|*  
*anugraheṇa viśveśa tadasmānanupālaya \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. All the activities in the world are well known to you. Therefore, О Lord of the universe, you kindly protect us with your blessings.”

## \|\| 2.38.58 \|\|

*vijñāpito munigaṇairviśvātmā kamalodbhavaḥ \|*  
*dhyātvā devaṃ triśūlāṅkaṃ kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. At these words of the sage, Lord Brahma, who was bom of lotus, devoted his mind to the trident-bearer Shiva with palms joined in reverence, and spoke.

## \|\| 2.38.59 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*hā kaṣṭaṃ bhavatāmadya jātaṃ sarvārthanāśanam \|*  
*dhigbalaṃ dhik tapaścaryā mithyaiva bhavatāmiha \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Brahma said, “Oh, you people are in trouble today, What happened today is destructive of everything of yours. Disgrace to your prowess, tapas and your birth which have become false.

## \|\| 2.38.60-61 \|\|

*saṃprāpya puṇyasaṃskārānnidhīnāṃ paramaṃ nidhim \|*  
*upekṣitaṃ vṛthācārairbhavadbhiriha mohitaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*kāṅkṣante yogino nityaṃ yatanto yatayo nidhim \|*  
*yameva taṃ samāsādya hā bhavadbhirupekṣitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Even after achieving the great treasure with auspicious sathsakaras, you have neglected that treasure due to delusion in your minds. The one who is desired by the great Yogins making all the efforts, you have disregarded and neglected the same after getting it. This is quite painful.

## \|\| 2.38.62 \|\|

*yajanti yajñairvividhairyatprāptyairvedavādinaḥ \|*  
*mahānidhiṃ samāsādya hā bhavadbhirupekṣitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. For achieving whom, the learned people well- versed in the Vedas, perform several yajnas, it is quite painful that you have neglected the same great treasure.

## \|\| 2.38.63-64 \|\|

*yatsamāpattijanitaṃ viśveśatvamidaṃ mama \|*  
*tadevopekṣitaṃ dṛṣṭvā nidhānaṃ bhāgyavarjitaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yasmin samāhitaṃ divyamaiśvaryaṃ yat tadavyayam \|*  
*tamāsādya nidhiṃ brāhma hā bhavadbhirvṛthākṛtam \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. I have acquired this lordship of the universe alter continuously worshipping the lord. But after seeing that Lord you have missed him like those who are devoid of good luck. Alas! the treasure in which the interest of all the gods is involved, the same indestructible treasure has been lost by you even after achieving it.

## \|\| 2.38.65 \|\|

*eṣa devo mahādevo vijñeyastu maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*na tasya paramaṃ kiñcit padaṃ samadhigamyate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He happens to be lord Mahadeva, the lord of all the gods. You must know him. The reality about him cannot be known anywhere else.

## \|\| 2.38.66-67 \|\|

*devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ cāpi śāśvataḥ \|*  
*sahasrayugaparyante pralaye sarvadehinām \|\| 66 \|\|*

*saṃharatyeṣa bhagavān kālo bhūtvā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*eṣa caiva prajāḥ sarvāḥ sṛjatyekaḥ svatejasā \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. The same lord Mahesvara is the most eternal of all deities, the Rishis, the Pitrs. At the end of a thousand Yugas, at the time of final dissolution, He, assuming the form of Kala, destroys all living beings. He is unique, and creates all the subjects with his lustre.

## \|\| 2.38.68 \|\|

*yogī kṛtayuge devastretāyāṃ yajña ucyate \|*  
*dvāpare bhagavān kālo dharmaketuḥ kalau yuge \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He is the carrier of cakra, and is adorned with the symbol of Srivatsa mark. He is the Supreme Ruler. The same lord is Yogin in Krtayuga, form of Yajna in Treta yuga, lord Kala in Dvapara and the form of Dharma in the age of Kali.

## \|\| 2.38.69 \|\|

*rudrasya mūrtayastistro yābhirviśvamidaṃ tatam \|*  
*tamo hyagnī rajo brahmā sattvaṃ viṣṇuriti prabhuḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. There are three forms of Rudra. He pervades in the universe. Agni is called his Tamoguna form, when there is the excess Rajoguna, there appears Brahma, and when there is the excess of sattva-guna, there appears Visnu. It is stated in Smrtis.

## \|\| 2.38.70 \|\|

*mūrtiranyā smṛtā cāsya digvāsā vai śivā dhruvā \|*  
*yatra tiṣṭhati tad brahma yogena tu samanvitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Не has another form which is without robes, eternal and is also known as Shivatmika. The Supreme Brahman in association with Yoga gets established in the same.

## \|\| 2.38.71 \|\|

*yā cāsya pārśvagā bhāryā bhavadbhirabhivīkṣitā \|*  
*sā hi nārāyaṇo devaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The one who was witnessed by you as his wife, he happens to be the eternal lord Narayana.

## \|\| 2.38.72 \|\|

*tasmāt sarvamidaṃ jātaṃ tatraiva ca layaṃ vrajet \|*  
*sa eva mohayet kṛtsnaṃ sa eva paramā gatiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Everything is bom of him and the same is absorbed in him. He alone can liberate all, and he also is the supreme position (or salvation).

## \|\| 2.38.73 \|\|

*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt \|*  
*ekaśṛṅgo mahānātmā purāṇo 'ṣṭākṣaro hariḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Narayana is the thousand-headed Purusa, having a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet. He is the great Atman. This has also been declared by the Srutis.

## \|\| 2.38.74 \|\|

*ṛtasya garbho bhagavānāpo māyātanuḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*stūyate vividhairmantrairbrāhmaṇairdharmamokṣibhiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The semen virile becomes the foetus in him. The lord also has an illusory aquatic body. The Brahmanas desirous of dharma and moksa pray to him with various mantras.

## \|\| 2.38.75 \|\|

*saṃhṛtya sakalaṃ viśvaṃ kalpānte puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*śete yogāmṛtaṃ pītvā yat tad viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. At the end of the kalpa, after the destruction of the universe, consuming nectar in the form of Yoga, lord Purusottama, sleeps in the greatest region of Visnu.

## \|\| 2.38.76 \|\|

*na jāyate na mriyate vardhate na ca viśvasṛk \|*  
*mūlaprakṛtiravyaktā gīyate vaidikairajaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. He is Visvadrk (the seer of the universe). He neither takes birth, nor does he meets with his end, nor does he expands. The Vedic people call him as the unmanifest original Prakrti.

## \|\| 2.38.77 \|\|

*tato niśāyāṃ vṛttāyāṃ sisṛkṣurakhilañjagat \|*  
*ajasya nābhau tad bījaṃ kṣipatyeṣa maheśvaraḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. When the night of dissolution comes to an end, then, he, lord Mahes'vara, with the desire of creating the universe afresh, establishes the seed in the navel of the unborn.

## \|\| 2.38.78 \|\|

*taṃ māṃ vitta mahātmānaṃ brahmāṇaṃ viśvato mukham \|*  
*mahāntaṃ puruṣaṃ viśvamapāṃ garbhamanuttamam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The same seed produces the four-faced Brahma, and I happen to be the same Purusa. I am the universal soul, and I am the excellent foetus of water.

## \|\| 2.38.79 \|\|

*na taṃ vidātha janakaṃ mohitāstasya māyayā \|*  
*devadevaṃ mahādevaṃ bhūtānāmīśvaraṃ haram \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Lord Mahadeva, Нага, the lord of all beings, who establishes the seed of the universe in me, could not be known by you, under the influence of his Maya.

## \|\| 2.38.80 \|\|

*eṣa devo mahādevo hyanādirbhagavān haraḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunā saha saṃyuktaḥ karoti vikaroti ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. He is everlasting lord Mahadeva, combining himself with Visnu, he resorts to creation and also destroys the same.

## \|\| 2.38.81 \|\|

*na tasya vidyate kāryaṃ na tasmād vidyate param \|*  
*sa vedān pradadau pūrvaṃ yogamāyātanurmama \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. He is inactive but nothing is beyond him as well. In earlier times, he had bestowed Vedas unto me through his Yogamaya.

## \|\| 2.38.82 \|\|

*sa māyī māyayā sarvaṃ karoti vikaroti ca \|*  
*tameva muktaye jñātvā vrajeta śaraṇaṃ bhavam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Such an illusory lord, by means of his Мауй, makes and destroys the universe. Since he is the source of redemption, therefore, all of you should take refuge with him.”

## \|\| 2.38.83 \|\|

*itīritā bhagavatā marīcipramukhā vibhum \|*  
*praṇamya devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ pṛcchanti sma suduḥ khitāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. At these words of lord Brahma, Marichi and other prominent Rishis, offered their salutation to the eternal Brahma, and with a concentrated heart asked him.

## Chapter 39. Entry in the forest of Devadaru

## \|\| 2.39.1 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ paśyema taṃ devaṃ punareva pinākinam \|*  
*brūhi viśvāmareśāna trātā tvaṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The sages said, “O Lord of all immortal beings, how can we have an audience with Shiva, the holder of Pinaka, once again; you are the saviour of those who seek refuge.

## \|\| 2.39.2-3 \|\|

*pitāmaha uvāca*  
*yad dṛṣṭaṃ bhavatā tasya liṅgaṃ bhuvi nipātitam \|*  
*talliṅgānukṛtīśasya kṛtvā liṅgamanuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūjayadhvaṃ sapatnīkāḥ sādaraṃ putrasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*vaidikaireva niyamairvividhairbrahmacāriṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The Grandsire said, “the linga of Mahesvara, had been observed by you as falling on the ground and as such you make an excellent linga of the same type, and it should be adored by you with your wives and sons, observing celibacy, as per Vedic practices.

## \|\| 2.39.4-5 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya śāṅkarairmantrairṛgyajuḥ sāmasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ paraṃ samāsthāya gṛṇantaḥ śatarudriyam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*samāhitāḥ pūjayadhvaṃ saputrāḥ saha bandhubhiḥ \|*  
*sarve prāñjalayo bhūtvā śūlapāṇiṃ prapadyatha \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The linga of Shiva should be consecrated reciting the mantras pertaining to Sankara, hymns from Rgveda, Yajurveda and Samaveda, performing great tapas reciting the Satarudriya- stotra, and with a concentrated mind, all of you with your wives and sons, should adore the lord Shiva and take refuge with him with folded hands.

## \|\| 2.39.6 \|\|

*tato drakṣyatha deveśaṃ durdarśamakṛtātmabhiḥ \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvamajñānamadharmaśca praṇaśyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then, you will see the lord of Devas, rarely visible to those who are not self-possessed. By meeting whom, the entire ignorance and adharma vanish.”

## \|\| 2.39.7 \|\|

*tataḥ praṇamya varadaṃ brahmāṇamamitaujasam \|*  
*jagmuḥ saṃhṛṣṭamanaso devadāruvanaṃ punaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thereafter, the sages, offering their salutation to lord Brahma of unmeasured prowess, with a delightful heart, again went back to the forest of Daruvana.

## \|\| 2.39.8 \|\|

*ārādhayitumārabdhā brahmaṇā kathitaṃ yathā \|*  
*ajānantaḥ paraṃ devaṃ vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Reaching there, they did as had been advised by Brahma. They started adoration of lord Shiva. Though they were not aware of the supreme lord, still the sages were free from attachment and jealousy.

## \|\| 2.39.9 \|\|

*sthaṇḍileṣu vicitreṣu parvatānāṃ guhāsu ca \|*  
*nadīnāṃ ca vivikteṣu pulineṣu śubheṣu ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They stationed themselves in the different kinds of pieces of grounds, caves of mountains and the auspicious lonely banks of the rivers.

## \|\| 2.39.10 \|\|

*śaivālabhojanāḥ kecit kecidantarjaleśayāḥ \|*  
*kecidabhrāvakāśāstu pādāṅguṣṭhāgraviṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Some of them consumed aquatic plants, some of them lived in water, some of them stood under the open sky on the tips of their big toes, and adored Shiva with concentrated mind.

## \|\| 2.39.11 \|\|

*danto 'lūkhalinastvanye hyaśmakuṭṭāstathā pare \|*  
*śākaparṇāśinaḥ kecit saṃprakṣālā marīcipāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Some of them consumed the cereals by chewing them with teeth without cooking them, some of them powdered the cereals over the stone and then consumed the same. Some of them lived on the vegetation washing it properly. Some of the sage remained alive by inhaling the sun rays.

## \|\| 2.39.12 \|\|

*vṛkṣamūlaniketāśca śilāśayyāstathā pare \|*  
*kālaṃ nayanti tapasā pūjayanto maheśvaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Some of them lived under the trees, others slept over the rocks. In this way they continued tapas for Shiva, for a long time.

## \|\| 2.39.13 \|\|

*tatasteṣāṃ prasādārthaṃ prapannārtiharo haraḥ \|*  
*cakā bhagavān buddhiṃ prabodhāya vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then lord Shiva, observing that the sages have thus taken refuge with him, the lord in order to grace them, decided to bestow the excellent knowledge to them.

## \|\| 2.39.14 \|\|

*devaḥ kṛtayuge hyasmin śṛṅge himavataḥ śubhe \|*  
*devadāruvanaṃ prāptaḥ prasannaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thus speaking, in the krtayuga, Mahesvara getting pleased, again visited the forest of Devadaru tress, over the auspicous Himalaya.

## \|\| 2.39.15 \|\|

*bhasmapāṇḍuradigdhāṅgo nagno vikṛtalakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ulmukavyagrahastaśca raktapiṅgalalocanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He was of white complexion because of the ashes smeared over his body. He was without robes and had a deformed appearance. His eyes were red and of yellow colour. He held firebrands in his hands.

## \|\| 2.39.16 \|\|

*kvacicca hasate raudraṃ kvacid gāyati vismitaḥ \|*  
*kvacinnṛtyati śṛṅgārī kvacidrauti muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Sometimes, he laughed in awful form, sometimes he sang feeling surprised, and danced artistically, while at times he wept as well again and again.

## \|\| 2.39.17 \|\|

*āśrame 'bhyāgato bhikṣāṃ yācate ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*māyāṃ kṛtvātmano rūpaṃ devastad vanamāgataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Creating such a Maya, Mahadeva wandered in the asramas in the form of a Bhiksu, begging for alms again and again.

## \|\| 2.39.18 \|\|

*kṛtvā girisutāṃ gaurīṃ pārśvedevaḥ pinākadhṛk \|*  
*sā ca pūrvavad deveśī devadāruvanaṃ gatā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Pinaka-bearer kept Gaurl, the daughter of Himalaya, by his side. As before, the goddess of Devas, came to the forest of Devadarus.

## \|\| 2.39.19 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ devaṃ devyā saha kapardinam \|*  
*praṇemuḥ śirasā bhūmau toṣayāmāsurīśvaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In this way lord Shiva, having the matted locks of hair over the head, reached the forest with Parvati. Finding the arrival of Shiva, the sages approached him and offered their salutation to him, besides the prayers.

## \|\| 2.39.20 \|\|

*vaidikairvividhairmantraiḥ sūktairmāheśvaraiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*atharvaśirasā cānye rudrādyairbrahmabhirbhavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. They started eulogising Shiva reciting various Vedic hymns, the auspicious Mahesvara-suktas, Atharvas'iras, and the Vedic hymns relating to Rudra.

## \|\| 2.39.21-22 \|\|

*namo devādidevāya mahādevāya te namaḥ \|*  
*tryambakāya namastubhyaṃ triśūlavaradhāriṇe \|\| 21 \|\|*

*namo digvāsase tubhyaṃ vikṛtāya pinākine \|*  
*sarvapraṇatadehāya svayamapraṇatātmane \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. They said, “You are the god of gods, salutation to you. Salutation to Mahadeva, salutation to the holder of the best of trident, salutation to the one having three eyes, the one who at his own will remains without robes and also remains in hideous forms, salutation to you. Salutation to the holder of the Pinaka bow, you are the refuge of all the devotees, and you yourself are without any refuge, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.39.23-27 \|\|

*antakāntakṛte tubhyaṃ sarvasaṃharaṇāya ca \|*  
*namo 'stu nṛtyaśīlāya namo bhairavarūpiṇe \|\| 23 \|\|*

*naranārīśarīrāya yogināṃ gurave namaḥ \|*  
*namo dāntāya śāntāya tāpasāya harāya ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vibhīṣaṇāya rudrāya namaste kṛttivāsase \|*  
*namaste lelihānāya śitikaṇṭhāya te namaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*aghoraghorarūpāya vāmadevāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*namaḥ kanakamālāya devyāḥ priyakarāya ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

*gaṅgāsaliladhārāya śambhave parameṣṭhine \|*  
*namo yogādhipataye brahmādhipataye namaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

23-27. You are destroyer of the god of death, and of all the living beings, salutation to you. Salutation to one whose sport is dance and who is of terrible forms. Salutation to the eternal and Bhairava forms. You take to the form of man and woman, are the preceptor of the Yogins, salutation to you. You have controlled your senses, you are calm, terrific, clad in elephant- hide, salutation to Rudra. Salutation to the one who lick with the tongue again and again. Salutation to the blue-throated one, salutation to Vamadeva with the terrific and pleasant forms. You wear the garland of thorn apples, and are beloved of the goddess Parvati, from whose head issues the holy river Ganga, Parameshthin, Sambhu, salutation to you. Salutation to the one, who is the overlord of Yoga and of all living beings.

## \|\| 2.39.28 \|\|

*prāṇāya ca namastubhyaṃ namo bhasmāṅgarāgine \|*  
*namaste ghanavāhāya daṃṣṭriṇe vahniretase \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Salutation to you since you are the form of Prana (vital airs). Salutation to the one who applies ashes over the body. Salutation to the carrier of havya, having curved fangs, and the form of fire.

## \|\| 2.39.29 \|\|

*brahmaṇaśca śiro hartre namaste kālarūpiṇe \|*  
*āgatiṃ te na janīmo gatiṃ naiva ca naiva ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. You are the one who removed the head of Brahma, the form of Kala, we are unaware always of your arrival and departure.

## \|\| 2.39.30 \|\|

*viśveśvara mahādeva yo 'si so 'si namo 'stu te \|*  
*namaḥ pramathanāthāya dātre ca śubhasaṃpadām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О! Lord of the universe, О Mahadeva, we offer salutation to you in whichever form (in which I meet you). You are the lord of Pramathas, and bestowers of the good fortunes, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.39.31 \|\|

*kapālapāṇaye tubhyaṃ namo mīḍhuṣṭamāya te \|*  
*namaḥ kanakaliṅgāya vāriliṅgāya te namaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. You hold the skull in your hand, and you are served by all, salutation to you. You are yellow like the gold having the lingas of water salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.39.32 \|\|

*namo vahnyarkaliṅgāya jñānaliṅgāya te namaḥ \|*  
*namo bhujaṅgahārāya karṇikārapriyāya ca \|*  
*kirīṭine kuṇḍaline kālakālāya te namaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Salutation to you having the linga of Agni, Sfirya and Jhana. You have garland of snakes, the Karnikara (oleander) flowers are liked by you, salutation to you. You wear the crown and earrings, and are destroyer of the god of death, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.39.33 \|\|

*vāmadeva maheśāna devadeva trilocana \|*  
*kṣamyatāṃ yatkṛtaṃ mohāt tvameva śaraṇaṃ hi naḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. You are Mahadeva, Mahadeva, god of gods, three-eyed lord of Devas, whatever was done by us out of delusion, you kindly forgive us for the same. All of us take refuge with you.

## \|\| 2.39.34 \|\|

*caritāni vicitrāṇi guhyāni gahanāni ca \|*  
*brahmādīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ durvijñeyo 'si śaṅkara \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Your activities are astonishing, deep and secret. Therefore, О Shiva, you are beyond the power of understanding by Brahma and others, and are invincible.

## \|\| 2.39.35 \|\|

*ajñānād yadi vā jñānād yatkiñcitkurute naraḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ bhagavānena kurute yogamāyayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A person who knowingly or unknowingly does something, it is done by you through your Yogic Maya.

## \|\| 2.39.36 \|\|

*evaṃ stutvā mahādevaṃ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā \|*  
*ūcuḥ praṇamya giriśaṃ paśyāmastvāṃ yathā purā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Thus the sages who were devoted to lord Mahadeva by heart, offered salutation to lord Mahadeva and prayed to him- “We are interested in looking at your true form.”

## \|\| 2.39.37 \|\|

*teṣāṃ saṃstavamākarṇya somaḥ momavibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*svameva paramaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Listening to the prayer of the sages, Shiva, adorned with the crescent as his head ornament, displayed before them his true form.

## \|\| 2.39.38 \|\|

*taṃ te dṛṣṭvātha giriśaṃ devyā saha pinākinam \|*  
*yathā pūrvaṃ sthitā viprāḥ praṇemurhṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then Shiva, the holder of Pinaka, together with goddess Parvati, appeared in his earlier fonn, which pleased the Brahmanas, who bowed to him in reverence.

## \|\| 2.39.39-40 \|\|

*tataste munayaḥ sarve saṃstūya ca maheśvaram \|*  
*bhṛgvaṅgirovasiṣṭhāstu viśvāmitrastathaiva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*gautamo 'triḥ sukeśaśca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ \|*  
*marīciḥ kaśyapaścāpi saṃvartaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*praṇamya devadeveśamidaṃ vacanamabruvan \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Thereafter, the sages like Bhrgu, Angiras, Vasistha, Visvamitra, Gautama, Atri, Sukesa, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Marichi, Kasyapa and Samvartaka, offered prayer to Mahesvara. Then they bowing in reference to the lord, said to Shiva.

## \|\| 2.39.41 \|\|

*kathaṃ tvāṃ devadeveśa karmayogena vā prabho \|*  
*jñānena vātha yogena pūjayāmaḥ sadaiva hi \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “O God of Gods, how should we always adore you? Should we do so by karmayoga (path of action) or Jitanayoga (path of knowledge)?

## \|\| 2.39.42 \|\|

*kena vā devamārgeṇa saṃpūjyo bhagavāniha \|*  
*kiṃ tat sevyamasevyaṃ vā sarvametad bravīhi naḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О Lord, how should we worship you? How should we serve you? What should be resorted to and what should be avoided? You please tell us.”

## \|\| 2.39.43 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca*  
*etad vaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi gūḍhaṃ gahanamuttamam \|*  
*brahmaṇe kathitaṃ pūrvamādāveva maharṣayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Lord Shiva said, “0 Great Rishis, I shall reveal before you the excellent and deep secret.” In earlier times, Lord Brahma had revealed the same to me.

## \|\| 2.39.44 \|\|

*sāṃkhyayogo dvidhā jñeyaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ hi sādhanam \|*  
*yogena sahitaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ vimuktidam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The means of salvation for the people, can be known by two means of Sarnkhya and Yoga. In reality, Sarnkhya together with Yoga surely bestows deliverance to the humans.

## \|\| 2.39.45 \|\|

*na kevalena yogena dṛśyate puruṣaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ tu kevalaṃ samyagapavargaphalapradam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. One cannot be face to face with great Purusa by means of Yoga alone, but in case Yoga is linked with Jnana, then both of them combined make the people to achieve moksa.

## \|\| 2.39.46 \|\|

*bhavantaḥ kevalaṃ yogaṃ samāśritya vimuktaye \|*  
*vihāya sāṃkhyaṃ vimalamakurvanta pariśramam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Eschewing the pure Sarnkhya and depending solely on Yoga, you made your attempts for salvation.

## \|\| 2.39.47 \|\|

*etasmāt kāraṇād viprānṛṇāṃ kevaladharmiṇām \|*  
*āgato 'hamimaṃ deśaṃ jñāpayan mohasaṃbhavam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Therefore, О Brahmanas, you had developed ignorance while performing the deeds alone, because of the confusion and to remove the ignorance, I had come to your place and am now speaking to you.

## \|\| 2.39.48 \|\|

*tasmād bhavadbhirvimalaṃ jñānaṃ kaivalyasādhanam \|*  
*jñātavyaṃ hi prayatnena śrotavyaṃ dṛśyameva ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Therefore, all of you depending upon the perfect knowledge, making all the efforts must listen to the speech of the lord and you can have audience with him accordingly.

## \|\| 2.39.49 \|\|

*ekaḥ sarvatrago hyātmā kevalaścitimātrakaḥ \|*  
*ānando nirmalo nityaṃ syādetat sāṃkhyadarśanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The Atman is all pervading, is spotless, spiritual, blissful, unblemished, eternal and one and only one. This is indeed the Sarnkhya philosophy.

## \|\| 2.39.50 \|\|

*etadeva paraṃ jñānameṣa mokṣo 'tra gīyate \|*  
*etat kaivalyamamalaṃ brahmabhāvaśca varṇitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. This alone is the supreme knowledge. This has been conceived as moksa. This is the spotless deliverance and also the auspicious Brahmabhava (the state of Brahman).

## \|\| 2.39.51 \|\|

*āśritya caitat paramaṃ tanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*paśyanti māṃ mahātmāno yatayo viśvamīśvaram \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Taking refuge in this knowledge, getting devoted to the same, the great ascetics and the у at is, have an audience with my universal form, the Ishvara.

## \|\| 2.39.52 \|\|

*etat tat paramaṃ jñānaṃ kevalaṃ sannirañjanam \|*  
*ahaṃ hi vedyo bhagavān mama mūrtiriyaṃ śivā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. This is the essence, spotless, the absolute Reality, and unique supreme knowledge. I am the lord to be known, and this Shiva also happens to be my own form.

## \|\| 2.39.53 \|\|

*bahūni sādhanānīha siddhaye kathitāni tu \|*  
*teṣāmabhyadhikaṃ jñānaṃ māmakaṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О Best of Brahmanas, for achieving of the success in the world, the means have been discussed. But out of them all, learning about myself, is the best of knowledge.

## \|\| 2.39.54-55 \|\|

*jñānayogaratāḥ śāntā māmeva śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*ye hi māṃ bhasmaniratā dhyāyanti satataṃ hṛdi \|\| 54 \|\|*

*madbhaktiparamā nityaṃ yatayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*nāśayāmyacirāt teṣāṃ ghoraṃ saṃsārasāgaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. The followers of Jnanayoga are peaceful and taking refuge in me, applying ashes over their bodies, they always devote their hearts to me. Those yatis are always absorbed in my devotion as a result of which they are freed from the sins. Because of this, 1 remove their sufferings in the ocean of the universe,

## \|\| 2.39.56 \|\|

*praśāntaḥ saṃyatamanā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahaḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryarato nagno vrataṃ pāśupataṃ caret \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In earlier times, I had introduced the holy Pas'upata vow for the liberation of the people, which is immensely secret, subtle, and the essence of the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.39.57 \|\|

*nirmitaṃ hi mayā pūrvaṃ vrataṃ pāśupataṃ param \|*  
*guhyād guhyatamaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vedasāraṃ vimuktaye \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A person with a peaceful mind and by controlling it, he should cover the body with ashes, observing celibacy, remaining without robes, should perform Pas'upata vow.

## \|\| 2.39.58 \|\|

*yad vā kaupīnavasanaḥ syād vaikavasano muniḥ \|*  
*vedābhyāsarato vidvān dhyāyet paśupatiṃ śivam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Or otherwise, he should be clad in a kaupln or a single cloth, practicing the reciting of the Vedas silently, and should always devote himself to Shiva-Pas'upati-the lord of beings,

## \|\| 2.39.59-60 \|\|

*eṣa pāśupato yogaḥ sevanīyo mumukṣubhiḥ \|*  
*bhasmacchannairhi satataṃ niṣkāmairiti viśrutiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ \|*  
*bahavo 'nena yogena pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. This Pasupata Yoga should be followed by the people desirous of achieving of the moksa. This has been ordained by the Srutis. The people free from attraction, fear, anger, who take refuge in me, who recite my name always mentally, getting purified with the practicing of this Yoga, achieve my own form.

## \|\| 2.39.61 \|\|

*anyāni caiva śāstrāṇi loke 'smin mohanānitu \|*  
*vedavādaviruddhāni mayaiva kathitāni tu \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. There are several other scriptures in this world which create confusion and are against the Vedic philosophy and have been propounded by me only. They are very fascinating in this world.

## \|\| 2.39.62 \|\|

*vāmaṃ pāśupataṃ somaṃ lākulaṃ caiva bhairavam \|*  
*asevyametat kathitaṃ vedavāhyaṃ tathetaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. They include Vama-marga, Pas'upata, Soma cult, Lakura, Bhairava, and others which are opposed to the Vedas. They should not be followed.

## \|\| 2.39.63 \|\|

*vedamurtirahaṃ viprā nānyaśāstrārthavedibhiḥ \|*  
*jñāyate matsvarūpaṃ tu muktvā vedaṃ sanātanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О Brahmanas, I am the form of the Vedas. Those who are well-versed in the other s'astras, cannot know about my true form, except the eternal lord (Visnu).

## \|\| 2.39.64 \|\|

*sthāpayadhvamidaṃ mārgaṃ pūjayadhvaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*acirādaiśvaraṃ jñānamutpatsyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Therefore, the Pasupata-marga should be established and by so doing, all of you shall achieve the best of knowledge shortly. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.39.65 \|\|

*mayi bhaktiśca vipulā bhavatāmastu sattamāḥ \|*  
*dhyātamātro hi sānnidhyaṃ dāsyāmi munisattamāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Best of the people, all of you are immensely devoted to me. О Best of the sages, I shall grant you my closeness, by your simply meditating for me.”

## \|\| 2.39.66-67 \|\|

*ityuktvā bhagavān somastatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*to 'pi dāruvane tasmin pūjayanti sma śaṅkaram \|*  
*brahmacaryaratāḥ śāntā jñānayogaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*sametya te mahātmāno munayo brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*vitenire bahūn vādānnadhyātmajñānasaṃśrayān \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Thus speaking, lord Shiva disappeared from that place along with Uma. The Rishis also with the peaceful mind, observing brahmacarya and following Jnanayoga, started adoring lord Shiva in the same Daruvana. Then the noble sages, collecting there, held many discussions relating to spirituality.

## \|\| 2.39.68-69 \|\|

*kimasya jagato mūlamātmā cāsmākameva hi \|*  
*ko 'pi syāt sarvabhāvānāṃ heturīśvara eva ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ manyamānānāṃ dhyānamārgāvalambinām \|*  
*āvirāsīnmahādevī devī girivarātmajā \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. What is the base or root of this world? What is our own root? There should be a cause for all rlie causes? He could be Is'vara alone. Thus when they believed like this, after resorting to the path of meditation, then the great goddess, Parvati, the daughter of Himalaya, also appeared there before them.

## \|\| 2.39.70 \|\|

*koṭisūryapratīkāśā jvālāmālāsamāvṛtā \|*  
*svabhābhirvimalābhistu pūrayantī nabhastalam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. She resembled a crore of suns. She was engulfed in a cluster of flames. She was spreading her spotless lustre in the whole sky.

## \|\| 2.39.71 \|\|

*tāmanvapaśyan girijāmameyāṃ*  
*jvālāsahasrāntarasanniviṣṭām \|*  
*praṇemurekāmakhileśapatnīṃ*  
*jānanti te tat paramasya bījam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. She was shining among the thousands of fire flames, Parvati was unparallel and they had an audience with her. Then all the sages offered their salutation to Parvati, the spouse of Shiva, because they were aware of the fact that she happened to be the seed of Supreme.

## \|\| 2.39.72 \|\|

*asamākameṣā parameśapatnī*  
*gatistathātmā gaganābhidhānā \|*  
*paśyantyathātmānamidaṃ ca kṛtsnaṃ*  
*tasyāmathaite munayaśca viprāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The Rxis thought, “She is the spouse of our lord, our goal and the soul. She is known as the sky.” Thus thinking, the sages looked at Parvati as their own soul lodged in her. They witnessed in her the entire universe.

## \|\| 2.39.73 \|\|

*nirīkṣitāste parameśapatnyā*  
*tadantare devamaśeṣahetum \|*  
*paśyanti śaṃbhuṃ kavimīśitāraṃ*  
*rudraṃ bṛhantaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Parvati, the spouse of Paramesvara, also started looking at the sages, or she glanced at them. In the meantime, the sages also found Shiva, the sole cause of the universe, extremely learned, controller of all, the great Rudra and Ригйпаригща.

## \|\| 2.39.74 \|\|

*ālokya devīmatha devamīśaṃ*  
*praṇemurānandamavāpuragryam \|*  
*jñānaṃ tadaiśaṃ bhagavatprasādā-*  
*dāvirbabhau janmavināśahetu \|\| 74 \|\|*
