74\. Thus finding both Parvati and Shiva there, the sages offered their salutation to both of them. They were immensely delighted. At the same time, they were bestowed with the divine bliss and knowledge, which removed the cause of birth and death, dawned in them.

## \|\| 2.39.75 \|\|

*iyaṃ hi sā jagato yonirekā*  
*sarvātmikā sarvaniyāmikā ca \|*  
*māheśvarīśaktiranādisiddhā*  
*vyomābhidhānā divi rājatīva \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. They felt that it was the goddess alone, who was the cause of the creation of the world, the universal soul, controller of all, and was known as iMahesVarl from the time eternal. She was known by the name of Vyoma (the sky), and was illumining in the heaven.

## \|\| 2.39.76 \|\|

*asyā mahatparameṣṭhī parastā-*  
*nmaheśvaraḥ śiva eko 'tha rudraḥ \|*  
*cakāra viśvaṃ paraśaktiniṣṭhāṃ*  
*māyāmathāruhya sa devadevaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Even the great Shiva -Paramethin, Mahesvara, who is beyond everything, Rudra, the lord of Devas, created the universe in her mounting over the Maya that is existing in the great Shakti.

## \|\| 2.39.77 \|\|

*eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍho*  
*māyī rudraḥ sakalo niṣkalaśca \|*  
*sa eva devī na ca tadvibhinna-*  
*metajjñātvā hyamṛtatvaṃ vrajanti \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Lord Shiva is also pervading in the bodies of all the living beings. The same Rudra is the wielder of Maya, is entire and undivided. He is also the form of the goddess. There is nothing separate from him. Thus realising, one achieves the amrtatatJva (immortality).

## \|\| 2.39.78 \|\|

*antarhito 'bhūd bhagavānatheśo*  
*devyā bhargaḥ saha devādidevaḥ \|*  
*ārādhayanti sma tameva devaṃ*  
*vanaukasaste punareva rudram \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thereafter lord Mahes'vara, the overlord of the Devas, together with the goddess suddenly disappeared from the place and the forest dweller Rishis started adoring the Supreme Rudradeva, the primordial lord.

## \|\| 2.39.79 \|\|

*etad vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ devadevaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*devadāruvane pūrvaṃ purāṇe yanmayā śrutam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Thus in the forest of Daruvana in the earlier times, the story relating to the lord Shiva, as had been heard by me, from the Puranas, has been narrated by me.

## \|\| 2.39.80 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyānnityaṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*śrāvayed vā dvijān śāntān sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The one who recites the same regularly, or listens to it, he is removed of all the sins. The one who shall narrate the same to others with a peaceful mind, he will surely achieve the greatest goal.

## Chapter 40. Glory of the river Narmada

## \|\| 2.40.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*eṣā puṇyatamā devī devagandharvasevitā \|*  
*narmadā lokavikhyātā tīrthānāmuttamā nadī \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “The auspicious goddess who is served by the gods and the Gandharvas is known by the name of Narmada in the world. Even in the form of the river, she is the best of all the tirthas.

## \|\| 2.40.2 \|\|

*tasyāḥ śṛṇudhvaṃ māhātmyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyena bhāṣitam \|*  
*yudhiṣṭhirāya tu śubhaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The sages Markandeya had spoken to Yudhisthira about the glory of this river. All of you should listen to the auspicious glory of the same, which relieves one of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.40.3 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*śrutāstu vividhā dharmāstvatprasādānmahāmune \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ ca prayāgasya tīrthāni vividhāni ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. “O Great sage, I have listened to the various dharmas by your grace. I have also heard about the glory of Prayaga and several other tirthas.

## \|\| 2.40.4 \|\|

*narmadā sarvatīrthānāṃ mukhyā hi bhavateritā \|*  
*tasyāstvidānīṃ māhātmyaṃ vaktumarhasi sattama \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. You have stated that Narmada is the foremost of all the sacred rivers. Therefore, kindly speak out the glory of the same.”

## \|\| 2.40.5 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā rudradehād viniḥ sṛtā \|*  
*tārayet sarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Markandeya said, “Narmada has emerged out of the body of Rudra and is the foremost of all the rivers. She in fact redeems all the mobile and immobile living beings.

## \|\| 2.40.6 \|\|

*narmadāyāstu māhātmyaṃ purāṇe yanmayā śrutam \|*  
*idānīṃ tatpravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ śubham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Whatever has been heared by me from the Puranas about her glory, I am going to repeat the same. All of you should listen to me with a concentrated mind,

## \|\| 2.40.7 \|\|

*puṇyā kanakhale gaṅgā kurukṣetre sarasvatī \|*  
*grāme vā yadi vāraṇye puṇyā sarvatra narmadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The Ganga is sacred at Kanakhala and Sarasvatl is sacred in Kuruksetra, but the river Narmada is auspicious everywhere in the villages or the forests.

## \|\| 2.40.8 \|\|

*tribhiḥ sārasvataṃ toyaṃ saptāhena tu yāmunam \|*  
*sadyaḥ punāti gāṅgeyaṃ darśanādeva nārmadam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The holy water of Sarasvatl sanctifies one in three days, the water of Yamuna in seven days and the water of Ganga sanctifies immediately. But the water of Narmada purifies a person, while simply looking at it.

## \|\| 2.40.9 \|\|

*kaliṅgadeśapaścārdhe parvate 'marakaṇṭake \|*  
*puṇyā ca triṣu lokeṣu ramaṇīyā manoramā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On the rear side of the Kalinga country, and in the half of its region over the Amarakantaka mountain, is the place of origin of the sacred, auspicious, pleasant and well-known river of Narmada.

## \|\| 2.40.10 \|\|

*sadevāsuragandharvā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*tapastaptvā tu rājendra siddhiṃ tu paramāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О leading king, the gods, the demons, besides Gandharvas, saints, and the ascetics, have met with great success, in their endeavours (while meditating over the banks of Narmada.)

## \|\| 2.40.11 \|\|

*tatra snātvā naro rājan niyamastho jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ kulānāṃ tārayecchatam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О king, a person by having a bath in Narmada, getting disciplined and controlling his sense organs, when fasts for a night, then he redeems a hundred generations of his race.

## \|\| 2.40.12 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ śataṃ sāgraṃ śrūyate sariduttamā \|*  
*vistāreṇa tu rājendra yojanadvayamāyatā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О Indra among the kings, it is heard that the excellent river, is a bit longer than a hundred yojanas and is spread (at places) nearly two yojanas in width.

## \|\| 2.40.13 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭitīrthasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathaiva ca \|*  
*parvatasya samantāt tu tiṣṭhantyamarakaṇṭake \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. All around the Amarakantaka mountain, there are sixty crores and sixty thousand tirthas.

## \|\| 2.40.14-15 \|\|

*brahmacārī śucirbhūtvā jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*sarvahiṃsānivṛttastu sarvabhūtahite rataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*evaṃ sarvasamācāro yastu prāṇān samutsṛjet \|*  
*tasya puṇyaphalaṃ rājan śṛṇuṣvāvahito nṛpa \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. A Brahmacarin who purifying himself, overcoming anger and the sense organs, getting relieved himself of all types of voilance, is engaged in the welfare of all the living beings, and conducts the auspicious deeds, when such person with excellent conduct, meets with his end there, he earns the enormous merit which you please listen, О Sinless King!

## \|\| 2.40.16 \|\|

*śatavarṣasahasrāṇi svarge modati pāṇḍava \|*  
*sapsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇo divyastrīparivāritaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О son of Pandu, the said person having been surrounded by the divine damsels in the heaven, enjoys all the pleasures for a hundred thousand years.

## \|\| 2.40.17 \|\|

*divyagandhānuliptaśca divyapuṣpopaśobhitaḥ \|*  
*krīḍate devaloke tu daivataiḥ saha modate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He will smear himself with the divine scents and unguents, and will shine with the divine flowers and enjoys sports in the Devaloka with the gods.

## \|\| 2.40.18-19 \|\|

*tataḥ svargāt paribhraṣṭo rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*gṛhaṃ tu labhate 'sau vai nānāratnasamanvitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*stambhairmaṇimayairdivyairvajravaidūryabhūṣitam \|*  
*ālekhyavāhanaiḥ śubhrairdāsīdāsasamanvitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. After falling off from the heaven, he, after many births, becomes a king and achieves the well decorated palaces having the gem studded pillars, besides the diamonds and rubies. He also gets the beautifully painted chariots and the palaces filled with slaves and the slave-girls.

## \|\| 2.40.20 \|\|

*rājarājeśvaraḥ śrīmān sarvastrījanavallabhaḥ \|*  
*jīved varṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ tatra bhogasamanvitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He becomes the king of kings, possessing all the fortunes, becomes beloved of all the damsels, and enjoying all the pleasures, remains alive over the earth for over a hundred years.

## \|\| 2.40.21 \|\|

*agnipraveśe 'tha jale athavānaśane kṛte \|*  
*anivartikā gatistasya pavanasyāmbare yathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Reaching that tirtha, in case one ends his life by entering the water or the fire flames, or by fasting, he achieves a place, from where, he does not have to return on earth, like that of the wind absorbed in the sky.

## \|\| 2.40.22 \|\|

*paścime parvatataṭe sarvapāpavināśanaḥ \|*  
*hrado jaleśvaro nāma triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On the western peak of the mountain, there is a lake known by the name of Jalesvara, which is well known in the three worlds and removes all the sins.

## \|\| 2.40.23 \|\|

*tatra piṇḍapradānena saṃdhyopāsanakarmaṇā \|*  
*daśavarṣāṇi pitarastarpitāḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By performing sandhya and pindadana there, the manes remain satisfied for ten thousand years. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.40.24 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe narmadākūle kapilākhyā mahānadī \|*  
*saralārjunasaṃcchannā nātidūre vyavasthitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. There is a great river named Kapila, on the southern bank of Narmada, which is stationed not very far, and is surrounded by the juicy Arjuna trees.

## \|\| 2.40.25 \|\|

*sā tu puṇyā mahābhāgā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā \|*  
*tatra koṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ tīrthānāṃ tu yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The said auspicious river, is well-known in the three worlds. О Yudhisthira, there are more than a hundred crore tirthas over the banks of that river.

## \|\| 2.40.26 \|\|

*tasmiṃstīrthe tu ye vṛkṣāḥ patitāḥ kālaparyayāt \|*  
*narmadātoyasaṃspṛṣṭāste yānti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The trees which fall there in due course of time, they with the touch of the water of the river Narmada, get redeemed.

## \|\| 2.40.27 \|\|

*dvitīyā tu mahābhāgā viśalyakaraṇī śubhā \|*  
*tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā viśalyo bhavati kṣaṇāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. There is another extremely auspicious river known by the name of Vis'alyakaranl. By taking a bath in that river, a person is relieved of all the sins, ailments and his wounds are healed up

## \|\| 2.40.28 \|\|

*kapilā ca viśalyā ca śrūyate rājasattama \|*  
*īśvareṇa purā proktā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О Best of the kings, this is the traditional belief that both Kapila and Visalya rivers, have been commanded by the lord to provide welfare to all the living beings.

## \|\| 2.40.29 \|\|

*anāśakaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt tasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О King of the humans, a person who performs there a fast until death, he, getting relieved of all the sins, proceeds to Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.40.30 \|\|

*tatra snātvā naro rājannaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*ye vasantyuttare kūle rudraloke vasanti te \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О king, by taking a bath there, a person achieves merit of performing an Asvamedha sacrifice. Those who live over the northern bank of the river Narmada, they live in Rudraloka. чшз'агщ wit чйгат ^arfirfgTi m тчтщ 3 ^11

## \|\| 2.40.31-32 \|\|

*sarasvatyāṃ ca gaṅgāyāṃ narmadāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*samaṃ snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca yathā me śaṅkaro 'bravīt \|\| 31 \|\|*

*parityajati yaḥ praṇān parvate 'marakaṇṭake \|*  
*varṣakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. О Yudhisthira as Sankara told me, by taking bath in Gahga, Sarasvati and Narmada, or by giving away the charities, one achieves enormous merits. The one who meets with the end of his life at Amarakantaka, he is adorned in Rudraloka for more than a hundred crores of years.

## \|\| 2.40.33 \|\|

*narmadāyāṃ jalaṃ puṇyaṃ phenormisamalaṅkṛtam \|*  
*pavitraṃ śirasā vandya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The water of Narmada is quite auspicious. By sprinkling the auspicious water along with its foam over the head, a person is relieved of his sins.

## \|\| 2.40.34 \|\|

*narmadā sarvataḥ puṇyā brahmahatyāpahāriṇī \|*  
*ahorātropavāsena mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Narmada is sacred everywhere and relieves one even from the sin of brahmahatya. By fasting there for a day and night, one is relieved of the sin of Brahmana-slaughter.

## \|\| 2.40.35-36 \|\|

*jāleśvaraṃ tīrthavaraṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*tatra gatvā niyamavān sarvakāmāṃllabhennaraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*candrasūryoparāge tu gatvā hyamarakaṇṭakam \|*  
*aśvamedhād daśaguṇaṃ puṇyamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. A sacred tirtha named Jalesvara, relieves one of all the sins. A humble person, who observes religious regulation and restraints on going there, he gets all his desires fulfilled. On the day of the solar or lunar eclipse, the one who goes on pilgrimage to Amarakantaka, he earns the merit ten times greater than the Asvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.40.37 \|\|

*eṣa puṇyo girivaro devagandharvasevitaḥ \|*  
*nānādrumalatākīrṇo nānāpuṣpopaśobhitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Amarakantaka is auspicious and the best of mountains. It is served by the gods and the Gandharvas and has many types of trees and creepers besides the flowers.

## \|\| 2.40.38 \|\|

*tatra saṃnihito rājan devyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇustathā cendro vidyādharagaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О King, here lord Mahesvara, lives with the goddess Parvati. Vidyadharas, Brahma, Visnu, besides Rudra is present there.

## \|\| 2.40.39 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt parvataṃ hyamarakaṇṭakam \|*  
*pauṇḍarīkasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A person, who goes round the Amarakantaka mountain, he achieves the merit of performing the Paundarika sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.40.40 \|\|

*kāverī nāma vipulā nadī kalpaṣanāśinī \|*  
*tatra snātvā mahādevamarcayed vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*saṃgame narmadāyāstu rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Similarly, there is also a famous river of Kaverl which removes all the blemishes or impurities. By taking a bath in the same, as also at the confluence of Narmada and Kaverl, one who adores lord Shiva, he is honoured in the Rudraloka.

## Chapter 41. Glory of the Narmada river

## \|\| 2.41.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā sarvapāpavināśinī \|*  
*munibhiḥ kathitā pūrvamīśvareṇa svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Markandeya said, “ The river Narmada is the best of all the rivers and is the remover of all the sins. This had been revealed by the sages as well as Brahma, formerly.

## \|\| 2.41.2 \|\|

*munibhiḥ saṃstutā hyeṣā narmadā pravarā nadī \|*  
*rudragātrād viniṣkrāntā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The excellent river Narmada has been praised by the sages, because, for the benefit of the people, it emerged out of the body of Rudra.

## \|\| 2.41.3 \|\|

*sarvapāpaharā nityaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtā \|*  
*saṃstutā devagandharvairapyarobhistathaiva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It always removes all the sins and is adored by all the Gods, Gandharvas and the apsards (heavenly ladies).

## \|\| 2.41.4 \|\|

*uttare caiva tatkūle tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*nāmnā bhadreśvaraṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājan daivataiḥ saha mohate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On the northern bank of Narmada, there are the holy places which are famous in the three worlds, by the name BhadresVara, which removes all the sins.

## \|\| 2.41.5 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra tīrthamāmrātakeśvaram \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājan gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О King, by taking a bath there, a person feels blissful, together with the gods. О Indra among the kings, one should go to Vimalesvara tirtha from this place.

## \|\| 2.41.6 \|\|

*tato 'ṅgāreśvaraṃ gacchenniyato niyatāśanaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О King, by taking a bath there, a person earns a merit equivalent to the donating of a thousand cows. Thereafter, taking the appropriate and restricted food, one should reach Angaresvara tirtha. By so doing, a person getting relieved of all the sins, becoming the purified soul, and achieves the Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.41.7 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra kedāraṃ nāma puṇyadam \|*  
*tatra snātvodakaṃ kṛtvā sarvān kāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О leading king, thereafter, one should visit the meritorious tirtha of Kedara. By consuming water, after taking bath there, one has all his desires fulfilled.

## \|\| 2.41.8 \|\|

*pippaleśaṃ tato gacchet sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*tatra snātvā mahārāja rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereafter, one should go to the Nisphales'a tirtha, which destroys all the sins. By taking a bath there a person is adored in Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.41.9 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra vimaleśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tatra prāṇān parityajya rudralokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O Rajendra, then one should go to the excellent Banatirtha. By meeting with one’s end there, the place of Rudra is achieved.

## \|\| 2.41.10 \|\|

*tataḥ puṣkariṇīṃ gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra indrasyārdhāsanaṃ labhet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereafter, one should take bath in PuskarinT river. By merely taking a bath there, a person achieves the lion throne of lord.

## \|\| 2.41.11 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra śūlabhedamiti śrutam \|*  
*tatra snātvārcayed devaṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereafter, one should go to the Sakra tirtha which is located over the southern bank of Narmada. By having a bath there, a person becomes eligible to achieve half of the throne of Indra.

## \|\| 2.41.12 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra balitīrthamanuttam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājan sihāsanapatirbhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О King, one should then move to a place known as Sulabheda. It is believed that by consuming the water, thereafter having a bath, a person achieves the merit of donation of a thousand cows.

## \|\| 2.41.13-14 \|\|

*śakratīrthaṃ tato gacchet kūle caiva tu dakṣiṇe \|*  
*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ārādhayenmahāyogaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim \|*  
*gosahasraphalaṃ prāpya viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. By fasting for a night there, and taking bath appropriately, getting purified, one should adore lord Hari, the god of great Yogic power, and by so doing, one achieves the merit of donating a thousand cows, and he achieves Visnuloka ultimately.

## \|\| 2.41.15 \|\|

*ṛṣitīrthaṃ tato gatvā sarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereafter, a person should reach the Rsi- tirtha, which is destructive of all sins of men, and by taking a bath there, one is adored in the Shivaloka.

## \|\| 2.41.16 \|\|

*nāradasya tu tatraiva tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The auspicious tirtha dedicated to Narada is also located there. By taking a bath there, one achieves the merit of donating a thousand cows there.

## \|\| 2.41.17 \|\|

*yatra taptaṃ tapaḥ pūrvaṃ nāradena surarṣiṇā \|*  
*pratīstasya dadau yogaṃ devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The divine sage Narada had performed tapas here in earlier times. Lord Mahesvara, getting pleased with him, bestoved the knowledge of Yoga to him at this place.

## \|\| 2.41.18 \|\|

*brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ liṅgaṃ brahmeśvaramiti śrutam \|*  
*yatra snātvā naro rājan brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О King, there is a linga which was consecrated here by Brahma, and is known as Brahmesvara linga. By taking a bath at this holy place, one achieves glory in the Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.41.19 \|\|

*ṛṇatīrthaṃ tato gacchet sa ṛṇānmucyate dhruvam \|*  
*maheśvaraṃ tato gacchet paryāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. From here, one should move towards Rnatirlha, and by reaching there, a person is surely relieved of all the debts. From here, one should go to the Vates'vara tirtha, where one achieves the full merits of the life.

## \|\| 2.41.20 \|\|

*bhīmeśvaraṃ tato gacchet sarvavyādhivināśanam \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra sarvaduḥkhaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then, one should move on to Bhlmesvara tirtha, which removes all the miseries, by taking a bath there.

## \|\| 2.41.21 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra piṅgaleśvaramuttamam \|*  
*ahorātropavāsena trirātraphalamāpnuyāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О Rajendra, after this tirtha, one should go to Pingales'vara tirtha. By fasting there for a day and night, one achieves the merit of performing Triratra sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.41.22 \|\|

*tasmiṃmastīrthe tu rājendra kapilāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*yāvanti tasyā romāṇi tatprasūtikuleṣu ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A person who donates a Kapila (tawny- coloured) cow there, he gets established in the heaven for an equal number of years in Rudraloka as the cow has the hair on her body and on that of its calves.

## \|\| 2.41.23 \|\|

*tāvad varṣasahasrāṇi rudraloke mahīyate \|*  
*yastu prāṇaparityāgaṃ kuryāt tatra narādhipa \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О Best of the rulers, one who meets with his death there, he achieves the bliss till the sun and the moon shines.

## \|\| 2.41.24 \|\|

*akṣayaṃ modate kālaṃ yāvaccandradivākarau \|*  
*narmadātaṭamāśritya tiṣṭhante ye tu mānavāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A person who takes refuge over the banks of Narmada, and starts living there, he achieves the heaven after his death like the meritorious sages of good conduct.

## \|\| 2.41.25 \|\|

*te mṛtāḥ svargamāyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā \|*  
*tato dīpteśvaraṃ gacched vyāsatīrthaṃ tapovanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. From there, one should move on to Dlptes'vara tirtha. It is a penance grove otherwise called Vyasatirtha.

## \|\| 2.41.26 \|\|

*nivartitā purā tatra vyāsabhītā mahānadī \|*  
*huṅkāritā tu vyāsena dakṣiṇena tato gatā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In ancient times, getting terrified, the river Narmada had returned to this place and with the performing of a Humkara sound by Vyasa, she took a turn towards the south.

## \|\| 2.41.27 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt tasmiṃstīrthe yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*prītastasya bhaved vyāso vāñchitaṃ labhate phalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О Yudhisthira, one who goes round this tirtha, the sage Vyasa feeling pleased with him, grant him the desired boon.

## \|\| 2.41.28 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra ikṣunadyāstu saṃgamam \|*  
*trailokyaviśrutaṃ puṇyaṃ tatra sannihitaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О Rajendra, thereafter one should go to the confluence of the Iksu river which is quite auspicious, in which lord Shiva always resides. By taking a bath there, a person achieves the position of a Ganapati.

## \|\| 2.41.29-30 \|\|

*tatra stanātvā naro rājan gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*skandatīrthaṃ tato gacchet sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ājanmanaḥ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ snātastīvraṃ vyapohati \|*  
*tatra devāḥ sagandharvā bhavātmajamanuttamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Thereafter, one should go to the Skanda tirtha, which removes all the sins. By taking a bath there, all the sins of earlier births are washed out. Here all the Devas, together with the Gandharvas, adore lord Skanda, the bearer of Shakti, the noble-souled excellent son of Shiva.

## \|\| 2.41.31 \|\|

*upāsate mahātmānaṃ skandaṃ śaktidhiraṃ prabhum \|*  
*tato gacchedāṅgirasaṃ snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. From there, one should go to the Angiras tirtha and take bath there. A person who does so, earns the merit of donating a thousand cows and reaches Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.41.32-33 \|\|

*gosahasraphalaṃ prāpya rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*aṅgirā yatra deveśaṃ brahmaputro vṛṣadhvajam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tapasārādhya viśveśaṃ labdhavān yogamuttamam \|*  
*kuśatīrthaṃ tato gacchet sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. This is the place, where, Angiras, the son of Brahma, had performed tapas for the bull- bannered lord of Devas and the universe, and had achieved the best of Yoga there. From there one should move on to the Kusatirtha, which removes all the sins. By taking a bath there, a person achieves the merit of performing an Asvam edha-yajha.

## \|\| 2.41.34 \|\|

*snānaṃ tatra prakurvota aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*koṭitīrthaṃ tato gacchet sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then, one should move to the Kotitirtha, which removes all the sins. By taking a bath there one earns great glory in the solar region.

## \|\| 2.41.35 \|\|

*tatra strātvā naro rājyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*candrabhāgāṃ tato gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thereafter, one should go to Candrabhaga and perform the rite of oblation there. Immediately after the bath there, the person is honoured in the region of moon.

## \|\| 2.41.36 \|\|

*snātamātro narastatra somaloke mahīyate \|*  
*narmadādakṣiṇe kūle saṃgameśvaramuttamam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. О King, there is an excellent Sangamesvara tirtha on the southern bank of the river Narmada, and by taking a bath there, a person achieves the merit of all the yajnas.

## \|\| 2.41.37-39 \|\|

*tatra snātvā naro rājan sarvayajñaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*narmadāyottare kūle tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ādityāyatanaṃ ramyamīśvareṇa tu bhāṣitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu rājendra dattvā dānaṃ tu śaktitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasya tīrthaprabhāveṇa labhate cākṣayaṃ phalam \|*  
*daridrā vyādhitā ye tu ye ca duṣkṛtakāriṇaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Similarly on the northern bank of Narmada, there is a holy place known as Adityayatana, which has been described as pleasant one even by Is'vara himself. A person by having bath there and performing charities as per his means, achieves the undecaying merit. The people who are indigent, sick, or performers of the evil deeds, they getting relieved of all the sins, proceed on to the solar region.

## \|\| 2.41.40 \|\|

*mucyante sarvapāpebhyaḥ sūryalokaṃ prayānti ca \|*  
*mārgeśvaraṃ tato gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. From there, one should go to the Matrtirtha, and take his bath there. By taking a bath there, a person reaches the heavenly world.

## \|\| 2.41.41-42 \|\|

*snātamātro narastatra svargalokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*tataḥ paścimato gacchenmarudālayamuttamam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra śucirbhūtvā prayatnataḥ \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ tu dvijo dadyād yathāvibhavavistaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. From there, one should go to westward to the excellent place of Vayu, known by Maratas'aya. О Rajendra, by taking a bath there, getting purified and with sound concentration, one should donate gold to a Brahmana according to his means. By doing so, one goes to Vayuloka boarding the Puspaka plane.

## \|\| 2.41.43 \|\|

*puṣpakeṇa vimānena vāyulokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra ahalyātīrthamuttamam \|*  
*snānamātrādapsarobhirmodate kālamakṣayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О Rajendra, from there, one should move on to Ahalya tirtha, and by taking a bath there one enjoys pleasures with apsaras for an indefinite period.

## \|\| 2.41.44-45 \|\|

*caitramāse tu saṃprāpte śuklapakṣe trayodaśī \|*  
*kāmadevadine tasminnahalyāṃ yastu pūjayet \|\| 44 \|\|*

*yatra tatra narotpanno varastatra priyo bhavet \|*  
*strīvallabho bhavecchrīmān kāmadeva ivāparaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. The thirteenth day in the bright half of the month of Caitra is the day of Kamadeva. A person who adores Ahalya there during this time, wherever he might have been born, be becomes excellent and the dearest of all. He particularly becomes the beloved of the women, besides being graceful, having enough of fortunes and turns like Kamadeva.

## \|\| 2.41.46 \|\|

*ayodhyāṃ tu samāsādya tīrthaṃ śakrasya viśrutam \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. At the bank of the excellent river Saridvara, there is a famous tirtha of Indra, known as Sakratirtha. By having a bath there, a person earns the merit of donating a thousand cows.

## \|\| 2.41.47-48 \|\|

*somatīrthaṃ tato gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 47 \|\|*

*somagrahe tu rājendra pāpakṣayakaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*trailokyaviśrutaṃ rājan somatīrthaṃ mahāphalam \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Then at the Somatirtha, one should take his bath there, by which one is relieved of all his sins. О Rajendra, at the time of the lunar eclipse, a bath there is really rewarding, which removes all the sins. О King, the Somatirtha, is well known the world over, and bestows enormous merits.

## \|\| 2.41.49 \|\|

*yastu cāndrāyaṇaṃ kuryāt tatra tīrthe samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā somalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A person who performs the Cmdrayana vrata with a concentrated mind there, he getting relieved of all the sins, becoming a purified soul, proceeds on to lunar region.

## \|\| 2.41.50 \|\|

*agnipraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryāt somatīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*jale cānaśanaṃ vāpi nāsau martyo 'bhijāyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. О Great king, a person who performs fasting or enters the fire or the water, there, he is never reborn as a mortal being.

## \|\| 2.41.51 \|\|

*stambhatīrthaṃ tato gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra somaloke mahīyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. From there, one should go to the Stambha- tirtha, should take a bath there, and by so doing one achieves Somaloka and gets established there.

## \|\| 2.41.52-53 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra viṣṇutīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*yodhanīpuramākhyātaṃ viṣṇoḥ sthānamanuttamam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*asurā yodhitāstatra vāsudevena koṭiśaḥ \|*  
*tatra tīrthaṃ samutpannaṃ viṣṇuśrīko bhavediha \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. О Rajendra, one should go to the Visnu-tirtha from there which is the abode of lord Visnu. Lord Vasudeva, had fought with crores of demons there who were destroyed. As a result of this, Visnu-tirtha emerged there. A person who serves this place, he becomes gracefi.il like Visnu. By fasting there for a day and night, the sin of brahmahatya is removed.

## \|\| 2.41.54-55 \|\|

*ahorātropavāsena brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|*  
*narmadādakṣiṇe kūle tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*kāmatīrthamiti khyātaṃ yatra kāmor'cayad bhavam \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe naraḥ snātvā upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. On the southern bank of Narmada, there is an extremely beautiful tirtha known as Kamatirtha, where the god of love, had adored lord Shiva. One who taking bath in that tirtha performs the fast, he turns as beautiful as the god of love and gets established in Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.41.56-57 \|\|

*kusumāyudharūpeṇa rudroloke mahīyate \|*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra brahmatīrthamanuttamam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*umāhakamiti khyātaṃ tatra saṃtarpayet pitṝn \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāmamāvāsyāṃ śrdhaṃ kuryād yathāvidhi \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. О Rajendra, thereafter, one should go to Brahmatirtha, which is known as Umahaka. One should perform there, oblation for the Pitrs. One should perform Srdddha on the moonless and the full moon days appropriately.

## \|\| 2.41.58 \|\|

*gajarūpā śilā tatra toyamadhye vyavasthitā \|*  
*tasmiṃstu dāpayet piṇḍān vaiśākhyāntu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. A stone slab of the size of an elephant is fixed in the middle of the water. One should perform pindadana with concentrated mind therein, during the month of Vaisakha.

## \|\| 2.41.59 \|\|

*snātvā samāhitamanā dambhamātsaryavarjitaḥ \|*  
*tṛpyanti pitarastasya yāvat tiṣṭhati medinī \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. One should take bath there, with concentrated mind, discarding wickedness and jealousy, the one who does so, his manes remain pleased till the earth remains.

## \|\| 2.41.60 \|\|

*siddheśvaraṃ tato gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra gāṇapatyapadaṃ labhet \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. From there he should go to Visvesvara tirtha and take his bath there and by so doing, one gets the position of Ganapati.

## \|\| 2.41.61 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra liṅgo yatra janārdanaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu rājendra viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. О Rajendra, there is a place, where Janardana, is himself consecrated in the form of linga and one should go to that place. By taking a bath there, one is respected in Visnuloka.

## \|\| 2.41.62 \|\|

*yatra nārāyaṇo devo munonāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*svātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa liṅgaṃ tat paramaṃ padam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Lord Narayana here had displayed before the devoted sages his linga form. Because of this, this llngatirtha is known as Visnu-dhama.

## \|\| 2.41.63-65 \|\|

*aṅkolaṃ tu tato gacchet sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*snānaṃ dānaṃ ca tatraiva brāhmaṇānāṃ ca bhojanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*piṇḍapridānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ pretyānantaphalapradam \|*  
*traiyambakena toyena yaścaruṃ śrapayet tataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*aṅkolamūle dadyācca piṇḍāṃścaiva yathāvidhi \|*  
*tāritāḥ pitarastena tṛpyantyācandratārakam \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-65. Thereafter, one should go to Akolla tirtha, where the charities perfonned by a person, besides the serving of the food to Brahmanas, and the performing of the pindadana, bestows unlimited reward after death. A Brahmana who reciting the Trayambaka mantra, cooking the Caru in the water, gives the pindas at the root of the Ankolla plant (Alangium Hexapetalum), all his manes are redeemed and they remain satisfied, till the stars and the moon shine.

## \|\| 2.41.66 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra tāpaseśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu rājendra prāpnuyāt tapasaḥ phalam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. О Rajendra, thereafter, one should go to the excellent Tapases'vara tirtha and by taking a bath there, one achieves the merit of performing the tapas.

## \|\| 2.41.67 \|\|

*śuklatīrthaṃ tato gacchet sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*nāsti tena sama tīrthaṃ narmadāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Thereafter, one should go to Suklatirtha which removes all the sins. О Yudhisthira, there is no other tirtha over Narmada comparable to the same.

## \|\| 2.41.68 \|\|

*darśanāt sparśanāt tasya snānadānatapojapāt \|*  
*homāccaivopavāsācca śuklatīrthe mahat phalam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. One achieves a great merit by its sight, taking a bath there, performing the charities, tapas, japam, homa and fasting there.

## \|\| 2.41.69 \|\|

*yojanaṃ tat smṛtaṃ kṣetraṃ devagandharvasevitam \|*  
*śuklatīrthamiti khyātaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. This place is spread in an area of a yojana. The Suklatirtha is quite well known and is served by the gods and the Gandharvas and also removes all the sins.

## \|\| 2.41.70 \|\|

*pādapāgreṇa dṛṣṭena brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|*  
*devyā saha sadā bhargastatra tiṣṭhati śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Even if the holy centre is seen from the top of a tree from far, it dispels the sin of Brahmana- slaughter. Lord Sankara and goddess Parvati reside there.

## \|\| 2.41.71 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ vaiśākhe māsi suvrata \|*  
*kailāsāccābhiniṣkramya tatra sannihito haraḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. О king of holy rites, on the dark fourteenth day of the month of Vaisakha, lord Shiva arrives here from his abode and lives here.

## \|\| 2.41.72 \|\|

*devadānavagandharvāḥ siddhavidyādharāstathā \|*  
*gaṇāścāpsarasāṃ nāgāstatra tiṣṭhanti puṅgava \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The best of the gods, demons, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Vidyadharas, the attendants of Shiva, the celestial damsels, and the leading Nagas, also stay there.

## \|\| 2.41.73 \|\|

*rajakena yathā vastraṃ śuklaṃ bhavati vāriṇā \|*  
*ājanmani kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ śuklatīrthe vyapohati \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. As a dirty cloth is deprived of the dirt of stains, by washing the same with water, similarly, by bathing in the Suklatirtha, all the sins since birth are removed.

## \|\| 2.41.74 \|\|

*snānaṃ dānaṃ tapaḥ śrāddhamanantaṃ tatra dṛśyate \|*  
*śuklatīrthāt paraṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The bath taken there and the charities, penance and sraddha performed there, bestow everlasting reward. There had never been a tlrlha better than Suklatirtha not shall it be there in future.

## \|\| 2.41.75 \|\|

*pūrve vayasi karmāṇi kṛtvā pāpāni mānavaḥ \|*  
*ahorātropavāsena śuklatīrthe vyapohati \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. All the sins committed by a person in earlier times are washed out by fasting here for a day and night.

## \|\| 2.41.76 \|\|

*kārtikasya tu māsasya kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśī \|*  
*ghṛtena snāpayed devamupoṣya parameśvaram \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Fasting on the black fourteenth day of the month of Karttika, one should bathe Paramesvara with ghee and by so doing he living in the abode of Ishvara with twenty one generations of his family, never falls off from there.

## \|\| 2.41.77 \|\|

*ekaviṃśatkulopeto na cyavedaiśvarāt padāt \|*  
*tapasā brahmacaryeṇa yajñadānena vā punaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The position one achieves in the Suklatirtha cannot be achieved by performing of enormous penance, celibacy, sacrifices and charities.

## \|\| 2.41.78 \|\|

*na tāṃ gatimavāpnoti śuklatīrthe tu yāṃ labhet \|*  
*śuklatīrthaṃ mahātīrthamṛṣisiddhaniṣevitam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Suklatirtha is a great holy place, served by the Rishis and the Siddhas. By taking a bath there, a person is never reborn.

## \|\| 2.41.79-80 \|\|

*tatra snātvā naro rājan punarjanma na vindati \|*  
*ayane vā caturdaśyāṃ saṃkrāntau viṣuve tathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*snātvā tu sopavāsaḥ san vijitātmā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*dānaṃ dadyād yathāśakti prīyetāṃ hariśaṅkarau \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. A person should give away charities there with great concentration and full self-control during the Uttardyana or Daksinayana, and on the fourteenth day of the fortnight, the devotee should after bath, observe fast. Hari and Sankara will become delighted.

## \|\| 2.41.81-82 \|\|

*etat tīrthaprabhāveṇa sarvaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|*  
*anāthaṃ durgataṃ vipraṃ nāthavantamathāpi vā \|\| 81 \|\|*

*udvādayati yastīrthe tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*yāvat tadromasaṃkhyā tu tatprasūtikuleṣu ca \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. Because of the influence of this tirtha everything become everlasting. A person who arranges marriage of a destitute or an unfortunate Brahmana, you listen to the merits he earns for the same. Whatever be the number of the hair on the bodies of his own as well as his progeny, he earns grace in Rudraloka for as many thousand years.

## \|\| 2.41.83-84 \|\|

*tāvad varṣasahasrāṇi rudraloke mahīyate \|*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra yamatīrtha manuttamam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ māghamāse yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*snānaṃ kṛtvā naktabhījī na paśyed yonisaṅkaṭam \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. О Rajendra, from there, one should move on to Yama tirtha. О Yudhisthira, on the fourteenth day in the dark half of the month of Magha, one should take bath in the Yamatirtha. One who takes food during the night alone, there, he never experiences the pain of being in womb.

## \|\| 2.41.85-87 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra eraṇḍītīrthamuttamam \|*  
*saṃgame tu naraḥ snāyādupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayedekaṃ koṭirbhavati bhojitāḥ \|*  
*eraṇḍīsaṃgame snātvā bhaktibhāvāt turañjitaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*mṛttikāṃ śirasi sthāpya avagāhya ca tajjalam \|*  
*narmadodakasaṃmiśraṃ mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. О Rajendra, thereafter, one should move on to the Erandltirtha and should have a bath at the confluence of the rivers, and then, the one while fasting, if serves food to a Brahmana, he earns the merit of serving food to a crore of Brahmanas. Taking his bath at the confluence of Erandl, getting filled with devotion, applying the clay of the river to his forehead, one who enters the eater of Narmada, at the confluence, such a person is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 2.41.88 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra tīrthaṃ kārṇāṭikeśvaram \|*  
*gaṅgāvatarate tatra dine puṇye na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. О Rajendra, thereafter, one should go to Kallolakesvara-tirtha, where the Ganga descends into it on the auspicious days.

## \|\| 2.41.89 \|\|

*tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca dattvā caiva yathāvidhi \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Taking a bath and sipping the water there, and performing the charities appropriately, a person getting relieved of all the sins, is honoured in Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.41.90 \|\|

*nanditīrthaṃ tato gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*prīyate tasya nandīśaḥ somaloke mahīyate \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Then, reaching the Nanditirtha, one should take a bath there. One who does so, pleases Nandlsvara and is respected immensely in Somaloka.

## \|\| 2.41.91 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra tīrthaṃ tvanarakaṃ śubham \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājan narakaṃ naiva paśyati \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. О Rajendra, a tirtha named Anaraka is there which is quite auspicious. О King, by taking a bath there, a person has never to face the hell.

## \|\| 2.41.92 \|\|

*tasmiṃstīrthe tu rājendra svānyasthīni vinikṣipet \|*  
*rūpavān jāyate loke dhanabhogasamanvitaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A person should consign the ashes of his relatives there. By so doing, the dead person, is reborn extremely beautiful and enjoys various pleasures.

## \|\| 2.41.93 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra kapilātīrtha muttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājan gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. О Rajendra, thereafter, one should go to the excellent Kapila tirtha. By taking a bath there, a person earns the merit of donating a thousand cows.

## \|\| 2.41.94-95 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhamāse tu saṃprāpte caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tatropoṣya naro bhaktyā dadyād dīpaṃ ghṛtena tu \|\| 94 \|\|*

*ghṛtena snāpayed rudraṃ saghṛtaṃ śrīphalaṃ dahet \|*  
*ghaṇṭābharaṇasaṃyuktāṃ kapilāṃ vai pradāpayet \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. During the month of Jyestha, on the fourteenth day of the fortnight, one should fast and devotedly give away a lamp, along with ghee in charity. Rudra should also be bathed with ghee. A cow adored with the bell and other ornaments should be given in charity. Then he shall attain riches as a benefit thereof.

## \|\| 2.41.96 \|\|

*sarvābharaṇasaṃyuktaḥ sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*śivatulyabalo bhūtvā śivavat krīḍate ciram \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. He shall himself become adorned with all the ornaments, and will be respected by the gods, and becomes powerful like Shiva, and then sports for long as Shiva.

## \|\| 2.41.97 \|\|

*aṅgārakadine prāpte caturthyāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*snāpayitvā śivaṃ dadyād brāhmaṇebhyastu bhojanam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. When the fourth day of the moon falls on Tuesday, one should perform ablution rite of Shiva here, and food should be given to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 2.41.98 \|\|

*sarvabhogasamāyukto vimānaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ \|*  
*gatvā śakrasya bhavanaṃ śakreṇa saha modate \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. By so doing, the concerned person enjoying all the pleasures, can move at all the places without any obstruction. Then boarding the planes, he enjoys all the pleasures in the abode of Indra. Then falling from the heaven, he becomes wealthy possessing all the fortunes and worldly enjoyments.

## \|\| 2.41.99 \|\|

*tataḥ svargāt paribhraṣṭo dhanavān bhogavān bhavet \|*  
*aṅgārakanavamyāṃ tu amāvāsyāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. One should perform the ablution rite of Shiva on Tuesdays, on the ninth day and on the new moon day assiduously, as a result of which he becomes handsome endowed with comely features.

## \|\| 2.41.100-101 \|\|

*snāpayet tatra yatnena rūpavān subhago bhavet \|*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra gaṇeśvaramanuttamam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*śrāvaṇe māsī saṃprāpte kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśī \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 101 \|\|*

100-101. О Rajendra, thereafter, one should go to the Ganes'vara-tirtha. On the arrival of the month of Sravana, on the dark fourteenth day of the month, one who takes his bath there, he is well- established in Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.41.102-103 \|\|

*pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā mucyate 'sāvṝṇatrayāt \|*  
*gaṅgeśvarasamīpe tu gaṅgāvadanamuttamam \|\| 102 \|\|*

*akāmo vā sakāmo vā tatra snātvā tu mānavaḥ \|*  
*ājanmajanitaiḥ pāpairmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

102-103. By offering oblation to the Pitrs, one is relieved of all the three debts. There is a Gangavadana tirtha close to the Ganesvara tirtha. One who takes a bath with or without desire, he is freed of all the sins throughout the life. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.41.104 \|\|

*tasya vai paścime deśe samīpe nātidūrataḥ \|*  
*daśāśvamedhikaṃ tīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. On the western side, not very far, of the aforesaid tirtha, there is a well known tirtha known as Dasasvamedhika.

## \|\| 2.41.105-106 \|\|

*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ māsi bhādrapade śubhe \|*  
*amāvasyāṃ naraḥ snātvā pūjayed vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 105 \|\|*

*kāñcanena vimānena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā \|*  
*gatvā rudrapuraṃ ramyaṃ rudreṇa saha modate \|\| 106 \|\|*

105-106. In the auspicious month of Bhadrapada, one who observing the fast for a night, adores lord Shiva there, he proceeds to the place of bull- bannered deity Нага, on the new moon day, boarding a beautifully decorated with clusters of tinkling bells, golden aerial chariot and rejoice with Rudra.

## \|\| 2.41.107 \|\|

*sarvatra sarvadivase snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kuryādaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. A person who perform the rite of ablution on any day at any place, and offers oblation to the Pitrs, he achieves the reward of Asvamedha sacrifice.

## Chapter 42. Description of holy places on the bank of Narmada

## \|\| 2.42.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra bhṛgutīrtha manuttamam \|*  
*tatra devo bhṛguḥ purvaṃ rudramārādhayat purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The sage Markandeya said, “O Rajendra, besides the tirthas described earlier, one should know about the excellent Bhrgu tirtha. In earlier times, the sage Bhrgu had worshipped lord Shiva there.

## \|\| 2.42.2 \|\|

*darśanāt tasya devasya sadyaḥ pāpāt pramucyate \|*  
*etat kṣetraṃ suvipulaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Therefore, by coming in face to face with Rudra, who is established there, one is atonce relieved of all his sins. This holy centre is very large and is destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 2.42.3-4 \|\|

*tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ \|*  
*upānahostathā yugmaṃ deyamannaṃ sakāñcanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhojanaṃ ca yathāśakti tadasyākṣayamucyate \|*  
*kṣaranti sarvadānāni yajñadānaṃ tapaḥ kriyā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. After having a bath in Narmada, a person after his death proceeds on to the heaven. By visiting the Bhrgu-tirtha, a person should give away in charity, some gold, a chariot horse, a pair of sandals or the food items, according to his capacity. All these are bound to yield enonnous reward. О Yudhisthira, all the charities, the yajnas and the penances fade out in due course of time, but the penance performed at Bhrgutirtha remains everlasting.

## \|\| 2.42.5 \|\|

*akṣayaṃ tat tapastaptaṃ bhṛgutīrthe yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*tasyaiva tapasogreṇa tuṣṭena tripurāriṇā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О Yudhisthira, Lord Rudra, the enemy of the Tripuras, getting pleased with the tapas of Bhrgu, lives there for ever. It is said by Rudra, the enemy of Tripuras.

## \|\| 2.42.6-7 \|\|

*sānnidhyaṃ tatra kathitaṃ bhṛgutīrthe yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra gautameśvaramuttamam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yatrārādhya triśūlāṅkaṃ gautamaḥ siddhimāpnuyāt \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājan upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. О Rajendra, thereafter one should go to Gautamesvara, the place of pilgrimage. By adoration of the lord Shiva, the holder of a trident, the great sage Gautama, had attained Siddhi. О King, by taking a bath at that holy place and by fasting there, a person proceeds on to Brahmaloka boarding the aerial chariot of gold, where he is respected immensely.

## \|\| 2.42.8 \|\|

*kāñcanena vimānena brahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*vṛṣotsargaṃ tato gacchecchāśvataṃ padamāpnuyāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereafter, a person should visit the place of pilgrimage known by the name of Vrsotsarga. It bestows the moksa. The people who are under the influence of the Maya of Visnu are ignorant of the glory of this place.

## \|\| 2.42.9-10 \|\|

*na jānanti narā mūḍhā viṣṇormāyāvimohitāḥ \|*  
*dhautapāpaṃ tato gacched dhautaṃ yatra vṛṣeṇa tu \|\| 9 \|\|*

*narmadāyāṃ sthitaṃ rājan sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Thereafter, one should visit the place of Dhautapapa, where are washed all the sins by means of this meritorious act. О King, this place of pilgrimage is also located at the bank of riverNamada, and removes all the sins. By having a bath at this tirtha, a person is relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya.

## \|\| 2.42.11 \|\|

*tatra tīrthe tu rājendra prāṇatyāgaṃ karoti yaḥ \|*  
*caturbhujastrinetraśca haratulyabalo bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Besides the above, whosoever meets with hjs death there, he taking the four-armed form, with three eyes, becomes as powerful as Нага himself.

## \|\| 2.42.12 \|\|

*vaset kalpāyutaṃ sāgraṃ śivatulyaparākramaḥ \|*  
*kālena mahatā jātaḥ pṛthivyāmekarāḍ bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Becoming powerful like Shiva, he lives in Shivaloka for a period of more than ten thousand kalpas there. After a long time, he is reborn on earth as a Cakravartin king,

## \|\| 2.42.13 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra haṃsatīrtha manuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājan brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О Rajendra, there is the Hastatirtha thereafter. By taking a bath there, a person earns great glory in Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.42.14 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra siddho yatra janārdanaḥ \|*  
*varāhatīrtha mākhyātaṃ viṣṇulokagatipradam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereafter, there is a Varaha tirtha, which leads one to Visnuloka. This is the place where Janardana is settled.

## \|\| 2.42.15 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra candratīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ viśeṣeṇa snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereafter, there is the Candra-tirtha. A person should take a bath there particularly on the full-moon day. By taking a bath there, a person becomes the sole emperor on the earth.

## \|\| 2.42.16 \|\|

*snātamātro narastatra candraloke bhavet \|*  
*devatīrtha tato gacchet sarvadevanamakṛtam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Rajendra, thereafter, one should go to the Devatirtha-the place which is worshipped even by the gods. By taking bath there, one rejoices along with deities.

## \|\| 2.42.17 \|\|

*tatra snātvā ca rājendra daivataiḥ saha modate \|*  
*tatra sanātvā ca rājenadra daivataiḥ saha modate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О Rajendra, then, one should visit the excellent Sankha-tirtha. Whatever charities are performed there, are multiplied into crores, in reward.

## \|\| 2.42.18 \|\|

*yat tatra dīyate dānaṃ sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra śikhitīrthamanuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. О Rajendra, one should visit the Paitamaha tirtha as well. A person who performs sraddha there, it bestows the everlasting reward.

## \|\| 2.42.19 \|\|

*yatatra dīyate śrāddhaṃ svaṃ tasyākṣayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sāvitrītīrthamāsādya yastu prāṇān parityajet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By reaching the Savitrl tirtha, if a person meets with his end there, he washing all his sins achieves the Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.42.20 \|\|

*vidhūya sarvapāpāni brahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*manoharaṃ tu tatraiva tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. There is also a place of pilgrimage known as Manohara. By taking a bath there a person is established in Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.42.21-22 \|\|

*tatra snātvā naro rājan daivataiḥ saha modate \|*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra mānasaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*snātvā tatra naro rājan rudraloke mahīyate \|*  
*svargabinduṃ tato gacchettīrthaṃ devanamaskṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Thereafter, there is an excellent Kanyatirtha. By taking a bath there, a person is relieved of all the sins. One should take a bath there on the third day of the bright fortnight and by so doing, a person immediately becomes the sole sovereign ruler over the earth.

## \|\| 2.42.23 \|\|

*snātamātro narastatra pṛthivyāmekarāḍ bhavet \|*  
*sargavinaduṃ tato gacchettīrthaṃ devanamaskṛtam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. There is also a holy place known by the name of Sargabindu. By taking a bath there a person never faces any misfortune.

## \|\| 2.42.24 \|\|

*tatra snātvā naro rājan durgatiṃ naiva gacchati \|*  
*apsareśaṃ tato gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thereafter, one should go to Apsaresvara tirtha and take his bath there. By so doing he enjoys all the sports in the heaven with the celestial damsels.

## \|\| 2.42.25-26 \|\|

*krīḍate nākalokastho hyapsarobhiḥ sa modate \|*  
*tato gaccheta rājendra bhārabhūtimanuttamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*upoṣitor'cayedīśaṃ rudraloke mahīyate \|*  
*asmiṃstīrthe mṛto rājan gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. From there, one should go to the BharabhUti- tirtha. By fasting there, in case one adores Ishvara, he is respected in the Rudraloka. By meeting with his end at this place, a person earns the position of a Ganapati.

## \|\| 2.42.27 \|\|

*kārtike māsi deveśamarcayet pārvatīpatim \|*  
*aśvamedhād daśaguṇaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In the month of Karttika, a person should worship Shiva, the lord of Parvati and according to the sages, one who does so, he achieves the merit ten times more than the Asvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.42.28 \|\|

*vṛṣabhaṃ yaḥ prayaccheta tatra kundendusaprabham \|*  
*vṛṣayuktena yānena rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One who offers a white bull as lustrous as the jasmine flower and the moon, there, he reaches the heaven (Rudraloka) in a vehicle, in which the bulls are yoked.

## \|\| 2.42.29 \|\|

*etat tīrthaṃ samāsādya yastu prāṇān parityajet \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Reaching this tirtha, one who meets with the end of his life, he getting relieved of all the sins, reaches Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.42.30 \|\|

*jalapraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryāt tasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*haṃsayuktena yānena svargalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. О Great king, a person who enters the water of this tirtha, he mounting a vehicle driven by swans proceeds on to the heaven.

## \|\| 2.42.31 \|\|

*eraṇḍyā narmadāyāstu saṃgamaṃ lokaviśrutam \|*  
*tatra tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The confluence of Erandi and Narmada river is well known the world over. This place of confluence is extremely sacred, and removes all the sins.

## \|\| 2.42.32 \|\|

*upavāsaparo bhūtvā nityaṃ vrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu rājendra mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Therefore, a person fasting there, should perform holy rites regularly. A person who takes a bath there, is relieved of the sin of brahmahatya even.

## \|\| 2.42.33-34 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra narmadodadhisaṃgamam \|*  
*jamadagniriti khyātaḥ siddho yatra janārdanaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājan narmadodadhisaṃgame \|*  
*triguṇaṃ cāśvamedhasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. О Rajendra, one should go to the confluence of Narmada and the ocean, known as Jamadagni, where lord Janardana is present, and by taking a bath there, a person achieves merits three times more than the Asvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 2.42.35 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra piṅgaleśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājan rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. О Rajendra, from there, one should go to the Pingalesvara-tirtha and by taking a bath there a person is respected in Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.42.36 \|\|

*tatropavāsaṃ yaḥ kṛtvā paśyeta vimaleśvaram \|*  
*saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ hitvā yāti śivālayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A person who visits Pingales'vara, and fast there, he is relieved of the sins performed in seven births and goes to Shiva’s abode.

## \|\| 2.42.37 \|\|

*tato gaccheta rājendra ālikātīrthamuttamam \|*  
*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ niyato niyatāśanaḥ \|*  
*asya tīrthasya māhātmyānmucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. From there, one should go to the Alakatirtha. Fasting there for a night, getting disciplined, one should consume satvika food and by so doing, a person is relieved of the sin of brahmahatya, because of the glory of this tirtha.

## \|\| 2.42.38 \|\|

*etāni tava saṃkṣepāt prādhānyāt kathitāni tu \|*  
*na śakyā vistarād vaktuṃ saṃkhyā tīrtheṣupāṇḍava \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О Son of Pandu, whatever tirthas have been described by me, in brief, are the prominent ones. All the tirthas of Narmada cannot, however, he described in detail or comprehensively.

## \|\| 2.42.39-40 \|\|

*eṣā pavitrā vimalā nadī trailokyaviśrutā \|*  
*narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā mahādevasya vallabhā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*manasā saṃsmaredyastu narmadāṃ vai yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*cāndrāyaṇaśataṃ sāgraṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Narmada, having the spotless and sacred water is well known in the three worlds and is best of all the rivers. She is the beloved of lord Mahadeva. О Yudhisthira, one who remembers Narmada mentally, he earns merits much more than the performing that of a hundred Candrayana vratas. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 2.42.41-42 \|\|

*aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā nāstikyaṃ ghoramāśritāḥ \|*  
*patanti narake ghore ityāha parameśvaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*narmadāṃ sevate nityaṃ svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tena puṇyā nadī jñeyā brahmahatyāpahāriṇī \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. But the one who is devoid of devotion or is an atheist, he fall in the terrific hell. This is what has been ordained by lord Shiva, Lord Mahesvara, himself resorts to Narmada. Therefore, this river should be adored as an extremely sacred one, which removes the grave sins like brahmahatya.

## Chapter 43. The glory of the tirthas of Narmada river

## \|\| 2.43.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*idaṃ trailokyavikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ naimiśamuttamam \|*  
*mahādevapriyakaraṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “there is a Naimisa-tirtha which is famous in the three worlds and is liked by lord Mahadeva. It removes the grave sins.

## \|\| 2.43.2 \|\|

*mahādevaṃ didṛkṣūṇāmṛṣīṇaṇāṃ parameṣṭhinām \|*  
*brahāmaṇā nirmitaṃ sthānaṃ tapastaptuṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Best of the Brahmanas, Brahma had created this place for the Rishis who intended to perform tapas for Shiva in order to have an audience with the lord.

## \|\| 2.43.3-4 \|\|

*marīcayo 'trayo viprā vasiṣṭhāḥ kratavastathā \|*  
*bhṛgavo 'ṅgirasaḥ pūrvā brahmāṇaṃ kamalodbhavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sametya sarvavaradaṃ caturmūrti caturmukham \|*  
*pṛcchanti praṇipatyainaṃ viśvakarmāṇamacyutam \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. О Brahmanas, in earlier times, six Brahmana families viz. from the races of Marici, Atri, Vasistha, Kratn, Bhrgu and Angiras, enquired from Brahma, who grants all the boons, was bom of lotus, having four faces, and the creator of the universe.

## \|\| 2.43.5 \|\|

*ṣaṭkulīyā ūcuḥ*  
*bhagavan devamīśānaṃ bhargamekaṃ kapardinam \|*  
*kenopāyena paśyāmo brūhi devanamaskṛtam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Rishis bom in the six races, asked him- О Lord, by what means, can we have an audience with the illustrious Isanadeva, the god with matted hair? You please tell us.

## \|\| 2.43.6 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*satraṃ sahasramāsadhvaṃ vāṅmanodoṣavarjitāḥ \|*  
*deśaṃ ca vaḥ pravakṣyāmi yasmin deśe cariṣyatha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Brahma said-All of you getting relieved of all the blemishes of mind and speech, should perform a sacrificial session of one thousand years. I shall point out the place where (this is to be done).

## \|\| 2.43.7 \|\|

*muktvā manomayaṃ cakraṃ sa sṛṣṭvā tānuvāca ha \|*  
*kṣiptametanmayā cakramanuvrajata mā ciram \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus speaking, Brahma then touched the mind wheel and said to the sages, “You should follow this wheel being issued by me. Do not delay.

## \|\| 2.43.8 \|\|

*yatrāsya nemiḥ śīryeta sa deśaḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ \|*  
*tato mumoca taccakraṃ te ca tatsamanuvrajan \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Wherever this cakra (wheel) gets shattered, it would be the auspicious place for the performing of tapas as well as the yajnas.” Thereafter Brahma released the mind wheel, and they followed it.

## \|\| 2.43.9 \|\|

*tasya vai vrajataḥ kṣipraṃ yatra nemiraśīryata \|*  
*naimisaṃ tatsmṛtaṃ nāmnā puṇyaṃ sarvatra pūjitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The wheel moved quickly and the place where it was shattered, that place came to be known as Naimisa. That auspicious place was adored by all.

## \|\| 2.43.10 \|\|

*siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ yakṣagandharvasevitam \|*  
*sthānaṃ bhagavataḥ śaṃbhoretannaimiśamuttamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It was filled with the Siddhas and Caranas besides was served by the Yaksas and Gandharvas. This Naimisaranya is therefore the auspicious abode of lord Sambhu.

## \|\| 2.43.11 \|\|

*atra devāḥ sagandharvāḥ sayakṣoragarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*tapastaptvā purā devā lebhire pravarān varān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Earlier, The Gods, Gandharvas, Yaksas, Nagas and Raksasas, performed tapas here and had achieved the best of boons.

## \|\| 2.43.12 \|\|

*imaṃ deśaṃ samāśritya ṣaṭkulīyāḥ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*satreṇārādhya deveśaṃ dṛṣṭavanto maheśvaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Rishis of the aforesaid six races, dwelling in this region, by performing the yajnas with the concentrated minds, and adoring lord Shiva, perceived Mahes'vara.

## \|\| 2.43.13 \|\|

*atra dānaṃ tapastaptaṃ snānaṃ japyādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*ekaikaṃ pāvayet pāpaṃ saptajanmakṛtaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О Brahmanas, the charities of food given there and the sraddha or tapas or yajna performed there, removes the sins committed in the past seven births.

## \|\| 2.43.14-15 \|\|

*atra pūrvaṃ sa bhagavānṛṣīṇāṃ satramāsatām \|*  
*provāca vāyurbrahmāṇḍaṃ purāṇaṃ brahmabhāṣitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*atra devo mahādevo rudrāṇyā kila viśvakṛt \|*  
*ramate 'dhyāpi bhagavān pramathaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. This is the place where lord Brahma had narrated the Brahmanda Parana sanctified by the description of the Brahman, to the sages who were performing the Satra. Even today, lord Mahadeva of universal vision, sports about alongwith with his spouse Rudrani and Pramathas live here.

## \|\| 2.43.16 \|\|

*atra prāṇān parityajya niyamena dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*brahmalokaṃ gamiṣyanti yatra gatvā na jāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The people of the three varnas, when living here, observing the rules and meet with their end, they reach Brahmaloka reaching which, one does not have to be reborn on earth.

## \|\| 2.43.17 \|\|

*anyacca tīrthapravaraṃ jāpyeśvaramitiśrutam \|*  
*jajāpa rudramaniśaṃ yatra nandī mahāgaṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. There is another tirtha known as Japyesvara tirtha which is an excellent one, where Nandin, the great Gana, always recites the Rudra stotra.

## \|\| 2.43.18 \|\|

*prītastasya mahādevo devyā saha pinākadhṛk \|*  
*dadāvātmasamānatvaṃ mṛtyuvañcanameva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Getting pleased, the holder of the Pinaka bow, Shiva had appeared with the goddess Parvati here. He bestowed Nandin with the boon of becoming free from death.

## \|\| 2.43.19 \|\|

*abhūdṛṣiḥ sa dharmātmā śilādo nāma dharmavit \|*  
*ārādhayanmahādevaṃ putrārthaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The story of the birth of Nandin is like this. Silada was an immensely learned and religious minded sage. He adored bull-bannered lord Shiva, for having a son.

## \|\| 2.43.20 \|\|

*tasya varṣasahasrānte tapyamānasya viśvakṛt \|*  
*śarvaḥ somo gaṇavṛto varado 'smītyabhāṣata \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Performing the tapas, a thousand years elapsed. Ultimately, lord Shiva appeared there with his ganas and said to the sage, “I shall bestow a boon on you.”

## \|\| 2.43.21 \|\|

*sa vavre varamīśānaṃ vareṇyaṃ girijāpatim \|*  
*ayonijaṃ mṛtyuhīnaṃ dehi putraṃ tvayā samam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then, Silada asked for a boon from Shiva, the foremost deity, the consort of the daughter of the mountain, “You get me a son like yourself, who should be free from death and should be bom without womb.

## \|\| 2.43.22 \|\|

*tathāstvityāha bhagavān devyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*paśyatastasya viprarṣerantardhānaṃ gato haraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then lord Shiva with Parvati said, “Be it so.” Thereafter, both of them disappeared in full view of the sage.

## \|\| 2.43.23-25 \|\|

*tato yiyakṣuḥ svāṃ bhūmiṃ śilādo dharmavittamaḥ \|*  
*cakarṣa lāṅgalenorvoṃ bhittvādṛśyata śobhanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*saṃvartakānalaprakhyaḥ kumāraḥ prahasanniva \|*  
*rūpalāvaṇyasaṃpannastejasā bhāsayan diśaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kumāratulyo 'pratimo meghagambhīrayā girā \|*  
*śilādaṃ tāta tāteti prāha nandī punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. Thereafter, the religious minded Silada, ploughed the land with the intention of performing a yajna. While ploughing the earth, he found an infant, shining like the Samvartaka fire (fire at the time of dissolution), with beautiful looks, who was illumining all the directions with his lustre, while smiling. The infant was quite handsome like Karttikeya. The infant Nandin then addressed Silada in his deep voice as l4ata" or a father. The same infant came to be known as Nandin, or the one who delights the people.

## \|\| 2.43.26 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā nandanaṃ jātaṃ śilādaḥ pariṣasvaje \|*  
*munibhyo darśayāmāsa ye tadāśramavāsinaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The delightful son, when found by Silada was embraced by him and he showed him to the Rishis living in the asrama.

## \|\| 2.43.27 \|\|

*jātakarmādikāḥ sarvāḥ kriyāstasya cakāra ha \|*  
*upanīya yathāśāstraṃ vedamadhyāpayat sutam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thereafter, the sage performed the post-natal and and all other rites of the child, besides investing him with a sacred thread and taught him the Vedas.

## \|\| 2.43.28 \|\|

*adhītavedo bhagavān nandī matimanuttamām \|*  
*cakre maheśvaraṃ draṣṭuṃ jeṣye mṛtyumiti prabhum \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After completing the studies in the Vedas, an idea splashed in the mind of Nandin, that, he, by adoring lord Shiva-Mahesvara, shall overcome death.

## \|\| 2.43.29 \|\|

*sa gatvā saritaṃ puṇyāmekāgraśraddhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*jajāpa rudramaniśaṃ maheśāsaktamānasaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. With this resolve in his mind, he went to the sacred seashore, and with a devoted mind he started reciting the Rudra-stotra.

## \|\| 2.43.30 \|\|

*tasya koṭyāṃ tu pūrṇāyāṃ śaṅkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ \|*  
*āgatya sāmbaḥ sagaṇo varado 'smītyuvāca ha \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. After completion of the japam a crore of times, lord Sankara, favourably disposed to his devotees, with Parvati and his ganas appeared before Nandin and said, “You ask for a boon.”

## \|\| 2.43.31 \|\|

*sa vavre punarevāhaṃ japeyaṃ koṭimīśvaram \|*  
*tāvadāyurmahādeva dehīti varamīśvara \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. While seeking the boon, Nandin said, “0 Lord I intend to recite the mantra a crore of times further, you kindly grant me a boon that I should have the life upto that length.”

## \|\| 2.43.32 \|\|

*evamastviti saṃprocya devo 'pyantaradhīyata \|*  
*jajāpa koṭiṃ bhagavān bhūyastadgatamānasaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then lord Shiva, the universal soul said, “Be it so.” Thus speaking, lord Shiva disappeared with ParvatT and his ganas from that place. Thereafter Nandin devoting his mind exclusively to Shiva, performed the japam a crore of times.

## \|\| 2.43.33 \|\|

*dvitīyāyāṃ ca koṭyāṃ vai saṃpūrṇāyāṃ vṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*āgatya varado 'smīti prāha bhūtagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. And with the completion of the japam two crores of times, the bull-bannered lord Shiva again appeared before Nandin, with his goblins and said, “I am the granter of boons.”

## \|\| 2.43.34 \|\|

*tṛtīyāṃ japtumicchāmi koṭiṃ bhūyo 'pi śaṅkara \|*  
*tathāstvityāha viśvātmā devo 'pyantaradhīyata \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then Nandin said, “O Lord Sankara, “I intend to perform the third crore of japam too.” Lord Shiva said, “Be it so.” Thereafter, lord Shiva again disappeared from the scene alongwith the goddess,

## \|\| 2.43.35 \|\|

*koṭitraye 'tha saṃpūrṇe devaḥ prītamanā bhṛśam \|*  
*āgatya varado 'smīti prāha bhūtagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. When the recitation of three crores of mantras was completed the third time, lord Shiva arrived with his bhtitas, and said, “I shall grant you the boon.”

## \|\| 2.43.36 \|\|

*japeyaṃ koṭimanyāṃ vai bhūyo 'pi tava tejasā \|*  
*ityukte bhagavānāha na japtavyaṃ tvayā punaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Nandin said, “By your grace, I would like to perform the mantra recitation for a crore of times further.” At these words of Nandin, Shiva said, “There is no need for you to perform the japam further.

## \|\| 2.43.37-38 \|\|

*amaro jarayā tyakto mama pārśvagataḥ sadā \|*  
*mahāgaṇapatirdevyāḥ putro bhava maheśvaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yogīśvaro yoganetā gaṇānāmīśvareśvaraḥ \|*  
*sarvalokādhipaḥ śrīmān sarvajño madbalānvitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Now you will be deprived of old age and death, remaining with me. You will be treated as the son of Parvati and the chief of my ganas. You will be a Yoges'vara, a great Yogin, lord of the ganas, lord of all the lokas, omniscient, possessing all the fortunes, besides identical with the Yajnas.

## \|\| 2.43.39 \|\|

*jñānaṃ tanmāmakaṃ divyaṃ hastāmalakavat tava \|*  
*ābhūtasaṃplavasthāyī tato yāsyasi matpadam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The divine knowledge with me, would be accesible to you like the fruit of the myrobalan placed in the palm. You will remain in this form till the time of dissolution, after which you will achieve my region.

## \|\| 2.43.40-41 \|\|

*etaduktvā mahādevo gaṇānāhūya śaṅkaraḥ \|*  
*abhiṣekeṇa yuktena nandīśvaramayojayat \|\| 40 \|\|*

*udvāhayāmāsa ca taṃ svayameva pinākadhṛk \|*  
*marutāṃ ca śubhāṃ kanyāṃ suyaśeti ca viśrutām \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Thus speaking, Mahadeva Sankara summoned his own ganas and established Nandin as the chief of the ganas. Then lord Shiva married Nandin with Suyasa, the blessed daughter of the Maruts. He himself attained Visnuloka.

## \|\| 2.43.42 \|\|

*etajjapyeśvaraṃ sthānaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*yatra tatra mṛto martyo rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The place where Nandin had performed tapas came to be known as Japyesvara-the place sacred to Shiva. A person, who meets with his end here, he earns grace in Rudraloka.

## Chapter 44. Glory of the holy places

## \|\| 2.44.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*anyacca tīrthapravaraṃ japyeśvarasamīpataḥ \|*  
*nāmnā pañcanadaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “Close to Japyes'vara, there is another excellent tirtha known by the name of Pancanada, which is quite sacred and removes all the sins.

## \|\| 2.44.2 \|\|

*trirātropoṣitastatra pūjayitvā maheśvaram \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A person who fasting for three nights there, performs adoration of Mahesvara, is relieved of all the sins. Then he, becoming the spotless soul is established in Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.44.3-4 \|\|

*anyacca tīrthapravaraṃ śaṅkarasyāmitaujasaḥ \|*  
*mahābhairavamityuktaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tīrthānāṃ ca paraṃ tīrthaṃ vitastā paramā nadī \|*  
*sarvapāpaharā puṇyā svayameva girīndrajā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. There is another tirtha dedicated to Indra, which is known by the name of Mahabhairava. It is the best of the sacred places on the bank of Vitasta river, which also removes all the sins and it itself is bom of the king of mountains.

## \|\| 2.44.5 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ pañcatapaṃ nāma śaṃbhoramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*yatra devādidevena cakrārthaṃ pūjito bhavaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There is a holy place named Pancatapas, which is dedicated to Shiva of unlimited splendour. It is here that Bhava (Shiva) was worshipped by the overlord of the Devas for the purpose of being mighty.

## \|\| 2.44.6 \|\|

*piṇḍadānādikaṃ tatra pretyānantaphalapradam \|*  
*mṛtastatrāpi niyamād brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The pindaddna etc. performed there, bestows everlasting bliss. A person who meets with his end at that place as a result of observance of holy rites, he is adored in the Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 2.44.7 \|\|

*kāyāvarohaṇaṃ nāma mahādevālayaṃ śubham \|*  
*yatra māheśvarā dharmā munibhiḥ saṃpravartitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Besides this, there is an auspicious place known by the name of Kayavarohana where the sages had promulgated the holy dharmas or religious doctrines pertaining to lord Mahesvara.

## \|\| 2.44.8 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ tapo homa upavāsastathākṣayaḥ \|*  
*parityajati yaḥ prāṇān rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The s'rdddha, charities, tapas, homa, and fasting performed there bestow undecaying reward. By meeting with his end there, one proceeds on to Rudraloka.

## \|\| 2.44.9 \|\|

*anyacca tīrthapravaraṃ kanyātīrthamiti śrutam \|*  
*tatra gatvā tyajet prāṇāṃllokān prāpnoti śāśvatān \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is another excellent place known as Kanya-tirtha which is better than any other holy centre. A person who dies there, he achieves the everlasting lokas.

## \|\| 2.44.10 \|\|

*jāmadagnyasya tu śubhaṃ rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā tīrtha vare gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There is a tirtha dedicated to Rama, the son of Jamadagni and of unimpaired activity. By taking a bath in that tirtha, one achieves merit of donating a thousand cows.

## \|\| 2.44.11 \|\|

*mahākālamiti khyātaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|*  
*gatvā prāṇān parityajya gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There is another tirtha known by the name of Mahakala in the three worlds. A person who dies there, he becomes the chief of the Shivaganas.

## \|\| 2.44.12 \|\|

*guhyād guhyatamaṃ tīrthaṃ nakulīśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tatra sannihitaḥ śrīmān bhagavān nakulīśvaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The mystic NalailIshvara-tirtha there happens to the most sacred of all places. It is the dwelling place of the glorious lord Nakulls'vara.

## \|\| 2.44.13 \|\|

*himavacchikhare ramye gaṅgādvāre suśobhane \|*  
*devyā saha mahādevo nityaṃ śiṣyaiśca saṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the charming peak of Himavan, there is a splendid tirtha known by the name of Garigadvara, where lord Mahadeva resides with Parvati, surrounded by his disciples.

## \|\| 2.44.14 \|\|

*tatra snātvā mahādevaṃ pūjayitvā vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*sarvapāpairvimucyeta mṛtastajjñānamāpnuyāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. By taking a bath there and adoring the bull- bannered Mahadeva, a person is relieved of all the sins. After his death, he attains the perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 2.44.15 \|\|

*anyacca devadevasya sthānaṃ puṇyatamaṃ śubham \|*  
*bhīmeśvaramiti khyātaṃ gatvā muñcati pātakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Another sacred and splendid place of Shiva, the lord of the Devas, is known as BhimesVara. By visiting that place, a person is relieved of all his sins.

## \|\| 2.44.16 \|\|

*tathānyaccaṇḍavegāyāḥ saṃbhedaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Similar is the case with the confluence of the river Candavega, which removes all the sins. By taking a bath there and consuming its water, a person is relieved of the sin of brahmahatya.

## \|\| 2.44.17 \|\|

*sarveṣāmapi caiteṣāṃ tīrthānāṃ paramā purī \|*  
*nāmnāvārāṇasī divyā koṭikoṭyayutādhikā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The city of Varanasi, is the best of all the tirthas. Because of its being divine, it is a ten thousand times, nay, a hundred million times more auspicious than all these holy centres.

## \|\| 2.44.18 \|\|

*tasyāḥ purastānmāhātmyaṃ bhāṣitaṃ vo mayā tviha \|*  
*nānyatra labhyate muktiryogināpyekajanmanā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Earlier, I had mentioned about its glory. Nowhere else does one attain salvation in a single birth even by means of Yoga.

## \|\| 2.44.19 \|\|

*ete prādhānyataḥ proktā deśāḥ pāpaharā nṛṇām \|*  
*gatvā saṃkṣālayet pāpaṃ janmāntaraśataiḥ kṛtam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I have described the selected and prominent tirthas. They relieve all the people of all the sins. One should visit them and wash out the sins of many births.

## \|\| 2.44.20 \|\|

*yaḥ svadharmān parityajya tīrthasevāṃ karoti hi \|*  
*na tasya phalate tīrthamahi loke paratra ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. But one should be careful, that when he discarding his own dharma, goes on pilgrimage to holy places, for such a person no tirtha is rewarding in the present life or the life beyond that.

## \|\| 2.44.21 \|\|

*prāyaścittī ca vidhurastathā pāpacaro gṛhī \|*  
*prakuryāt tīrthasaṃsevāṃ ye cānye tādṛśā janāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. One who is desirous of repentance, or the one who has become a widower, or a wandering mendicant, such a householder and the similar types of people should go to the holy places.

## \|\| 2.44.22 \|\|

*sahāgnirvā sapatnīko gacchet tīrthāni yatnataḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto yathoktāṃ gatimāpnuyāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The one who is an Agnihotrin, he should go with his wife carrying the sacrificial fires with him and should visit the sacred places, carefully, and by so doing, a person getting relieved of all the sins, achieves the best of deliverance mentioned before.

## \|\| 2.44.23 \|\|

*ṛṇāni trīṇyapākṛtya kuryād vā tīrthasevanam \|*  
*vidhāya vṛttiṃ putrāṇāṃ bhāryāṃ teṣu nidhāya ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Or otherwise, a person getting free from all the three debts (to Deva, Pitrs and sages), arranging livelihood for his sons, and entrusting the care of his wife to them, should go on to pilgrimage.

## \|\| 2.44.24 \|\|

*prāyaścittaprasaṅgena tīrthamāhātmyamīritam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyād vāpi mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus, the glory of the tirthas in the context of the expiatory rites has been spoken out. The one who reads it or listens to it, he is relieved of all the sins.

## Chapter 45. Dissolution of the world

## \|\| 2.45.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*etadākarṇya vijñānaṃ nārāyaṇamukheritam \|*  
*kūrmarūpadharaṃ devaṃ papracchurmunayaḥ prabhum \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said, “Listening to the excellent knowledge from the mouth of Narayana, the sages then asked the lord who had taken to the form of a tortoise.

## \|\| 2.45.2-3 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathitā bhavatā dharmā mokṣajñānaṃ savistaram \|*  
*lokānāṃ sargavistāraṃ vaṃśamanvantarāṇi ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pratisargamidānīṃ no vaktumarhasī mādhava \|*  
*bhūtānāṃ bhūtabhavyeśa yathā pūrvaṃ tvayoditam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The sages said, “You have spoken in detail about the dharma, knowledge about the attaining of salvation, the creation of the universe, the genealogies of kings and sages and the Manvantaras in sufficient details. Now, О Lord of the past and future, speak out the details about the dissolution of the world, the subject on which you have already spoken.”

## \|\| 2.45.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śrutvā teṣāṃ tadā vākyaṃ bhagavān kūrmarūpadhṛk \|*  
*vyājahāra mahāyogī bhūtānāṃ pratisaṃcaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Suta said, “Listening to the words of the sages, lord, the great Yogin, in the form of a tortoise, started speaking about the dissolution of all living beings.

## \|\| 2.45.5 \|\|

*kūrma uvāca*  
*nityo naimittikaścaiva prākṛtātyantikau tathā \|*  
*caturdhāyaṃ purāṇe 'smin procyate pratisaṃcaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Kurma said, “Four types of dissolutions are there-viz.: Nitya, Naimittika, Prakrta, and Atyantika, as mentioned in this Purana. These are the four types of dissolutions which are described below.

## \|\| 2.45.6 \|\|

*yo 'yaṃ saṃdṛśyate nityaṃ loke bhūtakṣayastviha \|*  
*nityaḥ saṃkīrtyate nāmnā munibhiḥ pratisaṃcaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The destruction of the living beings that is witnessed every day in this world is called Nitya dissolution by the sages.

## \|\| 2.45.7 \|\|

*brāhmo naimittiko nāma kalpānte yo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*trailokyasyāsya kathitaḥ pratisargo manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the end of the kalpa, the dissolution of three worlds by Brahma (due to his sleep at the end of his day), has been called as the Naimittika dissolution by the learned sages.

## \|\| 2.45.8 \|\|

*mahādādyāṃ viśeṣāntaṃ yadā saṃyāti saṃkṣayam \|*  
*prākṛtaḥ pratisargo 'yaṃ procyate kālacintakaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When the ultimate causes of the universe beginning with Mahat and ending with Visesa undergo dissolution, it is called the Pmbla Pratisarga (natural dissolution) by those who ponder over Kala.

## \|\| 2.45.9 \|\|

*jñānādātyantikaḥ prokto yoginaḥ paramātmani \|*  
*pralayaḥ pratisargo 'yaṃ kālacintāparairdvijaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*
