9\. The final absorption of Yogins into the Supreme Atman as a result of the realization {Jnana), the watchers of the Kala, call it the Atyantika Pratisarga (ultimate dissolution).

## \|\| 2.45.10 \|\|

*ātyantikaśca kathitaḥ pralayo 'tra sasādhanaḥ \|*  
*naimittikamidānīṃ vaḥ kathayiṣye samāsataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Atyantika Pratisarga achieved through Jnana has already been recounted. Now, I shall now speak on the Naimittika pralaya in detail.

## \|\| 2.45.11 \|\|

*caturyugasahasrānte saṃprāpte pratisaṃcare \|*  
*svātmasaṃsthāḥ prajāḥ kartuṃ pratipede prajāpatiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the end of the thousand sets of four Yugas, when the time of dissolution arrives, Prajapati Brahma, thought of absorbing all the people in his own self.

## \|\| 2.45.12 \|\|

*tato bhavatyanāvṛṣṭistīvrā sā śatavārṣikī \|*  
*bhūtakṣayakarī ghorā sarvabhūtakṣayaṅkarī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereafter, for a period of a hundred years since that time, there had been a terrific draught, as a result of which, all the living being were destroyed.

## \|\| 2.45.13 \|\|

*tato yānyalpasārāṇi sattvāni pṛthivītale \|*  
*tāni cāgre pralīyante bhūmitvamupayānti ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О lord of the Earth, the beings on earth who are physically weak, got destroyed first of all, and were reduced to Bhiimi (become one with the earth).

## \|\| 2.45.14 \|\|

*saptaraśmiratho bhūtvā samuttiṣṭhan divākaraḥ \|*  
*asahyaraśmirbhavati pibannambho gabhastibhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereafter, the sun with his seven rays, while rising becomes unbearable with the blazing heat. Through them he drinks up all water present on the earth.

## \|\| 2.45.15 \|\|

*tasya te raśmayaḥ sapta pibantyambu mahārṇave \|*  
*tenāhāreṇa tā dīptāḥ sūryāḥ sapta bhavantyuta \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In this way, the seven rays of the sun dry up the water from the middle of the ocean. Thanks to this intake, they become brilliant and change themselves into seven suns.

## \|\| 2.45.16 \|\|

*tataste raśmayaḥ sapta sūryā bhūtvā caturdiśam \|*  
*caturlokamidaṃ sarvaṃ dahanti śikhinastathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then, those seven rays (the seven suns), dries up all the lokas in the four directions and starts burning them like the fire.

## \|\| 2.45.17 \|\|

*vyāpnuvantaśca te viprāstūrdhvaṃ cādhaśca raśmibhiḥ \|*  
*dīpyante bhāskarāḥ sapta yugāntāgnipratāpinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. All the seven suns, by means of their rays penetrating into the upper and lower parts of the earth, bum the earth like the fire of dissolution.

## \|\| 2.45.18 \|\|

*te sūryā vāriṇā dīptā bahusāhastraraśmayaḥ \|*  
*khaṃ samāvṛtya tiṣṭhanti nirdahanto vasuṃdharām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus suns, having been illuminated by the water (sucked by them), shed forth thousands of rays, pervading the entire sky forcefully, and put the entire earth in flames.

## \|\| 2.45.19 \|\|

*tatasteṣāṃ pratāpena dahyamānā vasuṃdharā \|*  
*sādrinadyarṇavadvīpā nisnehā samapadyata \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thereafter, with the excessive heat of those suns, the burning earth, is deprived of water over the mountains, in the rivers and the oceans etc., besides the islands.

## \|\| 2.45.20-21 \|\|

*dīptābhiḥ saṃtatābhiśca raśmibhirvai samantataḥ \|*  
*adhaścordhvaṃ ca lagnābhistiryak caiva samāvṛtam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sūryāgninā pramṛṣṭānāṃ saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ parasparam \|*  
*ekatvamupayātānāmekajvālaṃ bhavatyuta \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. As the burning rays of the sun are spread in all the directions, covering all high and low regions, so powerfully and envelop everything. In this way, due to the fire of the sun rays, all the padarthas of the world are turned into a single mass of fire forming one fiery unit.

## \|\| 2.45.22 \|\|

*sarvalokapraṇāśaśca so 'gnirbhūtvā sukuṇḍalī \|*  
*caturlokamidaṃ sarvaṃ nirdahatyātmatejasā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. This fire of the time of dissolution which destroys all the lokas, takes to a spherical form and reduces to ashes all the worlds with its flames.

## \|\| 2.45.23 \|\|

*tataḥ pralīne sarvasmiñ jaṅgame sthāvare tathā \|*  
*nirvṛkṣā nistṛṇā bhūmiḥ kūrmapṛṣṭhā prakāśate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Therafler, all the mobile and immobile things are absorbed into that fire, the earth getting deprived of the vegetation and the trees, illumines like the back of a tortoise.

## \|\| 2.45.24 \|\|

*ambarīṣamivābhāti sarvamāpūritaṃ jagat \|*  
*sarvameva tadarcirbhiḥ pūrṇaṃ jājvalyate punaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The entire universe, with the sharp rays of the sun falling over it, looks like the frying pan. With those rays, everything bums in flames.

## \|\| 2.45.25 \|\|

*pātāle yāni sattvāni mahodadhigatāni ca \|*  
*tatastāni pralīyante bhūmitvamupayānti ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Similarly, in the netherworlds as well as in the great oceans, the creations living there have also to face the dissolution. They cmmble and get mixed into the earth.

## \|\| 2.45.26 \|\|

*dvīpāṃśca parvatāṃścaiva varṣāṇyatha mahodadhīn \|*  
*tān sarvān bhasmasāt kṛtvā saptātmā pāvakaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The fire god with seven souls (rays), reduces to ashes, all the islands, mountains, regions and the vast oceans.

## \|\| 2.45.27 \|\|

*samudrebhyo nadībhyaśca pātālebhyaśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*pibannapaḥ samiddho 'gniḥ pṛthivīmāśrito jvalan \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Besides, it also consume the waters of the oceans and the rivers. The flaming fire, keeps on burning on the earth.

## \|\| 2.45.28 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃvartakaḥ śailānatikramya mahāṃstathā \|*  
*lokān dahati dīptātmā rudratejovijṝmbhitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Thereafter, the great Samvartaka fire being ablaze, expanded by the forceful winds, crossing over the mountains, burns down the entire worlds.

## \|\| 2.45.29 \|\|

*sa dagdhvā pṛthivīṃ devo rasātalamaśoṣayat \|*  
*adhastāt pṛthivīṃ dagdhvā divamūrdhvaṃ dahiṣyati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The flaming fire, after burning the earth, dries up Rasatala as well. After burning the lower part of the earth, it starts burning the heaven above.

## \|\| 2.45.30 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ śatānīha sahasrāṇyayutāni ca \|*  
*uttiṣṭhanti śikhāstasya vahneḥ saṃvartakasya tu \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The flames of Samvartaka fire, rises upto the height of hundreds, thousands and ten thousands of yojanas.

## \|\| 2.45.31 \|\|

*gandharvāṃśca piśācāṃśca sayakṣoragarākṣasān \|*  
*tadā dahatyasau dīptaḥ kālarudrapracoditaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With the inspiration of Kalarudra, these flames start burning the Gandharvas, Pisacas, Yaksas, Nagas and the Raksasas.

## \|\| 2.45.32 \|\|

*bhūrlokaṃ ca bhuvarlokaṃ svarlokaṃ ca tathā mahaḥ \|*  
*dahedaśeṣaṃ kālāgniḥ kālo viśvatanuḥ svayam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. It appears as if Kalagni-the god of death has taken to the destructive form. Then, this fire completely bums out the regions of Bhurloka, Bhuvarloka and Maharloka.

## \|\| 2.45.33 \|\|

*vyāpteṣveteṣu lokeṣu tiryagūrdhvamathāgninā \|*  
*tat tejaḥ samanuprāpya kṛtsnaṃ jagadidaṃ śanaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. When the fire of dissolution, spreading on all the sides, rising above, engulfs the entire universe, then all of them start illuming in a huge flame.

## \|\| 2.45.34 \|\|

*ayoguḍanibhaṃ sarvaṃ tadā caikaṃ prakāśate \|*  
*tato gajakulonnādāstaḍidbhiḥ samalaṅkṛtāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thereafter, the vast and thick clouds known as Samvartaka, having shapes of huge elephants, decorated with the groups of lightnings, rise over the sky.

## \|\| 2.45.35-36 \|\|

*uttiṣṭhanti tadā vyomni ghorāḥ saṃvartakā ghanāḥ \|*  
*kecinnīlotpalaśyāmāḥ kecit kumudasannibhāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dhūmravarṇāstathā kecit kecit pītāḥ payodharāḥ \|*  
*kecid rāsabhavarṇāstu lākṣārasanibhāstathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. There arise in the sky the terrible Samvartaka clouds of world destruction. Some of those clouds are dark resembling the blue lotus flowers. Some of them are white like water-lily, some are of smoke colour, some are of yellow colour, and some are of colour like a donkey. Some of them of are of red colour like lac juice.

## \|\| 2.45.37 \|\|

*śaṅkhakundanibhāścānye jātyañjananibhāḥ pare \|*  
*manaḥ śilābhāstvanye ca kapotasadṛśāḥ pare \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Some of them are white like the conch or the lotus flowers, some are like the finest variety of collyrium, some are of the colour of red arsenic, white, others have the colour of a pigeon.

## \|\| 2.45.38 \|\|

*indragopanibhāḥ keciddharitālanibhāstathā \|*  
*indracāpanibhāḥ keciduttiṣṭhanti ghanā divi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Some of them appear like glow-worms, some resemble the yellow orpiment. Some are like rainbows. Such clouds rise up in the heaven.

## \|\| 2.45.39 \|\|

*kecit parvatasaṃkāśāḥ kecid gajakulopamāḥ \|*  
*kūṭāṅgāranibhāścānye kecinmīnakulodvahāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Some of them are of mountain size, some of them look like the herds of elephants, some of them are like the heaps of burning coal, and some like shoals of fishes.

## \|\| 2.45.40 \|\|

*bahūrūpā ghorūpā ghorasvaraninādinaḥ \|*  
*tadā jaladharāḥ sarve pūrayanti nabhaḥ sthalam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. They have several forms, which are quite terrific. By thundering aloud, they fill up the entire firmament.

## \|\| 2.45.41 \|\|

*tataste jaladā ghorā rāviṇo bhāskarātmajāḥ \|*  
*saptadhā saṃvṛtātmānastamagniṃ śamayantyuta \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then the clouds-beings the progeny of the sun, turning themselves into seven forms, extinguish the fire on earth with the pouring of the rain water.

## \|\| 2.45.42 \|\|

*tataste jaladā varṣaṃ muñcantīha mahaughavat \|*  
*sughoramaśivaṃ sarvaṃ nāśayanti ca pāvakam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Like a flood water gushes out from them as rain. The terrible and inauspicious rain destroys the fire.

## \|\| 2.45.43 \|\|

*pravṛṣṭe ca tadātyarthamambhasā pūryate jagat \|*  
*adbhistejobhibhūtatvāt tadāgniḥ praviśatyapaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thus, with the pouring of the excessive rain, the earth was filled with enormous quantity of water. On being thus overpowered by water the fire merges into the water.

## \|\| 2.45.44 \|\|

*naṣṭe cāgnau varṣaśataiḥ payodāḥ kṣayasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*plāvayanto 'tha bhuvanaṃ mahājalaparistravaiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. As a result of the rainfall showered by the clouds, the fire on earth is completely extinguished in hundred of years. The flood envelops the entire universe with huge currents of water.

## \|\| 2.45.45 \|\|

*dhārābhiḥ pūrayantīdaṃ codyamānāḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*atyantasalilaughaiśca velā iva mahodadhiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In this way, at the instance of Brahma, the earth is filled with the water, as the sea shore is submerged with excessive moving of the oceanic waves.

## \|\| 2.45.46 \|\|

*sādridvīpā tathā pṛthvī jalaiḥ saṃcchādyate śanaiḥ \|*  
*ādityaraśmibhiḥ pītaṃ jalamabhreṣu tiṣṭhati \|*  
*punaḥ patati tad bhūmau pūryante tena cārṇavāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Slowly the earth with the mountains and islands is covered with water, and the water soaked by the sun-rays stays in the clouds.

## \|\| 2.45.47 \|\|

*tataḥ samudrāḥ svāṃ velāmatikrāntāstu kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*parvatāśca vilīyante mahī cāpsu nimajjati \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The same water again is poured on earth and the oceans are so over filled, that, they overflowing the seashores cause a deluge.

## \|\| 2.45.48-49 \|\|

*tasminnekārṇave ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame \|*  
*yoganindrāṃ samāsthāya śete devaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*caturyugasahasrāntaṃ kalpamāhurmaharṣayaḥ \|*  
*vārāho vartate kalpo yasya vistāra īritaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Even the mountains become submerged in water besides the earth. All the mobiles and immobiles are destroyed. As a result of which lord Brahma, under the influence of Yoganidra goes to sleep in the ocean. The learned people consider the period a thousand cycles of four Yugas as a Kalpa.

## \|\| 2.45.50 \|\|

*asaṃkhyātāstathā kalpā brahmaviṣṇuśivātmakāḥ \|*  
*kathitā hi purāṇeṣu munibhiḥ kālacintakaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Presently the Varaha-kalpa is passing, the details of which have already been spoken by me. The Rishis who are conscious about the Kala (time), they have traced innumerable kalpas in the Puranas. Ali the kalpas resemble Brahma, Visnu and Shiva.

## \|\| 2.45.51 \|\|

*sāttvikeṣvatha kalpeṣu māhātmyamadhikaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*tāmaseṣu harasyoktaṃ rājaseṣu prajāpateḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The Sattvika kalpas out of them contain the excessive glory of Visnu, while the one of the lord Shiva is prominent in the Tamasa kalpas. The glory of Brahma is found in the Rajcisa kalpas.

## \|\| 2.45.52-53 \|\|

*yo 'yaṃ pravartate kalpo vārāhaḥ sāttviko mataḥ \|*  
*anye ca sāttvikāḥ kalpā mama teṣu parigrahaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dhyānaṃ tapastathā jñānaṃ labdhvā teṣveva yoginaḥ \|*  
*ārādhya giriśaṃ māṃ ca yānti tat paramaṃ padam \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. The current kalpa is known as Varaha kalpa, which has been considered to be the Sattvika one. There are other Sattvika kalpas in which I (Kurma Visnu) predominate. The Yogins achieving meditation, penance as well as the divine knowledge, adoring me and Girisa, achieve the great region.

## \|\| 2.45.54 \|\|

*so 'haṃ sattvaṃ samāsthāya māyī māyāmayīṃ svayam \|*  
*ekārṇave jagatyasmin yoganidrāṃ vrajāmi tu \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thus, I, being the illusory one, embracing the great illusion, enjoy the divine sleep of Yoganidra in the oceanic world.

## \|\| 2.45.55 \|\|

*māṃ paśyanti mahātmānaḥ suptaṃ kālaṃ maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*janaloke vartamānāstapasā yogacakṣuṣā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. During the period of my sleep, the great sages dwelling in the Janaloka, visualise me with the Yogic vision.

## \|\| 2.45.56 \|\|

*ahaṃ purāṇapuruṣo bhūrbhuvaḥ prabhavo vibhuḥ \|*  
*sahasracaraṇaḥ śrīmān sahasrāṃśuḥ sahasradṛk \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. I happen to be the Puranapurusa, besides being the place of origin of Bhuh (earth), and Bhuvah (the ether).

## \|\| 2.45.57-58 \|\|

*mantro 'gnirbrāhmiṇā gāvaḥ kuśāśca samidho hyaham \|*  
*prokṣaṇī ca śruvaścaiva somo ghṛtamathāsmyaham \|\| 57 \|\|*

*saṃvartako mahānātmā pavitraṃ paramaṃ yaśaḥ \|*  
*vedo vedyaṃ prabhurgoptā gopatirbrahmaṇo mukham \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. I am all pervading, having thousands of feet, eyes legs, and possessing the enormous beauty.

I am the Mantra, the Brahmanas, the cows, the sacrificial twigs, and the Proksanlya (that which should be sprinkled). I am Soma and the form of vratas. I am Samvartaka-the cloud of the time of dissolution, the great Soul, besides being the auspicious and excellent glory.

## \|\| 2.45.59 \|\|

*anantastārako yogī gatirgatimatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*haṃsaḥ prāṇo 'tha kapilo viśvamūrtiḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. I am the intelligence, the lord, the protector of cowherds, and the face of Brahma. I am endless, bestower of salvation on all, besides being a Yogin. I am the goal, the most excellent among those who afford the goal.

## \|\| 2.45.60 \|\|

*kṣetrajñaḥ prakṛtiḥ kālo jagadbījamathāmṛtam \|*  
*mātā pitā mahādevo matto hyanyanna vidyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. I happen to be Harhsa (Swan), Prana (vital breath), Kapila, of universal form, the eternal one, Jlvatma (the immanent soul), Prakrti, Kala (Time), the seed of the universe, the immortal nectar. The mother, father and Mahadeva, I represent all of them. There is nothing beyond me.

## \|\| 2.45.61 \|\|

*ādityavarṇo bhuvanasya goptā*  
*nārāyaṇaḥ puruṣo yogamūrtiḥ \|*  
*māṃ paśyanti yatayo yoganiṣṭhā*  
*jñātvātmānamamṛtatvaṃ vrajanti \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. I am Narayana, having the complexion of the sun, protector of the universe and the form of Yoga. The Ascetics well-versed in the Yogic practice, can visualise my form. After realising the Atman, they attain my reality.

## Chapter 46. Description of dissolution and subsidiary creation

## \|\| 2.46.1 \|\|

*kūrma uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi pratisargamanuttamam \|*  
*prākṛtaṃ hi samāsena śṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The lord in the form of the tortoise said, “I shall now describe the excellent creation as well as the Prakrta (natural) dissolution in brief. All of you should listen to the same.

## \|\| 2.46.2 \|\|

*gate parārdhadvitaye kālo lokaprakālanaḥ \|*  
*kālāgnirbhasmasāt kartuṃ karoti nikilaṃ matim \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On the end of two Paradha (i.e. after the life time of Brahma), Kala, which annihiliates the entire world, the dark fire of dissolution, wanders for reducing the entire universe to ashes.

## \|\| 2.46.3 \|\|

*svātmanyātmānamāveśya bhūtvā devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dahedaśeṣaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Lord Mahadeva, making his own form to enter his body starts burning the entire world together with the gods, demons and the human beings.

## \|\| 2.46.4 \|\|

*tamāviśya mahādevo bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*karoti lokasaṃhāraṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ rūpamāśritaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then Nilalohita-Mahadeva, taking to the terrific form, enters into the fire, turning as Mahakala, destroys the worlds.

## \|\| 2.46.5 \|\|

*praviśya maṇḍalaṃ sauraṃ kṛtvāsau bahudhā punaḥ \|*  
*nirdahatyakhilaṃ lokaṃ saptasaptisvarūpadhṛk \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then entering the solar region, turns it like himself and taking to the form of sun with seven rays, Mahesvara reduces the entire universe to ashes.

## \|\| 2.46.6 \|\|

*sa dagdhvā sakalaṃ sattvamastraṃ brahmaśiro mahat \|*  
*devatānāṃ śarīreṣu kṣipatyakhiladāhakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Reducing to ashes the entire universe, Mahesvara then shoots a terrific weapon called Brahmasiras, which can even bum the bodies of the gods.

## \|\| 2.46.7 \|\|

*dagdheṣvaśeṣadeveṣu devī girivarātmajā \|*  
*ekāsā sākṣiṇī śaṃbhostiṣṭhate vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When all the gods were reduced to ashes, Parvati, the excellent daughter of Himalaya, stands by Shiva as the only witness of his performance. This has been ordained by the Vedic Srutis.

## \|\| 2.46.8 \|\|

*śiraḥ kapālairdevānāṃ kṛtastragvarabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ādityacandrādigaṇaiḥ pūrayan vyomamaṇḍalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Lord Shiva, wears a garland of skulls of the gods, as an ornament. He fills the sky with the multitudes of suns and the moons.

## \|\| 2.46.9-10 \|\|

*sahasranayano devaḥ sahasrākṛtiriśvaraḥ \|*  
*sahasrahastacaraṇaḥ sahasrārcirmahābhujaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*daṃṣṭrākarālavadanaḥ pradīptānalalocanaḥ \|*  
*triśūlī kṛttivasano yogamaiśvaramāsthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. He possesses thousands of eyes and eyelids, thousands of arms and feet, thousands of rays of splendour, and had awful curved fangs and appears with terrific faces. His eyes resemble the fire flames. He carries a trident, is clad in elephant-hide. He then establishes himself in his lordly Yoga.

## \|\| 2.46.11 \|\|

*pītvā tatparamānandaṃ prabhūtamamṛtaṃ svayam \|*  
*karoti tāṇḍavaṃ devīmālokya parameśvaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then, He, imbibing the great bliss, the prolific effusion of nectar, looking at Parvati, consumes the nectar and then perform Tandava dance himself.

## \|\| 2.46.12 \|\|

*pītvā nṛttāmṛtaṃ devī bhartuḥ paramamaṅgalā \|*  
*yogamāsthāya devasya dehamāyāti śūlinaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Consuming the nectar of the dancing of her husband, the extremely auspicious goddess Parvati, depending on Yoga, becomes one with the body of lord Shiva.

## \|\| 2.46.13 \|\|

*saṃtyaktvā tāṇḍavarasaṃ svecchayaiva pinākadhṛk \|*  
*jyotiḥ svabhāvaṃ bhagavān dagdhvā brahmāṇḍamaṇḍalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then, burning the cosmic egg, lord Shiva, by his own sweet will, discarding the Tandava dance, returns to his blissful form.

## \|\| 2.46.14 \|\|

*saṃsthiteṣvatha deveṣu brahmaviṣṇupinākiṣu \|*  
*guṇairaśeṣaiḥ pṛthivīvilayaṃ yāti vāriṣu \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When Devas had been annihilated, Brahma, Visnu and Pinaka-bearing lord Shiva, are unified in a resting position, the earth with all the virtues get absorbed in the oceanic waters alongwith its attributes.

## \|\| 2.46.15 \|\|

*sa vāritattvaṃ saguṇaṃ grasate havyavāhanaḥ \|*  
*tejastu guṇasaṃyuktaṃ vāyau saṃyāti saṃkṣayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The Havyavahana (Fire), absorbs the water alongwith all its tattvas. The element of Tejas (fire) with all its attributes undergoes dissolution in the element of Vayu (wind).

## \|\| 2.46.16 \|\|

*ākāśe saguṇo vāyuḥ pralayaṃ yāti viśvabhṛt \|*  
*bhūtādau ca tathākāśaṃ līyate guṇasaṃyutam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the wind god, the preserver of the universe, alongwith his attributes, is absorbed in the akasa-tattva (ether). Then the sky with all its gunas is absorbed in Bhutadi (tamasa- ahamkara).

## \|\| 2.46.17 \|\|

*indriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi taijase yānti saṃkṣayam \|*  
*vaikārike devagaṇāḥ pralaṃya yānti sattamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О Excellent Rishis, all the sense organs, get dissolved in Rajasa ahamkdra. The gods on the other hand get absorbed in the Sattvika- ahamkara.

## \|\| 2.46.18 \|\|

*vaikārikastaijasaśca bhūtādiśceti sattamāḥ \|*  
*trividho 'yamahaṅkāro mahati pralaṃya vrajet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then the Vaikarika, Taijasa, and Tamasa- the three types of ahamkaras merges in the Mahat-tattva (principle of intellect). The Mahat principle gets dissolved in Brahma of unmeasured prowess, alongwith these.

## \|\| 2.46.19-20 \|\|

*mahāntamebhiḥ sahitaṃ brahmāṇamatitejasam \|*  
*avyaktaṃ jagato yoniḥ saṃharedekamavyayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evaṃ saṃhṛtya bhūtāni tattvāni ca maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*viyojayati cānyonyaṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣaṃ param \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Then the unmanifest imperishable source of origin of the universe which is single and unchanging, annihilates all things. In this way after destroying all the living beings, after the destruction of all the tattvas and the padarthas (things), Mahesvara, separates Pradhana-tattva and the great Purusa from each other. This is called the absorption of the unborn Pradhana and Purusa.

## \|\| 2.46.21 \|\|

*pradhānapuṃsorajayoreṣa saṃhāra īritaḥ \|*  
*maheśvarecchājanito na svayaṃ vidyate layaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The dissolution does not exist by itself. It originates from the will of Mahesvara. When Pradhana is in a state of equilibrium of attributes, it is mentioned as unmanifest Prakrti.

## \|\| 2.46.22 \|\|

*guṇasāmyaṃ tadavyaktaṃ prakṛtiḥ parigīyate \|*  
*pradhānaṃ jagato yonirmāyātattvamacetanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Pradhana, is the place of the origin of the universe and is ignorant because of the tattva (principle) of Maya, but the soul, the twentyfifth principle, is lodged within the hearts of all. It is pure consciousness, and perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 2.46.23 \|\|

*kūṭasthaścinmayo hyātmā kevalaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ \|*  
*gīyate munibhiḥ sākṣī mahānekaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It is sung about by sages as the Saksin (cosmic witness), the great grandfather. The same is called Mahes'vara Shakti, which bums all the padarthas from Pradhana onwards.

## \|\| 2.46.24 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃhārakaraṇī śaktirmāheśvarī dhruvā \|*  
*pradhānādyaṃ viśeṣāntaṃ dahed rudra iti śrutiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Everything beginning with Pradhana and ending with Vis'esa is present in the physical body of Rudra. This has been defined by the srutis. The same Rudra also destroys all the Yogins, the learned persons. This is called the endless absorption.

## \|\| 2.46.25-26 \|\|

*yogināmatha sarveṣāṃ jñānavinyastacetasām \|*  
*ātyantikaṃ caiva layaṃ vidadhātīha śaṅkaraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ityeṣa bhagavān rudraḥ saṃhāraṃ kurute vaśī \|*  
*sthāpikā mohanī śaktirnārāyaṇa iti śrutiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Thus lord Rudra, overpowering all, destroys them. His Shakti stablises every one. If confuses all as well. It is the form of Narayana. This has been described by the Vedas. Lord Hiranyagarbha, the twentyfifth principle, creates the entire universe comprising of sat and asat, taking to the form of Prakrti.

## \|\| 2.46.27 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbhā bhagavān jagat sadasadātmakam \|*  
*sṛjedaśeṣaṃ prakṛtestanmayaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus, all the Shaktis known as Brahma, Visnu and Mahes'a, are omniscient, all moving, all pervading, peaceful, and remain in their ownselves, they also reward pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 2.46.28 \|\|

*sarvajñāḥ sarvagāḥ śāntāḥ svātmanyevavyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*śaktayo brahmaviṇvīśā bhuktimuktiphalapradāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Not only this, the three gods are the Ishvaras for all, who bind everyone, everlasting, and have the endless pleasures with them. They represent one imperishable principle in the nature of Lord Purusa, Pradhana.

## \|\| 2.46.29 \|\|

*sarveśvarāḥ sarvavandyāḥ śāśvatānantabhoginaḥ \|*  
*ekamevākṣaraṃ tattvaṃ puṃpradhāneśvarātmakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Besides, several other divine forces are enshrined in them, who are adored in various yajnas in the form of Agni and others. Inspite of each one of these Shaktis having thousands of physical forms, there is only one attributeless potency described variously due to its greatness.

## \|\| 2.46.30 \|\|

*anyāśca śaktayo divyāḥ santi tatra sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*ijyante vividhairyajñaiḥ śakrādityādayo 'marāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. With the help of the same Shakti, lord Mahesvara, playfully creates many bodies. He is seen sporting about.

## \|\| 2.46.31 \|\|

*ekaikasya sahasrāṇi dehānāṃ vai śatāni ca \|*  
*kathyante caiva māhātmyācchaktirekaiva nirguṇāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In all the yajnas, it is He who is worshipped by the Brahmanas, well-versed in the Vedas. It is heard in the Vedas that Rudra alone is the bestower of all desires.

## \|\| 2.46.32 \|\|

*tāṃ tāṃ śaktiṃ samādhāya svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*karoti dehān vividhān grasate caiva līlayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Shaktis of the gods like Brahma, Visnu and Mahes'a, are treated as the foremost of all the Shaktis.

## \|\| 2.46.33-35 \|\|

*ijyate sarvayajñeṣu brāhmaṇairvedavādibhiḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmaprado rudra ityeṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sarvāsāmeva śaktīnāṃ brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|*  
*prādhānyena smṛtā devāḥ śaktayaḥ paramātmanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ādyaḥ parastād bhagavān paramātmā sanātanaḥ \|*  
*gīyate sarvaśaktyātmā śūlapāṇirmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Some people call Agni as Is'vara, while others call Narayana as such, some call it as Indra, some call it as Prana and others speak it as Brahma. Really speaking, Brahma, Visnu, Agni, Varuna, all Devas as well as sages are glorified as the variants of the same single entity viz. Rudra.

## \|\| 2.46.36 \|\|

*enameke vadantyagniṃ nārāyaṇamathāpare \|*  
*indrameke pare viśvān brahmāṇamapare jaguḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. In whatever form a devotee adores Parames'vara, the lord Shiva appears before him in the same fonn and bestow reward on him.

## \|\| 2.46.37 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇavagnivaruṇāḥ sarve devāstatharṣayaḥ \|*  
*ekasyaivātha rudrasya bhedāste parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Therefore, one should take refuge in any one of these forms, and should adore lord Mahadeva and by so doing a person achieves the moksa.

## \|\| 2.46.38-39 \|\|

*yaṃ yaṃ bhedaṃ samāśritya yajanti parameśvaram \|*  
*tat tad rūpaṃ samāsthāya pradadāti phalaṃ śivaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasmādekataraṃ bhedaṃ samāśrityāpi śāśvatam \|*  
*ārādhayanmahādevaṃ yāti tatparamaṃ padam \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. But the all powerful, eternal Lord Mahadeva, the omnipotent, lord Giris'a, should be adored in his form, whether Saguna or Nirguna (with or without attributes). I have already spoken to you about the Nirguna form.

## \|\| 2.46.40 \|\|

*kintu devaṃ mahādevaṃ sarvaśaktiṃ sanātanam \|*  
*ārādhayed vai giriśaṃ saguṇaṃ vātha nirguṇam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The people who are desirous of attaining to the Yoga of Saguna type, they should adore the Paramesvara with attributes, i.e., the Saguna form, with three eyes, bearing Pinaka with matter hair and clad in elephant hide,

## \|\| 2.46.41 \|\|

*mayā prokto hi bhavatāṃ yogaḥ prāgeva nirguṇaḥ \|*  
*ārurukṣustu saguṇaṃ pūjayet parameśvaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It has been ordained in the Vedas that one should devote his mind towards Rudra, having the complexion of gold, with thousands of rays emanating out of his body. О Best of the sages, thus I have enlightened you on the Sabija-yoga (i.e. the Yoga with seed).

## \|\| 2.46.42 \|\|

*pinākinaṃ trinayanaṃ jaṭilaṃ kṛttivāsasam \|*  
*padmāsanasthaṃ rukmābhaṃ cintayed vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In case a person is unable to perform this, he should adore Нага as Visva (the universe), or as Brahma. О leading sages, if one is incapable of even this, one should devotedly worship Vayu (wind), Agni (fire), Indra and others.

## \|\| 2.46.43 \|\|

*eṣa yogaḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ sabījo munisattamāḥ \|*  
*tasmāt sarvān parityajya devān brahmapurogamān \|*  
*ārādhayed virūpākṣamādimadhyāntasaṃsthitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Or otherwise, one should forsake all gods beginning with Brahma, and should adore the everlasting lord Vimpaksa i.e., Shiva, who is beyond the beginning, middle or end.

## \|\| 2.46.44-45 \|\|

*bhaktiyogasamāyuktaḥ svadharmanirataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*tādṛśaṃ rūpamāsthāya samāyātyantikaṃ śivam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*eṣa yogaḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ sabījo 'tyantabhāvane \|*  
*yathāvidhi prakurvāṇaḥ prāpnuyādaiśvaraṃ padam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Following one’s own dharma or karman, getting purified, with utmost devotion, whichever god is worshipped by a person, lord Shiva taking to the form of the same god, reaches him. This is pointed out as Sablja Yoga. It is extremely sanctifying.

## \|\| 2.46.46-47 \|\|

*atrāpyaśakto 'tha haraṃ viṣṇuṃ bahmāṇamarcayet \|*  
*atha cedasamarthaḥ syāt tatrāpi munipuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*tato vāyvagniśakrādīn pūjayed bhaktisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ye cānye bhāvane śuddhe prāgukte bhavatāmiha \|*  
*athāpi kathito yogo nirbojaśca sabījakaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. One who practises Yoga in accordance with the injunctions shall attain the region of Is'vara. The two types of the spotless meditations have been mentioned to you. Moreover, which have been discussed by me earlier, the Nirbija and the Sablja Yoga has also been highlighted therein. In fact, tattvajnana has been conceived to be the Nirblja-yoga which has already been discussed by me earlier.

## \|\| 2.46.48 \|\|

*jñānaṃ taduktaṃ nirbojaṃ pūrvaṃ hi bhavatāṃ mayā \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ rudraṃ virañciṃ ca sabījaṃ bhāvayed budhaḥ \|*  
*sathavāgnyādikān devāṃstatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The learned people should adore Brahma, Visnu and Rudra, in the Sablja Yoga. Or otherwise, the wind-god and others should be adored with a devoted and controlled mind.

## \|\| 2.46.49-50 \|\|

*pūjayet puruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ caturmūrtidharaṃ harim \|*  
*anādinidhanaṃ devaṃ vāsudevaṃ sanātanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇaṃ jagadyonimākāśaṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*talliṅgadhārī niyataṃ tadbhaktastadapāśrayaḥ \|*  
*eṣa eva vidhirbrāhme bhāvane cāntike mataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Or alternatively, the four-armed lord Visnu should be adored, who is beyond the beginning or end, has the divine and eternal form, also known as Vasudeva or Narayana. He is the source of the origin of the universe, the form of the sky and is the bestower of the heaven. He should invariably wear his linga, and should resort to him.

## \|\| 2.46.51 \|\|

*ityetat kathitaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvanāsaṃśrayaṃ param \|*  
*indradyumnāya munaye kathitaṃ yanmayā purā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The same process is also to be followed in the last stage of the meditation of Brahman. Thus the excellent knowledge related to Bhavana meditation has been imparted by me.

## \|\| 2.46.52 \|\|

*avyaktātmakamevedaṃ cetanācetanaṃ jagat \|*  
*tadīśvaraḥ paraṃ brahma tasmād brahmamayaṃ jagat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The same knowledge, in earlier times, had been spoken out by a sage known by the name of Indrayumna. The universe of the nature of the manifest is bom sentient and non-sentinent. The Supreme Brahman is its Ishvara. Therefore, the universe represents the form of Supreme Soul or the Supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 2.46.53 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*etāvaduktvā bhagavān virarāma janārdanaḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurmunayo viṣṇuṃ śakreṇa saha mādhavam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Suta said, “Thus speaking, lord Janardana, in the form of Kurma, kept quiet. At that point of lime, all the gods including Indra, as well as the sages, started eulogising Madhava-Visnu.

## \|\| 2.46.54-55 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*namaste kūrmarūpāya viṣṇave paramātmane \|*  
*nārāyaṇāya viśvāya vāsudevāya te namaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*namo namaste kṛṣṇāya govindāya namo namaḥ \|*  
*mādhavāya namastubhyaṃ namo yajñeśvarāya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. The sages said, “Salutation to lord Visnu in the form of Ktirma. Salutation to Narayana-the universal form, salutation to Vasudeva. Salutation to Krisna again and again. Salutation to Govinda again and again. Salutation to Madhava. Salutation to the lord of the yajnas.

## \|\| 2.46.56-57 \|\|

*sahasraśirase tubhyaṃ sahasrākṣāya te namaḥ \|*  
*namaḥ sahasrahastāya sahasracaraṇāya ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

*oṃ namo jñānarūpāya paramātmasvarūpiṇe \|*  
*ānandāya namastubhyaṃ māyātītāya te namaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. О Lord with thousands of heads and eyes, salutation to you. You have thousands of arms and feet, and are the embodiment of perfect knowledge, salutation to you. Salutation to the lord of blissful form, to the great Atman. You are beyond the pale of Maya, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.46.58 \|\|

*namo gūḍhaśarīrāya nirguṇāya namo 'stu te \|*  
*puruṣāya purāṇāya sattāmātrasvarūpiṇe \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. You are with mysterious body, salutation to you. You are without attributes, salutation to you. You are ancient Purusa, and of the form of pure Existence, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.46.59 \|\|

*namaḥ sāṃkhyāya yogāya kevalāya namo 'stu te \|*  
*dharmajñānādhigamyāya niṣkalāya namo namaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. You represent Sarhkhya and the Yoga, salutation to you. You are the form of dharma, salutation to you. Obeisance to the unsullied one.

## \|\| 2.46.60 \|\|

*namostu vyomatattvāya mahāyogeśvarāya ca \|*  
*parāvarāṇāṃ prabhave vedavedyāya te namaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. You are the principle of Yoga, salutation to you. Obeisance to the Ishvara of great Yoga. Salutation to the lord of the greater and the lesser beings. You can be known through the Vedas, salutation to you.

## \|\| 2.46.61 \|\|

*namo buddhāya śuddhāya namo yuktāya hetave \|*  
*namo namo namastubhyaṃ māyine vedhase namaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. You are the form of Jnana, are spotless salutation to you. You are illusory one, besides being the controller of illusion. Bows again and again to Vedhas.

## \|\| 2.46.62-63 \|\|

*namo 'stu te varāhāya nārasiṃhāya te namaḥ \|*  
*vāmanāya namastubhyaṃ hṛṣīkeśāya te namaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*namo 'stu kālarudrāya kālarūpāya te namaḥ \|*  
*svargāpavargadātre ca namo 'pratihatātmane \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Salutation to your Varaha form, as also to that of Narasimha, and Vamana. Salutation to lord Hrsikesa. You bestow the heavenly pleasures and salvation. You are the eternal soul, salutation to you. Obeisance to one attainable through Yoga; obeisance to the Yogin, to the bestower of Yogas.

## \|\| 2.46.64 \|\|

*namo yogādhigamyāya yogine yogadāyine \|*  
*devānāṃ pataye tubhyaṃ devārtiśamanāya te \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. You are the lord of gods, and remover of the miseries of the gods. Salutation to you. О Lord, by your grace, we have well understood the perfect knowledge relating to the destruction of the worldly existence, and by knowing the same a person achieves nectar.

## \|\| 2.46.65-66 \|\|

*bhagavaṃstvatprasādena sarvasaṃsāranāśanam \|*  
*asmābhirviditaṃ jñānaṃ yajjñātvāmṛtamaśnute \|\| 65 \|\|*

*śrutāstu vividhā dharmā vaṃśā manvantarāṇi ca \|*  
*sargaśca pratisargaśca brahmāṇyasyāsya vistaraḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. We have heard about the various types of dharma, races, Manvantaras, the Sarga, the Pratisarga etc. and have also listened attentively to the creation and dissolution of the cosmic egg. You happen to be the witness of the entire universe. You have the universal form, besides being Narayana-the Supreme Soul. You are the endless Soul, we take refuge in you. You alone are competent enough to redeem the world.”

## \|\| 2.46.67 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi sarvajagatsākṣī viśvo nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*trātumarhasyanantātmaṃstvameva śaraṇaṃ gatiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Suta said, “O Brahmanas, this Kurma Purana, bestows the worldly pleasures as well as the salvation, which has been related to you. It was narrated by lord Visnu himself, the holder of the club.

## \|\| 2.46.68-69 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*etad vaḥ kathitaṃ viprā yogamokṣapradāyakam \|*  
*kaurmaṃ purāṇamakhilaṃ yajjagāda gadādharaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*asmin purāṇe lakṣmyāstu saṃbhavaḥ kathitaḥ purā \|*  
*mohāyāśeṣabhūtānāṃ vāsudevena yojanam \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Initially, in this Purana, for the knowledge of the people, the episode of the birth of Lakshmi has been stated. In order to fascinate all the living beings, her birth has been intended by Vasudeva. In this way, the origin of Prajapatis, the duties of the four varnas, and the source of the livelihood of each one of the varnas has been described.

Similarly \[ПW6\] the characteristics of Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksa have also been spelt out.

## \|\| 2.46.70-72 \|\|

*prajāpatīnāṃ sargastu varṇadharmāśca vṛttayaḥ \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ yathāvallakṣaṇaṃ śubham \|\| 70 \|\|*

*pitāmahasya viṣṇośca maheśasya ca dhīmataḥ \|*  
*ekatvaṃ ca pṛthaktvaṃ ca viśeṣaścopavarṇitaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*bhaktānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ samācāraśca śobhanaḥ \|*  
*varṇāśramāṇāṃ kathitaṃ yathāvadiha lakṣaṇam \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-72. The unification, separation and characteristics of Brahma, the Grand-sire, Visnu and intelligent Mahesvara has also been described. The symptoms of the great devotees, the conduct, the diet etc. and the characteristics of the castes and stages of life have also been added in this Purana. Thereafter, the primordial creation, the seven coverings of the Anda (cosmic egg) and the origin of Hiranyagarbha have been related.

## \|\| 2.46.73-78 \|\|

*ādisargastataḥ paścādaṇḍāvaraṇasaptakam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhasargaśca kīrtito munipuṅgavāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*kālasaṃkhyāprakathanaṃ māhātmyaṃ ceśvarasya ca \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ śayanaṃ cāpsu nāmanirvacanaṃ tathā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*varāhavapuṣā bhūyo bhūmeruddharaṇaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*mukhyādisargakathanaṃ munisargastathāparaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*vyākhyato rudrasargaśca ṛṣisargaśca tāpasaḥ \|*  
*dharmasya ca prajāsargastāmasāt pūrvameva tu \|\| 76 \|\|*

*brahmaviṣṇuvivādaḥ syādantardehapraveśanam \|*  
*padmodbhavatvaṃ devasya mohastasya ca dhīmataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*darśanaṃ ca maheśasya māhātmyaṃ viṣṇuneritam \|*  
*divyadṛṣṭipradānaṃ ca brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

73-78. Thereafter, there is the description of periods and units of time in this Purana, in addition to the glory of Tsvara, sleeping in the waters by Brahma, besides the relative interpretation. Then, there is the mention of the event of the rescue of the earth by Visnu, taking to the form of Varaha, the narration of Mukhya and other creations, the creation of the sages; the cremation of the subjects by Dharma before the Tamasa creation; start of the controversy between Brahma and Visnu, the entry of Brahma into the body of Visnu, the birth from the lotus of the intelligent lord and his delusion; appearing of lord Mahesvara on the scene, the glory of Shiva highlighted by Visnu, bestowing of the divine sight unto Brahma-Paramesthin; prayer offered by Parmesthin Brahma to Shiva.

## \|\| 2.46.79 \|\|

*saṃstavo devadevasya brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*prasādo giriśasyātha varadānaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Then bestowing of the boons by Mahesvara on Brahma, getting pleased has been described. Discussions between Sankara, the great Atman and Visnu, the events of the granting of boon by Mahes'vara, and disappearing of Pinaka-bearing lord from the place thereafter, have also been included.

## \|\| 2.46.80-81 \|\|

*saṃvādo viṣṇunā sārdhaṃ śaṅkarasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*varadānaṃ tathāpūrvamantardhānaṃ pinākinaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*vadhaśca kathito viprā madhukaiṭabhayoḥ purā \|*  
*avatāro 'tha devasya brahmaṇo nābhipaṅkajāt \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. О Brahmanas, the events of the killing of Madhu and Kaitabha, and the emerging of Brahma from the navel of Visnu have been mentioned. Then, the unification of Brahma with Visnu, has been mentioned.

## \|\| 2.46.82 \|\|

*ekībhāvaśca devasya viṣṇunā kathitastataḥ \|*  
*vimoho brahmaṇaścātha saṃjñālābho harestataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The delusion of Brahma, and the recognition of Hari has been described. Then there is a mention of the performing of the penance by the god of Devas.

## \|\| 2.46.83 \|\|

*tapaścaraṇamākhyātaṃ devadevasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*prādurbhāvo maheśasya lalāṭāt kathitastataḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Then, there is the story of Mahes'a, emerging from the forehead of Brahma. Then, there is the mention of the creative activity of Rudra and its opposition by Brahma.

## \|\| 2.46.84-85 \|\|

*rudrāṇāṃ kathitā sṛṣṭirbrahmaṇaḥ pratiṣedhanam \|*  
*bhūtiśca devadevasya varadānopadeśakau \|\| 84 \|\|*

*antardhānaṃ ca rudrasya tapaścaryāṇḍajasya ca \|*  
*darśanaṃ devadevasya naranārīśarīratā \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. Then, the glory of the lord of Devas, the boon granted by Shiva, vanishing of lord Mahesvara, the performing of tapas by Brahma, who had emerged out of the egg and appearing of Shiva before him, Mahadeva’s appearing in the Ardhanc.rlsvara form, and the separation of Pinaka-bearing lord from the goddess Parvati, have been described.

## \|\| 2.46.86 \|\|

*devyā vibhāgakathanaṃ devadevāt pinākinaḥ \|*  
*devyāstu paścāt kathitaṃ dakṣaputrītvameva ca \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Afterwards the daughtership of the goddess of Daksa as well as that of Himalaya is described alongwith the reality of the goddess.

## \|\| 2.46.87 \|\|

*himavadduhitṛtvaṃ ca devyā māhātmyameva ca \|*  
*darśanaṃ divyarūpasya vaiśvarūpasya darśanam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Her appearing in the divine form, then there arc a thousand names of the goddess as enumerated by her father Himavan himself.

## \|\| 2.46.88 \|\|

*nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ kathitaṃ pitrā himavatā svayam \|*  
*upadeśo mahādevyā varadānaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The advice given by the goddess and bestowing of the boons on Himalaya, creation of the subjects by Bhrgu and other Rishis, the expansion of the royal race, have been descirbed in this Purana.

## \|\| 2.46.89 \|\|

*bhṛgvādīnāṃ prajāsargo rājñāṃ vaṃśasya vistaraḥ \|*  
*prācetasatvaṃ dakṣasya dakṣayajñavimardanam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Birth of Daksa as the son of Pracetas, destruction of the yajna of Daksa, then the rising of a controversy between Dadlcha and Daksa, is then narrated.
